chapters.title: Chapter 551: Partnering With Amazon [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki reached across the low table, taking Da Silva’s calloused battle-hardened hand between her two small soft palms, squeezing gently.

"You came here because you’re my friend, right? Because you wanted to help me? You didn’t come here just to use me as a bridge to get to Blessed Land, did you, Valeria? I know you would never do that to me..."
Da Silva’s mouth slowly closed.
She sat there, looking down at Aki’s wide earnest blue eyes, feeling the warm innocent squeeze of the girl’s hands.
Every single diplomatic counter-argument in her arsenal died a silent, agonizing death in her throat.
If she pushed the issue of a Blessed Land partnership now, she would be explicitly admitting that their entire friendship had been a calculated political sham.
She would be confirming that she had only ever answered Aki’s late-night messages because she wanted leverage over the court.
In front of her own attendees, in front of the Lord of Blessed Land, she was completely boxed into a corner.

’She played me,’ Da Silva thought, her head slowly dropping by a fraction of an inch with a quiet hollow defeat settling into her chest. ’The little bird didn’t just grow wings... She grew fangs as well.’
Throughout the entire exchange, Da Silva had been forced to maintain the role of the devoted protective older sister.

And because she couldn’t break character without shattering her own image, the opportunity of a lifetime... an exclusive binding charter with humanity’s newest Gold Core had slipped through her fingers like dry sand.
Across the room, Kara let out a long sigh, resting her head against the high backrest of the sofa.
"Man," Kara drawled, her voice cutting through the heavy tension like a dull cleaver. "You guys talk too much. My head is spinning."
Da Silva turned her head, her amber eyes carrying a desperate flicker of hope.
Kara waved her single right hand dismissively, looking at the Amazonian High Marshal with lazy half-lidded eyes.

"Look," Kara said, "as long as you and your girls actually pull your weight and help Aki during the Tournament, we can sit down and talk about a formal alliance with Blessed Land later... After the dust settles."
Da Silva’s eyes flared wide.
The hope wasn’t dead and the door was still open.
"Truly, Lord Vespera?" Da Silva asked, her voice steadying as she stood up, dipping her head in a sharp respectful bow. "You have my personal oath... The warriors of Amazon will not falter."
"Yeah, yeah, don’t write the press release yet," Kara muttered, waving her off. "You do your job in the dirt, and we’ll see how generous I feel over drinks."
Kara leaned back, her mind quietly categorizing the trade balance.
’All of this is fine,’ Kara thought.
An alliance with Amazon wouldn’t just be an administrative shield for Aki... it was an open conduit for Blessed Land to siphon resources directly from the southern continent.
If Da Silva wanted to sit at the high table with Silas, she was going to supply construction crews, heavy agricultural conduits, and deep-sea mineral convoys.
And that was before Kara began stripping constant assets from the World Council once this succession circus was over.
’I need some investments for myself after all too, don’t I?’

"Alright," Kara said, clapping her single hand against her thigh. "Since we’re doing this joint squad nonsense, why don’t you show me what we’re working with? Present your people and their kits so I can build a loose formation that doesn’t end with them stepping on my boots..."
Da Silva hesitated for half a heartbeat.
In high-tier martial circles, revealing the exact elemental parameters, core thresholds, and masteries of your elite retainers was a massive security risk.

Information was the difference between life and death in a tournament but she looked at Kara and knew instantly that withholding information from someone who could atomize their squad with a sneeze was pointless.
Da Silva turned toward the two female attendees standing rigidly behind her couch.
"Step forward," Da Silva commanded.
The two women immediately snapped their heels together with a crisp clack, stepping out from behind the sofa and moving to the center of the Persian rug.
The first woman was tall, with broad powerful shoulders, dark mahogany skin, and short-cropped black hair cut into a sharp military fade.
Her features carried a striking unmistakable resemblance to Da Silva’s own sharp cheekbones, though her amber-brown eyes were younger and burning with barely suppressed combat adrenaline.

"This is my younger sister," Da Silva introduced with a flicker of genuine familial pride touching her voice. "Lieutenant Maya Da Silva... She’s Twenty-two years old and she holds a Purple Core, refined to the peak of the Second Stage, specializing in Earth."
Maya snapped a heavy clenched fist across her left breastplate, her knuckles thudding against the olive wool.
"A pleasure to stand before the Lord of Blessed Land," she barked, her voice carrying the rigid discipline of an Amazonian strike officer.
The second woman was slightly shorter, lean, with pale, olive-toned skin, sharp hazel eyes, and long dark hair braided tightly against her scalp in cornrows.
Her forearms were bound in thick leather bracers studded with small glowing quartz conduits.
"And this is Captain Leona," Da Silva continued. "Twenty-three years old and she’s a Blue Core, mid-Second Stage, possessing a dual affinity for Wind and Water."
Leona bowed her head with equal precision, her posture coiled like a hunting cat.
"Standing ready for deployment, My Lord."

"These two are the finest combatants within the age limitation that Amazon can field," Da Silva stated with her tone firm. "They have survived forty-two suppression campaigns before so they will not crack under pressure."
Kara sat with her chin resting on her palm, her violet eyes sweeping over the two young women.
"Cool," Kara said casually. "I’m Kara White and I’m nineteen."
Silence!
The entire room seemed to stall out.
Maya’s clenched fist froze against her breastplate.

Leona’s hazel eyes dilated to the size of coins, her breath catching so hard in her throat that she nearly choked and even Da Silva looked as though someone had struck her across the nose with a wooden plank.
’Nineteen?!’
The thought screamed through the minds of both Amazonian warriors with violent intensity.

They were twenty-two and twenty-three and they were hailed across the entire southern hemisphere as once-in-a-generation martial geniuses... prodigies who had broken through to the second stage and were almost to their third stage before their twenty-fifth birthdays, a feat that usually took seasoned veterans decades of blood and near-fatal trauma to achieve.
They had bled in freezing mud, spent their teenage years locked in gravity chambers, and considered themselves the apex of their generation.

And sitting right in front of them, wearing an oversized suit, lounging like a delinquent on a velvet couch with an empty sleeve, was a nineteen-year-old girl who had already achieved a Second Phase Gold Core.
A wave of pure suffocating jealousy, accompanied by the crushing, bitter realization of cosmic unfairness, washed over both soldiers.
Why were the heavens so absurdly biased? What was the point of twenty years of agonizing training when a nineteen-year-old stray could casually shatter barriers with a flick of her wrist?
Kara watched their faces contort with suppressed existential dread, thoroughly enjoying every second of it.

"Look," Kara said, shifting her weight, "your performance today is going to decide whether this alliance actually goes anywhere... If you drag your feet, get sloppy, or fold the second someone throws high-tier mana in your face, the deal’s off."
Maya’s jaw clenched, her pride rushing back to the surface.
"We are Amazonian warriors, Lord Vespera! We will throw our bodies into the fire to ensure the Prince... to ensure Aki is kept safe at all costs!"
"Yeah, screw that," Kara cut her off immediately, waving her single hand with utter disgust.
Maya blinked, stunned. "What?"
"Screw that," Kara repeated, leaning forward, her eyes narrowing. "Aki can protect herself. Right, Aki?"
Aki sat up straight, puffing her chest out with her hands resting firmly on her knees.
The midnight-blue and black gloves on her wrists were hidden beneath her skirts, but the heat of Silas’s trust was still burning in her veins.
"Yes!" Aki said with fierce adorable determination. "I can protect myself!"

"See?" Kara pointed out, looking back at the two soldiers. "You aren’t her bodyguards... You’re our flank supervision. Your job is to keep the minor trash from crowding our airspace so I don’t have to waste time clearing out unranked pests. Understood?"
Maya and Leona exchanged a brief, bewildered glance before saluting again.
"Understood, Lord Vespera!"
Kara turned her head toward Da Silva. "How much time until the gates open?"
Da Silva checked the glowing digital clock on her wrist slate.
"Fifty-two minutes. The Council arbiters are finishing the stabilization anchors within the transitional corridor as we speak."

"Good," Kara nodded, standing up smoothly from the sofa. "An hour is plenty of time to get our gear sorted... Da Silva, you can go. As combatants, we need to make sure our kits are locked in without high-command brass hovering over our shoulders."
Da Silva didn’t argue as she recognized when a unit needed isolation so she offered a final respectful bow to her attendees while stepping back toward the entrance.
"I leave my vanguard in your hands, Lord Vespera," Da Silva said, meeting Kara’s gaze. "Aki... fight well."
"I will, Valeria," Aki smiled softly.
Da Silva stepped out into the vaulted hallway, her heavy boots fading into the distance, and the thick oak door clicked shut once more.
SLAM!
The moment the latch locked, Kara turned back toward the center of the Persian rug, her eyes sweeping over Maya, Leona, and Aki.
"Alright," Kara said, rolling her shoulders back. "Since we’re technically in a temporary truce with Blessed Land... I’m going to let you two wear our newest uniform. Consider it a field test."
She raised her single right hand.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A brilliant pulsing sphere of cerulean mana flared over her open palm as she reached into her Lord Inventory.
From the spatial ripple emerged two complete sets of pristine combat armor, hovering lightly in the air before descending onto the low coffee table with soft metallic clinks.
The armor was breathtaking.
It was composed of layered, razor-thin plates of treated void-ivory, polished to a dull pearl-like sheen that absorbed light rather than reflecting it.
Delicate filigree of beaten gold was etched along the chest plates and pauldrons, tracing stabilization runes that hummed with power.
The crest of Blessed Land was noticeably absent from the center breastplate... leaving the design clean and unaligned.

"It isn’t completely finished," Kara noted, tilting her head to inspect the pieces. "The full production models will have active barriers, but these prototypes will do... The void-ivory plates offer sixty percent higher durability than standard mythril, and my Dwarves personally imbued wind runes into the knee joints and spinal linkages to boost your sprint speed by thirty percent."
Maya stepped forward, her dark eyes wide and practically glued to the gold-etched plating.
Her gaze was sweeping frantically over the runic conduits with her lips moving silently as she attempted to memorize the intricate overlapping patterns of the runes etched into the metal.
An armament like this... which was lightweight, highly durable, pre-enchanted with passive acceleration runes would fetch a fortune in the southern military academies.
If she could replicate even ten percent of the design for the Amazonian—
"Don’t bother," Kara’s voice broke through the silence sounding dry and mocking.
Maya flinched, looking up with a guilty start.
Kara was watching her with an amused half-lidded smirk.

"You can’t copy it. It was made by an Asgardian and even if your engineers somehow managed to reverse-engineer the thread... I’d slap your entire government with an intellectual property lawsuit for copyright infringement and drain your national treasury dry before the first batch cleared the foundry."
Maya cleared her throat, stepping back with a sheepish embarrassed cough.
Kara, however, stopped dead.
Her violet eyes blinked behind her glasses as she stared down at the floorboards with her jaw tightening as an agonizing realization struck her like a freight train.
’Wait...’ Kara thought. ’Shit... I should have just kept my mouth shut!’
A wave of agonizing regret washed over Silas’s soul.

’If I had let them copy it... if I had let the Amazonian military forge three thousand counterfeit suits... I could have waited until all this ended, pulled out the registered patent papers, and sued their entire republic for patent infringement... I could have settled for billions of credits in industrial royalties and three deep-sea mining anchors! Why the hell did I warn them?! I’m an idiot!’
Kara cursed her own big mouth internally, but before she could dwell on her lost fortune, a sudden rustle of fabric snapped her back to reality.
SHLICK!
Kara’s eyes flicked forward and her brain stalled.
Lieutenant Maya Da Silva had reached down, grabbed the hem of her olive service blouse, and cleanly pulled it over her head, tossing the tailored military wool onto the sofa.
She didn’t stop there.
With the brisk utilitarian efficiency of a soldier who had changed uniforms in frontline trenches hundreds of times, her hands went to the brass buckle of her tactical trousers.
CLACK.

The belt unfastened and the trousers slid down her muscular chocolate-skinned thighs, kicked aside to join her boots, leaving the twenty-two-year-old Amazonian officer standing in the center of the lavish drawing room wearing nothing but a utilitarian black sports bra and low-cut athletic briefs.

Her physique was terrifyingly gorgeous... tall, lean, packed with functional corded muscle across her abdomen and obliques with her dark skin unbroken save for three pale jagged shrapnel scars running along her left ribcage.
Kara’s single right hand froze in her trouser pocket.
’Is she...’ Silas’s thoughts stumbled with a cold sweat breaking out across his neck beneath the female disguise. ’Is she trying to seduce me?! Right now?!’

chapters.title: Chapter 552: Hunted By The Sand...?
paragraphs: Before Kara could even formulate a retreat, Captain Leona stepped up beside Maya.
RUSTLE!
Leona unzipped her high-collared service jacket, pulled her arms free, and dropped her trousers in two fluid motions.
Unlike Maya’s athletic bulk, Leona’s body was slender, wiry, with pale olive skin, taut shoulder blades, and long toned legs, standing in matching black tactical undergarments.
And then, down on the sofa, a small flustered rustle joined them.
Aki, seeing the two seasoned soldiers stripping down to prepare for combat gear, bit her lower lip.

Her cheeks flushed a delicate embarrassed pink, but not wanting to look like an amateur who didn’t understand military etiquette, she reached behind her back, pulled down the concealed zipper of her heavy navy velvet gown, and let the voluminous fabric pool around her ankles.
She stood in a delicate white-silk chemise that clung softly to her small, slender waist with her pale thighs exposed to the cool air and her shoulders shivering slightly.
Maya reached down to pick up the void-ivory cuirass, paused, and looked over her shoulder at Kara with complete unbothered professionalism.
"Lord Vespera," Maya asked, holding the chest plate against her ribs. "Did the armor come with matching enchanted compression undergarments? Or do we wear our standard military-issue under-layers?"
Kara’s throat hitched.

Her violet eyes darted frantically between the three half-naked women standing in the middle of the Persian rug as even with the female body provided by the disguise ring, Silas’s eighteen-year-old male soul was currently undergoing a meltdown.
Why did it have to be so random?!
"O-Oh," Kara managed to stammer, her voice pitching up a bit before she forced it back down into that cool detached drawl. "Yeah... Right... Undergarments."
She reached into her Lord Inventory with her single hand, rummaging through the dimensional space with speed.
Leona cracked her neck, stepping toward the table and picking up the greaves as she glanced sideways, noticing the frozen tension in Kara’s posture, and let out a soft amused chuckle.
"Don’t be shy, Lord Vespera," Leona said, waving a hand casually. "We’re all women here... Frontier deployments mean you sleep eight to a tent so you get used to it."
Kara let out a high-strung hysterical chuckle that sounded unnatural.
"Haha... yeah! Totally! You’re so right! We’re all... women! Just a bunch of gals hanging out in our underwear!"
Down on the floor, Aki’s cheeks turned an even brighter shade of scarlet.
’All women... huh?’ Aki thought, her large blue eyes flicking from Maya’s toned abs to Leona’s lean shoulders, and finally locking onto Kara’s sharp, beautiful disguised profile.
Aki’s mind immediately began racing again.
’She says all women... but Silas is underneath that! He’s looking at them! He’s looking at me!’
The thought made Aki’s knees feel weak with her toes curling into the wool of the rug as she clutched the hem of her white chemise.
Kara quickly pulled out two bundles of pitch-black, enchanted silk compression gear, tossing them directly into Maya and Leona’s arms to break the visual line of sight.

"Put these on first," Kara instructed rapidly, gesturing with her chin. "The compression fabric actively regulates internal body heat so the void-ivory doesn’t chafe against your skin when you’re cycling mana. Snap the lateral latches along the ribs, then slide the cuirass over the shoulders. Make sure the spine rune sits directly over your lumbar vertebrae or the wind acceleration won’t trigger..."
Maya and Leona nodded, immediately stepping into the dark compression suits and beginning the meticulous process of fastening the overlapping plates.
Kara exhaled a long, silent breath, turning her attention down to Aki.
The First Princess was standing beside the sofa, looking completely lost.
She had the third set of void-ivory armor resting on the cushions beside her, staring at the straps and buckles as if they were an ancient, unsolved cipher.
"Need a hand, Princess?" Kara asked, stepping over.
"P-Please," Aki whispered, keeping her eyes firmly averted from Kara’s chest with her face still radiating heat.
"Alright, turn around," Kara said, stepping behind her.
Aki obeyed, her back facing Kara.

Kara reached out with her single hand as her long calloused fingers brushed lightly against the bare skin of Aki’s upper back as she smoothed the delicate white chemise down, reaching for the rear buckles of the lightweight breastplate.
SHK!
Aki’s entire frame jolted at the touch.
The heat of Kara’s palm against her bare skin was electric, sending a fierce shivering ripple of goosebumps cascading down her spine.
Aki gasped softly, her shoulders hunching inward with her hands coming up to nervously clutch her own collarbones.

"Relax," Kara murmured, her breath fluttering against the back of Aki’s ear as she leaned in to align the shoulder strap. "You’re stiff as a board. If you don’t relax your lats, the breastplate isn’t going to seat properly..."
"I-I am relaxed!" Aki squeaked, her heart hammering so violently against her ribs she was terrified Silas could hear it through her skin.
Kara pulled the top buckle tight, clicking the void-ivory strap into place.
She worked with surprising dexterity for someone with only one arm, using her chin to hold the strap steady while her fingers threaded the brass tongue through the loop.
CLICK!
"Now the waist," Kara said, moving her hand down.
Her fingers slid around Aki’s ribs, brushing against the soft curve of her waist as she hauled the lower flank-guards into position.
Aki’s breath caught in her throat.
The scent of Kara was completely drowning her senses as she felt clumsy with her balance wavering as she tried to lift her foot to step into the thigh-guards.
"Whoa... careful," Kara warned, reaching out to catch Aki’s elbow as the princess wobbled.
"I have it! I have it—" Aki insisted, trying to regain her footing on the slick silk chemise.
She didn’t have it.
The void-ivory armor, while lightweight for an Awakened warrior reinforced by mana, was still fifty pounds of dense treated beast-bone.
To an Unawakened civilian whose muscles were entirely mundane, the sudden shift in center of gravity was catastrophic.
Aki’s slipper caught the edge of her discarded navy gown.
SWOOSH!
Her legs tangled and her knees buckled under the weight of the breastplate then with an ungraceful yelp, the First Princess went pitching forward.
OOF!

Aki hit the Persian rug face-first, landing flat on her stomach like an upturned turtle with the heavy void-ivory cuirass pinning her to the floorboards as her legs kicked out in useless pathetic circles.
"I can’t get up..." Aki groaned into the wool with her voice muffled and her pride completely shattered.
Maya and Leona, who had just finished clicking their own greaves into place, froze, staring down at the fallen princess in stunned silence.
Kara stood above her, looking down at the small, armor-clad lump struggling against the floorboards.
For two seconds, Kara’s mouth hung open.
Then, she burst out laughing.

"Oh, man," Kara chuckled, crossing her single arm over her chest and shaking her head with deep fond amusement. "I forgot about the mass differential. Yeah... that set was forged for an Awakened frame. Don’t worry, Princess. We packed a completely different lightweight mesh suit for you."
"You... you told me to put this on..." Aki whimpered from the carpet, her face buried in her arms, refusing to look up at the world.
The private waiting suite reserved for the sovereign nation of Khemet was vast, styled after an ancient desert sepulcher.

Heavy drapes of deep crimson and gold-threaded linen hung from the sandstone arches, and braziers of blue chemical fire cast flickering, dancing shadows across the low marble tables laden with imported figs, roasted meats, and chilled palm wine.
This was the waiting room of the Sun-Crown of Khemet.
Standing before his divan were the two combatants chosen to carry Khemet’s standard into the Exhibition of Succession.
On the left stood his second son, Prince Tariq... a tall muscular youth with broad shoulders, clad in polished bronze scale-mail with his fingers resting casually on the hilt of a curved khopesh.
On the right stood Lady Samira, the daughter of the Vice President, an elite sand-weaver dressed in flowing desert robes of woven serpent-silk, her eyes lined with heavy black kohl.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur raised a heavy golden goblet of wine, his deep baritone filling the sandstone room with pride.

"The Exhibition of Succession is our stage," Menes Al-Mansur declared. "The Nine Major Powers believe House Castellian holds the apex of this generation... They look to Europa’s artillery, to Borealis’s frost, to Amazon’s shock-corps and they forget the sands of Khemet."
He leaned forward, his hawk-like eyes locking onto Tariq and Samira.

"Your youngest brother, Malikar, is currently concluding our exclusive pharmaceutical negotiations with Sterling Bio-Dynamics in Valoria City," the President continued, a satisfied smirk touching his weathered lips. "Once that contract is sealed, our legions will possess the finest cellular regeneration serums on Earth and when the two of you break the northern bracket today, that place will belong to the desert!"
Tariq banged his armored fist against his bronze breastplate. "We will not fail the sands, Father! The crown will recognize our blood!"
Menes Al-Mansur smiled, raising the goblet to take a deep, celebratory draft of the sweet wine.
TICK!
A strange unnatural feeling vibrated against the President’s ribs as Menes Al-Mansur stopped.
The goblet paused inches from his lips and a sudden freezing prickle of cold intuition crept up the back of his thick neck.
He reached into the inner pocket of his suit with his heavy fingers pulling out a small ornate box crafted from solid star-iron, sealed with an ancestral blood-lock.
CLICK.
He opened the lid.
Inside the velvet lining rested a smooth polished sphere of translucent amber... a Life-Orb of the royal house, bound directly to the soul-core and heartbeat of his third son, Prince Malikar.
Menes Al-Mansur looked down and his breath stopped.
The amber light inside the orb was not glowing... at all... It just looked pitch-black and stagnant.
And right before the President’s widening eyes—
CRACK!
A jagged hairline fracture split the sphere down the center.
SHATTER!

The ancient relic exploded into a shower of dul lifeless glass shards, disintegrating into a fine gray powder that spilled between his trembling fingers and scattered across the sandstone floorboards!
"NO!"
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur surged to his feet with an ear-splitting agonized roar that shattered the crystal wine flutes on the table!
"MALIKAR!"
The golden goblet slipped from his hand, crashing against the stone, splashing dark-red wine across his leather sandals like freshly spilled gore.
Tariq and Samira recoiled with their weapons rattling in their grips as they stared at the President in horror.
"Father?!" Tariq stammered, his face draining of all color. "What... what has happened?!"
"MALIKAR IS DEAD!" Menes Al-Mansur wailed, clutching his own chest, his powerful frame shaking with violent sobs of raw grief. "My son! My boy! The pride of Khemet!"
Tears carved clean, pale lines through the dust on the sovereign’s dark cheeks.
Of all his children, Malikar had been his masterpiece.
He had been born with the purest and most terrifying Sand Affinity the royal lineage had witnessed in three centuries...
He was a prodigy whose soul naturally harmonized with the earth, capable of dissolving physical barriers and manipulating microscopic particles with terrifying elegance.
How could he die in the middle of a civilized and secure metropolis like Valoria City?! An assassination?
Menes Al-Mansur looked down at his trembling open palm, where the gray powder of the shattered life-orb still clung to his skin.
His sobs hitched as his hawk-like eyes narrowed, staring intently at the dust.
’Wait...’
The powder wasn’t normal glass residue, instead the fine gray particles were shifting and granulating into tiny coarse flakes of pale-yellow sand.

’It turned into sand...?’ Menes Al-Mansur thought, his mind racing through the ancestral grimoires of his house. ’A broken life-orb dissolves into pure soul-vapor. It never manifests physical elemental residue. That has never happened in the history of our bloodline...’
A terrifying icy chill traveled down his spine as the hairs on the back of his arms stood up straight, his spiritual pathways locking up in sudden panic.
’Why does it feel...’
The President’s breath caught in his throat.
’Why does it feel like we are being hunted...?!’
HSSSSSSSS!
A dry sound echoed from the shadowed corner of the ceiling.
Tariq’s head snapped upward. "What is that?"
On the far wall of the sepulcher suite, mounted near the heavy stone lintel, was an iron ventilation grate leading into the Citadel’s exhaust shafts.
Through the narrow diamond-shaped gaps of the iron grate...
Something was moving.

A thick undulating stream of coarse, pale-yellow sand was seeping silently through the metal slats, pouring down the vertical sandstone wall like a waterfall of grinding earth, pooling on the floorboards with a soft persistent hiss.
Menes Al-Mansur’s pupils contracted into microscopic pinpricks, his voice choking in his throat.
"Sand...?"
SPLAT!

chapters.title: Chapter 553: The Curse Of Khemet [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: SPLAT!
The sound was wet and sickeningly flat, but it did not come from freshly pumped blood spraying out of their own chests.
’We weren’t attacked...?’

The interlocking slabs of crystalline golden sand that Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur, his son Tariq, and Lady Safira had violently thrust into the air hung frozen between the stone ceiling and the Persian rugs for three agonizing seconds.
The runes etched along the perimeter of their shields hummed with an unstable high-pitched whine, vibrating under the expected pressure of the impact above them.
Slowly, the golden barriers lost their internal tension.

The compacted mana bled out of the particulate matter, and the golden shields began to disintegrate, sloughing away into thousands of loose dry granules that pattered against the polished flagstones like dry summer rain.
Shshshshsh!
The three sand-weavers dropped their trembling hands.
Their gazes dropped in unison, locking onto the center of the sandstone room directly beneath the blackened iron slats of the exhaust vent.
What had dropped from the dark duct was not an explosive elemental cluster or a slug... It was a dense shifting globule of yellow coarse sand that had already begun to rot in mid-air.
As it hit the stone, the physical laws governing basic earth manipulation seemed to warp and curdle as the compacted mass began turning into blood.
’What the fuck is going on...?’

The blood was dark-crimson and rancid with the foul reek of dead cells, the fluid weeped from the core of the mass, bubbling outward in greasy concentric ripples that soaked the edges of the imported silk rugs and stained the carved stone tiles a deep rust-colored brown.
’I still don’t understand what’s going on... Are we being attacked...?’
The sand absorbed the moisture, held it in a pressurized hydraulic lock, and was now vomiting it back out onto the floor like a ruptured sponge.
And sitting right in the center of that glistening gore-slick mire, rolling twice before bumping against the gilded claw-foot of an ivory divan, was a severed head.
It was Malikar.
The Third Prince of Khemet looked unrecognizable to anyone who had known his golden arrogant profile in the pleasure palaces of the Nile.
His rich sun-baked bronze flesh had been totally drained of all moisture.

The skin was drawn taut across the skull like parchment stretched over an iron frame, blackening around the cheekbones, shriveled and cracked until the teeth jutted out from receded gums in a grotesque, mocking grimace.
His dark kohl-rimmed eyelids were sunken deep into hollow leathery sockets that looked vacant and dried out like an abandoned wasp’s nest.
THUD!
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur’s knees simply gave out beneath him.

The current ruler of Khemet... a man whose mana had carved riverbeds through mountain ranges and forced continental armies to negotiate on their knees hit the cold flagstones with a hollow bone-jarring impact.

His fingers, heavy with solid gold scarab rings and raw emerald cabochons, dug into the blood-soaked floor as he crawled forward on all fours with his immaculate white uniform dragging through the cooling gore and his breath catching in his throat with a dry wheeze.
"Malikar..."
The whisper tore through his cracked lips sounding small and shattered. The man really looked nothing like a President.
"My boy... Malikar... no, no, no..."
He reached out.

His trembling fingers hovered over the shriveled leathery brow of the severed head, hovering an inch away as if terrified that the illusion would break if he touched it but the metallic stench in the room was too thick and the heat rising off the dark blood was too real as well.
He touched the matted black hair.
Fsssshhhh!
The instant the skin of his thumb brushed the dry follicles, a soft dry whisper broke through the room.
The hair simply dissolved.

The flesh of the scalp, the desiccated brow, the sunken cheekbones... all of it gave way beneath the light pressure of his fingertips, crumbling into a stream of ultra-fine powdery grains of pitch-black sand.
Black sand.
Tariq choked on his own breath, stumbling backward until his bronze scale-mail slammed against the carved wall with a loud clang while Safira’s hands flew to her mouth, her eyes bulging with horror.
In the sacred ancestral codices of Khemet, black sand did not exist in nature.
It was not an elemental variation, nor was it a volcanic impurity.

Black sand was the undisputed mark of the Void-Devourer... It meant that the person had not merely been slaughtered by blade or spell, It meant the physical and spiritual vessel had been unmade at the cellular level, the core hollowed out and the soul eradicated without leaving behind a single spiritual filament to enter the ancestral halls that were meant for where the people of Khemet went.
Before Menes’s widening eyes, the crumbling accelerated.
The dry jaw collapsed inward and the hollow orbits caved in with the sound of snapping dried reeds.
Shshshshshsh!
The black sand spilled through the open spaces of Menes’s trembling fingers, cascading over his rings like dry gunpowder.
It hit the wet crimson puddle below, but it did not mix with the blood... it was almost as if the black grains repelled the gore completely, sitting on the surface of the fluid like floating oil.
A sudden sharp draft whistled through the high lancet window from the stormy sea outside.

The gust dipped low into the chamber, catching the black powder from the floor and Menes’s open palms, lifting it in a swirling shadowy vortex before carrying the dark remnants of the Third Prince out through the iron bars and scattering them into the endless rain-swept sky above the Citadel’s outer trenches.
Nothing was left on the stone except the cooling pool of blood.
Menes remained on his knees with his head hung low between his broad shoulders while his dark eyes were wide and fixed on his own stained hands.
His teeth clamped together with a force so violent that the sound of enamel grinding against enamel echoed like cracking stones through the sepulcher.
The tendons in his thick neck stood out like steel cables beneath his dark skin with his knuckles turning chalk-white against the floor.
’Why me...?’
The question was a silent venomous scream tearing his ribs apart from within.
’Why now?! Why during my reign?!’
Behind him, Tariq scrambled forward, dropping to one knee and reaching out to touch his father’s trembling shoulder with a trembling armored hand.

"Father!" Tariq shouted, his voice cracking with panic. "Father, speak to us! What was that?! Who breached the ventilation conduits?! Was it an imperial assassin sent by the King?! Did Columbia hire a death-squad?! Tell us what to do!"
Safira’s hand gripped the hilt of her curved khopesh so hard the leather wrapping creaked.

"Pharaoh, we have to sound the alarm! The World Council’s inquisitors are in the corridor! We can seal the sector and demand an immediate inquest into the breach! A foreign prince has been executed under the Council’s own roof!"
Menes did not turn around.
He didn’t acknowledge his second son’s touch, nor did he hear Safira’s frantic demands.
His eyes, usually burning with the fierce radiant gold of a midday desert sun, were slowly losing their luster.
Second by second, the light in his pupils died out, dulling into a flat muddy brown that looked dead.
The silence dragged on for twenty suffocating seconds.
’Why did the Curse of Khemet have to wake up at this time...?’
He knew what this was and he knew what that black sand meant... It wasn’t an assassin hired by Vanderbilt and it wasn’t a strike from the King of the World.
It was the rotting ancient sin of House Al-Mansur, wasn’t it?
The horror buried four thousand feet beneath the Great Dunes of Khemet, an apocalyptic terror that his ancestors had sworn under blood-oaths had been put to sleep forever.

And now, at the precise moment humanity was standing on the precipice of another succession war, the ancient plague had crawled out of the dark, bypassed the defensive wards, and took the skin of his favorite son like a cheap linen tunic.
Slowly, Menes Al-Mansur pushed himself up from the floor.
His movements were mechanical and unnervingly quiet as he didn’t look at Tariq or Safira at all.

He smoothed down the gold pectoral around his neck, adjusted the cuffs of his white military tunic with cold precision, and turned his hollow, dead eyes toward the double doors leading to the Grand Assembly Chamber.
"Not a word," Menes said, his voice dropping into a flat toneless rasp that sounded like gravel dragging across iron.
Tariq froze.
"Father...?"

"You speak of this to no one," Menes commanded, his gaze sliding over his son with the cold indifference of an undertaker. "Clean this stone... Burn the drapes... If a single rumor of this breach passes your lips before the tournament concludes, I will sever your tongue myself. The Exhibition begins in eight minutes. Stand tall, or die where you stand."
He turned and walked out the door with his boots tracking faint dark-red crescents across the pristine white marble of the outer hall.
In the Great Assembly Chamber, the temperature felt like the bottom of an abandoned mine shaft.
More than five hundred diplomats, guild arbiters, military attachés, and high scribes occupied the tiered risers, but not a single page rustled and not a single pen scraped across vellum.
At the center of the room sat the Grand Table of solid celestial marble.
The King of the World sat upon the massive star-iron throne at the Royal dais.

Princess Kiera was no longer perched casually on his armrest; she had taken a seat on one of the vacant star-iron chairs immediately adjacent to his throne with her slender hands folded neatly over her lap.
She looked a bit too excited.
To the King’s left and right, the governing bodies of the world were fully assembled.
The World Council Heads occupied the high northern arc.

All of them remained shrouded in heavy light-absorbing cloaks of midnight-silk, their faces completely obscured by smooth uncarved masks of polished white porcelain that caught the light with a dull bone-like finish.
Beside them sat the Magistrates, including Magistrate Bloom, whose hawkish features were cast in shadow as he leaned forward over his sheathed saber.
Around the rest of the celestial ring sat the nine heads of state.
High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva sat back in her heavy iron chair, looking for all the world like an empress who had just conquered three continents before breakfast.

Her dark scarred face was relaxed, her muscular arms folded across her broad ribbon-covered chest with a quiet smirk playing along the corners of her lips as her amber-brown eyes occasionally flicked toward the empty lower benches where the First Princess had previously been seated.
Directly across the circle, Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur was the antithesis of her poise.
He looked like an exhumed corpse propped up in a chair.
His bronze complexion was drained of all color, taking on the sickly translucent gray of spoiled milk.
His gold-ringed fingers were curled around the edge of the marble with such unconscious terrifying force that the stone around his fingertips was creaking with microscopic fractures.
His liquid-gold eyes were fixed forward, staring into the middle distance with an unmoving glassy vacancy that completely ignored the holographic documents floating before his seat.
The King of the World leaned slightly forward with his deep sapphire irises shifting downward and fixing directly upon the ruler of Khemet.

"Pharaoh-President Menes," the King’s baritone rumbled across the stone, carrying that deceptive polite weight that preceded an execution. "You appear remarkably unsettled... Does the deployment of your people to this tournament affect you or is there another issue?"

For two seconds, it seemed as though he hadn’t heard the supreme monarch at all.
Then, his head jerked slightly with his gaze dropping to the table as he avoided the King’s eyes entirely.
"A minor disturbance within our group, Your Majesty," Menes answered. "It’s a private matter of state and it most definitely does not affect the readiness of Khemet’s banner."
Before the King could speak again, a soft dry rustle of silk broke from the northern arc.
One of the masked World Council Heads leaned forward.

The white porcelain mask was completely blank with no painted features, no eye slits, and no mouth line yet the aura radiating from beneath the dark cowl rolled across the Grand Table like a suffocating wave of swamp air.
"Your third son, Prince Malikar, was terminated inside a commercial district within Valoria City twenty-five minutes ago," the masked figure stated.

sentences.text: SPLAT!
The sound was wet and sickeningly flat, but it did not come from freshly pumped blood spraying out of their own chests.
’We weren’t attacked...?’

The interlocking slabs of crystalline golden sand that Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur, his son Tariq, and Lady Safira had violently thrust into the air hung frozen between the stone ceiling and the Persian rugs for three agonizing seconds.
The runes etched along the perimeter of their shields hummed with an unstable high-pitched whine, vibrating under the expected pressure of the impact above them.
Slowly, the golden barriers lost their internal tension.

The compacted mana bled out of the particulate matter, and the golden shields began to disintegrate, sloughing away into thousands of loose dry granules that pattered against the polished flagstones like dry summer rain.
Shshshshsh!
The three sand-weavers dropped their trembling hands.
Their gazes dropped in unison, locking onto the center of the sandstone room directly beneath the blackened iron slats of the exhaust vent.
What had dropped from the dark duct was not an explosive elemental cluster or a slug...
It was a dense shifting globule of yellow coarse sand that had already begun to rot in mid-air.
As it hit the stone, the physical laws governing basic earth manipulation seemed to warp and curdle as the compacted mass began turning into blood.
’What the fuck is going on...?’

The blood was dark-crimson and rancid with the foul reek of dead cells, the fluid weeped from the core of the mass, bubbling outward in greasy concentric ripples that soaked the edges of the imported silk rugs and stained the carved stone tiles a deep rust-colored brown.
’I still don’t understand what’s going on...
Are we being attacked...?’
The sand absorbed the moisture, held it in a pressurized hydraulic lock, and was now vomiting it back out onto the floor like a ruptured sponge.
And sitting right in the center of that glistening gore-slick mire, rolling twice before bumping against the gilded claw-foot of an ivory divan, was a severed head.
It was Malikar.
The Third Prince of Khemet looked unrecognizable to anyone who had known his golden arrogant profile in the pleasure palaces of the Nile.
His rich sun-baked bronze flesh had been totally drained of all moisture.

The skin was drawn taut across the skull like parchment stretched over an iron frame, blackening around the cheekbones, shriveled and cracked until the teeth jutted out from receded gums in a grotesque, mocking grimace.
His dark kohl-rimmed eyelids were sunken deep into hollow leathery sockets that looked vacant and dried out like an abandoned wasp’s nest.
THUD!
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur’s knees simply gave out beneath him.

The current ruler of Khemet... a man whose mana had carved riverbeds through mountain ranges and forced continental armies to negotiate on their knees hit the cold flagstones with a hollow bone-jarring impact.

His fingers, heavy with solid gold scarab rings and raw emerald cabochons, dug into the blood-soaked floor as he crawled forward on all fours with his immaculate white uniform dragging through the cooling gore and his breath catching in his throat with a dry wheeze.
"Malikar..."
The whisper tore through his cracked lips sounding small and shattered.
The man really looked nothing like a President.
"My boy...
Malikar... no, no, no..."
He reached out.

His trembling fingers hovered over the shriveled leathery brow of the severed head, hovering an inch away as if terrified that the illusion would break if he touched it but the metallic stench in the room was too thick and the heat rising off the dark blood was too real as well.
He touched the matted black hair.
Fsssshhhh!
The instant the skin of his thumb brushed the dry follicles, a soft dry whisper broke through the room.
The hair simply dissolved.

The flesh of the scalp, the desiccated brow, the sunken cheekbones... all of it gave way beneath the light pressure of his fingertips, crumbling into a stream of ultra-fine powdery grains of pitch-black sand.
Black sand.
Tariq choked on his own breath, stumbling backward until his bronze scale-mail slammed against the carved wall with a loud clang while Safira’s hands flew to her mouth, her eyes bulging with horror.
In the sacred ancestral codices of Khemet, black sand did not exist in nature.
It was not an elemental variation, nor was it a volcanic impurity.
Black sand was the undisputed mark of the Void-Devourer...

It meant that the person had not merely been slaughtered by blade or spell, It meant the physical and spiritual vessel had been unmade at the cellular level, the core hollowed out and the soul eradicated without leaving behind a single spiritual filament to enter the ancestral halls that were meant for where the people of Khemet went.
Before Menes’s widening eyes, the crumbling accelerated.
The dry jaw collapsed inward and the hollow orbits caved in with the sound of snapping dried reeds.
Shshshshshsh!
The black sand spilled through the open spaces of Menes’s trembling fingers, cascading over his rings like dry gunpowder.
It hit the wet crimson puddle below, but it did not mix with the blood... it was almost as if the black grains repelled the gore completely, sitting on the surface of the fluid like floating oil.
A sudden sharp draft whistled through the high lancet window from the stormy sea outside.

The gust dipped low into the chamber, catching the black powder from the floor and Menes’s open palms, lifting it in a swirling shadowy vortex before carrying the dark remnants of the Third Prince out through the iron bars and scattering them into the endless rain-swept sky above the Citadel’s outer trenches.
Nothing was left on the stone except the cooling pool of blood.
Menes remained on his knees with his head hung low between his broad shoulders while his dark eyes were wide and fixed on his own stained hands.
His teeth clamped together with a force so violent that the sound of enamel grinding against enamel echoed like cracking stones through the sepulcher.
The tendons in his thick neck stood out like steel cables beneath his dark skin with his knuckles turning chalk-white against the floor.
’Why me...?’
The question was a silent venomous scream tearing his ribs apart from within.
’Why now?!
Why during my reign?!’
Behind him, Tariq scrambled forward, dropping to one knee and reaching out to touch his father’s trembling shoulder with a trembling armored hand.
"Father!" Tariq shouted, his voice cracking with panic.
"Father, speak to us!
What was that?!
Who breached the ventilation conduits?!
Was it an imperial assassin sent by the King?!
Did Columbia hire a death-squad?!
Tell us what to do!"
Safira’s hand gripped the hilt of her curved khopesh so hard the leather wrapping creaked.
"Pharaoh, we have to sound the alarm!
The World Council’s inquisitors are in the corridor!
We can seal the sector and demand an immediate inquest into the breach!
A foreign prince has been executed under the Council’s own roof!"
Menes did not turn around.
He didn’t acknowledge his second son’s touch, nor did he hear Safira’s frantic demands.
His eyes, usually burning with the fierce radiant gold of a midday desert sun, were slowly losing their luster.
Second by second, the light in his pupils died out, dulling into a flat muddy brown that looked dead.
The silence dragged on for twenty suffocating seconds.
’Why did the Curse of Khemet have to wake up at this time...?’
He knew what this was and he knew what that black sand meant...

chapters.title: Chapter 554: Not That You Could Understand [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The voice was bizarre and hollow, carrying an unnatural sound that seemed to sound from inside the ears of every person at the table rather than through the air.
Every head of state stiffened simultaneously.
Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov’s frost-dusted brows slammed together in a heavy frown.

President Julian Vanderbilt Senior’s hands paused on his pinstriped trousers, his eyes narrowing in calculation and across the table, Chief Minister Rajesh Varma of Indus lowered his prayer beads, his psionic guard-mages behind him subtly shifting their weight onto the balls of their feet.
A cold uneasy murmur began to simmer in the upper mezzanine.
The identities and capabilities of the five masked Council Heads were among the deepest, most jealously guarded secrets on the planet.
For centuries, their individual power profiles, core refinement tiers, and personal histories had been erased from every library and terminal.

The only thing humanity knew for certain was that they were ancient monsters who had survived the first horrors of the Apocalypse, their lifespans artificially locked by unspeakable cultivation methods.
Nobody knew what elements they commanded and nobody knew what weaknesses they possessed.
’What a pain in the ass...’

It was this lack of actionable intelligence that had kept the World Council untouchable... every Lord or Sovereign who had ever attempted to raise a rebellion had been slaughtered before they could even learn what kind of mana had pierced their heart.
Yet this specific masked figure was widely assumed by the high cabinets to be the Council’s all-seeing eye.

Whether through an ancient divination artifact, an omniscient sensory domain, or an underground network of parasitic informants, he commanded a terrifying near-instantaneous awareness of global events.

’Does this freak see everything?’ Chancellor Henri de Montmirail thought bitterly, his hand tightening around the silver frame of his spectacles as cold sweat beaded behind his collar. ’Or does he just cherry-pick what he reveals to keep the rest of us looking like blind children? If he knows everything that happens across the continents and only opens his mouth when it suits his agenda... what an insufferable bastard.’
The masked Council member did not care about the silent curses directed at his mask.
’Perhaps he’s a machine?’
He continued in that dead mechanical monotone.

"The initial incident report filed with the Valoria City Police Department identified the perpetrator as Harper Whitmore... That designation has been dismantled as video intelligence secured by an independent asset... Lord Evelyn has verified that the entity was an unregistered sand-based biological mimic. The subject’s dermal layer was actively fracturing into loose silt prior to the biological drain and the physical likeness of the corporate executive was merely a stolen shell."
The chamber went dead silent.
A dozen subtle suspicious glances darted across the ring, settling squarely upon Chancellor Montmirail of Europa.
Valoria City sat within Europa’s borders so its infrastructure, its security grid, and its policing fell under the Continental Directorate’s jurisdiction.
Yet nobody dared to openly level an accusation.
You couldn’t realistically hold the President of Europa accountable for a rogue mimic slipping into a luxury restaurant in broad daylight.
You couldn’t even pin the blame on the Mayor of Valoria or the defense wards.

In an era where high-tier Awakeners could warp physical mass and alter their mana-signatures, when a true Rogue Awakened decided to butcher a foreign prince, standard security networks were practically useless.
Menes Al-Mansur raised his right hand with his rings catching the harsh white light.

"I thank the Council for its report," Menes said, his voice dropping into a flat monotone that sounded completely hollow. "However... as I stated, this is a private family matter. A domestic concern of House Al-Mansur. It does not require an international inquest, nor does it concern the governing bodies so proceed with the docket."
He leaned back in his star-iron chair with his jaw clenched and his eyes returning to that empty dead stare.
A quiet ripple of unease passed through the surrounding rulers.
Everyone at that table was a seasoned political predator... they could see through the Pharaoh’s bravado in an instant.

If his son had been slaughtered by a common rogue, he would be screaming for Europa’s blood, demanding billions in reparations and trade concessions but to sit there, turning paler by the second, sweating through his gold-embroidered tunic while calling the brutal, desiccating slaughter of his favorite son a "family issue"?
And considering the assassin had utilized sand manipulation... the sacred hereditary mastery of Khemet’s royal line, the implications were quite chilling.
Something was rotting in the southern sands, and Menes was terrified that the World Council would smell the corpse.
The King of the World did not pursue the matter as he tilted his chin with his sapphire eyes turning cold and dismissive.
BEEP!
At the southern arc of the table, Chief Minister Rajesh Varma of the Indus Sovereignty raised his hand slightly with his serene voice breaking the tension.
"Your Majesty," Varma noted, dipping his white-bearded chin with polite poise. "The time on the grand pavilion display has reached the final increment and the staging corridor is primed."
"Thank you, Minister Varma," the King replied smoothly.
The King raised his broad right hand, the heavy star-iron signet ring glinting against the pale skin of his knuckles.
CLACK!
He tapped the ring once against the celestial marble.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A vibrant shocking eruption of deep purple mana surged from the point of contact, racing across the smooth stone surface in an intricate spiderweb network of glowing runic filaments.
The rulers around the table, including Vanderbilt and Da Silva, instinctively lifted their forearms from the stone as the table reacted.
The pristine celestial marble warped, its texture shifting from cool, polished stone into a seamless milky-white optical screen that hummed with dense magic.
SHING! SHING! SHING!
Dozens of high-definition glowing rectangular holographic displays snapped into existence, hovering four inches above the marble in front of each throne.
The public broadcast had officially begun.

The feeds displayed multiple ground-level angles of the Great Staging Pavilion and down on the polished steel staging floor, the seventy combatants chosen to represent the Nine Major Powers and the recognized independent houses were lining up in their designated team circles, their armor, robes, and armaments gleaming beneath the blinding arena lanterns as hundreds of millions of citizens across the globe watched the broadcast through screens and private terminals.

The King rested his elbow on the arm of his throne with his chin sinking into his palm and his deep blue gaze sweeping over the floating screens before drifting upward toward the elevated mezzanine box reserved for House Bloom.
His eyes locked onto the crimson-haired woman seated in the center of the box.

"Matriarch Etilga Bloom," the King spoke, his voice carrying effortlessly over the low sound of the holographic arrays. "You observe the staging floor with remarkable composure. Among the assembled scions of our global elite... who do you believe will emerge victorious from the Wastezone today?"
Etilga Bloom did not blink.
The crimson-haired matriarch sat tall in her high-backed chair, her heavy robes of layered burgundy silk cascading over the brass balustrade like flowing blood.
With a languid practiced flick of her slender wrist, she snapped open an exquisite folding fan of black lace and beaten gold, waving it with slow grace before the lower half of her face.
SNAP! SWISH!
A private holographic pane floated directly before her eyes, zooming in on the main waiting hall on the ground level.
There, standing amidst the armored ranks of the young heirs, was Seraphina Bloom.

The young woman was clad in her fitted, crimson-and-black strike cuirass, her twin curved hunting daggers sheathed horizontally across the small of her back and her ruby-red eyes burning with fierce razor-sharp focus as she completely ignored the nervous murmurs of the scions around her.
Etilga smiled behind her fan, her gaze never wavering from her daughter’s silhouette.
"My daughter, of course," Etilga replied, her voice sounding full of certainty.
Every head at the Grand Table turned to look at her.
The King’s sapphire eyes narrowed by a fraction of a millimeter.

"A bold declaration, Matriarch. Even against the warriors of Amazon, the frost-champions of the Tsardom, and the Crown Prince of the Throne himself? Pray tell... what is the foundation of your certainty?"
Etilga lowered her fan by half an inch, revealing full crimson-painted lips curled into a sharp, mocking smile.
Her ruby irises shifted away from the display, locking straight into the King’s cold blue gaze.

"It is an instinct, Your Majesty," Etilga purred softly, her tone carrying the terrifying velvety softness of a silk ribbon wrapping around a throat. "A certainty that an attentive parent feels deep within their marrow regarding the capabilities of their own flesh and blood..."
She paused, letting the silence hang over the assembly like a falling blade, before delivering the final strike.
"Not that you could ever understand such a thing."
SHK!
The King’s pupils violently contracted into microscopic pinpricks and the entire Great Assembly Chamber seemed to violently run out of air.
Julian Vanderbilt froze with his pen suspended three inches from his tablet.
Tsar Volkov stopped chewing the inside of his cheek with his massive frame locking up and even the masked Council Heads tilted their porcelain visages toward the mezzanine in stunned disbelief.
To mock the King’s parenting was an act of unfathomable madness.

Kara White had done so earlier, yes but Kara was a freak of nature, a Second Phase Gold Core who had physically pinned five hundred people to their seats with raw pressure and threatened to pull down the sky.
But Etilga Bloom?
She was merely the matriarch of a noble house... She commanded no continental legions, sat on no throne, and held no top core.
For an ordinary high-clan matriarch to strike the Supreme Monarch across the face with the exact same accusation... publicly, on a live international broadcast feed was suicidal beyond comprehension.
Across the aisle, Lohan Sterling stared at Etilga as though she had suddenly grown three heads and vomited fire onto the carpet.

His hands shook against his gold-topped cane with his mouth opening and closing like a suffocating carp, waiting for the King’s Destruction to vaporize the entire Bloom side into floating ash but the dark void-light did not pool in the King’s eyes and the Star-Iron throne did not shatter either.
Instead, after five excruciating seconds of suffocating silence, a dry chuckle rumbled from the King’s broad chest.

"I see," the King murmured, his voice dropping into a flat deadly tone that promised quiet retribution. "I certainly hope your daughter’s twin blades possess the strength to back up her mother’s tongue."
Etilga did not lower her head.
She merely snapped her fan shut with a clean clack, resting the gold filigree against the hollow of her collarbone, completely unbothered by the aura pressing against her box.
’Let him glare,’ Etilga thought, her pulse remaining completely, deliciously calm.
Her ruby eyes drifted sideways across the floating holographic panes, sliding past Seraphina’s fierce silhouette until the optical feed framed the far northern corner of the staging platform.
There, standing in an immaculate, tailored double-breasted suit of dark charcoal, was Kara White.

The one-armed woman had her right hand buried casually in her trouser pocket with her empty left sleeve pinned neatly to her ribcage, leaning against a pillar while chewing on a dried strip of spiced meat with an expression of unbothered boredom.
Beside her stood the First Princess, shifting nervously from foot to foot in her light gear.
Etilga’s ruby eyes darkened, a slow intoxicating heat flaring deep in the pit of her stomach.
She had been fascinated by the Lord of Blessed Land ever since their first live-streamed media appearance together.

Even during that chaotic public interview, Etilga had been captivated by the power of the woman’s composure, initially scheming to secure Kara through an arranged marriage alliance with Seraphina to elevate House Bloom above the Council.
’Marry her to Seraphina...?’
Etilga’s tongue slipped out between her lips, discreetly tracing the dark gloss from her upper lip behind the concealing lace of her sleeve.
’No... what a tragic waste that would be.’

The memory of Kara standing before the Throne minutes ago... she was so fearless, cruel, and utterly irreverent too, daring the King of the World to strike her down while treating the nine major powers like unranked street vendors... had shattered every polite matriarchal calculation in Etilga’s mind.

’I don’t want that creature for my daughter,’ Etilga mused, a shiver of heat rippling down her spine, making her toes curl inside her velvet slippers. ’I want to keep that magnificent, dangerous monster all for myself~’
It was a twisted scandalous thought, of course.
The woman was barely nineteen... practically the same age as her own daughter while Etilga was a reigning matriarch of high society with a reputation to protect.
’And who on this pathetic earth is going to stop me?’ Etilga sneered internally, her smile widening into something dark and insatiable. ’I am a Bloom... We take whatever we desire...’
Down in the Great Staging Pavilion, the massive overhead clock struck zero with a deep sound.
BZZZZZZZZT!
The combatants gathered across the polished steel staging floor stopped their conversations instantly.

"I thank the Council for its report," Menes said, his voice dropping into a flat monotone that sounded completely hollow.
"However... as I stated, this is a private family matter.
A domestic concern of House Al-Mansur.
It does not require an international inquest, nor does it concern the governing bodies so proceed with the docket."
He leaned back in his star-iron chair with his jaw clenched and his eyes returning to that empty dead stare.
A quiet ripple of unease passed through the surrounding rulers.
Everyone at that table was a seasoned political predator... they could see through the Pharaoh’s bravado in an instant.

If his son had been slaughtered by a common rogue, he would be screaming for Europa’s blood, demanding billions in reparations and trade concessions but to sit there, turning paler by the second, sweating through his gold-embroidered tunic while calling the brutal, desiccating slaughter of his favorite son a "family issue"?
And considering the assassin had utilized sand manipulation... the sacred hereditary mastery of Khemet’s royal line, the implications were quite chilling.
Something was rotting in the southern sands, and Menes was terrified that the World Council would smell the corpse.
The King of the World did not pursue the matter as he tilted his chin with his sapphire eyes turning cold and dismissive.
BEEP!
At the southern arc of the table, Chief Minister Rajesh Varma of the Indus Sovereignty raised his hand slightly with his serene voice breaking the tension.
"Your Majesty," Varma noted, dipping his white-bearded chin with polite poise.
"The time on the grand pavilion display has reached the final increment and the staging corridor is primed."
"Thank you, Minister Varma," the King replied smoothly.
The King raised his broad right hand, the heavy star-iron signet ring glinting against the pale skin of his knuckles.
CLACK!
He tapped the ring once against the celestial marble.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A vibrant shocking eruption of deep purple mana surged from the point of contact, racing across the smooth stone surface in an intricate spiderweb network of glowing runic filaments.
The rulers around the table, including Vanderbilt and Da Silva, instinctively lifted their forearms from the stone as the table reacted.
The pristine celestial marble warped, its texture shifting from cool, polished stone into a seamless milky-white optical screen that hummed with dense magic.
SHING!
SHING!
SHING!
Dozens of high-definition glowing rectangular holographic displays snapped into existence, hovering four inches above the marble in front of each throne.
The public broadcast had officially begun.

The feeds displayed multiple ground-level angles of the Great Staging Pavilion and down on the polished steel staging floor, the seventy combatants chosen to represent the Nine Major Powers and the recognized independent houses were lining up in their designated team circles, their armor, robes, and armaments gleaming beneath the blinding arena lanterns as hundreds of millions of citizens across the globe watched the broadcast through screens and private terminals.

The King rested his elbow on the arm of his throne with his chin sinking into his palm and his deep blue gaze sweeping over the floating screens before drifting upward toward the elevated mezzanine box reserved for House Bloom.
His eyes locked onto the crimson-haired woman seated in the center of the box.
"Matriarch Etilga Bloom," the King spoke, his voice carrying effortlessly over the low sound of the holographic arrays.
"You observe the staging floor with remarkable composure.
Among the assembled scions of our global elite... who do you believe will emerge victorious from the Wastezone today?"
Etilga Bloom did not blink.
The crimson-haired matriarch sat tall in her high-backed chair, her heavy robes of layered burgundy silk cascading over the brass balustrade like flowing blood.
With a languid practiced flick of her slender wrist, she snapped open an exquisite folding fan of black lace and beaten gold, waving it with slow grace before the lower half of her face.
SNAP!
SWISH!
A private holographic pane floated directly before her eyes, zooming in on the main waiting hall on the ground level.
There, standing amidst the armored ranks of the young heirs, was Seraphina Bloom.

The young woman was clad in her fitted, crimson-and-black strike cuirass, her twin curved hunting daggers sheathed horizontally across the small of her back and her ruby-red eyes burning with fierce razor-sharp focus as she completely ignored the nervous murmurs of the scions around her.
Etilga smiled behind her fan, her gaze never wavering from her daughter’s silhouette.
"My daughter, of course," Etilga replied, her voice sounding full of certainty.
Every head at the Grand Table turned to look at her.
The King’s sapphire eyes narrowed by a fraction of a millimeter.
"A bold declaration, Matriarch.
Even against the warriors of Amazon, the frost-champions of the Tsardom, and the Crown Prince of the Throne himself?
Pray tell... what is the foundation of your certainty?"
Etilga lowered her fan by half an inch, revealing full crimson-painted lips curled into a sharp, mocking smile.
Her ruby irises shifted away from the display, locking straight into the King’s cold blue gaze.
"It is an instinct, Your Majesty," Etilga purred softly, her tone carrying the terrifying velvety softness of a silk ribbon wrapping around a throat.
"A certainty that an attentive parent feels deep within their marrow regarding the capabilities of their own flesh and blood..."
She paused, letting the silence hang over the assembly like a falling blade, before delivering the final strike.
"Not that you could ever understand such a thing."
SHK!
The King’s pupils violently contracted into microscopic pinpricks and the entire Great Assembly Chamber seemed to violently run out of air.
Julian Vanderbilt froze with his pen suspended three inches from his tablet.
Tsar Volkov stopped chewing the inside of his cheek with his massive frame locking up and even the masked Council Heads tilted their porcelain visages toward the mezzanine in stunned disbelief.
To mock the King’s parenting was an act of unfathomable madness.

Kara White had done so earlier, yes but Kara was a freak of nature, a Second Phase Gold Core who had physically pinned five hundred people to their seats with raw pressure and threatened to pull down the sky.
But Etilga Bloom?
She was merely the matriarch of a noble house...
She commanded no continental legions, sat on no throne, and held no top core.
For an ordinary high-clan matriarch to strike the Supreme Monarch across the face with the exact same accusation... publicly, on a live international broadcast feed was suicidal beyond comprehension.
Across the aisle, Lohan Sterling stared at Etilga as though she had suddenly grown three heads and vomited fire onto the carpet.

His hands shook against his gold-topped cane with his mouth opening and closing like a suffocating carp, waiting for the King’s Destruction to vaporize the entire Bloom side into floating ash but the dark void-light did not pool in the King’s eyes and the Star-Iron throne did not shatter either.
Instead, after five excruciating seconds of suffocating silence, a dry chuckle rumbled from the King’s broad chest.
"I see," the King murmured, his voice dropping into a flat deadly tone that promised quiet retribution.
"I certainly hope your daughter’s twin blades possess the strength to back up her mother’s tongue."
Etilga did not lower her head.
She merely snapped her fan shut with a clean clack, resting the gold filigree against the hollow of her collarbone, completely unbothered by the aura pressing against her box.
’Let him glare,’ Etilga thought, her pulse remaining completely, deliciously calm.
Her ruby eyes drifted sideways across the floating holographic panes, sliding past Seraphina’s fierce silhouette until the optical feed framed the far northern corner of the staging platform.
There, standing in an immaculate, tailored double-breasted suit of dark charcoal, was Kara White.

The one-armed woman had her right hand buried casually in her trouser pocket with her empty left sleeve pinned neatly to her ribcage, leaning against a pillar while chewing on a dried strip of spiced meat with an expression of unbothered boredom.
Beside her stood the First Princess, shifting nervously from foot to foot in her light gear.
Etilga’s ruby eyes darkened, a slow intoxicating heat flaring deep in the pit of her stomach.
She had been fascinated by the Lord of Blessed Land ever since their first live-streamed media appearance together.

Even during that chaotic public interview, Etilga had been captivated by the power of the woman’s composure, initially scheming to secure Kara through an arranged marriage alliance with Seraphina to elevate House Bloom above the Council.
’Marry her to Seraphina...?’
Etilga’s tongue slipped out between her lips, discreetly tracing the dark gloss from her upper lip behind the concealing lace of her sleeve.
’No... what a tragic waste that would be.’

The memory of Kara standing before the Throne minutes ago... she was so fearless, cruel, and utterly irreverent too, daring the King of the World to strike her down while treating the nine major powers like unranked street vendors... had shattered every polite matriarchal calculation in Etilga’s mind.

’I don’t want that creature for my daughter,’ Etilga mused, a shiver of heat rippling down her spine, making her toes curl inside her velvet slippers. ’I want to keep that magnificent, dangerous monster all for myself~’
It was a twisted scandalous thought, of course.
The woman was barely nineteen... practically the same age as her own daughter while Etilga was a reigning matriarch of high society with a reputation to protect.
’And who on this pathetic earth is going to stop me?’ Etilga sneered internally, her smile widening into something dark and insatiable. ’I am a Bloom...
We take whatever we desire...’
Down in the Great Staging Pavilion, the massive overhead clock struck zero with a deep sound.
BZZZZZZZZT!
The combatants gathered across the polished steel staging floor stopped their conversations instantly.
