paragraphs: At the center of the platform, standing before the colossal circular archway of the primary transit gate, a scarred Warden of the World Council stepped forward.
He was clad from neck to heel in heavy rune-inscribed mythril plate, holding a massive star-iron lantern that burned with a cold pale-white spiritual fire.
"Silence for the edict of deployment!" the Warden’s voice boomed, amplified by runes embedded in the steel deck.
The heirs and retainers snapped into rigid formation.
Crown Prince Alexander stood at a hidden side of the circle with his posture stiff and his jaw locked in fury.
His arms were encased from wrist to bicep in the heavy glowing Star-Iron Suppression Rings he had demanded from his father.

The runic metal was pulsing with an aggressive hum, actively constricting two-thirds of his internal mana pathways, artificially bottlenecking his Fourth Stage advancement down to the Second Stage to ensure parity with the competition.
His bloodshot eyes were fixed with murderous hatred upon the back of Kara White’s head and his fists trembling against his thighs.
The Warden raised his gauntleted left hand, pointing toward the swirling translucent vortex of the transit gate behind him.

"You are deploying to Sector Forty-Four of the Sovereign Realm," the Warden announced with his voice lacking any sort of emotion. "Under the statutes of the Exhibition of Succession, the barrier strictly prevents all external summoning... You cannot call forth Heroes, Troops, or legions from your home territories. You cross the threshold with only your designated two-person squad, your immediate personal armaments, and your native core."
A low rustle of leather, silk, and scabbards ran through the ranks.

"The deployment zone is vast," the Warden continued. "The transit array will scatter each team to random isolated coordinates across the sector... The sector is an uncolonized wilderness, populated by indigenous Tier-1 and Tier-2 monsters with stronger ones happening sometimes. The Exhibition operates under an absolute Two-Hour Time Limit."
He held up two fingers with his scarred face turning grim.

"The victory conditions are absolute... If a faction successfully eliminates all rival squads before the two-hour mark expires, that faction is declared the immediate undisputed victor. If multiple factions remain standing when the timer concludes, the surviving teams will be forcibly compressed into the central caldera for a sudden-death convergence until only one standard remains standing."
From the Khemet team circle, Lady Safira stepped forward with her voice cutting through the silence.
"Warden! What is the topographical profile of Sector Forty-Four?"
The Warden glanced toward her with his eyes looking impassive.
"The sector is predominantly an arid Wastezone of shifting sand dunes, broken by central greenlands anchored to river aquifers, surrounded by jagged granite mountain ridges."
’A sand wastezone...?’
A wave of sharp irritated glances swept across the floor toward the Khemet representatives.
The people from Borealis and Columbia gripped their weapons with tight bitter scowls.
Khemet was the cradle of sand-affinity casting.
To drop all the combatants into a silica-dense basin was practically handing the desert nation an overwhelming home-field advantage on a silver platter.
It looked blatantly rigged.
Safira and Tariq, however, did not smile. The phantom memory of the black sand dissolving in their private quarters was still burning in their minds, keeping their blood cold as ice.
The Warden raised the star-iron lantern high above his head.
"Are there any final inquiries?"
Dead silence answered him.
"Then let the Succession be settled in blood," the Warden declared.
CLACK!
He released the mechanical safety latch on the lantern.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!

The pale-white spiritual fire inside the housing erupted into an all-consuming, blinding wave of luminescence as the spatial fabric around the pavilion groaned under terrifying gravitational tension, warping and folding inward in a massive swirling vortex that swallowed all combatants whole, ripping their physical vessels out of the mortal plane in the span of a single heartbeat.
Aki blinked.
"Gah–!"
Her chest hitched violently as cold thin air rushed back into her lungs, burning her windpipe like crushed glass.
The gut-wrenching sensation of freefalling through a lightless gravity-free void snapped shut with concussive finality, replaced by the hard bite of jagged granite beneath the soles of her boots.
She stumbled forward, her small hands scraping against the rough face of a lichen-covered boulder to keep her balance.
Her vision swam with dancing white spots and her stomach violently churning with the spatial sickness that plagued unawakened mortals during long-range teleportation.

She swallowed hard, blinking rapidly, trying to force her equilibrium to settle as the howling roar of transitional void-wind gave way to the desolate whistle of high-altitude gales whipping through narrow mountain gorges.
Aki straightened her back with her heart hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird, and looked around.
She was standing on a wide elevated rocky plateau high along the jagged spine of a massive granite mountain range.
Below her, stretching out for tens of leagues beneath a bruised twilight-purple sky, the Wastezone was an intimidating sprawling expanse.

To the far east lay an ocean of rolling, yellow-sand dunes that churned and shifted in the wind like an inland sea... directly below the sheer mountain cliffs, a narrow belt of emerald-green jungle clung to a winding pale-blue river and beyond the jungle, rising like an ancient blackened crown in the center of the horizon, was the dark rim of a massive volcanic caldera.
"You awake now...?"
The smooth relaxed voice came from the edge of the precipice and Aki turned her head with her breath hitching.
Kara was sitting casually on the very lip of the thousand-foot drop, her legs dangling out over the empty abyss.

She was leaning forward, resting her chin on her single right palm with her wire-rimmed glasses pushed neatly up the bridge of her nose, looking down at the vast expanse of the Wastezone with the bored unimpressed posture of someone waiting for a delayed bus.
Aki blinked, rushing forward two steps before catching herself.
"Sil—I mean, Kara! How long have we been here?!"

"About four minutes," Kara answered without looking back, casually flicking a small pebble off the cliff edge with her thumb. "You were completely out cold, Princess... The spatial pressure hit your nervous system pretty hard, it seems unawakened biological channels don’t process dimensional folding well so you looked like a stunned deer for a second there."
She tilted her head slightly toward the narrow goat path winding up the rocky ridge behind them.
"Gave these two enough time to track our transponder beacon, at least."
CLACK! CLACK!
The sound of armored boots striking stone echoed from the lower rocks.
Emerging onto the plateau, their breathing heavy but controlled, were Lieutenant Maya Da Silva and Captain Leona.
Both Amazonian officers were fully clad in the pristine void-ivory strike armor Kara had provided.
The pearl-white plates were unmarked, the gold stabilization runes humming with a soft pale-green luminescence as the wind-acceleration runes actively regulated their momentum.
Maya immediately snapped a clenched fist over her breastplate, dipping her chin.

"Lord Vespera! We locked onto your personal transponder the instant our squad materialized in the lower ravine! The immediate perimeter is clear, but we registered three separate kinetic mana flares five kilometers south... Columbia and Shogya have already initiated contact in the lower basin!"
Kara let out a soft amused hum through her nose, still staring out over the vast plains below.
Over the past four minutes, while Aki had been unconscious on the rocks, Silas had been sitting quietly on that ledge, conducting a thorough internal diagnostic of his spiritual pathways.
’They gave me full reins...?’ Kara thought, her brow furrowing slightly behind her clear lenses.
It made no sense.

Silas had fully expected the World Council’s arbiters to slap an array of high-grade suppression cuffs on his soul pathways before shoving him through the transit gate... something to artificially bottleneck his Gold Core down to match the rest of the children, just as Alexander had done to himself.
Yet... nothing.
His soul pathways were wide open.
The Second Phase Gold Core was spinning smoothly in the center of his chest, radiating that dense liquid-gold authority without a single dampening ward or restriction placed upon his vessel.

’Do these idiots actually believe I’m going to hold back out of the goodness of my heart just to make the broadcast look entertaining?’ Kara wondered, a dark dangerous smirk curling the corner of her lips. ’Or does the King have some hidden contingency waiting for me in the caldera...?’
Silas wanted to find out.
He wanted to see what happened when the high court realized they had locked all of their prized noble heirs in an arena with an unchained apex predator.
Kara pushed herself off the ledge, standing upright on the absolute edge of the drop.
She turned around to face the three women with her double-breasted jacket flapping gently in the mountain gale.
"Alright," Kara said casually, raising her single right hand in a lazy wave. "Take care of each other, ladies. I’m going to go enjoy this whole thing."
Maya and Leona blinked in unison, their jaws dropping in utter disbelief.
"Wait—what?!"
Aki’s eyes widened in mounting panic. "Kara! What do you mean you’re going to enjoy it?! Where are you going?!"
Kara gave a slow deliberate wink behind her wire-rimmed glasses.
She leaned backward... stepping clean off the edge of the thousand-foot cliff.
"KARA!" Aki screamed, her boots scraping violently against the granite as she sprinted toward the ledge with her hands reaching out into empty air.
Kara was falling.
The mountain wind howled in her ears, tearing at her tailored charcoal suit, her dark hair whipping wildly around her face as the rocky abyss rushed up to meet her at terminal velocity.
Yet she looked up at the receding ledge, raising her single right hand to offer Aki a cheerful parting wave.
"Take care of yourself, Aki!" Kara’s voice boomed up. "Fight like your life is on the line, because it is! But if you really, really need help... if you’re truly about to break..."
Kara’s violet eyes flared with the usual warmth.
"Call my name and I’ll show up."
She twisted her body in mid-air.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A concentrated vortex of pale-green wind-mana detonated beneath her dress shoes and the gale did not only break her descent but it propelled her forward like a fired cruise missile.

Kara flattened her silhouette, cutting horizontally through the mountain gorges, soaring across the vast expanse of the Wastezone with terrifying speed, leaving behind a thunderous boom that echoed off the granite peaks.
BOOOOOOOOM!
Up on the precipice, Aki stood with her fingers gripping the cold edge of the stone with the howling mountain wind whipping her navy skirts and tossing her loose dark hair across her face.
She watched the tiny charcoal-suited figure streak across the sky toward the distant battlefields and her chest heaving with rapid shallow breaths.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
Her small hand rose, her gloved fingers curling tightly around the cold Star-Iron pendant resting against her collarbone.
’Silas...’ Aki thought, her vision blurring with fierce burning resolve as she turned back to face the Amazonian soldiers.
’I won’t let you down.’

The thunderous concussive boom of Kara’s departure was still rolling through the granite crevices of the mountain ridge, sending cascades of loose slate and powdered quartz tumbling thousands of feet into the valley below.
On the narrow wind-battered precipice, the air smelled sharply of ozone.
’I’m beginning to hate this smell...’
Aki slowly pulled her boots back from the crumbling edge of the cliff.

The howling updraft tore at her blue hair, whipping it across her face, but she didn’t blink as she took three deep, measured breaths through her nose, feeling the cold air bite all the way down into her lungs.
The intoxicating rush of adrenaline was still singing through her veins, but beneath it, the cold reality of their situation clamped shut like an iron jaw.
Kara was gone.
She had plunged into the lower atmosphere like an artillery shell, cutting a straight line across the bruised purple sky toward the central caldera.
Aki turned her back to the precipice and faced the two Amazonian warriors standing ten paces away.
"What do we do now?" Aki asked.
Her voice was surprisingly steady, lacking the fragile trembling hesitation that had defined her in the corridors of the Citadel.
She reached down, adjusting the strap of the lightweight harness cinched tightly over her dark training clothes. "Can either of you sense anyone else nearby? Anyone tracking our beacon?"
Lieutenant Maya Da Silva stood with her heavy combat boots planted wide on the granite shelf.

She closed her eyes for three seconds, her breathing slowing to a deep cadence as her Second Stage Purple Core pulsed within her chest, sending an invisible concentric ripple of earth-mana vibrating down through the bedrock.
Beside her, Captain Leona stood in a half-crouch, her fingers resting lightly against the twin hunting daggers strapped to her hips.
Her cornrows were pulled back tight against her scalp with her sharp hazel eyes scanning the crags above them.

"Nothing close," Maya said, opening her eyes. "About four miles south, down in the salt flats, two factions are throwing high-tier elemental strikes like drunken sailors... One’s Columbia since I know the crack of their shock-cannons anywhere. The other feels like Shogya’s wind arts as they spiked their mana signatures within ninety seconds of landfall."

What do you mean you’re going to enjoy it?!
Where are you going?!"
Kara gave a slow deliberate wink behind her wire-rimmed glasses.
She leaned backward... stepping clean off the edge of the thousand-foot cliff.
"KARA!" Aki screamed, her boots scraping violently against the granite as she sprinted toward the ledge with her hands reaching out into empty air.
Kara was falling.
The mountain wind howled in her ears, tearing at her tailored charcoal suit, her dark hair whipping wildly around her face as the rocky abyss rushed up to meet her at terminal velocity.
Yet she looked up at the receding ledge, raising her single right hand to offer Aki a cheerful parting wave.
"Take care of yourself, Aki!" Kara’s voice boomed up.
"Fight like your life is on the line, because it is!
But if you really, really need help... if you’re truly about to break..."
Kara’s violet eyes flared with the usual warmth.
"Call my name and I’ll show up."
She twisted her body in mid-air.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A concentrated vortex of pale-green wind-mana detonated beneath her dress shoes and the gale did not only break her descent but it propelled her forward like a fired cruise missile.

Kara flattened her silhouette, cutting horizontally through the mountain gorges, soaring across the vast expanse of the Wastezone with terrifying speed, leaving behind a thunderous boom that echoed off the granite peaks.
BOOOOOOOOM!
Up on the precipice, Aki stood with her fingers gripping the cold edge of the stone with the howling mountain wind whipping her navy skirts and tossing her loose dark hair across her face.
She watched the tiny charcoal-suited figure streak across the sky toward the distant battlefields and her chest heaving with rapid shallow breaths.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
Her small hand rose, her gloved fingers curling tightly around the cold Star-Iron pendant resting against her collarbone.
’Silas...’ Aki thought, her vision blurring with fierce burning resolve as she turned back to face the Amazonian soldiers.
’I won’t let you down.’

The thunderous concussive boom of Kara’s departure was still rolling through the granite crevices of the mountain ridge, sending cascades of loose slate and powdered quartz tumbling thousands of feet into the valley below.
On the narrow wind-battered precipice, the air smelled sharply of ozone.
’I’m beginning to hate this smell...’
Aki slowly pulled her boots back from the crumbling edge of the cliff.

The howling updraft tore at her blue hair, whipping it across her face, but she didn’t blink as she took three deep, measured breaths through her nose, feeling the cold air bite all the way down into her lungs.
The intoxicating rush of adrenaline was still singing through her veins, but beneath it, the cold reality of their situation clamped shut like an iron jaw.
Kara was gone.
She had plunged into the lower atmosphere like an artillery shell, cutting a straight line across the bruised purple sky toward the central caldera.
Aki turned her back to the precipice and faced the two Amazonian warriors standing ten paces away.
"What do we do now?" Aki asked.
Her voice was surprisingly steady, lacking the fragile trembling hesitation that had defined her in the corridors of the Citadel.
She reached down, adjusting the strap of the lightweight harness cinched tightly over her dark training clothes.
"Can either of you sense anyone else nearby?
Anyone tracking our beacon?"
Lieutenant Maya Da Silva stood with her heavy combat boots planted wide on the granite shelf.

She closed her eyes for three seconds, her breathing slowing to a deep cadence as her Second Stage Purple Core pulsed within her chest, sending an invisible concentric ripple of earth-mana vibrating down through the bedrock.
Beside her, Captain Leona stood in a half-crouch, her fingers resting lightly against the twin hunting daggers strapped to her hips.
Her cornrows were pulled back tight against her scalp with her sharp hazel eyes scanning the crags above them.
"Nothing close," Maya said, opening her eyes.
"About four miles south, down in the salt flats, two factions are throwing high-tier elemental strikes like drunken sailors...
One’s Columbia since I know the crack of their shock-cannons anywhere.
The other feels like Shogya’s wind arts as they spiked their mana signatures within ninety seconds of landfall."

chapters.title: Chapter 556: The Tournament Of Succession [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Fools," Leona scoffed softly, sniffing at the thin air.
She reached up with a gloved thumb, wiping a bead of clear moisture from the tip of her nose with a faint snort.

"Spiking that much heat on deployment is an open invitation for every scavenger within ten leagues but the others? Silence. The Tsardom, Indus, House Bloom... they aren’t making amateur mistakes. They’re running silent, masking their heat signatures, and letting the loud idiots butcher each other first."

"Which means we can’t stay here," Maya said, stepping toward the narrow descent trail that snaked along the mountain’s spine. "Sitting on an elevated ridge makes us silhouette targets against the sky. Being sitting ducks up here is asking for an orbital bombardment or a long-range mana lance."
Aki swallowed hard with her fingers tightening around the straps of her harness.
"Especially since Alexander is down there," Aki said quietly and the name hung in the cold mountain air like a blade of ice.
Maya’s jaw tightened as Leona’s hazel eyes darkened with cold professional caution.
...Crown Prince Alexander.

Even with the heavy Star-Iron Suppression Rings clamped around his forearms, artificially strangling two-thirds of his internal mana channels to force his Fourth Stage power down to the Second Stage, the man was still a prodigy of House Castellian.

If Alexander caught wind of Aki’s coordinates... if he realized that his unawakened, discarded sister was traversing the Wastezone without the Gold Core standing directly in front of her, he wouldn’t hesitate for a single second.
He would descend upon them with the full fury of an insecure prince desperate to wash out his public humiliation in blood.
Aki looked over her shoulder, out across the vast expanse of the Wastezone toward the volcanic caldera looming on the horizon.

’Is that where Silas went...?’she wondered with her heart clenching slightly.’He left us behind because he knew his presence would draw the heaviest fire... If Alexander or the high scions sense a Gold Core moving, they’ll converge on him like wolves so he’s buying us room to breathe.’
She turned back to the Amazonians, her jaw setting with hard resolve.
"Let’s move," Aki commanded. "We need to get off this peak."
Before Maya could take the lead down the rocks, a strange hollow sound reverberated across the entirety of Sector Forty-Four.𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
VUUUUUUUM!
It wasn’t an explosion but an atmospheric broadcast array, woven through the ceiling of the realm.
A smooth synthetic voice echoed from the purple clouds above, vibrating in their teeth.

"Attention all combatants of the Exhibition... The Time limit remains set at one hundred and fourteen minutes and for the duration of the trial, defensive structures designated as Safe Zones will periodically manifest across the grid."
Aki, Maya, and Leona froze, listening intently.

"A Safe Zone is identified by an active cylindrical cerulean barrier. Upon crossing the threshold, a squad will be granted a ten-minute non-combat respite, during which external mana signatures are suppressed and restoration is accelerated. After ten minutes, the zone will collapse permanently. Be advised, competitors... the sands of the Wastezone are old and the sands do not always tell the truth."
PING!
The announcement cut off with a flat, sharp tone.
Almost simultaneously, five miles away in the lower valley... nestled right at the border where the rocky foothills bled into the endless sea of golden dunes...
A towering pale-blue pillar of light shot into the sky as a massive translucent dome of sapphire energy expanded over a ruined sandstone amphitheater, humming with visible calming mana.
Maya and Leona glanced at the blue pillar, their expressions looking unimpressed.
Without a word, both soldiers tore their gazes away from the safe zone, turning their backs on it as if it didn’t exist.

"Nobody’s using that," Leona muttered, rolling her shoulders within the void-ivory cuirass. "Only a squad that took catastrophic damage would willingly trap themselves inside a glowing blue beacon in the middle of an open desert. It’s a neon sign telling every sniper on the rim...Free kills in ten minutes."
Aki stood quietly, her blue eyes narrowing as she studied the glowing blue dome in the distance.
Her mind was already breaking down the mechanics of the game.
"Wait," Aki spoke up, stepping between the two soldiers. "Think about it from another angle."
Maya turned, her brow furrowing slightly. "What do you mean, Princess?"

"Leona is right... smart squads won’t enter it unless they’re desperate," Aki explained, her voice gaining momentum. "Which means squads that have already taken heavy wounds from the initial clashes like the ones who ran into Columbia’s shock-corps or took shrapnel from Shogya’s wind blades will have no choice. They’ll be forced to crawl into that barrier to keep their channels from burning out."
Aki pointed a gloved finger down toward the rocky ridges flanking the blue dome.

"And the ruthless squads? The ones hunting for easy eliminations? They won’t ignore the Safe Zone either. They’ll do exactly what Leona just described... they’ll set up camp in the crags outside the perimeter, zero their sights on the threshold, and wait for the ten-minute timer to expire so they can slaughter the wounded as they step out."
Maya blinked as a slow savage grin began to split her broad face.
"Ambush the ambushers," Maya said, her knuckles cracking against her palm with a sharppop.

"Exactly," Aki nodded. "Why waste energy combing thousands of square miles of dunes trying to hunt scattered signatures...? We go down the mountain, we identify the high ground overlooking the Safe Zone, and we camp the people who are camping the dome."
Leona let out a low whistle looking at the First Princess with genuine newfound respect. "Cold-blooded. For a girl who grew up reading poetry, you think like a trench scout."
"When you spend your entire life being the target," Aki said, her voice dropping into a quiet whisper, "you learn how predators set their traps... It’s really nothing."
"Alright," Maya decided, gesturing down the trail. "That’s the play. But we need to move fast. Leona, how’s the air?"
Leona took another deep sniff of the mountain draft, her nose twitching.
She reached up, wiping her upper lip once more as her hazel eyes darted toward the jagged rock formations rising fifty yards above them on the upper ridge.
"It smells wrong," Leona said, her tone suddenly dropping into an urgent whisper. "There’s a musky heat on the wind so somebody’s up there or down, I don’t know."
Aki blinked, looking at the Amazonian captain in confusion. "How does that work? You can smell mana?"
Maya stepped closer, lowering her voice.

"Leona’s native mutation is mostly for her senses... Her dual affinity for Wind and Water lets her read microscopic shifts in atmospheric moisture and air density. She can’t pinpoint their exact core stage or read their specific mana, but she knows when living mass enters her immediate airspace. If she says there are bodies above or below us, there are bodies above or below us."
A cold prickle of dread ran down Aki’s spine.

She glanced up at the towering shadow-draped crags of the peak. A squad could be perched fifty feet directly overhead, masked by anti-detection cloaks, aiming high-caliber rifles down at their skulls at this very moment.
VUUUUUM!
The atmospheric broadcast flared one final time.
"Notice... Indigenous Tier-1 and Tier-2 fauna have completed their territorial cycles and competitors are advised to maintain constant armament readiness. Killing of monsters is fully authorized."
Aki didn’t wait.
She reached down to her thighs, checking the three balanced throwing daggers sheathed in low-friction leather along each leg.
Her hand moved to the heavy mechanism mounted along the outer edge of her right forearm... a fully retractable spring-loaded composite recurve bow designed by Blessed Land’s artisans or rather Thora.

With a subtle flick of her wrist, the star-iron limbs snapped forward with a cleanshlick, locking into firing position, while a low-draw quiver of carbon-tipped arrows rested flat against the small of her back.
She was fully armed on the mundane front.
And more importantly...
"Haah..."
She kept her hands relaxed, letting the pitch-black beast-leather gloves blend seamlessly into the dark sleeves of her gear.
The World Council’s broadcast drones hovering in the clouds saw only an unawakened princess carrying mechanical weapons.
They had no idea that beneath the leather of those gloves lay the artificial mana pathways forged by Silas... a hidden spark of elemental magic waiting to detonate.
"Move out," Maya barked.
The three women sprinted down the narrow mountain trail.

The path was treacherous, especially since it was a steep jagged ledge barely two feet wide, bordered on the left by the granite wall of the mountain and on the right by a staggering two-thousand-foot vertical drop into the mist-choked ravines below.
Maya led the vanguard as her boots hit the rock with heavy thuds.

Despite the fifty-pound void-ivory cuirass she wore, the passive wind runes etched into the knee joints flared with green light, absorbing the downward shock and propelling her forward with supernatural grace.
Leona brought up the rear, her daggers drawn, sweeping their flanks.
Aki ran between them.
Without native mana to reinforce her ligaments, every step required razor-sharp focus.
Her lungs burned as the thin air scraped her throat, but the grueling physical conditioning Silas and the other girls had subjected her to in Blessed Land paid off.
’Well including the ones I subjected myself in... A little bit of credit goes to me after all.’
Her balance was centered, her core tight and her canvas combat boots gripping the loose gravel without slipping.
"GRAAAHHHH!"
The sound was not human.

It was a guttural wet vibration that came from the shadows of a wide fissure split into the granite wall thirty paces ahead and Maya skidded to a halt, her boots digging into the slate with a harshsound.
SKRRRR!
"Contact!" Maya hissed.
From the dark cavernous crack, three massive shapes detached from the stone.
They wereCrag Stalkers... indigenous Tier-2 predators that inhabited the high mountain rims of the Sovereign Realm.

Standing four feet tall at the shoulder, they resembled hairless four-eyed mountain panthers with hideously elongated forelimbs, their skin a mottled jagged gray that matched the rough granite perfectly and their jaws split open horizontally, revealing rows of black needle-sharp teeth dripping with viscous acidic saliva that hissed as it struck the stone.
HSSSSSSSS!
The lead Stalker lunged instantly as it crossed twenty feet in seconds, its massive forepaws tipped with curved three-inch obsidian talons aiming straight for Maya’s throat.
SWISH... SLAM!
Maya didn’t even draw a blade.
Her Purple Core flared violently behind her sternum as a dense, dark-violet aura erupted along her right arm, coating her skin in a thick vibrating mantle of crystallized earth-mana.
She stepped forward into the beast’s reach, dipping her left shoulder beneath the slashing claws, and drove her right fist upward in a vicious short-range uppercut.
BOOOOOOM!
The concussive shockwave sounded like a sledgehammer hitting a concrete slab.
The reinforced impact blew straight through the beast’s lower jaw, shattering the bone into a dozen jagged fragments and caving in its skull.
The four-eyed predator was launched five feet into the air, completely lifeless before its carcass crashed over the cliff edge and tumbled into the abyss.
"Flank!" Maya roared, already pivoting on her heel.
The second Stalker had bypassed Maya, using the granite wall to wall-kick horizontally through the air with its jaws wide open, diving directly at Aki’s exposed chest.
Time seemed to slow for the First Princess.
A long time ago, Aki would have frozen but not today.
’I can handle it...’
Her left foot slid back six inches, locking her balance into the slate.

With terrifying fluidity, her right hand swept to the small of her back, plucking a carbon-tipped arrow from the quiver, seating the nock into the star-iron string of her forearm bow, and drawing the cable back to her cheek in a single unbroken arc.
THWIP!
She released and while the arrow didn’t have mana behind it, the mechanical spring-tension of the dwarven mechanism was immense.
SPLAT!
The carbon-tipped point drove cleanly through the beast’s upper-left eye socket, punching through the optic nerve and burying six inches of steel into its frontal lobe.
"SKREEEEEE!"

The Stalker shrieked, its momentum dying in mid-air as its body convulsed, crashing heavily onto the path three feet from Aki’s boots and it kicked twice in the gravel with its black blood pooling on the stone, before lying completely still.
Aki didn’t even pause to breathe.

She dropped the bow mechanism, reached down with her left hand, drew a six-inch hunting dagger from her thigh, and drove the steel blade straight down into the creature’s spinal joint with a sharpcrack, severing the neural cord to ensure it was dead.
She looked up, wiping a stray drop of black bile from her cheek.
Behind her, Leona had already concluded her business with the third beast.
The Amazonian captain stood over a headless Stalker carcass with her twin daggers glowing with pale-blue water-mana as she smoothly sliced the fluid off her steel with a clean flick.
Leona looked at Aki, then looked at the dead beast at the princess’s feet.
"Clean shot," Leona muttered, an appreciative grin tugging at her mouth. "Direct through the orbital cavity... You do have a lot of experience in killing monsters, who taught you?"
"I was taught by a person who don’t tolerate missed shots," Aki said, stepping over the carcass, her breath coming in quick shallow puffs. "It’s not the best feeling in the world..."
Maya surveyed the narrow canyon ahead with her scowl deepening.

"I was taught by a person who don’t tolerate missed shots," Aki said, stepping over the carcass, her breath coming in quick shallow puffs.
"It’s not the best feeling in the world..."
Maya surveyed the narrow canyon ahead with her scowl deepening.

paragraphs: "We’re moving too slow," Maya complained, kicking a piece of loose shale off the path. "Leona’s readings seem to be getting heavier... There’s something lingering on the wind above us, and walking down this mountain on foot is going to take forty-five minutes. By the time we reach the foothills, the first squads will already have butchered each other and scattered."
Leona glanced back at Aki, assessing her smaller unarmored frame.
"I could carry you on my back, Princess. With my wind reinforcement, I can leap down the rock faces three times faster."
Aki shook her head immediately.

"No," Aki said firmly, patting the lightweight harness strapped across her torso and more on the inside. "These armaments are designed to absorb environmental mana-shear and keep my organs from liquefying under high-altitude pressure and the pressure of the Sovereign Realm too. If you carry me while cycling your Second Stage core, the passive mana-friction bleeding off your skin will clash with the runes on my harness. It could rupture the stabilization and knock me unconscious so I need to move on my own."
Maya groaned, rubbing the back of her neck. "Then we need transport. Walking is out of the question."
As if answering her complaint, a low rumbling chorus of snarls vibrated from the rocky terrace thirty yards below them.
The three women crept to the edge of the shelf, peering over the rock face.
Gathered in a wide, sandy hollow carved into the mountain flank was a pack of five Dune Wolves... a mutated desert variation of the Dire Wolves found everywhere in the Sovereign Realm.
...Well almost everywhere.
These beasts were massive, standing five feet tall, their bodies covered in thick bristling coats of sandy-gold fur that naturally deflected friction.
Their tails were segmented and heavy like scorpions with their yellow eyes glowing and full of intelligence as they gnawed on the bones of an indigenous mountain ram.
"Well," Leona whispered, a sharp smirk spreading across her lips. "Look what the gods dropped in our path."
"Don’t kill them," Aki whispered urgently, grabbing Maya’s armored forearm. "We need them alive..."
Maya turned, raising an eyebrow. "You want to ride desert predators? They’ll rip your legs off before you place saddles, Princess."
"Just beat them into submission..." Aki insisted. "Break their stance! Don’t puncture their lungs or sever their leg tendons! I can handle the rest..."
Maya and Leona exchanged a swift glance... Frontline soldiers didn’t argue when an objective was clear.
"On my mark," Maya hissed.
Her Purple Core roared.
BOOM!

Maya launched herself off the ten-foot ledge, descending upon the pack like a falling meteor as she struck the center of the hollow with both boots, channeling her earth-mana straight into the bedrock.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
The stone floor ruptured as massive blunt pillars of jagged granite shot upward from the sand, striking two of the Dune Wolves squarely in their ribs.
WHAM! WHAM!
The beasts yelped in shock, their breath exploding from their lungs as they were launched into the rock walls, stunned and gasping for air.
The remaining three wolves whipped around, their hackles rising, their jaws snapping with concussive force as they lunged at Maya from three angles.
SWOOSH!
Leona was already there.
The Amazonian captain dropped from above with her twin daggers spinning in reverse grips.
She didn’t use the blades to cut though as she wrapped her forearms in dense pressurized coils of swirling water-mana.
SMACK! CRACK!

She delivered two lightning-fast palm strikes to the muzzles of the attacking wolves with the hydraulic pressure concussing their sensory organs, sending them crashing into the sand, whimpering and clawing at their bleeding noses.
The alpha wolf... a scarred massive brute with one blind eye roared, coiling its muscular hind legs to leap at Leona’s exposed flank—
THUMP!
Aki landed from the ledge, dropping into a low controlled roll and in her hands, she held fifty feet of heavy, braided star-iron rope that Maya had carried in her rucksack.
Before the alpha wolf could complete its lunge, Aki moved and she didn’t hesitate either.
’I need to do this at the very least...’

She stepped straight into the beast’s blind spot, whipped the star-iron rope around its thick muscular neck in a wide, running loop, slid beneath its belly, and yanked the line tight with all her body weight.
SKRRRRRR!
The wolf’s momentum slammed its chin into the dirt but Aki didn’t let go.
She twisted the rope around its long, pointed muzzle, locking the jaw shut, and tied a complex multi-layered friction knot behind its ears with blinding four-second speed.
’Heh, I knew all of that knotting would come in handy one day.’
She pulled the remaining lengths of cord back over its broad shoulders, creating two perfectly balanced makeshift reins.
"GRR!"
The alpha wolf thrashed violently, its claws tearing up the sand as it was trying to shake the small human off its back.
Aki didn’t flinch.
She grabbed the beast by its heavy sandy ears, leaned down until her face was inches from its glowing yellow eye, and spoke with a coldness that didn’t match her face.
"Down," Aki commanded. "Or I let the woman behind me turn your skull into gravel."
The wolf froze.

It felt the bite of the star-iron cord around its jaw but it also smelled the fresh blood of the Crag Stalker still clinging to her boots and most importantly, it saw Maya Da Silva standing five feet away, her fist glowing with enough dark-purple mana to level a hill.
The alpha’s ears pinned back against its skull.
It slowly lowered its massive belly into the sand, letting out a submissive rumbling whine.
Within three minutes, Maya and Leona had bound the muzzles of two other wolves with identical harnesses.
Maya stood back, crossing her arms over her void-ivory breastplate, staring at the First Princess in wide-eyed astonishment.
"Where in the hell did you learn to rig beast reins like that?" Maya asked, genuinely baffled. "That’s a nomad knot if I’m not mistaken."
Aki sat atop the massive alpha wolf, running her gloved fingers gently through the coarse, sandy fur of its neck.
A soft melancholic smile touched her lips.
"It’s just... a little something I learned from someone," Aki murmured softly.
Her mind drifted back to the quiet snow-drenched courtyards of Blessed Land.

She remembered Reina, the cute Beast Tamer... Reina had spent days with Aki, patiently showing her how to read the muscle tension of wild predators, how to bind an alpha’s jaw without crushing its windpipe, and how to assert mental dominance over creatures that operated purely on the law of the jungle.
’Thank you, Reina,’ Aki thought with a surge of gratitude warming her chest. ’Everything Silas gave me... it’s all keeping me alive.’
"Hold on," Leona said, stepping forward.
The captain placed her glowing water-coated palms against the bruised flanks of the three captured wolves.
GLUG... GLUG...

Cool soothing azure mana washed over the beasts’ bruised ribs and concussed muzzles and the swelling receded instantly while their breathing evened out as Leona’s mid-Second Stage healing arts restored their stamina without restoring their feral aggression.
"They’re prepped," Leona said, vaulting onto the back of the second wolf with effortless cat-like grace. "They can run for three hours without stopping..."
Maya mounted the third beast, her heavy armor settling into the creature’s spine with a low grunt.
"Let’s move. We take the low ravines and loop around the northern ridge. We’ll be at the perimeter of that Safe Zone in ten minutes."
"Go!" Aki commanded, snapping the makeshift star-iron reins.
"AWOOOOOOOOOO!"
The three Dune Wolves surged forward in unison as their powerful clawed paws tore into the mountain shale, carrying them down the steep switchbacks with terrifying breathtaking speed.

The wind whipped violently against Aki’s face, tearing tears from her eyes, but she leaned low over the alpha’s shoulders, locking her knees against its thick ribs, matching the bounding stride of the predator beneath her.
They tore down the mountain, covering ground five times faster than they could have on foot, slicing through narrow ravines and dodging falling boulders with supernatural agility.
Yet as they descended past the two-thousand-foot marker...
Aki’s shoulders suddenly twitched.
A sharp unnatural chill crawled across the exposed skin of her neck.
It wasn’t the thin dry cold of high altitude, no, it was like a crystalline frost that seemed to creep through the air like an invisible fog, numbing the tips of her fingers inside her gloves.
Aki frowned, glancing at the rocky crags flanking the ravine.
’When did it get so cold around here...?’ Aki wondered, her breath pluming into thick white clouds of steam. ’We’re approaching the desert floor... the temperature should be rising, not dropping.’
She looked ahead, opening her mouth to warn Maya—
Three hundred feet below them, lodged behind a massive overhang boulder that jutted out over the switchback like a jagged tooth, two figures sat in motionless silence.
They were the representatives of the Tsardom of Borealis.
Draped across their broad shoulders were the heavy silver-furred pelts of Tier-4 frost-bears, the white fur dusted with persistent, unmelting rime.

Beneath the pelts, their charcoal-and-steel plate armor was covered in an advanced chalky camouflage paste that matched the weathered granite perfectly, rendering them completely invisible to standard searches.

Yuri Volkov... a hulking broad-shouldered youth with a jagged combat scar running across his nose, his dark-blonde hair cut short, sat back against the rock, chewing slowly on a strip of cured reindeer fat.
Resting across his knees was a massive two-handed greathammer forged from frozen star-steel, its head covered in brutal diamond-shaped spikes.
Beside him crouched Svetlana Morozova.
She was lean, sharp-featured, with pale, ice-blue eyes that seemed to lack any sort of warmth.
Her silver hair was tied into two tight warrior braids, and her pale hands rested against a six-foot-long hunting spear whose tip was carved from a single translucent shard of glacier crystal.
Svetlana held her right palm flat against the granite rock face.
TICK! TICK! TICK!
Her Second Stage Purple Core was cycling at a whisper, sending microscopic pulses of mana through the stone’s crystalline lattice, reading the vibrations of the upper trail.
Svetlana’s ice-blue eyes snapped open.
"Three mounts," Svetlana whispered. "Rapid descent and moving at full sprint down the western gully."
Yuri swallowed his meat, a slow brutal grin spreading across his scarred face.
"Three mounts? Did Columbia get lost?"
"No," Svetlana said, her brow furrowing slightly. "I only register two native mana signatures... One is a dense high-tier Purple Core while the second is a mid-tier Blue Core."
Yuri paused, his grin widening until his teeth showed.
"Two signatures... and three mounts? The First Princess."

"It’s the Castellian," Svetlana confirmed, her grip tightening around her frost-spear. "And High Marshal Da Silva’s vanguard is running escort for her... They must have linked up immediately after the transit drop."
Yuri chuckled, a deep rumbling sound in his chest.
He reached down, picking up the massive star-steel greathammer with one hand as if it weighed nothing.

"The King’s discarded daughter," Yuri muttered, shaking his head. "They really thought they could parade an unawakened girl through Sector Forty-Four without paying the toll... The path below us is a ledge so if they clear this switchback, they enter the open sand."
Svetlana stood up, her posture coiling like an arctic viper.

"We don’t let them reach the sand. We break the shelf beneath their paws. We throw them into the ravine, separate the guards, and execute the Princess before Da Silva’s people can form a perimeter..."
Yuri stepped up beside her with his massive boots making no sound on the frost-coated rock.
"On my strike," Yuri whispered.
Through the narrow gap between the boulders, the thunderous pounding of heavy wolf paws echoed from the trail above.
THUD-THUD-THUD-THUD!
The lead Dune Wolf, carrying the First Princess, rounded the corner of the switchback at full sprint.
Yuri’s hand snapped upward in a sharp signal.
"NOW!" Yuri roared!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Yuri violently detonated the entire forty-ton overhang boulder with a single colossal swing of his frost-hammer.

The concussive shockwave shattered the rock into thousands of jagged, flying boulders, while Svetlana’s frost-spear thrust downward into the mountain path, unleashing a massive expanding glacier-wave that sheared the entire two-hundred-foot section of the stone ledge clean off the mountain.
CRACK-CRACK-SHATTER!
The ground completely ceased to exist beneath the wolves’ paws!
"SKREEEEEE!"
The Dune Wolves howled in sheer terror as the mountain collapsed into a catastrophic landslide.

The three mounts, Aki, Maya, and Leona were violently thrown off the mountainside, pitching out into the open sky in an uncontrolled terrifying free fall heading straight toward the jagged granite floor two thousand feet below.

paragraphs: The wind screamed and the gravity wrenched Aki’s stomach into her throat.
Yet for the Awakened, the catastrophic fall did not mean panic.
In high-tier combat, the perception of time operated on an entirely different scale.
As the debris fell around them in mid-air, the falling boulders seemed to slow to a lazy floating crawl.
Yuri Volkov plunged through the clouds of dust, falling alongside them with a wild smirk plastered across his scarred face.
"Good morning, Amazon!" Yuri yelled across the empty air, raising his greathammer high above his head to cleave Maya in two.
WHAM!
He didn’t get to swing as Maya Da Silva had already twisted her body in the open air.
Her Purple Core roared like an active volcano, her dark eyes blazing with fury as she swung her heavy combat boot in a blindingly fast horizontal roundhouse kick.
CRACK!

Her void-ivory-armored heel slammed squarely into the side of Yuri’s jaw with the reinforcement shattering his teeth, sending the hulking northern berserker spinning violently through the air until his back slammed into the vertical face of the mountain with a thunderous boom.
SMASH!
Yuri didn’t fall.
He dug his free hand into the granite cliff, his fingers tearing through the stone like butter and his head snapping up with blood pouring from his split lips.
"Hehe..."
His eyes blazed with berserker joy.
"THAT’S IT!" Yuri roared, his laughter booming over the gale. "COME ON, WARRIOR!"
He pushed off the cliff face with both boots, rocketing down the vertical wall like a mountain goat with his greathammer whistling through the air as he charged after Maya.
Maya hit the vertical wall feet-first, her void-ivory greaves absorbing the inertia, and sprinted down the sheer rock face at full speed to meet his advance.
CLANG! BOOM! SMASH!
The two titans clashed horizontally along the mountain wall, their blows creating concussive shockwaves that blew away the falling rubble.
Down below them in the open sky, Aki was tumbling helplessly through the air.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The ground was rushing up with terrifying speed... fifteen hundred feet... twelve hundred feet...
Aki flinched, her hands clawing at empty air, her heart hammering violently.
But even amidst the absolute terror of the fall, her eyes remained wide open as she looked around and for a fraction of a second, she was completely mesmerized.
’This... this is an Awakened battle...’ Aki thought, her breath catching in her throat.
It was terrifying, but it was brutally magnificent.
Above her, Maya and Yuri were tearing the mountain apart.
Yuri’s physical strength was monstrous as he was a true berserker whose blows carried the weight of falling glaciers.
Every time his star-steel hammer struck, the air cracked with thunder, forcing Maya to give ground.
"GET OFF HER!" Maya screamed mid-air.
While parrying Yuri’s hammer with her forearm, Maya thrust her open palm toward the cliff face below Aki.
RUMBLE!
A colossa, fifty-foot pillar of solid granite erupted horizontally from the mountain wall, shooting out directly beneath Aki’s descent, aiming to catch the falling princess and break her plunge.
"I DON’T THINK SO!" Yuri bellowed!
The northern berserker twisted in mid-air, his hammer igniting with terrifying pale-blue frost-mana but he didn’t hit Maya.
He brought the hammer down squarely onto the base of Maya’s stone pillar.
BOOOOOOM!
The massive granite pillar was pulverized into gravel before Aki’s boots could even touch it.
"DIE, PRINCESS!" Svetlana’s melodic voice echoed from the falling mist!
Svetlana Morozova was descending from the clouds like an arctic valkyrie with her frost-spear leveled straight at Aki’s throat.
WHOOSH!
"NOT TODAY!"
Leona materialized between them however the Amazonian captain didn’t rely on brute force... She was a master of the magical aspect of combat instead so in mid-free-fall, Leona snapped her fingers!
GLUG-GLUG-FSSSSSH!

A massive churning ribbon of high-pressure azure water materialized out of thin air, coiling around Aki’s falling body like a gentle liquid cradle, instantly dampening the princess’s terminal velocity and redirecting her momentum horizontally toward a soft sand dune five hundred feet below!
"I’ve got you, Princess!" Leona shouted.
"You have nothing," Svetlana whispered coldly.
In mid-air, Svetlana’s spear twitched and she released the handle as her hands wove a complex three-stage somatic sign in a tenth of a second.
"Rim-weave!"
CRACKLE!
It was a bizarre horrifying application of high-tier cryo-magic as Svetlana didn’t freeze the outside of Leona’s water-ribbon... she targeted the microscopic oxygen molecules within the liquid.
Instantly, the entire twenty-yard coil of water supporting Aki flashed into millions of razor-sharp jagged ice needles!
SHATTER!
The liquid cradle exploded outward, severing Leona’s mana connection and sending Aki plunging back into free fall.
Leona’s hazel eyes widened in pure shock.
"What kind of sick magic is—"
SWOOSH!
Svetlana was already inside her guard.
The northern spear-mistress had closed the five-yard gap in the blink of an eye with her movement looking frictionless.
She caught her falling spear in a reverse grip, drove the blunt butt of the shaft into Leona’s solar plexus, and followed up with a vicious, ice-coated palm strike directly to Leona’s chin.
CRACK!
"Gah—!"

Leona coughed out a spray of blood, the shock paralyzing her nervous system for a split second as Svetlana spun smoothly in the empty air, her right leg whipping around in a brutal axe-kick that struck Leona’s shoulder, violently knocking the Amazonian captain completely off course.
SKIDDDDD-WHOOSH!
Leona was blasted thirty yards away through the air, tumbling violently toward the rocky ravine.

"Princess!" Leona choked out, desperately channeling a burst of wind-mana beneath her boots to stabilize her flight as she thrust her open palm toward Aki, attempting to conjure another water stream to catch the girl—
FZZZZT!
Only a thin sputtering mist erupted from her hand...
Leona’s heart sank into her stomach.
The hit had thrown her too far.
In the dry silica-choked atmosphere of the Wastezone, atmospheric moisture was practically nonexistent.
Without proximity, her mid-Second Stage Blue Core simply didn’t have the casting range to reach Aki.
"Damn it!" Leona screamed, watching helplessly as Svetlana leveled her spear and dove straight after the falling princess.
...Three hundred feet from the ground.
...Two hundred feet.
The wind roared in Aki’s ears, tearing at her hair with the vast expanse of yellow sand and jagged boulders rushing up to meet her at over a hundred miles per hour!
Above her, Svetlana Morozova descended with terrifying grace, falling feet-first with her ice-spear aimed dead center at Aki’s chest.
Svetlana looked down at the First Princess, her pale ice-blue eyes carrying a trace of genuine pity.

"Under normal circumstances," Svetlana said, her voice cutting clean through the roaring gale as she drew closer, "I would be terrified of what your father would do to my family for this... House Castellian does not forgive the execution of royal blood."
The spear tip began to glow with a sharp, blinding azure point of concentrated frost.

"But this is the Exhibition of Succession," Svetlana continued, her tone chillingly flat. "The World Council watches, the rules are absolute and for the glory of the Tsardom... First Princess, you need to go."
...One Hundred feet from the ground.
...Eighty Feet.
Svetlana prepared to thrust her spear through Aki’s heart, ready to use the recoil of the impact to cushion her own landing on the sand below yet as Svetlana looked into the girl’s face...
The northern spear-mistress’s breath hitched.
Aki wasn’t screaming, she wasn’t closing her eyes or curling into a pathetic ball either.
The First Princess of House Castellian was staring directly back at Svetlana with wide unblinking azure eyes that burned with fearless defiance.
VUUUUUUUM.
Before Svetlana’s widening horrified eyes... Aki’s eyes began to glow.
"Hehe..."
Her pupils erupted into a brilliant radiant emerald green.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
From the midnight-black beast-leather glove encasing Aki’s left hand, a massive vortex of concentrated Wind Mana roared into existence.
The gale detonated around her smaller frame in a howling spiraling cyclone of pressurized jade currents that tore the falling dust to shreds.
Svetlana’s jaw dropped in shock.
’WIND MAGIC?!’ Svetlana’s mind screamed in pandemonium. ’SHE’S AN UNAWAKENED MORTAL! HOW IS SHE CYCLING WIND MANA?!’
Aki didn’t answer her.
"Like Leona said, Not today..." Aki whispered, her voice cutting through the cyclone with razor-sharp venom.
SNAP!
Aki clenched her left fistand the wind-mana swirling around her body condensed into a high-pressure cushion beneath her boots.
With a brilliant fluid spin that would have made an acrobat weep, Aki kicked off the air, twisting her entire silhouette three hundred and sixty degrees through empty space.
SWOOSH!
She spun cleanly past Svetlana’s outstretched spear and in a fraction of a second, their positions completely inverted!
Svetlana was now at the bottom, plummeting toward the hard earth fifty feet below and Aki was positioned directly above her, riding the crest of the jade cyclone.
...Aki didn’t hesitate as her right hand flew to the mechanism on her right forearm!
SHLICK!
The star-iron recurve bow snapped open.
Her fingers blurred to the small of her back, plucking a carbon-tipped arrow, seating the nock, and drawing the string all the way back to her ear in a single smooth motion.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
From the midnight-blue glove on her right hand, the Star-Iron necklace around her throat flared with blinding brilliance.
A massive concentration of emerald wind-mana poured through her artificial pathways, wrapping around the carbon arrowhead in a screaming rotating drill of hyper-pressurized air blades.
HSSSSSSSS!
Aki looked down through the sights, her glowing green eyes locking onto Svetlana’s pale terrified face.
Aki clicked her tongue.
...Tsk.
"Fall."
TWANG!
She released the string!
BOOOOOOOOM!
The arrow detonated as a wide lance of roaring jade wind-mana erupted from the bowstring, swallowing the lower airspace in an all-consuming gale that followed.
Down below, Svetlana had barely enough time to cross her forearms and summon a desperate paper-thin sheet of frost before the world turned green.
The roar of the rushing wind was the last thing she heard.
CRASH!

The pressurized arrow slammed squarely into Svetlana’s chest plate as the elemental shockwave drove the northern champion down with the unstoppable force of a falling meteor, smashing her violently into the solid sandstone bedrock of the desert floor.
BOOOOOOOOM!
A crater twenty yards wide ruptured across the desert floor, sending plumes of pulverized sand and shattered stone roaring three hundred feet into the air.
[In the Great Assembly Chamber]
The silence was... unexplainable.

It was not the respectful tense silence of a court watching a duel, more or less was the suffocating silence of more than five hundred people whose fundamental understanding of physical reality had just been violently shattered across the floor.
At the Grand Table, Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur sat frozen. Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov’s jaw hung completely open, his massive hands resting paralyzed on his knees.
High Marshal Valeria Da Silva’s smirk was gone, replaced by wide stunned amber eyes staring at the holographic feed.
Up in the mezzanine, Matriarch Etilga Bloom’s lace fan hung loosely from her limp fingers, completely forgotten against her lap.
Down at the main dais...
The King of the World sat upon his star-iron throne and his face was paper-white.
The color had completely drained from his noble features, his sapphire pupils contracted into microscopic trembling dots as he stared at the center screen hovering before his seat.
Across the globe, the live broadcast chat which had been scrolling at millions of messages per second with over 1.4 billion active viewers watching Kara White’s departure had ground to a dead halt.
There were Zero comments as not a single soul on Earth could process the visual feed displayed before their eyes.

The First Princess of House Castellian... the useless unawakened failure who had been cast out into the dark for twenty-five years floating gracefully down on a cushion of jade wind-mana, holding a smoking bow over the pulverized crater of a northern prodigy.
Finally, after fifteen excruciating seconds of dead, frozen silence...
A choked ragged gasp tore through the Grand Table.

President Julian Vanderbilt Senior leaned forward, his face turning an angry apoplectic purple, his hands trembling so violently against the celestial marble that his signet rings clattered like teeth.
He looked around the room, clutching his own throat as if he were suffocating, his voice cracking into an incredulous high-pitched scream.
"The First Princess..." Vanderbilt choked out, his eyes bulging out of their sockets.
"...CAN USE MAGIC?!"
