paragraphs: The silence in the Great Assembly Chamber curdled.
Across the five risers, the soft sound of the optical projectors was the only sound cutting through the frozen air.

The white holographic panes hovering above the celestial marble table continued to transmit the panoramic overhead feeds from Sector Forty-Four, casting shifting cyan and pale emerald reflections across the pale unblinking faces of the world’s monarchs.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior remained half-risen from his star-iron seat, his broad pinstriped chest heaving as if he had just dragged himself out of an icy river.

His fingers, adorned with the heavy gold signet rings of the Columbian mining trusts, dug so violently into the polished stone that the white projection beneath his palms flickered with static distortion.
"It’s an armament," Sir Arthur Pendelton of the Albion Concordat suggested, his dry voice cutting through the vacuum.
He tapped the silver ferrule of his walking stick against the obsidian floor, though his icy blue eyes were narrowed to needles as he leaned toward his personal console.
"It has to be an integrated relic, perhaps a mechanical item woven into the glove with a pre-charged spell?"
"That has been debunked long ago," Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov rumbled, his deep bass vibrating the glassware along the southern arc.
The massive northern sovereign leaned forward, his heavy silver-wolf mantle spilling across his scarred forearms.

"Look at the particle dispersion on the third optical angle, Arthur. A stored spell from an ether-battery discharges in a linear uniform cone as it has no organic curve... What the girl just cast did not release from a chamber, It responded to the micro-twitches of her body of course which is why she was able to use it like that."
The man took a deep breath.
"There is not an artifact pulled from the entirety of the explored Sovereign Realm that can grant an unawakened frame the neuromuscular dexterity to manipulate wind-mana like a caster."

"And she is not wearing those kinds of technology," Chancellor Henri de Montmirail adjusted his spectacles, his hand visibly shaking against the silver wireframe. "The Warden already cleared her, apart from the items she’s wearing to survive in the sovereign realm, she is truly mundane. If she has no native pathways, controlling a second-tier wind-lance with that degree of directional density is an impossibility... To shape the mana around the arrow shaft requires active responsive channels running straight through the brachial plexus so her nervous system should have burned to charcoal from the inside out."
The murmurs swelled, rising from the mezzanine tiers where the younger scions and diplomatic attachés were leaning over the brass balustrades, their voices bleeding into a panicked discordant roar.
Princess Kiera did not look at the holographic panes.
She turned her head slowly, her pale golden eyes sliding up the star-iron steps toward the throne of the Throne.
The King of the World sat completely rigid.

The sapphire of his irises was stripped of its normal detached majesty as his pupils were contracted to microscopic vibrating points, staring directly through the image of the First Princess suspended in the air.
His broad shoulders were locked like stone masonry with his jaw clamped shut so tightly that a sharp spasm jumped beneath his cheekbone.
The authority that usually hung over the room like an immovable mountain felt strangely brittle, hollowed out by the sudden violent shattering of a reality he had spent years enforcing.
"Calm yourselves," the King’s voice sounded.
The chamber fell dead silent once more with every delegate freezing in place.
The King slowly opened his right hand, the star-iron signet ring glinting against the pale skin of his knuckles as he exhaled a breath that smelled of scorched iron.
"This is..."
He paused, his eyes darkening as he watched the smoking crater on the Wastezone floor.
"...the work of Blessed Land."
Fsssssssssh!

The howling updrafts that had accompanied the violent explosion of the wind-arrow slowly died away, leaving behind a thick suffocating curtain of pulverized sandstone and white quartz dust that hung over the desert floor like a low morning fog.
Aki drifted downward.
Her boots touched the coarse yellow grit of the Wastezone with barely a whisper of friction, the jade-colored glow clinging to her midnight-black glove fading back into the supple leather.
The recoil of the bow was still humming in her wrist in a dull throbbing ache that vibrated along the bones of her forearm, but her breathing was surprisingly steady.
She lowered the recurve mechanism with her blue hair plastered to her forehead with cold sweat and her azure eyes staring fixedly into the center of the twenty-yard crater five paces ahead.
’Did it work...?’
The question bounced nervously inside her skull.
The arrow had struck dead center.

Aki had seen the carbon tip punch through the frost barrier... she had watched the compressed vortex of pressurized jade blades engulf Svetlana Morozova’s chest plate before driving her straight into the bedrock with a lot of force...
An unawakened mortal would have been reduced to red paste and even an ordinary Awakened should have had every rib pulverized into powder.
Yet the hair on the back of Aki’s neck refused to lie flat.
Her instinct suddenly screamed like a siren and Aki didn’t hesitate.
She didn’t pause to confirm the kill either as her left fingers snapped shut inside the black glove.
POP!
A violent burst of wind-mana detonated against the sand beneath her heels, launching her backward and upward in an erratic, ten-foot arc.
SHIIIIING... BOOOOOOM!
A crescent blade of pure translucent glacial ice that was six feet wide and moving with the screaming velocity of a bullet erupted straight out of the dust cloud.
It whistled through the exact coordinates where Aki’s neck had been half a second prior, tearing through the air before slamming into the vertical granite wall of the mountain behind her.
CRASH!
The ice blade cleaved three feet deep into solid stone, leaving behind a weeping frost-scar that crackled with blue lightning.
The shockwave from the strike blew the hanging dust curtain violently outward, laying bare the floor of the crater.
Svetlana Morozova was still standing.
...Barely.
The northern spear-mistress was down on one knee with her six-foot hunting spear planted deep into the bedrock to keep her balance.

The pristine silver-bear pelt across her shoulders had been shredded down to ragged blood-soaked tufts of wool, and the heavy charcoal-and-steel cuirass covering her torso was split wide open from collarbone to hip, revealing an inner layer of shattered crystal-blue ice armor that was actively crumbling away in jagged smoking shards.
"Gah—!"
Svetlana violently spat a thick mouthful of dark blood onto the sand, her breath whistling through broken ribs with a wet gasp.
Her pale face was covered in a mask of chalky dust and gore with a jagged laceration running from her hairline down to the edge of her lip, but her ice-blue eyes were blazing with fury.

’She caught me,’ Svetlana’s mind raced with her fingers trembling against the shaft of her spear as she slowly forced herself to stand upright. ’The little stray actually caught me off guard. At the last second... if I hadn’t reflexively collapsed my entire defensive core into an internal cryo-cocoon between my skin and the armor... that wind would have ripped my lungs straight out of my back.’
She looked up, her gaze locking onto the First Princess who was currently floating ten yards in the air, riding a subtle draft of emerald wind-mana.
Svetlana gritted her teeth, the metallic taste of her own blood fueling the cold rage that defined the hunters of the Tsardom.

’She has no core,’ Svetlana analyzed, her mind working with frigid clarity despite the ringing in her ears. ’I scanned her and she had zero internal circulation during the drop, which means that the bow or those gloves are an external converter... It’s an artificial reservoir and artificial reservoirs have an immutable law which are known as capacity limits.’
’How many of those high-density wind lances can she fire before the battery runs dry? Two? Three? She definitely can’t sustain continuous flight while generating offensive output.’
Svetlana brought her spear back, shifting her weight onto her back foot, dropping into the low stance of the northern tundra clans.

"Impressive, Your Highness," Svetlana’s voice cut through the whistling desert wind. "A mortal managing to draw first blood against the Morozova bloodline so you’ll be a legend in the history books for twelve minutes."
She raised her left hand, wiping the blood from her chin with the back of her wrist with her eyes narrowing into cold slits.

"But a trick only works once," the northern champion continued, her tone dropping into a deadly whisper. "You landed a hit because I treated you like a piece of dead baggage... That mistake won’t happen twice. How long do you think you can stay suspended up there, Princess? And what on this earth made you believe you were out of my reach?"
VUUUUUUUM!
Behind Svetlana’s back, the air within a twenty-yard radius suddenly began to shimmer.
It wasn’t ordinary ice magic.
The microscopic moisture particles suspended in the dry desert air began to violently vibrate, turning into hundreds of razor-sharp translucent diamonds of crystallized rime.
They hung in the air like an executioner’s firing squad, each one no larger than a coin, but vibrating at high frequencies that tore tiny hissing fissures into the atmosphere.
"Move," Svetlana dared, a bloody psychotic smile twitching across her lips. "Let’s see if your little wind-toy can outrun three hundred frost-needles converging from every angle..."
Up in the air, Aki took a slow deep breath through her nose.
Her heart was thumping against her ribs, but the panic that had once ruled her childhood was nowhere to be found.
’She’s right...’ Aki thought, her mind calculating the resources left in her gear.
The Star-Iron necklace around her throat was warm, but the first diamond’s light had noticeably dimmed.
Firing that wind-arrow had consumed nearly a third of the reserve stored inside the pendant.
’I don’t want to draw upon the gloves themselves for now...’
Her left glove was dialed to Wind, which gave her mobility, but its destructive power had peaked with that ambush strike.
If she wanted to end Svetlana permanently, she needed to switch to the right hand... the glove that held the compressed Fire mana Silas had loaded for her.
Fire beats Ice.

It was the most basic elemental law in creation as a single point-blank detonation of the fire lance like the one she had tested in the Citadel would vaporize Svetlana’s cracked armor and incinerate her defensive channels.
’The problem is the opening,’ Aki realized, her eyes scanning the floating cloud of frost-needles.
Svetlana was an Awakened spear-mistress of the Second Stage.
Her physical reaction time, even with cracked ribs and internal bleeding, was three times faster than an unawakened human’s mundane muscle reflex.
If Aki tried to dive straight down, those needles would turn her into a sieve before her fingers could even align the palm socket of the blue glove.

’I have to take a hit,’ the realization settled in Aki’s stomach like a cold stone. ’I have to use the wind to dodge the lethal cluster, let the non-vital needles graze the harness, and use the momentum of the fall to force the palm right into her chest... It’s a fifty-fifty gamble.’
Aki’s jaw set as she reached up with her right hand, her gloved fingers curling into a fist as she was preparing to cycle the red runes—
TWITCH!
Down in the crater, Svetlana’s fingers tightened on the spear shaft with her psychotic smile widening as she prepared to unleash the storm—
BOOOOOOOOOOM!

A concussive shockwave of compressed roaring air detonated from the blind spot directly to Svetlana’s right and the northern spear-mistress didn’t even have time to register the shift in air pressure.
A heavy leather-bound combat boot, reinforced with a howling shroud of pressurized wind-mana, slammed squarely into the right side of Svetlana’s jaw with the force of a pneumatic battering ram.
CRACK!
The sound of teeth fracturing and bone groaning under violence echoed through the canyon.

Svetlana’s head whipped violently to the left with a spray of spit and dark crimson blood exploding from her lips as her entire body was lifted off the ground, spinning horizontally through the air like a discarded rag doll.
SKIDDDDD-CRASH!

She hit the sand fifteen yards away, carving a deep bloody furrow through the yellow grit before slamming into an outcropping of jagged sandstone boulders, the impact shattering the rock into powdery fragments.
"Don’t count me out yet, you northern bitch!"
Leona dropped from the sky, landing heavily in the center of the clearing with a low predator’s crouch.

The Amazonian captain’s combat uniform was torn at the shoulder with a thin line of blood running from her temple where Svetlana had struck her during the free fall, but her sharp hazel eyes were glowing with adrenaline.
The void-ivory armor plates on her shins hummed with pale-green wind runes, actively shedding the friction of the landing.
Svetlana scrambled to her feet among the broken boulders, coughing and sputtering blood as her jaw was dislocated at an ugly sickening angle.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
She jammed her thumb against her own chin, violently popping the joint back into place with a sickening crunch as her eyes began blazing with murderous hysteria while she locked onto Leona.
"DIE!" Svetlana shrieked, her voice muffled by blood.
She swept her spear horizontally.

The three hundred hovering frost-needles in the air responded instantly, abandoning their tracking on Aki as they turned in unison, their crystalline tips aiming down at Leona, descending from the sky in a screaming blizzard of projectiles.
WHOOSH-WHOOSH-WHOOSH-WHOOSH!
The air turned white with magic but Leona didn’t retreat an inch.

sentences.text: The silence in the Great Assembly Chamber curdled.
Across the five risers, the soft sound of the optical projectors was the only sound cutting through the frozen air.

The white holographic panes hovering above the celestial marble table continued to transmit the panoramic overhead feeds from Sector Forty-Four, casting shifting cyan and pale emerald reflections across the pale unblinking faces of the world’s monarchs.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior remained half-risen from his star-iron seat, his broad pinstriped chest heaving as if he had just dragged himself out of an icy river.

His fingers, adorned with the heavy gold signet rings of the Columbian mining trusts, dug so violently into the polished stone that the white projection beneath his palms flickered with static distortion.
"It’s an armament," Sir Arthur Pendelton of the Albion Concordat suggested, his dry voice cutting through the vacuum.
He tapped the silver ferrule of his walking stick against the obsidian floor, though his icy blue eyes were narrowed to needles as he leaned toward his personal console.
"It has to be an integrated relic, perhaps a mechanical item woven into the glove with a pre-charged spell?"
"That has been debunked long ago," Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov rumbled, his deep bass vibrating the glassware along the southern arc.
The massive northern sovereign leaned forward, his heavy silver-wolf mantle spilling across his scarred forearms.
"Look at the particle dispersion on the third optical angle, Arthur.
A stored spell from an ether-battery discharges in a linear uniform cone as it has no organic curve...
What the girl just cast did not release from a chamber, It responded to the micro-twitches of her body of course which is why she was able to use it like that."
The man took a deep breath.
"There is not an artifact pulled from the entirety of the explored Sovereign Realm that can grant an unawakened frame the neuromuscular dexterity to manipulate wind-mana like a caster."
"And she is not wearing those kinds of technology," Chancellor Henri de Montmirail adjusted his spectacles, his hand visibly shaking against the silver wireframe.
"The Warden already cleared her, apart from the items she’s wearing to survive in the sovereign realm, she is truly mundane.
If she has no native pathways, controlling a second-tier wind-lance with that degree of directional density is an impossibility...
To shape the mana around the arrow shaft requires active responsive channels running straight through the brachial plexus so her nervous system should have burned to charcoal from the inside out."
The murmurs swelled, rising from the mezzanine tiers where the younger scions and diplomatic attachés were leaning over the brass balustrades, their voices bleeding into a panicked discordant roar.
Princess Kiera did not look at the holographic panes.
She turned her head slowly, her pale golden eyes sliding up the star-iron steps toward the throne of the Throne.
The King of the World sat completely rigid.

The sapphire of his irises was stripped of its normal detached majesty as his pupils were contracted to microscopic vibrating points, staring directly through the image of the First Princess suspended in the air.
His broad shoulders were locked like stone masonry with his jaw clamped shut so tightly that a sharp spasm jumped beneath his cheekbone.
The authority that usually hung over the room like an immovable mountain felt strangely brittle, hollowed out by the sudden violent shattering of a reality he had spent years enforcing.
"Calm yourselves," the King’s voice sounded.
The chamber fell dead silent once more with every delegate freezing in place.
The King slowly opened his right hand, the star-iron signet ring glinting against the pale skin of his knuckles as he exhaled a breath that smelled of scorched iron.
"This is..."
He paused, his eyes darkening as he watched the smoking crater on the Wastezone floor.
"...the work of Blessed Land."
Fsssssssssh!

The howling updrafts that had accompanied the violent explosion of the wind-arrow slowly died away, leaving behind a thick suffocating curtain of pulverized sandstone and white quartz dust that hung over the desert floor like a low morning fog.
Aki drifted downward.
Her boots touched the coarse yellow grit of the Wastezone with barely a whisper of friction, the jade-colored glow clinging to her midnight-black glove fading back into the supple leather.
The recoil of the bow was still humming in her wrist in a dull throbbing ache that vibrated along the bones of her forearm, but her breathing was surprisingly steady.
She lowered the recurve mechanism with her blue hair plastered to her forehead with cold sweat and her azure eyes staring fixedly into the center of the twenty-yard crater five paces ahead.
’Did it work...?’
The question bounced nervously inside her skull.
The arrow had struck dead center.

Aki had seen the carbon tip punch through the frost barrier... she had watched the compressed vortex of pressurized jade blades engulf Svetlana Morozova’s chest plate before driving her straight into the bedrock with a lot of force...
An unawakened mortal would have been reduced to red paste and even an ordinary Awakened should have had every rib pulverized into powder.
Yet the hair on the back of Aki’s neck refused to lie flat.
Her instinct suddenly screamed like a siren and Aki didn’t hesitate.
She didn’t pause to confirm the kill either as her left fingers snapped shut inside the black glove.
POP!
A violent burst of wind-mana detonated against the sand beneath her heels, launching her backward and upward in an erratic, ten-foot arc.
SHIIIIING...
BOOOOOOM!
A crescent blade of pure translucent glacial ice that was six feet wide and moving with the screaming velocity of a bullet erupted straight out of the dust cloud.
It whistled through the exact coordinates where Aki’s neck had been half a second prior, tearing through the air before slamming into the vertical granite wall of the mountain behind her.
CRASH!
The ice blade cleaved three feet deep into solid stone, leaving behind a weeping frost-scar that crackled with blue lightning.
The shockwave from the strike blew the hanging dust curtain violently outward, laying bare the floor of the crater.
Svetlana Morozova was still standing.
...Barely.
The northern spear-mistress was down on one knee with her six-foot hunting spear planted deep into the bedrock to keep her balance.

The pristine silver-bear pelt across her shoulders had been shredded down to ragged blood-soaked tufts of wool, and the heavy charcoal-and-steel cuirass covering her torso was split wide open from collarbone to hip, revealing an inner layer of shattered crystal-blue ice armor that was actively crumbling away in jagged smoking shards.
"Gah—!"
Svetlana violently spat a thick mouthful of dark blood onto the sand, her breath whistling through broken ribs with a wet gasp.
Her pale face was covered in a mask of chalky dust and gore with a jagged laceration running from her hairline down to the edge of her lip, but her ice-blue eyes were blazing with fury.
’She caught me,’ Svetlana’s mind raced with her fingers trembling against the shaft of her spear as she slowly forced herself to stand upright. ’The little stray actually caught me off guard.

At the last second... if I hadn’t reflexively collapsed my entire defensive core into an internal cryo-cocoon between my skin and the armor... that wind would have ripped my lungs straight out of my back.’
She looked up, her gaze locking onto the First Princess who was currently floating ten yards in the air, riding a subtle draft of emerald wind-mana.
Svetlana gritted her teeth, the metallic taste of her own blood fueling the cold rage that defined the hunters of the Tsardom.

’She has no core,’ Svetlana analyzed, her mind working with frigid clarity despite the ringing in her ears. ’I scanned her and she had zero internal circulation during the drop, which means that the bow or those gloves are an external converter...
It’s an artificial reservoir and artificial reservoirs have an immutable law which are known as capacity limits.’
’How many of those high-density wind lances can she fire before the battery runs dry?
Two?
Three?
She definitely can’t sustain continuous flight while generating offensive output.’
Svetlana brought her spear back, shifting her weight onto her back foot, dropping into the low stance of the northern tundra clans.
"Impressive, Your Highness," Svetlana’s voice cut through the whistling desert wind.
"A mortal managing to draw first blood against the Morozova bloodline so you’ll be a legend in the history books for twelve minutes."
She raised her left hand, wiping the blood from her chin with the back of her wrist with her eyes narrowing into cold slits.
"But a trick only works once," the northern champion continued, her tone dropping into a deadly whisper.
"You landed a hit because I treated you like a piece of dead baggage...
That mistake won’t happen twice.
How long do you think you can stay suspended up there, Princess?
And what on this earth made you believe you were out of my reach?"
VUUUUUUUM!
Behind Svetlana’s back, the air within a twenty-yard radius suddenly began to shimmer.
It wasn’t ordinary ice magic.
The microscopic moisture particles suspended in the dry desert air began to violently vibrate, turning into hundreds of razor-sharp translucent diamonds of crystallized rime.
They hung in the air like an executioner’s firing squad, each one no larger than a coin, but vibrating at high frequencies that tore tiny hissing fissures into the atmosphere.
"Move," Svetlana dared, a bloody psychotic smile twitching across her lips.
"Let’s see if your little wind-toy can outrun three hundred frost-needles converging from every angle..."
Up in the air, Aki took a slow deep breath through her nose.
Her heart was thumping against her ribs, but the panic that had once ruled her childhood was nowhere to be found.

chapters.title: Chapter 560: Counter Attack [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’It’s a direct spell, huh? That means I should move fast...’
"Hah!"
Leona burst forward and she didn’t try to summon a static water barrier to tank the assault.
In this arid desert-adjacent valley, conjuring enough liquid mass to stop three hundred cryo-needles would drain half her remaining blue-core reserves.
Instead, she leaned into her agility.
SWOOSH! SWISH!
Dense pressurized coils of jade wind-mana wrapped around Leona’s calves and waist.
She moved not in a straight line, but in a chaotic zig-zagging sprint that left afterimages across the sand.
’Her movement is so different...’ Aki thought, watching her. They both had control of wind but Leona used it much better.
The frost-needles tore into the ground behind her heels.
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
They rained down, pulverizing the sand into frozen glass, but Leona was already ten feet ahead of the impact zone.
When a cluster of twelve needles dropped directly in her path, she crossed her forearms, releasing two pressurized gale-discs from her wrists.
FSSSSSH... CLANG!

The wind aggressively redirected their trajectory as the ice projectiles were violently deflected sideways, screaming past her ears and embedding themselves deep into the granite mountain wall, detonating in showers of pale sparks.
She closed the fifteen-yard gap in less than a second.
SHING!

From the small of her back, Leona drew her primary weapon... a three-foot-long, single-edged combat machete crafted from deep-sea trench-steel, its blade glowing with a sharp vibrating film of high-frequency water-mana.
Svetlana lunged forward from the rubble, thrusting her six-foot hunting spear with two hands with the glacier-crystal tip aiming straight for Leona’s sternum.
BOOM!
The weapons collided as a massive circular shockwave detonated from the point of impact, blowing the sand away from their boots in a clean, ten-yard circle.
CLANG! CLANG! SHIIING!
What followed was a terrifying high-speed exchange of close-quarters violence that rattled the surrounding canyon.

Svetlana fought with the cold perfection of the northern spear academies as every thrust was a piston-strike aimed at a lethal junction that would lead to the death of her opponent... the throat, the armpit and even the femoral artery.
The reach of her six-foot shaft gave her initial leverage, her spear spinning in icy arcs that left trails of freezing mist in the air.
CLINK!

Leona parried a low thrust with the forte of her trench-blade, the metal groaning as frost crept along the edge, but she immediately channeled a burst of scalding high-pressure water through the steel, violently melting the rime and slipping her guard forward along the shaft.
’We of the Mo—’ Svetlana began to think, her ancestral pride flaring as she prepared to shift into her clan’s signature defensive stance.
BANG!
She didn’t get to finish the thought.
Leona’s left knee drove violently upward into Svetlana’s solar plexus, bypassing the spear entirely.
"Gah!"
The breath exploded from Svetlana’s lungs, her eyes bulging as she stumbled backward, only for Leona’s left elbow to whip around in a savage horizontal smash aimed at her ear.
Svetlana barely raised the haft of her spear to block it...
CRACK!
The force of the attack rattled her teeth, forcing her to scramble three steps back across the sand.
’We of the Morozova clan are the apex of northern hand-to-hand—’ Svetlana’s internal voice snarled, her pride refusing to accept reality as she thrust her spear forward again in a three-stage feint.
WHAM!
Leona didn’t fall for the feint.
The Amazonian captain stepped directly into the attack, letting the spear tip graze the void-ivory plating on her ribcage, and drove her armored forehead straight into the bridge of Svetlana’s nose.
CRUNCH!
Blood sprayed across both their faces.
"Gah!" Svetlana shrieked, her vision flashing white with agony as she desperately tried to summon a wall of ice between them...
’We of the—’
BOOM!

A brutal spinning back-kick from Leona caught Svetlana dead in the center of her cracked breastplate, shattering the remaining metal into fragments and sending her skidding five yards across the sand on her knees.
Svetlana’s head was spinning.
Her nose was broken, her jaw was throbbing, and her chest felt like someone had driven an iron spike through her sternum.
’How?!’ Svetlana raged internally, dragging herself upright with her grip trembling on her spear. ’How is this southern dog matching me in close quarters?!’
Yet as Svetlana looked up through the blood dripping into her eyes, she noticed something... Leona was breathing hard.
The Amazonian captain’s shoulders were heaving with her footing slightly wider than before and her left arm hanging a fraction of an inch lower than her guard.
’She’s exhausted,’ Svetlana realized, a flicker of vicious triumph igniting in her chest. ’She burned through her mana trying to sprint through my needles and her guard is dropping!’
"Haah!"

Svetlana roared, gathering the very last dregs of her Purple Core into the tip of her crystal spear as she lunged forward with everything she had, committing all her momentum to a single overextended thrust aimed straight at Leona’s exposed throat.
"DIE, YOU BITCH!"
The spear point whistled through the air and Leona smiled.
It wasn’t a panicked grimace at all, instead all that was on her face was a cruel smirk.
’Fell for it,’ Leona thought.
The exhaustion was a complete fabrication and the dropped guard was bait.
At the exact second Svetlana committed her weight past the point of recovery, Leona didn’t try to block.
She tilted her head by a mere two inches, letting the icy spear tip graze the skin of her cheek, and stepped inside the reach of the long shaft.
Her left hand shot out like an iron vice, clamping shut around Svetlana’s right wrist, locking the northern champion in place.
"Your form is sloppy when you’re angry," Leona whispered.
SHLICK... CRACK!
"That’s why they teach us not to succumb to anger... that much."
Leona drove the blunt steel pommel of her trench-machete straight into the side of Svetlana’s skull.
BOOM!
A sickening wet concussive crack echoed through the canyon.
Svetlana’s eyes rolled back into her head, the spear slipping from her paralyzed fingers as her nervous system completely short-circuited.
She collapsed forward onto the sand like a severed puppet, completely motionless with her breath coming in shallow unconscious rattles.
Leona stood over her, breathing heavily and wiping the blood from her cheek with the back of her sleeve.

’I managed to defeat her...’ Leona thought, well it was because of the fact that Aki had been the one to damage and weaken her to that level. ’If the Princess didn’t use that spell, then most certainly, I wouldn’t have been able to finish this so easily.’
The reputation of this woman preceded her... compared to her, Leona was far much weaker.
She opened her mouth to call out to Aki—
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
A high-pitched atmospheric scream tore through the sky above them as Leona and Aki snapped their heads upward.
Plummeting through the low clouds at the speed of sound, descending from the mountain peaks like a rogue ballistic missile, was a mass of tumbling bodies and sheared rock.
It was Yuri Volkov and he wasn’t alone.
The scarred northern berserker was locked in a brutal mutual strangulation with Lieutenant Maya Da Silva.
Yuri’s two massive calloused hands were wrapped like iron vices around Maya’s throat, his thick veins bulging with dark-blue mana as he snarled through bloody broken teeth.
"I’LL SNAP YOUR PRETTY LITTLE SOUTHERN NECK BEFORE WE HIT THE GROUND, YOU JUNGLE WHORE!"
Maya didn’t panic.
Her dark face was turning purple from the lack of oxygen, but her amber-brown eyes were burning with cold venomous disgust.
"I told you on the mountain," Maya choked out through gritted teeth, her lips peeling back in a savage snarl. "...I’m not into choking, you ugly bastard!"
WHAM!
Maya drove both her armored knees violently into Yuri’s solar plexus.
"Ggh–!"
Yuri spat a geyser of blood, his grip loosening for a fraction of a second and Maya didn’t waste the window.
She grabbed both of his wrists, twisted her hips with terrifying core strength then completely inverted their positions in mid-air.
She pulled her legs free, planted both heavy combat boots squarely onto Yuri’s broad chest, and pushed off with everything she had.
BOOM!
The concussive shove sent Yuri rocketing toward the earth at twice his original velocity, while Maya used the backward kinetic momentum to vault horizontally toward the face of the mountain.
CRASH!

Yuri Volkov slammed into the desert floor like an artillery shell as the sandstone bedrock ruptured into a thirty-yard-wide five-foot-deep crater, sending plumes of sand and shattered stone roaring into the sky.
Fifty feet above, Maya hit the vertical granite wall of the mountain feet-first.
Her void-ivory greaves groaned under the impact, but she didn’t stop as her hands slapped the bare rock.
’Not yet... I doubt he would die from just that...’
RUMBLE!

She seized control of the mountain’s tectonic grain and the stone beneath her boots liquefied for a microsecond before hardening into a massive forty-five-degree launch ramp that propelled her forward like a fired missile.
WHOOOOOOOSH!
Down in the crater, Yuri was already pushing himself up through the debris.
His nose was broken, his chest armor was dented concave against his ribs, and blood was pouring freely from his scalp, soaking his blonde hair into a crimson mess.
He reached down, grabbing his massive two-handed star-steel greathammer from the rubble, his laughter echoing through the dust like a barking hyena.
"HA! HAHAHA! IS THAT ALL—"
BOOM!
Maya zipped through the air like a streak of black-and-gold lightning as her void-ivory-armored boot slammed directly into Yuri’s scarred nose with the full force of her accelerated momentum.
CRACK!
Yuri was blasted backward twenty yards with his boots tearing two deep, jagged trenches through the sandstone floor.
Yet... he didn’t fall.
Against all logic, against every law of physical concussive trauma, the massive northern berserker dug his heels into the stone and forcefully ground his momentum to a halt.
’Again and again... he keeps coming back. I want to be durable like him.’
He stood there, hunched forward with his arms hanging loose and his greathammer resting point-down in the dirt.
"Guh–!"
A thick dark stream of blood dripped from his shattered nose, splattering against the sand.
Drip! Drip!
Yuri slowly lifted his head.
His eyes were not dazed like Maya expected, instead they were wide and burning with a terrifying luminescence that seemed completely disconnected from reality.
A low chuckle rumbled in his throat, building into a full chest-heaving cackle.
"More..." Yuri whispered, his voice trembling with ecstasy. "...more... give me MORE!"
WHOOSH!
From the bruised battered flesh of his chest, a visible azure aura erupted into the air.
’Is he insane...?’
It wasn’t ordinary mana.

It was thick, boiling, and unstable, crackling around his limbs like liquid electricity, actively knitting the fractured bone in his nose and setting his cracked ribs back into alignment with audible sickening pops.
Maya was caught off guard by this, after all...
’I never heard that he had a healing factor.’
Maya landed ten paces away, dropping into a defensive crouch with her breath coming in ragged gasps as her eyes widened in revulsion.
"What kind of sick freak..." Maya muttered, her teeth clenching.
The volume of mana radiating off the man was staggering.
It wasn’t depleting at all even while he was healing, instead it was multiplying!
Every single blow she had landed on him... from the kick on the mountain cliff to the drop-smash into the crater hadn’t weakened him.
His soul pathways were gorging on the trauma, converting physical impact directly into raw spiritual reserves.
’A Bide ability...’ Maya realized with a cold sweat breaking out beneath her void-ivory cuirass. ’He has a conversion trait...? That wasn’t in his information at all.’
People with Bide spells like this were the most annoying group of people to deal with, the more trauma their body endured, the denser their output became.
Yuri lifted his massive star-steel greathammer with one hand, resting the diamond-spiked head against his shoulder.
The boiling blue aura around his frame was now so dense that the yellow sand beneath his boots was vitrifying into dark sheets of scorched glass.

"You like it, Amazon?!" Yuri roared, his voice booming like rolling thunder. "This is the Frost-Borealis Crucible! Our ancestral gift! The soft weaklings in Europa think defense is about hiding behind shields! In the Tsardom, we let you hit us! We let you break our bones! Because every drop of blood I lose becomes a hammer to cave your skull in!"
He stepped forward, the earth shaking beneath his boots.
"Come on, little girl! Let’s see if you can break me before I turn your spine into kindling!"
Maya didn’t answer him with words.
She reached behind her back with her right hand finding a compact eight-inch cylinder of polished star-iron strapped to her waist.
CLICK!
’Do not falter... Big sis is watching...’
She pressed the runic release catch.
SHSHSH-CLACK!

The cylinder violently expanded as four telescoping sections of void-forged steel shot outward with mechanical precision, locking into a heavy eight-foot-long combat spear tipped with a leaf-shaped blade of dark volcanic quartz.
"You talk too much," Maya said. "Let’s see how much energy your soul can eat when I put a foot of steel through your throat."
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The two titans rushed at each other simultaneously and the clash was apocalyptic.
Yuri swung his greathammer in massive sweeping horizontal arcs that tore the air apart with high-pressure shockwaves.
WHOOOOOOSH... SLAM!

Every swing carried the concussive force of an explosive shell and once again, Maya didn’t dare to parry the spiked head directly... Even with her void-ivory armor, taking the blunt force of that Bide-enhanced hammer would have shattered her forearms.
Instead, she fought with the mastery of an elite Amazonian earth-shaper.
THUD!
As Yuri’s hammer descended in a vertical overhead strike meant to cleave her in two, Maya’s left boot stomped the ground.
CRACK!
A five-foot slab of solid granite shot out of the sand at a sixty-degree angle!
The hammer struck the stone slab...
BOOOOM!
That single attack pulverized it into powder, but the second delay gave Maya the exact opening she needed.
She slid beneath the shattered debris, her volcanic quartz spear thrusting upward like a striking viper, aiming straight for the soft junction between Yuri’s neck and shoulder.
SKR-SHLICK!
The spear blade pierced the flesh and blood sprayed.
"YES!" Yuri bellowed, not even flinching!
He didn’t pull away from the blade as he stepped forward, driving Maya’s spear deeper into his own shoulder just to close the distance.
His free left hand shot out, grabbing the quartz blade with his bare, bleeding palm, locking Maya’s weapon in place.
"MY TURN!"
Yuri’s right arm coiled back with his fist glowing with blinding, superheated blue mana, aiming a concussive haymaker straight for Maya’s face.
Maya let go of the spear shaft instantly.
She dropped low, her hands slapping the ground on either side of Yuri’s planted boots.
"Terra Maw!"
SNAP!
The sandstone beneath Yuri’s feet liquefied into quicksand for half a heartbeat, swallowing his boots up to his calves, and then instantly petrified back into solid granite.
Yuri’s momentum violently stalled with his haymaker whistling harmlessly through empty air above Maya’s ducking head.
"What the—?!" Yuri snarled, struggling against the stone cuffs locking his legs as Maya sprang up from the ground like an uncoiling spring.

sentences.text: ’It’s a direct spell, huh?
That means I should move fast...’
"Hah!"
Leona burst forward and she didn’t try to summon a static water barrier to tank the assault.
In this arid desert-adjacent valley, conjuring enough liquid mass to stop three hundred cryo-needles would drain half her remaining blue-core reserves.
Instead, she leaned into her agility.
SWOOSH!
SWISH!
Dense pressurized coils of jade wind-mana wrapped around Leona’s calves and waist.
She moved not in a straight line, but in a chaotic zig-zagging sprint that left afterimages across the sand.
’Her movement is so different...’ Aki thought, watching her.
They both had control of wind but Leona used it much better.
The frost-needles tore into the ground behind her heels.
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
They rained down, pulverizing the sand into frozen glass, but Leona was already ten feet ahead of the impact zone.
When a cluster of twelve needles dropped directly in her path, she crossed her forearms, releasing two pressurized gale-discs from her wrists.
FSSSSSH...
CLANG!

The wind aggressively redirected their trajectory as the ice projectiles were violently deflected sideways, screaming past her ears and embedding themselves deep into the granite mountain wall, detonating in showers of pale sparks.
She closed the fifteen-yard gap in less than a second.
SHING!

From the small of her back, Leona drew her primary weapon... a three-foot-long, single-edged combat machete crafted from deep-sea trench-steel, its blade glowing with a sharp vibrating film of high-frequency water-mana.
Svetlana lunged forward from the rubble, thrusting her six-foot hunting spear with two hands with the glacier-crystal tip aiming straight for Leona’s sternum.
BOOM!
The weapons collided as a massive circular shockwave detonated from the point of impact, blowing the sand away from their boots in a clean, ten-yard circle.
CLANG!
CLANG!
SHIIING!
What followed was a terrifying high-speed exchange of close-quarters violence that rattled the surrounding canyon.

Svetlana fought with the cold perfection of the northern spear academies as every thrust was a piston-strike aimed at a lethal junction that would lead to the death of her opponent... the throat, the armpit and even the femoral artery.
The reach of her six-foot shaft gave her initial leverage, her spear spinning in icy arcs that left trails of freezing mist in the air.
CLINK!

Leona parried a low thrust with the forte of her trench-blade, the metal groaning as frost crept along the edge, but she immediately channeled a burst of scalding high-pressure water through the steel, violently melting the rime and slipping her guard forward along the shaft.
’We of the Mo—’ Svetlana began to think, her ancestral pride flaring as she prepared to shift into her clan’s signature defensive stance.
BANG!
She didn’t get to finish the thought.
Leona’s left knee drove violently upward into Svetlana’s solar plexus, bypassing the spear entirely.
"Gah!"
The breath exploded from Svetlana’s lungs, her eyes bulging as she stumbled backward, only for Leona’s left elbow to whip around in a savage horizontal smash aimed at her ear.
Svetlana barely raised the haft of her spear to block it...
CRACK!
The force of the attack rattled her teeth, forcing her to scramble three steps back across the sand.
’We of the Morozova clan are the apex of northern hand-to-hand—’ Svetlana’s internal voice snarled, her pride refusing to accept reality as she thrust her spear forward again in a three-stage feint.
WHAM!
Leona didn’t fall for the feint.
The Amazonian captain stepped directly into the attack, letting the spear tip graze the void-ivory plating on her ribcage, and drove her armored forehead straight into the bridge of Svetlana’s nose.
CRUNCH!
Blood sprayed across both their faces.
"Gah!" Svetlana shrieked, her vision flashing white with agony as she desperately tried to summon a wall of ice between them...
’We of the—’
BOOM!

A brutal spinning back-kick from Leona caught Svetlana dead in the center of her cracked breastplate, shattering the remaining metal into fragments and sending her skidding five yards across the sand on her knees.
Svetlana’s head was spinning.
Her nose was broken, her jaw was throbbing, and her chest felt like someone had driven an iron spike through her sternum.
’How?!’ Svetlana raged internally, dragging herself upright with her grip trembling on her spear. ’How is this southern dog matching me in close quarters?!’
Yet as Svetlana looked up through the blood dripping into her eyes, she noticed something...
Leona was breathing hard.
The Amazonian captain’s shoulders were heaving with her footing slightly wider than before and her left arm hanging a fraction of an inch lower than her guard.
’She’s exhausted,’ Svetlana realized, a flicker of vicious triumph igniting in her chest. ’She burned through her mana trying to sprint through my needles and her guard is dropping!’
"Haah!"

Svetlana roared, gathering the very last dregs of her Purple Core into the tip of her crystal spear as she lunged forward with everything she had, committing all her momentum to a single overextended thrust aimed straight at Leona’s exposed throat.
"DIE, YOU BITCH!"
The spear point whistled through the air and Leona smiled.
It wasn’t a panicked grimace at all, instead all that was on her face was a cruel smirk.
’Fell for it,’ Leona thought.
The exhaustion was a complete fabrication and the dropped guard was bait.
At the exact second Svetlana committed her weight past the point of recovery, Leona didn’t try to block.
She tilted her head by a mere two inches, letting the icy spear tip graze the skin of her cheek, and stepped inside the reach of the long shaft.
Her left hand shot out like an iron vice, clamping shut around Svetlana’s right wrist, locking the northern champion in place.
"Your form is sloppy when you’re angry," Leona whispered.
SHLICK...
CRACK!
"That’s why they teach us not to succumb to anger... that much."
Leona drove the blunt steel pommel of her trench-machete straight into the side of Svetlana’s skull.
BOOM!
A sickening wet concussive crack echoed through the canyon.
Svetlana’s eyes rolled back into her head, the spear slipping from her paralyzed fingers as her nervous system completely short-circuited.
She collapsed forward onto the sand like a severed puppet, completely motionless with her breath coming in shallow unconscious rattles.
Leona stood over her, breathing heavily and wiping the blood from her cheek with the back of her sleeve.

’I managed to defeat her...’ Leona thought, well it was because of the fact that Aki had been the one to damage and weaken her to that level. ’If the Princess didn’t use that spell, then most certainly, I wouldn’t have been able to finish this so easily.’
The reputation of this woman preceded her... compared to her, Leona was far much weaker.
She opened her mouth to call out to Aki—
SKREEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
A high-pitched atmospheric scream tore through the sky above them as Leona and Aki snapped their heads upward.
Plummeting through the low clouds at the speed of sound, descending from the mountain peaks like a rogue ballistic missile, was a mass of tumbling bodies and sheared rock.
It was Yuri Volkov and he wasn’t alone.
The scarred northern berserker was locked in a brutal mutual strangulation with Lieutenant Maya Da Silva.
Yuri’s two massive calloused hands were wrapped like iron vices around Maya’s throat, his thick veins bulging with dark-blue mana as he snarled through bloody broken teeth.
"I’LL SNAP YOUR PRETTY LITTLE SOUTHERN NECK BEFORE WE HIT THE GROUND, YOU JUNGLE WHORE!"
Maya didn’t panic.
Her dark face was turning purple from the lack of oxygen, but her amber-brown eyes were burning with cold venomous disgust.
"I told you on the mountain," Maya choked out through gritted teeth, her lips peeling back in a savage snarl.
"...I’m not into choking, you ugly bastard!"
WHAM!
Maya drove both her armored knees violently into Yuri’s solar plexus.
"Ggh–!"
Yuri spat a geyser of blood, his grip loosening for a fraction of a second and Maya didn’t waste the window.
She grabbed both of his wrists, twisted her hips with terrifying core strength then completely inverted their positions in mid-air.
She pulled her legs free, planted both heavy combat boots squarely onto Yuri’s broad chest, and pushed off with everything she had.
BOOM!
The concussive shove sent Yuri rocketing toward the earth at twice his original velocity, while Maya used the backward kinetic momentum to vault horizontally toward the face of the mountain.
CRASH!

Yuri Volkov slammed into the desert floor like an artillery shell as the sandstone bedrock ruptured into a thirty-yard-wide five-foot-deep crater, sending plumes of sand and shattered stone roaring into the sky.
Fifty feet above, Maya hit the vertical granite wall of the mountain feet-first.
Her void-ivory greaves groaned under the impact, but she didn’t stop as her hands slapped the bare rock.
’Not yet...
I doubt he would die from just that...’
RUMBLE!

She seized control of the mountain’s tectonic grain and the stone beneath her boots liquefied for a microsecond before hardening into a massive forty-five-degree launch ramp that propelled her forward like a fired missile.
WHOOOOOOOSH!
Down in the crater, Yuri was already pushing himself up through the debris.
His nose was broken, his chest armor was dented concave against his ribs, and blood was pouring freely from his scalp, soaking his blonde hair into a crimson mess.
He reached down, grabbing his massive two-handed star-steel greathammer from the rubble, his laughter echoing through the dust like a barking hyena.
"HA!
HAHAHA!
IS THAT ALL—"
BOOM!
Maya zipped through the air like a streak of black-and-gold lightning as her void-ivory-armored boot slammed directly into Yuri’s scarred nose with the full force of her accelerated momentum.
CRACK!
Yuri was blasted backward twenty yards with his boots tearing two deep, jagged trenches through the sandstone floor.
Yet... he didn’t fall.
Against all logic, against every law of physical concussive trauma, the massive northern berserker dug his heels into the stone and forcefully ground his momentum to a halt.
’Again and again... he keeps coming back.
I want to be durable like him.’
He stood there, hunched forward with his arms hanging loose and his greathammer resting point-down in the dirt.
"Guh–!"
A thick dark stream of blood dripped from his shattered nose, splattering against the sand.
Drip!
Drip!
Yuri slowly lifted his head.
His eyes were not dazed like Maya expected, instead they were wide and burning with a terrifying luminescence that seemed completely disconnected from reality.
A low chuckle rumbled in his throat, building into a full chest-heaving cackle.
"More..." Yuri whispered, his voice trembling with ecstasy.
"...more... give me MORE!"
WHOOSH!
From the bruised battered flesh of his chest, a visible azure aura erupted into the air.
’Is he insane...?’
It wasn’t ordinary mana.

It was thick, boiling, and unstable, crackling around his limbs like liquid electricity, actively knitting the fractured bone in his nose and setting his cracked ribs back into alignment with audible sickening pops.
Maya was caught off guard by this, after all...
’I never heard that he had a healing factor.’
Maya landed ten paces away, dropping into a defensive crouch with her breath coming in ragged gasps as her eyes widened in revulsion.
"What kind of sick freak..." Maya muttered, her teeth clenching.
The volume of mana radiating off the man was staggering.
It wasn’t depleting at all even while he was healing, instead it was multiplying!
Every single blow she had landed on him... from the kick on the mountain cliff to the drop-smash into the crater hadn’t weakened him.
His soul pathways were gorging on the trauma, converting physical impact directly into raw spiritual reserves.
’A Bide ability...’ Maya realized with a cold sweat breaking out beneath her void-ivory cuirass. ’He has a conversion trait...?
That wasn’t in his information at all.’
People with Bide spells like this were the most annoying group of people to deal with, the more trauma their body endured, the denser their output became.
Yuri lifted his massive star-steel greathammer with one hand, resting the diamond-spiked head against his shoulder.
The boiling blue aura around his frame was now so dense that the yellow sand beneath his boots was vitrifying into dark sheets of scorched glass.
"You like it, Amazon?!" Yuri roared, his voice booming like rolling thunder.
"This is the Frost-Borealis Crucible!
Our ancestral gift!
The soft weaklings in Europa think defense is about hiding behind shields!
In the Tsardom, we let you hit us!
We let you break our bones!
Because every drop of blood I lose becomes a hammer to cave your skull in!"
He stepped forward, the earth shaking beneath his boots.
"Come on, little girl!
Let’s see if you can break me before I turn your spine into kindling!"
Maya didn’t answer him with words.
She reached behind her back with her right hand finding a compact eight-inch cylinder of polished star-iron strapped to her waist.
CLICK!
’Do not falter...
Big sis is watching...’
She pressed the runic release catch.
SHSHSH-CLACK!

The cylinder violently expanded as four telescoping sections of void-forged steel shot outward with mechanical precision, locking into a heavy eight-foot-long combat spear tipped with a leaf-shaped blade of dark volcanic quartz.
"You talk too much," Maya said.
"Let’s see how much energy your soul can eat when I put a foot of steel through your throat."
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The two titans rushed at each other simultaneously and the clash was apocalyptic.
Yuri swung his greathammer in massive sweeping horizontal arcs that tore the air apart with high-pressure shockwaves.
WHOOOOOOSH...
SLAM!

Even with her void-ivory armor, taking the blunt force of that Bide-enhanced hammer would have shattered her forearms.

Maya let go of the spear shaft instantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 561: Three Countries Out [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Maya didn’t have her spear, so she used her elbows, her knees, and the void-ivory plating on her forearms...
CRACK! WHAM! BOOM!
She delivered a brutal five-strike combination directly to Yuri’s ribs, kidneys, and jaw.
Every blow shattered rock, drew blood, and tore muscle yet Yuri’s laughter only grew louder and more terrifying.
’Why don’t you fucking fall already...?’
WHAM!
"WEAK! IT’S NOT ENOUGH!"
CRACKLE!
The boiling blue aura around his chest exploded outward in a shockwave, violently shattering the granite cuffs around his ankles and blowing Maya ten yards backward across the sand.
Yuri pulled Maya’s quartz spear from his shoulder, tossing it aside like a useless toothpick as his eyes rolled back as though he was intoxicated.
’I don’t like Bide abilities and I never will... all their users are crazy.’
His physical mass seemed to have swelled, the muscles in his arms bulging with dark pulsing veins that hummed with enough power to level a high tier barrier.
Yuri raised his massive star-steel greathammer with both hands, the weapon screaming as pure compressed energy wrapped around the head like a miniature sun.

"THIS IS THE END, AMAZON!" Yuri roared, his voice vibrating the mountain peaks as he lunged forward, crossing thirty yards in seconds while his hammer was raised high for a strike that would leave nothing but a smoking crater in the earth.
Maya planted her boots with her breath ragged and her hands trembling as she crossed her forearms.
’I’m going to do it...’ She thought as she began preparing to burn every single drop of her remaining Purple Core to manifest an earth-bastion to protect herself. ’Is there going to be enough ti—’
TWANG!
The sound was tiny.
In the middle of the roaring gale, amidst the apocalyptic thunder of Yuri’s charging hammer, the mechanical release of a star-iron bowstring was practically a whisper.
Yet in the air twenty feet above Yuri’s left flank...
A bright emerald-green projectile tore through the sky.
It wasn’t an arrow meant to pierce his skull and it wasn’t an attack meant to deal heavy physical trauma that his Bide ability could consume either.
It was an arrow carrying a high-frequency sonic wind-vortex!
POP!
The arrow detonated three inches from the side of Yuri’s left ear, while the concussive shockwave didn’t break his bones... It did something far more lethal to a berserker mid-stride.
It violently ruptured his left eardrum and scrambled the delicate fluid balance inside his inner ear canal.
SKR-STUMBLE!
In the middle of his unstoppable full-speed charge, Yuri’s balance completely dissolved.

His left leg gave out beneath him, his center of gravity violently listing to the side as his eyes twitched erratically and the massive glowing greathammer pulling him off course like a dragging anchor.
"WHAT—?!" Yuri snarled with his vision spinning in nauseating circles. Maya to her credit didn’t ask where the arrow came from.
A veteran strike officer never questioned an opening... she exploited it with merciless violence.
Maya’s eyes flared with dark-purple fire.
’I’ll end all of this...!’

She poured every single shred of her remaining Second Stage mana straight into her right arm... The void-ivory gauntlet on her hand groaned, the gold filigree burning white-hot as she seized the jagged five-foot shard of granite that had broken from her earlier barrier.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Maya stepped inside the off-balance berserker’s guard, swinging the massive razor-sharp granite slab like an executioner’s axe.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The granite slab struck Yuri Volkov squarely across the temple and the concussive force sounded like that of falling rubble!
Even with his Bide ability boiling at its peak, the human brain could not overcome the violent instantaneous deceleration of a five-hundred-pound stone moving at two hundred miles per hour.

The shockwave violently disconnected Yuri’s consciousness from his nervous system as his bloodshot eyes rolled completely into the back of his head, his hands went limp and the massive star-steel greathammer crashed harmlessly into the sand.
THUD!
The hulking berserker hit the ground face-first, completely unconscious.
Ten paces away, Svetlana Morozova lay equally motionless in the dirt, her body trembling faintly in deep coma.
Maya stood over the fallen giant with her chest heaving in violent, agonizing gasps and blood dripping freely from her knuckles and chin.
She dropped the shattered remains of the granite slab, turned her head, and looked up at the sky.
Floating gently down to the sand twenty feet away with her bow lowered and her hair blowing softly in the desert wind, was First Princess Aki.
Beside her, Leona was leaning against an outcropping, resting her hands on her knees while grinning through her split lips.
"Nice shot, Princess," Leona panted, raising a trembling thumb.
Aki offered a tired fragile smile, her fingers still shaking slightly inside the midnight-blue glove.
"Thanks."
Before Maya could reply, the bodies of Yuri Volkov and Svetlana Morozova began to react.
WHOOSH!
A pair of bright, ethereal white beacons erupted from the emergency transponder badges pinned to their lapels.

The spatial fabric around the two fallen northern champions warped and rippled with dense magic as their physical bodies, their weapons, and their discarded armor plates dissolved into thousands of shimmering motes of pure white light, surging upward into the clouds as the World Council’s automated extraction protocols yanked them clean out of Sector Forty-Four.
The representatives of the Tsardom of Borealis were officially eliminated.
Maya collapsed onto her rear in the sand, leaning back against a boulder with a long groaning sigh of relief.
"Gods above," Maya wheezed, wiping the sweat and blood from her eyes. "My ribs feel like someone ran a mining drill through them."
Aki walked over, reaching into her pocket to pull out a clean cloth to help Maya clean the laceration on her brow.
Yet before Aki’s hand could touch her forehead—
BZZZZZZZZT!

The massive broadcast array embedded in the ceiling of the Sovereign Realm roared to life once more, echoing across the vast expanses of the mountains, the jungles, and the distant dunes.𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝔀𝓮𝒃𝙣𝓸𝒗𝒆𝒍.𝙘𝒐𝒎
"Notice of Official Elimination."
"The representatives of the Tsardom of Borealis have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Aki and Maya shared a satisfied glance however the broadcast continued.
"The representatives of the United Hegemony of Shogya have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Maya froze as her hand stopped halfway to her canteen.
"The representatives of the Republic of Columbia have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Silence followed and the broadcast chime died out, leaving only the desolate empty whistling of the Wastezone wind.
Aki blinked once... Twice...
Leona’s jaw hung completely open with her hazel eyes staring blankly at the purple clouds above.
Maya looked from Leona to Aki as her face was completely pale beneath the dust and blood.
"Wait..." Leona stammered, her voice cracking in disbelieving confusion. "Shogya... and Columbia...? Both of them?!"
Columbia’s armored shock-corps and Shogya’s synchronized twin-swordsmen...

Four of the most funded combat scions on the face of the Earth... These were teams that had commanded private armies and trained in spatial simulation chambers for a decade, eliminated in the exact same eight-minute window?!
Aki’s head slowly turned.
She looked out across the vast rolling expanse of the yellow dunes, staring past the emerald jungle toward the jagged, smoking crown of the central volcanic caldera five miles away.
A tiny breathless whisper escaped Aki’s lips.
"...What in the world is Kara doing over there?"
After that singular thought, she forced the sudden image of Silas out of her mind.
In an arena like this, wandering thoughts got you gutted.
Silas had carved his way through the Umbral Basin long before she had ever laid eyes on him; whatever hell he was orchestrating miles across the basin was his business.
Her business was keeping her throat intact, holding onto her retainers, and seeing the two-hour clock bleed to zero.
Behind her, Captain Leona finished wiping the dark crust of dried blood from the corner of her split lower lip with a rough swipe of her leather bracer.
Her breath was steady now, falling back into the regular breathing of a seasoned trench scout.
She drove the broad point of her deep-sea trench-machete back into the friction-sheath strapped along her lumbar with a shlick.

"That broadcast just changed the whole board," Leona said, her hazel eyes scanning the sharp ridges of the western mesa. "Columbia’s armored shock-corps folded and Shogya’s twin swordsmen were wiped in the exact same breath while Borealis dissolved right at our boots... The weaklings and the loudmouths are off the grid and that leaves the real bastards."
Maya Da Silva knelt on one knee in the coarse grit, using the flat of a combat dagger to pry a jagged wedge of frozen granite from between the articulated joints of her void-ivory greaves.
She tossed the rock aside with a dull click, her dark face set into a rigid humorless grimace.

"Khemet," Maya muttered, her voice dropping into a tired tone that rasped over the dry desert wind. "The terrain belongs to them... You drop Tariq Al-Mansur and Safira into thousands of square miles of sun-baked dunes, and you’re basically fighting two sharks in their own blood-slicked pool. Every grain of silica out there is an eye, a snare, or a localized kinetic spike. If we try to push through the dunes toward the eastern basin, we won’t even see the blades that sever our Achilles tendons."
Aki nodded once, a cold certainty settling into the hollow of her chest.
She raised a gloved hand, pointing past the crumbling foothills toward a wide, snaking band of dense emerald-green jungle that followed the course of an ancient riverbed.

"Then we abandon the dunes entirely," Aki said. "We stick to the plan. We set up our perimeter above the Safe Zone... Once we dismantle whatever squad is foolish enough to try camping the barrier, we break straight for the tree line."
Maya looked up from her greaves, squinting toward the thick canopy winding through the basin floor as a slow approving nod tugged at her chin.

"Smart," Maya grunted. "None of the high houses cultivate Nature magic... House Bloom is pure combustion and shadow-stepping while Indus relies on superheated volcanic magma and psychic compression fields. If we pull the battlefield under that canopy, Khemet loses their infinite medium of sand, and the snipers lose their long-range sightlines."

"Sound logic, Princess," Leona chimed in, crossing her arms over the pearl-white chest plate of her prototype armor. "Except for one glaring operational reality... Our mounts took a two-thousand-foot header off the mountain wall when Yuri shattered the shelf. Traversing six miles of broken badlands on foot while carrying sixty pounds of combat gear is going to eat half our stamina."
Aki turned her head, her azure eyes dropping toward the base of the shattered cliff where the avalanche had settled into a towering scree of pulverized stone.
A bitter knot formed in her stomach.
"They fell with the rock," Aki murmured with her shoulders tightening. "Without anything to cushion the drop, the impact alone—"
Maya chuckled as she pushed herself up from the dirt, slapping the yellow grit from her thighs.
"Who told you they hit the ground?" Maya said with an arrogant grin splitting her dark features.
Aki blinked. "What?"
Maya stepped to the edge of the shelf, planting her heavy boots right where the rock sheared away into the abyss.

She closed her eyes, rolling her neck until the vertebrae popped like firecrackers and then she extended her right hand downward with her fingers splayed wide and the Second Stage Purple Core within her chest flared with a deep violet glow.
"Trust me..."
She made a sharp upward-pulling motion with her forearm.
RUMBLE!
The base of the mountain groaned.
Two thousand feet below, in the shadowed hollow where the landslide had settled against the canyon wall, the compacted mound of shattered granite and red silt began to shift like a living mass.
The stone liquefied for three fractions of a second, parting like soft mud, and three golden-furred shapes scrambled violently out of the subterranean hollow.
"AROOOOOO!"
The Dune Wolves tore up the rocky slope, leaping from boulder to boulder with terrifying muscular agility.
Their thick coats were caked in yellow silt and powdered shale, their flanks bruised from the initial impact, but their powerful limbs were intact.
The makeshift reins Aki had braided from star-iron cord were still cinched securely behind their wide pointed ears.
The massive alpha wolf bounded up the final ledge, skidding to a halt three feet from Aki, dropping its broad snout into the dirt and letting out a low huffing whine of recognition.

"I manifested a small pocket beneath their descent while Yuri was trying to cave my face in," Maya explained, rolling her right shoulder to work out a lingering knot. "Buried them under eight feet of loose sand to insulate them from the falling boulders, then reinforced the chamber ceiling with a stone spell... after all Frontier deployment rule number four states that you should never abandon your transport if you can build a cellar around it."
