sentences.text: Maya didn’t have her spear, so she used her elbows, her knees, and the void-ivory plating on her forearms...
CRACK!
WHAM!
BOOM!
She delivered a brutal five-strike combination directly to Yuri’s ribs, kidneys, and jaw.
Every blow shattered rock, drew blood, and tore muscle yet Yuri’s laughter only grew louder and more terrifying.
’Why don’t you fucking fall already...?’
WHAM!
"WEAK!
IT’S NOT ENOUGH!"
CRACKLE!
The boiling blue aura around his chest exploded outward in a shockwave, violently shattering the granite cuffs around his ankles and blowing Maya ten yards backward across the sand.
Yuri pulled Maya’s quartz spear from his shoulder, tossing it aside like a useless toothpick as his eyes rolled back as though he was intoxicated.
’I don’t like Bide abilities and I never will... all their users are crazy.’
His physical mass seemed to have swelled, the muscles in his arms bulging with dark pulsing veins that hummed with enough power to level a high tier barrier.
Yuri raised his massive star-steel greathammer with both hands, the weapon screaming as pure compressed energy wrapped around the head like a miniature sun.

"THIS IS THE END, AMAZON!" Yuri roared, his voice vibrating the mountain peaks as he lunged forward, crossing thirty yards in seconds while his hammer was raised high for a strike that would leave nothing but a smoking crater in the earth.
Maya planted her boots with her breath ragged and her hands trembling as she crossed her forearms.
’I’m going to do it...’ She thought as she began preparing to burn every single drop of her remaining Purple Core to manifest an earth-bastion to protect herself. ’Is there going to be enough ti—’
TWANG!
The sound was tiny.
In the middle of the roaring gale, amidst the apocalyptic thunder of Yuri’s charging hammer, the mechanical release of a star-iron bowstring was practically a whisper.
Yet in the air twenty feet above Yuri’s left flank...
A bright emerald-green projectile tore through the sky.
It wasn’t an arrow meant to pierce his skull and it wasn’t an attack meant to deal heavy physical trauma that his Bide ability could consume either.
It was an arrow carrying a high-frequency sonic wind-vortex!
POP!
The arrow detonated three inches from the side of Yuri’s left ear, while the concussive shockwave didn’t break his bones...
It did something far more lethal to a berserker mid-stride.
It violently ruptured his left eardrum and scrambled the delicate fluid balance inside his inner ear canal.
SKR-STUMBLE!
In the middle of his unstoppable full-speed charge, Yuri’s balance completely dissolved.

His left leg gave out beneath him, his center of gravity violently listing to the side as his eyes twitched erratically and the massive glowing greathammer pulling him off course like a dragging anchor.
"WHAT—?!" Yuri snarled with his vision spinning in nauseating circles.
Maya to her credit didn’t ask where the arrow came from.
A veteran strike officer never questioned an opening... she exploited it with merciless violence.
Maya’s eyes flared with dark-purple fire.
’I’ll end all of this...!’
She poured every single shred of her remaining Second Stage mana straight into her right arm...
The void-ivory gauntlet on her hand groaned, the gold filigree burning white-hot as she seized the jagged five-foot shard of granite that had broken from her earlier barrier.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Maya stepped inside the off-balance berserker’s guard, swinging the massive razor-sharp granite slab like an executioner’s axe.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The granite slab struck Yuri Volkov squarely across the temple and the concussive force sounded like that of falling rubble!
Even with his Bide ability boiling at its peak, the human brain could not overcome the violent instantaneous deceleration of a five-hundred-pound stone moving at two hundred miles per hour.

The shockwave violently disconnected Yuri’s consciousness from his nervous system as his bloodshot eyes rolled completely into the back of his head, his hands went limp and the massive star-steel greathammer crashed harmlessly into the sand.
THUD!
The hulking berserker hit the ground face-first, completely unconscious.
Ten paces away, Svetlana Morozova lay equally motionless in the dirt, her body trembling faintly in deep coma.
Maya stood over the fallen giant with her chest heaving in violent, agonizing gasps and blood dripping freely from her knuckles and chin.
She dropped the shattered remains of the granite slab, turned her head, and looked up at the sky.
Floating gently down to the sand twenty feet away with her bow lowered and her hair blowing softly in the desert wind, was First Princess Aki.
Beside her, Leona was leaning against an outcropping, resting her hands on her knees while grinning through her split lips.
"Nice shot, Princess," Leona panted, raising a trembling thumb.
Aki offered a tired fragile smile, her fingers still shaking slightly inside the midnight-blue glove.
"Thanks."
Before Maya could reply, the bodies of Yuri Volkov and Svetlana Morozova began to react.
WHOOSH!
A pair of bright, ethereal white beacons erupted from the emergency transponder badges pinned to their lapels.

The spatial fabric around the two fallen northern champions warped and rippled with dense magic as their physical bodies, their weapons, and their discarded armor plates dissolved into thousands of shimmering motes of pure white light, surging upward into the clouds as the World Council’s automated extraction protocols yanked them clean out of Sector Forty-Four.
The representatives of the Tsardom of Borealis were officially eliminated.
Maya collapsed onto her rear in the sand, leaning back against a boulder with a long groaning sigh of relief.
"Gods above," Maya wheezed, wiping the sweat and blood from her eyes.
"My ribs feel like someone ran a mining drill through them."
Aki walked over, reaching into her pocket to pull out a clean cloth to help Maya clean the laceration on her brow.
Yet before Aki’s hand could touch her forehead—
BZZZZZZZZT!

The massive broadcast array embedded in the ceiling of the Sovereign Realm roared to life once more, echoing across the vast expanses of the mountains, the jungles, and the distant dunes.𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝔀𝓮𝒃𝙣𝓸𝒗𝒆𝒍.𝙘𝒐𝒎
"Notice of Official Elimination."
"The representatives of the Tsardom of Borealis have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Aki and Maya shared a satisfied glance however the broadcast continued.
"The representatives of the United Hegemony of Shogya have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Maya froze as her hand stopped halfway to her canteen.
"The representatives of the Republic of Columbia have been incapacitated and extracted from the field."
Silence followed and the broadcast chime died out, leaving only the desolate empty whistling of the Wastezone wind.
Aki blinked once...
Twice...
Leona’s jaw hung completely open with her hazel eyes staring blankly at the purple clouds above.
Maya looked from Leona to Aki as her face was completely pale beneath the dust and blood.
"Wait..." Leona stammered, her voice cracking in disbelieving confusion.
"Shogya... and Columbia...?
Both of them?!"
Columbia’s armored shock-corps and Shogya’s synchronized twin-swordsmen...
Four of the most funded combat scions on the face of the Earth...
These were teams that had commanded private armies and trained in spatial simulation chambers for a decade, eliminated in the exact same eight-minute window?!
Aki’s head slowly turned.
She looked out across the vast rolling expanse of the yellow dunes, staring past the emerald jungle toward the jagged, smoking crown of the central volcanic caldera five miles away.
A tiny breathless whisper escaped Aki’s lips.
"...What in the world is Kara doing over there?"
After that singular thought, she forced the sudden image of Silas out of her mind.
In an arena like this, wandering thoughts got you gutted.
Silas had carved his way through the Umbral Basin long before she had ever laid eyes on him; whatever hell he was orchestrating miles across the basin was his business.
Her business was keeping her throat intact, holding onto her retainers, and seeing the two-hour clock bleed to zero.
Behind her, Captain Leona finished wiping the dark crust of dried blood from the corner of her split lower lip with a rough swipe of her leather bracer.
Her breath was steady now, falling back into the regular breathing of a seasoned trench scout.
She drove the broad point of her deep-sea trench-machete back into the friction-sheath strapped along her lumbar with a shlick.
"That broadcast just changed the whole board," Leona said, her hazel eyes scanning the sharp ridges of the western mesa.
"Columbia’s armored shock-corps folded and Shogya’s twin swordsmen were wiped in the exact same breath while Borealis dissolved right at our boots...
The weaklings and the loudmouths are off the grid and that leaves the real bastards."
Maya Da Silva knelt on one knee in the coarse grit, using the flat of a combat dagger to pry a jagged wedge of frozen granite from between the articulated joints of her void-ivory greaves.
She tossed the rock aside with a dull click, her dark face set into a rigid humorless grimace.
"Khemet," Maya muttered, her voice dropping into a tired tone that rasped over the dry desert wind.
"The terrain belongs to them...
You drop Tariq Al-Mansur and Safira into thousands of square miles of sun-baked dunes, and you’re basically fighting two sharks in their own blood-slicked pool.
Every grain of silica out there is an eye, a snare, or a localized kinetic spike.
If we try to push through the dunes toward the eastern basin, we won’t even see the blades that sever our Achilles tendons."
Aki nodded once, a cold certainty settling into the hollow of her chest.
She raised a gloved hand, pointing past the crumbling foothills toward a wide, snaking band of dense emerald-green jungle that followed the course of an ancient riverbed.
"Then we abandon the dunes entirely," Aki said.
"We stick to the plan.
We set up our perimeter above the Safe Zone...
Once we dismantle whatever squad is foolish enough to try camping the barrier, we break straight for the tree line."
Maya looked up from her greaves, squinting toward the thick canopy winding through the basin floor as a slow approving nod tugged at her chin.
"Smart," Maya grunted.
"None of the high houses cultivate Nature magic...
House Bloom is pure combustion and shadow-stepping while Indus relies on superheated volcanic magma and psychic compression fields.
If we pull the battlefield under that canopy, Khemet loses their infinite medium of sand, and the snipers lose their long-range sightlines."
"Sound logic, Princess," Leona chimed in, crossing her arms over the pearl-white chest plate of her prototype armor.
"Except for one glaring operational reality...
Our mounts took a two-thousand-foot header off the mountain wall when Yuri shattered the shelf.
Traversing six miles of broken badlands on foot while carrying sixty pounds of combat gear is going to eat half our stamina."
Aki turned her head, her azure eyes dropping toward the base of the shattered cliff where the avalanche had settled into a towering scree of pulverized stone.
A bitter knot formed in her stomach.
"They fell with the rock," Aki murmured with her shoulders tightening.
"Without anything to cushion the drop, the impact alone—"
Maya chuckled as she pushed herself up from the dirt, slapping the yellow grit from her thighs.
"Who told you they hit the ground?" Maya said with an arrogant grin splitting her dark features.
Aki blinked.
"What?"
Maya stepped to the edge of the shelf, planting her heavy boots right where the rock sheared away into the abyss.

She closed her eyes, rolling her neck until the vertebrae popped like firecrackers and then she extended her right hand downward with her fingers splayed wide and the Second Stage Purple Core within her chest flared with a deep violet glow.
"Trust me..."
She made a sharp upward-pulling motion with her forearm.
RUMBLE!
The base of the mountain groaned.
Two thousand feet below, in the shadowed hollow where the landslide had settled against the canyon wall, the compacted mound of shattered granite and red silt began to shift like a living mass.
The stone liquefied for three fractions of a second, parting like soft mud, and three golden-furred shapes scrambled violently out of the subterranean hollow.
"AROOOOOO!"
The Dune Wolves tore up the rocky slope, leaping from boulder to boulder with terrifying muscular agility.
Their thick coats were caked in yellow silt and powdered shale, their flanks bruised from the initial impact, but their powerful limbs were intact.
The makeshift reins Aki had braided from star-iron cord were still cinched securely behind their wide pointed ears.
The massive alpha wolf bounded up the final ledge, skidding to a halt three feet from Aki, dropping its broad snout into the dirt and letting out a low huffing whine of recognition.
"I manifested a small pocket beneath their descent while Yuri was trying to cave my face in," Maya explained, rolling her right shoulder to work out a lingering knot.

"Buried them under eight feet of loose sand to insulate them from the falling boulders, then reinforced the chamber ceiling with a stone spell... after all Frontier deployment rule number four states that you should never abandon your transport if you can build a cellar around it."

chapters.title: Chapter 562: Moving Forward [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki breathed a quiet genuine sigh of relief.
She stepped forward, reaching out with her gloved hand to run her fingers over the coarse wire-stiff fur between the alpha’s ears.
The beast leaned its heavy weight into her palm, its feral yellow eyes blinking with submissive calm.
"Thank you, Maya," Aki said softly, the tension bleeding from her shoulders as she glanced over her shoulder at Leona. "Do you have any water left?"
Leona unclipped a heavy insulated steel canteen from her harness and tossed it across the terrace.
CLACK!
Aki snatched the metal cylinder out of the air, twisted the cap with a hiss of released seal-pressure, and lifted it to her lips.
She took three deep greedy gulps of the chilled, mineral-heavy water, letting the cold rush cut through the dry, sulfurous heat coating her tongue and throat.
It cleared the chalky dust of the mountain from her lungs and grounded her pulse.

She recapped the canteen, tossed it back to Leona, and swung her left leg over the alpha wolf’s broad muscular back as her fingers gripped the coarse star-iron cords, gathering the tension until the beast’s ears snapped back in ready anticipation.
"Haaahhh..."
As the wolf stood up to its full intimidating five-foot shoulder height, Aki’s gaze drifted back toward the south.
Across the shimmering heat haze of the salt flats, far past the jagged perimeter of the central caldera, the sky remained dark, churned up by ripples of lingering mana.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
The broadcast had announced the simultaneous extermination of two major powers within an eight-minute window.
’Did Silas already run into Alexander...?’ Aki wondered, her knuckles turning white against the star-iron rope. ’Or did he tear through the perimeter just to clear the board for us?’
She didn’t have time to ponder the answer.

"Reins tight," Maya commanded, vaulting onto the back of the second wolf with a dull creak of void-ivory armor settling into place. "We drop into the western canyon, hug the shadow line of the rock wall, and push directly for the bluffs overlooking the Safe Zone... If anyone is crouching in the crags waiting for the barrier to drop, we take their heads before they even register our heat signatures."
"Understood," Aki said, leaning her torso low over the alpha’s shoulders, locking her knees against the dense muscle of its ribs.
"AROOOOOOOOOO!"

The three beasts surged forward in an explosive sprint as their clawed paws tore into the hard-packed clay, leaving gouges of red dust behind while they plunged down the switchback paths with their bodies moving like fluid golden shadows beneath the towering cliffs of Sector Forty-Four.
[Minutes Earlier]
WHOOOOOOSH... BOOOOM!
The blur tore through the low canyon first, shearing the atmosphere around them into a howling vacuum.
The sound followed a fraction of a heartbeat later... a violent, concussive boom that ripped a twelve-yard-long six-foot-deep trench straight through the sun-baked clay floor!
Marcus Vanderbilt dropped his center of gravity, throwing his entire torso violently to the right.
SKID-CRASH!
His heavy combat boots carved deep lines through the gravel as the displaced vacuum snatched at his tailored charcoal tunic, shearing the top three brass buttons clean off the fabric.
He rolled across the jagged stones, scrambled back to his feet in a frantic wide-legged crouch, his right hand slamming down onto the heavy custom-forged kinetic sidearm holstered along his hip.

"What in the hell is wrong with you?!" Marcus roared, his voice cracking with fury as he glared across the smoking trench. "We haven’t been on the ground for three minutes! You’re burning your signature draw on an opening skirmish?!"
Forty yards away, perched on the flat, elevated spine of a fractured sandstone ridge, Ren Minamoto let the single katana in his right hand settle into a lazy horizontal low-guard.
The white silk haori of the United Hegemony whipped violently around his slender frame, snapping like a war banner against the dry desert wind.
His shoulder-length black hair hung forward in loose damp strands that completely obscured his eyes, but the thin razor-sharp smirk tugging at the corner of his lips was bright and dangerous too.
The cold steel of his blade hummed with a high-pitched vibrating whine, wreathed in a crackling pale-blue film of azure lightning that licked across the edge like living wire.
...Lightning Sword.
It was the first and most foundational of the four ancestral techniques belonging to the Minamoto sword-clans of the Yamato Sector.
Ren had practiced the draw from the hour his fingers could wrap around a wooden hilt.

While other children were learning regional geography and corporate accounting, Ren was standing waist-deep in freezing mountain rapids, cutting downstream leaves in half before they could pass his shins.
When he encountered a martial artist he deemed worthy of respect, he drew both of his paired matched blades.
Against Marcus Vanderbilt? A single sword was an act of deliberate, condescending charity.
Ten yards behind Ren, seated cross-legged upon a sun-bleached granite boulder, Fang Zhao was running a silk cloth soaked in clove oil down the length of his own curved katana.
The second representative of the United Hegemony looked uninterested in the shouting match below.
His white haori was unfastened at the throat, revealing a collarbone cross-hatched with old dueling scars from the southern island trials.
His gaze was distant, drifting far past the boundaries of the Wastezone, crossing the continental divide toward the western Directorate.

’I hope Shiori is doing well in Europa...’ Fang mused silently, turning the blade slightly to catch the ambient light along the hamon line. ’The academies in the capital are filled with arrogant nobles... If one of those bastards tries to touch her hair, I’ll commandeer a military unit and cut down their whole family.’
"Oi! Fang!" Ren called out over his shoulder with his blade not wavering an inch from Marcus’s silhouette.
Fang sighed, lifting his eyes from the steel with slow exasperation.
"What is the holdup, brother? We are supposed to clear this sector, lock down the central caldera, and establish an intercept perimeter before the others consolidate themselves."
"I am adjusting our operational objectives," Ren announced, his grin splitting wider with his white teeth catching the light.
He shifted his footing, dropping his hips by two inches into a formal high-crane stance.
"I am going to face Lord Vespera."
A dead heavy silence fell over the ridge.
Down in the clay trench, Marcus Vanderbilt stared up at the swordsman as though Ren had just stripped naked and begun howling at the sun.
Fang paused his cleaning cloth in mid-air. He looked at his twin, blinking twice with utter unvarnished fatigue.

"You have completely lost your mind," Fang said flatly. "There is a broad perfectly reasonable gulf between possessing healthy martial pride and being suicidal... You crossed that gulf, built a fortress on the other side, and started planting crops."

"The old men in the capital call me the Strongest Sword of Shogya!" Ren shouted back, his laughter booming over the canyon gale. "The intelligence reports claim she is a Second Phase Gold Core! They claim she shattered a barrier over the Citadel with a flick of her wrist! If a swordsman spends twenty years cutting stones under waterfalls and never tests his edge against a sovereign, then his entire life is an empty lie! I want to taste the pressure of her blade!"
Fang rolled his eyes so violently he looked like he might pull a cranial nerve.
’Why does he sound like a Cultivation novel’s protagonist...?’

"She does not even carry a blade, you illiterate lunatic... She would crush your internal organs with raw pressure and toss you away without a thought. If she flares that Gold Core aura within fifty yards of you, your nervous system will violently reject itself and you will soil your silk trousers before your thumb can even nudge the tsuba..."
"Then I’ll cut the pressure!" Ren barked, his eyes blazing with mad electric joy behind his dark bangs.
While the two eastern swordsmen traded insults like bickering siblings on a training field, Marcus Vanderbilt’s face darkened into an ugly mottled mask of malice.
His left hand dipped slowly behind the heavy ballistic weave of his combat tunic with his fingers wrapping around a palm-sized rectangular remote crafted from matte-black carbon composite.

"You eastern primitives," Marcus whispered under his breath, his knuckles turning white as his thumb slammed down onto the red actuator button. "You stand on your rocks and talk like you own the earth. Die in the fire!"
BEEP! BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!
The entire thirty-yard expanse of the sandstone ridge erupted into an apocalyptic wall of white-hot fire.
Sixteen high-powered seismic plasma charges... planted in secret by the guards that they had bribed before the formal deployment detonated in a perfectly coordinated overlapping grid.

The concussive violence sheared the bedrock into flying razor-shards, sending a towering superheated mushroom cloud of black soot and pulverized stone roaring three hundred feet into the sky as the heat alone was enough to instantly vitrify the loose sand into black glass.
SWOOSH!
Ren Minamoto tore straight out of the heart of the fireball.
His white silk haori was singed at the hems with faint embers dancing across his shoulders but his posture was terrifyingly clean.
He cut through the smoke like a white arrow, his single katana extended forward, the azure lightning screaming along the blade as he aimed straight for Marcus’s exposed throat.
CLACK-HSSSSSSSS!
Marcus didn’t attempt to parry with steel.
The Columbian scion leaned backward, his spine curving into a deep arch as two miniature high-output combustion thrusters embedded into the heels of his combat boots ignited with deafening shrieks.
WHOOOOOOSH!

The concentrated thrust launched him vertically into the air as he rocketed thirty feet upward like a surface-to-air missile, flipping through the smoke like a ballerina while Ren’s lightning blade cleaved empty air beneath his soles.
Hovering thirty feet above the smoking crater on twin plumes of pale-blue plasma exhaust, Marcus spread his arms wide with a venomous sneer contorting his face.

"You like the hardware, sword-boy?!" Marcus shouted down, his voice carrying over the roar of the thrusters. "Custom-fabricated by Sterling Bio-Dynamics! You eastern fools spend forty years bleeding in the mud trying to cut trees! In the Republic of Columbia, the only god that matters is capital and with enough money—"
WHOOSH!

A sickly luminescent emerald mana pulsed outward from his core and from the soles of his thruster-boots, crawling up his shins, calves, thighs, as well as the torso, overlapping plates of a dark gunmetal alloy began violently expanding across his flesh.
The mechanized plating snapped together efficiently as it locked into airtight pressurized joints that glowed with internal coolant lines.
CLACK-CLACK-SHLICK!

Heavy hydraulic actuators hissed along his spine and shoulders and a reinforced star-iron faceplate slammed shut over his features with a whirring sound as two burning crimson optical visors flaring to life in the shadow of the smoke.
He wasn’t a regular Awakened anymore... he was a walking mechanized siege engine wrapped in three tons of classified ballistic alloy.
Fifty yards away, concealed in the dense shadow of a fractured boulder on the western perimeter, Talia Knox lay completely motionless in the dirt.
Columbia’s second representative had not uttered a single word since landfall.
Her breath was slow and suppressed, her right eye pressed tightly against the ocular interface of an anti-material rail-sniper.
The long fluted barrel of the weapon was charged with pressurized gravity-mana, humming at an inaudible frequency as she tracked Ren Minamoto’s landing trajectory.
’Just need to snipe him out without him noticing...’ Talia thought, that wouldn’t be that hard if she was to be honest.
His guard was completely let down.
’A little bit more...’
Her finger rested on the cold steel of the hair-trigger, her crosshairs locked dead center on the bridge of Ren’s nose...
SWOOSH!
The air pressure above her skull simply ceased to exist.
Fang Zhao dropped out of the sky directly above her prone form with his white haori settling around his shins like a funeral shroud.
His right sandal descended with the velocity of falling rubble.
CRACK!
The reinforced sole of his sandal drove the back of Talia’s skull straight through the heavy titanium receiver of her rail-sniper.

The delicate optical prisms, gravity-mana batteries, and fluted steel disintegrated into a shower of twisted springs and crushed composite glass with her forehead shattering the granite bedrock beneath the weapon.
Fang didn’t pause.
’I hate women like this...’
His heel rose and fell three more times in rapid, piston-like succession.
BOOM! CRACK! WHAM!
’What weaklings...’
Each stomp discharged seismic shockwaves that fractured the bedrock, caving in her cheekbones, shattering her orbital bones, and snapping her left collarbone like dry balsa wood.
Talia slumped sideways into the broken stones with her limbs twitching once before going limp, her consciousness extinguished as dark blood pooled around her ruined visor.
"You should be lucky I’m not trying to kill you..."
Fang stepped off her spine, shaking a wet speck of blood from his heel with his curved katana still resting undisturbed inside its wooden saya.
"Boring," Fang muttered into the dust.
Thirty feet in the air, Marcus’s red optical sensors flared as his internal feed registered the flatline of Talia’s vitals, she was really about to die.
"Useless corporate dog," Marcus snarled through his external speakers as his voice warped into a grating growl. "Couldn’t even provide five seconds of covering fire..."
CLACK-SHLICK!
The heavy alloy plates across Marcus’s pauldrons and chest snapped open, revealing two twelve-tube micro-missile pods.
The warheads inside glowed with superheated mana, arming with high-pitched electronic whines while Ren Minamoto stood in the dust below, his smile widening until his jaw muscles ached.
He brought his left hand up, gripping the hilt of his katana with both palms, sinking his weight into a deep aggressive forward stance.
"Now that is a proper target!" Ren laughed. "Let’s see if those gears of yours can turn fast enough to catch a lightning draw!"
[Author’s Note]

He rolled across the jagged stones, scrambled back to his feet in a frantic wide-legged crouch, his right hand slamming down onto the heavy custom-forged kinetic sidearm holstered along his hip.
"What in the hell is wrong with you?!" Marcus roared, his voice cracking with fury as he glared across the smoking trench.
"We haven’t been on the ground for three minutes!
You’re burning your signature draw on an opening skirmish?!"
Forty yards away, perched on the flat, elevated spine of a fractured sandstone ridge, Ren Minamoto let the single katana in his right hand settle into a lazy horizontal low-guard.
The white silk haori of the United Hegemony whipped violently around his slender frame, snapping like a war banner against the dry desert wind.
His shoulder-length black hair hung forward in loose damp strands that completely obscured his eyes, but the thin razor-sharp smirk tugging at the corner of his lips was bright and dangerous too.
The cold steel of his blade hummed with a high-pitched vibrating whine, wreathed in a crackling pale-blue film of azure lightning that licked across the edge like living wire.
...Lightning Sword.
It was the first and most foundational of the four ancestral techniques belonging to the Minamoto sword-clans of the Yamato Sector.
Ren had practiced the draw from the hour his fingers could wrap around a wooden hilt.

While other children were learning regional geography and corporate accounting, Ren was standing waist-deep in freezing mountain rapids, cutting downstream leaves in half before they could pass his shins.
When he encountered a martial artist he deemed worthy of respect, he drew both of his paired matched blades.
Against Marcus Vanderbilt?
A single sword was an act of deliberate, condescending charity.
Ten yards behind Ren, seated cross-legged upon a sun-bleached granite boulder, Fang Zhao was running a silk cloth soaked in clove oil down the length of his own curved katana.
The second representative of the United Hegemony looked uninterested in the shouting match below.
His white haori was unfastened at the throat, revealing a collarbone cross-hatched with old dueling scars from the southern island trials.
His gaze was distant, drifting far past the boundaries of the Wastezone, crossing the continental divide toward the western Directorate.

’I hope Shiori is doing well in Europa...’ Fang mused silently, turning the blade slightly to catch the ambient light along the hamon line. ’The academies in the capital are filled with arrogant nobles...
If one of those bastards tries to touch her hair, I’ll commandeer a military unit and cut down their whole family.’
"Oi!
Fang!" Ren called out over his shoulder with his blade not wavering an inch from Marcus’s silhouette.
Fang sighed, lifting his eyes from the steel with slow exasperation.
"What is the holdup, brother?
We are supposed to clear this sector, lock down the central caldera, and establish an intercept perimeter before the others consolidate themselves."
"I am adjusting our operational objectives," Ren announced, his grin splitting wider with his white teeth catching the light.
He shifted his footing, dropping his hips by two inches into a formal high-crane stance.
"I am going to face Lord Vespera."
A dead heavy silence fell over the ridge.
Down in the clay trench, Marcus Vanderbilt stared up at the swordsman as though Ren had just stripped naked and begun howling at the sun.
Fang paused his cleaning cloth in mid-air.
He looked at his twin, blinking twice with utter unvarnished fatigue.
"You have completely lost your mind," Fang said flatly.
"There is a broad perfectly reasonable gulf between possessing healthy martial pride and being suicidal...
You crossed that gulf, built a fortress on the other side, and started planting crops."
"The old men in the capital call me the Strongest Sword of Shogya!" Ren shouted back, his laughter booming over the canyon gale.
"The intelligence reports claim she is a Second Phase Gold Core!
They claim she shattered a barrier over the Citadel with a flick of her wrist!
If a swordsman spends twenty years cutting stones under waterfalls and never tests his edge against a sovereign, then his entire life is an empty lie!
I want to taste the pressure of her blade!"
Fang rolled his eyes so violently he looked like he might pull a cranial nerve.
’Why does he sound like a Cultivation novel’s protagonist...?’
"She does not even carry a blade, you illiterate lunatic...
She would crush your internal organs with raw pressure and toss you away without a thought.
If she flares that Gold Core aura within fifty yards of you, your nervous system will violently reject itself and you will soil your silk trousers before your thumb can even nudge the tsuba..."
"Then I’ll cut the pressure!" Ren barked, his eyes blazing with mad electric joy behind his dark bangs.
While the two eastern swordsmen traded insults like bickering siblings on a training field, Marcus Vanderbilt’s face darkened into an ugly mottled mask of malice.
His left hand dipped slowly behind the heavy ballistic weave of his combat tunic with his fingers wrapping around a palm-sized rectangular remote crafted from matte-black carbon composite.
"You eastern primitives," Marcus whispered under his breath, his knuckles turning white as his thumb slammed down onto the red actuator button.
"You stand on your rocks and talk like you own the earth.
Die in the fire!"
BEEP!
BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!
The entire thirty-yard expanse of the sandstone ridge erupted into an apocalyptic wall of white-hot fire.
Sixteen high-powered seismic plasma charges... planted in secret by the guards that they had bribed before the formal deployment detonated in a perfectly coordinated overlapping grid.

The concussive violence sheared the bedrock into flying razor-shards, sending a towering superheated mushroom cloud of black soot and pulverized stone roaring three hundred feet into the sky as the heat alone was enough to instantly vitrify the loose sand into black glass.
SWOOSH!
Ren Minamoto tore straight out of the heart of the fireball.
His white silk haori was singed at the hems with faint embers dancing across his shoulders but his posture was terrifyingly clean.
He cut through the smoke like a white arrow, his single katana extended forward, the azure lightning screaming along the blade as he aimed straight for Marcus’s exposed throat.
CLACK-HSSSSSSSS!
Marcus didn’t attempt to parry with steel.
The Columbian scion leaned backward, his spine curving into a deep arch as two miniature high-output combustion thrusters embedded into the heels of his combat boots ignited with deafening shrieks.
WHOOOOOOSH!

The concentrated thrust launched him vertically into the air as he rocketed thirty feet upward like a surface-to-air missile, flipping through the smoke like a ballerina while Ren’s lightning blade cleaved empty air beneath his soles.
Hovering thirty feet above the smoking crater on twin plumes of pale-blue plasma exhaust, Marcus spread his arms wide with a venomous sneer contorting his face.
"You like the hardware, sword-boy?!" Marcus shouted down, his voice carrying over the roar of the thrusters.
"Custom-fabricated by Sterling Bio-Dynamics!
You eastern fools spend forty years bleeding in the mud trying to cut trees!
In the Republic of Columbia, the only god that matters is capital and with enough money—"
WHOOSH!

A sickly luminescent emerald mana pulsed outward from his core and from the soles of his thruster-boots, crawling up his shins, calves, thighs, as well as the torso, overlapping plates of a dark gunmetal alloy began violently expanding across his flesh.
The mechanized plating snapped together efficiently as it locked into airtight pressurized joints that glowed with internal coolant lines.
CLACK-CLACK-SHLICK!

Heavy hydraulic actuators hissed along his spine and shoulders and a reinforced star-iron faceplate slammed shut over his features with a whirring sound as two burning crimson optical visors flaring to life in the shadow of the smoke.
He wasn’t a regular Awakened anymore... he was a walking mechanized siege engine wrapped in three tons of classified ballistic alloy.
Fifty yards away, concealed in the dense shadow of a fractured boulder on the western perimeter, Talia Knox lay completely motionless in the dirt.
Columbia’s second representative had not uttered a single word since landfall.
Her breath was slow and suppressed, her right eye pressed tightly against the ocular interface of an anti-material rail-sniper.
The long fluted barrel of the weapon was charged with pressurized gravity-mana, humming at an inaudible frequency as she tracked Ren Minamoto’s landing trajectory.
’Just need to snipe him out without him noticing...’ Talia thought, that wouldn’t be that hard if she was to be honest.
His guard was completely let down.
’A little bit more...’
Her finger rested on the cold steel of the hair-trigger, her crosshairs locked dead center on the bridge of Ren’s nose...
SWOOSH!
The air pressure above her skull simply ceased to exist.
Fang Zhao dropped out of the sky directly above her prone form with his white haori settling around his shins like a funeral shroud.
His right sandal descended with the velocity of falling rubble.
CRACK!
The reinforced sole of his sandal drove the back of Talia’s skull straight through the heavy titanium receiver of her rail-sniper.

The delicate optical prisms, gravity-mana batteries, and fluted steel disintegrated into a shower of twisted springs and crushed composite glass with her forehead shattering the granite bedrock beneath the weapon.
Fang didn’t pause.
’I hate women like this...’
His heel rose and fell three more times in rapid, piston-like succession.
BOOM!
CRACK!
WHAM!
’What weaklings...’
Each stomp discharged seismic shockwaves that fractured the bedrock, caving in her cheekbones, shattering her orbital bones, and snapping her left collarbone like dry balsa wood.
Talia slumped sideways into the broken stones with her limbs twitching once before going limp, her consciousness extinguished as dark blood pooled around her ruined visor.
"You should be lucky I’m not trying to kill you..."
Fang stepped off her spine, shaking a wet speck of blood from his heel with his curved katana still resting undisturbed inside its wooden saya.
"Boring," Fang muttered into the dust.
Thirty feet in the air, Marcus’s red optical sensors flared as his internal feed registered the flatline of Talia’s vitals, she was really about to die.
"Useless corporate dog," Marcus snarled through his external speakers as his voice warped into a grating growl.
"Couldn’t even provide five seconds of covering fire..."
CLACK-SHLICK!
The heavy alloy plates across Marcus’s pauldrons and chest snapped open, revealing two twelve-tube micro-missile pods.
The warheads inside glowed with superheated mana, arming with high-pitched electronic whines while Ren Minamoto stood in the dust below, his smile widening until his jaw muscles ached.
He brought his left hand up, gripping the hilt of his katana with both palms, sinking his weight into a deep aggressive forward stance.
"Now that is a proper target!" Ren laughed.
"Let’s see if those gears of yours can turn fast enough to catch a lightning draw!"

chapters.title: Chapter 563: What Are You, Ironman? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "I am going to turn your bones into ash, you eastern rat!" Marcus roared with his targeting computers locking onto Ren’s sternum..
Then...
The entire valley went completely quiet.
The screaming roar of Marcus’s jet thrusters abruptly died, choked down by a sudden suffocating shift in atmospheric pressure that dropped from the upper atmosphere like an iron ceiling.
The air grew impossibly heavy, freezing the dust particles in mid-air as a single slender hand materialized out of the empty air behind Marcus’s mechanized thruster-pack.
The fingers closed casually around the solid star-iron faceplate of Marcus’s armored helmet.
CRRRRRRRK!

The reinforced ballistic alloy... certified by Columbian military engineers to withstand direct hits from Tier-4 artillery groaned, buckling inward under the effortless casual pressure of five bare fingertips like an empty soda can.
Marcus froze in mid-air as the plasma jets beneath his heels sputtered out entirely.
He slowly twisted his armored neck to the left.
Through the cracked, flickering display of his red optical visor, he found himself staring directly into a pair of bored razor-sharp violet eyes sitting behind wire-rimmed glasses.
Kara was hovering casually in the open air, wrapped in a lazy translucent shroud of pale-green wind-mana.

Her dark hair was neatly parted, her tailored charcoal suit completely lacking any sort of dust or wrinkles, her empty left sleeve pinned neatly against her ribs, and her single right hand palming his entire armored head like a basketball.
She looked at the towering missile-laden mechanical monstrosity with an expression of exhausted pity.
"So what’s the concept here?" Kara asked, her voice becoming a flat unimpressed drawl that cut cleanly through the high-altitude wind. "You trying to be Iron Man?"
Marcus’s vocal synthesizer crackled with static.
"Iron... wha—"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Kara didn’t let him finish the syllable.
She snapped her hips in mid-air, her shoulder whipping forward with terrifying leverage, and hurled the three-ton armored chassis straight down into the bedrock like a pitcher firing a fastball.
CRASH-BOOM!
The velocity created a shockwave before the chassis even cleared twenty feet as Marcus slammed into the desert floor at a high velocity.

The concussive impact violently detonated the internal thermite fuel cells packed into his shoulder missile pods, erupting the entire mechanical suit in a massive secondary explosion of white-hot shrapnel and black smoke.
SKIDDDDDD-CRACK!

From the heart of the flaming crater, a blackened smoking human figure shot out across the dirt, tumbling violently across twenty yards of hard clay before coming to an unceremonious halt right at Ren Minamoto’s sandals.
Marcus Vanderbilt lay face-up in the grit, his armored suit completely vaporized away with his skin blistered and charred from scalp to heel as his breath was reduced to a whistling wheeze.
WHOOSH!
Before Ren could even process the sight, the emergency transponder badges pinned to Marcus and Talia’s bodies flared with white light.

The World Council’s spatial extraction runes triggered as well and in two rapid ascending pillars of pure luminescence, both Columbian representatives dissolved into thousands of shimmering motes of light, torn clean out of Sector Forty-Four by the automated salvage protocols.
Up in the air, Kara slowly drifted downward, her dress shoes touching the rim of the smoking crater with a light crunch of loose shale.
She looked down at the scorched circle of sand where Marcus had just been lying, shaking her head with deep disgust.𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦

"Is the main Vanderbilt line really that pathetic?" Kara sighed, her right hand slipping lazily into her trouser pocket. "I flew all the way across the badlands hoping for a proper warm-up, and the kid folds the second someone touches his helmet... A complete waste of good tailoring."
Ren Minamoto chuckled, flicking the blood from his katana before sliding the blade back into its lacquered scabbard with a crisp clack.

"I have to agree with you, Lord Vespera," Ren said, bowing his head with sharp respect. "The Columbians believe machines and credits can replace thirty years of drawing steel under the waterfalls... They truly have no soul."
Kara flexed her single right hand with her violet eyes sweeping across the broken ridge, ignoring the flattery.
"The one I’m actually looking for isn’t here," Kara said, her voice dropping into a colder tone.
Her gaze locked squarely onto the two white-clad swordsmen standing on the ridge. "Which means I have to deal with both of you."
She stood with her single arm hanging loose, her mind working quickly.
’These two are too dangerous to leave roaming the sector,’ Kara thought, her eyes narrowing slightly as she assessed the calmness of Ren’s breathing despite the threat.
If Aki, Maya, and Leona ran into this pair in the open badlands, it would be a massacre.
Even Maya, with all her stubborn earth-shaping grit and that void-ivory armor, wouldn’t survive three minutes against Ren Minamoto.
The aura bleeding off this guy’s posture wasn’t ordinary high-tier mana... Kara could swear she could see the experience of the blade emanate from him too.
He moved with the terrifying instinctive movements of someone who had spent his entire conscious existence with a hilt welded to his palm.
...Which wasn’t that far from the truth.
’Practicing swordsmanship since the hour he came out of the womb,’ Kara mused with a dark smirk tugging at the corners of her lips. ’Talk about atrocious parenting.’
The intelligence dossiers Evelyn had forced Silas to study back in Blessed Land had detailed the bizarre obsessive history of the Minamoto clan.
According to the imperial birth records from the Yamato Sector, Ren hadn’t cried once when he was delivered.
No matter how many times the attending midwives had struck his back, the infant hadn’t shed a single tear.

Instead, his tiny fingers had reached out from his swaddling clothes, wrapping around the polished wooden hilt of the ancestral short-blade resting in his cradle, gripping the cord so tightly that they had to oil his knuckles just to pry the weapon loose.
’That’s going to be a mild headache,’ Kara thought, shaking her head a bit.
Still, she felt a sudden surge of quiet appreciation for her friend.

’Evelyn is a lifesaver,’ Silas reflected warmly. ’Forcing me to sit down for four hours in the Keep and memorize the combat habits, core stages, and personal neuroses of every scion in this tournament was miserable at the time, but it’s paying off right now... I’ll make sure to bring her back a crate of some pastries from the upper district when this succession circus wraps up.’
Though the memory of Evelyn’s departure that morning brought a dry scowl to Kara’s face.

’Claiming she had a date,’ Silas thought, he was still unconvinced. ’What an absurd, transparent lie. Who on this green earth would voluntarily take that woman out for a romantic dinner? Her breath perpetually smells of cheap cigars, she possesses the resting temperament of an angry badger, and she spends her days hoarding hundreds of millions of credits while walking around in threadbare cardigans pretending she’s on the verge of bankruptcy. Truly... only someone who survived the slums could possibly tolerate her bullshit.’
Ren took two slow deliberate steps forward with his fingers resting lightly against the twin pommels of the katanas sheathed at his left hip.

"Draw your weapon, Lord Vespera," Ren urged, his voice dropping into a low breathless rasp of intense anticipation. "The records don’t say what your weapon is but give me the honor of facing your steel."
Kara let out a soft amused chuckle as she raised her single right hand, curling her fingers in a lazy dismissive "come-at-me" gesture.
"Give it your best shot, kid," Kara spoke, her voice dripping with effortless arrogance. "Swing with everything you have. At the end of the day... you aren’t going to leave a single scratch on me."
Ren’s eyes flashed with a mix of fury and joy.
"Don’t regret those words!"
SHIIIIING!
Ren didn’t even take a running step as his right hand vanished!
The katana cleared the scabbard in a single imperceptible fraction of a second, the friction generating a screaming blinding arc of condensed azure lightning that tore the air apart.
[Lightning Sword]!
As the blade snapped forward, Ren’s mind flashed through twenty years of agonizing bloody repetition.

Ten thousand draws a day against the falling maple leaves... Ten thousand draws an evening against the torrential monsoons of the eastern islands... He had refined this single instantaneous draw until the steel ceased to be physical metal...
It had become an unbendable law of motion.
It moved faster than sight, faster than neural reflex, cutting through barriers like dry paper.
’Die or bleed!’ Ren thought with a savage triumphant grin as the lightning blade closed the distance to her throat—
SLAP!
The sound was insultingly mundane as Kara’s single right hand had not drawn steel.

Her bare open palm simply blurred forward, intercepting the lightning-sheathed katana at the exact midpoint of its trajectory, slapping the flat of the steel with the casual dismissive motion of someone swatting away an annoying housefly.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The concussive redirection shattered the surrounding air.
The lightning slash didn’t touch her flesh as the entire attack was violently wrenched ninety degrees to the left.
The massive pale-blue lightning crescent whistled across the Wastezone, tearing three miles across the open basin before slamming squarely into the face of a granite mountain peak on the far horizon.
CRASH-SHATTER!

The entire upper third of the mountain peak disintegrated into a roaring avalanche of pulverized stone and blue sparks, collapsing into the valley below with a rumble that shook the bedrock beneath their feet.
Silence descended on the ridge once more.
Ren Minamoto stood frozen in his follow-through stance, his eyes wide as dinner plates and his breath catching so hard in his throat that he nearly choked.
Ten yards behind him, Fang Zhao’s curved blade slipped from his paralyzed fingers, clattering loudly against the rock.
Kara slowly lowered her right hand.
The palm of her hand was a bit blackened with thin wisps of pale-blue static and ozone smoke curling off her calloused skin where the lightning had made contact.
She lifted her hand, turning her palm back and forth before her eyes, inspecting the faint soot with an amused half-lidded smirk.
She looked up, meeting Ren’s completely paralyzed gaze.
"See...?" Kara drawled, flexing her unblemished fingers in the mountain breeze.
"Not even a scratch."
Ren Minamoto’s jaw remained slack, his tongue glued to the dry roof of his mouth.
The tsuka of his primary katana vibrated in his palm with a low shudder that traveled straight up the radial nerve of his forearm, rattling his collarbone.
’I still can’t believe it...’
That hadn’t been an elemental nullification field and she hadn’t summoned a spell to swallow the voltage or disperse the arc either.

She had used the bare unarmored skin of her hand, judged the exact vibrational frequency of the lightning singing through the steel, and shoved the physical vector off its track with unadorned brute strength.
"You slapped it," Ren whispered, the syllables scraping over his dry teeth like two pieces of rough slate. "You slapped away a First Strike draw with your bare hand..."
Kara White stood three paces out from the smoking trench, her right hand still held up before her face.
She turned her palm over once, inspecting the light dusting of gray soot clinging to her skin with half-lidded unimpressed eyes.
"Want me to be honest? Your edge-alignment was off by three millimeters," Kara said, letting her arm drop until her knuckles brushed the seam of her tailored trousers.

"When you draw against water, you compensate for fluid resistance... When you draw against air, you forget that heat expands the medium but you were cutting thin air and assuming the lightning would bridge the gap. That’s quite sloppy."
Ren’s throat bobbed.

A violent twitching flush crawled up from his collar, burning through his pale skin as the pride cultivated across twenty years of undefeated sparring bouts in the high stone pavilions of the Yamato Sector flared white-hot in his sternum.
CLACK!
His left hand dropped to the second scabbard resting along his sash and he drew his second blade.

The twin katanas crossed before his chest, their tips humming in mana as the pale-blue lightning coating the primary steel deepened, bleeding into an aggressive violet that kicked up loose shale around his sandals.
The wind whipped his dark bangs back from his eyes, revealing pupils dilated with focus.
"Fang!" Ren shouted without breaking eye contact with the woman in the charcoal suit. "Get your ass off the rock! We take her together or we don’t leave this canyon!"
Ten yards away, Fang Zhao kicked his scabbard upright with the toe of his sandal, catching the polished lacquered wood in mid-air with his left hand.
His face had lost every trace of its earlier sleepy boredom. The muscles along his scarred neck were drawn taut like bowstrings and his dark eyes fixed dead center on Kara’s chest.
"I told you she was an anomaly," Fang said, his voice dropping into a tight whisper.
He slid his left foot back, settling his weight into a wide, low-slung stance.
"You never listen to the scout reports... You just hear ’Gold Core’ and start foaming at the mouth like a rabid street hound."
"Shut up and draw!" Ren snarled.
Fang drew.
SHSHSHSHICK!

Kara let out a soft amused chuckle as she raised her single right hand, curling her fingers in a lazy dismissive "come-at-me" gesture.
"Give it your best shot, kid," Kara spoke, her voice dripping with effortless arrogance.
"Swing with everything you have.
At the end of the day... you aren’t going to leave a single scratch on me."
Ren’s eyes flashed with a mix of fury and joy.
"Don’t regret those words!"
SHIIIIING!
Ren didn’t even take a running step as his right hand vanished!
The katana cleared the scabbard in a single imperceptible fraction of a second, the friction generating a screaming blinding arc of condensed azure lightning that tore the air apart.
[Lightning Sword]!
As the blade snapped forward, Ren’s mind flashed through twenty years of agonizing bloody repetition.
Ten thousand draws a day against the falling maple leaves...
Ten thousand draws an evening against the torrential monsoons of the eastern islands...
He had refined this single instantaneous draw until the steel ceased to be physical metal...
It had become an unbendable law of motion.
It moved faster than sight, faster than neural reflex, cutting through barriers like dry paper.
’Die or bleed!’ Ren thought with a savage triumphant grin as the lightning blade closed the distance to her throat—
SLAP!
The sound was insultingly mundane as Kara’s single right hand had not drawn steel.

Her bare open palm simply blurred forward, intercepting the lightning-sheathed katana at the exact midpoint of its trajectory, slapping the flat of the steel with the casual dismissive motion of someone swatting away an annoying housefly.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The concussive redirection shattered the surrounding air.
The lightning slash didn’t touch her flesh as the entire attack was violently wrenched ninety degrees to the left.
The massive pale-blue lightning crescent whistled across the Wastezone, tearing three miles across the open basin before slamming squarely into the face of a granite mountain peak on the far horizon.
CRASH-SHATTER!

The entire upper third of the mountain peak disintegrated into a roaring avalanche of pulverized stone and blue sparks, collapsing into the valley below with a rumble that shook the bedrock beneath their feet.
Silence descended on the ridge once more.
Ren Minamoto stood frozen in his follow-through stance, his eyes wide as dinner plates and his breath catching so hard in his throat that he nearly choked.
Ten yards behind him, Fang Zhao’s curved blade slipped from his paralyzed fingers, clattering loudly against the rock.
Kara slowly lowered her right hand.
The palm of her hand was a bit blackened with thin wisps of pale-blue static and ozone smoke curling off her calloused skin where the lightning had made contact.
She lifted her hand, turning her palm back and forth before her eyes, inspecting the faint soot with an amused half-lidded smirk.
She looked up, meeting Ren’s completely paralyzed gaze.
"See...?" Kara drawled, flexing her unblemished fingers in the mountain breeze.
"Not even a scratch."
Ren Minamoto’s jaw remained slack, his tongue glued to the dry roof of his mouth.
The tsuka of his primary katana vibrated in his palm with a low shudder that traveled straight up the radial nerve of his forearm, rattling his collarbone.
’I still can’t believe it...’
That hadn’t been an elemental nullification field and she hadn’t summoned a spell to swallow the voltage or disperse the arc either.

She had used the bare unarmored skin of her hand, judged the exact vibrational frequency of the lightning singing through the steel, and shoved the physical vector off its track with unadorned brute strength.
"You slapped it," Ren whispered, the syllables scraping over his dry teeth like two pieces of rough slate.
"You slapped away a First Strike draw with your bare hand..."
Kara White stood three paces out from the smoking trench, her right hand still held up before her face.
She turned her palm over once, inspecting the light dusting of gray soot clinging to her skin with half-lidded unimpressed eyes.
"Want me to be honest?
Your edge-alignment was off by three millimeters," Kara said, letting her arm drop until her knuckles brushed the seam of her tailored trousers.
"When you draw against water, you compensate for fluid resistance...
When you draw against air, you forget that heat expands the medium but you were cutting thin air and assuming the lightning would bridge the gap.
That’s quite sloppy."
Ren’s throat bobbed.

A violent twitching flush crawled up from his collar, burning through his pale skin as the pride cultivated across twenty years of undefeated sparring bouts in the high stone pavilions of the Yamato Sector flared white-hot in his sternum.
CLACK!
His left hand dropped to the second scabbard resting along his sash and he drew his second blade.

The twin katanas crossed before his chest, their tips humming in mana as the pale-blue lightning coating the primary steel deepened, bleeding into an aggressive violet that kicked up loose shale around his sandals.
The wind whipped his dark bangs back from his eyes, revealing pupils dilated with focus.
"Fang!" Ren shouted without breaking eye contact with the woman in the charcoal suit.
"Get your ass off the rock!
We take her together or we don’t leave this canyon!"
Ten yards away, Fang Zhao kicked his scabbard upright with the toe of his sandal, catching the polished lacquered wood in mid-air with his left hand.
His face had lost every trace of its earlier sleepy boredom.
The muscles along his scarred neck were drawn taut like bowstrings and his dark eyes fixed dead center on Kara’s chest.
"I told you she was an anomaly," Fang said, his voice dropping into a tight whisper.
He slid his left foot back, settling his weight into a wide, low-slung stance.
"You never listen to the scout reports...
You just hear ’Gold Core’ and start foaming at the mouth like a rabid street hound."
"Shut up and draw!" Ren snarled.
Fang drew.
SHSHSHSHICK!

chapters.title: Chapter 564: Two Brothers Against A Wall [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: His katana didn’t ignite with lightning, but that was something Kara already expected, it pulled the sound clean out of the immediate airspace.
A vacuum field formed along Fang’s cutting edge, wrapping the steel in an invisible high-velocity atmospheric blade that tore trenches into the rock beneath his feet.
The dust hovering in the air between them was sucked toward the steel, sliced into powder, and expelled in a whistling spiral.
"Wooh..."
These were two very distinct styles in this battle with the first being Ren’s explosive lightning and Fang’s soundless vacuum.
Kara looked between the two of them with her wire-rimmed glasses catching the harsh glare of the purple sky.

"Two swords for the loud one, one for the quiet one," Kara muttered, her mouth twitching into a sharp mocking grin. "Cute... Let me guess, you two have some synchronized twin formation that took five years of monastery beatings to master? Come on, then. Show me what the United Hegemony Of Shogya considers elite before I fall asleep on my feet."
Ren lunged first.
BOOM!
The sandstone beneath his sandals ruptured into gravel as he detonated his Second Stage core.
He crossed thirty yards in the span of seconds as his twin katanas blurred into a violent intersecting cross of violet lightning.
’Rushing Thunderstorm!’
The blades came in high and low simultaneously... the primary aiming for the carotid artery on her right side while the secondary cutting a brutal horizontal arc toward her floating ribs.
The lightning screeched like a thousand dying birds, superheating the air between them to five hundred degrees in a fraction of a second.
SWOOSH!

Kara stepped in, she leaned her upper torso forward by three inches, letting the high lightning arc scream over her head, shearing off three loose strands of her dark hair, while her right hand blurred downward.
SMACK!
Her open palm struck the flat of Ren’s lower blade just below the habaki, killing the weapon’s rotational torque before the edge could bite into her suit.
"Too wide!" Kara grinned with her face inches from his. "Your left shoulder is dipping! Who taught you to drop your elbow on a low cut, your grandmother?!"
Ren’s eyes bulged with rage with his spit flying across the gap.
"DIE!"
He twisted his wrists to reverse the grip—
SHIIIIING!
From the blind spot behind Kara’s pinned left sleeve, Fang materialized like a ghost.

He had moved without a sound, sliding across the sand on the crest of his vacuum currents as his blade came in from below in an upward diagonal slash aimed straight through Kara’s left armpit, moving with zero atmospheric drag making it completely silent.
’Vacuum Sword... Rising Gale!’
The invisible air-blade whistled through the space where Kara’s ribs were anchored.
SNAP!
Kara didn’t turn her head.
Her Second Phase Gold Core pulsed once and a ripple of pure gravitational pressure detonated from her left shoulder.
WHAM!
The invisible vacuum blade shattered against the wall as the backlash traveled down the steel, sending an acoustic shockwave into Fang’s wrist that popped his radial joint with a sickening sound.
"Gah!" Fang grunted through clenched teeth with his foot skidding across the sand as the impact pushed him back three paces.
"Nice timing, terrible penetration!" Kara shouted, spinning on her right heel. "Eh, I didn’t mean it that way!"
Her right leg whipped around in a vicious horizontal roundhouse kick that tore through the air with a concussive crack.
WHOOSH!
Ren threw both katanas up in an emergency cross-guard to intercept the strike.
BOOOOOOM!

The force of the kick slammed into the steel with the shockwave blowing the white haori off Ren’s shoulders and driving him backward fifteen yards across the dirt, his sandals tearing two deep smoking trenches through the hard clay.
"Ren!" Fang shouted, his left hand immediately weaving an intricate one-handed somatic sign while his injured right wrist adjusted its grip on the katana.
"Vacuum Sword: Gale-Sphere Snare!"
HSSSSSSSS!

The air around Kara’s boots suddenly turned into a swirling high-pressure atmospheric vortex as the air molecules compressed, locking her lower legs in an invisible vice of descending pressure designed to anchor high-mobility combatants to the earth.
"Hold her!" Ren roared, charging back into the fray with his face covered in sweat and dust.

His twin blades blurred into an unrecognizable storm of violet arcs as he threw attacks... ten slashes, twenty slashes, thirty slashes per second, descending upon Kara from every conceivable angle like an executioner’s iron cage.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
Kara didn’t break the snare with brute force.
Her violet eyes narrowed behind her glasses as the moisture in the dry canyon air suddenly responded to her core.
Within the ocular channels of her own eyes, a fine microscopic film of water-mana began to circulate, cycling with extreme precision.
’Surprisingly I still haven’t shown Morwenna...’
She took a deep breath watching the attacks coming for her.
’Tidal-Blade Arts: Second Style... Rip-Current Perception.’
The world slowed to a crawl.
By rooting the technique directly within the moisture of her own eyes, the scorching heat radiating from Ren’s violet lightning didn’t blur her vision.
It didn’t warp the reading into flickering useless wisps like it had against Morrighan.
’I’m glad I got a better version of this technique... Truly that Mafia arc wasn’t a waste of time, completely.’
Instead, glowing razor-sharp blue current lines snapped into existence across the dusty air.

She saw the micro-twitch in Ren’s right pectoral two tenths of a second before the blade moved and she saw the minute shift in Fang’s center of gravity as he maintained the gale-snare fifteen paces away.
She saw the exact trajectory of every single strike before the steel even cleared the arc.
To the twins, it looked like horrifying witchcraft as Kara’s right hand moved in small increments.
TAP! SLAP! WHOOSH!
Kara batted some of the strikes away by the flats as she then tilted her chin by half an inch, letting a violet lightning bolt scrape the air beside her ear.
She leaned her shoulder two millimeters to the left, letting a vacuum blade graze the empty fabric of her pinned sleeve.
Every single strike missed her flesh by the width of a single hair...
"What is this?!" Ren screamed, his veins bulging against his temples as he swung with everything his lungs had left. "You’re not even looking at the blades! How are you reading this?!"

"Because you’re telegraphing like a billboard, sweetheart!" Kara laughed, leaning back to let a double overhead chop whistle harmlessly past her nose. "You inhale every time you commit to a heavy thrust! You tighten your toes before a low sweep! A blind dog from the slums could read your footwork!"
CLACK!
Kara reached into the void of her personal storage and a flash of pale gray light erupted from her right palm.
When her fingers closed, she wasn’t empty-handed anymore.
She held a four-foot-long single-edged arming sword forged by Thora. It was a new one made specifically for this form...
"You wanted me to use a sword?" Kara’s voice dropped into a dark whisper that sent a cold shudder down Ren’s spine. "Here’s your sword."
Fang’s eyes widened in horror from the perimeter. "Ren! Break off! BREAK OFF!"
...It was too late.
Kara’s Second Phase core surged.
A dense suffocating film of phantom heavy-water erupted along the matte-gray steel of the blade, wrapping the metal in a translucent fluid mantle that weighed more than twenty tons of solid lead.
Kara swung.
BOOOOM!
The void-blade met Ren’s descending twin katanas mid-air and the mass behind Kara’s strike didn’t just stop the swords... it violently pulverized the violet lightning into non-existence.
The concussive water pressure blew through Ren’s guard like a breaking tsunami, snapping the blade of his secondary katana clean in half with an ear-splitting crack.
WHAM!
The flat of the heavy-water blade slammed into Ren’s chest, caving his ribs in and blasting him fifty yards horizontally across the salt flats.
WHOOSH!
He skipped across the hard-packed clay four times, coughing up plumes of blood and shattered enamel, before crashing into the base of a shattered boulder.
"Ren!" Fang screamed.
The quiet twin didn’t hesitate since he knew his brother was down and he knew the gap in strength was an uncrossable abyss but the discipline of the Shogunate Isles was absolute.
Fang dropped his katana into a two-handed reverse grip, channeling every remaining drop of his Blue Core into the steel.
’Vacuum Sword... Heaven’s Eye.’
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!

A sixty-foot-wide cyclone of pressurized razor-sharp vacuum blades erupted from Fang’s stance, tearing the bedrock into millions of flying shrapnel shards as the storm converged directly on Kara’s flank.
The sound was deafening like a high-frequency shriek that shattered every loose stone within fifty yards but Kara didn’t even look at the cyclone.
"Annoying~"
She turned her body with her right arm coiling back like a loaded ballista.

The Rip-Current Perception running through the moisture of her eyes highlighted a single thin blue filament running through the exact eye of the vacuum storm... the microscopic pressure fault where Fang was anchoring the spell with his breathing.
"Once again, you really have a good technique," Kara muttered. "It’s just a terrible foundation."
She took another deep breath.
’Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style... Severing Horizon!’
Kara released the coil.
Her hips snapped forward with explosive leverage and the blade swept through the air in a clean horizontal three-hundred-and-sixty-degree arc.
BOOOM!
A thirty-foot-wide crescent-shaped wave of roaring pale-blue phantom heavy-water detonated from the blade’s edge.
The tidal crescent violently obliterated the cyclone as the mass of twenty thousand gallons of pressurized water smashed through Fang’s wind-blades, scattering the storm like dry autumn leaves.
Fang’s eyes widened in paralyzed disbelief as the thirty-foot tidal wave bore down on him.
CRASH!

The heavy-water wave slammed squarely into Fang’s chest and the shockwave crushed his sternum, blew his katana from his pulverized fingers while hammering him fifty yards backward into the solid granite wall of the canyon.
BOOM!
Fang hit the rock face, coughing out a massive spray of dark blood with his eyes rolling back into his skull as his legs crumpled beneath him.
He slumped against the stone, critically injured with his breathing reduced to a shallow broken whistle.
...He was completely out of the fight.

Kara flicked the blade, sending a fine sheet of phantom water spraying off the edge to patter against the dry dirt as she turned her head slowly, looking across the scarred clearing toward the boulder where the other twin was struggling.
"One down," Kara called out with her voice echoing off the canyon walls. "You still want to taste the steel, Strongest Sword?"
From behind the shattered boulder, fifty paces away, a ragged, choking gasp sounded.
Ren Minamoto dragged himself upright.
His white silk haori was torn to shreds, drenched in dark red blood that soaked through the linen from his fractured ribs.
The broken half of his secondary katana lay abandoned in the dust ten yards behind him, but his right hand was still locked around the hilt of his primary blade.
His knuckles were chalk-white with the skin split and bleeding across his joints.
He spat a thick globule of gore onto the sand, his chest heaving in violent agonizing spasms.
"Not... yet..." Ren wheezed, his voice trembling with a mixture of agony and obsession that bordered on madness. "The Heir... does not yield to a single arm..."
Kara scoffed, resting the flat of the heavy void-blade against her shoulder.
"You’re fighting with four broken ribs, an internal hemorrhage, and half your teeth missing, kid. Sit down before you drown in your own blood."
Ren didn’t sit down.
His eyes, sunken and bloodshot behind his tangled hair, suddenly rolled back into his head.
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The violet lightning coating his blade died out completely as instead, the space surrounding his body began to subtly warp, like the heat haze rising off an asphalt road at noon.
The katana in his hand seemed to flicker, its physical outline blurring until the steel looked semi-transparent, vibrating at a frequency so high that the human ear couldn’t register the sound.
’Minamoto Secret Art... Third Style... Void-Severing Mirage.’
Kara’s brows lifted slightly behind her wire-rimmed glasses.

’Invisible slashes,’ Kara noted, her grip shifting slightly along the hilt of the blade. ’He’s not projecting mana outward... He’s vibrating the steel at the frequency of the local fabric of space as the cuts travel through the atmospheric seam before the visual light catches up.’
Once again, it was something that she had studied.
"DIE!" Ren screamed, his voice cracking into a raw bloody screech and he swung!
There was no sound.
SHLICK!

A three-inch laceration suddenly appeared across the right shoulder of Kara’s tailored suit jacket as the fine charcoal wool parted cleanly with a thin hair-line crimson scratch blooming across her skin.
SHLICK! SHLICK!
Two more invisible cuts whistled through the air! One grazed the side of her collar while the other severed a clean slice of fabric from the hem of her trousers.
Kara’s eyes widened slightly.
’Fast,’ Silas thought, the adrenaline finally surging with genuine, focused sharpness. ’The guy actually has some teeth.’
Ren was moving forward in a limping charge, swinging the flickering blade with everything his dying stamina possessed.
SWISH-SWISH-SWISH!
Ten invisible slashes tore through the space around her as every swing was aimed at a lethal biological junction... her throat, her femoral artery and her remaining eye!
The attacks were completely invisible to mundane vision, cutting through the air with zero telegraphs so Kara had to actively give ground.
She took three rapid, evasive steps backward, her boots carving lines through the gravel as she twisted her torso to dodge the unseen edges.
A cut whistled past her cheek, severing another lock of hair while another sliced across the back of her wrist, drawing a thin bead of dark blood.
Up in the mezzanine of the Great Assembly Chamber, the delegates were leaning forward with their breaths caught in their throats.
"He’s landing hits!" an Indus minister shouted. "The Minamoto heir is pushing the Gold Core back!"
[Author’s Note]

"Not... yet..." Ren wheezed, his voice trembling with a mixture of agony and obsession that bordered on madness.
"The Heir... does not yield to a single arm..."
Kara scoffed, resting the flat of the heavy void-blade against her shoulder.
"You’re fighting with four broken ribs, an internal hemorrhage, and half your teeth missing, kid.
Sit down before you drown in your own blood."
Ren didn’t sit down.
His eyes, sunken and bloodshot behind his tangled hair, suddenly rolled back into his head.
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The violet lightning coating his blade died out completely as instead, the space surrounding his body began to subtly warp, like the heat haze rising off an asphalt road at noon.
The katana in his hand seemed to flicker, its physical outline blurring until the steel looked semi-transparent, vibrating at a frequency so high that the human ear couldn’t register the sound.
’Minamoto Secret Art...
Third Style...
Void-Severing Mirage.’
Kara’s brows lifted slightly behind her wire-rimmed glasses.
’Invisible slashes,’ Kara noted, her grip shifting slightly along the hilt of the blade. ’He’s not projecting mana outward...
He’s vibrating the steel at the frequency of the local fabric of space as the cuts travel through the atmospheric seam before the visual light catches up.’
Once again, it was something that she had studied.
"DIE!" Ren screamed, his voice cracking into a raw bloody screech and he swung!
There was no sound.
SHLICK!

A three-inch laceration suddenly appeared across the right shoulder of Kara’s tailored suit jacket as the fine charcoal wool parted cleanly with a thin hair-line crimson scratch blooming across her skin.
SHLICK!
SHLICK!
Two more invisible cuts whistled through the air!
One grazed the side of her collar while the other severed a clean slice of fabric from the hem of her trousers.
Kara’s eyes widened slightly.
’Fast,’ Silas thought, the adrenaline finally surging with genuine, focused sharpness. ’The guy actually has some teeth.’
Ren was moving forward in a limping charge, swinging the flickering blade with everything his dying stamina possessed.
SWISH-SWISH-SWISH!
Ten invisible slashes tore through the space around her as every swing was aimed at a lethal biological junction... her throat, her femoral artery and her remaining eye!
The attacks were completely invisible to mundane vision, cutting through the air with zero telegraphs so Kara had to actively give ground.
She took three rapid, evasive steps backward, her boots carving lines through the gravel as she twisted her torso to dodge the unseen edges.
A cut whistled past her cheek, severing another lock of hair while another sliced across the back of her wrist, drawing a thin bead of dark blood.
Up in the mezzanine of the Great Assembly Chamber, the delegates were leaning forward with their breaths caught in their throats.
"He’s landing hits!" an Indus minister shouted.
"The Minamoto heir is pushing the Gold Core back!"
