chapters.title: Chapter 565: Ren’s Final Blade [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Down in the canyon, Ren’s face split into a bloody triumphant sneer.
"CAN YOU SEE THEM?! CAN YOU READ THE VOID, LORD VESPERA?!"
Kara stopped retreating as her boots dug into the dirt, grinding her momentum to a halt.
"I don’t need to see the void," Kara’s voice rang out.
Within her eyes, the moisture channels pulsed with azure intensity.
The Rip-Current Perception didn’t look for the invisible steel... It looked at Ren’s hands.
It read the tension in the flexor tendons of his wrist and it read the micro-shift in the alignment of his metacarpals too.
She could sense space since she had started learning it from Thor and even used it but it was a whole lot of stress and burned a lot of mana... This was much better.
Every time his muscles coiled to release the spatial vibration, the blue current lines mapped the exact angle of the blade three fractions of a second before the cut was born.
’Three cuts high... One cut low and two seconds of recovery between the spatial pulses.’
Kara caught the rhythm.
CLANG!
Her blade blurred forward, intercepting an invisible slash four inches from her throat with the impact rang out like a church bell.
CLANG! CLANG!
Two more unseen strikes were batted aside with effortless precision as the sparks detonated in empty air, illuminating the invisible seams of the spatial vibration.
Ren’s sneer froze and his pupils contracted in horror.
"No..." Ren stammered with his arms trembling violently as he tried to reverse the momentum. "That’s... that’s impossible..."

"Your rhythm is predictable," Kara said, stepping straight into his guard. "Three heavy swings, a pause to breathe through your punctured lung, and a low sweep to cover your retreat... You’ve been doing the exact same sequence since the first clash on the ridge."
WHAM!
Kara’s forehead drove forward in a brutal headbutt straight into the bridge of Ren’s nose.
CRUNCH!
Blood exploded across both their faces.
Ren stumbled backward with his vision flashing white and his grip on the katana nearly slipping as his brain rattled against his skull.
"Gah—!"
He fell back five paces with his breath coming in dry strangulated sobs and his body trembling so violently that he could barely keep his knees from buckling.
Every single technique had failed.
...The Lightning Sword had been slapped away like a toy... The Twin Heavens had been shattered into scrap... The Void-Severing Mirage had been read like a children’s picture book...
He was standing on the edge of the grave with his core flickering like a dying candle and his body screaming for unconsciousness.
Yet... there was one more.
The fourth and final style.
The forbidden technique of House Minamoto... an art that demanded the caster burn their own life-force to ignite their soul pathways.
Ren slowly lifted his head.
The blood running from his shattered nose and split forehead covered his face in a grotesque crimson mask, but his eyes burned with a terrifying luminescence.
"If I die here..." Ren whispered, his voice shaking with mad poetry, "...then let my soul become the blade that cuts the sky."
’Truly they do sound like cultivators...’
The entire Wastezone seemed to violently contract as Ren’s Purple Core cracked.

A pillar of pitch-black and violet lightning erupted from his sternum, roaring two hundred feet into the bruised clouds as the violence of the ascension blew the surrounding boulders into dust, melting the sand within thirty yards into bubbling black glass.
"Minamoto Ultimate Secret Art... Fourth Style... Falling Heaven, Severed God!"
The entire sky above the canyon turned purple as Ren held his katana with both hands, lifting the steel high above his head.
The blade was no longer metal... it had become a colossal, eighty-foot-tall lance of concentrated screaming lightning that warped the dimensional fabric around its edges.
It was an attack capable of leveling what he wanted... An attack that poured twenty-two years of obsession, pain, and blood into a single stroke.
"LORD VESPERA!" Ren screamed, his vocal cords tearing and vomiting blood with every syllable! "WITNESS THE STRONGEST SWORD OF SHOGYA!"
He brought the lightning blade down with everything his existence possessed.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOMMMM!
The sky split and the canyon floor cleaved in two as Kara stood beneath the falling cataclysm.
’Are we in an anime...? How did he randomly manage to get enough power to do this?’
However she didn’t run as she lowered her blade until the matte-gray steel pointed toward the earth and her Second Phase Gold Core finally glowed.
’Mine won’t be as action-packed as this but I guess I can release as much power as I can...’
The water in the air didn’t vaporize under the lightning as it submitted to Kara’s will instead.

Millions of gallons of atmospheric moisture condensed in a microsecond, wrapping around Kara’s void-blade in a spiraling roaring drill of deep heavy-water that turned as black as the deep ocean trenches.
"Tidal-Blade Arts... First Style... Severing Horizon!"
Kara swung upward.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The collision crated several shockwaves across the entire southern hemisphere of Sector Forty-Four as the eighty-foot lightning blade struck the heavy-water crescent!
For one agonizing fraction of a second, the two forces hung suspended in mid-air with the desperate burning life-force of a young prodigy clashing against the ocean of a monster.
Then... the lightning broke as the heavy-water wave tore through the black lightning like a cleaver through paper.

The concussive shockwave blasted upward into the clouds, blowing a two-mile-wide hole straight through the purple sky, while the downward backwash drove Ren Minamoto’s katana from his hands, shattering the steel into a hundred glowing smoking fragments that rained down across the desert floor.
SHATTER!
The storm died instantly and the dust settled too as Ren Minamoto stood in the center of the smoking glass crater.
His hands were empty as his arms hung limply at his sides with the skin blackened and burned down to the meat while his white haori completely incinerated away.
He stared at his empty trembling palms.
Then...
THUD!
His knees gave out beneath him.
Ren hit the scorched glass with his hands resting on his thighs and his head hanging low between his shoulders.
A strange wet sound broke from his throat.
Hiccup!
Ren froze.
Another sound followed.
A tight choked gasp that tore through his broken chest, followed by a hot salty drop of liquid that fell from his chin, splattering against the black glass between his knees.
Drip!
Ren blinked, staring at the wet drop in uncomprehending bewilderment.
’What... what is this...?’
He reached up with a trembling, blackened finger, touching the wet trail running down his cheek.
Tears... that was what it was, Ren Minamoto was crying... He had never cried in his entire conscious existence.

Not when the midwives struck him at birth, not when his father drove wooden bokkens into his ribs until he coughed blood at six years old and not when his flesh was cleaved to the bone during the island trials at fourteen.
He had been taught that tears were the ultimate failure which was the mark of a broken spirit and a pathetic disgusting display of weakness.
And now, on a live international broadcast feed with over 1.4 billion people watching across nine continents...
He was sobbing like a terrified, abandoned child.
"I... I..." Ren choked, his shoulders heaving as the tears poured freely down his bloody face and his voice cracked into a high-pitched pathetic wail. "Why... why can’t I... why wasn’t it enough...?"
He looked up, his tear-filled eyes meeting Kara’s unblinking violet gaze.

"I gave everything..." Ren wept with his hands clawing at the glass. "Twenty years... every day... I cut until my hands bled... I never slept... I never lived... and I couldn’t even make you draw your second arm..."
Kara stood five paces away with her single arm hanging loose at her side and the blade resting point-down in the dirt but she didn’t laugh and she didn’t deliver a cruel cutting one-liner either.
She stood in silence, letting the young swordsman weep.
Kara let him sit in the dirt and bleed out every ounce of repressed, suffocating grief that twenty years of conditioning had beaten into his marrow.

She knew what bad parenting looked like since she had seen enough broken children in her past life to recognize a boy who had been forged into a weapon before he ever had the chance to be a human being.
’Ah... all nobles are bad parents, huh?’
For two full minutes, the only sound in the canyon was Ren’s raw weeping.
Finally, when the sobs began to subside into shuddering, exhausted hiccups...
Kara took two slow steps forward.
"You fought well, Ren." Kara said softly and Ren’s tear-stained face lifted slightly.
WHAM!
Kara’s heavy combat boot buried itself directly into Ren’s solar plexus with concussive force.
"GAH!"
Ren coughed out a geyser of blood with his eyes rolling back into his skull as the kick blasted him thirty yards backward across the crater.
SKID-CRASH!
He hit the base of the canyon wall, slumping sideways into the rubble beside his brother, completely unconscious.
WHOOSH!
The emergency transponders pinned to Ren and Fang’s collars flared with blinding light as the spatial extraction runes ignited in unison.

In two towering pillars of pure white luminescence, the bodies of the Shogya twins dissolved into thousands of shimmering motes of light, surging into the upper clouds as the World Council’s recovery relays tore them out of the Sovereign Realm.
The United Hegemony of Shogya was officially wiped from the board and silence returned to the canyon.
Kara let out a long exhale through her nose, shaking the residual numbness from her right wrist.
She dismissed the blade back into her personal storage with a hum of gray light, then reached up, carefully adjusting the bridge of her wire-rimmed glasses.
She looked around the vast scorched crater, assessing the shattered stone and vitrified glass.

’Good swordsmen,’ Silas thought, rolling his right shoulder until the joint popped with a dull thud. ’Both of them... If they survive the core backlash from today, they’ll be terrifying monsters in ten years.’
She paused, her brow furrowing slightly as her gaze swept across the empty horizons of the Wastezone.
’But that aside...’
Silas frowned.
’...where the hell is Alexander?’
She closed her eyes, expanding her sensory perimeter across a four-mile radius.
...Nothing.
The Crown Prince’s oppressive arrogant mana signature was completely absent from his senses.
For a man who had publicly demanded Star-Iron Suppression Rings just to prove he could butcher her at an equal core stage, he was suspiciously quiet.
"Cowardly little prick," Kara muttered under her breath. "Probably hiding in the high crags waiting for the sudden-death compression."
She looked over toward a massive flat-topped granite boulder that had survived the lightning bombardment.
The stone was smooth, sun-warmed, and shaded from the harsh glare of the upper rift.
"Whatever," Kara sighed, walking toward the rock with heavy, dragging steps. "I’ll find him when the time comes."
She hopped up onto the flat boulder, brushed a few loose pebbles off the surface, and sprawled out on her back with a long groan of exhaustion.
Kara crossed her legs, resting her single right hand behind her head, staring up at the purple clouds.
"After I rest for ten minutes..." Kara mumbled to herself with her eyelids fluttering half-shut.
Silas let out a soft self-deprecating grunt.

’Turning into a woman makes me absurdly lazy for some reason,’ Silas mused, feeling the warm desert breeze ruffle his dark bangs. ’Or does this disguise have a distinct irritating personality of its own that amplifies every time I slip into her skin...? First the craving for sweets and wine, now the urge to take a nap in the middle of an active war zone. How ridiculous.’
Within thirty seconds, her breathing slowed to a soft one, completely unbothered by the fact that elite nobles were still hunting each other across the sector.
Miles to the east, deep within the shifting yellow ocean of the Great Dunes...
The air was suffocatingly hot, thick with the dry choking reek of fine silica.
Two figures moved through the crests of the sand with their silhouettes completely invisible to mundane eyes.
From head to toe, Prince Tariq Al-Mansur and Lady Safira were encased in dense shifting mantles of yellow quartz sand that matched the exact coloration and temperature of the surrounding dunes.
The sand clung to their skin, their bronze scale-mail, and their weapons like living chitin, masking their heat signatures and dampening their mana pathways to microscopic whispers.
Beneath the sand-shroud, Tariq crawled along the crest of a ninety-foot dune, his liquid-gold eyes scanning the shimmering heat haze of the salt flats below.
Every three paces, he dipped his fingers into the dune, injecting tiny hair-thin filaments of earth mana into the silica beneath them.

Deep beneath the surface, thirty interconnected Sand-Viper Snares were already primed and waiting... quicksand sinkholes packed with compressed quartz spikes that would swallow and impale any squad attempting to cross this part.
"The perimeter is set," Safira whispered, her voice carrying the dry hiss of sliding sand.
She knelt beside him, her curved khopesh resting across her thighs and her serpent-silk robes blending seamlessly with the ridge.
"If the Albion duelists push through this ravine, the sinkhole will snap their femurs before they can draw their rapiers."
Tariq nodded, his jaw set in a cold brutal grimace.

"And if House Bloom tries to flank through the low flats," Tariq added, his eyes narrowing, "the quartz spikes will pierce their boots and we don’t engage in fair duels... We let the desert drink their blood, we harvest their transponder badges, and we secure the eastern point."
Safira paused, her kohl-lined eyes shifting toward the far western mountains where the thunderous booms of Kara’s clashes had just died down.
A faint uneasy tremor touched her voice.
"And... what about Kara White?" Safira asked quietly. "What do we do if the Lord of Blessed Land turns toward the dunes?"𝑓𝓇𝘦ℯ𝘸𝘦𝑏𝓃𝑜𝘷ℯ𝑙.𝑐𝑜𝓂
Tariq froze.

chapters.title: Chapter 566: House Bloom Hunts [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The image of the severed head dissolving into black sand inside their Citadel quarters flashed violently behind his eyelids, sending a cold nauseating chill through his gut.
He stayed silent for five agonizing seconds, staring down at his sand-covered palms.
Then, he forced a low mocking scoff through his teeth.

"Kara White is an anomaly, Safira," Tariq said, his voice gaining false desperate momentum as he tried to convince himself as much as her. "The intelligence reports from Europa confirmed it... she only awakened her core when she was nineteen years old so she’s a street brawler who stumbled into power."
He scooped up a fistful of golden sand, letting the dry grains pour through his fingers.

"Meanwhile... you and I have been swimming in the sands of Khemet since we were sixteen. Our bloodline has commanded silica manipulation for centuries. Do you honestly believe an unrefined barbarian who learned magic three months ago can match the ancestral masters of the desert on our own soil?"
Safira looked at the falling sand, then nodded slowly, some of the tension draining from her shoulders.
"You’re right. In the dunes, we are gods."
Tariq exhaled a long, quiet breath through his nose, slumping slightly against the ridge.

’I hope to the gods she believes it,’ Tariq thought with cold sweat prickling beneath his bronze armor. ’Because if that monster actually comes out here... what if she decides to summon high-tier lightning? Lightning strikes sand and turns it into solid, brittle glass... She could vitrify our entire domain in a single strike or fire? A high-density flame blast could superheat the dunes and bake us alive inside our own mantles.’
The possibilities were terrifying suffocating nightmares.
"Tariq," Safira’s voice suddenly hissed, sounding very sharp and urgent which made Tariq snap his head up.
"What?"
Safira pointed a trembling sand-coated finger toward the northern ridge, two miles away where the yellow dunes met the jagged foothills of the mountains.
"Look," Safira whispered. "Something is flashing."
Tariq squinted through the shimmering heat waves and high along the spine of the northern sandstone ridge, a tiny point of light was pulsing.
Flick! Flick!
"A transponder beacon?" Tariq muttered, his brow furrowing beneath his sand cowl. "A distress flare between separated squads? Or is someone trying to regroup?"
Before the thought could finish forming in his mind... The tiny point of light didn’t flicker again.
It ignited.
WHOOSH!
The flashing light transformed into a blinding sphere of white-hot crimson flame.
The heat was staggering... even some distance away across the open desert, the ambient temperature spiked by twenty degrees in the span of a single second.
The air screamed as the sphere of fire detached from the ridge, rocketing across the sky toward their exact coordinates with the terrifying roaring velocity of a missile.
Tariq’s pupils violently dilated into microscopic points.
"SUBMERGE!" Tariq screamed, his voice cracking in panic. "SUBMERGE NOW!"
WHOOOOOOSH!
Tariq and Safira threw their hands forward, violently diving headfirst into the crest of the dune.
Their ancestral mana liquefied the silica around them, swallowing their armored bodies thirty feet down into the subterranean belly of the sand.
A microsecond later...
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The colossal crimson fireball detonated against the surface of the dune and the apocalyptic explosion ripped a fifty-yard-wide, twenty-foot-deep crater into the desert floor.

The ungodly temperature of the blast didn’t just scatter the silica... it instantly superheated millions of metric tons of sand, fusing the earth into a smooth translucent lake of boiling red glass that crackled with persistent dancing tongues of crimson fire.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
From the smoke and heat haze on the northern ridge two miles away...
A slender elegant silhouette stepped casually onto the edge of the glass-crater’s rim.
Her heavy opulent robes were gone, replaced by a skin-tight, reinforced strike cuirass of midnight-black leather and dark crimson steel that hugged her athletic frame.

Two curved, serrated hunting daggers rested horizontally across the small of her back, their blades humming with hungry dancing embers and her long, vivid crimson hair whipped wildly in the superheated desert wind, framing a porcelain face touched by a cruel smirk.

Seraphina Bloom slowly spun one of her curved hunting daggers around her index finger with effortless dexterity, her ruby-red eyes glowing with pure sadistic anticipation as she looked down into the bubbling glass crater.
"Well, well~" Seraphina purred softly, her melodic voice cutting through the hissing heat like a sharp razor.
"Just the little desert rats I was looking for."
She snapped the dagger into a reverse grip, her crimson mana flaring along her calves like twin comets.
It was time for House Bloom to hunt.
Seraphina then reached up with a pale bare hand, hooking two fingers beneath a stray lock of vivid crimson hair that had plastered itself to the side of her neck.

The strands burned with the dark unblemished luster of fresh furnace coals, catching the sulfurous light of the lower sky as she pushed the hair behind the shell of her ear with slow deliberate precision making the black lacquered plates of her strike cuirass clicking quietly against the silver wire cinching her waist.
A low amused murmur stirred in the back of her throat.
’He better be watching this stream,’ Seraphina thought, her gaze drifting lazily toward the nearest administrative lens hovering forty paces out over the rocks.
Silas had to see this.
He needed to sit down, keep his eyes open, and watch his prospective consort dismantle these people without needing to call on a single piece of external armor.
It was a matter of basic household discipline.
If they were going to formalize the union before their elders and shut her mother’s relentless nagging down for good, the man needed to understand the standard he was marrying into.

’Right now, his water magic is able to suppress my base fire,’ she considered, her thumb tracing the smooth bone pommel of the curved hunting dagger riding horizontally along the small of her back. ’Val also mentioned his water was strong and had weight behind it the last time they saw, but base flames are just the floor. If we get married, I expect his arts to fully extinguish my standard output on demand... A prospective consort whose husband cannot even handle a minor domestic disagreement without receiving third-degree burns across his chest is an embarrassment to House Bloom. He needs to take his core training seriously. The elder council already looks at his commoner origins like a bad case of crop rot so if he cannot physically dominate the family dueling rings, those withered old hags in the inner court will never let him hear the end of it.’
She exhaled through her nose, the breath pluming into a faint wisp of scorched air that dissolved against the arid wind.
Turning her head three inches to the right, Seraphina glanced over her shoulder at the figure standing motionless against the gray granite crag five paces behind her.
Tyon Bloom stood with her combat boots planted wide on the shale with her arms crossed over a broad compact chest encased in dull bronze-washed chain and charcoal cuirass leather.
Her face was locked into an aggressive sour scowl, her jaw clenched so tight the muscles bulged beneath her skin like knots in wet rope.
Her short russet hair had been cropped down to the scalp with sheep shears, leaving jagged tufts that bristled against the high collar of her gambeson.
Seraphina understood the scowl.

Tyon was third-generation stock from the cinder garrisons out on the volcanic perimeter... the border marches where the lesser branches of the Bloom bloodline spent their lives eating salted mutton, sleeping on gravel, and trading skin with feral salamanders while the main house in the city held court under silk awnings.

Seraphina knew for a fact that if she had been dumped into an ash trench at four years old to fight over water rations, she would wear the exact same miserable blood-seeking expression every minute of the day.
"Tyon," Seraphina said.
The retainer did not shift her weight.
Her head snapped toward Seraphina with a sharp militaristic jerk, her hand dropping flat against the hilt of the serrated broad-cleaver strapped across her thigh with a dull clack.
"My Lady," Tyon barked with her voice sounding rough and dry since it was scraped raw by two decades of breathing hot basalt dust.

"Clear out," Seraphina commanded, her tone lazy and unhurried as she waved a lazy hand toward the jagged canyon pass cutting west toward the river basin. "Take the ridgeline... The Albion Concordat and those arrogant dogs from the Indus Directorate are skirmishing near the secondary aqueduct. Go put your boot in their ribs. Flush them into the open, break their spirits, and keep the northern approach clear. We are here to secure this bracket without wasting time."
Tyon’s brow pulled down, her small dark eyes narrowing with immediate suspicion.
"You intend to sweep this quadrant solo? The scan registered two heavy signatures diving into the basin before the strike."
"I am saving my power for Kara White," Seraphina replied, her voice dropping into a cold tone that brooked no debate. "The trash down here is not worth the wear on my sole leather... Go."
Tyon stared at her lady for one full second, searching for hesitation and finding none.
She grunted once.
BOOM!𝙛𝓻𝒆𝒆𝒘𝙚𝓫𝙣𝙤𝒗𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
Tyon’s heels ignited with a sudden violent burst of dense orange fire with the kick launching her forward like a stone from a siege engine.

The displaced shockwave whipped Seraphina’s crimson hair across her eyes as the retainer blurred across the shale, clearing the fifty-yard span of the crag in three bounding strides before dropping into the shadowed cleft of the western canyon.
Once the sound of Tyon’s boots faded, Seraphina looked south.
Far across the cracked salt flats, miles past the shimmering heat waves where the badlands gave way to the central caldera, the atmosphere was still trembling.

The residual ripples of that clash between Ren Minamoto and the Lord of Blessed Land were washing through the lower crust in low-frequency shudderings that made the loose gravel around her boots dance like boiling water.
A cold prickle traced the skin between Seraphina’s shoulder blades.
She had awakened her Lord Core and bonded her Primordial Fire Spirit when she was five years old.

She was not some pampered bureaucratic heiress stuffed into silk robes to make the family crest look respectable during trade summits... She had buried her daggers into beasts before her permanent teeth had finished coming in so she knew what slaughter looked like.

Looking at the sheared profile of that mountain peak on the far horizon... seeing how the upper third of a granite massif had been cleanly erased from existence, she knew she could not have matched that volume of destructive output without fully fusing with her Primordial Spirit and burning thirty percent of her soul pathways to cinder.
Yet Kara White had attacked the strike somehow, without releasing even half the presence Ren had brought to bear.
Seraphina took a slow deep breath, pulling the dry desert air down into the furnace of her lungs, letting the heat settle the sudden racing of her pulse.

’She is absurdly strong,’ Seraphina admitted, her jaw tightening as she stared at the distant smoke. ’Completely outside the normal curve but I just have to be stronger... Simple as that as there is no other path.’
She was prideful to the point of arrogance, quick to draw steel, and notoriously vicious when cross-examined, but she was not stupid.
Her objectives in this tournament had never matched her mother’s grand designs.

Etilga Bloom had spent three straight days before the opening ceremonies pacing the drawing rooms of the mansion, barking orders, reviewing balance sheets, and demanding that House Bloom use this arena to demonstrate military dominance over every foreign delegation.

But even Etilga, for all her political posturing and venomous ambition, possessed enough strategic clarity to know that tossing Seraphina straight into a meat-grinder match against Kara White in the first hour was a fool’s wager with terrible returns.

’Mother is playing the secondary board,’ Seraphina realized, a sharp, wicked smile curving her lips as she adjusted the leather vambraces along her forearms. ’She probably entered into some screaming match with the King of the World before the gates opened so she does not need me to kill Blessed Land today. She wants me to hunt the next best trophy on the roster... Crown Prince Alexander. She wants House Bloom to publicly drag the golden boy of House Castellian through the dirt, strip his suppression rings, and prove to the High Council that the Royal lineage is brittle, corrupt, and ripe for replacement.’
Seraphina gripped the pommels of her paired daggers, feeling the cold power of the star-tempered steel through her leather wraps.

"I will fetch your royal scalp, Mother," Seraphina murmured softly to the empty desert. "I will crack Alexander’s teeth across the marble before the broadcast ends but first... let me bully these two little desert rats."
Forty feet beneath the surface of the Great Dunes, the world was pitch-black, suffocating, and motionless.

chapters.title: Chapter 567: Khemet’s Weakness [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Tariq Al-Mansur lay horizontally suspended in a pressurized sheath of liquefied silica, his limbs coated in a three-inch-thick membrane of liquid-gold earth-mana.
The dense quartz silt pressed against his skin with the crushing weight of twenty atmospheres, but his ancestral channels drank the pressure like mother’s milk.

Beside him, suspended in the same current, Safira floated like a serpent in dark water, the green-and-bronze scales of her ceremonial mail shifting rhythmically as she filtered microscopic air pockets through her throat.

Their breathing had ceased five minutes ago as they were running purely on the ancient Khemetian lung-stasis arts, circulating the minerals in their blood to feed their brains while their senses spread outward through the sand.
Through the infinite sands of the dunes, they felt everything. They felt the twitch of a horned viper burrowing into the cool sand seventy yards to the north.
They felt the steady low-frequency hum of the realm’s underground fluid conduits three miles to the south.
And right above them... standing directly over the ceiling of where they had dove into, they felt the searing oppressive weight of an active volcano.

’She is not leaving,’ Safira’s thought pulsed through their shared link, the mental transmission vibrating with cold static. ’Tariq... the surface signature did not dissipate after the explosion... It is still reading above two thousand degrees and the sand up there is melting into slag. How does she have that much persistent output without entering an active casting stance?’

’Shut your mind down and crawl,’ Tariq answered sharply, the psychic command ringing like iron inside her skull. ’This is our soil... The dunes belong to the Pharaohs. She is an atmospheric burner as she commands open air and surface fire but down here, she has no line of sight, no directional medium, and no leverage. We drop our depth to sixty feet, skirt the lower granite shelf, and surface directly inside the focal point of the third snare... Once she steps onto the quicksand trigger, we pull her down thirty feet, lock the quartz cuffs around her throat, and let the pressure cave her lungs in before she can strike a spark.’
They shifted their weight with their cores pulsing in unison as they prepared to part the dense silica ahead of them.
Then...
The sand around their faces violently contracted.
TZZZZZZZZT!
It was a sudden sickening spike in conductivity that tore straight through the earth like an electric arc as Tariq’s eyes snapped open in the pitch darkness.
The cold soothing yellow quartz surrounding his forehead and chest abruptly flashed into a blinding crimson.
The loose sand grains pressing against his cheeks and eyelids suddenly went from cool silt to superheated lead, hissing violently as they vaporized the protective mana membrane coating his pores.

’WHAT IS THIS?!’ Safira shrieked through the link, her mind staggering under a wave of blistering agony as the scale-mail across her ribs began to scorch her skin! ’HOW IS SHE REACHING THROUGH FORTY FEET OF SOLID BEDROCK?!’
’MOVE!’ Tariq bellowed, his voice tearing through the mental channel in a roar of raw panic. ’SURFACE NOW!’
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The ceiling of the subterranean chamber vaporized as Seraphina Bloom had not bothered to dig.

She had planted her right heel on the center of the sand dune and dumped a continuous, concentrated spike of three-thousand-degree solar flame straight downward, using the silica’s natural mineral density as a direct conductor.

The heat traveled through the quartz strata with terrifying speed, flash-melting thousands of metric tons of sand into boiling bubbling lakes of liquid red glass that collapsed into the hollows like molten wax.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The superheated backdraft roared through the pocket and Tariq as well as Safira had no choice.
Remaining underground for another two seconds meant having their lungs filled with liquid quartz and their flesh fused to the bedrock.
CRACK-SHATTER!
Sixty paces north of the original impact point, the surface of the dune ruptured in a violent geyser of smoking sand and shattered glass.
Two bodies shot upward into the daylight, spinning through the air before hitting the dry hard-packed earth with staggering thuds.
Tariq hit the ground on one knee and one forearm, coughing violently, spitting out thick mouthfuls of scorched dust and bile as the bronze plates of his greaves hissed against the arid wind.
His scale-mail was blackened, smoking from the collar with the skin beneath his leather undergarments red and blistered from the radiant power.

Beside him, Safira rolled across the dirt, scrambling into a low, three-point crouch with both khopeshes drawn, her dark hair wild and caked in white ash as her kohl-lined eyes went wide with panting horror.
Fifteen paces away, standing casually on the raised rim of the newly formed glass crater, Seraphina Bloom was waiting for them.
She had not moved an inch.
Her arms were folded loosely over her black strike cuirass with her boots resting cleanly on the glowing red-rimmed edge of the vitrified pit.
The desert wind caught the loose strands of her crimson hair, fanning them out behind her head like living ribbons of fire.
She looked down at the two panting soot-stained scions with an expression of pure amusement.

"Look at you two," Seraphina purred, her melodic voice slicing through the crackle of cooling glass like a silver blade. "The proud scions of Khemet and the undisputed sovereigns of the eastern dunes... You are standing in the middle of your ancestral biome, surrounded by thousands of square miles of your favorite element and your first tactical maneuver is to bury your faces forty feet into the dirt like frightened field mice. Aren’t you embarrassed?"
Tariq’s teeth ground together with a harsh sickening scrape, his hands trembling where they gripped the hilt of his broad-khopesh.
Seraphina tilted her chin, looking down the slope of her nose with cool disdain.

"Seriously. If this were an active volcanic area... if we were standing on a sea of boiling basalt where House Bloom claims dominion, I cannot begin to comprehend the gut-wrenching humiliation of diving under a rock to hide from an outsider. Is this what passes for royal education in the Pharaoh’s court these days? Or does your whole family just inherit a genetic urge to cower in holes whenever someone raises the temperature?"
"Hold your tongue, woman!" Tariq snarled, his voice cracking with humiliated rage as his liquid-gold core surged behind his ribs, sending a visible shockwave through the sand around his boots.
"Tariq, do not engage her words!" Safira hissed, her voice tight and strained to the breaking point as she caught his shoulder with the flat of her bracer.
Her eyes were fixed on the terrifying wavy air distortion rising off Seraphina’s leather armor.

"She is trying to draw out a direct physical exchange! Look at the glass beneath her feet! She is sustaining three thousand degrees without even manifesting a formal casting circle! If she lands a flame lance on your chest, the silica in your veins will solidify!"
That was the fatal unalterable reality of the high lineages of Khemet.

Through centuries of ritual breeding and deep communion with the sacred silica strata of the Sun Basin, the royal houses of Khemet carried dense concentrations of microscopic quartz particulates fused into their cellular walls, their blood serum, and their skeletal marrow.
It was the source of their legendary physical resilience.

It allowed them to dissolve their flesh into fluid sand, shrug off trauma that would pulverize ordinary bones, and purge deadly biological poisons by crystallizing the foreign matter and expelling it through their skin.

The royals used this natural vitrification process for dozens of medical and martial advantages... they could petrify their own muscle fibers to form instant, natural tourniquets around severed arteries, they could turn their bone marrow into dense quartz to withstand crushing blunt-force impacts and they could crystallize chronic viral infections within their organs, cutting the diseased glass from their bodies and regenerating the tissue with sand-shaping arts in less than an hour.
But concentrated fire was their nightmare.
Under temperatures exceeding the melting threshold of quartz, the silica flowing through their blood and tissue underwent instantaneous vitrification as their flesh did not merely burn...
It turned into rigid brittle glass.
And once that organic glass shattered, the damage was completely irreversible.

Unless a master of sand-transmutation was physically present to weave the shattered glass back into organic bone and meat within an hour, the victim died of systemic shock and internal exsanguination.
In this open desert, against any other opponent, they were gods but against Seraphina Bloom, the very blood in their veins was a powder keg waiting for a match.
"We do not need to run," Tariq growled, his voice dropping into a harsh vibrating bass as he violently knocked Safira’s bracer away.

His gold eyes flared with savage cornered ferocity. "There are two of us. There is one of her. Fire cannot burn without atmosphere so we will drown her in the dunes! We bury her under fifty tons of quartz and let the weight crush her throat!"
Tariq stomped his right heel into the earth with deafening concussive force.
BOOM!
"Maw of the Great Devourer!"
The thirty paces of hard-packed earth separating them did not simply crack... the entire landscape liquefied into an ocean of churning roaring sand.

From the boiling yellow sea, eight massive serpentine constructs crafted from abrasive silica erupted into the sky, their jaws lined with three rows of spinning quartz teeth that screeched like circular saws as they descended on Seraphina from eight converging angles.
Seraphina’s lips curved into a sharp cruel grin.
WHOOSH.

Her core flared with a ruby flash that turned the shadows beneath the dunes into blinding noon as a thirty-foot disc of roaring horizontal solar flame detonated from her waist with the explosive report of a heavy mortar.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sand serpents did not even reach within ten feet of her leather armor.

The attack truck the incoming constructs mid-lunge, instantly superheating the silica past its melting point as the abrasive sand heads froze mid-air, their spinning teeth and thrashing necks vitrifying in a single microsecond into fragile hollow statues of glowing translucent red glass.
SHATTER!

Before the glass could even fall, the concussive expansion of Seraphina’s aura smashed into them, reducing the eight massive constructs to millions of glittering razor-sharp shards that rained down across the desert like a blizzard of red diamonds.
SWOOSH!
Through the glittering cloud of falling glass, a shadow blurred forward at fast speeds.
"Haah!"
Safira had not waited for the serpents to land.
She had dematerialized her lower body into a swirling high-velocity sand vortex, skimming three inches above the ground at eighty miles per hour.

She crossed the twenty-yard gap in the blink of an eye, her twin khopeshes spinning in an intricate figure-eight pattern that whistled through the air like screaming scythes, aiming straight for Seraphina’s exposed throat and left flank.
CLANG! CLINK!
Seraphina drew both curved hunting daggers in an upward reverse-cross.
The blades collided with an ear-splitting shriek of grinding metal, spraying showers of white-hot sparks across their faces.
Safira was terrifyingly fast, her balance shifting with unnatural liquid fluidity as she constantly dissolved and reformed her center of gravity to slip past Seraphina’s leverage.
She pressed the attack with feral desperation, the bronze edge of her left khopesh sliding along Seraphina’s dagger spine, dipping down to slice toward the soft gap between her cuirass and gorget.
Seraphina tilted her head back by half an inch, feeling the cold, displaced air of the bronze blade whistle across her throat while her ruby eyes danced with wild sadistic delight.
"Fast!" Seraphina laughed, her breath hot as a furnace blast. "A little sloppy on the follow-through, but at least you have some vinegar in your blood...!"
WHAM!
Seraphina snapped her left wrist outward, deflecting the khopesh into the dirt, and drove her armored right knee violently upward into Safira’s solar plexus.
The breath exploded from Safira’s lungs in a wet choke with her eyes bulging as she stumbled backward—
SHLICK!
Seraphina spun on the ball of her right foot, her right dagger tracing a clean horizontal scarlet arc through the air.
The serrated tip caught Safira across the meat of her upper bicep, cleaving through the bronze scale-mail and slicing a four-inch gash through the muscle.
"Tariq!" Safira screamed through the blinding pain, leaping backward as the laceration hissed with immediate third-degree cauterization.
From the sky directly above Seraphina’s head, a shadow eclipsed the sun!

Tariq had launched himself thirty feet into the air on the crest of a compressed sand pillar with his broad-khopesh gripped with both hands and his liquid-purple core burning with every ounce of mana his soul could force through his channels.
"Fall of the Obelisk!"
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
He brought the massive blade down with the full momentum of his descent, dragging a seventy-foot pillar of solid compressed quartz sandstone down behind the strike like a falling mountain.
’I do like the names of his moves though...’ Sera thought as she brought both daggers up in an emergency cross-block to meet the descending monolith!
BOOM!
The concussive violence of the collision blew a twenty-yard crater into the bedrock beneath her boots, sending shockwaves rolling through the dunes that flattened the surrounding sand ridges.

The physical mass of the seventy-foot sandstone pillar was immense and even with Seraphina’s peak second Stage Lord Core bracing her musculature, the crushing momentum drove her three inches into the stone.
A three-foot slab of sheared quartz bypassed her cross-guard, slicing across the meat of her left shoulder.
SHLICK!
A line of bright crimson blood welled up, soaking through the dark leather of her collar.

sentences.text: Tariq Al-Mansur lay horizontally suspended in a pressurized sheath of liquefied silica, his limbs coated in a three-inch-thick membrane of liquid-gold earth-mana.
The dense quartz silt pressed against his skin with the crushing weight of twenty atmospheres, but his ancestral channels drank the pressure like mother’s milk.

Beside him, suspended in the same current, Safira floated like a serpent in dark water, the green-and-bronze scales of her ceremonial mail shifting rhythmically as she filtered microscopic air pockets through her throat.

Their breathing had ceased five minutes ago as they were running purely on the ancient Khemetian lung-stasis arts, circulating the minerals in their blood to feed their brains while their senses spread outward through the sand.
Through the infinite sands of the dunes, they felt everything.
They felt the twitch of a horned viper burrowing into the cool sand seventy yards to the north.
They felt the steady low-frequency hum of the realm’s underground fluid conduits three miles to the south.
And right above them... standing directly over the ceiling of where they had dove into, they felt the searing oppressive weight of an active volcano.
’She is not leaving,’ Safira’s thought pulsed through their shared link, the mental transmission vibrating with cold static. ’Tariq... the surface signature did not dissipate after the explosion...
It is still reading above two thousand degrees and the sand up there is melting into slag.
How does she have that much persistent output without entering an active casting stance?’
’Shut your mind down and crawl,’ Tariq answered sharply, the psychic command ringing like iron inside her skull. ’This is our soil...
The dunes belong to the Pharaohs.
She is an atmospheric burner as she commands open air and surface fire but down here, she has no line of sight, no directional medium, and no leverage.
We drop our depth to sixty feet, skirt the lower granite shelf, and surface directly inside the focal point of the third snare...
Once she steps onto the quicksand trigger, we pull her down thirty feet, lock the quartz cuffs around her throat, and let the pressure cave her lungs in before she can strike a spark.’
They shifted their weight with their cores pulsing in unison as they prepared to part the dense silica ahead of them.
Then...
The sand around their faces violently contracted.
TZZZZZZZZT!
It was a sudden sickening spike in conductivity that tore straight through the earth like an electric arc as Tariq’s eyes snapped open in the pitch darkness.
The cold soothing yellow quartz surrounding his forehead and chest abruptly flashed into a blinding crimson.
The loose sand grains pressing against his cheeks and eyelids suddenly went from cool silt to superheated lead, hissing violently as they vaporized the protective mana membrane coating his pores.

’WHAT IS THIS?!’ Safira shrieked through the link, her mind staggering under a wave of blistering agony as the scale-mail across her ribs began to scorch her skin! ’HOW IS SHE REACHING THROUGH FORTY FEET OF SOLID BEDROCK?!’
’MOVE!’ Tariq bellowed, his voice tearing through the mental channel in a roar of raw panic. ’SURFACE NOW!’
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The ceiling of the subterranean chamber vaporized as Seraphina Bloom had not bothered to dig.

She had planted her right heel on the center of the sand dune and dumped a continuous, concentrated spike of three-thousand-degree solar flame straight downward, using the silica’s natural mineral density as a direct conductor.

The heat traveled through the quartz strata with terrifying speed, flash-melting thousands of metric tons of sand into boiling bubbling lakes of liquid red glass that collapsed into the hollows like molten wax.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The superheated backdraft roared through the pocket and Tariq as well as Safira had no choice.
Remaining underground for another two seconds meant having their lungs filled with liquid quartz and their flesh fused to the bedrock.
CRACK-SHATTER!
Sixty paces north of the original impact point, the surface of the dune ruptured in a violent geyser of smoking sand and shattered glass.
Two bodies shot upward into the daylight, spinning through the air before hitting the dry hard-packed earth with staggering thuds.
Tariq hit the ground on one knee and one forearm, coughing violently, spitting out thick mouthfuls of scorched dust and bile as the bronze plates of his greaves hissed against the arid wind.
His scale-mail was blackened, smoking from the collar with the skin beneath his leather undergarments red and blistered from the radiant power.

Beside him, Safira rolled across the dirt, scrambling into a low, three-point crouch with both khopeshes drawn, her dark hair wild and caked in white ash as her kohl-lined eyes went wide with panting horror.
Fifteen paces away, standing casually on the raised rim of the newly formed glass crater, Seraphina Bloom was waiting for them.
She had not moved an inch.
Her arms were folded loosely over her black strike cuirass with her boots resting cleanly on the glowing red-rimmed edge of the vitrified pit.
The desert wind caught the loose strands of her crimson hair, fanning them out behind her head like living ribbons of fire.
She looked down at the two panting soot-stained scions with an expression of pure amusement.
"Look at you two," Seraphina purred, her melodic voice slicing through the crackle of cooling glass like a silver blade.
"The proud scions of Khemet and the undisputed sovereigns of the eastern dunes...

You are standing in the middle of your ancestral biome, surrounded by thousands of square miles of your favorite element and your first tactical maneuver is to bury your faces forty feet into the dirt like frightened field mice.
Aren’t you embarrassed?"
Tariq’s teeth ground together with a harsh sickening scrape, his hands trembling where they gripped the hilt of his broad-khopesh.
Seraphina tilted her chin, looking down the slope of her nose with cool disdain.
"Seriously.

If this were an active volcanic area... if we were standing on a sea of boiling basalt where House Bloom claims dominion, I cannot begin to comprehend the gut-wrenching humiliation of diving under a rock to hide from an outsider.
Is this what passes for royal education in the Pharaoh’s court these days?
Or does your whole family just inherit a genetic urge to cower in holes whenever someone raises the temperature?"
"Hold your tongue, woman!" Tariq snarled, his voice cracking with humiliated rage as his liquid-gold core surged behind his ribs, sending a visible shockwave through the sand around his boots.
"Tariq, do not engage her words!" Safira hissed, her voice tight and strained to the breaking point as she caught his shoulder with the flat of her bracer.

chapters.title: Chapter 568: Devil [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Tariq landed five paces back in the crater with his breath coming in ragged triumphant gasps as his golden eyes went wide with savage blood-slicked ecstasy.
"I cut you!" Tariq roared, wiping blood and grit from his chin. "You bleed like any other mortal, Bloom!"
Seraphina looked down at her shoulder as he stared at the thin line of red soaking her collar for two full seconds.
Her expression did not darken with fear and her jaw did not tighten with pain.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
A delicate golden-red flame flickered to life over the severed skin.
’Is she burning herself...?’
Unfortunately for Tariq, the solar fire did not burn her flesh... it accelerated her cellular metabolism with unnatural efficiency.
In less than two heartbeats, the laceration closed, the severed muscle fibers knitting together beneath the skin, leaving the porcelain flesh smooth and whole.
Seraphina slowly looked up through her dark bangs, her ruby eyes blazing with a cold terrifying amusement that froze the breath in Tariq’s throat.
"Did you really think drawing a thimble of blood meant you were winning, little prince?" Seraphina whispered, her voice carrying a soft melodic chill that made his skin crawl.
"Tariq, fall back!" Safira screamed, charging forward from the crater’s rim with both khopeshes igniting with dull yellow earth-mana. "Form the dual barrier! Do not let her isolate you!"
"Out of my way, nuisance," Seraphina muttered.
She did not even turn to face Safira as she extended her left arm backward, flicking her wrist toward the charging woman like someone brushing away an irritating gnat.
BOOM!
A concentrated high-velocity lance of compressed volcanic flame erupted from the palm of her hand.

The backwash alone tore a three-foot trench through the dirt as the flame lance struck Safira squarely in the center of her bronze breastplate, shattering the metal into molten slag and blasting her body sixty yards backward across the desert floor.
SKID-CRASH!
Safira hit the base of a towering sand dune, tumbling through the hot silt, coughing up dark blood as she lay temporarily paralyzed, clutching her scorched ribs.
Now, the crater belonged to two people.
Seraphina Bloom turned her full attention to the Second Prince of Khemet.
She looked at the trembling broad-khopesh in his hands then, with slow deliberate movements, she released her grip on both of her curved hunting daggers.
THUD! THUD!
The weapons dropped into the sand at her feet, sinking into the grit.
Tariq blinked, his pupils contracting with uncomprehending disbelief.
"You... you discard your steel?"

"Against you?" Seraphina’s laughter was loud and dripping with mockery. "Carrying weapons against a spoiled third-rate royal who hides behind sand dunes would be an insult to the smiths who forged them... My hands are more than enough to take you apart, Prince."
WHOOSH!
She disappeared.
Tariq’s combat instincts flared violently as he swung his broad-khopesh horizontally in a desperate, blind semicircle meant to clear his entire forward perimeter—
SMACK!
Seraphina had already crossed the ten-pace gap, slipping beneath the arc of the heavy blade.

Her left palm slapped the flat of his steel with contemptuous ease, violently redirecting the weapon’s momentum into the dirt, while her right fist drove upward in a vicious short-range uppercut that caught Tariq squarely on the underside of his chin.
CRACK!

The sound of his jaw fracturing sounded like a dry branch snapping under a heavy boot and Tariq’s head snapped violently backward with a spray of dark blood and three shattered molars bursting from his lips as his vision exploded into white static.
Before his boots could leave the ground, Seraphina’s left hand shot out like an iron clamp, snatching him by the collar of his bronze scale-mail.
She yanked his heaving, off-balance frame downward, meeting his chest with a rising solar-infused elbow strike directly into his sternum.
WHAM!
The bronze breastplate caved inward with a sickening hollow sound with the concussive shockwave blowing through his chest, driving every drop of oxygen from his lungs.
Tariq’s eyes rolled back in their sockets, his body convulsing as blackness crept across the edges of his sight.

The overwhelming brutality of the assault... this terrifying unanswerable speed and the physical disrespect with which she dismantled his guard suddenly triggered something buried deep within the dark corners of his memory.
FLASH!
The desert heat faded into the sterile marble glare of the Sun Palace in the capital of Khemet.
He was eight years old again.
He was kneeling on the scorching stone tiles of the private sparring pavilion with his nose broken and his child’s tunic soaked in his own vomit and blood.
Standing over him was his dead older brother... Prince Khensu, the towering merciless berserker who commanded the southern frontier garrisons.

Khensu was laughing, his heavy star-iron-plated gauntlets dripping with Tariq’s blood, kicking him in the ribs every time he tried to push himself up, mocking his weak pathetic sand-shaping, telling him that the other sons were born only to serve as stepping stones for the strong...
’No... not again...’ Tariq’s mind screamed in a haze of childhood terror. ’I survived the frontier... I survived the trials... I am a Prince of the Sun...!’
BLINK!
The memory shattered.

Tariq snapped back to reality just in time to see Seraphina Bloom standing before him with her right fist coiled back at her hip, wrapped in a mantle of roaring three-thousand-degree solar flame that turned the surrounding air into a shimmering mirage.
"Die with some dignity, little prince," Seraphina purred.
Tariq crossed both arms in front of his face in a instinctual block, pouring every drop of mana he possessed into the bone and muscle of his forearms!
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The punch struck the crossed forearms of his bronze armor and the heat did not disperse outward.
It poured straight into his biological inner with the unstoppable violence of an erupting magma vent...
The dense quartz silica flowing through the blood vessels, marrow, and skin of Tariq’s wrists and forearms underwent instantaneous vitrification.
CRRRRRRRK!
Before his wide horror-struck eyes, the skin, tendons, and bones of both his hands and wrists transformed into solid translucent red glass.
...And the force of the punch had not finished moving.
BANG!
Under the crushing concussive weight of her fist, both of Tariq’s glass-crystallized hands completely shattered into a thousand glittering bloody shards.
"AAAAAAAAAAAAGH!"
Tariq howled in agony, stumbling backward and clutching the smoking, shattered stumps of his wrists as hot arterial blood sprayed across the sand.
His knees gave out beneath him, and he collapsed onto his face in the dirt, sobbing and choking on his own gore.
Seraphina stepped forward with her expression settling into a cold detachment.
"Very disappointing..."
She raised her right foot with her heel glowing with a sharp point of crimson flame, preparing to bring it down onto the base of his skull to extinguish his life-force permanently—
"TARIQ!"
A blood-curdling hysterical shriek tore through the basin.
Fifty paces away, on the crest of the sand dune, Safira had dragged herself upright and her face was pale as chalk, covered in blood and dust too but her eyes burning with mad resolve.
She plunged both arms deep into the sand with her Second Stage Purple Core roaring as she tore open her own soul pathways.
"I’ll fucking kill you...!"
RUMBLE-CRASH!
The entire hundred-yard basin of the dunes erupted into an apocalyptic boiling tidal wave of yellow sand as Safira poured her own living flesh directly into the construct.
Her legs, her thighs, and her lower abdomen dissolved into the raging storm of sand, merging her body directly with hundreds of metric tons of churning earth!

Only her face, her bare shoulders, and her upper chest remained visible, protruding from the wrist of a colossal thirty-foot hand of compressed sandstone that shot out of the ground like a titan’s claw!
WHOOOOOOSH... SNAP!
The colossal hand swept across the crater with its massive fingers snapping shut around Seraphina Bloom’s entire body.
"Just fucking die already!"
The thirty-foot earthen claw hoisted Seraphina thirty feet into the air, squeezing her frame with the hydraulic pressure of a tectonic fault!
Tariq, kneeling in the dirt and clutching his bleeding ruined stumps, looked up through the red haze of his agony, his eyes widening in horror.
"SAFIRA, STOP!" Tariq screamed, vomiting blood onto the sand. "STOP IT! You are merging your body with the silica! If she releases her heat now, your entire body will—"
"I don’t care!" Safira shrieked from the wrist of the titan’s hand with blood pouring freely from her ears and eyes as she strained against the immense weight of the spell.

The sand fingers around Seraphina began to violently compress, transmuting from loose silica into dense unyielding basalt rock, seeking to crush every rib and organ in the high lady’s body into paste.

"If I do not hold her, you die!" Safira wept, her voice echoing through the stone with loyalty. "I will crush her! I will turn this entire basin into bedrock and bury her sixty feet deep! If I can just hold her for ten seconds—"
Inside the tightening crushing basalt fist thirty feet in the air... A soft melodic chuckle echoed through the stone.
"How cute," Seraphina’s voice sounded relaxed and completely untroubled by the tons of rock pressing against her ribs.
Safira froze.
FWOOOOSH!
From between the seams of the massive basalt fingers, filaments of incandescent, silver-white light began to bleed into the sky as the temperature detonated.
Seraphina Bloom opened the floodgates of her Primordial Fire Spirit.
"Burn," Seraphina commanded.
BOOOOOM!
A vortex of three-thousand-degree solar flame erupted from Seraphina’s trapped frame and the basalt rock did not withstand the heat for a single microsecond.
The suffocating wave of heat poured through the earthen construct, racing straight down the tectonic conduits into the living cellular pathways Safira had merged with the stone.
"NO!" Tariq screamed, clawing at the dirt with his bloody elbows with tears streaming down his dust-caked cheeks. "MOVE, SAFIRA! DISPERSE THE MERGE! GET OUT OF THE EARTH!"
It was already over as the solar heat was merciless, and instantaneous.

Starting from the massive stone fingers encasing Seraphina, traveling down the wrist of the titan’s arm, and tearing straight into the organic tissue of Safira’s upper chest... the quartz particulates within her cells flashed.
CRRRRRK-CRACK!
Her arms turned to clear glowing red glass, her collarbone turned to glass and her neck turned to glass.
Safira’s kohl-lined eyes widened in terror as the crystalline vitrification swept upward across her chin, freezing her vocal cords in mid-shriek.
’Wait...’ Safira’s final thought echoed in the freezing darkness of her mind, cut off before it could finish. ’I... I cannot breathe... the heat... it is not burning... it is turning my heart into—’
SNAP!
The thought died.
Her lips, her open mouth, her wide dilated pupils... everything vitrified into a solid hollow statue of brilliant translucent red glass.
The massive earthen construct froze in mid-air, transformed from an apocalyptic crushing claw into a fragile glittering monument of superheated glass suspended thirty feet above the desert floor.
Tariq looked up with his chest heaving in violent strangulated gasps as a desperate irrational flicker of hope clutched at his shattered sanity.

’She is glass...’ Tariq thought, his mind scrambling through the madness. ’The core... the core is still inside the crystalline shell... if the construct does not break... if the glass stays whole... I can use my remaining mana to stabilize her... I can take her to an expert after the match... they can reverse the vitrification... she can survive this...’
Thirty feet above the desert floor, standing casually on the palm of the frozen glass hand, Seraphina looked down at the crystalline statue of Safira.
Her long crimson hair flowed around her shoulders like liquid flame, her ruby eyes glowing with cruel curiosity.
"I wonder," Seraphina murmured aloud, her voice carrying cleanly down through the dead silence of the basin.

She raised her right arm, the muscles along her forearm tightening as a blinding sphere of compressed solar flame coalesced around her knuckles, spinning with the high-pitched shriek of an active turbine.
"Would you really die from this?" she asked.
Tariq’s heart stopped beating as the blood in his veins ran completely cold.

"NO!" Tariq shrieked, dragging his battered bleeding body across the sand, sobbing hysterically as he reached toward the base of the construct with his ruined stumps! "NO, PLEASE! SERAPHINA, STOP! SHE IS DEFEATED! KHEMET SURRENDERS! I CONCEDE THE MATCH! PLEASE, BY THE GODS, DO NOT BREAK HER!"
His frantic pathetic pleas fell on deaf ears as Seraphina did not even glance down at him.
TWITCH!
"Flame-Slash." Seraphina whispered and she released the strike.
A concentrated crescent-shaped blade of pure, compressed solar fire detonated from her hand, slamming dead-center into the chest of the glass statue.
CRASH-SHATTER!
The glass violently disintegrated.

The three-thousand-degree blade punched clean through Safira’s vitrified torso, vaporizing the crystalline core into microscopic powder, while the concussive shockwave rippled through the rest of the thirty-foot construct.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-SHATTER!
The colossal glass hand collapsed into hundreds of thousands of sharp glittering red shards, raining down across the sand like a macabre blizzard of shattered crystal!
Tariq knelt in the dirt with his mouth hanging open, staring blankly as the glittering glass showered down around his shoulders.
CLINK!
A single curved shard of red glass tumbled from the air, landing softly in the bloody hollow of his ruined left wrist.
Tariq looked down.
Embedded within the translucent crimson shard of crystal was the perfectly preserved contour of Safira’s right eye looking wide and forever frozen in a state of uncomprehending shock.
Silence fell over the Great Dunes.

sentences.text: Tariq landed five paces back in the crater with his breath coming in ragged triumphant gasps as his golden eyes went wide with savage blood-slicked ecstasy.
"I cut you!" Tariq roared, wiping blood and grit from his chin.
"You bleed like any other mortal, Bloom!"
Seraphina looked down at her shoulder as he stared at the thin line of red soaking her collar for two full seconds.
Her expression did not darken with fear and her jaw did not tighten with pain.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
A delicate golden-red flame flickered to life over the severed skin.
’Is she burning herself...?’
Unfortunately for Tariq, the solar fire did not burn her flesh... it accelerated her cellular metabolism with unnatural efficiency.
In less than two heartbeats, the laceration closed, the severed muscle fibers knitting together beneath the skin, leaving the porcelain flesh smooth and whole.
Seraphina slowly looked up through her dark bangs, her ruby eyes blazing with a cold terrifying amusement that froze the breath in Tariq’s throat.
"Did you really think drawing a thimble of blood meant you were winning, little prince?" Seraphina whispered, her voice carrying a soft melodic chill that made his skin crawl.
"Tariq, fall back!" Safira screamed, charging forward from the crater’s rim with both khopeshes igniting with dull yellow earth-mana.
"Form the dual barrier!
Do not let her isolate you!"
"Out of my way, nuisance," Seraphina muttered.
She did not even turn to face Safira as she extended her left arm backward, flicking her wrist toward the charging woman like someone brushing away an irritating gnat.
BOOM!
A concentrated high-velocity lance of compressed volcanic flame erupted from the palm of her hand.

The backwash alone tore a three-foot trench through the dirt as the flame lance struck Safira squarely in the center of her bronze breastplate, shattering the metal into molten slag and blasting her body sixty yards backward across the desert floor.
SKID-CRASH!
Safira hit the base of a towering sand dune, tumbling through the hot silt, coughing up dark blood as she lay temporarily paralyzed, clutching her scorched ribs.
Now, the crater belonged to two people.
Seraphina Bloom turned her full attention to the Second Prince of Khemet.
She looked at the trembling broad-khopesh in his hands then, with slow deliberate movements, she released her grip on both of her curved hunting daggers.
THUD!
THUD!
The weapons dropped into the sand at her feet, sinking into the grit.
Tariq blinked, his pupils contracting with uncomprehending disbelief.
"You... you discard your steel?"
"Against you?" Seraphina’s laughter was loud and dripping with mockery.
"Carrying weapons against a spoiled third-rate royal who hides behind sand dunes would be an insult to the smiths who forged them...
My hands are more than enough to take you apart, Prince."
WHOOSH!
She disappeared.
Tariq’s combat instincts flared violently as he swung his broad-khopesh horizontally in a desperate, blind semicircle meant to clear his entire forward perimeter—
SMACK!
Seraphina had already crossed the ten-pace gap, slipping beneath the arc of the heavy blade.

Her left palm slapped the flat of his steel with contemptuous ease, violently redirecting the weapon’s momentum into the dirt, while her right fist drove upward in a vicious short-range uppercut that caught Tariq squarely on the underside of his chin.
CRACK!

The sound of his jaw fracturing sounded like a dry branch snapping under a heavy boot and Tariq’s head snapped violently backward with a spray of dark blood and three shattered molars bursting from his lips as his vision exploded into white static.
Before his boots could leave the ground, Seraphina’s left hand shot out like an iron clamp, snatching him by the collar of his bronze scale-mail.
She yanked his heaving, off-balance frame downward, meeting his chest with a rising solar-infused elbow strike directly into his sternum.
WHAM!
The bronze breastplate caved inward with a sickening hollow sound with the concussive shockwave blowing through his chest, driving every drop of oxygen from his lungs.
Tariq’s eyes rolled back in their sockets, his body convulsing as blackness crept across the edges of his sight.

The overwhelming brutality of the assault... this terrifying unanswerable speed and the physical disrespect with which she dismantled his guard suddenly triggered something buried deep within the dark corners of his memory.
FLASH!
The desert heat faded into the sterile marble glare of the Sun Palace in the capital of Khemet.
He was eight years old again.
He was kneeling on the scorching stone tiles of the private sparring pavilion with his nose broken and his child’s tunic soaked in his own vomit and blood.
Standing over him was his dead older brother...
Prince Khensu, the towering merciless berserker who commanded the southern frontier garrisons.

Khensu was laughing, his heavy star-iron-plated gauntlets dripping with Tariq’s blood, kicking him in the ribs every time he tried to push himself up, mocking his weak pathetic sand-shaping, telling him that the other sons were born only to serve as stepping stones for the strong...
’No... not again...’ Tariq’s mind screamed in a haze of childhood terror. ’I survived the frontier...
I survived the trials...
I am a Prince of the Sun...!’
BLINK!
The memory shattered.

Tariq snapped back to reality just in time to see Seraphina Bloom standing before him with her right fist coiled back at her hip, wrapped in a mantle of roaring three-thousand-degree solar flame that turned the surrounding air into a shimmering mirage.
"Die with some dignity, little prince," Seraphina purred.
Tariq crossed both arms in front of his face in a instinctual block, pouring every drop of mana he possessed into the bone and muscle of his forearms!
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The punch struck the crossed forearms of his bronze armor and the heat did not disperse outward.
It poured straight into his biological inner with the unstoppable violence of an erupting magma vent...
The dense quartz silica flowing through the blood vessels, marrow, and skin of Tariq’s wrists and forearms underwent instantaneous vitrification.
CRRRRRRRK!
Before his wide horror-struck eyes, the skin, tendons, and bones of both his hands and wrists transformed into solid translucent red glass.
...And the force of the punch had not finished moving.
BANG!
Under the crushing concussive weight of her fist, both of Tariq’s glass-crystallized hands completely shattered into a thousand glittering bloody shards.
"AAAAAAAAAAAAGH!"
Tariq howled in agony, stumbling backward and clutching the smoking, shattered stumps of his wrists as hot arterial blood sprayed across the sand.
His knees gave out beneath him, and he collapsed onto his face in the dirt, sobbing and choking on his own gore.
Seraphina stepped forward with her expression settling into a cold detachment.
"Very disappointing..."
She raised her right foot with her heel glowing with a sharp point of crimson flame, preparing to bring it down onto the base of his skull to extinguish his life-force permanently—
"TARIQ!"
A blood-curdling hysterical shriek tore through the basin.
Fifty paces away, on the crest of the sand dune, Safira had dragged herself upright and her face was pale as chalk, covered in blood and dust too but her eyes burning with mad resolve.
She plunged both arms deep into the sand with her Second Stage Purple Core roaring as she tore open her own soul pathways.
"I’ll fucking kill you...!"
RUMBLE-CRASH!
The entire hundred-yard basin of the dunes erupted into an apocalyptic boiling tidal wave of yellow sand as Safira poured her own living flesh directly into the construct.
Her legs, her thighs, and her lower abdomen dissolved into the raging storm of sand, merging her body directly with hundreds of metric tons of churning earth!

Only her face, her bare shoulders, and her upper chest remained visible, protruding from the wrist of a colossal thirty-foot hand of compressed sandstone that shot out of the ground like a titan’s claw!
WHOOOOOOSH...
SNAP!
The colossal hand swept across the crater with its massive fingers snapping shut around Seraphina Bloom’s entire body.
"Just fucking die already!"
The thirty-foot earthen claw hoisted Seraphina thirty feet into the air, squeezing her frame with the hydraulic pressure of a tectonic fault!
Tariq, kneeling in the dirt and clutching his bleeding ruined stumps, looked up through the red haze of his agony, his eyes widening in horror.
"SAFIRA, STOP!" Tariq screamed, vomiting blood onto the sand.
"STOP IT!
You are merging your body with the silica!
If she releases her heat now, your entire body will—"
"I don’t care!" Safira shrieked from the wrist of the titan’s hand with blood pouring freely from her ears and eyes as she strained against the immense weight of the spell.

The sand fingers around Seraphina began to violently compress, transmuting from loose silica into dense unyielding basalt rock, seeking to crush every rib and organ in the high lady’s body into paste.
"If I do not hold her, you die!" Safira wept, her voice echoing through the stone with loyalty.
"I will crush her!
I will turn this entire basin into bedrock and bury her sixty feet deep!
If I can just hold her for ten seconds—"
Inside the tightening crushing basalt fist thirty feet in the air...
A soft melodic chuckle echoed through the stone.
"How cute," Seraphina’s voice sounded relaxed and completely untroubled by the tons of rock pressing against her ribs.
Safira froze.
FWOOOOSH!
From between the seams of the massive basalt fingers, filaments of incandescent, silver-white light began to bleed into the sky as the temperature detonated.
Seraphina Bloom opened the floodgates of her Primordial Fire Spirit.
"Burn," Seraphina commanded.
BOOOOOM!
A vortex of three-thousand-degree solar flame erupted from Seraphina’s trapped frame and the basalt rock did not withstand the heat for a single microsecond.
The suffocating wave of heat poured through the earthen construct, racing straight down the tectonic conduits into the living cellular pathways Safira had merged with the stone.
"NO!" Tariq screamed, clawing at the dirt with his bloody elbows with tears streaming down his dust-caked cheeks.
"MOVE, SAFIRA!
DISPERSE THE MERGE!
GET OUT OF THE EARTH!"
It was already over as the solar heat was merciless, and instantaneous.

Starting from the massive stone fingers encasing Seraphina, traveling down the wrist of the titan’s arm, and tearing straight into the organic tissue of Safira’s upper chest... the quartz particulates within her cells flashed.
CRRRRRK-CRACK!
Her arms turned to clear glowing red glass, her collarbone turned to glass and her neck turned to glass.
Safira’s kohl-lined eyes widened in terror as the crystalline vitrification swept upward across her chin, freezing her vocal cords in mid-shriek.
’Wait...’ Safira’s final thought echoed in the freezing darkness of her mind, cut off before it could finish. ’I...
I cannot breathe... the heat... it is not burning... it is turning my heart into—’
SNAP!
The thought died.
Her lips, her open mouth, her wide dilated pupils... everything vitrified into a solid hollow statue of brilliant translucent red glass.
The massive earthen construct froze in mid-air, transformed from an apocalyptic crushing claw into a fragile glittering monument of superheated glass suspended thirty feet above the desert floor.
Tariq looked up with his chest heaving in violent strangulated gasps as a desperate irrational flicker of hope clutched at his shattered sanity.
’She is glass...’ Tariq thought, his mind scrambling through the madness. ’The core... the core is still inside the crystalline shell... if the construct does not break... if the glass stays whole...
I can use my remaining mana to stabilize her...
I can take her to an expert after the match... they can reverse the vitrification... she can survive this...’
Thirty feet above the desert floor, standing casually on the palm of the frozen glass hand, Seraphina looked down at the crystalline statue of Safira.

PLEASE, BY THE GODS, DO NOT BREAK HER!"

A concentrated crescent-shaped blade of pure, compressed solar fire detonated from her hand, slamming dead-center into the chest of the glass statue.
