chapters.title: Chapter 569: Devil [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: FSH!
An administrative beacon flared from the shattered dust where Safira’s emergency transponder had been pulverized, registering the total death of the combatant.
Tariq did not move and he did not scream either.
He simply sat in the dust, staring down at the glass eye resting in his severed arm with his mind completely hollowed out by the horror.
Thirty feet above, Seraphina dropped lightly to the sand making her boots land with a soft crunch on the cooling shale.
She rolled her right shoulder, working out a small stiffness in her trapezius, and let out a long satisfied sigh that puffed into the hot wind.
"Ah..." Seraphina murmured softly, a genuine smile spreading across her porcelain face. "It has been quite a long time since I actually killed someone."
She paused as a sudden flush of pink bloomed across her pale cheeks.
Her ruby eyes darted nervously toward the hovering broadcast probes in the sky, her fingers coming up to tuck another lock of crimson hair behind her ear.
Her heart fluttered with sudden flustered anticipation.
’Will Silas find that cool...?’ Seraphina wondered, biting her lower lip with quiet girlish delight.
Behind her, the ruined dunes burned in silence.
The desert wind swept low over the vitrified basin, whining through the cooling cracks of the red glass crater like steam escaping an iron boiler.

Seraphina stood poised on the crystalline rim with her crimson hair settling against the dark leather mantle of her strike cuirass as the soft self-satisfied smirk playing across her lips suddenly wavered and went completely stiff.
She lowered her hand from her ear, the sudden rush of romantic vanity chilling down into an unpleasant prickle of real-world consequence.
’Wait,’ Seraphina thought, her jaw tightening. ’Silas wouldn’t like this.’
He looked like someone that hadn’t killed much, would he be able to understand this feeling...? Not at all!

’He is too soft in that regard,’ she realized with the warmth draining out of her cheeks. ’If he saw me shatter her like a cup, he’s going to scowl. He’s going to cross his arms and give me an unbearable lecture about respecting and not killing unnecessarily...’
Worse yet, the broadcast.
Over a billion people were watching this feed across every country district on Earth.

The optical lenses floating in the violet sky above weren’t just piping images to the high-ranking delegates in the Great Assembly... they were streaming directly into public viewing squares, private residences, everywhere that could view a stream.
’What if Silas’s younger sister is watching this right now?’
The thought struck her ribs like an unpadded sparring blow.
Seraphina knew Silas had family.

If that little girl was seated in front of a living room screen, watching her prospective future sister-in-law obliterate an opponent into thousands of bloody glass teeth on global television, would she be terrified?
Would she run to Silas in tears, telling him that his future consort was a bloodthirsty psycho who butchered people for sport?
The flush of pride vanished entirely as the bright cruel smile faded from Seraphina’s face, replaced by a cold irritated scowl.

’This entire mess could have been avoided if they had just surrendered or died cleanly on the initial drop,’ she rationalized, her ruby eyes narrowing into dangerous smoldering slits. ’Dragging this out makes it look untidy... It makes me look undisciplined.’
She turned her head slowly, looking down into the dust at the bottom of the slope.
Prince Tariq Al-Mansur knelt in the coarse grit with his hands gone.
The blackened cauterized stumps of his wrists hung limp against his thighs, leaking thin trickles of dark marrow that hissed and dried instantly against the hot sand.
His head hung low, his shoulders trembling in small violent spasms as his golden eyes stared through the single unblinking glass eye of Safira resting on his forearm.
Seraphina stepped off the glass rim, her combat boots crunching softly over the cooling shale as she stalked down toward him.
"Well, Prince?" she asked. "Are you just going to sit there in the dirt leaking on yourself, or are you going to stand up and avenge the woman you love?"
Tariq’s breathing hitched violently.
His bloodshot pupils dilated, trembling within the dark circles of his kohl-stained eyelids as he jerked his chin upward.
’How did she know...?’ Tariq’s mind raced in nauseating circles.
Their relationship had been a state secret.

In the rigid, dynastic hierarchy of the Sun Court, a royal prince of the direct bloodline was forbidden from taking the daughter of an administrative vice president as anything more than a low-ranking concubine.
They had hidden their vows behind the heavy tapestries of the eastern palaces for four years and they had never spoken of it aloud outside of ward-shielded chambers...
Seraphina’s smile returned, though this time it was lacking any sort of humor like a mocking line that cut straight to the bone.

"Oh, please," Seraphina scoffed, rolling her eyes with exasperation. "Do you think you two were subtle? The desperate screams? The way she melted her own marrow into the sand just to buy you ten seconds of breathing room? It was practically a doomed romance so come on... Get on your feet and prove that your feelings are worth something. Show me that you have half the spine my fiancé has."
Tariq’s jaw twitched, his teeth grinding together so hard a hairline fracture shot through his remaining molar.
"Your... fiancé...?"

"Silas," Seraphina said, pronouncing the name with the unquestioned gravity of the King reading a decree. "If I were the one lying shattered across this crater, Silas wouldn’t be sitting in the dust sniveling like an abandoned puppy... He would have torn this entire basin down to the bedrock by now. He would have dragged your corpse three leagues across the salt flats just to use your ribs as firewood and he wouldn’t hesitate for half a second. So what’s your excuse?"
Tariq trembled, the rage and humiliation boiling through his veins until his vision blurred red.
’Who is this Silas...?!’ Tariq screamed internally, his mind fracturing under the weight of the name. ’Who on this earth is she talking about?!’
Inside the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence was suffocating.
Up along the high southern mezzanine, Matriarch Etilga Bloom sat rigid in her high-backed velvet chair with her lace-trimmed fan hovering an inch from her nose.
SMACK!
Etilga’s free hand rose, slapping her own forehead with an audible exasperated crack that turned the heads of three Albion ministers sitting two rows down.

’Is this girl completely out of her mind...?’ Etilga groaned internally, her fingers dragging down her temple in mortification. ’She is standing on a live, multi-continent broadcast feed, representing the honor of our bloodline before the High Council, and she is openly shouting the name of a commoner from Valoria City as if he were an anointed king... Does she want everyone to think House Bloom has lost its collective senses?!’
Etilga blew a slow hot breath through her nostrils, forcing her posture back into immaculate alignment.
Still... she had to admit, the execution had been magnificent.
The Matriarch’s fan dropped slightly, revealing her dark red lips curved into a sharp sneer.
She flicked her tongue lightly across her upper lip with her gaze sliding across the tiered chamber toward the delegation from Khemet.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur sat completely motionless.
His heavy golden headdress hung slightly askew, his dark sun-weathered hands resting limp and open upon the celestial marble table.

The color had drained from his face, leaving him looking hollow and broken... the look of an monarch who had just watched his bloodline’s future shattered into decorative parlor glass before the eyes of the entire world.

’Magnificent,’ Etilga purred within the privacy of her thoughts, a shiver of dark sadistic pleasure running down her spine. ’That look... That beautiful, vacant stare of a man who has lost everything and finally accepted that the world does not care about his pride. That is the exact expression I want to carve onto Kara White’s face when I get some alone time with her.’
It was a look that always did something strange to her blood.
It was, in fact, one of the only reasons she had kept her own husband around for thirty years.
He had that exact same pathetic defeated look whenever she stripped him of his budget allowances.
Down in Sector Forty-Four, the temperature began to rise again.
FSSSSSSSSSH!

A tight whistling crown of incandescent crimson flame ignited around Seraphina’s right hand with the distortion bending the desert horizon behind her fingers as the air grew thin, smelling of pure heat.
Tariq did not look away.
The Second Prince of Khemet looked directly into the roaring core of her solar flame with his bloodshot eyes going wide and lacking a look of terror.
Seraphina paused with a flicker of genuine surprise catching in her chest.
’Look at that,’ she thought, her heart giving an involuntary thud. ’Not an ounce of fear... The boy has actually accepted his death.’
Her lips curled into an eager grin.
A warrior who looked into the furnace without closing his eyes was a warrior worth extinguishing.
It was an insult to keep him waiting.
"Good," Seraphina whispered, her core surging to deliver the final strike. "At least you’ll die like—"
WHOOSH!
The sand beneath Tariq’s knees simply vanished as his entire physical body liquefied into an explosive, churning vortex of abrasive silica, plunging straight down into the desert floor.
The violent displacement threw a blinding sixty-foot dust storm directly into Seraphina’s face, whipping coarse yellow grit across her eyes!
Seraphina blinked, spitting a mouthful of dry dirt with her fist still burning with unused fire as she stared at the empty hole.
"Are you serious?!" she screamed into the wind, her voice cracking with pure incredulous disgust. "You ran away?!"
Thirty yards away, beneath the crust of the earth, Tariq was tearing through the silica like a runaway bullet shell.
’Devil!’ Tariq’s mind screamed, panic and adrenaline flooding his channels with sickening force. ’She is not human! That woman is a primordial calamity stuffed into an aristocratic skin!’
He wasn’t suicidal.
That dead-eyed stare had not been acceptance... It had been the cold calculation of a predator waiting for the hunter to lower their guard.

He knew he couldn’t survive another direct physical exchange since his hands were gone and his armor was ruined but the desert was vast, and as long as he was moving through the silica, he still had a board to play.
RUMBLE-CRACK!
As he rocketed through the subterranean strata, Tariq poured every drop of his remaining ancestral mana into his severed limbs.

The loose sand flowing past his forearms was drawn inward by his will, compacting, calcifying, and fusing into dense five-fingered quartz appendages that snapped onto his wrist stumps with stone-on-stone clicks.
They weren’t real flesh, but they were reinforced with earth-mana and capable of channeling runic arts.
’I will avenge you, Safira...’ Tariq swore, his teeth grinding together in the dark.

He remembered the cool night breezes of the palace gardens, he remembered her fingers running through his hair under the shadow of the desert obelisks and he remembered the solemn unshakeable promise he had made beneath the stars that they would rule the Sun Court together, side by side, free from the shadow of his elder brothers.
’I cannot die here like a dog,’ he told himself with tears leaking from his eyes and washing into the sand. ’I wear her down... I set the snares... I bleed her core dry, and then I take her head.’
As he moved, his new quartz hands blurred, weaving somatic triggers through the silica strata.
Ten snares...
Twenty snares...
Quicksand traps, underground quartz spikes, inverted gravity wells... he laid them like mines behind his wake, priming the entire eastern corridor to detonate the moment heat brushed the surface.
He was three hundred yards out, preparing to loop around the northern bluffs to trigger the collapse...
CRACK!
The atmosphere above him ceased to exist as the air parted with a sound like ripping steel.
Every single grain of sand within fifty yards of the surface instantly calcified, flash-vitrifying into solid screaming green glass.
BOOOOOOOOOM!
A blinding meteor of pure silver-white fire crashed out of the sky as it obliterated the top thirty feet of the dune in an instantaneous, thunderous shockwave that tore the strata wide open.

Tariq was ripped out of the earth, launched twenty feet into the air by the concussive eruption and he hit the hard glass rim of the new crater, rolling violently across the superheated surface, coughing up dark lung-blood as his newly formed quartz hands scraped against the slick burning stone.
He forced his chin up, his eyes widening in paralyzed horror as standing ten paces away, floating three inches above the bubbling glass, was Seraphina Bloom.
Except she was no longer merely a prodigy of House Bloom.
She had fused.
Her vivid crimson hair had bleached into a celestial silver-white that drifted weightlessly around her skull like vaporized mercury.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖

Across the left side of her porcelain face, running down her jawline and burning across the bare skin of her neck, a jagged runic crest flared with radiance and the air around her wasn’t red anymore...
It was a pure white, crackling with thermal output so high that the air molecules themselves were weeping ionized plasma.
She had fused with the Primordial Fire Spirit and her regular output had just multiplied by ten.
Seraphina looked down at him through glowing silver irises, her voice carrying a deep resonance that sounded like two voices speaking in unison.
"Coward," she said softly.
The heat radiating from her skin alone began to vitrify the sand beneath Tariq’s knees.

Seraphina knew Silas had family.

If that little girl was seated in front of a living room screen, watching her prospective future sister-in-law obliterate an opponent into thousands of bloody glass teeth on global television, would she be terrified?
Would she run to Silas in tears, telling him that his future consort was a bloodthirsty psycho who butchered people for sport?
The flush of pride vanished entirely as the bright cruel smile faded from Seraphina’s face, replaced by a cold irritated scowl.

’This entire mess could have been avoided if they had just surrendered or died cleanly on the initial drop,’ she rationalized, her ruby eyes narrowing into dangerous smoldering slits. ’Dragging this out makes it look untidy...
It makes me look undisciplined.’
She turned her head slowly, looking down into the dust at the bottom of the slope.
Prince Tariq Al-Mansur knelt in the coarse grit with his hands gone.
The blackened cauterized stumps of his wrists hung limp against his thighs, leaking thin trickles of dark marrow that hissed and dried instantly against the hot sand.
His head hung low, his shoulders trembling in small violent spasms as his golden eyes stared through the single unblinking glass eye of Safira resting on his forearm.
Seraphina stepped off the glass rim, her combat boots crunching softly over the cooling shale as she stalked down toward him.
"Well, Prince?" she asked.
"Are you just going to sit there in the dirt leaking on yourself, or are you going to stand up and avenge the woman you love?"
Tariq’s breathing hitched violently.
His bloodshot pupils dilated, trembling within the dark circles of his kohl-stained eyelids as he jerked his chin upward.
’How did she know...?’ Tariq’s mind raced in nauseating circles.
Their relationship had been a state secret.

In the rigid, dynastic hierarchy of the Sun Court, a royal prince of the direct bloodline was forbidden from taking the daughter of an administrative vice president as anything more than a low-ranking concubine.
They had hidden their vows behind the heavy tapestries of the eastern palaces for four years and they had never spoken of it aloud outside of ward-shielded chambers...
Seraphina’s smile returned, though this time it was lacking any sort of humor like a mocking line that cut straight to the bone.
"Oh, please," Seraphina scoffed, rolling her eyes with exasperation.
"Do you think you two were subtle?
The desperate screams?
The way she melted her own marrow into the sand just to buy you ten seconds of breathing room?
It was practically a doomed romance so come on...
Get on your feet and prove that your feelings are worth something.
Show me that you have half the spine my fiancé has."
Tariq’s jaw twitched, his teeth grinding together so hard a hairline fracture shot through his remaining molar.
"Your... fiancé...?"
"Silas," Seraphina said, pronouncing the name with the unquestioned gravity of the King reading a decree.
"If I were the one lying shattered across this crater, Silas wouldn’t be sitting in the dust sniveling like an abandoned puppy...
He would have torn this entire basin down to the bedrock by now.
He would have dragged your corpse three leagues across the salt flats just to use your ribs as firewood and he wouldn’t hesitate for half a second.
So what’s your excuse?"
Tariq trembled, the rage and humiliation boiling through his veins until his vision blurred red.
’Who is this Silas...?!’ Tariq screamed internally, his mind fracturing under the weight of the name. ’Who on this earth is she talking about?!’
Inside the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence was suffocating.
Up along the high southern mezzanine, Matriarch Etilga Bloom sat rigid in her high-backed velvet chair with her lace-trimmed fan hovering an inch from her nose.
SMACK!
Etilga’s free hand rose, slapping her own forehead with an audible exasperated crack that turned the heads of three Albion ministers sitting two rows down.

’Is this girl completely out of her mind...?’ Etilga groaned internally, her fingers dragging down her temple in mortification. ’She is standing on a live, multi-continent broadcast feed, representing the honor of our bloodline before the High Council, and she is openly shouting the name of a commoner from Valoria City as if he were an anointed king...
Does she want everyone to think House Bloom has lost its collective senses?!’
Etilga blew a slow hot breath through her nostrils, forcing her posture back into immaculate alignment.
Still... she had to admit, the execution had been magnificent.
The Matriarch’s fan dropped slightly, revealing her dark red lips curved into a sharp sneer.
She flicked her tongue lightly across her upper lip with her gaze sliding across the tiered chamber toward the delegation from Khemet.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur sat completely motionless.
His heavy golden headdress hung slightly askew, his dark sun-weathered hands resting limp and open upon the celestial marble table.

The color had drained from his face, leaving him looking hollow and broken... the look of an monarch who had just watched his bloodline’s future shattered into decorative parlor glass before the eyes of the entire world.
’Magnificent,’ Etilga purred within the privacy of her thoughts, a shiver of dark sadistic pleasure running down her spine. ’That look...
That beautiful, vacant stare of a man who has lost everything and finally accepted that the world does not care about his pride.
That is the exact expression I want to carve onto Kara White’s face when I get some alone time with her.’
It was a look that always did something strange to her blood.
It was, in fact, one of the only reasons she had kept her own husband around for thirty years.
He had that exact same pathetic defeated look whenever she stripped him of his budget allowances.
Down in Sector Forty-Four, the temperature began to rise again.
FSSSSSSSSSH!

A tight whistling crown of incandescent crimson flame ignited around Seraphina’s right hand with the distortion bending the desert horizon behind her fingers as the air grew thin, smelling of pure heat.
Tariq did not look away.
The Second Prince of Khemet looked directly into the roaring core of her solar flame with his bloodshot eyes going wide and lacking a look of terror.
Seraphina paused with a flicker of genuine surprise catching in her chest.
’Look at that,’ she thought, her heart giving an involuntary thud. ’Not an ounce of fear...
The boy has actually accepted his death.’
Her lips curled into an eager grin.
A warrior who looked into the furnace without closing his eyes was a warrior worth extinguishing.
It was an insult to keep him waiting.
"Good," Seraphina whispered, her core surging to deliver the final strike.
"At least you’ll die like—"
WHOOSH!
The sand beneath Tariq’s knees simply vanished as his entire physical body liquefied into an explosive, churning vortex of abrasive silica, plunging straight down into the desert floor.
The violent displacement threw a blinding sixty-foot dust storm directly into Seraphina’s face, whipping coarse yellow grit across her eyes!
Seraphina blinked, spitting a mouthful of dry dirt with her fist still burning with unused fire as she stared at the empty hole.
"Are you serious?!" she screamed into the wind, her voice cracking with pure incredulous disgust.
"You ran away?!"
Thirty yards away, beneath the crust of the earth, Tariq was tearing through the silica like a runaway bullet shell.
’Devil!’ Tariq’s mind screamed, panic and adrenaline flooding his channels with sickening force. ’She is not human!
That woman is a primordial calamity stuffed into an aristocratic skin!’
He wasn’t suicidal.
That dead-eyed stare had not been acceptance...
It had been the cold calculation of a predator waiting for the hunter to lower their guard.

He knew he couldn’t survive another direct physical exchange since his hands were gone and his armor was ruined but the desert was vast, and as long as he was moving through the silica, he still had a board to play.
RUMBLE-CRACK!
As he rocketed through the subterranean strata, Tariq poured every drop of his remaining ancestral mana into his severed limbs.

The loose sand flowing past his forearms was drawn inward by his will, compacting, calcifying, and fusing into dense five-fingered quartz appendages that snapped onto his wrist stumps with stone-on-stone clicks.
They weren’t real flesh, but they were reinforced with earth-mana and capable of channeling runic arts.
’I will avenge you, Safira...’ Tariq swore, his teeth grinding together in the dark.

He remembered the cool night breezes of the palace gardens, he remembered her fingers running through his hair under the shadow of the desert obelisks and he remembered the solemn unshakeable promise he had made beneath the stars that they would rule the Sun Court together, side by side, free from the shadow of his elder brothers.
’I cannot die here like a dog,’ he told himself with tears leaking from his eyes and washing into the sand. ’I wear her down...
I set the snares...
I bleed her core dry, and then I take her head.’
As he moved, his new quartz hands blurred, weaving somatic triggers through the silica strata.
Ten snares...
Twenty snares...
Quicksand traps, underground quartz spikes, inverted gravity wells... he laid them like mines behind his wake, priming the entire eastern corridor to detonate the moment heat brushed the surface.
He was three hundred yards out, preparing to loop around the northern bluffs to trigger the collapse...
CRACK!
The atmosphere above him ceased to exist as the air parted with a sound like ripping steel.
Every single grain of sand within fifty yards of the surface instantly calcified, flash-vitrifying into solid screaming green glass.
BOOOOOOOOOM!
A blinding meteor of pure silver-white fire crashed out of the sky as it obliterated the top thirty feet of the dune in an instantaneous, thunderous shockwave that tore the strata wide open.

Tariq was ripped out of the earth, launched twenty feet into the air by the concussive eruption and he hit the hard glass rim of the new crater, rolling violently across the superheated surface, coughing up dark lung-blood as his newly formed quartz hands scraped against the slick burning stone.
He forced his chin up, his eyes widening in paralyzed horror as standing ten paces away, floating three inches above the bubbling glass, was Seraphina Bloom.
Except she was no longer merely a prodigy of House Bloom.
She had fused.
Her vivid crimson hair had bleached into a celestial silver-white that drifted weightlessly around her skull like vaporized mercury.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖

Across the left side of her porcelain face, running down her jawline and burning across the bare skin of her neck, a jagged runic crest flared with radiance and the air around her wasn’t red anymore...
It was a pure white, crackling with thermal output so high that the air molecules themselves were weeping ionized plasma.
She had fused with the Primordial Fire Spirit and her regular output had just multiplied by ten.
Seraphina looked down at him through glowing silver irises, her voice carrying a deep resonance that sounded like two voices speaking in unison.
"Coward," she said softly.
The heat radiating from her skin alone began to vitrify the sand beneath Tariq’s knees.

chapters.title: Chapter 570: Information Broker In The Tournament Of Succession [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The quartz hands he had just formed started to groan with the artificial joints fusing together into brittle useless lumps under the ungodly temperature!
’Move!’ Tariq’s mind screamed through the panic but he didn’t run as there was nowhere left to run.
Tariq roared, throwing his remaining soul-power into his quartz forearms.
"Wrath of the Thousand Scorpions!"
BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!

Thirty massive barbed tendrils of compressed quartz and bedrock erupted from the surrounding dunes, screaming through the air like ballista bolts, aiming straight for her throat, her chest, and her limbs from every conceivable angle.

He flipped backward off the glass rim with his feet touching the earth as he channeled every remaining grain of sand into a continuous, rolling barrage of razor-sharp projectiles... however Seraphina didn’t even draw a blade.
She blinked.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
Sera simply waved her right hand outward and a single rippling wave of silver-white fire washed through the airspace!
The thirty quartz tendrils instantly liquefied into glowing glass syrup, redirected mid-flight and splashing harmlessly across the ground like molten paint.
Seraphina ran downward.
Her boots hit the vitrified slope with the glass cracking beneath her accelerated momentum with sharp musical pings as she closed the distance in a fraction of a second!
She raised her right palm, a tennis-ball-sized orb of compressed silver-white solar fire condensing between her fingers.
"Die properly this time," she whispered.
She hurled the orb.
WHOOSH!
The white fireball tore through the sound barrier, dragging a vacuum funnel of superheated air behind it.
Tariq Al-Mansur saw the white light rushing toward his face.
’I’m done...’
He saw the outline of death itself looking cold and unavoidable.
’I tried my best...’
Tariq did the only thing he could do... He closed his eyes, bracing for the total erasure of his soul—
DING!
A fraction of a microsecond before the solar fire could vaporize his skull, the emergency transponder pinned to his lapel detonated with blinding light.
The spatial fabric warped with authoritative force.

Tariq’s physical body, along with the scattered glass shards of Safira’s frozen corpse across the dunes, dissolved simultaneously into millions of shimmering ethereal white particles, surging upward into the clouds as the World Council’s emergency extraction protocol ripped them clean out of the realm.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The silver-white fireball detonated against empty dirt, tearing a hundred-yard crater into the desert floor that sent shockwaves rolling for miles.

Seraphina skidded to a halt on the edge of the blast zone with the silver-white flames slowly receding from her hair and the runic mark fading back into her porcelain skin as her locks returned to their natural deep crimson.
BZZZZZZZZT.
From the purple sky above, the flat broadcast chime echoed across Sector Forty-Four.
"Notice of Official Withdrawal."
"The representatives of the Khemet have suffered critical combat casualties and have been extracted from the field... Khemet is eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Seraphina stood in the smoking crater, blinking once and then twice.

"Cowards," she spat, her hands dropping to her hips with a loud disgusted huff. "Such cowards... Making me drop into Spirit fusion just to tap an emergency extraction button! What a waste of good mana."
She rolled her shoulders, shaking the heat haze from her leather bracers, feeling the familiar hollow fatigue that always followed a brief Spirit merge.
She needed to clear the taste of sulfur from her mouth.
Looking across the jagged salt flats toward the western foothills, something caught her eye.
Two miles away, nestled at the base of a jagged sandstone ridge where the badlands bled into the river basin, a massive cylindrical pillar of pale-blue energy was humming against the sky.
...A Safe Zone.
Seraphina scoffed as she had zero interest in cowering inside an administrative resting dome since the ten-minute timers were traps for wounded dogs.
Yet as she narrowed her ruby eyes, peering through the shimmering heat distortion at the center of the blue dome...
Her jaw dropped.
"No way," Seraphina muttered, her eyebrows shooting up into her hairline. "Are you kidding me?"
She kicked off the dirt, striding toward the blue beacon with quick angry steps.
Inside the perimeter of the Safe Zone, the atmosphere was offensively peaceful.
The cerulean barrier did not just suppress external mana, it completely neutralized environmental heat, dropping the temperature down to a cool breezy twenty-two degrees.
A tiny, crystal-clear spring bubbled up from a crack in the sandstone, feeding a small lush grove of dwarf date palms that rustled softly in the artificial breeze.
Sitting cross-legged on a smooth, flat boulder beside the water, completely bare-chested, was Valerius Sterling.
The young heir of House Sterling wore only a pair of lightweight canvas combat trousers rolled up to his calves, his pale, lean torso showing several old dueling scars.
In his right hand, he held a freshly cleaved coconut, sipping casually from a hollow reed straw while humming a jaunty off-key tune from a movie he had seen recently.
’How do I get Silas’s number...?’ Valerius mused, staring lazily at the rippling surface of the spring.
It was a serious dilemma.
They were friends.
They had shared food, survived in a secret realm, and Silas also took most of his treasure. What kind of respectable friend didn’t have his comrade’s direct comm-line?
It wasn’t like Valerius had a massive circle of confidants to lean on.
Despite his noble title, most high scions avoided him because of his family’s chaotic history.

The only person who consistently tolerated his presence was Seraphina and when he had cornered Sera in the staging pavilion this morning, politely asking for Silas’s contact information, she had immediately bristled, bared her teeth like a feral badger, and threatened to singe his eyebrows off if he ever asked again.

’She’s guarding that comm-code like it’s an ancient relic,’ Valerius thought with a quiet rueful sigh, taking another sip of coconut water. ’She probably keeps it locked in an adamantine vault inside her vanity table. What a ridiculous wo—’
WHOOSH... SLAM!
The cerulean barrier rippled violently as a figure tore through the threshold, landing heavily on the grass three paces from his boulder.
Seraphina Bloom stood there, covered in soot, her leather armor radiating residual furnace heat and her ruby eyes blazing with fury.
"Valerius!" she roared, her voice echoing off the palm fronds. "What in the seven hells are you doing in here?!"
Valerius didn’t even drop his coconut. He slowly lifted his head, blinking through his messy dark hair, offering her a lazy lopsided grin.

"Oh. Hey, Sera," Valerius greeted her pleasantly, taking a slow sip through his reed straw. "You look warm. Want some coconut? The water in here is actually shockingly sweet. I think the administrative staff seeded the aquifer with glucose filters."

"Are you out of your mind?!" Seraphina snapped, storming toward him, her combat boots tearing up the manicured grass. "People are tearing each other to pieces across this sector! Kara White just vaporized a mountain peak and I just slaughtered the Khemet people... Then you are sitting here half-naked, drinking fruit juice like you’re on a holiday in the southern archipelago?!"
’Oh so she was the one that did that? It’s not surprising though.’
Sera was really strong.

"Well, yeah," Valerius said, shrugging with shameless ease. "Who wants to fight in this heat? Fighting is sweaty. It’s loud... People keep shouting ridiculous technique names before they swing so I decided about four minutes after landfall that this whole tournament was an administrative disaster."
"I am going to incinerate your stupid face," Seraphina growled, rearing her right fist back with her jaw clenching as she prepared to unleash a point-blank blast of solar flame.
CLICK!
Nothing happened.
Seraphina froze, staring down at her unblemished inert knuckles in wide-eyed bewilderment.
Valerius pointed his reed straw at the glowing blue ceiling above them.

"Safe Zone, Sera," Valerius reminded her gently, shaking his head. "This is a non-combat zone and all internal offensive mana pathways are artificially dampened by the field spell... You couldn’t light a candle in here if you had a box of matches."
Seraphina’s teeth ground together with a harsh scrape with her fingers curled into tight fists as the veins stood out along her forearms.
"I don’t need magic to break your jaw," she hissed, taking a heavy step forward.
"Don’t shoot the messenger!" Valerius yelped, leaning backward on his boulder and holding the coconut up like a shield. "I’m running an essential public utility here!"
Before Seraphina could close the distance, the cerulean barrier flickered once more.
THUD!
A second figure dropped into the oasis, landing cleanly on the grass beside the spring.
It was Rook Sterling, Valerius’s first cousin and the second representative of House Sterling.
Rook wore full matte-black reconnaissance gear, three optical scopes strapped across his chest harness, and a thick leather courier pouch slung over his shoulder.
He looked exhausted, covered in a fine layer of gray dust with his knuckles scraped raw from climbing the rocky escarpments.
"Val," Rook grunted, unzipping the pouch and pulling out a thick sheaf of high-resolution photographic plates. "I swept the northern rim and the lower caldera corridors... Got the full spread."
"Beautiful work, cousin," Valerius said, setting his coconut down and taking the stack of images with a bright smile. "See? Professionalism."
Seraphina looked between the two cousins, her brow furrowing in deep, profound confusion.
"What is this? What are you doing with optical prints?"
Valerius flipped through the top three photographs, nodding approvingly before glancing up at her.

"Look, Sera, let’s be realistic," Valerius said, his tone turning surprisingly grounded. "Rook and I are solid casters, but we aren’t equipped to box with the apex freaks in this bracket... You’ve got Kara White throwing attacks around, Alexander running loose with his royal ego, and you running around turning people into chandeliers. If Rook and I try to play the hero, we’re leaving this arena in pine boxes."
Seraphina crossed her arms with her ruby eyes narrowing.
’Bullshit,’ she thought immediately.
Valerius was strong.
He was significantly stronger than he ever gave himself credit for.
He possessed a dense Second Stage core and an extraordinarily rare wind affinity that also let him redirect impacts with terrifying precision.
During their childhood sparring matches, he had deflected her fireballs more times than she cared to remember.
The only real issue with Valerius was his head.
Ever since they were seven years old, he had suffered from a pathological urge to downplay his own capabilities and Seraphina knew exactly whose fault that was... His mother.

That wretched venomous woman had spent a decade constantly telling Valerius he was an unremarkable, second-rate spare before she eventually packed her bags, emptied half the family’s western bank vaults, and ran off with an Albion guild merchant.

The emotional rot had set deep into his bones so Seraphina had sworn years ago that if she ever crossed paths with the woman in an open street, she would crush her skull against the curb without asking for a name first.
Unfortunately, the woman had vanished into the unregulated border territories, leaving Valerius with this pathetic self-deprecating complex.

"So," Valerius continued, fanning the photographs out across the flat surface of the rock. "We adapted... We’re providing an essential market service which is tactical intelligence. We’ve mapped the coordinates, defensive formations, and lingering mana signatures of every major fighter left on the board. You looking for someone specific?"
Seraphina paused.
Her initial instinct was to tell him to choke on his coconut, but practical reality asserted itself.
Sector Forty-Four covered thousands of square miles of fractured badlands, underground aqueducts, and shifting dunes.
Combing the entire zone on foot while burning her core to run down signatures would take hours.
"Alexander," Seraphina said. "Where is the Crown Prince?"
Valerius’s eyebrows twitched as a slow knowing smirk spread across his face.
"Ah," he murmured. "Going for the big fish."
He shuffled through the stack of photographs, his fingers sliding two plates aside before pulling out a crisp aerial print taken from the high crags above the western mesa.
He held it out...
Seraphina stepped forward, snatching the photograph from his fingers.
The image was sharp as it showed a desolate, shadow-draped ravine nestled deep within the jagged basalt towers of the western rim.
Leaning against a massive, cracked granite monolith in the center of the clearing was Crown Prince Alexander.
Even in the still print, his arrogant blue-haired silhouette was unmistakable.
Seraphina flipped the paper over.
Written across the back in Rook’s precise, military shorthand were six lines of dense topographical coordinates, elevation markers, and wind-shear vectors.
One needed an advanced comprehension of military cartography to decipher the route, but Seraphina had been drilled in terrain navigation since she was six.
She understood the map instantly.
’Well good work, not like I’ll ever tell him that...’
She moved to tuck the photograph into the inner pocket of her strike cuirass—
SWOOSH!
Valerius’s fingers snapped forward, catching the corner of the print and pulling it back out of her reach.
Seraphina’s ruby eyes flared with dangerous heat. "What do you think you’re doing?"
"Business is business, Sera," Valerius said smoothly, tapping the edge of the print against his knee. "Information has value... You want the coordinates, you have to pay the toll."
"With what?" Seraphina snapped, crossing her arms. "Do you see a phone on my hip? What am I supposed to pay you with, desert rocks?"

"Non-aggression," Valerius answered immediately. "A formal verbal covenant. You agree that House Bloom will not target, engage, or eliminate the representatives of House Sterling for the remainder of this tournament. We stay in our little oasis, you go hunt the royal family, and nobody gets burned..."

Kara White just vaporized a mountain peak and I just slaughtered the Khemet people...
Then you are sitting here half-naked, drinking fruit juice like you’re on a holiday in the southern archipelago?!"
’Oh so she was the one that did that?
It’s not surprising though.’
Sera was really strong.
"Well, yeah," Valerius said, shrugging with shameless ease.
"Who wants to fight in this heat?
Fighting is sweaty.
It’s loud...
People keep shouting ridiculous technique names before they swing so I decided about four minutes after landfall that this whole tournament was an administrative disaster."
"I am going to incinerate your stupid face," Seraphina growled, rearing her right fist back with her jaw clenching as she prepared to unleash a point-blank blast of solar flame.
CLICK!
Nothing happened.
Seraphina froze, staring down at her unblemished inert knuckles in wide-eyed bewilderment.
Valerius pointed his reed straw at the glowing blue ceiling above them.
"Safe Zone, Sera," Valerius reminded her gently, shaking his head.
"This is a non-combat zone and all internal offensive mana pathways are artificially dampened by the field spell...
You couldn’t light a candle in here if you had a box of matches."
Seraphina’s teeth ground together with a harsh scrape with her fingers curled into tight fists as the veins stood out along her forearms.
"I don’t need magic to break your jaw," she hissed, taking a heavy step forward.
"Don’t shoot the messenger!" Valerius yelped, leaning backward on his boulder and holding the coconut up like a shield.
"I’m running an essential public utility here!"
Before Seraphina could close the distance, the cerulean barrier flickered once more.
THUD!
A second figure dropped into the oasis, landing cleanly on the grass beside the spring.
It was Rook Sterling, Valerius’s first cousin and the second representative of House Sterling.
Rook wore full matte-black reconnaissance gear, three optical scopes strapped across his chest harness, and a thick leather courier pouch slung over his shoulder.
He looked exhausted, covered in a fine layer of gray dust with his knuckles scraped raw from climbing the rocky escarpments.
"Val," Rook grunted, unzipping the pouch and pulling out a thick sheaf of high-resolution photographic plates.
"I swept the northern rim and the lower caldera corridors...
Got the full spread."
"Beautiful work, cousin," Valerius said, setting his coconut down and taking the stack of images with a bright smile.
"See?
Professionalism."
Seraphina looked between the two cousins, her brow furrowing in deep, profound confusion.
"What is this?
What are you doing with optical prints?"
Valerius flipped through the top three photographs, nodding approvingly before glancing up at her.
"Look, Sera, let’s be realistic," Valerius said, his tone turning surprisingly grounded.
"Rook and I are solid casters, but we aren’t equipped to box with the apex freaks in this bracket...
You’ve got Kara White throwing attacks around, Alexander running loose with his royal ego, and you running around turning people into chandeliers.
If Rook and I try to play the hero, we’re leaving this arena in pine boxes."
Seraphina crossed her arms with her ruby eyes narrowing.
’Bullshit,’ she thought immediately.
Valerius was strong.
He was significantly stronger than he ever gave himself credit for.
He possessed a dense Second Stage core and an extraordinarily rare wind affinity that also let him redirect impacts with terrifying precision.
During their childhood sparring matches, he had deflected her fireballs more times than she cared to remember.
The only real issue with Valerius was his head.
Ever since they were seven years old, he had suffered from a pathological urge to downplay his own capabilities and Seraphina knew exactly whose fault that was...
His mother.

That wretched venomous woman had spent a decade constantly telling Valerius he was an unremarkable, second-rate spare before she eventually packed her bags, emptied half the family’s western bank vaults, and ran off with an Albion guild merchant.

The emotional rot had set deep into his bones so Seraphina had sworn years ago that if she ever crossed paths with the woman in an open street, she would crush her skull against the curb without asking for a name first.
Unfortunately, the woman had vanished into the unregulated border territories, leaving Valerius with this pathetic self-deprecating complex.
"So," Valerius continued, fanning the photographs out across the flat surface of the rock.
"We adapted...
We’re providing an essential market service which is tactical intelligence.
We’ve mapped the coordinates, defensive formations, and lingering mana signatures of every major fighter left on the board.
You looking for someone specific?"
Seraphina paused.
Her initial instinct was to tell him to choke on his coconut, but practical reality asserted itself.
Sector Forty-Four covered thousands of square miles of fractured badlands, underground aqueducts, and shifting dunes.
Combing the entire zone on foot while burning her core to run down signatures would take hours.
"Alexander," Seraphina said.
"Where is the Crown Prince?"
Valerius’s eyebrows twitched as a slow knowing smirk spread across his face.
"Ah," he murmured.
"Going for the big fish."
He shuffled through the stack of photographs, his fingers sliding two plates aside before pulling out a crisp aerial print taken from the high crags above the western mesa.
He held it out...
Seraphina stepped forward, snatching the photograph from his fingers.
The image was sharp as it showed a desolate, shadow-draped ravine nestled deep within the jagged basalt towers of the western rim.
Leaning against a massive, cracked granite monolith in the center of the clearing was Crown Prince Alexander.
Even in the still print, his arrogant blue-haired silhouette was unmistakable.
Seraphina flipped the paper over.
Written across the back in Rook’s precise, military shorthand were six lines of dense topographical coordinates, elevation markers, and wind-shear vectors.
One needed an advanced comprehension of military cartography to decipher the route, but Seraphina had been drilled in terrain navigation since she was six.
She understood the map instantly.
’Well good work, not like I’ll ever tell him that...’
She moved to tuck the photograph into the inner pocket of her strike cuirass—
SWOOSH!
Valerius’s fingers snapped forward, catching the corner of the print and pulling it back out of her reach.
Seraphina’s ruby eyes flared with dangerous heat.
"What do you think you’re doing?"
"Business is business, Sera," Valerius said smoothly, tapping the edge of the print against his knee.
"Information has value...
You want the coordinates, you have to pay the toll."
"With what?" Seraphina snapped, crossing her arms.
"Do you see a phone on my hip?
What am I supposed to pay you with, desert rocks?"
"Non-aggression," Valerius answered immediately.
"A formal verbal covenant.
You agree that House Bloom will not target, engage, or eliminate the representatives of House Sterling for the remainder of this tournament.
We stay in our little oasis, you go hunt the royal family, and nobody gets burned..."

chapters.title: Chapter 571: A Force Of Nature [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Seraphina let out a loud mocking scoff.

"Are you an idiot, Valerius?" she sneered. "What good is a verbal agreement in the middle of a succession exhibition...? If I promise with my mouth, what stops me from turning around and melting your coconut the second we step outside this blue circle?"
Valerius smiled, pointing a single finger up toward the floating lenses hovering outside the cerulean barrier.

"Because of that," Valerius said, his voice dropping into a quiet remarkably shrewd tone. "Over one billion active viewers. Every high magistrate, every corporate guild master, and every sovereign monarch is watching this exact frame... If the proud heir of House Bloom makes a solemn, public pledge on a live global feed and breaks it five minutes later like a petty cutpurse, your mother’s reputation will be dragged through the mud for the next twenty years as the public will assume your entire clan’s word is worthless and Etilga Bloom would rather swallow broken glass than let the world think her house lacks honor."
Seraphina stared at him with her jaw locking tight.
’Clever bastard,’ she thought, her teeth grinding together.
He had calculated the political pressure perfectly.

In private, she would have broken his nose and taken the map without a second thought but here? Under the gaze of the World Council? Her mother would skin her alive if she publicly demonstrated bad faith.
"Fine," Seraphina spat, snatching the photograph from his hand with a sharp violent yank. "House Bloom will not touch the Sterling dogs. Happy?"
"Ecstatic," Valerius beamed, raising his coconut in a cheerful toast. "Pleasure doing business with you, Lady Sera."
Seraphina spun on her heel, marching toward the edge of the cerulean barrier.
As she crossed the threshold into the open desert, she raised her left hand over her shoulder, extending her middle finger straight toward his face without looking back.
"Fuck you, Val," she called out over the wind.
BOOOOOOM!
The instant her boots cleared the Safe Zone, the mana suppression dropped and dense roaring crimson flames detonated from the soles of her combat boots.
The propulsion blasted her thirty feet into the air, clearing the low sandstone ridges in an explosive arc-like leap,
She hit the crest of a massive dune two hundred paces out, her boots carving lines through the sand before she pushed off again, rocketing forward like a red comet skipping across the desert floor.
She couldn’t sustain true flight like a Wind caster, but her explosive flame-boosted bounds covered hundreds of yards per second, tearing a straight smoking line toward the western mesa.
Back inside the cool, breezy oasis, Valerius took another slow sip of his coconut water through the reed straw.
He looked out through the blue barrier, watching the distant plume of red smoke disappear into the jagged basalt towers.

’I wonder how her scrap with the Crown Prince is going to turn out,’ Valerius mused with an amused grin touching his lips. ’Alexander is an arrogant psychopath, but Sera is a force of nature... I’ll make sure to watch the full broadcast highlights once I get back home.’
Four miles to the west, nestled within the deep shadow-choked throat of a narrow granite ravine...
The massive basalt towers flanking the pass rose three hundred feet into the purple sky, blocking out the harsh glare of the upper rift and casting the canyon floor in perpetual gray twilight.
Leaning casually against the flat face of a colossal cracked granite monolith was Crown Prince Alexander.
His immaculate blue hair was swept back from his brow with his regal high-bridged features completely composed.

He wore the tailored deep-indigo combat tunic of House Castellian, trimmed with gold thread and imperial star-iron filigree and clamped tightly around both of his forearms were the heavy void-black Star-Iron Suppression Rings...
The restraints that forcefully choked down two-thirds of his internal mana channels, artificially restricting his native Fourth Stage power to the Second Stage.
He held a slender polished combat rapier in his right hand, using the point to lazily carve intricate runes into the bedrock between his boots.
Despite that, Alexander did not look up when the wind shifted.
THUD!
Seraphina dropped out of the sky, landing heavily in the center of the ravine twenty paces away with her boots kicking up a sharp cloud of dry shale.
Alexander’s rapier paused mid-stroke.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
He slowly lifted his chin, his cold eyes sliding over her soot-stained armor and windblown crimson hair with detached boredom.

"Turn around and walk away, girl," Alexander said. "I have zero interest in squandering my stamina on secondary house squabbles... If you leave now, I will allow you to keep your transponder intact until the final compression."
To punctuate his command, Alexander’s suppressed Second Stage core surged.
WOO!
A suffocating aura of heavy blue mana rolled outward from his frame, flattening the loose dust across the ravine and pressing against Seraphina’s shoulders with the weight of an iron ceiling.
It was a demonstration of dominance... the kind of overwhelming spiritual pressure that normally brought lesser nobles to their knees but Seraphina didn’t move.
"Heh."
Instead, her lips slowly peeled back into a wide, venomous, utterly feral smile.
"You think you’re scary, Alexander?" Seraphina whispered.
WHOOOOOSH!
Seraphina Bloom released her core.
A violent pillar of incandescent crimson and solar-white flame erupted from her frame, roaring straight up toward the basalt cliffs.
The staggering power of her spiritual pressure violently shattered Alexander’s blue aura like brittle glass, blowing the royal pressure completely out of the canyon.
The concussive expansion struck the bedrock, spreading deep jagged fissures through the stone that tore twenty yards across the ravine, splintering the monolith behind his back.
Alexander’s pupils violently contracted.
His teeth clamped shut with an audible sound with his knuckles whitening around the hilt of his rapier as the suffocating heat wave washed over his face, singeing the tips of his blue hair.
’What...?!’ Alexander’s mind staggered in shock. ’This presence... this heat... she’s commanding output beyond a standard Second Stage!’
Through the swirling wall of roaring crimson embers, Seraphina took two slow steps forward.
Her ruby eyes locked onto his pale arrogant face, burning with unapologetic contempt.
"Hey, Your Highness..." Seraphina drawled, her voice cutting through the roar of her flames like an executioner’s axe.
"Aren’t you about five years too late to be fighting in this tournament?"
Alexander’s jaw twitched violently with his composure cracking down the middle which only grew worse as Seraphina’s grin widened.
"...You fucking bum."
The insult hung in the narrow throat of the basalt ravine, refusing to dissipate against the dead air.
Alexander’s left eye twitched.
The detached languid boredom that had armored his handsome features completely shattered, peeling back to reveal a vein throbbing violently at the edge of his blue hairline.
The knuckles of his right hand turned the color of bleached bone around the hilt of his rapier with the leather wraps groaning under the sudden clamp of his grip.
SHIIIING!
He put the blade back and drew the blade from its scabbard with a slow deliberate scrape of polished star-iron.

"You insolent loudmouthed little bitch," Alexander snarled, his voice dropping into a low rasp that shed every pretense of restraint. "You think having a famous mother and a dead spirit inside your soul gives you the right to bare your teeth at the crown? I accepted these suppression rings to humiliate Blessed Land on equal footing, not to be lectured by an overbred brat from House Bloom... You want a challenge? Fine. I will carve that smug, filthy tongue right out of your skull and pin it to the monolith."
Seraphina did not back down. She took a slow, deep breath through her nose, drawing the stagnant canyon air into the furnace of her lungs.
HSSSSSSSS!
The ambient temperature within a forty-yard radius spiked instantly, leaping from the dry chill of the shadowed canyon to an oppressive suffocating furnace blast.
The loose pebbles and fine shale resting near the soles of her combat boots began to smoke, their edges glowing cherry-red as radiant waves bled from the seams of her midnight strike cuirass.

"Let’s be clear about one thing, Your Highness," Seraphina said. "On a normal day, out in the open world, with your Fourth Stage core completely unlocked? You would beat me into the dirt... I am not an idiot. I know where I stand on the global ladder, and I haven’t reached the threshold of yours yet."
She tilted her chin up, looking straight into his cold sapphire eyes with her mouth curling into that same razor-sharp mocking smile.
"However... down here? Locked inside those pretty little black cuffs? Restricted to the exact same Second Stage output as the rest of the children?"
Her ruby eyes narrowed, burning with malice.

"If you don’t come at me with every single scrap of power your choked-down channels can push out... if you hesitate for even a tenth of a second because of your precious royal pride, I’m afraid this fight is going to end before you can even remember how to beg."
Alexander’s jaw clicked shut as he didn’t answer with words.
He moved instead.
BOOM!
The granite bedrock beneath the Crown Prince’s heels shattered into powder under the explosive release of his suppressed Second Stage core.
He crossed the twenty-pace gap in the span of a single heartbeat, moving at a linear velocity that defied the natural limits of the physical body.

His indigo combat tunic turned into a dark blur, cutting through the stagnant heat haze with terrifying perfection as the tip of his rapier became a needle-point of screaming condensed royal-blue mana, aimed dead-center at the soft hollow of Seraphina’s throat.

It was a thrust executed with the flawless machine-like precision of the Castellian swordsmen of the past... filled with a lethality designed to end the exchange before the opponent’s nervous system could fire a defensive reflex.
Yet, Seraphina’s ruby eyes simply flashed and her core violently contracted.
Alexander’s combat instincts honed by thousands of hours of life-and-death drills suddenly screamed an emergency alarm behind his temples.
His pupils contracted as he registered the sudden catastrophic drop in local atmospheric pressure and without a second of hesitation, the Prince aborted his linear charge.
He planted the toe of his front boot, torqueing his hips with brutal agility, and propelled himself forty feet straight up into the air.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
In the exact footprint where Alexander had been lunging half a heartbeat earlier, the earth detonated into an inferno.
A massive spiraling cage of superheated crimson fire erupted from the bedrock, wrapping around Seraphina’s silhouette like towering, interlocking petals of solid flame.
The construct twisted upward with hydraulic violence, forming the tightly shut bud of a monstrous primordial flower made of roaring flames.
High in the air, Alexander looked down as he reached the apex of his leap with a cold drop of sweat rolling down his temple and instantly vaporizing in the rising heat.

’If that swallowed me...’ his mind calculated with sudden clarity, ’if I had committed to the thrust and let that cage close around my limbs, the kinetic heat alone would have melted the meat off my ribs before my defensive aura could stabilize.’
Down below, the phenomenon evolved.
WHOOM!

The deep roaring crimson of the closed flower petals began to shift as the outer edges hissed, the combustion accelerating past three thousand degrees as the fire began to bleed, purify, and bleach itself into a celestial silver-white.
The heat radiating from the construct was no longer volcanic... it was stellar.
Alexander descended, his boots touching down thirty paces away on the sun-baked sand at the base of the canyon wall.
CRRRRRRRK!
The instant his boots made contact with the earth, the ground beneath him groaned as the sand had ceased to be loose silt.

The radiant temperature bleeding off the white construct had vitrified the top six inches of the ground, turning the earth around him into a brittle fractured crust of smoking, translucent green glass that cracked like thin ice beneath his weight.
The Prince stared across the clearing, his heart hammering against his ribs.
Slowly and gracefully, the tightly coiled petals of the massive silver-white flower began to peel backward.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
The fire did not rage wildly anymore, it folded outward like delicate, luminous silk with each massive petal weeping trails of white plasma as it opened to reveal the figure standing at its center.
Seraphina emerged from the core of the bloom.
Her crimson hair had fully transformed, burning with the weightless radiance of pure liquid silver that floated softly in the heat.
The runic mark carved into the left side of her face burned with cold unearthly light, tracking down the curve of her jawline and disappearing beneath the high leather collar of her cuirass.

She stood balanced lightly on the balls of her feet with her single-edged hunting dagger resting in a loose casual reverse-grip in her right hand, her ruby eyes glowing with the untamed fury of the Primordial Fire Spirit fused directly to her marrow.
Alexander’s throat went bone-dry.

’This isn’t an Awakened trait,’ his mind screamed with his grip on the rapier tightening until his knuckles ached. ’She’s channeling a tenfold multiplier right now! I cannot let her dictate the pace... I really need to—’
BOOM!
He didn’t get to finish the thought as the ground beneath Seraphina’s boots didn’t just vanished!
A shockwave of silver-white fire roared out from beneath her soles, launching her forward like an artillery shell fired at point-blank range.
Alexander’s regal face twisted with grim desperate focus but he didn’t run.
He slammed his left hand into a complex somatic seal with his suppressed Second Stage core burning red-hot against the restrictive bite of the Star-Iron Suppression Rings clamped to his forearms.
"Great Vaultl Of Water!"
RUMBLE-CRASH!

Alexander descended, his boots touching down thirty paces away on the sun-baked sand at the base of the canyon wall.
CRRRRRRRK!
The instant his boots made contact with the earth, the ground beneath him groaned as the sand had ceased to be loose silt.

The radiant temperature bleeding off the white construct had vitrified the top six inches of the ground, turning the earth around him into a brittle fractured crust of smoking, translucent green glass that cracked like thin ice beneath his weight.
The Prince stared across the clearing, his heart hammering against his ribs.
Slowly and gracefully, the tightly coiled petals of the massive silver-white flower began to peel backward.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
The fire did not rage wildly anymore, it folded outward like delicate, luminous silk with each massive petal weeping trails of white plasma as it opened to reveal the figure standing at its center.
Seraphina emerged from the core of the bloom.
Her crimson hair had fully transformed, burning with the weightless radiance of pure liquid silver that floated softly in the heat.
The runic mark carved into the left side of her face burned with cold unearthly light, tracking down the curve of her jawline and disappearing beneath the high leather collar of her cuirass.

She stood balanced lightly on the balls of her feet with her single-edged hunting dagger resting in a loose casual reverse-grip in her right hand, her ruby eyes glowing with the untamed fury of the Primordial Fire Spirit fused directly to her marrow.
Alexander’s throat went bone-dry.
’This isn’t an Awakened trait,’ his mind screamed with his grip on the rapier tightening until his knuckles ached. ’She’s channeling a tenfold multiplier right now!
I cannot let her dictate the pace...
I really need to—’
BOOM!
He didn’t get to finish the thought as the ground beneath Seraphina’s boots didn’t just vanished!
A shockwave of silver-white fire roared out from beneath her soles, launching her forward like an artillery shell fired at point-blank range.
Alexander’s regal face twisted with grim desperate focus but he didn’t run.
He slammed his left hand into a complex somatic seal with his suppressed Second Stage core burning red-hot against the restrictive bite of the Star-Iron Suppression Rings clamped to his forearms.
"Great Vaultl Of Water!"
RUMBLE-CRASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 572: In The Sands [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: PSSH!
From the deep moisture veins running beneath the cracked bedrock of the canyon, an immense torrent of pressurized deep-blue water violently erupted through the fissures.
The torrent obeyed the Prince’s will, coiling upward in an overlapping spiral that completely encased Alexander within a massive rotating fifteen-foot sphere of pressurized heavy water.
’This is it...’
The outer shell of the sphere spun at hundreds of miles per hour, creating a churning hydraulic barrier specifically designed to smother, suffocate, and disperse high-temperature elemental strikes.
’Just because I limited my core to the second stage doesn’t mean that I can’t cast proper spells...’
It was a masterclass in elemental defense, truly a textbook application of water supremacy meant to drown any incoming flame assault in an instant.
However...
It didn’t matter.
Seraphina did not alter her trajectory, instead she dove straight into the rotating wall of water.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The collision generated an explosion of superheated steam that completely swallowed the ravine.
The three-thousand-degree silver-white flames coating Seraphina’s dagger and flesh met the heavy water, instantly flash-boiling thousands of gallons into a deafening screech.
The water however did not extinguish her as her Primordial Spirit tore clean through the hydraulic pressure like an iron spike through wet paper.
She punched straight through the boiling core of the sphere with her silver hair trailing steam and her reverse-gripped hunting dagger flashing like a falling star.
’How... It’s my vault!’
Alexander’s eyes dilated in shock as she breached his inner sanctum.
He thrust his rapier forward with everything his body possessed, pouring his imperial blue mana into the steel to meet her blade head-on!
CLANG-BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The weapons collided and the physical impact sounded like two armored locomotives colliding at high velocity.

A concussive shockwave detonated from the point where the curved hunting dagger met the fluted steel of the rapier as the displaced pressure blew the remaining thousands of gallons of boiling water outward in a violent horizontal ring, shattering the surrounding basalt spires into falling boulders and sending an earthquake tearing through the foundations of the canyon.
Through the screaming curtain of white steam and flying sparks, their eyes locked.
Alexander’s teeth were bared in a furious straining grimace with the veins in his neck bulging as his knees groaned beneath the crushing downward leverage of her strike.
And Seraphina...
Seraphina simply smiled.
Her silver hair whipped wildly in the boiling tempest, her ruby eyes blazing with wild amusement as the silver-white fire along her blade began to aggressively eat through the aura of his rapier.
"Told you," she whispered with her voice cutting through the ringing steel. "Let’s see you defend against this."𝐟𝗿𝐞𝚎𝚠𝐞𝚋𝕟𝐨𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝕔𝕠𝚖
The amber numerals of the overhead projection hung frozen against the vaulted sapphire barrier, suspended forty feet above the scorched sandstone floor of the Safe Zone.
Every pulse of the timer shaved away fractions of a second with cold, mechanical indifference, casting long pale shadows across the naked stone shelf.
Inside the perimeter, the heat was suffocating.
Unlike the lush, shaded depression three leagues to the northwest where natural mountain seepage fed date palms and cold pools, this place was situated upon a raw slab of wind-scoured quartz bedrock.
There were no trees and there were no moisture here either.
There was only the low static sound of the administrative barrier, separating fifty square yards of dead air from the blinding furnace-blast gales of Sector Forty-Four.
Outside that glowing perimeter, the desert rolled out in endless wind-rippled swells of yellow silica and shattered shale, completely stripped of life.
Jax Sterling-Cross sat hunched on a low outcrop near the northern threshold of the dome with his back wedged tight against the granite spine of the mesa.
His breathing came in uneven, shallow hitches that rattled with a wet wheeze against the roof of his mouth.
’I fucking hate this place...’
RIIIIP!
He caught the hem of his gray inner tunic between his teeth, yanking his head back with a sharp violent jerk that tore a long uneven ribbon of coarse linen free from the seam.
"Fuck."

His jaw throbbed from the clench and between his knees, he balanced a dented brass tin of field-grade coagulant salve, the pungent medicinal reek of mint and crushed bitter-root biting through the dry air.
His entire left forearm was a ruined blistering catastrophe.
The armored ballistic weave of his combat tunic had been dissolved into tacky, bubbling threads of melted polymer, bonded directly into the charred meat of his skin.
Where the fabric had peeled away, the flesh was weeping a cloudy alkaline fluid that dripped steadily onto the stone between his boots.
"Fucking butchers," Jax muttered, his voice cracking into a dry gravelly rasp.
He dug two calloused fingers into the tin, scooping out a heavy dollop of the pungent green paste and he didn’t hesitate.
He drove his fingers down across the exposed, weeping muscle fibers of his wrist.
TZZZZZZZZ!

A sharp violent sizzle rose from his skin as the alkaline salve met the lingering acidic toxins as a jolt of white-hot agony shot up the radial nerve of his arm, bypassing his spine and slamming directly into his teeth.
’Again and again...’
Jax clamped his jaw shut so hard the enamel ground together with an audible crunch with his temples bulging like blue twine beneath his damp hairline.
A muffled animal groan vibrated behind his ribs, but he forced his hand forward, smearing the thick grease from his knuckles up to his elbow joint.
Above his head, the timer flickered.
Four minutes and twelve seconds of artificial sanctuary before the magic circle disintegrated, dumping his battered frame straight back into the open dunes.
His thoughts drifted back to the narrow shadow-draped ravine two miles out where the disaster had unfolded.
He had been tracking an erratic mana signature, moving low along the floor of a dry gully, when the air itself had turned into a chemical weapon.
’Genevieve de Montmirail...’

The primary skirmisher from the Europa Directorate hadn’t even bothered to draw the heavy fluted rapier sheathed at her hip as she had simply stood atop the crag in that pristine high-collared coat of imperial teal with her emerald-green hair spilling across her shoulders like woven silk.

Even in the dead center of a high-stakes multi-continental succession tournament, she carried herself with the effortless poise of an aristocrat attending a private salon in the upper districts of Europa.
Jax let out a short self-deprecating grunt, spitting a loose thread of linen onto the shale.
’She’s quite a beauty.’
A man would have to be blind or dead not to recognize the striking beauty of the woman.

The pale, immaculate line of her jaw, the cool, mocking detachment in her gray eyes, the way her tailored uniform accentuated an athletic grace... It was the kind of presence that made an unrefined soldier freeze for half a heartbeat before he remembered where his hands were.
Then, with an elegant and almost bored flick of her lace-gloved index finger, she had exhaled a cloud of translucent emerald-tinted mist.

The airborne vapor had touched his field breastplate, and within two seconds, eight inches of hardened star-iron had liquefied into smoking corrosive sludge, eating straight through to his collarbone.
Jax gave the linen bandage a vicious final tug, knotting the ends with his teeth and his right thumb.
"Pretty face," he spat, rubbing the back of his hand across his dry mouth. "Rotten to the core... A venomous little snake from the scalp down."
He pushed himself upright, testing his weight against his left leg.

The knee joint held, though a dull throbbing ache pulsed through his hip as his eyes tracked through the translucent blue sheen of the barrier, scanning the rippling heat mirages that warped the yellow horizon.
His gaze fixed on a jagged, serrated ridge of black basalt rising half a mile to the east.

’Kira better be in position,’ Jax thought, his right hand dropping down to trace the cold knurled grips of the three star-iron cylinders resting in his harness. ’If that girl decides to go rogue out there, we’re dead meat... The Commonwealth didn’t burn through three years of maritime mineral tariffs just to watch us get butchered like sheep in the preliminary round.’

Kira Bennett was feral, half-mad, and possessed the social temperament of a rabid coastal dingo, but her authority over Spirit Beasts was the only reason their delegation hadn’t been wiped in the opening twenty minutes.

If she maintained her perimeter, anchored the lower quartz strata, and used her burrowing beasts to choke the underground approaches, they could turn this exposed flat into a slaughterhouse the moment the dome collapsed.
Jax leaned his shoulder against the granite shelf with a small raspy chuckle vibrating in his throat.

"Let them think I’m crippled," he whispered, his eyes narrowing into cold slits as his knuckles whitened. "Let Europa think they ran me into a corner like an injured mongrel. The moment that clock hits zero and the heavy hitters start tearing each other apart... I’ll show every pompous lord in that Assembly what Australis has been hiding in the southern vaults."
The amber digits flickered down.
Six hundred yards to the southwest, the low thud of heavy paws against sun-baked clay reverberated through the floor of a sunken canyon.
The three Dune Wolves moved in an immaculately coordinated formation, their golden-furred flanks caked in dried red silt that masked their heat signatures against the rising thermal drafts.
Their wide padded paws struck the hard-packed clay without a sound with their bodies staying low to the ground as they skirted the base of a crumbling sandstone escarpment.
Aki rode the alpha, her thighs locked tight around the broad ribs of the beast.
Her fingers held the braided star-iron reins with a steady relaxed tension with her hands circulating mana through the friction knots.

With every bounding leap, the Star-Iron necklace resting against her throat tapped rhythmically against her collarbone, humming with the warm feeling of the compressed mana Silas had woven into the core-gems.
To her right, Leona rode with one hand resting on the pommel of her deep-sea trench-machete, her hazel eyes flicking across the high ridges with the seasoned paranoia of an old trench veteran.
To the left, Maya Da Silva kept her mount at an effortless lope, the void-ivory greaves protecting her shins clicking softly against the wolf’s leather harness.
Maya raised her right hand, extending two fingers toward the horizon.
The three beasts slowed instantly, dropping from an aggressive gallop into a creeping trot before coming to a halt behind the jagged lip of an elevated sandstone ridge.
Maya reached into her chest rig, unhooking a heavy brass-framed pair of long-range tactical binoculars.
She rested her elbows against the rough stone of the ridge, adjusting the knurled focal rings with quick precise movements of her thumbs.
The internal quartz prisms hummed softly, filtering out the blinding glare of the afternoon sun and overlaying a grid-like mana-reticle across the terrain.
The lenses locked onto the flat sandstone terrace eight hundred yards out.

"Target acquired," Maya muttered, her voice sounding low and even. "Blue dome is active... It’s sitting out on the open flats with zero natural defilade and completely exposed. If someone tries to run from that position, they’re eating fire from three directions."
"Who’s inside?" Leona asked, leaning her chest over her wolf’s neck with her hand tightening around the grip of her machete.
Maya adjusted the secondary lens, zooming in on the seated figure propped against the granite shelf.

"Jax Sterling-Cross," Maya said, her amber eyes narrowing behind the eyepieces. "The primary representative from the Commonwealth of Australis... He’s sitting on the rock, patching up his left arm that looks like it got hit by some chemical attack. His chest armor is completely gone, and he’s wrapping the limb in emergency field dressing."
Aki leaned forward, peering over the crest of the ridge. "He’s wounded? Did he run into an ambush on the way to the zone?"

"Could be," Maya replied, lowering the brass binoculars to examine the surrounding dunes with her naked eyes. "The intelligence reports on the Commonwealth were almost non-existent... Australis runs their elite programs under oceanic military secrecy laws. We know they breed Spirit Beasts in the red outback and rely on hybrid beast-merges, but specific combat data on Jax is virtually blank... The reports listed him as an adaptable mid-range warrior, but beyond that, we’re flying completely blind."

"A wounded dog in a corner is the one that takes your fingers," Leona muttered with her eyes scanning the shimmering heat haze. "He knows the timer is bleeding out so he wouldn’t be sitting out in the open like a target dummy unless he had someone watching his back from the sand."
Leona wasn’t wrong at all.
