chapters.title: Chapter 573: Imminent War [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Stay sharp," Maya cautioned, turning her head to meet Aki’s gaze. "I don’t like the feel of this flat... It’s too quiet. A lone, bleeding scion sitting inside an open-air Safe Zone is the oldest bait-trap in the manual so keep your reins gathered."
Aki nodded, her jaw setting with quiet resolve.
"Understood."
They urged the mounts forward, descending the reverse slope of the ridge and cutting through the mouth of a dry wash to close the distance.
They slowed their advance two hundred yards out, using a series of fractured shale shelves to break their line of sight.
Aki’s gaze swept across the sweeping yellow dunes flanking the blue dome.
The sand was immaculate as there were no tracks, no disturbed silt, and no obvious mana signatures bleeding into the sky.
Yet the hair on the back of Aki’s forearms stood straight up.

’There has to be someone here,’ Aki thought, her pulse picking up a steady rhythm against her ribs. ’A Safe Zone in the open desert is a focal point so everyone knows the timers. If Jax was chased here, whoever burned his armor wouldn’t just turn around and walk away to let him recover.’
She looked around, her eyes darting between the empty ridges with an expression of open puzzled frustration.
Where were they hiding? In the rock? Under the silt?
Maya caught the look on Aki’s face and let out a soft chuckle beneath her breath.
"Don’t strain your neck, Princess," Maya said, the corner of her mouth twitching with quiet amusement. "You look like a barn owl trying to spot a mouse in a wheat field. Hold your reins..."
Maya swung her leg over the back of her mount, her combat boots hitting the coarse sand with a solid muted crunch.
She rolled her broad shoulders, the void-ivory plates along her collar shifting smoothly over her linen tunic.
"The surface can lie," Maya said, rolling her neck until the joints popped with dull wet thuds. "The earth doesn’t... If there’s steel or bone waiting in these dunes, the bedrock knows about it."
Aki watched her carefully.
She raised her right hand, tapping into the Star-Iron necklace resting against her chest.
VUUUM!
A fine microscopic trickle of water-mana, refined and compressed through her temporary pathways, flowed upward through her carotid channels and into the fluid membranes of her eyes.
Her vision sharpened instantly.
The harsh, blinding glare of the desert sun softened, the heat mirages pulling back like thin gauze, allowing her to see the micro-currents of atmospheric density curling over the sand.
Something heavy was hanging in the air just ahead like a stagnant pressure waiting to snap.
Maya took two paces forward, stepping out onto the open flat.
She closed her eyes and then drew a slow deliberate breath through her nose with her chest expanding beneath her cuirass.
"Haah..."
Her Second Stage Purple Core flared with a deep violet hum.
THUD!
Maya took a single, deliberate step forward, planting the heel of her heavy combat boot into the crust of the desert floor.
For one fraction of a second, the world seemed to lose all color as the yellow of the sand, the blue of the sky, and the purple hue of the distant clouds drained away into a cold monochrome slate.
RUMBLE!
A subtle high-frequency vibration tore outward from her heel in a perfect, three-hundred-and-sixty-degree radial wave.
The shockwave traveled through the dense granite beneath the dunes, mapping every void, every hollow, and every foreign mass resting within four hundred yards.
Maya’s eyes snapped open, her amber-brown irises flashing with sharp clarity.
"We’ve got guests," Maya barked with her jaw snapping tight. "Three signatures. Two on the eastern ridge, one below the—"
PING!
A sharp snap cut through the air from five hundred yards to the north!
A single blinding streak of high-velocity crimson light tore through the desert air, cutting through the atmosphere with a screaming shriek.
’The hell...?’
It most definitely wasn’t an ordinary round, the projectile was sheathed in a boiling reactive crimson aura that left a spiraling trail of green noxious smoke in its wake.
The round covered five hundred yards in less than a quarter of a heartbeat and Maya didn’t even have time to turn her hips.
Her instincts, honed through years of warfare, took over entirely.
SNAP!
She thrust her left hand forward with her fingers clawing at the empty air.
"Granite Gauntlet..."

The loose sand and rock around her forearm liquefied, rushing upward in a violent spiraling cyclone that solidified into a massive, three-foot-thick gauntlet of dense compressed stone wrapped around her arm.
CRACK!

The high-velocity round slammed directly into the palm of the stone gauntlet and Maya’s boots were driven four inches into the bedrock by the impact with the shockwave blowing the sand away from her knees in a violent circle.
The bullet didn’t ricochet.
The moment its kinetic momentum halted, the crimson core of the projectile flared with unstable intensity.
’It’s a primer!’ Maya’s mind screamed and thirty feet back, Leona’s combat instincts fired simultaneously.
WHOOSH!
Leona didn’t waste a syllable.

She lunged horizontally off her wolf, her right arm wrapping around Aki’s waist with bruising force, yanking the First Princess clean out of the saddle as she detonated a pressurized burst of jade wind-mana beneath her boots.
They were thrown backward twenty yards through the air.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The bullet detonated with the concussive fury of an artillery shell as a massive twenty-foot fireball of superheated crimson combustion erupted from Maya’s palm, instantly consuming the three Dune Wolves where they stood.
The concussive blast shredded the beasts into bloody mist and flying ash before they could even let out a dying howl.
"MAYA!" Aki screamed through the rushing wind, her eyes wide with horror as Leona hit the dirt and rolled, shielding the Princess with her own armored back.
The black smoke boiled upward smelling thick and foul while carrying the suffocating acidic reek of chemical defoliants.
SWOOS!
From the heart of the smoke cloud, a silhouette vaulted backward.
Maya hit the sand twenty paces back, skidding on the heels of her void-ivory greaves, leaving two smoking trenches through the clay.

The three-foot stone gauntlet covering her left arm was completely gone, shattered into blackened gravel and powdered shale but her actual arm... her bare flesh and her leather bracer was completely intact, protected by the sudden last-second crystallization of her earth-skin.
She shook her hand, wincing slightly as small flecks of a corrosive, bubbling green liquid sizzled against her leather wraps.
"Fucking disgusting..."
She flicked her wrist, shedding the acid onto the sand, where it hissed and ate three inches into the rock in seconds.
’They were waiting for us,’ Maya thought with her breath turning heavy and her amber eyes burning with cold venomous fury. ’And I know the exact bitch who cooked this venom.’
A chemical-reactive shell followed by an airborne vapor of flesh-eating acid.
In the entire roster of the World Council delegations, only one person fought with that specific disgusting blend of alchemical sadism... Genevieve de Montmirail.
Yet as Maya took a defensive crouch, her brow furrowed.

’That shot didn’t have enough mass to pierce an elite earth-shaper,’ she analyzed in a fraction of a second. ’The angle was off and she didn’t aim for my skull or my core. She aimed for the ground between our mounts...’
The realization hit her like ice water.
’The shot wasn’t meant to kill us. It was a beacon. It blew our cover and pinned our coordinates for every hunter within three miles!’
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
The desert air on their northern flank tore open with high-speed movement as Maya’s head snapped toward the smoke cloud.
Through the thinning curtain of black soot, a tall slender silhouette moved through.
"Up!" Maya roared, slapping both palms flat against the desert floor.
"Bulwark!"
RUMBLE-CRASH!
A four-foot-thick eight-foot-tall slab of solid compressed granite tore out of the bedrock between them, rising like a fortress gate!
BOOOOOOM!
A single silver-wrapped thrust from a fluted military rapier slammed dead-center into the granite slab.

The stone completely shattered into thousands of flying fragments under an explosive burst of pale-blue mana and through the exploding rubble, Lucian de Montmirail surged forward like a striking viper!
The primary sword-scion of the Europa Directorate wore a double-breasted coat of midnight-teal, trimmed with silver braid and reinforced with flexible titanium mesh.
His pale sharp-featured face was cold, his ice-blue eyes fixed dead on Maya’s throat as his rapier whistled through the flying stone shards with machine-like lethality but Maya didn’t give ground.
She twisted her hips, her left arm sweeping upward as she pulled three jagged shards of broken granite from the air, transmuting them into stone daggers that shot straight at Lucian’s eyes.
CLANG! CLANG! CLINK!
Lucian’s rapier moved in blinding arcs, parrying all three stone daggers in three-tenths of a second, but the microscopic delay forced him to abort his lunge.
He bounded backward ten paces with his polished leather boots touching the sand without making a sound and his blade settling into an immaculate textbook high-tier dueling guard.

"Pesky little dogs," Lucian said, his voice carrying the smooth, haughty drawl of an aristocrat brushing a cobweb from his lapel. "You survived the drop and you survived the northern berserkers... Admirable grit for low-born Amazonians but your run ends here."
Before Maya could retort, a low vibration rumbled beneath the sand dunes eighty paces to the east.
From the crest of a high yellow dune, Kira Bennett rose slowly from the sand like a specter.
The second representative of Australis wore weathered sand-bleached leathers with her arms bare and covered in intricate spiraling tattoos depicting predatory marsupials and oceanic leviathans.
Her coarse sun-streaked blonde hair was tied back in a messy knot, and her dark eyes were alight with wild feral cunning.
Her hands were locked in an intricate three-stage somatic mudra, her core glowing with a sickly yellow-green resonance.

Beneath the sand, thirty feet directly beneath Lucian’s boots and thirty feet beneath where Aki and Leona were standing... shifting shapes were coiled, waiting for the signal to tear through the crust and drag them into the dark.
Kira’s lips pulled back into a wide, predatory sneer.
"You talk too much, Europa boy," Kira whispered with her fingers shifting to spring the trap...
Lucian didn’t even turn his head.

"I can hear your beasts breathing through the quartz, Australis savage," Lucian called out. "If you think two underground sand crawlers are enough to catch an officer of the Directorate off-guard, your education was even cheaper than your boots..."
Kira’s sneer froze with her jaw clenched tight and her knuckles whitening around her somatic seal.
CLACK! CLACK!𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
From the rocky bluffs seventy paces to the north, two more figures stepped into the harsh sunlight.
The representatives of the Albion Concordat.
Gareth Pendelton stood with a broad arrogant smile plastered across his ruddy handsome face.
He wore the traditional scarlet-and-white dueling tunic of Albion’s Royal Guard, a heavy star-iron basket-hilted broadsword resting casually across his shoulder.

Beside him, leaning with her hip against a cracked granite pillar, was Isolde Vivnr with her slender frame encased in dark blue duel-leathers, a pair of matched silver-plated parrying daggers spinning lazily between her fingers.

"Well, well, well," Gareth chuckled, his rich voice booming across the quiet basin. "Look at the gathering... Australis in the sand, Europa on the flats, and the little runaway Princess caught right in the crosshairs. What a splendid little slaughter this is going to be."
Isolde didn’t smile.
She blew a loose strand of fair hair from her forehead as her cold blue eyes scanned the gathered fighters with boredom.

"Can we just get this over with, Gareth?" Isolde muttered, her voice sounding flat and irritable. "It’s forty degrees out here, my boots are full of silt, and the broadcast relays are hovering right over our heads... Kill who you need to kill so we can get out of here before the tea goes cold."
Gareth turned his head, his smile widening with disappointment.

"Oh, come now, Isolde! Where is your sporting spirit? Don’t you appreciate a proper, old-fashioned royal melee? It’s not every day you get to cross steel with three different continental bloodlines on the same patch of dirt!"
Before Isolde could reply, the air along the western ridge suddenly grew impossibly hot.
HSSSSSSSS!
The loose sand on the western rocks began to smoke.
Stepping onto the highest promontory overlooking the Safe Zone, two figures descended like gods descending to a mortal arena.
The representatives of the Indus Sovereignty.

chapters.title: Chapter 574: Strange Attack [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Devan Varma stood at the edge of the drop with his muscular torso bare except for heavy gold armlets forged in the likeness of coiling nagas and a sash of deep saffron silk.
His skin was deep bronze, marked with ancient glowing volcanic runes that pulsed with slow magma-mana.
He slowly twisted his neck from side to side, the vertebrae popping with the dull thuds of striking stones.
Standing half a pace behind his right shoulder was Ananya Rao.
Her long black hair was woven with gold beads while her body was adorned in crimson silk and delicate gold filigree armor.
She did not look at the other fighters.
Her dark almond-shaped eyes were fixed entirely on the broad scarred profile of Devan’s back, her face glowing with quiet unshakeable adoration.

’Look at them,’ Ananya thought, a reverent shiver running down her spine. ’Insects scrambling in the dirt... None of them understand what stands before them. From the day that my Lord was born, no warrior has ever managed to draw a single drop of blood from Devan’s skin... His volcanic aura is the purest and most terrifying manifestation Indus has ever produced, therefore he is not a mere scion... he is the foundation of a new pantheon. He has the potential to ascend beyond mortality and become a living god and I will stand at his side, his chosen woman, when the world bends the knee.’
Devan looked down upon the basin, his gaze sweeping over Lucian, Kira, Gareth, Isolde, and finally landing on First Princess Aki.
A slow rumbling breath escaped his chest, pluming into a cloud of black volcanic ash that drifted across the rocks.
"A crowded field," Devan rumbled, his voice sounding like two grinding tectonic plates. "Good... Weak flesh burns quickly."
Silence fell over the basin.
The factions stood locked in a rigid suffocating standoff.
Seventy paces separated the nearest fighters and two hundred yards spanned the entire perimeter.
The Safe Zone barrier hummed quietly in the distance with its blue light washing over the tense frozen faces of humanity’s elite scions.
Nobody moved and nobody breathed.
Every single person on the field understood the mathematics of the situation.
It was a powder keg.

The moment the first strike landed, the field would dissolve into a chaotic bloodbath where every alliance was temporary, every blind spot was fatal, and every fighter would seek to cannibalize the wounded to secure their own survival.
Aki stood with her boots planted in the sand with her bow lowered and her azure eyes darting between the distinct factions surrounding them.
Her knuckles were white against the star-iron grip of her weapon.

’This is an all-out war,’ Aki realized with the cold reality sinking deep into her gut. ’Europa wants us gone to win... Australis wants the same, Albion is treating this like an afternoon fox hunt, and Indus is looking to incinerate the entire field to show their godhood.’
Leona slid up beside Aki’s shoulder with her trench-machete held in a low, defensive guard and her hazel eyes flicking toward Isolde with sharp wariness.
"They’re circling," Leona whispered under her breath, barely moving her lips. "Everyone is waiting for the first idiot to draw mana so they can jump the flank."
Maya did not look back.
She stood five paces ahead of them with her broad back straight and her void-ivory cuirass catching the pale blue light of the Safe Zone dome.
She slowly lowered her chin with her amber eyes locking dead center onto Lucian de Montmirail’s pale face.

"Listen to me, both of you," Maya muttered, her voice dropping into a deadly unshakeable tone that cut through the whistling wind. "When this starts, do not look for clean formations and do not look for elegance. Give everything you have from the first breath... Burn your reserves, crack their bones, and fight like you have nothing left to go home to. We survive this bracket, or we don’t leave the sand."
Aki swallowed hard, then nodded. "Understood."
Leona’s lips pulled back into a grim ruthless smirk. "Let’s crack some teeth."
Maya took a slow, deep breath through her nose.
The tension in the air was so thick it could be cut with a dull knife.
Every fighter was coiled like an iron spring, their gazes locked across the divide, waiting for that single microscopic spark that would detonate the entire basin into violence.
Maya Da Silva had no intention of waiting for someone else to write the opening line.
She would be the spark.
WHOOOOSH!

Maya’s Second Stage Purple Core violently detonated as a suffocating aura of deep, tectonic brown mana erupted from her frame, roaring twenty feet into the air like a geyser of liquid mud and pulverized bedrock.
The physical gravity of her release struck the surrounding desert like a physical hammer, cracking the stone beneath her boots and blowing the loose yellow sand outward in a violent fifty-foot ring.
Across the basin, every single fighter stiffened as Lucian’s ice-blue eyes widened with his rapier twitching in his grip.
Gareth Pendelton’s broad smile vanished as his hand clamped onto the hilt of his broadsword while Devan Varma’s brow pulled down, his volcanic runes flaring with sudden reactive crimson heat.
’What is she doing?!’ Kira Bennett gasped from the ridge, her fingers trembling against her mudra.
Maya didn’t lunge forward yet...
She dropped her center of gravity by six inches, sinking her hips into a stance.

Her left foot slid forward three inches, carving a line through the rock while her right arm coiled back against her ribs and her fist clenched so tightly that the skin across her knuckles turned chalk-white.
Leona recognized the stance instantly and her hazel eyes dilated with raw alarm-bell terror.
"AKI, JUMP!" Leona screamed but she didn’t wait.
She grabbed Aki by the shoulder of her tunic and detonated every drop of her wind-mana, launching both of them forty feet vertically into the air.

Aki’s instincts responded instantly with her left hand clamped into a fist inside the midnight-blue glove, releasing an explosive high-pressure updraft of emerald wind-mana beneath her boots that propelled her higher into the sky.
Down below, Kira Bennett’s hands snapped shut.
"TEAR HER APART!" Kira shrieked.
BOOM-BOOM!

The sand directly beneath Maya’s planted boots exploded outward as an armored subterranean Spirit Beast... a thirty-foot-long chitinous Dune-Crusher Scylla with eight serrated mandibles and a barbed, venomous tail erupted from the bedrock.
Its monstrous tooth-lined maw tore through the earth, lunging upward to swallow Maya whole from the waist down!
Simultaneously, fifty paces away, a second massive beast burst from the sand behind Lucian de Montmirail with its massive claws sweeping to pin the European scion to the earth.
Maya didn’t even look down.
Her stance was set, her core was locked and the earth itself was answering her marrow.
So she did the one thing she could do in this situation...
She punched.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
For one fraction of a second, the world fell completely silent as there was no sound and there was no wind either.
...Then, reality caught up to the strike.
A concussive shockwave of pure tectonic pressure detonated from Maya’s knuckles as the thirty-foot Dune-Crusher Scylla erupting beneath her boots didn’t even get to bite.
The apocalyptic pressure of the punch struck the beast’s skull before the teeth could close and the monster’s head simply ceased to exist.

The thick, reinforced chitin, the compound eyes, the mandibles, and the brain-matter were violently pulverized into a red liquefied mist that splattered across twenty yards of sand but the force didn’t stop moving.

The atmospheric shockwave tore straight through the dead beast, surged across the fifty paces of open sand, and blew through the second Spirit Beast attacking Lucian, blowing a clean four-foot hole through its torso before slamming squarely into Lucian de Montmirail’s chest.
WHAM!
’Huh?’
Lucian didn’t even have time to scream!
His ice-blue eyes bulged violently out of their sockets with the sclera turning dark red as the capillaries instantly burst under the crushing deceleration.
Thick dark veins popped up all over his pale face, his throat, and his forearms like writhing worms as the shockwave blew through his defensive mana like paper.
CRACK-CRUNCH!

His breastplate shattered inward, driving his ribs straight into his lungs and Lucian was launched backward like an artillery shell with his feet tearing clean off the dirt as he rocketed horizontally across the desert.
BOOOOOOM!

He struck a seventy-foot sand dune three hundred yards away, tore straight through the center of the massive earth-mound, obliterating the dune into an explosive avalanche of falling sand, before tumbling violently across the rocks on the other side.
Maya stood in the center of the pulverized crater with her right arm extended and the brown tectonic aura smoking off her bare knuckles like boiling mud.
She slowly drew her arm back, settling into a wide immoveable combat guard as she wiped a speck of beast-blood from her cheek with the back of her wrist.
Her amber eyes scanned the frozen horrified faces of the remaining fighters with defiance.
"We better get this war under way, shouldn’t we?" Maya rasped, her voice booming across the basin.
The next moment...
The entire battlefield erupted into madness.
The thunderous roar of the collapsing dune three hundred yards to the south rolled across the salt flats like a localized tectonic fracture.
High atop an elevated promontory of compacted quartz sand, Genevieve de Montmirail did not flinch.

Her posture remained completely straight with her feet planted cleanly within the coarse silt as the concussive wind from Maya Da Silva’s tectonic shockwave whipped her tailored teal-colored coat against her shins.
She lowered the heavy matte-black receiver of her anti-material rifle by two inches.
Her cold gray eyes, framed by emerald-green bangs that cascaded down past her delicate jawline like braided river moss, tracked the flying debris where Lucian had disappeared.
’Taken out in the opening volley,’ Genevieve thought, letting out a melodic sigh through her nose.
She felt neither panic nor burning outrage.
An exasperated weariness washed through her chest instead.
Her cousin had spent the past few hours boasting about his peerless dueling style and the immaculate lineage of the Montmirail family.

He had insisted on orchestrating the opening strike... demanding that she prime the target with an alchemical beacon so he could swoop in for an elegant decisive decapitation before the eyes of the High Council.

’What an idiot,’ she reflected dryly, her thumb clicking the rifle’s internal cooling cycle. ’You don’t charge an Amazonian earth-shaper in the middle of a dry bedrock basin while her feet are still touching the ground... You bleed her from four hundred yards out.’
Yet, beneath the icy layer of aristocratic irritation, a small quiet knot tightened in her throat.
The concussive thud of that punch had sounded like a siege hammer splitting an oak door.
The dispersion had fractured the stone beneath Lucian’s boots before his body even cleared the ground.

’He’ll survive,’ Genevieve reassured herself with her jaw tightening by a fraction of a millimeter. ’The Montmirail bone-grafts are reinforced with flexible titanium mesh... If he dies from a single blunt-force redirection, he had no business carrying the family crest into this arena anyway.’
She dismissed her cousin from her mind after that.
In an active war zone, mourning the incompetent was a luxury that earned you an early grave.
Genevieve shifted her footing, pivoting three inches to the southwest.
She brought the heavy rifle back to her shoulder with liquid grace and the cold star-iron cheek-rest pressed smoothly against her cheekbone as her right eye aligned with the internal optics.
The crosshairs drifted across the chaotic airspace above the pulverized crater.
...They locked onto the silhouette of First Princess Aki.
The girl was currently suspended forty feet in the air with her combat gloves channeling pressurized emerald drafts to arrest her upward momentum.
Her pale delicate features were framed by blue hair that billowed wildly in the wind and her posture looked tense as she surveyed the multi-faction battlefield unfolding beneath her boots.
’Aki,’ Genevieve mused, her finger resting lightly against the hair-trigger. ’Kara named her, didn’t she?’
A private smirk tugged at the corner of Genevieve’s lips.

’It’s a pretty name for a remarkably pretty woman... I can certainly understand the Lord of Blessed Land’s aesthetic tastes. Soft eyes, unblemished skin, and the kind of quiet delicate grace that makes powerful monsters want to build high walls around her... Too bad that aesthetic appreciation doesn’t buy diplomatic immunity in Sector Forty-Four.’
Her index finger began to apply pressure to the star-iron trigger.
The battery beneath the barrel whined, priming a high-power cartridge laced with an alchemical neurotoxin designed to shut down motor functions within three heartbeats.
Her crosshairs settled dead center on the hollow between Aki’s collarbones.
Then...
The short hairs along the nape of Genevieve’s neck prickled with sudden violent heat.
It was an immediate suffocating spike in local air pressure that felt like the door of a blast furnace swinging open directly behind her skull and Genevieve did not turn her head to look.
She did not verify the threat with her eyes.
SWOOSH!
She let go of the rifle’s forward grip, abandoned her stabilized shooting stance, and threw her entire body sideways off the elevated sand promontory.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

sentences.text: Devan Varma stood at the edge of the drop with his muscular torso bare except for heavy gold armlets forged in the likeness of coiling nagas and a sash of deep saffron silk.
His skin was deep bronze, marked with ancient glowing volcanic runes that pulsed with slow magma-mana.
He slowly twisted his neck from side to side, the vertebrae popping with the dull thuds of striking stones.
Standing half a pace behind his right shoulder was Ananya Rao.
Her long black hair was woven with gold beads while her body was adorned in crimson silk and delicate gold filigree armor.
She did not look at the other fighters.
Her dark almond-shaped eyes were fixed entirely on the broad scarred profile of Devan’s back, her face glowing with quiet unshakeable adoration.
’Look at them,’ Ananya thought, a reverent shiver running down her spine. ’Insects scrambling in the dirt...
None of them understand what stands before them.
From the day that my Lord was born, no warrior has ever managed to draw a single drop of blood from Devan’s skin...
His volcanic aura is the purest and most terrifying manifestation Indus has ever produced, therefore he is not a mere scion... he is the foundation of a new pantheon.
He has the potential to ascend beyond mortality and become a living god and I will stand at his side, his chosen woman, when the world bends the knee.’
Devan looked down upon the basin, his gaze sweeping over Lucian, Kira, Gareth, Isolde, and finally landing on First Princess Aki.
A slow rumbling breath escaped his chest, pluming into a cloud of black volcanic ash that drifted across the rocks.
"A crowded field," Devan rumbled, his voice sounding like two grinding tectonic plates.
"Good...
Weak flesh burns quickly."
Silence fell over the basin.
The factions stood locked in a rigid suffocating standoff.
Seventy paces separated the nearest fighters and two hundred yards spanned the entire perimeter.
The Safe Zone barrier hummed quietly in the distance with its blue light washing over the tense frozen faces of humanity’s elite scions.
Nobody moved and nobody breathed.
Every single person on the field understood the mathematics of the situation.
It was a powder keg.

The moment the first strike landed, the field would dissolve into a chaotic bloodbath where every alliance was temporary, every blind spot was fatal, and every fighter would seek to cannibalize the wounded to secure their own survival.
Aki stood with her boots planted in the sand with her bow lowered and her azure eyes darting between the distinct factions surrounding them.
Her knuckles were white against the star-iron grip of her weapon.
’This is an all-out war,’ Aki realized with the cold reality sinking deep into her gut. ’Europa wants us gone to win...
Australis wants the same, Albion is treating this like an afternoon fox hunt, and Indus is looking to incinerate the entire field to show their godhood.’
Leona slid up beside Aki’s shoulder with her trench-machete held in a low, defensive guard and her hazel eyes flicking toward Isolde with sharp wariness.
"They’re circling," Leona whispered under her breath, barely moving her lips.
"Everyone is waiting for the first idiot to draw mana so they can jump the flank."
Maya did not look back.
She stood five paces ahead of them with her broad back straight and her void-ivory cuirass catching the pale blue light of the Safe Zone dome.
She slowly lowered her chin with her amber eyes locking dead center onto Lucian de Montmirail’s pale face.
"Listen to me, both of you," Maya muttered, her voice dropping into a deadly unshakeable tone that cut through the whistling wind.
"When this starts, do not look for clean formations and do not look for elegance.
Give everything you have from the first breath...
Burn your reserves, crack their bones, and fight like you have nothing left to go home to.
We survive this bracket, or we don’t leave the sand."
Aki swallowed hard, then nodded.
"Understood."
Leona’s lips pulled back into a grim ruthless smirk.
"Let’s crack some teeth."
Maya took a slow, deep breath through her nose.
The tension in the air was so thick it could be cut with a dull knife.
Every fighter was coiled like an iron spring, their gazes locked across the divide, waiting for that single microscopic spark that would detonate the entire basin into violence.
Maya Da Silva had no intention of waiting for someone else to write the opening line.
She would be the spark.
WHOOOOSH!

Maya’s Second Stage Purple Core violently detonated as a suffocating aura of deep, tectonic brown mana erupted from her frame, roaring twenty feet into the air like a geyser of liquid mud and pulverized bedrock.
The physical gravity of her release struck the surrounding desert like a physical hammer, cracking the stone beneath her boots and blowing the loose yellow sand outward in a violent fifty-foot ring.
Across the basin, every single fighter stiffened as Lucian’s ice-blue eyes widened with his rapier twitching in his grip.
Gareth Pendelton’s broad smile vanished as his hand clamped onto the hilt of his broadsword while Devan Varma’s brow pulled down, his volcanic runes flaring with sudden reactive crimson heat.
’What is she doing?!’ Kira Bennett gasped from the ridge, her fingers trembling against her mudra.
Maya didn’t lunge forward yet...
She dropped her center of gravity by six inches, sinking her hips into a stance.

Her left foot slid forward three inches, carving a line through the rock while her right arm coiled back against her ribs and her fist clenched so tightly that the skin across her knuckles turned chalk-white.
Leona recognized the stance instantly and her hazel eyes dilated with raw alarm-bell terror.
"AKI, JUMP!" Leona screamed but she didn’t wait.
She grabbed Aki by the shoulder of her tunic and detonated every drop of her wind-mana, launching both of them forty feet vertically into the air.

Aki’s instincts responded instantly with her left hand clamped into a fist inside the midnight-blue glove, releasing an explosive high-pressure updraft of emerald wind-mana beneath her boots that propelled her higher into the sky.
Down below, Kira Bennett’s hands snapped shut.
"TEAR HER APART!" Kira shrieked.
BOOM-BOOM!

The sand directly beneath Maya’s planted boots exploded outward as an armored subterranean Spirit Beast... a thirty-foot-long chitinous Dune-Crusher Scylla with eight serrated mandibles and a barbed, venomous tail erupted from the bedrock.
Its monstrous tooth-lined maw tore through the earth, lunging upward to swallow Maya whole from the waist down!
Simultaneously, fifty paces away, a second massive beast burst from the sand behind Lucian de Montmirail with its massive claws sweeping to pin the European scion to the earth.
Maya didn’t even look down.
Her stance was set, her core was locked and the earth itself was answering her marrow.
So she did the one thing she could do in this situation...
She punched.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
For one fraction of a second, the world fell completely silent as there was no sound and there was no wind either.
...Then, reality caught up to the strike.
A concussive shockwave of pure tectonic pressure detonated from Maya’s knuckles as the thirty-foot Dune-Crusher Scylla erupting beneath her boots didn’t even get to bite.
The apocalyptic pressure of the punch struck the beast’s skull before the teeth could close and the monster’s head simply ceased to exist.

The thick, reinforced chitin, the compound eyes, the mandibles, and the brain-matter were violently pulverized into a red liquefied mist that splattered across twenty yards of sand but the force didn’t stop moving.

The atmospheric shockwave tore straight through the dead beast, surged across the fifty paces of open sand, and blew through the second Spirit Beast attacking Lucian, blowing a clean four-foot hole through its torso before slamming squarely into Lucian de Montmirail’s chest.
WHAM!
’Huh?’
Lucian didn’t even have time to scream!
His ice-blue eyes bulged violently out of their sockets with the sclera turning dark red as the capillaries instantly burst under the crushing deceleration.
Thick dark veins popped up all over his pale face, his throat, and his forearms like writhing worms as the shockwave blew through his defensive mana like paper.
CRACK-CRUNCH!

His breastplate shattered inward, driving his ribs straight into his lungs and Lucian was launched backward like an artillery shell with his feet tearing clean off the dirt as he rocketed horizontally across the desert.
BOOOOOOM!

He struck a seventy-foot sand dune three hundred yards away, tore straight through the center of the massive earth-mound, obliterating the dune into an explosive avalanche of falling sand, before tumbling violently across the rocks on the other side.
Maya stood in the center of the pulverized crater with her right arm extended and the brown tectonic aura smoking off her bare knuckles like boiling mud.
She slowly drew her arm back, settling into a wide immoveable combat guard as she wiped a speck of beast-blood from her cheek with the back of her wrist.
Her amber eyes scanned the frozen horrified faces of the remaining fighters with defiance.
"We better get this war under way, shouldn’t we?" Maya rasped, her voice booming across the basin.
The next moment...
The entire battlefield erupted into madness.
The thunderous roar of the collapsing dune three hundred yards to the south rolled across the salt flats like a localized tectonic fracture.
High atop an elevated promontory of compacted quartz sand, Genevieve de Montmirail did not flinch.

Her posture remained completely straight with her feet planted cleanly within the coarse silt as the concussive wind from Maya Da Silva’s tectonic shockwave whipped her tailored teal-colored coat against her shins.
She lowered the heavy matte-black receiver of her anti-material rifle by two inches.

chapters.title: Chapter 575: Genevieve’s Situation [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The seconds her boots cleared the rim, an incandescent sphere of roaring volcanic fire descended vertically out of the upper sky.
The fireball struck the sandstone mound with the concussive fury of a falling mortar shell and the compacted sand exploded into an outward geyser of superheated dust and molten shale.
The entire four-yard promontory where Genevieve had been standing a heartbeat earlier was completely erased, collapsed into a smoking blackened crater of boiling quartz.
WHOOSH!
Genevieve fell through the air, her teal coat snapping like a whip as she rotated her core to face the sky.
Hovering thirty feet above the smoking ruin was a woman.
She wore no high-tier silk robes, no shimmering runic mantles, and no decorative crests.

Her athletic frame was clad in a brutal functional uniform of scorched charcoal leather and dull bronze-washed chainmail while her short-cropped russet hair was hacked close to the scalp, bristling aggressively against the arid wind.

...But it was her face that caught Genevieve’s attention. Her jaw was set in a bitter sneer, her dark eyes blazing with the raw fury of someone who had just walked five hundred miles over broken glass specifically to slit your throat.
In short, she looked eternal pissed off.
’What the fuck...’ Genevieve thought with her gray eyes narrowing. ’A Bloom retainer?’
Tyon Bloom did not pause to introduce herself.
CRACKLE!

Her right hand blurred forward and a secondary sphere of dense orange-red fire ignited in her open palm, whining with compressed pressure as she hurled it straight down toward Genevieve’s falling silhouette.
"Eat basalt, you whore!" Tyon snarled as the fireball tore downward, dragging a screaming vacuum of displaced air behind its trajectory.
Genevieve remained entirely composed in mid-air.
’It seems she has a temper...’
She swung the long fluted barrel of her anti-material rifle upward.
The weapon was forged from fireproof void-tungsten, specifically heat-treated to withstand the high-temperature friction of chemical discharges.
CLANG-HSSSSSSSSS!
Genevieve caught the descending fireball with the flat of the heavy rifle barrel, meeting the projectile like a batter stepping into a fast pitch.
With a sharp, fluid twist of her forearms, she redirected the attack.
The roaring sphere of flame bounced violently off the blackened steel, screaming back into the sky at a forty-five-degree angle before detonating harmlessly against the upper cloud layer.
THUD!
Genevieve’s boots touched the loose sand below as she immediately kicked off her heels, executing a flawless backward aerial flip that carried her fifteen yards across the desert floor.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Three more fireballs rained down in rapid succession, striking the sand along her retreat path with deafening concussions.

Geysers of yellow silt erupted around her, falling like hot rain, but not a single spark touched the hem of her coat as she landed softly in a low crouch with her right hand releasing the heavy rifle.
THUMP!
The firearm dropped into the coarse grit, discarded without a second thought.
In close-quarters combat against a high-output flame skirmisher, a long-range firearm was nothing more than an anchor.
CRASH!
Tyon Bloom descended from the sky with her boots slamming into the desert floor twenty paces away with the weight of an anvil.
The impact threw up a blinding ring of red clay, but she walked through the dust without blinking with her broad hands resting at her sides and her russet hair bristling in the hot air.

A sudden aggressive desert gale kicked up between them, howling through the narrow gap between two low dunes, whipping Genevieve’s emerald hair across her shoulders and rustling Tyon’s bronze chainmail.
Genevieve slowly rose to her full height.
She smoothed the lapel of her teal coat with a gloved thumb, looking at the scarred furious woman before her.
"Genevieve de Montmirail," she said with her voice sounding smooth and lacking any sort of fear. "Representative of the Europa Directorate."
Tyon spat a globule of yellow grit onto the sand between them as her dark eyes were locked dead onto Genevieve’s throat.
"Tyon Bloom," she grated out, the syllables sounding like grinding millstones. "And I don’t give a solitary shit about your Directorate..."
Genevieve smiled faintly. "A woman of few words. How refreshing."
Tyon took a slow heavy step forward with the sand crunching loudly beneath her thick combat soles.
The instruction had been beaten into her since childhood... In the arena, you dismantle the mind before you crack the bone.
High nobles are brittle glass as a single well-placed insult makes their mana shake.

"You know," Tyon said, her scarred lip curling into a venomous mocking sneer, "I expected Europa to send actual soldiers into this bracket... Instead, they ship out a pair of over-perfumed court whores in tailored coats. Your cousin folded like a wet sack of grain the second an Amazonian woman touched his chest, and you’re standing out here with paint on your eyes pretending you belong on a battlefield. Is everyone in your family this pathetic, or did they just pick the two biggest cowards so the rest of the house wouldn’t have to bleed?"
Genevieve did not flinch.

Instead, a quiet amused chuckle slipped past her lips as she tilted her head with her gray eyes sliding over Tyon’s cheap mismatched chainmail, the rough linen of her sleeves, and the harsh weathered leather of her boots.

"A valiant effort," Genevieve said, her tone dripping with light effortless amusement. "Truly. The standard psychological conditioning of House Bloom... Bully the opponent, mock their lineage, force an emotional overextension. It’s very effective against sheltered scions."
Genevieve took a single elegant step forward with her hands resting casually at her hips.
"Except... you aren’t House Bloom, are you?"
Tyon’s left brow twitched.

"Look at that armor," Genevieve continued, her voice sounding melodic and devastatingly precise. "Dull bronze wash over stamped low-grade iron... A tunic sewn from rough border-flax and those boots... standard garrison issue from the sulfur mines of the volcanic perimeter. You aren’t from the main estate in the capital, my guess is you are from a broken third-tier border family. The kind of branch lineage that lives in mud huts, chokes on ash, and trades their daughters to the front lines just to get a tax exemption on sheep feed."
Genevieve’s smile widened looking like she was a scary doll.

"You aren’t a warrior of House Bloom, little girl... You are a disposable hunting dog they dragged out of the sulfur trenches, wiped the shit off your nose, and pointed at the arena so their precious Seraphina wouldn’t have to scuff her manicure. Tell me... when this tournament is over, do you get to sleep in the stables, or do they make you ride back to the border in a wooden crate?"
SNAP!
The air pressure between them detonated as every drop of blood in Tyon’s body rushed straight to her temples.
"I will burn the skin off your fucking bones!" Tyon shrieked!
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Tyon’s heels ignited with violent explosive orange fire as she tore across the twenty-pace gap in the span of seconds, leaving a smoking gouged trench through the sand!
She drew a heavy serrated broad-cleaver from her hip, channeling a roaring mantle of flame along the cutting edge as she swung horizontally for Genevieve’s throat.
SWOOSH!
Genevieve did not attempt to parry the massive steel blade at all, she did know her limits so she stepped inside the arc instead.

Her movement was terrifyingly fluid, like water flowing around a jagged rock as she ducked beneath the flaming cleaver, letting the three-thousand-degree heat scorch the tips of her emerald bangs, while her right hand flicked a concealed lace-wrapped cylinder from her sleeve.
PFFFFFFFFT!
A dense pale-yellow mist hissed from the nozzle of the cylinder, spraying directly into Tyon’s face.
Tyon’s combat instincts flared as she held her breath, but the chemical wasn’t meant to be inhaled...
The moment the pale-yellow alchemical vapor touched the roaring volcanic flame coating her own cleaver, the chemical reaction occurred.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A secondary chemical explosion detonated right between their chests.
"Gahh!"
The blast tore through Tyon’s guard with the concussive pressure blowing her broad-cleaver out of alignment and staggering her footing across the sand.
Genevieve rode the shockwave backward, completely unharmed as her core was circulating a protective film of dense mana.
’I think I might add this to my own techniques.’
Truly making your opponents rage before fighting them made them very predictable... Perhaps if Tyon was in the right state of mind, she would have been able to see that attack coming from miles away.
’But then again, she doesn’t really look very smart, does she?’
Before Tyon could regain her center of gravity, Genevieve blurred forward again.
She drew a slender silver-plated combat stiletto from her inner coat, pouring her Second Stage core into the weapon.
The metal hummed with a terrifying high-frequency kinetic vibration that turned the tip into an invisible blur.
SHLICK!
The stiletto pierced straight through the bronze chainmail on Tyon’s left bicep, severing muscle and scraping hard against the bone.
"Gah!" Tyon grunted through clamped teeth but she didn’t retreat.
She had been on the borders all her life... pain was just a reminder that she was still breathing.
Tyon dropped her cleaver, letting the heavy steel fall into the sand, and drove her left forehead forward in a brutal bone-shattering headbutt aimed straight for Genevieve’s nose.
CRACK!
Genevieve’s head snapped back with blood spraying from her split lip, but the European scion didn’t panic.
As she stumbled, Genevieve’s left hand flicked a second alchemical capsule against Tyon’s collarbone.
CRACKLE-HSSSSSSSSS!
A thick emerald-green gel coated Tyon’s chest and neck, instantly smoking as it began to liquefy the leather and chainmail, eating into the flesh beneath with agonizing acidic heat.
"Die in the ditch you crawled out of," Genevieve hissed, her gray eyes cold as ice as she spun on her heel, driving a reinforced combat boot squarely into Tyon’s wounded ribs.
WHAM!
The kick sent Tyon skidding fifteen yards across the dirt, leaving a trail of smoking blood and dissolved leather behind her boots.
"Haah... Haah... Haah..."
Tyon hit the ground on one knee, panting heavily, her left arm hanging limp as her chest sizzled with green acid.
Blood dripped from her brow, running down into her eye, but she forced herself upright, her dark eyes blazing with feral hatred.
Genevieve wiped the blood from her lip with the back of her glove.

"You have grit, dog," Genevieve said, circling slowly like a wolf inspecting a dying stag. "I will give you that but grit without technique is just slow suicide. You are outmatched in alchemy, outmatched in speed, and outmatched in intellect."
Tyon spat another mouthful of blood, her right fist igniting with a fresh burst of orange fire.
"I don’t need intellect to snap your spine," Tyon growled, lunging forward again!
She closed the distance with terrifying ferocity, throwing a rapid combination of heavy flame-laced punches... left hook, right straight, spinning back-fist!
The flames roared, superheating the surrounding air, but Genevieve slipped every single strike with infuriating efficiency.𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
SWISH! TAP! DUCK!
Genevieve moved like a ghost, her slender frame twisting just outside Tyon’s reach.
Every time Tyon overextended, Genevieve’s stiletto flashed, carving shallow bleeding lines across the border girl’s forearms, thighs, and flanks.
In less than two minutes, Tyon was covered in dozens of lacerations, her uniform soaked in blood and the corrosive gel eating deeper into her collarbone.
Genevieve was dominating the engagement.
’I find it hard to believe that she’s a Bloom...’
This was a merciless dissection of a brute force fighter by an elite academy prodigy.
Inside the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence was tense.
Along the high southern mezzanine, several ministers from the Europa Directorate were already nodding approvingly, murmuring praises about the Montmirail dueling doctrine.
Sitting in her velvet chair, Matriarch Etilga Bloom watched the live projection with her lace-trimmed fan resting gently against her collarbone.
Her expression held no trace of worry.
In fact, behind the painted silk of her fan, Etilga’s dark red lips were curled into a wide satisfied smile.
Her amber eyes glittered with dark anticipation as she watched Tyon bleed across the sand.

’Cut her deeper, little viper,’ Etilga thought, a shiver of genuine delight running down her spine. ’Keep cutting and strip the flesh from her ribs. You think you are winning a duel... you have no idea what kind of monster you are waking up.’
Down in the basin, the clash reached its boiling point.
"Haaargh!"
Tyon threw a desperate lunging overhand right, pouring every drop of her remaining core into the fist but Genevieve caught the telegraph instantly.
She ducked beneath the roaring punch, stepped deep into Tyon’s pivot, and drove her left hand forward, slapping a heavy pressurized alchemical canister directly against the left side of Tyon’s face.
CLICK.
"Checkmate," Genevieve whispered.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The thermite-grade canister detonated at point-blank range and a blinding white-hot flash enveloped the left side of Tyon’s skull.
The horrific temperature instantly incinerated her hair, burned away her left eyebrow and eyelid, and charred the skin, cheekbone, and ear down to the blackened, smoking meat.
"AAAAAAAAGH!"
A raw agonizing shriek tore from Tyon’s throat as the concussive explosion blew her off her feet, sending her crashing horizontally into the sand thirty yards away.
She tumbled through the dirt like a ragdoll, finally coming to a halt face-down in the coarse grit.
The left side of her face was completely blackened, smoking with sizzling chemical residue with blood and blister-fluid pooling beneath her jaw.
Her body twitched once, twice, before going still.
Genevieve stood in the center of the clearing with her chest heaving slightly as she flicked the soot from her stiletto.
"Disappointing," Genevieve murmured, shaking her head as she sheathed the blade. "All that shouting for nothing."
She turned her back, preparing to retrieve her anti-material rifle and reposition toward the Safe Zone—
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!

Her right hand blurred forward and a secondary sphere of dense orange-red fire ignited in her open palm, whining with compressed pressure as she hurled it straight down toward Genevieve’s falling silhouette.
"Eat basalt, you whore!" Tyon snarled as the fireball tore downward, dragging a screaming vacuum of displaced air behind its trajectory.
Genevieve remained entirely composed in mid-air.
’It seems she has a temper...’
She swung the long fluted barrel of her anti-material rifle upward.
The weapon was forged from fireproof void-tungsten, specifically heat-treated to withstand the high-temperature friction of chemical discharges.
CLANG-HSSSSSSSSS!
Genevieve caught the descending fireball with the flat of the heavy rifle barrel, meeting the projectile like a batter stepping into a fast pitch.
With a sharp, fluid twist of her forearms, she redirected the attack.
The roaring sphere of flame bounced violently off the blackened steel, screaming back into the sky at a forty-five-degree angle before detonating harmlessly against the upper cloud layer.
THUD!
Genevieve’s boots touched the loose sand below as she immediately kicked off her heels, executing a flawless backward aerial flip that carried her fifteen yards across the desert floor.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
Three more fireballs rained down in rapid succession, striking the sand along her retreat path with deafening concussions.

Geysers of yellow silt erupted around her, falling like hot rain, but not a single spark touched the hem of her coat as she landed softly in a low crouch with her right hand releasing the heavy rifle.
THUMP!
The firearm dropped into the coarse grit, discarded without a second thought.
In close-quarters combat against a high-output flame skirmisher, a long-range firearm was nothing more than an anchor.
CRASH!
Tyon Bloom descended from the sky with her boots slamming into the desert floor twenty paces away with the weight of an anvil.
The impact threw up a blinding ring of red clay, but she walked through the dust without blinking with her broad hands resting at her sides and her russet hair bristling in the hot air.

A sudden aggressive desert gale kicked up between them, howling through the narrow gap between two low dunes, whipping Genevieve’s emerald hair across her shoulders and rustling Tyon’s bronze chainmail.
Genevieve slowly rose to her full height.
She smoothed the lapel of her teal coat with a gloved thumb, looking at the scarred furious woman before her.
"Genevieve de Montmirail," she said with her voice sounding smooth and lacking any sort of fear.
"Representative of the Europa Directorate."
Tyon spat a globule of yellow grit onto the sand between them as her dark eyes were locked dead onto Genevieve’s throat.
"Tyon Bloom," she grated out, the syllables sounding like grinding millstones.
"And I don’t give a solitary shit about your Directorate..."
Genevieve smiled faintly.
"A woman of few words.
How refreshing."
Tyon took a slow heavy step forward with the sand crunching loudly beneath her thick combat soles.
The instruction had been beaten into her since childhood...
In the arena, you dismantle the mind before you crack the bone.
High nobles are brittle glass as a single well-placed insult makes their mana shake.
"You know," Tyon said, her scarred lip curling into a venomous mocking sneer, "I expected Europa to send actual soldiers into this bracket...
Instead, they ship out a pair of over-perfumed court whores in tailored coats.
Your cousin folded like a wet sack of grain the second an Amazonian woman touched his chest, and you’re standing out here with paint on your eyes pretending you belong on a battlefield.
Is everyone in your family this pathetic, or did they just pick the two biggest cowards so the rest of the house wouldn’t have to bleed?"
Genevieve did not flinch.

Instead, a quiet amused chuckle slipped past her lips as she tilted her head with her gray eyes sliding over Tyon’s cheap mismatched chainmail, the rough linen of her sleeves, and the harsh weathered leather of her boots.
"A valiant effort," Genevieve said, her tone dripping with light effortless amusement.
"Truly.
The standard psychological conditioning of House Bloom...
Bully the opponent, mock their lineage, force an emotional overextension.
It’s very effective against sheltered scions."
Genevieve took a single elegant step forward with her hands resting casually at her hips.
"Except... you aren’t House Bloom, are you?"
Tyon’s left brow twitched.
"Look at that armor," Genevieve continued, her voice sounding melodic and devastatingly precise.
"Dull bronze wash over stamped low-grade iron...
A tunic sewn from rough border-flax and those boots... standard garrison issue from the sulfur mines of the volcanic perimeter.
You aren’t from the main estate in the capital, my guess is you are from a broken third-tier border family.
The kind of branch lineage that lives in mud huts, chokes on ash, and trades their daughters to the front lines just to get a tax exemption on sheep feed."
Genevieve’s smile widened looking like she was a scary doll.
"You aren’t a warrior of House Bloom, little girl...
You are a disposable hunting dog they dragged out of the sulfur trenches, wiped the shit off your nose, and pointed at the arena so their precious Seraphina wouldn’t have to scuff her manicure.
Tell me... when this tournament is over, do you get to sleep in the stables, or do they make you ride back to the border in a wooden crate?"
SNAP!
The air pressure between them detonated as every drop of blood in Tyon’s body rushed straight to her temples.
"I will burn the skin off your fucking bones!" Tyon shrieked!
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Tyon’s heels ignited with violent explosive orange fire as she tore across the twenty-pace gap in the span of seconds, leaving a smoking gouged trench through the sand!
She drew a heavy serrated broad-cleaver from her hip, channeling a roaring mantle of flame along the cutting edge as she swung horizontally for Genevieve’s throat.
SWOOSH!
Genevieve did not attempt to parry the massive steel blade at all, she did know her limits so she stepped inside the arc instead.

Her movement was terrifyingly fluid, like water flowing around a jagged rock as she ducked beneath the flaming cleaver, letting the three-thousand-degree heat scorch the tips of her emerald bangs, while her right hand flicked a concealed lace-wrapped cylinder from her sleeve.
PFFFFFFFFT!
A dense pale-yellow mist hissed from the nozzle of the cylinder, spraying directly into Tyon’s face.
Tyon’s combat instincts flared as she held her breath, but the chemical wasn’t meant to be inhaled...
The moment the pale-yellow alchemical vapor touched the roaring volcanic flame coating her own cleaver, the chemical reaction occurred.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A secondary chemical explosion detonated right between their chests.
"Gahh!"
The blast tore through Tyon’s guard with the concussive pressure blowing her broad-cleaver out of alignment and staggering her footing across the sand.
Genevieve rode the shockwave backward, completely unharmed as her core was circulating a protective film of dense mana.
’I think I might add this to my own techniques.’
Truly making your opponents rage before fighting them made them very predictable...
Perhaps if Tyon was in the right state of mind, she would have been able to see that attack coming from miles away.
’But then again, she doesn’t really look very smart, does she?’
Before Tyon could regain her center of gravity, Genevieve blurred forward again.
She drew a slender silver-plated combat stiletto from her inner coat, pouring her Second Stage core into the weapon.
The metal hummed with a terrifying high-frequency kinetic vibration that turned the tip into an invisible blur.
SHLICK!
The stiletto pierced straight through the bronze chainmail on Tyon’s left bicep, severing muscle and scraping hard against the bone.
"Gah!" Tyon grunted through clamped teeth but she didn’t retreat.
She had been on the borders all her life... pain was just a reminder that she was still breathing.
Tyon dropped her cleaver, letting the heavy steel fall into the sand, and drove her left forehead forward in a brutal bone-shattering headbutt aimed straight for Genevieve’s nose.
CRACK!
Genevieve’s head snapped back with blood spraying from her split lip, but the European scion didn’t panic.
As she stumbled, Genevieve’s left hand flicked a second alchemical capsule against Tyon’s collarbone.
CRACKLE-HSSSSSSSSS!
A thick emerald-green gel coated Tyon’s chest and neck, instantly smoking as it began to liquefy the leather and chainmail, eating into the flesh beneath with agonizing acidic heat.
"Die in the ditch you crawled out of," Genevieve hissed, her gray eyes cold as ice as she spun on her heel, driving a reinforced combat boot squarely into Tyon’s wounded ribs.
WHAM!
The kick sent Tyon skidding fifteen yards across the dirt, leaving a trail of smoking blood and dissolved leather behind her boots.
"Haah...
Haah...
Haah..."
Tyon hit the ground on one knee, panting heavily, her left arm hanging limp as her chest sizzled with green acid.
Blood dripped from her brow, running down into her eye, but she forced herself upright, her dark eyes blazing with feral hatred.
Genevieve wiped the blood from her lip with the back of her glove.
"You have grit, dog," Genevieve said, circling slowly like a wolf inspecting a dying stag.
"I will give you that but grit without technique is just slow suicide.
You are outmatched in alchemy, outmatched in speed, and outmatched in intellect."
Tyon spat another mouthful of blood, her right fist igniting with a fresh burst of orange fire.
"I don’t need intellect to snap your spine," Tyon growled, lunging forward again!
She closed the distance with terrifying ferocity, throwing a rapid combination of heavy flame-laced punches... left hook, right straight, spinning back-fist!
The flames roared, superheating the surrounding air, but Genevieve slipped every single strike with infuriating efficiency.𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
SWISH!
TAP!
DUCK!
Genevieve moved like a ghost, her slender frame twisting just outside Tyon’s reach.
Every time Tyon overextended, Genevieve’s stiletto flashed, carving shallow bleeding lines across the border girl’s forearms, thighs, and flanks.
In less than two minutes, Tyon was covered in dozens of lacerations, her uniform soaked in blood and the corrosive gel eating deeper into her collarbone.
Genevieve was dominating the engagement.
’I find it hard to believe that she’s a Bloom...’
This was a merciless dissection of a brute force fighter by an elite academy prodigy.
Inside the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence was tense.
Along the high southern mezzanine, several ministers from the Europa Directorate were already nodding approvingly, murmuring praises about the Montmirail dueling doctrine.
Sitting in her velvet chair, Matriarch Etilga Bloom watched the live projection with her lace-trimmed fan resting gently against her collarbone.
Her expression held no trace of worry.
In fact, behind the painted silk of her fan, Etilga’s dark red lips were curled into a wide satisfied smile.
Her amber eyes glittered with dark anticipation as she watched Tyon bleed across the sand.
’Cut her deeper, little viper,’ Etilga thought, a shiver of genuine delight running down her spine. ’Keep cutting and strip the flesh from her ribs.
You think you are winning a duel... you have no idea what kind of monster you are waking up.’
Down in the basin, the clash reached its boiling point.
"Haaargh!"
Tyon threw a desperate lunging overhand right, pouring every drop of her remaining core into the fist but Genevieve caught the telegraph instantly.
She ducked beneath the roaring punch, stepped deep into Tyon’s pivot, and drove her left hand forward, slapping a heavy pressurized alchemical canister directly against the left side of Tyon’s face.
CLICK.
"Checkmate," Genevieve whispered.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The thermite-grade canister detonated at point-blank range and a blinding white-hot flash enveloped the left side of Tyon’s skull.
The horrific temperature instantly incinerated her hair, burned away her left eyebrow and eyelid, and charred the skin, cheekbone, and ear down to the blackened, smoking meat.
"AAAAAAAAGH!"
A raw agonizing shriek tore from Tyon’s throat as the concussive explosion blew her off her feet, sending her crashing horizontally into the sand thirty yards away.
She tumbled through the dirt like a ragdoll, finally coming to a halt face-down in the coarse grit.
The left side of her face was completely blackened, smoking with sizzling chemical residue with blood and blister-fluid pooling beneath her jaw.
Her body twitched once, twice, before going still.
Genevieve stood in the center of the clearing with her chest heaving slightly as she flicked the soot from her stiletto.
"Disappointing," Genevieve murmured, shaking her head as she sheathed the blade.
"All that shouting for nothing."
She turned her back, preparing to retrieve her anti-material rifle and reposition toward the Safe Zone—
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!

chapters.title: Chapter 576: Your Next Line Is...?
paragraphs: A sound broke through the quiet desert air but it was not the sound of wind and it was not the sound of sliding sand either.
It was the high-pitched screaming whistle of atmospheric pressure collapsing in on itself and Genevieve’s boots froze while a cold primal dread seized her spine, locking her joints in place.
’It can’t be...?’
Slowly like a robot, she turned her head back toward the fallen body and in the red dirt thirty paces away, Tyon Bloom was pushing herself upright.
Her fingers clawed into the coarse sand, dragging her battered bleeding torso off the ground.

The left side of her face was a ruined blackened crater of charred meat and exposed bone, but her remaining right eye which looked wide and was burning with a terrifying unholy luminescence locked dead center onto Genevieve’s face.
"Mm?"
At first, she looked very confused... Perhaps she couldn’t understand what was going on or she didn’t recognize Genevieve, however that changed after.
"AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
And then... her flames ignited.
BOOM!
They were no longer the coarse orange-red flames of a common magic user.
Dancing within the roaring fire, long spiraling wisps of deep, incandescent blue began to bleed into the crimson as the temperature shattered the ceiling in a single second.
CRRRRRRRK!
The loose sand within twenty yards of Tyon’s boots instantly liquefied, fusing into a smooth bubbling sheet of glowing red glass and Genevieve’s pupils shrank to microscopic pinpricks.
’What... what is this?!’ Genevieve’s mind screamed, taking an involuntary stumbling step backward. ’Her output... it’s multiplying! The wounds... she’s getting stronger because she was maimed?!’
That was the dark, ungodly secret of Tyon Bloom’s cultivation.
She was not a pampered prodigy like Seraphina, blessed with an ancestral Primordial Spirit from childhood... Tyon was like a dog.
She had survived the volcanic trenches by cultivating an ancient masochistic bloodline art that Lady Etilga had personally beaten into her marrow.
Her core was forged through mortal agony.

Etilga Bloom had dragged Tyon to death’s door dozens of times in the private torture chambers beneath the capital manse... breaking her bones, burning her flesh, severing her tendons and forcing her soul pathways to adapt to terminal trauma.
The closer Tyon stood to the grave, the hotter her flames burned.
When she was whole, she was an unremarkable Second Stage brawler.
When she was critically maimed... When half her face was burned away and her blood was flooding her lungs, her soul-fire could reach temperatures that rivaled Seraphina’s own output.
Tyon hoped for one thing in this miserable blood-soaked life... to impress Matriarch Etilga enough to be granted a low-tier elemental spirit.
With a spirit bonded to her soul, her power would stabilize.
Her family would be elevated from the ash trenches to the main house and her younger brothers would never have to eat boiled leather again...
She would tear through the gates of hell itself to make that happen.
"You..." Tyon croaked, her voice a terrifying roar that sounded like cracking stone, "...talked too much."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Tyon detonated as two massive, roaring wings of blue-and-crimson flame erupted from her shoulder blades, propelling her vertically into the sky.
She achieved sustained high-speed flight through pure brute-force combustion, rocketing through the air at high speeds and Genevieve’s composure completely shattered.
"Fall back!" she screamed to herself, frantically whipping both hands forward!
She threw six alchemical canisters into the air, detonating them simultaneously to create a massive three-hundred-foot wall of corrosive green mist between them.
WHOOOOOOSH!

The blue-flame comet tore through the green mist without slowing down as the three-thousand-degree heat incinerated the chemical compounds before they could even react, flash-boiling the moisture in the air into dry plasma.
Tyon descended from above like an executioner’s axe.
BOOM!
Her fist, wrapped in dense, howling blue fire, crashed down toward Genevieve’s skull.
Genevieve crossed her arms, desperately manifesting a defensive mana barrier, while simultaneously revealing her final secret trump card.
’I d-don’t want to d-die... die!’
SWOOSH!
A violent high-velocity current of emerald wind-mana erupted from Genevieve’s boots and sleeves.
She had never been purely an alchemist... Her true hidden elemental affinity was Wind.
WHOOSH!
She used the air currents to warp her trajectory, sliding three inches to the left to let Tyon’s fist crater the bedrock.
BANG!
The earth fractured, but Tyon did not miss a beat.
"AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"
She was crashing out, operating on pure berserker instinct as she threw a savage point-blank backhand with her knuckles catching Genevieve across the ribs.
CRACK!
"Augh..."
Genevieve gasped as two ribs snapped, but she channeled her wind-mana into her stiletto, driving the silver blade straight into Tyon’s right thigh.
SHLICK!
Tyon didn’t even flinch, hell she didn’t look down at the blade buried four inches in her meat.
"Th-thank you."
It made her stronger...
WHOOSH!
She grabbed Genevieve by the throat of her teal coat with her burned, blackened left hand, yanking the Europa noblewoman forward until their faces were inches apart.
Tyon’s single right eye blazed with manic bloodthirsty triumph.
"Die," Tyon whispered as she shoved her right palm dead center into Genevieve’s sternum.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A point-blank catastrophic explosion of blue-and-crimson fire detonated directly between them!

The concussive blast blew Genevieve backward across eighty yards of sand with her teal coat was completely incinerated away, her skin covered in severe blistering burns and her breathing cut off as she hit the earth, tumbled across the shale as she went completely limp, knocked out cold.
VUUUUUM.
An administrative light flared over Genevieve’s fallen body, registering critical combat incapacitation.
Tyon stood in the center of the smoking glass crater with her chest heaving in violent, agonizing gasps.
Blood was pouring from her mouth, her thigh, and her burned skull, but she threw her head back toward the purple sky and let out a deafening roar of victory.
"I DID IT!" Tyon screamed with her voice cracking. "LADY ETILGA! WITNESS ME!"
She was dying.

Her soul channels were screaming under the catastrophic strain of the blue flames, but her heart was soaring... She had broken an elite scion of the Directorate and her family’s ascension was within reach.
Suddenly...
The crunch of loose gravel broke through the quiet.
Tyon snapped her head toward the sound with her single eye narrowing through a curtain of blood.
Standing twenty paces away, picking his way across the cooling shale, was a young man.
Jax Sterling-Cross wore only a torn soot-stained combat tunic, his left forearm tightly wrapped in coarse field linen that leaked small traces of green salve.
He was limping slightly with his posture loose and his face pale as he looked between the charred crater and the unconscious blistered body of Genevieve de Montmirail.
Jax took one look at Tyon’s smoking, half-incinerated skull and visibly flinched with his jaw dropping.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
"What in the actual hell...?" Jax stammered, taking a stumbling step backward and pointing a trembling finger at her face. "Are you... are you even human?"
Tyon looked at him like a wolf looking at a crippled sheep.
’Prey,’ she thought instantly.
He was wounded as his mana was fluctuating erratically.
He carried no heavy armor either, and his presence was pathetic compared to the Europa scion she had just broken.
...He was an easy effortless harvest to cap off her glory.
Tyon grinned, her charred lips splitting and weeping dark blood.
"Turn around and run, little boy," Tyon rasped, her voice dripping with sadistic promise. "Or I’ll turn your bones into glass too."
She reached down with her left hand, grabbing the hilt of the broad-cleaver resting in the dirt.
Without hesitation, Tyon drove the serrated blade two inches deep into her own left shoulder.
CRUNCH!
Blood geysered from the wound, splashing across the glass as Tyon staggered with her knees buckling under the fresh wave of agony, but her single eye flared with terrifying ecstasy.
WHOOSH!
The crimson fire around her body vanished completely.
In its place, a pure, blinding mantle of deep celestial cobalt-blue flame erupted from her flesh.
The temperature soared to staggering heights, flash-vitrifying the surrounding fifty yards of sand into a lake of translucent green glass in less than a second.
...She had brought herself to the threshold of death.
’This is the limit of my power.’
She felt so strong, she was going crazy... perhaps it was the chemicals, but she felt like she was high
Jax looked at the screaming wall of blue fire with his eyes wide then, his trembling stopped.
His lopsided lazy smirk returned to his face as he dropped his weight into a loose unorthodox street-boxing guard, bouncing lightly on the balls of his boots.
"You know," Jax said, "you really shouldn’t stab yourself like that... Tetanus is a serious hazard."
"DIE!" Tyon roared, lunging forward with high speed.
She covered the distance in heartbeats as her fist of pure blue flame aimed straight for his sternum but Jax didn’t dodge left or right.
"Your next line is," Jax announced, pointing his unbandaged right finger directly at her face, "’I’ll turn your ash into fertilizer!’"
Tyon’s mouth opened mid-lunge.
"I’LL TURN YOUR ASH INTO FERTI—WHAT?!"
She choked on her own syllable.
The absurd shock of hearing her exact internal thought predicted out loud caused her neural pathways to stutter for a microsecond as her forward momentum hitched and her elbow dropped by two inches.
CLACK!
In that microscopic window of hesitation, Jax’s right hand didn’t throw a punch.
He reached into his combat belt, pulling out a single palm-sized star-iron canister... the exact same high-density coagulant salve he had used on his arm earlier.
With the casual flick of a bar patron tossing a coaster, Jax hurled the brass tin straight into the roaring blue flames coating Tyon’s fist.
TZZZZZZZZZZZZ-BOOM!
The high-density alkaline salve, formulated with volatile mountain mint and heavy mineral salts, met the four-thousand-degree cobalt fire.
The chemical reaction was catastrophic...
The alkaline compound expanded into an instantaneous opaque cloud of thick choking white foam that completely smothered the fire on her right arm, sealing her knuckles in a crust of hardened lime.
"What is this shit?!" Tyon roared, thrashing her arm to break the crust.
"And your next line is," Jax shouted, sliding effortlessly beneath her wild left hook, "’You cowardly little trickster!’"
"YOU COWARDLY LITTLE TRICKST... HOW DO YOU KEEP DOING THAT?!" Tyon screamed, her single eye bulging with fury.
She was completely insane... Her spatial awareness was gone, her balance ruined by the rage boiling through her veins.
Still, Tyon raised both arms to unleash a radial burst of blue flame to incinerate the entire area.
’I’ll just extend all of my pow—’
TUG!
Tyon’s boots suddenly refused to move as she looked down.
Crisscrossing the smooth glass floor between her legs was a complex, interlocking web of thin translucent wires!
It was the linen bandage Jax had supposedly ’wasted’ earlier!

When he had walked across the clearing limping, he hadn’t been stumbling... he had been unspooling sixty feet of star-iron thread he had carefully woven into the linen, anchoring the lines to the jagged edges of the vitrified glass.
The moment Tyon stepped into the center of the crater, she had walked right into the web.
YANK!
Jax pulled the master knot wrapped around his pinky finger and the tension snapped tight as the star-iron wires caught Tyon behind both ankles, violently yanking her feet out from under her!
"GAH!"
Tyon’s center of gravity collapsed.
Her body tipped horizontally in mid-air, completely helpless with her blue flames sputtering as her core momentarily lost connection with the earth.

Jax stepped in as he swung his heavy, brass-plated field canteen... filled to the brim with three pounds of undiluted desert sand in a clean rotational horizontal arc straight into the side of her unburned right temple.
BONK!
The sound was insultingly hollow as Tyon’s single eye rolled back into her skull.
The blue flames instantly vanished, popping out like a blown candle and her body hit the vitrified glass with a limp unceremonious thud, completely knocked unconscious.
Silence descended over the desert basin as the wind whistled softly through the cracked glass.
Jax Sterling-Cross stood in the center of the carnage, holding his dented canteen by the strap, looking down at the two unconscious, elite scions lying at his boots.
He blinked once.
He blinked twice.
He took a slow deep breath, looking around at the empty, smoking wasteland in genuine bewilderment.
Jax scratched the back of his neck with his bandaged hand, staring at the sky.
"Eh..." Jax muttered aloud.
"...I won?"
