Tyon’s single right eye blazed with manic bloodthirsty triumph.
"Die," Tyon whispered as she shoved her right palm dead center into Genevieve’s sternum.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A point-blank catastrophic explosion of blue-and-crimson fire detonated directly between them!

The concussive blast blew Genevieve backward across eighty yards of sand with her teal coat was completely incinerated away, her skin covered in severe blistering burns and her breathing cut off as she hit the earth, tumbled across the shale as she went completely limp, knocked out cold.
VUUUUUM.
An administrative light flared over Genevieve’s fallen body, registering critical combat incapacitation.
Tyon stood in the center of the smoking glass crater with her chest heaving in violent, agonizing gasps.
Blood was pouring from her mouth, her thigh, and her burned skull, but she threw her head back toward the purple sky and let out a deafening roar of victory.
"I DID IT!" Tyon screamed with her voice cracking.
"LADY ETILGA!
WITNESS ME!"
She was dying.
Her soul channels were screaming under the catastrophic strain of the blue flames, but her heart was soaring...
She had broken an elite scion of the Directorate and her family’s ascension was within reach.
Suddenly...
The crunch of loose gravel broke through the quiet.
Tyon snapped her head toward the sound with her single eye narrowing through a curtain of blood.
Standing twenty paces away, picking his way across the cooling shale, was a young man.
Jax Sterling-Cross wore only a torn soot-stained combat tunic, his left forearm tightly wrapped in coarse field linen that leaked small traces of green salve.
He was limping slightly with his posture loose and his face pale as he looked between the charred crater and the unconscious blistered body of Genevieve de Montmirail.
Jax took one look at Tyon’s smoking, half-incinerated skull and visibly flinched with his jaw dropping.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
"What in the actual hell...?" Jax stammered, taking a stumbling step backward and pointing a trembling finger at her face.
"Are you... are you even human?"
Tyon looked at him like a wolf looking at a crippled sheep.
’Prey,’ she thought instantly.
He was wounded as his mana was fluctuating erratically.
He carried no heavy armor either, and his presence was pathetic compared to the Europa scion she had just broken.
...He was an easy effortless harvest to cap off her glory.
Tyon grinned, her charred lips splitting and weeping dark blood.
"Turn around and run, little boy," Tyon rasped, her voice dripping with sadistic promise.
"Or I’ll turn your bones into glass too."
She reached down with her left hand, grabbing the hilt of the broad-cleaver resting in the dirt.
Without hesitation, Tyon drove the serrated blade two inches deep into her own left shoulder.
CRUNCH!
Blood geysered from the wound, splashing across the glass as Tyon staggered with her knees buckling under the fresh wave of agony, but her single eye flared with terrifying ecstasy.
WHOOSH!
The crimson fire around her body vanished completely.
In its place, a pure, blinding mantle of deep celestial cobalt-blue flame erupted from her flesh.
The temperature soared to staggering heights, flash-vitrifying the surrounding fifty yards of sand into a lake of translucent green glass in less than a second.
...She had brought herself to the threshold of death.
’This is the limit of my power.’
She felt so strong, she was going crazy... perhaps it was the chemicals, but she felt like she was high
Jax looked at the screaming wall of blue fire with his eyes wide then, his trembling stopped.
His lopsided lazy smirk returned to his face as he dropped his weight into a loose unorthodox street-boxing guard, bouncing lightly on the balls of his boots.
"You know," Jax said, "you really shouldn’t stab yourself like that...
Tetanus is a serious hazard."
"DIE!" Tyon roared, lunging forward with high speed.
She covered the distance in heartbeats as her fist of pure blue flame aimed straight for his sternum but Jax didn’t dodge left or right.
"Your next line is," Jax announced, pointing his unbandaged right finger directly at her face, "’I’ll turn your ash into fertilizer!’"
Tyon’s mouth opened mid-lunge.
"I’LL TURN YOUR ASH INTO FERTI—WHAT?!"
She choked on her own syllable.
The absurd shock of hearing her exact internal thought predicted out loud caused her neural pathways to stutter for a microsecond as her forward momentum hitched and her elbow dropped by two inches.
CLACK!
In that microscopic window of hesitation, Jax’s right hand didn’t throw a punch.
He reached into his combat belt, pulling out a single palm-sized star-iron canister... the exact same high-density coagulant salve he had used on his arm earlier.
With the casual flick of a bar patron tossing a coaster, Jax hurled the brass tin straight into the roaring blue flames coating Tyon’s fist.
TZZZZZZZZZZZZ-BOOM!
The high-density alkaline salve, formulated with volatile mountain mint and heavy mineral salts, met the four-thousand-degree cobalt fire.
The chemical reaction was catastrophic...
The alkaline compound expanded into an instantaneous opaque cloud of thick choking white foam that completely smothered the fire on her right arm, sealing her knuckles in a crust of hardened lime.
"What is this shit?!" Tyon roared, thrashing her arm to break the crust.
"And your next line is," Jax shouted, sliding effortlessly beneath her wild left hook, "’You cowardly little trickster!’"
"YOU COWARDLY LITTLE TRICKST...
HOW DO YOU KEEP DOING THAT?!" Tyon screamed, her single eye bulging with fury.
She was completely insane...
Her spatial awareness was gone, her balance ruined by the rage boiling through her veins.
Still, Tyon raised both arms to unleash a radial burst of blue flame to incinerate the entire area.
’I’ll just extend all of my pow—’
TUG!
Tyon’s boots suddenly refused to move as she looked down.
Crisscrossing the smooth glass floor between her legs was a complex, interlocking web of thin translucent wires!
It was the linen bandage Jax had supposedly ’wasted’ earlier!

When he had walked across the clearing limping, he hadn’t been stumbling... he had been unspooling sixty feet of star-iron thread he had carefully woven into the linen, anchoring the lines to the jagged edges of the vitrified glass.
The moment Tyon stepped into the center of the crater, she had walked right into the web.
YANK!
Jax pulled the master knot wrapped around his pinky finger and the tension snapped tight as the star-iron wires caught Tyon behind both ankles, violently yanking her feet out from under her!
"GAH!"
Tyon’s center of gravity collapsed.
Her body tipped horizontally in mid-air, completely helpless with her blue flames sputtering as her core momentarily lost connection with the earth.

Jax stepped in as he swung his heavy, brass-plated field canteen... filled to the brim with three pounds of undiluted desert sand in a clean rotational horizontal arc straight into the side of her unburned right temple.
BONK!
The sound was insultingly hollow as Tyon’s single eye rolled back into her skull.
The blue flames instantly vanished, popping out like a blown candle and her body hit the vitrified glass with a limp unceremonious thud, completely knocked unconscious.
Silence descended over the desert basin as the wind whistled softly through the cracked glass.
Jax Sterling-Cross stood in the center of the carnage, holding his dented canteen by the strap, looking down at the two unconscious, elite scions lying at his boots.
He blinked once.
He blinked twice.
He took a slow deep breath, looking around at the empty, smoking wasteland in genuine bewilderment.
Jax scratched the back of his neck with his bandaged hand, staring at the sky.
"Eh..." Jax muttered aloud.
"...I won?"

chapters.title: Chapter 577: Earthborn [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The shattered spine of the dune groaned as tons of dry powdery quartz slipped downward in a continuous yellow cascade.
Beneath the suffocating drift fifty paces from the fractured bedrock rim, a single hand clawed through the silt.
The glove of silver-plated mesh was torn to ribbons with the skin beneath blackened and scraped down to raw dermis by the friction of his three-hundred-yard movement through the earth.
Lucian de Montmirail dragged his torso out of the crater, his breath tearing from his throat in a series of wet rattling heaves.
"Gah—!"
He spat a thick glob of arterial crimson onto the sand with his vision swimming in sickening rings of yellow and gray.

Every breath felt like dragging a rusted saw across his pleural lining... at least three ribs on his left side were completely stove-in, the fractured bone fragments clicking against one another with a dull sickening friction every time his diaphragm expanded.
His tailored teal coat... the pride of the Montmirail line was reduced to scorched rags clinging to his titanium mesh undergarment.
’What in the name of the High Council was that...?’ Lucian thought, his fingers trembling violently as they dug into the shale for purchase.
His teeth ground together with a harsh ceramic scrape.
’Was that pure kinetic dispersion? A pressurized air vortex? An unregistered wind-compression art...?’
His mind frantically cycled through the combat dossiers of the Amazonian border regiments.
There was no record of a brute-force brawler producing a directional shockwave that could bypass a master’s parrying power and obliterate sixty yards of bedrock without an incantation.
"Filthy... border animal," he hissed through blood-stained teeth.
His right hand fumbled at his waist, reaching for the reinforced brass clasp of his survival kit.

His thumb hooked into the leather strap, dragging out a cylindrical glass phial filled with glowing luminescent green fluid... a military-grade cellular reconstructive tonic synthesized in the central laboratories of the Europa Directorate.

’Once the marrow stitches... once my thoracic wall seals...’ Lucian’s eyes burned with cold malice as he brought the phial toward his mouth, ’I will dismantle that Amazonian bitch piece by piece. I’ll peel the tendons from her wrists before the broadcast relays can cut the feed and I’ll make her understand the gap between low-born clay and direct Europa blood—’
A shadow fell over his face and Lucian froze with the glass phial hovering half an inch from his split swollen lips.
The harsh glare of the twin suns vanished, eclipsed by a massive high-velocity mass dropping vertically out of the sky.
He didn’t even have the luxury of turning his neck.
A figure was descending from the heavens like a falling siege engine... not aimed at him, but dropping along a trajectory toward the shallow ridge thirty paces behind his crater.
Lucian turned his head by two inches, his blood-filmed gaze catching sight of Maya Da Silva standing on the rim above.
The Amazonian woman looked at him.
Her amber eyes were cold, completely indifferent to his existence with her lips curled into a mocking smirk that cut deeper than any blade.
She looked at him the way a laborer looked at a crushed beetle on a threshing floor.
Then, the sky split.
BOOOOOOOOOM!
Gareth Pendelton made landfall.

The Royal Scion of the Albion Concordat didn’t bleed off his kinetic momentum with wind-dampening runes or feather-fall charms, instead he slammed into the earth with the violence of a two-ton iron meteor.
The point of impact was less than three paces from Lucian’s exposed flanks.
The displaced shockwave that followed tore the granite shelf apart as a circular crater twelve feet deep detonated outward with the concussive backdraft catching Lucian’s broken body dead-center.
CRACK-CRUNCH-SHATTER!
The sickening sound of Lucian’s remaining ribs, pelvis, and collarbones snapping under the atmospheric overpressure sounded like dry firewood being trampled by a war-horse.
Lucian didn’t even get to release a scream.
The air in his lungs was driven out in an instantaneous red fog, his eyes rolling back until only the blood-veined sclera showed.
WHOOSH!
The administrative transponder pinned to the shredded lapel of his teal coat flashed with a white light.
The World Council’s spatial extraction protocol engaged with an authoritative, metallic chime.
Lucian’s limp, mangled form dissolved into millions of shimmering, ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the stratosphere alongside the distant particles of Genevieve.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating optical relays suspended above the canyon, the cold voice echoed across Sector Forty-Four:
"Notice of Elimination."
"The representatives of the Europa Directorate have suffered critical combat incapacitation and collapse... The Europa Directorate is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Gareth Pendelton stood in the smoking pit of his own making with his heavy combat boots buried ankle-deep in crushed quartz.
He didn’t spare a single glance for the white particles drifting into the sky.
He carried his massive basket-hilted star-iron broadsword rested horizontally across the back of his neck with his hands draped casually over the cross-guard.
His scarlet-and-white dueling tunic was dusted with pale sand, but his ruddy, square-jawed face was glowing with genuine joy.
He slowly pivoted on his heel, his sharp blue eyes locking onto Maya Da Silva standing twenty feet up the slope.

"Well, now," Gareth grinned, his rich voice cutting through the settling dust. "That was rather unceremonious for a Montmirail, wasn’t it?... Though I suppose I should thank you for softening the meat before I arrived—"
His voice died in his throat.
WHOOSH!
Gareth’s combat instincts, honed by fifteen years of brutal dueling academies in the high towers of Albion screamed an immediate red-line warning behind his temples.
Maya had not waited for him to finish his sentence.
She had already dropped her hips with her heavy leather boots sinking into the bedrock and her right fist coiled back against her ribs.
’Huu—?’
Gareth attempted to spring backward to establish dueling distance, but the moment his heels pressed into the dirt, his eyes widened in disbelief.
The air surrounding Maya wasn’t behaving like the regular one he knew at all...
It was coiling, bending, and undulating in serpentine spirals... not like wind, but like invisible tectonic plates sliding over one another.
The gravity within three yards of her knuckles warped, pulling the loose shale into a high-speed orbital spin that hissed like a nest of vipers.
’She has an air affinity?!’ Gareth’s mind panicked for a fraction of a heartbeat. ’No... that isn’t wind! That’s displacement!’
Maya’s amber eyes flared with a terrifying luminescence.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
She struck the open air.
The blow didn’t connect with physical meat, but the atmospheric medium detonated with the exact same violence that had shattered Lucian de Montmirail’s chest.
A concentrated cone-shaped shockwave of compressed force ripped through the canyon, carrying pulverized earth-pressure straight toward Gareth’s face but Gareth didn’t try to dodge.
There was no dodging a wave that covered thirty paces of width in a millisecond.
"Crucible Wall!" he roared.

He whipped his massive broadsword off his neck, planting the flat of the three-foot star-iron blade directly against his forearms, locking his elbows against his ribs, and driving his boots six inches into the living stone.
CRASH-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The air hammer slammed into the blade and Gareth’s boots became plows.
He was hurled backward fifty yards across the canyon floor, his soles tearing two smoking, three-foot-deep trenches straight through the solid granite bedrock.
The concussive pressure rattled through the star-iron steel, traveling through his forearms and slamming into his shoulder joints with terrifying force!
POW-POW!
The sound of his radius and ulna dislodging from their wrist sockets echoed beneath his tunic with small sprays of capillary blood bursting through the pores of his forearms.
"RAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"
Yet, with a savage animalistic roar, Gareth twisted the flat of his blade by five degrees.
SCREEEEEEECH!
He didn’t try to absorb the entirety of the strike... that would be suicide so instead, he parried it!

The massive concussive cone was split down the middle by the star-iron edge with the deflected pressure roaring past his flanks and slamming into a towering eighty-foot sand dune behind his left shoulder.
KER-BLAM!
The massive dune ceased to exist as the eighty-foot mountain of yellow silt was blown into an expansive cloud of microscopic dust that darkened the sun across the entire northern quadrant.
Gareth came to a halt fifty paces out with his chest heaving and his boots smoking where the friction had burned through his leather soles.
His hands were shaking violently around the grip of his broadsword with his wrist bones clicking as his core frantically worked to re-seat the dislodged joints.
He stared across the clearing at the Amazonian woman with his breath catching in his throat.

’How in the seven hells did she generate that kind of directional torque without a runic circle...?!’ Gareth thought with sweat mixing with the grit on his forehead. ’That wasn’t a standard spell at all... What is that?’
Twenty paces away on the shattered ridge, Maya Da Silva remained in her follow-through stance.

Her right knuckles were smoking thin wisps of brown mana that smelled of crushed granite and copper an beneath her void-ivory cuirass, her teeth were clamped together so hard her jaw muscles felt like petrified wood.
’This state... is hell to maintain,’ Maya thought with a sharp cold sweat beading beneath her leather wraps.
Inside her chest, her internal organs were screaming.
She could feel her liver, her spleen, and the lining of her lungs being squeezed as if wrapped in wet rawhide.
Her Second Stage Purple Core wasn’t merely circulating mana through her meridians... it was dragging the tectonic weight of the sovereign realm’s crust directly into her marrow.
This was the forbidden technique she had forged in the blood-soaked trenches of the southern perimeter... Earthborn.
By forcing her core to sync its vibration frequency with the deep tectonic plates of the earth, she turned her physical flesh into an extension of the planetary bedrock.

In the Earthborn state, her physical acceleration multiplied threefold, her muscle density bypassed the limitations of mortal bone, and her strikes ceased to be regular punches... they became similar to tectonic faults.
’The drawback is devastating,’ Maya analyzed with cold detachment, feeling a thin hot trickle of blood begin to slide down the inside of her left nostril.
Once Earthborn was active, she couldn’t cast complex external earth spells.
She couldn’t raise massive stone walls, she couldn’t sculpt intricate sand traps, and she couldn’t summon earthen golems.
The overwhelming power of this form choked out her precision so instead, she became hyper-attuned to the world’s rotation.
She could feel the minute microscopic rotational drag of the tectonic plates beneath her feet... the immense perpetual energy of the earth grinding against itself.

Those devastating, air-shattering punches weren’t powered by her own stamina... they were released by cycling the rotational force up through her heels, coiling it through her hips, and discharging the inertia outward through her knuckles in a single catastrophic burst.
Maya called them, the Rotations.
She had used the First Rotation to execute the Spirit Beasts and blast Lucian through the sand dune.
She had used the Second Rotation to shatter Gareth’s defensive perimeter.

’I have two more strikes left in this body,’ Maya thought with her vision blurring slightly before her will snapped it back into focus. ’Two more Rotations, and my core will collapse from the internal compression... If I push past the Fourth, I will tear my own heart in half.’
She didn’t let a single flicker of weakness reach her face.
FSSSSSS!
With a subtle internal circulation of her remaining mana, Maya forced a fine layer of pressurized earth and quartz dust to bleed outward through the pores of her skin.

The brown mineral dust settled instantly over her face and neck, forming a hardened crystalline shell that absorbed the trickle of blood from her nose and sealed the hairline fractures along her cheekbones before Gareth’s eyes could register them.
To the scion of Albion, she looked completely untouched... Maya was sure she looked like an invincible monolith carved from living granite.
The psychological warfare was paramount.
The more effortlessly she appeared to command this cataclysmic power, the more hesitant, defensive, and vulnerable he would become.
Across the trench, Gareth Pendelton looked down at his broadsword.
His blue eyes narrowed.
Running along the thick star-iron spine of his ancestral weapon, three jagged hairline fractures had appeared, weeping tiny sparks of displaced mana.
A slow low laugh rumbled in his chest.
He didn’t panic at all as the smile returned to his face.

"Magnificent," Gareth said, rolling his shoulders until his dislodged wrist joints snapped back into their sockets with loud wet clacks. "Truly magnificent! To crack star-iron with the displaced air of a bare fist! What a savage you are, Da Silva!"
Maya did not reply as she kept her chin lowered with her amber eyes tracking the micro-twitches of his shoulder blades.
Gareth tilted his head, his gaze drinking in her broad muscular silhouette, the sharp curve of her jaw, and the fierce pride burning in her eyes.

"You know," Gareth said, his voice carrying a smooth confidence that echoed across the rocks, "when this tournament concludes and Albion claims its rightful seat as the winners, I think I’ll bypass the usual ceremonies... I think I’ll take you back to the capital of Albion as my wife."
Maya’s left eyebrow twitched as she rolled her eyes with slow bored contempt.
"I’d rather marry a dead mule," she rasped.

She could feel the minute microscopic rotational drag of the tectonic plates beneath her feet... the immense perpetual energy of the earth grinding against itself.

Those devastating, air-shattering punches weren’t powered by her own stamina... they were released by cycling the rotational force up through her heels, coiling it through her hips, and discharging the inertia outward through her knuckles in a single catastrophic burst.
Maya called them, the Rotations.
She had used the First Rotation to execute the Spirit Beasts and blast Lucian through the sand dune.
She had used the Second Rotation to shatter Gareth’s defensive perimeter.

’I have two more strikes left in this body,’ Maya thought with her vision blurring slightly before her will snapped it back into focus. ’Two more Rotations, and my core will collapse from the internal compression...
If I push past the Fourth, I will tear my own heart in half.’
She didn’t let a single flicker of weakness reach her face.
FSSSSSS!
With a subtle internal circulation of her remaining mana, Maya forced a fine layer of pressurized earth and quartz dust to bleed outward through the pores of her skin.

The brown mineral dust settled instantly over her face and neck, forming a hardened crystalline shell that absorbed the trickle of blood from her nose and sealed the hairline fractures along her cheekbones before Gareth’s eyes could register them.
To the scion of Albion, she looked completely untouched...
Maya was sure she looked like an invincible monolith carved from living granite.
The psychological warfare was paramount.
The more effortlessly she appeared to command this cataclysmic power, the more hesitant, defensive, and vulnerable he would become.
Across the trench, Gareth Pendelton looked down at his broadsword.
His blue eyes narrowed.
Running along the thick star-iron spine of his ancestral weapon, three jagged hairline fractures had appeared, weeping tiny sparks of displaced mana.
A slow low laugh rumbled in his chest.
He didn’t panic at all as the smile returned to his face.
"Magnificent," Gareth said, rolling his shoulders until his dislodged wrist joints snapped back into their sockets with loud wet clacks.
"Truly magnificent!
To crack star-iron with the displaced air of a bare fist!
What a savage you are, Da Silva!"
Maya did not reply as she kept her chin lowered with her amber eyes tracking the micro-twitches of his shoulder blades.
Gareth tilted his head, his gaze drinking in her broad muscular silhouette, the sharp curve of her jaw, and the fierce pride burning in her eyes.

"You know," Gareth said, his voice carrying a smooth confidence that echoed across the rocks, "when this tournament concludes and Albion claims its rightful seat as the winners, I think I’ll bypass the usual ceremonies...
I think I’ll take you back to the capital of Albion as my wife."
Maya’s left eyebrow twitched as she rolled her eyes with slow bored contempt.
"I’d rather marry a dead mule," she rasped.

chapters.title: Chapter 578: The Fourth Rotation [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Gareth’s laughter was loud and utterly unfazed.
"A spirited one!" he boomed. "I wouldn’t have it any other way! But first... let’s see if that pretty granite shell can hold up against proper Albion steel!"
WHOOOSH!
Gareth roared as his Second Stage Purple Core flared with an incandescent silver light.
His flesh, his skin, and the hair along his arms underwent an instantaneous metallic transmutation.

The ruddy human tone vanished, replaced by the cold, unyielding luster of solid polished steel... His skin didn’t simply look metallic, it adopted the exact density, shear resistance, and thermal tolerance of high-grade star-iron as he raised his left hand, extending his palm flat toward the sky.
PING-PING-PING-PING-PING!
His Inventor opened directly above his open hand warped with a pale-blue light.
From the spatial pocket, a dozen heavy, star-iron weapons began to cascade out into the daylight.

Broadswords, spiked war-picks, serrated trench-axes, and heavy throwing spathas tumbled through the air though they were not falling to the dirt, but locking into a floating circular orbit around his frame!
Gareth was not merely an armored swordsman... He commanded the rare affinity of Metal Magic!
’What a pain in the ass... It’s as the research said.’
The floating arsenal began to spin, rotating around his steel-clad body with the deafening high-pitched screech of an active buzzsaw.
The displaced air whistled like screaming shrapnel as he lowered his primary blade, pointing the fractured tip dead center at Maya’s heart.
"Come, my lovely!" Gareth roared, his voice sounding metallic and booming. "Show me if your earth can break the crown’s iron!"
BOOM!
Gareth launched forward.

His steel boots pulverized the bedrock as he charged, tearing across the fifty paces at terrifying speed with the cloud of orbiting star-iron blades surged forward with him, screaming through the air like an undulating swarm of metal hornets.
Maya took a slow deep breath through her teeth.
The blades whistled through the air with their razor edges reflecting the harsh sunlight, but her focus did not waver.
The world seemed to slow down as the chaotic noise of the battlefield faded into a low thrum.
’I will win,’ Maya thought, the image of her older sister flashing brightly behind her eyes.

Her older sister had not wanted to be the President... she wanted to enjoy her life however a leader was needed and since their father had no sons and she had not been of age that time, her sister had risen into power.
Valerie left everything related to having a normal life behind to make sure that not only would she protect the country but her as well and Maya was going to repay the favor as quickly as she could.
’As long as I can stand, my sister will have her life back.’
STOMP!
Maya’s right boot hammered down into the earth.
...The Third Rotation
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
She didn’t punch forward this time, instead Maya drove the rotational energy directly down into the bedrock!
The thirty feet of hard clay and quartz sand separating them violently detonated upward in a colossal curtain of pulverized rock and yellow silt that rose forty feet into the sky.
The erupting wall of earth completely obliterated Gareth’s line of sight, creating an opaque smokescreen between their trajectories.
"Cheap trick!" Gareth laughed from behind the dirt wall.
He didn’t slow his charge, instead with a sharp mental command, he snapped his fingers.
SWOOSH-SWOOSH-SWOOSH!

The orbiting swarm of star-iron weapons surged forward, penetrating the earthen curtain like a volley of ballista bolts, blind-firing across every square foot of the corridor to shred whatever was waiting on the other side.
The blades tore through the dust—
CLANG! CRASH!
Nothing was there.
Through the thinning haze of yellow dust, Maya did not appear on the ground...
She had used the concussive upward eruption of her Third Rotation to launch herself twenty feet horizontally through the cloud.
WHOOSH!
’I only have one chance to land the Fourth rotation in a way he can’t defend.’
She had to make it count...

Maya descended from his high-right flank and her hands were not empty, but grasping two jagged five-foot slabs of dense compressed granite she had ripped directly out of the bedrock during the detonation.
Gareth’s eyes snapped up just in time to see the stone slabs swinging down like twin guillotines.
WHAM! CRASH!
Maya slammed the massive granite slabs into both sides of Gareth’s steel-clad skull simultaneously.

The concussive force of the stone-on-metal collision sounded like two church bells colliding at high speeds as the granite slabs shattered into millions of flying fragments against his steel skin, but the blunt force was immense as it bypassed his armor and rattled his brain inside his skull.
Gareth staggered, his vision exploding into white stars and his ears ringing with high-pitched feedback!
"You little—!" Gareth snarled, swinging his heavy broadsword in a desperate blind backhand arc.
SHLICK!

Maya twisted her torso in mid-air, but she couldn’t completely clear the trajectory as the fractured tip of the star-iron broadsword tore across her left flank, cleaving through the void-ivory cuirass and carving a deep four-inch gash through her ribs.
Hot crimson blood sprayed across the sand, hissing against the hot shale.
Simultaneously, two of Gareth’s orbiting throwing spathas answered his mental recoil, whipping around from behind and piercing straight through Maya’s right thigh and left shoulder.
THUNK! THUNK!
"Gah!" Maya grunted, her boots hitting the sand as agony flared through her nervous system.

The protective layers of pressurized earth dust she had coated over her skin shattered and washed away in the spray of her own blood as her true state was laid bare... Her clothes was soaked in red, her breath coming in suffocating gasps and her internal channels weeping from the strain of the Earthborn state.
Gareth shook the dizziness from his head, his steel-skinned face contorting with triumphant blood-slicked fury.
"Got you!" Gareth roared, pulling his broadsword back with both hands for a downward bisection stroke. "Now yield, you stubborn—"
He never finished the word.
Maya stepped straight into the descending sword, letting the cross-guard strike her bruised collarbone, closing the final two inches of distance between their chests.
’Finally...’
Her amber eyes were ablaze with terrifying finality.
During the entire exchange... during the stone-slab strike and during the mid-air clash, she hadn’t just been throwing blunt mass.
With every shard of granite that had struck his chest, she had been embedding quartz seeds directly into the microscopic fissures of his steel-transmuted armor and she had found the flaw.
Right over his heart, where the star-iron grain was uneven...
’The Fourth Rotation,’ Maya thought, her heart giving one final thud.
She coiled her left hip, dragged the deepest frequency of the sovereign realm up through her shattered thigh, and drove her bare, blood-slicked palm dead center into the fractured point on his chest.
...The Fourth Rotation!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sound was similar to the sound of a mountain collapsing under its own weight.
The entire force of the rotation was focused into a single microscopic square inch of Gareth’s breastbone.
CRRRRRRRRACK-SHATTER!

Gareth’s steel-transmuted skin completely fractured and shattered as a spiderweb of jagged black cracks tore across his entire chest, the structural integrity of his metal shattering like a plate of brittle glass.
"BLUURGH!"
A massive geyser of dark blood erupted from Gareth’s mouth, painting the sky crimson as his sternum caved inward by three inches.
His eyes bulged in pure agony as the shockwave tore straight through his heart and spine, exiting out his back in a conical spray of torn muscle and shattered armor.
WHOOOOOOSH-BANG!

Gareth was launched backward like an artillery shell fired from a siege mortar as he cleared seventy yards of airspace in less than a second, his limp bleeding body skipping violently across the rocky basin... bouncing off boulders, shattering shale shelves, and leaving a continuous fifty-yard smear of crimson across the desert floor before finally coming to a halt, twitching in a pool of his own blood.
...He didn’t move again.
His core flickered and dropped to critical, it was at a state where it was barely sustaining the thread of his life.
On the other side of the canyon, Maya Da Silva stood motionless as the Earthborn state collapsed.
SNAP!
The internal pressure she had been holding back finally broke its banks as a massive rush of dark blood poured from Maya’s mouth, her nose, and the corners of her eyes.
Her vision faded into pitch-black nothingness.
’I... I did it...’
Her knees buckled and her broad muscular frame tipped forward, hitting the coarse red sand face-first with a dull heavy thud.
She lay still beside the shattered granite, the desert wind slowly dusting her dark hair in yellow silt.
Two hundred paces to the east, in the shadow of a jagged basalt overhang, another war was raging.
CLANG! CLINK! SCREEEEECH!
"Fuck you!"
The sound of grinding steel was deafening, ringing with high-frequency friction that threw showers of white-hot sparks against the dark rock walls.
Leona Vivnr’s jaw was clamped tight with her teeth aching from the relentless pressure as she parried a high-low combination from Isolde Vivnr.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
Leona’s deep-sea trench-machete moved in tight defensive movements... They were short deflections designed to absorb hits without exposing her ribs but Isolde was like a phantom.
"Stop leaving yourself wide open!"
The second scion of the Albion Concordat moved with terrifying elegance, her twin, silver-plated parrying daggers spinning between her slender fingers like humming propeller blades.
SWISH-SHLICK!

Isolde slipped inside Leona’s guard with the serrated tip of her left dagger carving a shallow three-inch line across Leona’s forearm, while her right blade lunged for the soft hollow of Leona’s throat.
’Fucking annoying woman...’
Leona didn’t blink.

She dipped her chin, catching the pommel of the dagger against the reinforced rim of her leather gorget, while her right boot snapped upward in a vicious short-range front kick aimed straight for Isolde’s kneecap.
SMACK!
Isolde checked the kick with the heel of her boot, spinning three hundred and sixty degrees on the ball of her left foot and using the momentum to drive a spinning elbow strike toward Leona’s jaw.
BANG!
Leona threw her left forearm up to block the elbow, the impact sending a dull concussive jolt through her shoulder, but she used the close proximity to channel her Second Stage core.
WHOOSH!
A sharp pressurized blade of emerald wind-mana erupted from the edge of her machete, forcing Isolde to leap backward three paces with her dark blue duel-leathers fluttering in the displaced gale.
Both women landed in low crouches with their breath misting a bit in the hot stagnant air of the overhang.
Leona’s eyes flicked over Isolde’s shoulder, looking toward the far side of the canyon where the concussive booms of Maya’s battle had just fallen dead silent.
Her heart gave a hard anxious thud against her ribs.
’Maya...’ Leona thought, her knuckles whitening around the grip of her trench-machete. ’The mana signature just vanished... Did she take Gareth out, or did he—’

"Eyes on the steel, cousin," Isolde’s voice sliced through the tension as she twirled the matched daggers across her knuckles with not a single hair out of place as her pale immaculate features were set in an expression of icy superiority.

"Looking away during a duel with direct Albion blood is an extraordinarily fast way to lose an ear," Isolde continued, stepping forward with slow confidence. "Though I suppose I shouldn’t expect battlefield etiquette from the branch of the family that was exiled to the fishing docks of Amazon... How is the salt trade these days, Leona? Still smelling of dead cod and cheap grog?"
Leona’s hazel eyes narrowed into dangerous slits.

"My branch earns our bread with calloused hands, Isolde," Leona spat, shifting her center of mass into a low-slung trench-fighter’s guard. "We don’t sit in high towers letting our cousins do the bleeding while we paint our nails and polish parrying daggers. Let’s see how well that blood holds up when I drive six inches of scrap-iron through your pretty teeth..."
WHOOSH!
Leona exploded forward but she didn’t use refined dueling forms.
’I’m sure she can read them...’

So she fought like an oceanic privateer in a boarding action... She closed the distance with violent erratic footwork, her trench-machete chopping downward in heavy cleaving diagonals that carried the full weight of her shoulders.
CLANG! CLANG! BANG!
Isolde parried with terrifying precision as her daggers moved in interlocking crosses but Leona wasn’t fighting with just her blade.
As Isolde deflected a descending chop, Leona’s left hand shot out like an iron clamp, snatching Isolde by the lapel of her leather coat.
"U-ugh?!"
Leona yanked her forward and slammed a brutal headbutt straight into Isolde’s cheekbone.
CRACK!
Blood sprayed from Isolde’s nose, but the Albion noblewoman didn’t cry out.
With feral grace, Isolde drove her right knee violently into Leona’s solar plexus, simultaneously reversing her grip on her left dagger and burying the hilt straight into Leona’s collarbone.
WHAM!
Both women broke apart, skidding across the shale with blood dripping from their faces and their hearts hammering against their ribs at the wild ecstasy of pure violence.
’I’ll surely take her down next time.’ The both of them thought at the same time.
It was a magnificent breathless clash of bloodline against bloodline—
BOOM!
A massive armored body came tumbling out of the upper canyon, skipping across the rocks between them.

Gareth Pendelton’s shattered bleeding frame rolled across the sand, coming to a halt directly in the center of their duel, coughing up thick, dark blood as his chest was crushed inward like a broken barrel.
"Huh...? Gareth?"
Isolde froze, her eyes widening in disbelief as she looked at the man lying broken in the dirt.

Leona landed lightly on her toes with her trench-machete held high and her pulse racing with pure adrenaline.
"One down!" Leona grinned, wiping the blood from her brow with her sleeve. "Gareth is scrap, Isolde! You’re next!"
Isolde ground her teeth, her daggers flashing as she reset her stance—
PING!
The air above their heads suddenly turned a sickening violent electric violet!
PING! PING! PING!
Three massive condensed orbs of crackling psionic energy tore through the airspace between them, screaming with high-pitched sounds that made both women’s eardrums throb with instant piercing pain.
The psionic orbs slammed into the basalt shelf between them, detonating with concussive shockwaves that blew both Leona and Isolde ten paces in opposite directions!
SKID-CRASH!
Leona hit the dirt, shaking the agonizing high-frequency ringing from her ears with her vision swimming as she pushed herself up on one knee.
Beside her, Isolde was clutching her temples as her daggers held low in a defensive reflex.
Both women snapped their heads up toward the rocky outcrop overlooking the gully and standing on the high ledge, framed by the violet sky, was Ananya Rao.

The second representative of the Indus Sovereignty stood adorned in flowing crimson silks and delicate gold filigree armor, her long black hair braided with heavy gold coins that chimed softly in the wind.
In her right hand, she held an ornate gold-tipped lotus staff that was radiating dense pulsing waves of deep purple psionic mana.
Her dark almond-shaped eyes looked down at Leona and Isolde with haughty irritation.
"What the hell is your problem?!" Leona roared, shaking her fist at the ledge. "We were in the middle of a duel, you crazy bitch!"

"Do you have any concept of decorum?!" Isolde snapped simultaneously, wiping blood from her nose and glaring up at the Indus scion. "Interfering in a formal battle between cousins? Have they completely abandoned battlefield honor in the southern palaces?!"
Ananya did not look intimidated.
She slowly lowered her lotus staff, tapping the gold ferrule against the stone with a clear clink.
Her chin tilted upward, her expression settling into an intolerable self-righteous scowl.
"Your pathetic screeching squabble was generating turbulent wind-shear across the western ridge," Ananya said, her voice smooth, melodic, and entirely devoid of apology.

She turned her head slightly, her gaze drifting toward the far promontory where Devan Varma stood completely motionless, his arms crossed over his massive bronze chest and his eyes closed in deep undisturbed meditation.

"Devan is communing with the magma conduits of this realm," Ananya continued, her voice softening into a tone of reverence. "He is preparing to reveal his power to the World Council and the wind from your little blades was making his hair fly out of alignment... It was offensive to his presence."
Leona stared at her and Isolde stared at her.
For two full seconds, the desert canyon fell completely silent then Leona slowly blinked, her mouth opening in bewilderment.
"Are you serious?" Leona deadpanned. "You interrupted a death match... because of his hair?"
Isolde let out a sharp incredulous scoff, shaking her head in pure disgust.

"Good lord," Isolde sneered, looking up at Ananya with unmasked mockery. "I thought Indus bred conquerors but instead, they sent out a pathetic, drooling simp for a man who isn’t even that good-looking... He looks like an unwashed quarry worker who fell into a vat of turmeric."
SNAP!
The atmospheric mana around the ledge turned completely purple as Ananya’s face twisted in hysterical murderous outrage.
The golden beads in her hair rattled violently as her psionic aura detonated, sending gravity fluctuations rippling through the rock that cracked the basalt beneath her sandals.

"You dare...?" Ananya shrieked, her voice vibrating with mind-crushing force. "You dare speak of my lord with those filthy, common mouths?! He is the future sovereign of the world... He is a living deity... Take it back! TAKE IT BACK BEFORE I TEAR YOUR SOULS OUT OF YOUR SKULLS!"
Down below, Leona looked at Isolde and Isolde looked at Leona.
Between the two cousins, through fifteen years of familial estrangement and bitter political rivalry, a single silent understanding passed in the blink of an eye.
’We jump her...’
’Immediately...’
"Temporary truce?" Leona muttered under her breath, tightening her grip on her machete.
"Until this screeching harpy is choking on her own teeth," Isolde answered coldly.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
BOOM!
Both women moved in perfect unison as they charged straight up the rocky slope together with their boots tearing up the shale at high speeds.
Ananya grinned wildly from the ledge, her eyes glowing with psychotic psionic light.
"Die, insects!" Ananya screamed, thrusting her lotus staff forward. Thousand-Needle Lotus!"
BOOOOOOM!
A massive barrage of hundreds of razor-sharp psionic needles erupted from the head of her staff, screaming down the narrow rocky path like a purple machine-gun volley.
"My lead!" Isolde barked!
Isolde surged half a pace ahead of Leona, crossing both of her silver parrying daggers in front of her face.
Her Second Stage Core flared with dense mana.
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!

Isolde didn’t dodge any of the attacks, she moved her daggers in a geometric web of micro-parries, deflecting twenty psionic needles in a tenth of a second, while letting the remaining needles strike her reinforced leather cuirass, tanking the mental backlash through stubborn will.
"NOW!" Isolde shouted through clamped teeth with blood leaking from her ears as she held the breach open.
SWOOSH!
From beneath Isolde’s shadow, Leona slipped through.
’Just like the old days...’
Leona dropped low to the stone, sliding across the gravel like an eel as she completely bypassed the psionic fire.
’I won’t tell her thank you though.’
She reached the ledge in the blink of an eye, rising like a striking sea serpent with her trench-machete flashing in an upward brutal thrust.
SHLICK.
The heavy steel blade punched clean through the golden filigree armor on the right side of Ananya’s chest, carving four inches into the meat.
"GAH!" Ananya screamed, her eyes bulging in shock.
Leona grabbed the collar of Ananya’s crimson silk with her left hand, pulling the woman down until their noses almost touched, her hazel eyes burning with savage ferocity.
"Don’t you dare try to run away from this, pretty girl," Leona snarled into her face.
Ananya’s face contorted with panic.
"YOU FOO—"
She released her staff with one hand with her fingers clawing frantically toward Leona’s eyes, channeling a point-blank burst of psionic fire...
WHOOSH!
Leona detonated a burst of emerald wind-mana beneath her own armpit.

The pressurized wind threw her body backward five feet, slipping out of Ananya’s reach just as the purple psionic blast screamed through the empty air where her skull had been half a heartbeat earlier.
"Augh... You fools..."
Ananya staggered forward, clutching her bleeding chest with her mind reeling from the sudden displacement...
WHOOSH!
From the high-left flank, a shadow eclipsed the sun as Isolde descended from the sky like a falling hawk.

She had vaulted off the rock, twisting her body horizontally in mid-air, bringing her right combat boot around in a vicious three-hundred-and-sixty-degree rotational heel-drop aimed dead center at the side of Ananya’s skull.
"Hold on~," Isolde purred, her melodic voice full of sadistic mockery.
BOOOOOOOM!
The kick landed with the concussive force of an executioner’s axe and the violence of Isolde’s steel-reinforced boot slammed into Ananya’s temple.
The force drove Ananya’s head violently downward.
CRACK-SMASH!
Ananya’s skull struck the solid basalt ledge with the stone fracturing into a three-foot spiderweb crater beneath her forehead.
Her face bounced upward off the shattered stone and a fountain of blood and broken gold beads sprayed across the ledge as a raw, blood-curdling shriek tore from her shattered jaw.
"AAAAAAAAAAAGH!"
Ananya collapsed onto her side, twitching violently in the dirt with her lotus staff clattering down the rocky slope into the canyon below.
Isolde landed lightly on the ledge beside her, flicking a drop of blood from the heel of her boot, looking down at the twitching Indus scion with a cold immaculate smile.
"Much better," Isolde murmured. "Now her hair can fly however it likes."
High above the battlefield, suspended in the upper airspace... Aki was still caught in the rising currents.
The emerald wind-mana venting from her combat gloves kept her body suspended in a slow controlled rotation with her dark blue hair billowing around her pale focused face.
Her azure eyes, enhanced by the compressed water-mana humming from Silas’s Star-Iron necklace, took in the entire panorama of Sector Forty-Four.
It was an unadorned slaughterhouse.
To the south, the massive craters from Seraphina’s battle were still smoking with white fire.
To the west, the basin was torn apart by Maya’s tectonic strikes, with Gareth broken in the dirt and Maya lying unconscious beside the stone.
Below her, Leona and Isolde were standing over the broken body of Ananya Rao, while Devan Varma’s volcanic aura began to pulse with dangerous heat.
’It’s just destruction everywhere,’ Aki thought, her chest tightening as she gripped the star-iron limbs of her composite bow.
She had never asked for this to happen...
’It’s not like I wanted to join them,’ she thought, watching the plumes of red smoke drift across the wasteland. ’But do I really have a choice?’
"SCREEEE!"
A sharp piercing cry tore through the airspace directly behind her head.
WHOOSH!
An airborne Spirit Beast which was a nine-foot-wide razor-winged Obsidian Sand-Falcon summoned by Kira Bennett’s power dove out of the sun, its razor-sharp talons outstretched to sever Aki’s neck.
"I’m not scared of you."
She twisted her torso in mid-air, sliding a slender, curved star-iron dagger from the sheath at her thigh.
SHLICK!
With a single blinding horizontal slash, Aki cut the beast’s throat clean open.
The Obsidian Falcon didn’t even get to screech as it dissolved instantly into a spray of yellow sand and dying spiritual particles that dissipated against the wind.
"Now who attacked me...?"
Aki landed lightly on the crest of a high narrow sandstone pillar overlooking the eastern dunes as she lowered her dagger with her sharp azure eyes scanning the vast yellow expanse below.
A mile out, tearing across the sand dunes like a frightened desert hare, was Kira Bennett.
The Australis scion was using the loose silt as cover, slipping between the hollows of the dunes, frantically running away after realizing her traps had been dismantled and her Spirits were down.
Aki looked at the fleeing woman as she slowly clicked her tongue against the roof of her mouth.
WHOOSH!
The glove on her right hand began to glow with pressurized emerald light as the wind-channels roared with high-speed torque.
She gripped her bow with her boots pressing into the stone as she leaned forward into the boots.
’I might as well contribute to the destruction,’ Aki thought, a sharp resolve settling behind her eyes.
BOOM!
She shot off the pillar like a falling star, plunging down toward the dunes to hunt.
"Fuck... Fuck... Fuck...!"
Kira Bennett’s breath came in ragged desperate hitches.
Her bare sun-darkened shoulders were slick with a mixture of sweat and fine sand that clung to the spiraling ink of her predator tattoos.
With every stride, her worn combat leathers groaned, her boots plunging six inches into the loose crests of the dunes and wrenching free with wet suctioning thuds.
Half a mile to the northwest, past the jagged ribs of an sandstone escarpment, a silhouette was limping across the cracked flats.
Jax.
’He’s on his feet,’ Kira thought, her throat burning like she had swallowed hot lye. ’The bastard actually dragged himself out of the Safe Zone...’
A flicker of relief sparked against her ribs, but it died before she could draw another lungful of dry air.
WHOOSH!

The atmospheric pressure above her head plummeted as the loose grains of sand along the knife-edge of the dune suddenly stopped tumbling, caught in a rising emerald-tinted wind that curled like a vortex of transparent green water.
"Stand down."
The voice was soft and terrifyingly steady.
Kira dug her heels into the reverse slope of the dune, violently arresting her forward momentum.
A spray of hot shale hissed against her calves as she threw her head back, her eyes narrowing into venomous slit-like pupils.
Hovering twenty feet above her in the purple sky, drifting weightlessly against a wind of her own making, was First Princess Aki.

chapters.title: Chapter 580: Aki Joins Violence [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Princess’s midnight-blue combat tunic fluttered against her slender frame with the void-black fabric drinking in the harsh desert glare.

Her azure hair whipped around her temples like silk ribbons, framing a face that was remarkably calm, though her jaw was clamped with the nervous electric tension of someone whose pulse was hammering at two hundred beats a minute.
In her hands, the limbs of her composite star-iron bow were drawn to maximum deflection.
A single needle-thin arrow of compressed, high-frequency emerald wind-mana was nocked to the braided string, humming with a frequency that made the enamel of Kira’s molars throb.
The glowing broadhead was aimed dead center at the hollow of Kira’s throat.
Kira’s knuckles whitened with her hands instinctively dropping into a defensive posture.
’Damn it,’ Kira’s mind raced, her core channels aching with cold empty fatigue. ’This is the worst matchup.’
Her Spirit Beast manipulation relied on surprise, depth, and misdirection.
When an opponent knew she was a summoner... when they had already watched her Dune-Crusher Scyllas get pulverized by an Amazonian siege-strike, the elemental advantage evaporated.
You couldn’t spring a trap on a woman who refused to touch the ground.
’Four,’ Kira calculated with bitter precision. ’I have four bonded spirits left in my soul-well.’
Dozens of lesser beasts had already been snuffed out across the northern sector.

On any normal campaign in the red wastes of Australis, she would have stopped, poured water onto the earth, and sung the guttural mourning dirges for the bonded souls she had lost but out here? In this slaughterhouse? Mourning was a luxury reserved for the dead.
She needed to survive.
She needed to drag her delegation across the finish line, if only to claim the amount promised by Australis’s President yet, Kira wasn’t blind.
’What chance do we actually have to take the crown?’ she thought with cold despair pooling beneath her breastbone.
She had been the Commonwealth’s primary offensive anchor, and her highest-tier beasts had been swatted out of existence like midges against an iron wall.
...Then Jax?
Jax was a marvel of low-rent improvisation, but there was a hard immutable ceiling to how much bullshit a man could spin when facing monsters who turned square miles of rock into boiling glass.
Still, Kira had not crawled out of the salt marshes of the southern rim just to roll onto her back and present her throat to a pampered royal.
CRACK!
Kira dropped her weight six inches with her thighs coiling like tempered springs and her tattooed forearms rising into a low-slung outback claw-guard.
Up in the air, Aki observed the shift but the Princess didn’t speak.
She simply tilted her chin with her azure hair whistling in the whistling desert gale, and gave a single firm nod.
WHOOSH!
A vibrant jade-green luminescence ignited within Aki’s azure irises, bleeding outward along the delicate contours of her eyelashes...
The wind-channels woven into the midnight-blue leather of her gloves flared to maximum saturation, venting fine micro-pressurized jets of air that hissed like coiled serpents around her wrists.
TWANG!
The star-iron bowstring snapped and the emerald wind-arrow tore through the twenty-foot gap with high speed.
WHOOOOOSH!
Kira didn’t try to track the projectile with her eyes, instead the second the bowstring hummed, she threw her entire torso horizontally across the face of the dune.
BOOM!

The wind-arrow struck the sand where her chest had been a fraction of a second earlier and the compressed mana detonated upon contact, blowing a six-foot crater into the dune and showering Kira’s back in stinging superheated grit.
Kira used the concussive expansion of the blast to accelerate her roll, snapping both hands together in a brutal twin-palm mudra.
"Blood-Stalker Pack!"
RUMBLE-SNAP!
The sand directly in front of her tore open!
Two massive canine constructs... Chitin-Plated Dune Jackals, their bodies woven from dark compressed earth-spirit mana and tipped with three-inch bone fangs erupted from the silt.
’Are they going to lunge at me...?’ Aki thought.
They didn’t lunge at the sky though, the monsters bounded off the sand, crossing their trajectories to create a double-helix pincer leap aimed straight at Aki’s descending form.
"Heh."
Aki was falling, but she wasn’t falling helplessly.
Her right hand released the bow, letting the star-iron weapon hang across her back by its braided leather sling, while her gloves ignited with emerald combustion.
WHOOSH!

She detonated a directional air-burst beneath her left heel, violently pivoting her body horizontally in mid-air as the first Dune Jackal snapped its jaws on empty air, its teeth clacking together like iron traps inches from her shoulder.
Aki didn’t let it pass.
As the beast cleared her flank, her right boot... reinforced with a dense razor-sharp edge of compressed wind-mana snapped out in a vicious, sweeping roundhouse kick.
CRACK!

The kick caught the Spirit Beast dead in the jaw and the concussive force shattered the construct’s bone-plated skull into flying calcified shards, dispersing its spiritual core into a cloud of dying yellow dust.
Before the second Jackal could re-orient its airborne arc, Aki brought her hands together.
"Disperse!" Aki gasped.
POW!
A twin-palm blast of pressurized wind erupted from her gloves, catching the second beast squarely in the ribs.
The concussive force sounded like a muffled thunderclap, blowing the construct backward forty yards where it tumbled and dissolved against the face of the opposite dune.
Aki hit the sand on the balls of her feet with her boots sinking three inches into the soft yellow silt.
Her heart was hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
’I’m doing this,’ she realized, a sudden cold jolt of adrenaline prickling across her scalp. ’This is real... No one is standing in front of me...’
WHOOSH-SHLICK!
Kira burst through the cloud of settling spirit-dust like a feral cat.

Her fingers were curled into rigid, iron-like talons with her fingernails elongated and hardened by dense earth-mana into three-inch quartz claws as she threw a savage diagonal claw-swipe aimed straight for Aki’s eyes.
"Oop!"
Aki leaned her upper body backward with the razor-sharp quartz claws whistling a quarter of an inch past the tip of her nose.
Kira’s follow-through was relentless as she stepped deep into Aki’s guard, driving her left elbow up toward the Princess’s chin.
SMACK!
Aki brought her left forearm up, intercepting the elbow with a desperate unrefined block.

The blunt impact sent a dull numbing shockwave up Aki’s arm, but instead of retreating, Aki’s eyes flared as she drove her right palm straight into Kira’s solar plexus, releasing a microscopic point-blank jet of pressurized wind.
WHAM!

The air-burst blew the oxygen clean out of Kira’s lungs as Kira gagged with her footing slipping backward across the loose silt, but the Australis scion threw her weight sideways as her right leg whipped around in a low, sweeping kick that caught Aki behind the left ankle.
THUD!
Aki’s balance broke and both women crashed hard into the sand, rolling down the thirty-degree slope of the dune in a tangled chaotic blur of limbs, leathers, and flying grit!
CRUNCH! SMACK!
Kira threw a short brutal right cross that grazed Aki’s cheekbone, splitting the skin and drawing a bead of red.
Aki’s teeth snapped shut, once again, the stinging pain didn’t make her panic but it made her vision go crystal-clear.
As they tumbled to the base of the dune, Aki planted both hands in the sand, torqued her hips with desperate agility, and planted both heels firmly into Kira’s chest.
WHOOOOOOSH!

Aki channeled an explosive wind blast through the soles of her boots and Kira was launched eight feet vertically into the air as the Princess rolled onto her feet, surging upright before Kira could hit the ground.
Her midnight-blue gloves roared with emerald luminescence and she stepped in.
"Hah!"
The Princess struck first with sharp piston-like left jab to the floating ribs.
THUMP!
Then she followed up with a snapping right cross to the collarbone.
CRACK!
’Just get knocked out already!’
Aki spun her body with wind magic in order to land a spinning back-kick that connected squarely with Kira’s sternum.
BOOM!

And finally, as Kira’s body began to pitch backward, Aki gathered every remaining drop of her wind-mana into her right fist, planting her front foot so deeply into the bedrock beneath the silt that the stone cracked.
She drove the straight right dead center into Kira’s jaw.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The detonation blew the surrounding sand outward in a ten-foot ring as Kira’s eyes rolled back into her head with the last of her consciousness erased in an instant.
Her body went completely limp, flying backward fifteen yards before skipping across the hard shale and coming to a motionless, sprawling halt in the dust.
Aki stood with her right arm fully extended with her chest heaving in violent agonizing gasps.
"Haaah... Haah... Haah..."
She doubled over, resting her hands against her knees, wheezing as hot air tore through her raw throat.
Blood dripped from her split cheek, landing in tiny dark circles on the yellow silt.

’It’s... so exhausting,’ Aki thought, her vision swimming with gray spots. ’To keep hitting someone... to keep forcing yourself forward when every nerve is screaming to stop... How do Maya and Silas do this every single day?’
Before she could wipe the sweat from her eyes—
PING!
The fine hairs on the back of Aki’s neck snapped upright as her internal alarms went off like a ringing bell!
Without a second of conscious thought, Aki detonated an emergency wind-burst beneath her soles, launching her body twenty feet straight up into the air.
SWOOSH-CLACK!

A low whistling arc of razor-sharp star-iron wire snapped across the empty airspace where her knees had been standing half a heartbeat earlier as Aki landed lightly atop an isolated sandstone boulder with her chest heaving and her azure eyes immediately tracking down toward the canyon floor.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Approaching from the eastern rise, stepping with a slow exaggerated limp, was Jax Sterling-Cross.
His soot-stained combat tunic was torn open, his left forearm tightly bound in dirty field linen that still carried the pungent minty reek of alchemical salve.
His hair was a wild, windblown mess, but his face carried an expression of mild curiosity as Aki’s hand drifted back to her bow and her heart gave a hard triumphant thud.
’I took out Kira,’ the thought flashed through her mind. ’If I take him out right now... Australis is eliminated. That’s an entire sovereign delegation wiped off the board by my hands...’

The exhilaration surged through her channels, washing away the ache in her lungs as she drew three star-iron arrows from her quiver simultaneously, nocking all three to the bowstring in an interlocking fan!
WHOOSH!
She poured her emerald wind-mana into the shafts as the arrows began whining with high-speed rotational torque!
TWANG-TWANG-TWANG!
She released.
Three screaming streaks of jade-green light plunged out of the sky, forming a lethal triangular bracket designed to leave zero escape.
Jax took a casual half-stumbling step to the left, tilted his chin backward by three inches, and hopped lightly off his right heel.
THWIP! THWIP! THWIP!
The three arrows buried themselves feathers-deep into the sandstone boulder behind him, missing his flesh by millimeters and Aki blinked with her mouth falling slightly open.
’How...?’ her mind stuttered. ’He didn’t even accelerate his core! He just... walked through the trajectory?!’
Jax didn’t look up at her.

He casually sauntered over to where Kira lay motionless in the dust as he bent down, effortlessly hoisting the unconscious summoner over his broad shoulder like a sack of grain, before finally lifting his eyes to meet the First Princess’s gaze.
"You know," Jax drawled. "it’s extraordinarily rude to shoot at a man while he’s rescuing his comrade. Didn’t they teach you royal manners in that fancy palace?"
Aki dropped off the boulder, landing on the sand ten paces away, her bow lowered as her jaw went tight with mounting irritation.
"Drop her and yield, Jax," Aki demanded, forcing herself to sound like an authoritative royal. "You’re injured, your partner is down, and you have nowhere left to run."
Jax let out a short snort.
"Your next line is," Jax announced, pointing his unbandaged right index finger dead at her nose. "’Please stand down, I do not wish to hurt you any further!’"
Aki’s mouth opened, completely on instinct.
"Please stand down, I do not wish to hurt you any furth—"
She choked on the syllables with the words cutting off with a sharp sound as her eyes went wide as saucers.
A violent burning crimson flooded up her neck, rushing all the way to the tips of her ears.
’H-How did he do that?!’ she panicked internally, her heart practically leaping into her throat.
Her cheeks puffed out into an enormous mortified pout with her small hands trembling around her bow.

"See?" Jax grinned, his eyes crinkling with shameless smugness. "Predictable! You royals always talk like you’re reading straight out of an etiquette manual... It’s always ’please this’ and ’I do not wish that.’ Have you ever had an original thought in your life, Princess?"
"B-Be quiet!" Aki squeaked, her face flaming as her composure shattered into flustered chaos.

The wind-channels woven into the midnight-blue leather of her gloves flared to maximum saturation, venting fine micro-pressurized jets of air that hissed like coiled serpents around her wrists.

The star-iron bowstring snapped and the emerald wind-arrow tore through the twenty-foot gap with high speed.
WHOOOOOSH!

BOOM!

"Blood-Stalker Pack!"
RUMBLE-SNAP!

Her right hand released the bow, letting the star-iron weapon hang across her back by its braided leather sling, while her gloves ignited with emerald combustion.
WHOOSH!
