chapters.title: Chapter 581: Compression [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She didn’t reach for an arrow.
WHOOSH!
Aki clenched her right hand into a fist as the other glove began to flare with a crimson-orange radiance.
’Have this one!’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A roaring torrent of high-power elemental fire erupted from her open palm, tearing across the ten paces like an erupting volcano.
The heat was immense, flash-scorching the sand and turning the air into a shimmering distorted furnace but Jax’s lazy smirk didn’t waver.
He didn’t try to block the fire.
The microsecond her glove flared orange, Jax fell backward like a cut timber.
He used Kira’s weight on his shoulder as a counter-balance, dropping flat against the reverse slope of the dune and letting the three-thousand-degree torrent of flame roar harmlessly over his head...
The heat wave washed over the crest, but Jax was already moving!
He kicked off the sandstone, sliding forty yards down the loose yellow silt like an alpine skater, using the smoke and the distortion of Aki’s own blast to completely break line of sight.
"Hey! Get back here!" Aki yelled, coughing through the hot smoke and then she stepped forward to give chase...
TUG!
Her right wrist refused to move.
Aki froze as she looked down at her arm.
Wrapped tightly around her leather bracer was a translucent thread of star-iron wire.
’When did he—?!’
Before she could channel her wind to sever the cord, her body shifted forward by an inch.
SNAP-SNAP-SNAP-SNAP!
The movement triggered a horrific interlocking chain-reaction.
From four concealed anchor points buried beneath the sand, dozens of pre-rigged star-iron wires whipped out of the silt...
They coiled around her ankles, snapped across her waist, pinned her elbows to her ribs, and locked her wrists together in an immaculate suffocating web of high-tension wire!
Aki was rendered utterly immobile!
She stood frozen on the face of the dune, bound like a decorative holiday roast with her composite bow pinned uselessly against her spine.
"Mmmph!" Aki growled, her cheeks puffing out into an enormous furious pout as she thrashed against the wires but the star-iron didn’t budge.
The harder she pulled, the tighter the knots bit into her armor.
Down at the base of the gully, Jax slid to a smooth halt behind a shelf of fractured basalt.
He gently set Kira down against the stone, shaking the sand from his hair with a satisfied grin.
Kira groaned softly with her eyelids fluttering open as she reached up, clutching her swollen jaw with a weak trembling hand, her dark eyes blinking through the haze of unconsciousness.
"Ugh..." Kira croaked, spitting a drop of blood. "Did we... did we leave this place yet...?"
"Not yet, sleeping beauty," Jax whispered, crouching beside her and peering over the rock. "Keep your head down. The Princess is currently throwing a royal tantrum on the slope."
Kira forced herself upright, her gaze tracking up the dune to see Aki trussed up like a netted fish.
She looked at Jax, her brow furrowing in genuine confusion.
"How... how the hell did you tie her up?" Kira rasped. "She was hovering forty feet in the air and she has wind-mana!"
Jax tapped the side of his nose, his grin widening with pure smugness.

"Simple arithmetic, my dear Kira," Jax whispered with theatrical gravity. "When she jumped off that boulder, she kicked up a dust vortex. I simply palmed three micro-spools of star-iron thread into the rising wind... The wind she generated to stabilize her descent actually drew the lines right into her own blind spots then, when she fired that big dramatic fireball, the expansion expanded the air pressure, forcing the anchor pins deep into the bedrock! She literally tied her own knots!"
Kira stared at him with complete deadpan disgust.
"That is the biggest load of horseshit I have ever heard in my entire life," Kira muttered. "You just dropped a spool in the dirt and she stepped on it, didn’t she?"
"Details, details," Jax waved his hand dismissively. "The point is, we have superiority—"
CRACKLE!
The air above the dune suddenly turned cherry-red.
BOOOOM!
The star-iron wires were vaporized as Aki tore through the following firestorm like an enraged little demon with her azure hair whipping wildly as her gloves roared like superheated plasma!
"Hey, get back here!"
She descended from the sky like a falling meteor, her face completely flushed with murderous embarrassment.
"JAX STERLING-CROSS!" Aki’s voice echoed across the canyon and Jax’s jaw dropped.
"Whoa, whoa, whoa!" Jax yelped, scrambling backward on his hands and knees. "Kira! Spirits! Deploy the beasts! Put up a wall!"
Kira looked down at her empty palms with her voice cracking.
"They’re dead, you idiot! I told you, my soul-well is completely drained! I don’t have a single lizard left!"
"Fuck!" Jax barked!
He scrambled to his feet, thrusting both palms forward toward the descending fireball as his internal core surged, finally revealing his native elemental signature.
FWOOSH!

Dense pressurized torrents of water mana erupted from Jax’s hands as he unleashed five high-velocity water blades, screaming through the air like spinning hydraulic saws aimed straight at Aki’s trajectory.
’Is that how it is...?’
Her azure eyes tracked the water blades with a cold look in her eyes.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!

Aki twisted her body in mid-air with liquid elegance as she slipped between the five water blades by inches, letting the high-pressure spray mist harmlessly against her leather cuirass, before detonating a final concussive wind-burst beneath her heels.
THUD!
She landed three paces in front of Jax, the concussive landing throwing a ring of sand across his boots and Jax froze.
His hands were still raised with his core flickering and his eyes were wide as he looked into Aki’s furious unblinking glare.
He swallowed hard, forcing his mouth into a trembling, nervous smile as he lifted his right index finger, clearing his throat to deploy his ultimate psychological defense.
"Your next line is," Jax bluffed, pointing at her chest, "’Surrender now, or I will have no choice but to use force!’"
Aki did not speak.
She stood completely motionless.
Jax blinked.
"Uh... wait. Aren’t you going to say it?"
Aki maintained dead suffocating silence and beneath her cold exterior, her mind was working at high speed.
’How do I get revenge on this clown?’ Aki thought, her azure eyes narrowing into dangerous slits.
She had watched him fight and she had felt his tricks... It was safe to say that she had deciphered his entire methodology.
Jax Sterling-Cross was not a bumbling idiot... he was a brilliant, psychological combatant.
He didn’t rely on overwhelming mana or high-tier martial arts as he thrived entirely on his opponent’s confusion, frustration, and predictable emotional reactions.
He baited high-borns into shouting standard noble lines, guessed those lines through basic behavioral reading, and used their momentary shock to deploy cheap mundane traps.
Apart from his dirty tricks and his sliver of water-mana, he had virtually nothing left in the tank.
A slow terrifying grin began to spread across Aki’s delicate face as she raised her right hand, pointing her glove straight at his forehead.
She puffed out her chest, mimicking his exact insolent posture, and raised her voice in a loud dramatic declaration.
"Your next line is...!"
Jax blinked and Kira blinked as well as Aki’s mouth stayed open.
Her mind suddenly went terrifyingly blank.
’Wait,’ Aki panicked internally, her pulse stuttering. ’What was he going to say?! What does an Australis scion even say when they’re cornered?!’
The silence stretched for one second... Two seconds... Three seconds...
Aki’s cheeks puffed out like a pair of ripe plums with her face turning violently red from forehead to collarbone.
"Uh..." Aki squeaked as her voice cracked. "Uh... uh..."
Jax and Kira stared at her in utter bewilderment and Jax’s left eyebrow twitched as a small involuntary snort escaped his nose.
PFFFFT!
Jax started to chuckle.
"Did you... did you forget your own line, Princess?"
That snicker was the fatal mistake as the embarrassed flush on Aki’s face instantly vanished, replaced by an expression of pure malice.
Her azure hair floated upward as her gloves detonated with terrifying fury.
"YOUR NEXT LINE IS SCREAMING IN PAIN AT BEING BURNED ALIVE!" Aki shrieked at the top of her lungs.
Jax’s smile died and Kira’s eyes bulged.
"Huh?!" both Australis scions shouted in unison.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Aki unleashed everything as a wall of roaring superheated crimson-and-white solar fire detonated from her glove.

The cataclysmic inferno completely swallowed the rocky area, vaporizing the basalt, flash-boiling the sand into an ocean of green glass, and tearing a screaming mushroom cloud of black soot and fire into the sky.
WHOOSH!
Inside the heart of the explosion, two emergency transponders detonated simultaneously with a bit of light.

The physical bodies of Jax Sterling-Cross and Kira Bennett dissolved into millions of shimmering ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple stratosphere as the World Council’s extraction protocol ripped them clean out of the realm.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating optical relays, the mechanical voice chimed with authority.
"Notice of Elimination."
"The representatives of the Commonwealth of Australis have suffered catastrophic combat trauma... The Commonwealth of Australis is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Aki stood in the center of the roaring crater, panting heavily with her face covered in black soot and her chest heaving as she lowered her smoking glove.
Before she could even catch her breath—
BZZZZZZZZT!
A second administrative chime echoed across the entire Sector Forty-Four.
"CRITICAL ANNOUNCEMENT."
"The Primary Representative of the Crown, Crown Prince Alexander of House Castellian, has suffered decisive defeat and incapacitation. Crown Prince Alexander has been extracted from the field..."
Silence fell over the world.
Alexander? The Crown Prince? The undisputed Fourth Stage titan who had accepted star-iron suppression rings just to mock those of the lower stages?
Defeated?
In every surviving warrior’s mind, a single terrifying name surfaced simultaneously.
’Kara White...’
Had the mysterious Lord of Blessed Land already reached him? Had she hunted down the Prince of the World and crushed him beneath her power?
Before anyone could process the earth-shattering news, the broadcast relay chimed for a third time.
"The two-hour preliminary engagement phase has concluded."
"Territory compression protocol is now active... All surviving participants will be immediately transported to the Central Ring for the final resolution."
WHOOSH!
A suffocating pressure seized the fabric of space and the familiar, nauseating sensation of long-distance spatial displacement gripped Aki’s stomach but this time, she didn’t close her eyes.
’I don’t want to faint again...’
Aki circulated her compressed mana through her temporary pathways, preparing herself for the teleportation that was about to happen.
WHOOSH!
The desert vanished in a flash of blinding white light and when reality snapped back into focus, Aki didn’t stumble.
She didn’t feel dizzy either.
Her boots touched down firmly upon an immense circular plateau of polished black star-iron that hovered thousands of feet above the shattered landscape... the Central Ring.
She looked around and the field was decimated.
Fifty paces to the north, Devan Varma was still sitting cross-legged upon a raised dais of scorched basalt.
His muscular bronze chest was unmarked with his arms crossed over his coiling gold nagas and his eyes closed in deep undisturbed meditation.

Near the base of his dais sprawled face-down in the dirt, was Ananya Rao... she was completely unconscious, her gold beads scattered across the stone and her skull swollen where Leona and Isolde had brutally double-teamed her before the compression.
Standing twenty paces away, Leona leaned heavily against her trench-machete, breathing hard, while Isolde stood beside her, coldly wiping blood from her silver parrying daggers.
Then... Aki’s gaze drifted toward the western edge of the ring.
Her breath caught in her throat.
Sitting casually on a low star-iron bench, propping her chin up with one hand, was Kara.
The Lord of Blessed Land looked offensively relaxed.
’Was she... sleeping?!’ Aki thought, her jaw dropping in disbelief.
Sitting twenty paces behind Kara were Valerius Sterling and Rook Sterling.
Valerius was fully armored now, though he still looked vaguely bored, while Rook was busy organizing his reconnaissance plates.
Suddenly, the air temperature across the entire platform spiked violently.
CRRRRRRRK!
Aki spun on her heel with her boots shifting back as she raised a guard and stepping onto the eastern edge of the star-iron ring was a woman.
Her hair was no longer crimson... it flowed in long weightless waves of celestial silver-white that drifted against the thermal updrafts like vaporized mercury.
A runic crest burned with radiance along the left side of her porcelain jaw.

The heat radiating from her skin alone was so much that the polished star-iron beneath her boots was groaning, the fine sand drifting across the platform flash-vitrifying into sheets of translucent green glass with every step she took.
Seraphina Bloom.
Aki instinctively cleared out of her path with a cold shiver running down her spine.
’Is that... Seraphina...?’ Aki thought, her azure eyes wide with awe. ’She looks completely different. What level of fire is that...?’
Seraphina’s chest heaved slightly beneath her scorched cuirass.
She was exhausted.
The brutal high-intensity battle against Alexander had pushed her core to its limit, and she knew her Primordial Spirit fusion had less than two minutes remaining before the backlash set in.
Yet, she held her head high, her glowing silver eyes sweeping across the surviving fighters with cold disdain.
"So," Seraphina drawled, her melodic voice carrying a dual-toned spirit-resonance that echoed across the platform. "You’re the ones who survived, huh?"

sentences.text: She didn’t reach for an arrow.
WHOOSH!
Aki clenched her right hand into a fist as the other glove began to flare with a crimson-orange radiance.
’Have this one!’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A roaring torrent of high-power elemental fire erupted from her open palm, tearing across the ten paces like an erupting volcano.
The heat was immense, flash-scorching the sand and turning the air into a shimmering distorted furnace but Jax’s lazy smirk didn’t waver.
He didn’t try to block the fire.
The microsecond her glove flared orange, Jax fell backward like a cut timber.
He used Kira’s weight on his shoulder as a counter-balance, dropping flat against the reverse slope of the dune and letting the three-thousand-degree torrent of flame roar harmlessly over his head...
The heat wave washed over the crest, but Jax was already moving!
He kicked off the sandstone, sliding forty yards down the loose yellow silt like an alpine skater, using the smoke and the distortion of Aki’s own blast to completely break line of sight.
"Hey!
Get back here!" Aki yelled, coughing through the hot smoke and then she stepped forward to give chase...
TUG!
Her right wrist refused to move.
Aki froze as she looked down at her arm.
Wrapped tightly around her leather bracer was a translucent thread of star-iron wire.
’When did he—?!’
Before she could channel her wind to sever the cord, her body shifted forward by an inch.
SNAP-SNAP-SNAP-SNAP!
The movement triggered a horrific interlocking chain-reaction.
From four concealed anchor points buried beneath the sand, dozens of pre-rigged star-iron wires whipped out of the silt...
They coiled around her ankles, snapped across her waist, pinned her elbows to her ribs, and locked her wrists together in an immaculate suffocating web of high-tension wire!
Aki was rendered utterly immobile!
She stood frozen on the face of the dune, bound like a decorative holiday roast with her composite bow pinned uselessly against her spine.
"Mmmph!" Aki growled, her cheeks puffing out into an enormous furious pout as she thrashed against the wires but the star-iron didn’t budge.
The harder she pulled, the tighter the knots bit into her armor.
Down at the base of the gully, Jax slid to a smooth halt behind a shelf of fractured basalt.
He gently set Kira down against the stone, shaking the sand from his hair with a satisfied grin.
Kira groaned softly with her eyelids fluttering open as she reached up, clutching her swollen jaw with a weak trembling hand, her dark eyes blinking through the haze of unconsciousness.
"Ugh..." Kira croaked, spitting a drop of blood.
"Did we... did we leave this place yet...?"
"Not yet, sleeping beauty," Jax whispered, crouching beside her and peering over the rock.
"Keep your head down.
The Princess is currently throwing a royal tantrum on the slope."
Kira forced herself upright, her gaze tracking up the dune to see Aki trussed up like a netted fish.
She looked at Jax, her brow furrowing in genuine confusion.
"How... how the hell did you tie her up?" Kira rasped.
"She was hovering forty feet in the air and she has wind-mana!"
Jax tapped the side of his nose, his grin widening with pure smugness.
"Simple arithmetic, my dear Kira," Jax whispered with theatrical gravity.
"When she jumped off that boulder, she kicked up a dust vortex.
I simply palmed three micro-spools of star-iron thread into the rising wind...

The wind she generated to stabilize her descent actually drew the lines right into her own blind spots then, when she fired that big dramatic fireball, the expansion expanded the air pressure, forcing the anchor pins deep into the bedrock!
She literally tied her own knots!"
Kira stared at him with complete deadpan disgust.
"That is the biggest load of horseshit I have ever heard in my entire life," Kira muttered.
"You just dropped a spool in the dirt and she stepped on it, didn’t she?"
"Details, details," Jax waved his hand dismissively.
"The point is, we have superiority—"
CRACKLE!
The air above the dune suddenly turned cherry-red.
BOOOOM!
The star-iron wires were vaporized as Aki tore through the following firestorm like an enraged little demon with her azure hair whipping wildly as her gloves roared like superheated plasma!
"Hey, get back here!"
She descended from the sky like a falling meteor, her face completely flushed with murderous embarrassment.
"JAX STERLING-CROSS!" Aki’s voice echoed across the canyon and Jax’s jaw dropped.
"Whoa, whoa, whoa!" Jax yelped, scrambling backward on his hands and knees.
"Kira!
Spirits!
Deploy the beasts!
Put up a wall!"
Kira looked down at her empty palms with her voice cracking.
"They’re dead, you idiot!
I told you, my soul-well is completely drained!
I don’t have a single lizard left!"
"Fuck!" Jax barked!
He scrambled to his feet, thrusting both palms forward toward the descending fireball as his internal core surged, finally revealing his native elemental signature.
FWOOSH!

Dense pressurized torrents of water mana erupted from Jax’s hands as he unleashed five high-velocity water blades, screaming through the air like spinning hydraulic saws aimed straight at Aki’s trajectory.
’Is that how it is...?’
Her azure eyes tracked the water blades with a cold look in her eyes.
SWISH!
SWISH!
SWISH!

Aki twisted her body in mid-air with liquid elegance as she slipped between the five water blades by inches, letting the high-pressure spray mist harmlessly against her leather cuirass, before detonating a final concussive wind-burst beneath her heels.
THUD!
She landed three paces in front of Jax, the concussive landing throwing a ring of sand across his boots and Jax froze.
His hands were still raised with his core flickering and his eyes were wide as he looked into Aki’s furious unblinking glare.
He swallowed hard, forcing his mouth into a trembling, nervous smile as he lifted his right index finger, clearing his throat to deploy his ultimate psychological defense.
"Your next line is," Jax bluffed, pointing at her chest, "’Surrender now, or I will have no choice but to use force!’"
Aki did not speak.
She stood completely motionless.
Jax blinked.
"Uh... wait.
Aren’t you going to say it?"
Aki maintained dead suffocating silence and beneath her cold exterior, her mind was working at high speed.
’How do I get revenge on this clown?’ Aki thought, her azure eyes narrowing into dangerous slits.
She had watched him fight and she had felt his tricks...
It was safe to say that she had deciphered his entire methodology.
Jax Sterling-Cross was not a bumbling idiot... he was a brilliant, psychological combatant.
He didn’t rely on overwhelming mana or high-tier martial arts as he thrived entirely on his opponent’s confusion, frustration, and predictable emotional reactions.
He baited high-borns into shouting standard noble lines, guessed those lines through basic behavioral reading, and used their momentary shock to deploy cheap mundane traps.
Apart from his dirty tricks and his sliver of water-mana, he had virtually nothing left in the tank.
A slow terrifying grin began to spread across Aki’s delicate face as she raised her right hand, pointing her glove straight at his forehead.
She puffed out her chest, mimicking his exact insolent posture, and raised her voice in a loud dramatic declaration.
"Your next line is...!"
Jax blinked and Kira blinked as well as Aki’s mouth stayed open.
Her mind suddenly went terrifyingly blank.
’Wait,’ Aki panicked internally, her pulse stuttering. ’What was he going to say?!
What does an Australis scion even say when they’re cornered?!’
The silence stretched for one second...
Two seconds...
Three seconds...
Aki’s cheeks puffed out like a pair of ripe plums with her face turning violently red from forehead to collarbone.
"Uh..." Aki squeaked as her voice cracked.
Jax and Kira stared at her in utter bewilderment and Jax’s left eyebrow twitched as a small involuntary snort escaped his nose.
PFFFFT!
Jax started to chuckle.
"Did you... did you forget your own line, Princess?"
That snicker was the fatal mistake as the embarrassed flush on Aki’s face instantly vanished, replaced by an expression of pure malice.
Her azure hair floated upward as her gloves detonated with terrifying fury.
"YOUR NEXT LINE IS SCREAMING IN PAIN AT BEING BURNED ALIVE!" Aki shrieked at the top of her lungs.
Jax’s smile died and Kira’s eyes bulged.
"Huh?!" both Australis scions shouted in unison.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Aki unleashed everything as a wall of roaring superheated crimson-and-white solar fire detonated from her glove.

The cataclysmic inferno completely swallowed the rocky area, vaporizing the basalt, flash-boiling the sand into an ocean of green glass, and tearing a screaming mushroom cloud of black soot and fire into the sky.
WHOOSH!
Inside the heart of the explosion, two emergency transponders detonated simultaneously with a bit of light.

The physical bodies of Jax Sterling-Cross and Kira Bennett dissolved into millions of shimmering ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple stratosphere as the World Council’s extraction protocol ripped them clean out of the realm.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating optical relays, the mechanical voice chimed with authority.
"Notice of Elimination."
"The representatives of the Commonwealth of Australis have suffered catastrophic combat trauma...
The Commonwealth of Australis is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Aki stood in the center of the roaring crater, panting heavily with her face covered in black soot and her chest heaving as she lowered her smoking glove.
Before she could even catch her breath—

chapters.title: Chapter 582: Devan Is A Fraud...?
paragraphs: Over where she was on the field, Kara slowly stood up.
"Haah..."
She rolled her broad shoulders, arching her back with a long lazy stretch that popped several vertebrae.
’What a nice nap.’
She lifted her right hand, offering Aki a small casual wave.
"What’s up, Aki?" Kara called out. "I’m glad you’re still alive."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright delicate pink as she quickly dropped her gaze, coughing into her fist to hide her embarrassment.
’I’m glad you’re alive too...’
Seraphina’s glowing eyes snapped toward Kara and a sharp focus sharpened her gaze.
Her core flared, feeling the immense ocean of gravity and gold-core mana humming beneath the woman’s skin.
’As expected,’ Seraphina thought with her teeth setting. ’She’s stronger than me. In raw unsuppressed output, she’s far beyond what I can reach without the Spirit.’
Seraphina took a half-step forward, ready to issue a challenge... She was going to face Spirit backlash shortly but still, she was going to put her full body into it.
’I want to test the limits of her power...’
Then...
Seraphina paused as her silver eyebrows twitched.
Her gaze slid from Kara’s face, dropping three inches down to the woman’s exposed throat.
’Isn’t that...?’
Seraphina’s breath caught in her throat as resting against Kara’s collarbone was a necklace.
Seraphina blinked once and she blinked twice. She rubbed her eyes with the back of her glove, wondering if the exhaustion was finally causing her eyes to hallucinate.
’It must be...’
However it wasn’t a hallucination.
’I bought that necklace for Silas at the Obsidian Sanhedrin,’ Seraphina’s mind screamed with her jaw locking rigidly.
It was on the double date with Harper... she had purchased this for him because it looked beautiful and complimented him nicely and she also made him promise to not take it off.
’It’s the exact same piece,’ she analyzed frantically. ’Even the lines I carved into the rear clasp while he was looking awa... they’re right there!’
A cold suffocating silence descended over Seraphina’s thoughts.
The puzzle pieces, which had seemed so absurdly disjointed for a long time, violently snapped together with the clarity of a lightning strike.
The mysterious prodigy from Blessed Land... and the mysterious feeling she felt when she was with Silas.
’It’s Silas,’ Seraphina realized with her heart thumping violently against her ribs. ’This isn’t a rival... This is Silas in a female disguise.’
Her knuckles whitened until the skin threatened to tear as her teeth ground together with a harsh audible scrape that turned the heads of Leona as well as Isolde.
She wasn’t angry that he had kept it a secret from her.

Seraphina was a high-tier noble so she understood secrets. She knew she hadn’t earned his complete unreserved trust yet as in a world of political assassinations and bloodline purges, a man who showed all his cards was a man who died in an alley.
She understood the logic and she accepted the secrecy.
Seraphina’s ruby-silver eyes drifted down by three more inches, locking dead center onto Kara’s chest.
’WHY?!’ Seraphina screamed in the privacy of her own soul. ’WHY IN THE SEVEN HELLS DOES HIS FEMALE DISGUISE HAVE BIGGER BREASTS THAN MINE?!’
"Fuuu... Fuuu... Fuuu..."

’It looks like she’s about to explode, is something wrong?’ Silas thought inwardly as he blinked, she couldn’t be annoyed just from looking at Kara’s face right. ’I can’t be that beautiful that I’m making her insecure just looking at me right...?’
Seraphina took a slow deliberate breath, letting the roaring pressure coiled within her ribcage settle down by a fraction.
The initial wave of murderous petty outrage gradually subsided, replaced by a cold calm.
She smoothed the charred leather edge of her cuirass, folding her arms over her chest with an icy sharp-edged composure.
’Look at the positives,’ she told herself, clamping down on the frantic urge to rip the star-iron ring in half with her bare hands. ’Just breathe and look at the bloody positives.’
Silas was alive.
Silas was standing fifty paces away under the broad daylight of Sector Forty-Four, completely intact, bearing the banner of Blessed Land without a single broken bone.
He had slipped past the watchful scrying eyes of the World Council and outmaneuvered even her Mother’s web of informants in the city.
It was brilliant and it was infuriating as well.
’Just like Silas is...’

Once again, she understood secrecy since her mother had drilled it into her marrow since she could walk... an exposed weapon invited counter-measures, and a noble who showed all his cards was dead before his first campaign so she didn’t fault the logic.
’That does not mean I will forgive him for this,’ Seraphina thought, her jaw tightening until the enamel ground audibly together.

Her silver eyebrows twitched, her eyes drifting downward again toward Kara’s silhouette with raw pettiness. ’The moment the teleportation seals break and I visit him again, I’m locking him in an iron vault until he explains every single inch of this absurdity... Starting with why he padded that chest three sizes larger than mine.’
Before her temper could spark a flare of silver flame across the platform, the heavy silence hanging over the Central Ring was shattered by a low grinding sound as basalt cracked and slag hissed.
Fifty paces to the north, Devan Varma rose from his dais.
He moved with the ponderous momentum of a magma shelf shifting beneath continental plates.

’Devan, huh?’ Sera thought, she was not too worried about him... well since Silas was here, the Indus man would naturally go for him instead. ’If I were to face him in this state, it would be a different outcome...’
Sera was sure that the battle could go either way because of the amount of mana she had spent dispatching the Prince.
He did not spare a single downward glance for Ananya Rao, whose limp beaten body lay sprawled in the dust at his heels with her skull swollen and her lotus staff shattered into broken kindling.
CLENCH!
Devan’s knuckles popped like small mortar shells.
WHOOSH!
The runes carved across his collarbones, his broad deltoids, and the thick meat of his forearms flared into an angry vermilion.
’H-huh?’ Aki thought.

The mana radiating off him was not the bright fire Seraphina as well as she commanded... It was thick magma that felt viscous and heavy with sulfur as well as liquefied iron while carrying the crushing kinetic density of the mantle itself.
His molten gaze locked dead-center onto Kara.

"I have waited for this moment," Devan rumbled, his voice scraping low vibrating straight through the floor into everyone’s boot soles. "From the hour the rosters were drafted, I knew the others were merely dry chaff waiting for the spark... Cowards hiding behind bows, nobles prancing with thin rapiers, animals screaming in the dirt. Only you carried the weight of a true beast."
Kara remained standing on the edge of the western flagstones, her dark suit fluttering lazily against her shins.
Her right hand rested loose at her hip as her left arm hung limp in its dark sling.
"Huh?"
She offered him a half-lidded flat gaze that looked less like an opponent appraising a rival and more like a clerk waiting for a tedious patron to finish counting copper coins.
Devan took a heavy step forward and with every stride, the soles of his boots left smoking black-rimmed rings in the ground.

"Do you know the curse of the apex, woman?" Devan asked. "Do you know the agonizing hollow boredom of being the peak in an entire country? In Indus, the elders wept over thresholds and bottlenecks... They spent decades meditating before ancient steles, praying for a drop of divine marrow but to me... those bottlenecks were nothing more than shallow curbs in the road. I stepped over them before my twentieth winter and I have never met an equal as no blade has drawn my blood and no spell has forced me to yield half an inch of ground."
’I’m beginning to get tired of these overconfident fuckers.’ Kara thought, at this point, she would rather face another Ren.
Devan extended both hands with his palms facing outward and his thick fingers curling into heavy iron talons.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A massive circular shockwave of pure volcanic domain aura blasted radially outward from his heels.

The temperature on the platform spiked past the boiling point of lead as a suffocating sulfurous fog rolled across the black metal, the fine quartz sand that had settled on the platform melting instantly into a bubbling translucent film of boiling red slag.
Devan sank his center of gravity into an iron-rooted combat stance with his molten eyes burning into Kara’s forehead.

"You have survived the purge," Devan boomed, his aura churning like an active volcano. "Therefore, I grant you the highest honor a son of Indus can bestow... I grant you permission to be my rival. Stand, Kara White, and let us see if your flesh can endure the molten blood of the world!"
BOOM!
Devan launched and the star-iron beneath his rear foot dented inward by three inches as he closed the thirty-pace gap in seconds.
He tore through the sulfur haze, leaving a twin wake of boiling liquefied iron behind his boots with his right arm cocked back like the piston of a hydraulic press.
Seraphina of course took this opportunity to analyze him.

’He’s not just fast,’ Seraphina analyzed instantly, her eyes narrowing as she read the physical displacement. ’He’s using the liquid magma beneath his boots as a propulsion slide to produce low friction and maximum forward inertia.’
That was quite smart actually...
Devan’s right fist drove forward though it was not a simple punch, instead a condensed three-foot battering ram of boiling four-thousand-degree basalt.
FSSSSSSSSSH... CRASH!
Kara grinned.
"Heh."
She took half a step backward with her left heel, dropping her chin by two inches.
The massive smoking ram of lava screamed past the bridge of her nose with a sickening deafening roar with the blistering hot wind whipping the black hair across her temples.
’Missed?!’ Devan’s mind sparked with immediate violent irritation but he didn’t reset.
"Arrrgh!"
He leaned into the momentum, his left elbow snapping upward in a tight, vicious rising hook, channeling a jagged blade of cooling obsidian along the forearm to take her jaw off.
SWOOSH!
Kara simply tilted her upper torso back by four inches, letting the obsidian edge cleave through the empty airspace above her collarbone.

Devan’s combat instincts took over instantly as he converted the missed hook into a spinning back-fist, pouring a fresh wave of liquid magma into his knuckles to create a blinding cone-shaped spray of molten shrapnel across her entire front.
’Dodge that, rat!’
Kara didn’t dodge the spray.
TAP!
Her boot sole met the star-iron floor.
With an imperceptible twitch of her right shoulder, she stepped straight into the rotation, slipping into his blind spot directly beneath his extended armpit.

The molten spray whistled harmlessly over her right shoulder, scorching the empty air behind her, while her right index and middle fingers snapped out like steel pincers, delivering a sharp double-tap to the nerve cluster right at the hinge of Devan’s floating ribs.
THWACK-THWACK.
"Ghk!" Devan grunted, a sudden jolt of paralysis shooting up his thoracic wall as his breath hitched with his left side going completely numb for half a second.

"Is that all?" Kara asked with her voice completely smooth and drifting into his ear with icy amusement. "You gave that entire theatrical speech about being a lonely god, and you can’t even land a clean hit on a woman with one arm tied behind her back...?"
SNAP!
The veins along Devan’s neck bulged like thick blue cables.
The sheer humiliation of having his elite sequence dismantled by two finger-taps in front of the surviving nobles detonated every restraint in his mind.
"Arrogant wench!" Devan bellowed!
He abandoned close-quarters martial arts as he ripped both palms upward toward the sky, stomping both boots down with as much force as he could.
"Abyssal Magma Geyser!"
RUMBLE-CRUNCH!
The star-iron ring groaned and beneath the metal platform, the structural supports screamed as six massive towering geysers of bubbling white-hot magma ripped through the floor.
The magma curved inward, forming a forty-foot cage of liquid rock and toxic sulfur designed to incinerate every possible method of escape.
’Let’s see you dance across that!’ Devan snarled internally with his teeth bared in feral triumph however to his surprise, she didn’t try and escape.
TAP!
Her boot touched down on the rising wall of the first geyser.
Seraphina’s eyes widened.
’What is he—?!’
Kara didn’t burn as the second her sole met the surface of the three-thousand-degree liquid rock, she released a paper-thin film of high-frequency vibrational mana beneath her leather.
"You’ll have to do better..."
She didn’t fight the heat as she converted the immense upward force to make her move.
STEP! STEP! VAULT!

She skated up the curving face of the erupting lava pillar as if it were a flight of carved marble stairs and with three effortless, fluid strides, she vaulted cleanly over the crest of the magma cage, flipping weightlessly through the sulfurous smoke before dropping back toward the star-iron floor behind him like a falling hawk.
Down below, Seraphina watched the maneuver with her breath caught in her throat.
’That’s my man,’ she thought with a fierce burning pride roaring through her chest.
She had seen high-level movement arts across all the sovereign territories, but nobody moved like Silas.
He didn’t waste a single drop of mana and he didn’t show off... He just took whatever the enemy threw at him and turned it into his personal footstool.
’Show me,’ Seraphina urged silently, her silver eyes glowing with hungry fascination. ’I want to see what you actually are.’
Devan spun around with his boots skidding through cooling slag and his chest heaving like an industrial bellows.
Sweat poured down his bronze skin, boiling away into steam before it could reach his waist.
His knuckles were trembling... not from physical fatigue, but from the raw vibrating fury that was rapidly poisoning his judgment.
Every single rule of combat he had learned in the royal academy was failing him.
The girl wasn’t matching his output at all, instead, she was treating his arts like bad weather.

"Stand still!" Devan roared, his voice cracking with animalistic frustration. "Stop running like a gutter-rat! Stand your ground and cross mana with me! Or was the mighty reputation of Blessed Land just a collection of cheap parlor tricks and circus acrobatics?!"
Kara landed lightly on the scorched metal twenty paces away with the hem of her dark suit settling softly around her ankles.
She sighed.

sentences.text: Over where she was on the field, Kara slowly stood up.
"Haah..."
She rolled her broad shoulders, arching her back with a long lazy stretch that popped several vertebrae.
’What a nice nap.’
She lifted her right hand, offering Aki a small casual wave.
"What’s up, Aki?" Kara called out.
"I’m glad you’re still alive."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright delicate pink as she quickly dropped her gaze, coughing into her fist to hide her embarrassment.
’I’m glad you’re alive too...’
Seraphina’s glowing eyes snapped toward Kara and a sharp focus sharpened her gaze.
Her core flared, feeling the immense ocean of gravity and gold-core mana humming beneath the woman’s skin.
’As expected,’ Seraphina thought with her teeth setting. ’She’s stronger than me.
In raw unsuppressed output, she’s far beyond what I can reach without the Spirit.’
Seraphina took a half-step forward, ready to issue a challenge...
She was going to face Spirit backlash shortly but still, she was going to put her full body into it.
’I want to test the limits of her power...’
Then...
Seraphina paused as her silver eyebrows twitched.
Her gaze slid from Kara’s face, dropping three inches down to the woman’s exposed throat.
’Isn’t that...?’
Seraphina’s breath caught in her throat as resting against Kara’s collarbone was a necklace.
Seraphina blinked once and she blinked twice.
She rubbed her eyes with the back of her glove, wondering if the exhaustion was finally causing her eyes to hallucinate.
’It must be...’
However it wasn’t a hallucination.
’I bought that necklace for Silas at the Obsidian Sanhedrin,’ Seraphina’s mind screamed with her jaw locking rigidly.
It was on the double date with Harper... she had purchased this for him because it looked beautiful and complimented him nicely and she also made him promise to not take it off.
’It’s the exact same piece,’ she analyzed frantically. ’Even the lines I carved into the rear clasp while he was looking awa... they’re right there!’
A cold suffocating silence descended over Seraphina’s thoughts.
The puzzle pieces, which had seemed so absurdly disjointed for a long time, violently snapped together with the clarity of a lightning strike.
The mysterious prodigy from Blessed Land... and the mysterious feeling she felt when she was with Silas.
’It’s Silas,’ Seraphina realized with her heart thumping violently against her ribs. ’This isn’t a rival...
This is Silas in a female disguise.’
Her knuckles whitened until the skin threatened to tear as her teeth ground together with a harsh audible scrape that turned the heads of Leona as well as Isolde.
She wasn’t angry that he had kept it a secret from her.
Seraphina was a high-tier noble so she understood secrets.
She knew she hadn’t earned his complete unreserved trust yet as in a world of political assassinations and bloodline purges, a man who showed all his cards was a man who died in an alley.
She understood the logic and she accepted the secrecy.
Seraphina’s ruby-silver eyes drifted down by three more inches, locking dead center onto Kara’s chest.
’WHY?!’ Seraphina screamed in the privacy of her own soul. ’WHY IN THE SEVEN HELLS DOES HIS FEMALE DISGUISE HAVE BIGGER BREASTS THAN MINE?!’
"Fuuu...
Fuuu...
Fuuu..."

’It looks like she’s about to explode, is something wrong?’ Silas thought inwardly as he blinked, she couldn’t be annoyed just from looking at Kara’s face right. ’I can’t be that beautiful that I’m making her insecure just looking at me right...?’
Seraphina took a slow deliberate breath, letting the roaring pressure coiled within her ribcage settle down by a fraction.
The initial wave of murderous petty outrage gradually subsided, replaced by a cold calm.
She smoothed the charred leather edge of her cuirass, folding her arms over her chest with an icy sharp-edged composure.
’Look at the positives,’ she told herself, clamping down on the frantic urge to rip the star-iron ring in half with her bare hands. ’Just breathe and look at the bloody positives.’
Silas was alive.
Silas was standing fifty paces away under the broad daylight of Sector Forty-Four, completely intact, bearing the banner of Blessed Land without a single broken bone.
He had slipped past the watchful scrying eyes of the World Council and outmaneuvered even her Mother’s web of informants in the city.
It was brilliant and it was infuriating as well.
’Just like Silas is...’

Once again, she understood secrecy since her mother had drilled it into her marrow since she could walk... an exposed weapon invited counter-measures, and a noble who showed all his cards was dead before his first campaign so she didn’t fault the logic.
’That does not mean I will forgive him for this,’ Seraphina thought, her jaw tightening until the enamel ground audibly together.

Her silver eyebrows twitched, her eyes drifting downward again toward Kara’s silhouette with raw pettiness. ’The moment the teleportation seals break and I visit him again, I’m locking him in an iron vault until he explains every single inch of this absurdity...
Starting with why he padded that chest three sizes larger than mine.’
Before her temper could spark a flare of silver flame across the platform, the heavy silence hanging over the Central Ring was shattered by a low grinding sound as basalt cracked and slag hissed.
Fifty paces to the north, Devan Varma rose from his dais.
He moved with the ponderous momentum of a magma shelf shifting beneath continental plates.

’Devan, huh?’ Sera thought, she was not too worried about him... well since Silas was here, the Indus man would naturally go for him instead. ’If I were to face him in this state, it would be a different outcome...’
Sera was sure that the battle could go either way because of the amount of mana she had spent dispatching the Prince.
He did not spare a single downward glance for Ananya Rao, whose limp beaten body lay sprawled in the dust at his heels with her skull swollen and her lotus staff shattered into broken kindling.
CLENCH!
Devan’s knuckles popped like small mortar shells.
WHOOSH!
The runes carved across his collarbones, his broad deltoids, and the thick meat of his forearms flared into an angry vermilion.
’H-huh?’ Aki thought.
The mana radiating off him was not the bright fire Seraphina as well as she commanded...
It was thick magma that felt viscous and heavy with sulfur as well as liquefied iron while carrying the crushing kinetic density of the mantle itself.
His molten gaze locked dead-center onto Kara.
"I have waited for this moment," Devan rumbled, his voice scraping low vibrating straight through the floor into everyone’s boot soles.
"From the hour the rosters were drafted, I knew the others were merely dry chaff waiting for the spark...
Cowards hiding behind bows, nobles prancing with thin rapiers, animals screaming in the dirt.
Only you carried the weight of a true beast."
Kara remained standing on the edge of the western flagstones, her dark suit fluttering lazily against her shins.
Her right hand rested loose at her hip as her left arm hung limp in its dark sling.
"Huh?"
She offered him a half-lidded flat gaze that looked less like an opponent appraising a rival and more like a clerk waiting for a tedious patron to finish counting copper coins.
Devan took a heavy step forward and with every stride, the soles of his boots left smoking black-rimmed rings in the ground.
"Do you know the curse of the apex, woman?" Devan asked.
"Do you know the agonizing hollow boredom of being the peak in an entire country?
In Indus, the elders wept over thresholds and bottlenecks...
They spent decades meditating before ancient steles, praying for a drop of divine marrow but to me... those bottlenecks were nothing more than shallow curbs in the road.
I stepped over them before my twentieth winter and I have never met an equal as no blade has drawn my blood and no spell has forced me to yield half an inch of ground."
’I’m beginning to get tired of these overconfident fuckers.’ Kara thought, at this point, she would rather face another Ren.
Devan extended both hands with his palms facing outward and his thick fingers curling into heavy iron talons.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A massive circular shockwave of pure volcanic domain aura blasted radially outward from his heels.

The temperature on the platform spiked past the boiling point of lead as a suffocating sulfurous fog rolled across the black metal, the fine quartz sand that had settled on the platform melting instantly into a bubbling translucent film of boiling red slag.
Devan sank his center of gravity into an iron-rooted combat stance with his molten eyes burning into Kara’s forehead.
"You have survived the purge," Devan boomed, his aura churning like an active volcano.
"Therefore, I grant you the highest honor a son of Indus can bestow...
I grant you permission to be my rival.
Stand, Kara White, and let us see if your flesh can endure the molten blood of the world!"
BOOM!
Devan launched and the star-iron beneath his rear foot dented inward by three inches as he closed the thirty-pace gap in seconds.
He tore through the sulfur haze, leaving a twin wake of boiling liquefied iron behind his boots with his right arm cocked back like the piston of a hydraulic press.
Seraphina of course took this opportunity to analyze him.

’He’s not just fast,’ Seraphina analyzed instantly, her eyes narrowing as she read the physical displacement. ’He’s using the liquid magma beneath his boots as a propulsion slide to produce low friction and maximum forward inertia.’
That was quite smart actually...
Devan’s right fist drove forward though it was not a simple punch, instead a condensed three-foot battering ram of boiling four-thousand-degree basalt.
FSSSSSSSSSH...
CRASH!
Kara grinned.
"Heh."
She took half a step backward with her left heel, dropping her chin by two inches.
The massive smoking ram of lava screamed past the bridge of her nose with a sickening deafening roar with the blistering hot wind whipping the black hair across her temples.
’Missed?!’ Devan’s mind sparked with immediate violent irritation but he didn’t reset.
"Arrrgh!"
He leaned into the momentum, his left elbow snapping upward in a tight, vicious rising hook, channeling a jagged blade of cooling obsidian along the forearm to take her jaw off.
SWOOSH!
Kara simply tilted her upper torso back by four inches, letting the obsidian edge cleave through the empty airspace above her collarbone.

Devan’s combat instincts took over instantly as he converted the missed hook into a spinning back-fist, pouring a fresh wave of liquid magma into his knuckles to create a blinding cone-shaped spray of molten shrapnel across her entire front.
’Dodge that, rat!’
Kara didn’t dodge the spray.
TAP!
Her boot sole met the star-iron floor.
With an imperceptible twitch of her right shoulder, she stepped straight into the rotation, slipping into his blind spot directly beneath his extended armpit.

The molten spray whistled harmlessly over her right shoulder, scorching the empty air behind her, while her right index and middle fingers snapped out like steel pincers, delivering a sharp double-tap to the nerve cluster right at the hinge of Devan’s floating ribs.
THWACK-THWACK.
"Ghk!" Devan grunted, a sudden jolt of paralysis shooting up his thoracic wall as his breath hitched with his left side going completely numb for half a second.
"Is that all?" Kara asked with her voice completely smooth and drifting into his ear with icy amusement.
"You gave that entire theatrical speech about being a lonely god, and you can’t even land a clean hit on a woman with one arm tied behind her back...?"
SNAP!
The veins along Devan’s neck bulged like thick blue cables.
The sheer humiliation of having his elite sequence dismantled by two finger-taps in front of the surviving nobles detonated every restraint in his mind.
"Arrogant wench!" Devan bellowed!
He abandoned close-quarters martial arts as he ripped both palms upward toward the sky, stomping both boots down with as much force as he could.
"Abyssal Magma Geyser!"
RUMBLE-CRUNCH!
The star-iron ring groaned and beneath the metal platform, the structural supports screamed as six massive towering geysers of bubbling white-hot magma ripped through the floor.
The magma curved inward, forming a forty-foot cage of liquid rock and toxic sulfur designed to incinerate every possible method of escape.
’Let’s see you dance across that!’ Devan snarled internally with his teeth bared in feral triumph however to his surprise, she didn’t try and escape.
TAP!
Her boot touched down on the rising wall of the first geyser.
Seraphina’s eyes widened.
’What is he—?!’
Kara didn’t burn as the second her sole met the surface of the three-thousand-degree liquid rock, she released a paper-thin film of high-frequency vibrational mana beneath her leather.
"You’ll have to do better..."
She didn’t fight the heat as she converted the immense upward force to make her move.
STEP!
STEP!
VAULT!

She skated up the curving face of the erupting lava pillar as if it were a flight of carved marble stairs and with three effortless, fluid strides, she vaulted cleanly over the crest of the magma cage, flipping weightlessly through the sulfurous smoke before dropping back toward the star-iron floor behind him like a falling hawk.
Down below, Seraphina watched the maneuver with her breath caught in her throat.
’That’s my man,’ she thought with a fierce burning pride roaring through her chest.
She had seen high-level movement arts across all the sovereign territories, but nobody moved like Silas.
He didn’t waste a single drop of mana and he didn’t show off...
He just took whatever the enemy threw at him and turned it into his personal footstool.
’Show me,’ Seraphina urged silently, her silver eyes glowing with hungry fascination. ’I want to see what you actually are.’
Devan spun around with his boots skidding through cooling slag and his chest heaving like an industrial bellows.
Sweat poured down his bronze skin, boiling away into steam before it could reach his waist.
His knuckles were trembling... not from physical fatigue, but from the raw vibrating fury that was rapidly poisoning his judgment.
Every single rule of combat he had learned in the royal academy was failing him.
The girl wasn’t matching his output at all, instead, she was treating his arts like bad weather.
"Stand still!" Devan roared, his voice cracking with animalistic frustration.
"Stop running like a gutter-rat!
Stand your ground and cross mana with me!
Or was the mighty reputation of Blessed Land just a collection of cheap parlor tricks and circus acrobatics?!"
Kara landed lightly on the scorched metal twenty paces away with the hem of her dark suit settling softly around her ankles.
She sighed.

chapters.title: Chapter 583: Think Fast
paragraphs: It was a slow exhausted sound that echoed across the dead quiet of the platform as she rolled her uninjured right shoulder with her gaze lifting slowly to meet Devan’s wild bloodshot eyes.

"You really love the sound of your own voice, don’t you?" Kara said, her voice lacking any sort of mockery as it stripped down to cold crushing boredom. "All that noise about the agony of the apex... the heavy burden of being unmatched... the tragic loneliness of high potential..."
She shook her head once with her eyes narrowing into cold slits.
’God, I hate this guy.’

"You aren’t lonely because you’re strong, Devan," Kara said quietly, each word cutting through the sulfur haze like a razor. "You’re lonely because you’re a loudmouthed mediocre frog sitting at the bottom of a very small puddle, convinced the mud you’re choking on is the entire world..."
Devan’s jaw dropped.
The insult was so blunt and so lacking of any sort of courtly subtlety, that his brain stalled for an entire heartbeat.
Then, the blood rushed to his eyes.
"I WILL TEAR YOU TO PIECES!" Devan screamed, throwing his entire weight forward in a blind hysterical charge.
WHOOSH!
He gathered every remaining drop of volcanic mana in his core, channeling it straight down his right arm to form a massive screaming drill of molten basalt.
’So getting your opponents riled up like this before a fight helps this much?’ Kara thought, perhaps next time, she would try it against another unfortunate fellow.
’For now...’
WHOOOSH!

The atmosphere across the entire Central Ring instantly ceased to exist as up in the air, Aki who had been hovering on a thin delicate gust of emerald wind gasped with her eyes dilating in instinctual terror as her wind-cushion vanished beneath her boots.
’What... what spell is he about to—?!’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A catastrophic detonation of pure compressed air displacement exploded from Kara’s single forward step.
The attack was not a blade made of wind nor was it an air cutter, If Sera had to put it into words... It was like an invisible train.

The concussive overpressure ripped through the thirty paces of star-iron plate, gouging a massive six-foot-deep trench straight through the solid metal, tearing the structural supports beneath the ring to ribbons.
"Aughhhhh!"
Devan’s charge was violently erased by this train.
WHAM!
The concussive mass of the vacuum hammer struck Devan dead center in the chest!
CRACK-CRUNCH-SHATTER!

The volcanic runes etched into his bronze flesh were pulverized out of existence as his sternum, clavicles, and thoracic cage caved inward by four agonizing inches with a wet sickening crunch that echoed across the entire basin.
"Ungggghhhhh—!"
He couldn’t even let out a proper sound as the breath in his lungs blew out of his throat in an instantaneous red fog.
BOOM!
The directional power of the vacuum strike was angled forty-five degrees downward and Devan Varma was driven vertically into the solid star-iron floor like a common iron nail under a hydraulic forge.
WHOOOOOSH! BANNNGGG!
The metal ring buckled with a thirty-foot crater detonating around his mangled form as he was hammered flat into the floor as his limbs twitched once before going completely limp!
His eyes rolled back until only the blood-shot sclera showed with his mouth hanging slack and his core collapsing into protective shutdown.
The vacuum pulled the trailing dust cloud through the crater, leaving the platform suffocatingly quiet while in the center of the warped, dented trench, Devan lay motionless and completely out of it.
PING!

The extraction runes pinned to Devan’s sash and the unconscious Ananya Rao flared simultaneously with luminescence as their bodies dissolved into millions of shimmering ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple sky to be reclaimed by the World Council’s recovery barges.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating relays suspended above the arena, the voice chimed across the ruins of Sector Forty-Four.
"Notice of Elimination."
"The representatives of the Indus Sovereignty have been defeated and so the Indus Sovereignty is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Silence settled over the black platform.
Kara stood at the edge of the crater, casually dusting a speck of gray soot from her uninjured sleeve with her breathing calm and completely undisturbed.
"Boring," she muttered, rolling her shoulder as she turned her back on the pit.
The lingering ozone of vaporized basalt still hung heavy in the air, but the blinding vermilion light of Devan Varma’s volcanic power was gone.
Only a scattered constellation of dying white extraction particles drifted toward the purple troposphere, dissolving into nothingness alongside the broken form of Ananya Rao.
Isolde stood completely petrified on the scorched rim of the eastern flagstones.
DRIP!
A bead of cold sweat rolled down her neck, slipping beneath the high star-iron collar of her dueling tunic.
Her slender fingers, usually so steady and effortless with her matched parrying daggers, twitched violently against the polished wire-wrapped hilts.
She didn’t look at her cousin Leona, nor did she look toward the sky where the World Council’s surveillance eyes spun in their orbits.
Her gaze was utterly pinned to Kara White.

’One single blow,’ Isolde thought, her throat constricting until every breath felt like swallowing dry sand. ’She didn’t even draw a blade and she didn’t use an incantation either... She crushed the apex of the southern line like an insect beneath an anvil.’
In the refined courts of Albion, they taught you that true supremacy was an art of lineage and measured resource management.
You measured an enemy’s core reserves, you calculated the angle of their guard, and you whittled them down with peerless parrying combinations until an opening presented itself...
Yet looking at Kara standing over that smoking six-foot-deep trench, dusting off her lapel with complete dismissive boredom, Isolde felt an alien terrifying emotion blossom behind her ribs.
It was reverence.

’That isn’t just martial mastery...’ Isolde mused, her heart thumping against her ribs in a chaotic rhythm. ’That is true authority, If Albion possessed an anchor like her... if someone could stand in the High Council and project that kind of undeniable immovable gravity...’

She found herself staring at the effortless tilt of Kara’s shoulders, the casual arrogance of her stance, unconsciously seeing in the mysterious Lord of Blessed Land the ultimate paradigm of what a sovereign warrior ought to be.
A genuine role model and a standard to strive toward.
"Think fast!"
WHOOSH!
The sharp abrasive rasp of Leona’s voice shattered the reverie like a rock hurled through a glass window.
"Ugh... Not you again..."
Isolde’s eyes dilated.
Her dueling instincts fired on raw reflex, however before her heels could even complete their half-pivot across the basalt dust, a shadow completely blocked out the desert sun.
Leona was already inside her perimeter.
SWOOSH-BANG!

Leona didn’t bother with fancy footwork as she came in low with her heavy trench-machete held behind her like a trailing counterweight and her right boot snapping outward in a vicious horizontal roundhouse kick aimed straight for Isolde’s floating ribs.
CRACK!
The steel toe of Leona’s combat boot connected with Isolde’s defensive parrying dagger, but the concussive transfer of force was immense.
BANG!
Isolde was knocked violently sideways with her boots sliding three paces across the black star-iron floor and her teeth rattling inside her skull.
"Damn gutter rat!" Isolde snarled, spitting blood from her split lip as she immediately dropped her center of gravity; however she didn’t retreat. "I’ll teach you a big lesson!"
Using the sideways momentum of the impact, Isolde spun on the ball of her right foot with her left arm whipping forward in a blinding low-angle thrust with her secondary stiletto.
The silver-plated blade hummed with a needle-thin conduit of pale wind-mana, aimed directly to pierce through the joint of Leona’s right shoulder.
It was a textbook riposte that was clean and perfect... This woman wouldn’t be able to block i—
SLIP!
Leona didn’t try to block it.
The moment the stiletto lunged forward, Leona’s upper body seemed to lose all its skeletal rigidity.
She flowed like heavy sea-water slipping around a breakwater with her head and torso dipping beneath the incoming steel by less than half an inch.
The blade pierced through empty air with the razor-thin wind-mana barely grazing the coarse fabric of her sleeve.
In that single second of overextension, Isolde’s eyes snapped down to Leona’s feet.
Leona’s front heel had dug into the metal plate with her knees bent inward at an acute angle and both of her hands dropping down near her hips in an open-palm coiled posture.
A cold icy terror gripped Isolde’s chest.
She recognized that stance... It was something that Isolde herself had used against Leona before, when they were still twelve during their first spar.
’This bitch wouldn’t dare—’ Isolde screamed internally.
WHAM!
"Too slow, high-and-mighty!" Leona yelled as her left leg snapped upward like an uncoiling iron spring!
It wasn’t a standard kick at all, instead it was an executioner’s heel-axe.
Her heavy reinforced boot slammed straight down onto the crown of Isolde’s head with the concussive violence of a falling boulder.
CRUNCH-BOOM!
The impact drove Isolde’s skull violently downward into the star-iron platform.

The polished metal rang like a church bell as Isolde’s forehead slammed into the floor with the shockwave making her skull bounce upward like a rubber ball with a fountain of scarlet spraying from her broken nose and split forehead.
Her parrying daggers slipped from her limp fingers, clattering uselessly across the stone.
Before Isolde’s airborne head could even reach the apex of the rebound, Leona was already rotating her entire torso into a vicious piston-driven right hook.
"This is good revenge, bitch!"
WHOO KER-BLAM!

She poured every remaining shred of her emerald wind-mana straight into the impact and the punch caught Isolde dead-center in the temple, blowing a concussive shockwave of pulverized air and blood across the arena.

Isolde was launched horizontally through the air like an artillery shell, soaring thirty yards across the Central Ring before skidding face-down into the crushed quartz dust with her consciousness snuffed out instantly.
PING!
The moment Isolde’s body stopped moving, her transponder flared into an incandescent burst of white light!
Down below, the broken battered form of Gareth Pendelton, who had been lying motionless in the dirt since Maya’s Fourth Rotation dismantled his chest flared simultaneously.
BZZZZZZZZT!
Both of their physical bodies dissolved into millions of dancing, ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple sky as the spatial extraction protocol reclaimed them.
"Notice of Elimination," the cold metallic voice of the World Council boomed from the floating optical relays overhead.
"The representatives of the Albion Concordat have suffered catastrophic incapacitation and collapse. The Albion Concordat is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
"Haah... Haah... Haah..."
Leona stood with her legs planted wide with her trench-machete held loosely in her left hand and her knuckles slick with her cousin’s blood.
She wiped her brow with the back of her forearm, smearing soot and sweat across her tanned forehead with her breath tearing from her lungs in ragged heaves.
SNAP!

Her instincts flared as she spun on her heel, her right hand reaching down to draw a curved, eight-inch trench-dagger from her utility belt, bringing both blades up in an immediate lethal cross-guard toward the western ridge.
Standing twenty paces away, watching her calmly, was Valerius Sterling.
The young heir of the Sterling line looked like he had stepped straight out of an imperial gala rather than a continental death match.

His golden armor gleamed under the harsh sunlight without a single dent, scratch, or speck of ash tarnishing its pristine lacquer and beside him, Rook Sterling was casually leaning against a basalt pillar, chewing on a dried ration strip with his eyes flicking between the optical relays and the horizon without the slightest trace of tension.
Valerius’s pale eyes slowly shifted, locking directly onto Leona’s dagger.
WHOOOSH!
For half a second, a soft emerald-green radiance flickered behind Valerius’s irises as the atmospheric pressure around the platform dropped instantly by three full bars.

The loose sand near Leona’s boots stopped falling, caught in a series of micro-pressurized air currents that began slicing microscopic grooves into the star-iron floor with whistling vibrations as a sharp dread seized Leona’s gut.

’This man...’ Leona realized, her jaw clenching so hard her molars ached. ’His wind affinity... it’s insane. It’s on an entirely different level compared to mine. Hell, it feels denser than even the Princess’s attacks.’
She could read the control written in the air around him.
If Valerius chose to unleash that purple-core wind reserves right now, she was entirely at his mercy.
Her battered ribs were cracked, her mana channels were weeping from the brutal exchange with Isolde, and her stamina was running on absolute fumes.
If they clashed, he would slice her down in three seconds flat, and the Sovereign Territory of Amazonia would be wiped clean off the leaderboard.
