The metal ring buckled with a thirty-foot crater detonating around his mangled form as he was hammered flat into the floor as his limbs twitched once before going completely limp!
His eyes rolled back until only the blood-shot sclera showed with his mouth hanging slack and his core collapsing into protective shutdown.
The vacuum pulled the trailing dust cloud through the crater, leaving the platform suffocatingly quiet while in the center of the warped, dented trench, Devan lay motionless and completely out of it.
PING!

The extraction runes pinned to Devan’s sash and the unconscious Ananya Rao flared simultaneously with luminescence as their bodies dissolved into millions of shimmering ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple sky to be reclaimed by the World Council’s recovery barges.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating relays suspended above the arena, the voice chimed across the ruins of Sector Forty-Four.
"Notice of Elimination."
"The representatives of the Indus Sovereignty have been defeated and so the Indus Sovereignty is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
Silence settled over the black platform.
Kara stood at the edge of the crater, casually dusting a speck of gray soot from her uninjured sleeve with her breathing calm and completely undisturbed.
"Boring," she muttered, rolling her shoulder as she turned her back on the pit.
The lingering ozone of vaporized basalt still hung heavy in the air, but the blinding vermilion light of Devan Varma’s volcanic power was gone.
Only a scattered constellation of dying white extraction particles drifted toward the purple troposphere, dissolving into nothingness alongside the broken form of Ananya Rao.
Isolde stood completely petrified on the scorched rim of the eastern flagstones.
DRIP!
A bead of cold sweat rolled down her neck, slipping beneath the high star-iron collar of her dueling tunic.
Her slender fingers, usually so steady and effortless with her matched parrying daggers, twitched violently against the polished wire-wrapped hilts.
She didn’t look at her cousin Leona, nor did she look toward the sky where the World Council’s surveillance eyes spun in their orbits.
Her gaze was utterly pinned to Kara White.
’One single blow,’ Isolde thought, her throat constricting until every breath felt like swallowing dry sand. ’She didn’t even draw a blade and she didn’t use an incantation either...
She crushed the apex of the southern line like an insect beneath an anvil.’
In the refined courts of Albion, they taught you that true supremacy was an art of lineage and measured resource management.
You measured an enemy’s core reserves, you calculated the angle of their guard, and you whittled them down with peerless parrying combinations until an opening presented itself...
Yet looking at Kara standing over that smoking six-foot-deep trench, dusting off her lapel with complete dismissive boredom, Isolde felt an alien terrifying emotion blossom behind her ribs.
It was reverence.

’That isn’t just martial mastery...’ Isolde mused, her heart thumping against her ribs in a chaotic rhythm. ’That is true authority, If Albion possessed an anchor like her... if someone could stand in the High Council and project that kind of undeniable immovable gravity...’

She found herself staring at the effortless tilt of Kara’s shoulders, the casual arrogance of her stance, unconsciously seeing in the mysterious Lord of Blessed Land the ultimate paradigm of what a sovereign warrior ought to be.
A genuine role model and a standard to strive toward.
"Think fast!"
WHOOSH!
The sharp abrasive rasp of Leona’s voice shattered the reverie like a rock hurled through a glass window.
"Ugh...
Not you again..."
Isolde’s eyes dilated.
Her dueling instincts fired on raw reflex, however before her heels could even complete their half-pivot across the basalt dust, a shadow completely blocked out the desert sun.
Leona was already inside her perimeter.
SWOOSH-BANG!

Leona didn’t bother with fancy footwork as she came in low with her heavy trench-machete held behind her like a trailing counterweight and her right boot snapping outward in a vicious horizontal roundhouse kick aimed straight for Isolde’s floating ribs.
CRACK!
The steel toe of Leona’s combat boot connected with Isolde’s defensive parrying dagger, but the concussive transfer of force was immense.
BANG!
Isolde was knocked violently sideways with her boots sliding three paces across the black star-iron floor and her teeth rattling inside her skull.
"Damn gutter rat!" Isolde snarled, spitting blood from her split lip as she immediately dropped her center of gravity; however she didn’t retreat.
"I’ll teach you a big lesson!"
Using the sideways momentum of the impact, Isolde spun on the ball of her right foot with her left arm whipping forward in a blinding low-angle thrust with her secondary stiletto.
The silver-plated blade hummed with a needle-thin conduit of pale wind-mana, aimed directly to pierce through the joint of Leona’s right shoulder.
It was a textbook riposte that was clean and perfect...
This woman wouldn’t be able to block i—
SLIP!
Leona didn’t try to block it.
The moment the stiletto lunged forward, Leona’s upper body seemed to lose all its skeletal rigidity.
She flowed like heavy sea-water slipping around a breakwater with her head and torso dipping beneath the incoming steel by less than half an inch.
The blade pierced through empty air with the razor-thin wind-mana barely grazing the coarse fabric of her sleeve.
In that single second of overextension, Isolde’s eyes snapped down to Leona’s feet.
Leona’s front heel had dug into the metal plate with her knees bent inward at an acute angle and both of her hands dropping down near her hips in an open-palm coiled posture.
A cold icy terror gripped Isolde’s chest.
She recognized that stance...
It was something that Isolde herself had used against Leona before, when they were still twelve during their first spar.
’This bitch wouldn’t dare—’ Isolde screamed internally.
WHAM!
"Too slow, high-and-mighty!" Leona yelled as her left leg snapped upward like an uncoiling iron spring!
It wasn’t a standard kick at all, instead it was an executioner’s heel-axe.
Her heavy reinforced boot slammed straight down onto the crown of Isolde’s head with the concussive violence of a falling boulder.
CRUNCH-BOOM!
The impact drove Isolde’s skull violently downward into the star-iron platform.

The polished metal rang like a church bell as Isolde’s forehead slammed into the floor with the shockwave making her skull bounce upward like a rubber ball with a fountain of scarlet spraying from her broken nose and split forehead.
Her parrying daggers slipped from her limp fingers, clattering uselessly across the stone.
Before Isolde’s airborne head could even reach the apex of the rebound, Leona was already rotating her entire torso into a vicious piston-driven right hook.
"This is good revenge, bitch!"
WHOO KER-BLAM!

She poured every remaining shred of her emerald wind-mana straight into the impact and the punch caught Isolde dead-center in the temple, blowing a concussive shockwave of pulverized air and blood across the arena.

Isolde was launched horizontally through the air like an artillery shell, soaring thirty yards across the Central Ring before skidding face-down into the crushed quartz dust with her consciousness snuffed out instantly.
PING!
The moment Isolde’s body stopped moving, her transponder flared into an incandescent burst of white light!
Down below, the broken battered form of Gareth Pendelton, who had been lying motionless in the dirt since Maya’s Fourth Rotation dismantled his chest flared simultaneously.
BZZZZZZZZT!
Both of their physical bodies dissolved into millions of dancing, ethereal white particles, shooting vertically into the purple sky as the spatial extraction protocol reclaimed them.
"Notice of Elimination," the cold metallic voice of the World Council boomed from the floating optical relays overhead.
"The representatives of the Albion Concordat have suffered catastrophic incapacitation and collapse.
The Albion Concordat is officially eliminated from the tournament bracket."
"Haah...
Haah...
Haah..."
Leona stood with her legs planted wide with her trench-machete held loosely in her left hand and her knuckles slick with her cousin’s blood.
She wiped her brow with the back of her forearm, smearing soot and sweat across her tanned forehead with her breath tearing from her lungs in ragged heaves.
SNAP!

Her instincts flared as she spun on her heel, her right hand reaching down to draw a curved, eight-inch trench-dagger from her utility belt, bringing both blades up in an immediate lethal cross-guard toward the western ridge.
Standing twenty paces away, watching her calmly, was Valerius Sterling.
The young heir of the Sterling line looked like he had stepped straight out of an imperial gala rather than a continental death match.

His golden armor gleamed under the harsh sunlight without a single dent, scratch, or speck of ash tarnishing its pristine lacquer and beside him, Rook Sterling was casually leaning against a basalt pillar, chewing on a dried ration strip with his eyes flicking between the optical relays and the horizon without the slightest trace of tension.
Valerius’s pale eyes slowly shifted, locking directly onto Leona’s dagger.
WHOOOSH!
For half a second, a soft emerald-green radiance flickered behind Valerius’s irises as the atmospheric pressure around the platform dropped instantly by three full bars.

The loose sand near Leona’s boots stopped falling, caught in a series of micro-pressurized air currents that began slicing microscopic grooves into the star-iron floor with whistling vibrations as a sharp dread seized Leona’s gut.
’This man...’ Leona realized, her jaw clenching so hard her molars ached. ’His wind affinity... it’s insane.
It’s on an entirely different level compared to mine.
Hell, it feels denser than even the Princess’s attacks.’
She could read the control written in the air around him.
If Valerius chose to unleash that purple-core wind reserves right now, she was entirely at his mercy.
Her battered ribs were cracked, her mana channels were weeping from the brutal exchange with Isolde, and her stamina was running on absolute fumes.
If they clashed, he would slice her down in three seconds flat, and the Sovereign Territory of Amazonia would be wiped clean off the leaderboard.

chapters.title: Chapter 584: Seraphina’s Last Stand
paragraphs: ’Not that it truly matters for the grand alliance,’ Leona thought with her fingers white-knuckled around her dagger. ’We made a mutual non-aggression pact with Aki before the drop so our standing is already secure but damn it all, I am not rolling over like a kicked dog without leaving a scratch on that pretty golden chestplate—’
She lowered her center of gravity, preparing to throw her life into a desperate, all-or-nothing blitz...
"We yield."
The words were spoken so casually that Leona’s boots slipped on the metal.
Valerius didn’t draw a sword as he casually raised both hands in the air, his slender palms open toward the sky, offering an easy polite smile that belonged in a drawing room rather than a war zone.
Beside him, Rook let out a low grunt and raised both of his hands as well.
WHOOOSH!
The spatial extraction arrays pinned to their armor flared with brilliant white luminescence.
Before Leona could even take a single forward step, the spatial spell swallowed them whole with their forms dissolving into shimmering pillars of light that rocketed into the upper stratosphere.
Leona stood completely frozen, her dagger still pointed at the empty flagstones.
"Huh?"
She blinked once and then she blinked twice.

"Huh?!" she yelled, lowering her blades in pure, unadulterated exasperation. "Are you kidding me?! He had all that power humming behind his teeth, and he just... threw his hands up and walked away?! What kind of high-born bastard just gives up without swinging his sword?! What a monumental waste of good mana!"
"You look like you just got dragged through a rock crusher, Leona."
The dry voice drifted from her flank as Leona turned her head to see Kara sauntering over from the edge of the crater.

Her dark coat was draped casually over her shoulders with her single working hand resting loosely in the pocket of her tailored trousers and her face wearing that same infuriating unbothered smirk that looked like she was on an evening stroll through a garden.
"Haaah..."
Leona let out a long shuddering breath, sliding her trench-machete back into the leather sheath at her hip with a dull clack.

"Look who’s talking," Leona grunted, leaning heavily against her left knee and wincing as her cracked ribs protested. "You’re walking around like you didn’t just turn an Indus titan into a pancake. Though... damn it, Miss Kara. What about Maya?"
Leona’s face darkened genuine panic flashing in her hazel eyes.

"Her core power vanished right at the end of the skirmish... Gareth had a full metal-arsenal deployed, and Maya was using that insane technique, I think she took catastrophic internal bleeding, Kara. Did she—"
Kara casually waved her right hand dismissively, rolling her uninjured shoulder.

"Calm your nerves," Kara said smoothly. "Before the World Council initiated the territory compression stuff and dragged us all up to this ring, I dropped into the lower gully and stabilized her meridians, spliced the torn channels, flushed the internal pooling out of her lungs, and made sure her body could circulate mana... Whatever spell she was doing, she took enough recoil to kill a war rhino, but her body is built like a granite wall so she’s completely out of danger."
Up in the air above them, a soft emerald-tinted breeze began to spiral downward.
Aki gently lowered herself from the sky with her boots touching down onto the star-iron floor without making a sound.
Her composite bow was slung across her back and her slender hands resting against her thighs while her azure hair dusted with fine quartz silt.
"Phewwwww~"
A massive trembling sigh of pure relief escaped Aki’s chest.
Her smaller shoulders sagged with her fingers unclamping from her weapon strap as she pressed a trembling gloved palm over her racing heart.

’Thank goodness...’ Aki thought, her azure eyes welling with emotional warmth. ’Maya is safe. If she had died because I was too clumsy to handle the Australis skirmish quickly, I never would have forgiven myself...’
"Now then," Kara murmured, her tone shifting slightly as she turned her head toward the eastern perimeter. "There’s only one matter left to settle."
Leona and Aki turned their eyes toward the edge of the platform as the heat was still radiating from the blackened stone, but it was thinning rapidly.
Standing alone amidst the scorched flagstones was Seraphina Bloom.
Her long celestial waves of silver-white hair were rapidly losing their brilliant luster, flickering violently between pure divine silver and her native fiery crimson.
Her breathing came in shallow, agonizing hitches, her scorched leather cuirass stained with streaks of black soot and drying red.
Her delicate porcelain face was pale as chalk, save for the dark bruising circles under her eyes.

The Primordial Spirit fusion was reaching its limit as the overwhelming divine fire was no longer radiating outward... it was eating her internal stamina from within, turning her channels into brittle carbonized thread.
WHOOSH!
Kara drifted forward, hovering a few inches above the floor, closing the distance until she stood barely ten paces from the trembling noblewoman.
Kara tilted her head with her dark eyes locking onto Seraphina’s flickering gaze.
"So," Kara asked, her voice carrying a quiet ease, "you’re the one who dismantled Crown Prince Alexander, huh?"
Seraphina’s chin snapped upward.
Even with her legs shaking so violently that her knees clicked beneath her dueling leathers, her pride refused to yield an inch.
She planted her boots into the cracked star-iron, forcing her scorched weapon up into a stance.

"So what if I am?" Seraphina challenged with her voice hoarse and the ethereal dual-toned spirit echo peeling away to reveal her raw strained human vocal cords. "Are you going to step across this line, Kara White?"
Kara looked at the trembling point of the rapier, then raised an eyebrow.

"Are you sure about that?" Kara asked. "Your mana channels are running on dry fumes. In about five seconds, the spiritual backlash is going to collapse your nervous system, and you won’t even have the strength to hold that piece of metal."
Seraphina clamped her jaw shut, biting her lower lip until the metallic taste of blood flooded her tongue.
’I know that!’ Seraphina raged internally, her vision swimming in sickening rings of yellow and gray. ’I know I have barely three heartbeats left before my core locks up!’
Under any rational assessment, yielding right here was the obvious choice.
House Bloom had already secured an astronomical political triumph by bringing down the Crown’s prince so there was no dishonor in bowing out after reaching the final circle.
’Except it isn’t just an opponent standing in front of me,’ Seraphina thought, her crimson-silver eyes blazing with fierce desperate determination. ’It’s Silas.’

How could she ever demand his respect... How could she ever stand beside him as an equal partner, or look him in the eye when she confronted him about this female disguise if she dropped her sword the moment she felt pain?
She was Seraphina Bloom.
She was the heir to the Primordial Flame and she needed him to see her as an unbreakable woman of iron.
"House Bloom..." Seraphina choked out, forcing her spine straight, "...never surrenders!"
WHOOSH!
With a final desperate burst of spiritual willpower, Seraphina flared her core.
A thin fragile tongue of silver-white fire ignited along the blade of her rapier as she lunged forward.
STEP... STUMBLE.
Her acceleration failed instantly with her right boot dragged heavily through the basalt grit and her momentum dying before she could even clear five paces.
Mid-stride, the celestial silver in her hair snapped off with the violent finality of an extinguished candle.
Her locks collapsed into pure crimson, and the primordial spirit link shattered as the sudden severance tore through her nervous system like a thousand white-hot needles.
"Gah–!"
A thick spray of crimson burst from Seraphina’s lips with her weapon clattering loudly across the metal floor as her knees gave out completely.
SWOOSH!
In a single fluid blink of acceleration, Kara closed the gap.
Her right arm reached out, catching Seraphina firmly around her slender waist before her face could hit the stone.
Seraphina froze, hanging limply against Kara’s right hip with her head resting against Kara’s shoulder.
Up close, the burning sulfur of the battlefield vanished, replaced by the unmistakably clean scent of her perfume.

’You really pushed yourself right to the edge, didn’t you?’ Silas thought silently behind Kara’s impassive eyes, looking down at the girl’s blood-spattered exhausted face with an imperceptible softening in his gaze.
Seraphina blinked up at her.
The overwhelming physical proximity, the lingering realization of his identity, and the absurdity of being held in this bridal-like grip by his female disguise hit her all at once.
A violent burning flush exploded across Seraphina’s cheeks, turning her entire face completely, unmistakably scarlet.
"Y-You..." Seraphina croaked, mortified to the core of her being.
PING!
Her tournament transponder engaged its emergency sequence as Seraphina’s body dissolved into millions of warm, dancing white particles.
A hundred yards to the north, in the shadowed ruins of the battle between Tyon and the Europa representative, Tyon’s unconscious body dissolved into light simultaneously.
With one final glaring look that held equal measures of embarrassment, fury, and secret affection, Seraphina vanished into the wind.
Kara casually lowered her arm, waving her hand through the dissipating particles.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating optical relays suspended thousands of feet above the ring, the grand administrative trumpet blared across the entire expanse of Sector Forty-Four.
"FINAL TOURNAMENT RESOLUTION."
"All hostile factions have been eliminated from the active theater."
"The surviving combatants on the field represent the coalition of the First Princess’s Group and the Sovereign Territory of Amazonia, operating under a formal treaty of mutual alliance."
"By decree of the World Council... the Continental Sovereign Tournament of Sector Forty-Four has officially concluded!"
"THE VICTORS ARE THE COALITION OF THE FIRST PRINCESS AND AMAZONIA!"
Silence settled over the platform for two seconds then, Leona let out a strange choked wheeze from the back of her throat.
Her hazel eyes went wide, looking down at her battered boots with a deep flustered pink creeping onto her bruised cheeks as reality slammed into her skull.
’W-we did it...’
Aki stood frozen beside her with her small mouth opened and closed in pure shock.
’I... uh...’ Aki’s thoughts stumbled over each other. ’We won? We actually won the entire thing?! Against the Directorate? Against Albion? Against... against everyone?!’
Kara floated over, touching down lightly three paces away, folding her single working arm across her chest with an amused smirk.
"Well?" Kara chuckled, raising an eyebrow. "What’s with the dumb expression, Princess? You just took the tournament so celebrate a little."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright delicate crimson.

"H-How am I supposed to celebrate?!" Aki stammered, flustered down to her fingernails. "In the royal palace, there are formal procedures! You recite the ancestral victory ode, you offer thanks to the World King, you bow at forty-five degrees—"
"Protocols are for dead politicians," Kara teased with her smirk widening. "You know how to celebrate. Stop thinking and just do it."
Aki’s face turned completely red.
Her cheeks puffed out into an adorable rounded pout as she looked at Leona, who was holding her sides and laughing through her bruises, and then looked down at the gloves humming softly on her hands.
The relief, the joy, the wild thrill of survival finally shattered her sheltered royal decorum.
WHOOSH!
A sudden sharp pop of emerald wind-mana detonated beneath the soles of Aki’s boots.
She launched herself three feet into the air, throwing both of her fists toward the purple heavens with every shred of breath left in her chest.
"YEAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHH!" Aki screamed at the top of her lungs, her joyous triumphant shout ringing across the silent shattered ruins of the world.
BEEP... BEEP... BEEP.
The rhythmic chime of a diagnostic terminal hummed softly in the quiet room.
"Haah!"
Maya Da Silva’s eyes flew wide open as her torso violently jerked upward.
"Agh—damn it!"
A sharp tearing agony flashed through her thoracic wall, forcing a harsh hiss through her clamped teeth as she fell back against the stiff starch-scented pillows of the recovery bed.
"I would strongly advise against sudden exertion," a calm voice sounded from the corner.
Maya’s head snapped to the right, her amber eyes instantly narrowing into sharp slits despite the blinding headache throbbing behind her temples.
Sitting on a simple wooden chair beside the medical cart was Valerius Sterling.
The blond man was still wearing his pristine golden armor, though he had removed his heavy gauntlets, resting his pale hands casually across his knees.
He looked immaculate, unaffected by the dirt or blood of the wasteland, watching her with a calm curiosity.
Maya looked around the room, taking in the sterile white walls, the rows of empty medical cots, and the glowing runic vitals monitor mounted above her head.

"You’re in the eastern recovery pavilion," Valerius stated, his voice quiet, devoid of the usual aristocratic arrogance. "The tournament concluded roughly forty-five minutes ago and your coalition claimed the victory."
Maya shifted her weight slightly to the right, testing the tension in her ribs.

With one final glaring look that held equal measures of embarrassment, fury, and secret affection, Seraphina vanished into the wind.
Kara casually lowered her arm, waving her hand through the dissipating particles.
BZZZZZZZZT!
From the floating optical relays suspended thousands of feet above the ring, the grand administrative trumpet blared across the entire expanse of Sector Forty-Four.
"FINAL TOURNAMENT RESOLUTION."
"All hostile factions have been eliminated from the active theater."
"The surviving combatants on the field represent the coalition of the First Princess’s Group and the Sovereign Territory of Amazonia, operating under a formal treaty of mutual alliance."
"By decree of the World Council... the Continental Sovereign Tournament of Sector Forty-Four has officially concluded!"
"THE VICTORS ARE THE COALITION OF THE FIRST PRINCESS AND AMAZONIA!"
Silence settled over the platform for two seconds then, Leona let out a strange choked wheeze from the back of her throat.
Her hazel eyes went wide, looking down at her battered boots with a deep flustered pink creeping onto her bruised cheeks as reality slammed into her skull.
’W-we did it...’
Aki stood frozen beside her with her small mouth opened and closed in pure shock.
’I... uh...’ Aki’s thoughts stumbled over each other. ’We won?
We actually won the entire thing?!
Against the Directorate?
Against Albion?
Against... against everyone?!’
Kara floated over, touching down lightly three paces away, folding her single working arm across her chest with an amused smirk.
"Well?" Kara chuckled, raising an eyebrow.
"What’s with the dumb expression, Princess?
You just took the tournament so celebrate a little."
Aki’s cheeks flushed a bright delicate crimson.
"H-How am I supposed to celebrate?!" Aki stammered, flustered down to her fingernails.
"In the royal palace, there are formal procedures!
You recite the ancestral victory ode, you offer thanks to the World King, you bow at forty-five degrees—"
"Protocols are for dead politicians," Kara teased with her smirk widening.
"You know how to celebrate.
Stop thinking and just do it."
Aki’s face turned completely red.
Her cheeks puffed out into an adorable rounded pout as she looked at Leona, who was holding her sides and laughing through her bruises, and then looked down at the gloves humming softly on her hands.
The relief, the joy, the wild thrill of survival finally shattered her sheltered royal decorum.
WHOOSH!
A sudden sharp pop of emerald wind-mana detonated beneath the soles of Aki’s boots.
She launched herself three feet into the air, throwing both of her fists toward the purple heavens with every shred of breath left in her chest.
"YEAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHHHH!" Aki screamed at the top of her lungs, her joyous triumphant shout ringing across the silent shattered ruins of the world.
BEEP...
BEEP...
BEEP.
The rhythmic chime of a diagnostic terminal hummed softly in the quiet room.
"Haah!"
Maya Da Silva’s eyes flew wide open as her torso violently jerked upward.
"Agh—damn it!"
A sharp tearing agony flashed through her thoracic wall, forcing a harsh hiss through her clamped teeth as she fell back against the stiff starch-scented pillows of the recovery bed.
"I would strongly advise against sudden exertion," a calm voice sounded from the corner.
Maya’s head snapped to the right, her amber eyes instantly narrowing into sharp slits despite the blinding headache throbbing behind her temples.
Sitting on a simple wooden chair beside the medical cart was Valerius Sterling.
The blond man was still wearing his pristine golden armor, though he had removed his heavy gauntlets, resting his pale hands casually across his knees.
He looked immaculate, unaffected by the dirt or blood of the wasteland, watching her with a calm curiosity.
Maya looked around the room, taking in the sterile white walls, the rows of empty medical cots, and the glowing runic vitals monitor mounted above her head.
"You’re in the eastern recovery pavilion," Valerius stated, his voice quiet, devoid of the usual aristocratic arrogance.
"The tournament concluded roughly forty-five minutes ago and your coalition claimed the victory."
Maya shifted her weight slightly to the right, testing the tension in her ribs.

chapters.title: Chapter 585: The Holy Grail Of A New Age
paragraphs: Her torso was wrapped in tight medical-grade compression linen that carried the sharp tang of restorative spirit-salve.
The massive gash Gareth’s broadsword had carved into her side was completely sealed, held together by a translucent alchemical membrane.
Even so, every single muscle fiber in her body felt like it had been shredded and re-stitched with star-iron wire.
She turned her head and glared at Valerius with a look that practically screamed... What the hell do you even want?
"If you’re here to gloat about missing the final fight, gold-boy," Maya rasped with her throat rough as dry bark, "give me five minutes to catch my breath and I’ll break that pretty jaw of yours."
Valerius offered a remarkably polite smile, shaking his head.

"That won’t be necessary," Valerius replied smoothly. "While Kara stabilized your internal channels before the extraction was engaged, your body remains severely compromised. Given the sheer load you forced through your marrow... it will take at least three days of total core inactivity before your channels regain standard elasticity."
Maya didn’t answer as she kept her amber eyes locked on his face with her guard fully raised.
Valerius shifted on his chair, his gaze dropping to his hands for a fraction of a second as a subtle flicker of hesitation crossed his features.
"I remained here," Valerius said slowly, "because I was... profoundly fascinated by the sequence you displayed in the lower canyon."
Maya’s eyes narrowed into alarmed dangerous slits.
’Fascinated?’

"The technique you utilized," Valerius continued, his analytical cadence picking up speed like a scholar dissecting a rare manuscript. "You call it [Earthborn], correct? You’ve been muttering it for a while in your sleep... that aside... You didn’t merely circulate earth-mana through your body as a way to strengthen yourself, instead you altered the harmonic frequency of your Second Stage core to synchronize directly with the movement of the ground."
Maya’s jaw locked rigid with a cold prickly sensation crept down her spine.
’How does he know that?’ she thought, her pulse spiking. ’Nobody outside my sister has ever seen the circulation pattern!’

"By anchoring yourself to the tectonic bedrock," Valerius murmured, his eyes gleaming with genuine excitement, "you bypassed the physical limitations of your body and you harnessed the natural inertia of the ground’s rotation and discharged it through your strikes. However..."
He leaned forward slightly, gesturing with two slender fingers.

"...the drawback is immense, is it not? The overwhelming static of that power completely overwhelms your mana pathways so I can guess while the state is active, you are functionally incapable of executing complex earth magic... You cannot raise walls, you cannot transmute distant sand or Earth, and you cannot command silica threads."
Maya stared at him in utter chilled disbelief.

’Was this bastard stalking me through the relays?!’ Maya raged internally, her fists clenching under the linen sheet. ’To deduce the internal flaws and mechanics of my art just by watching a broadcast feed?!’
Valerius caught the hostile murderous glare in her eyes and abruptly paused.
He cleared his throat softly.
"I... apologize if that sounded overly presumptuous," Valerius said, his voice suddenly losing its confidence as he looked away toward the curtained exit.
A distinct undeniable shade of crimson began creeping up the back of his neck, spreading all the way to the tips of his ears.

"I only investigated it because... well," Valerius stammered slightly, the composure of House Sterling crumbling into awkward embarrassment. "I was planning on developing a technique similar to that utilizing atmospheric pressure and wind... which is why I, uh..."
He locked eyes with her again for half a second, saw her intense unblinking amber stare, and his face turned red.
CLATTER!
He stood up so violently his golden armor chimed loudly against the metal chair!
"In any case!" Valerius blurted out, stiffening his posture and pulling his formal cape straight. "I should not intrude upon your recovery any longer. Please... get better soon, Da Silva."
Without waiting for a response, he turned on his polished boots and practically marched out of the room with his cape swishing behind him in a blur of golden fabric.
Maya sat frozen on the cot, staring at the empty doorway in complete utter bafflement.
"What a weird guy," Maya muttered aloud, scratching her tangled dark hair with an exasperated scowl. "What was his face turning all red for anyway? Did the sun fry his noble brain?"
Her eyes drifted down to the small side table beside her bed and resting on a clean linen cloth was a brass flask with a threaded silver lid sealing the top with wisps of steam venting from the seam.
Maya leaned over, wincing as her ribs pulled, and unscrewed the lid with a dull pop.
"Fuck..."
A rich savory aroma immediately filled the room... It was a thick steaming stew packed with shredded mountain pheasant, roasted root tubers, and crushed high-tier spirit-ginseng.
’Does this belong to him...?’ Maya thought, her brow furrowing. ’Did he leave this here for me, or...?’
She picked up the small silver spoon beside the flask, eyeing the broth suspiciously.
’Is it poisoned?’
She let out a short scoffing snort.
’Whatever. My system has processed enough Amazonian swamp venom to kill a dragon... probably so poison would just taste like extra salt at this point.’
GRRRRRR!
Her stomach let out a ferocious roar that shook her ribcage.
"I’ll eat it..."

Discarding the spoon, Maya gripped the hot brass flask with both hands and began swallowing the stew down like a starving hawk with the rich boiling broth burning a warm miraculous path of nourishment down into her aching core.
As she drank, her mind naturally drifted back to the combat data.

’If I alter the third rotational pivot... if I vent the excess static through the soles of my boots instead of letting it bottleneck in my kidneys... could I maintain Earthborn without tearing my own organs apart...?’
SWISH!
The door was thrown open with tremendous force.
"Maya! Oh thank the gods you’re not in pieces!"
Leona marched into the pavilion, her arms loaded with clean wraps and canteens, her face covered in dried grime but beaming with frantic energy.

"I was convinced that Albion bastard had pulverized your spine! Isolde was being a terror, Devan tried to drown the whole arena in lava, but Kara... oh, Maya, you should have seen it! One punch! She dropped him right into the bedrock! We won the entire bracket, Maya!"
Maya set the empty brass flask down, wiped her chin with the back of her wrist, and accepted the water canteen Leona thrust toward her.
GLUG! GLUG! GLUG!
She downed half the cold water in three massive gulps, letting out a satisfied refreshed gasp.
"Good," Maya grunted, leaning back against the pillows. "How’s the grand council meeting going?"
Leona stopped mid-stride with her wild grin instantly collapsing into a grimace of pure exhausted awkwardness.
"Well..." Leona winced, scratching her ear. "...it’s certainly an experience."
Inside the Grand Meeting Room, the tension was thick enough to choke a horse.
...Quite literally.
Gathered around the massive conference table were the supreme rulers of the world as well as the Magistrates of the World Council and the members itself.
And seated directly across from them, occupying the primary high-backed leather chair with offensive disrespect, was Kara White.
Kara had both of her boots propped up on the polished wood with her ankles crossed casually over some paper.
Balanced effortlessly across her knees was an enormous, overflowing silver platter of chilled deep-sea tiger shrimp, a bowl of spiced garlic butter, and a tall crystal glass of sparkling iced cider.
With slow deliberate calm, she peeled the shell from a massive shrimp using only her single hand, dipped it deep into the garlic butter, and bit down with a loud crunch.
"As I was explaining, Lord White," President Julian Vanderbilt Senior spoke with his voice strained and his knuckles turning white where they gripped the polished armrests of his executive chair.

The ruthless corporate titan of the Republic of Columbia adjusted his gold-rimmed spectacles, his iron-gray hair impeccably combed back, though the lenses could barely conceal the smoldering wrath beneath his heavy brow.
His charcoal pinstripe suit was tailored to perfection with heavy signet rings glinting against the obsidian table, yet his jaw remained locked in a tight venomous clench.

"The gloves utilized by the First Princess during her engagements are of astronomical strategic value," Vanderbilt pressed, forcing his domineering voice into a semblance of dignified diplomacy. "The capability to externalize multi-elemental pathways without a core could redefine humanity’s survival percentages against portals to the Sovereign Realm... It has the potential to usher in an entirely new epoch of Awakened military infrastructure. The Republic, alongside the World Council’s executive arm, is prepared to offer Blessed Land full autonomy, three permanent high-tier mining corridors in the southern gulf, and an initial endowment of fifty billion credits for the manufacturing blueprints."
Kara chewed the deep-sea tiger shrimp slowly, savoring the sweet brine and garlic.
’Haah... Such stress...’
She swallowed with an easy deliberate tilt of her chin, took a leisurely sip of sparkling iced cider, and dabbed her mouth with an ornate silk napkin bearing the World Council’s golden crest.
"Not for sale," Kara said flatly.
Vanderbilt’s left eyelid twitched violently with a thick vein pulsing along his temple.
"Miss Kara," Chancellor Henri de Montmirail spoke up from the Europa Directorate’s station, adjusting his thin wire spectacles as his guild arbiters shuffled holographic treaties.

His sharp aristocratic face dripped with polished indignation. "You cannot adopt such an isolationist stance. We are discussing the defense of the Nine Major Powers and the collective security of humanity cannot be held hostage by the stubborn whims of a single territory."
Kara didn’t even bother to take her boots off the polished celestial marble.
Her dark trousers were dusty, her boots resting square across the papers.
With slow precision, she reached out her single working hand, picking up another massive chilled shrimp from the overflowing silver platter perched across her knees.
CRACK!
She snapped the chitinous shell off with a wet crisp pop.
"I don’t care," Kara replied, her voice dropping into a dry deadpan tone that carried less warmth than a frozen tombstone.
Vanderbilt took a sharp trembling breath, his signet rings clicking hard against the conference table as he leaned forward, tapping a holographic ledger into the air between them.

"Every creation has an evaluation, Lord White," Vanderbilt growled, the predatory corporate tyrant bleeding through his diplomatic veneer. "If fifty billion is insufficient, Columbia can negotiate exclusive maritime shipping exemptions across the entirety of the southern sea lanes... We can grant Blessed Land unfettered access to our deep-vault refinement refineries—"
Kara’s half-lidded eyes slowly lifted.
WHOOOSH!
An invisible suffocating hammer of power slammed down upon the circular pavilion.
CREAK... CRUNCH!

Once again, the massive table groaned under the pressure of the Gold core Lord as the crystal water carafes shattered into thousands of microscopic shards with liquid hissing as it was flattened into a paper-thin film against the floor tiles.
The sparkling cider in Kara’s glass vibrated with violent rings, while the air in the chamber grew so heavy that drawing a single breath felt like inhaling liquid mercury.
Kara tilted her head, her dark eyes igniting with a cold terrifying luminescence that seemed to drink in the light of the room.

"Listen to me very carefully, Vanderbilt," Kara murmured softly, each syllable landing like an iron mace swung into an open chest. "The more you flap your gums about those gloves... the more enticed I feel to blow your head off your shoulders and paint this pretty little table with your brain matter."
A gasp ran across the room.
Vanderbilt physically recoiled, slamming hard against the high back of his executive leather chair, col with sweat instantly drenching his tailored collar.
The blood drained from his face until his skin resembled spoiled milk.
Across the circular table, every single leader, prime minister, and director flinched in raw terror.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur of Khemet stiffened, his liquid-gold eyes narrowing in dead silence...

Sir Arthur Pendelton of Albion gripped his star-iron cane until his knuckles turned gray, even Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov of Borealis let his hand hover over the white wolf-pelt on his shoulder, his massive jaw tightening.
Their elite personal bodyguards instinctively dropped their hands toward their weapons, but not a single sentinel dared to do anything.𝓯𝙧𝙚𝒆𝙬𝙚𝒃𝙣𝙤𝒗𝓮𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
They were completely paralyzed.
The bloodlust radiating from the single-armed woman eating shrimp felt like a divine guillotine resting against their collective necks.

’When in the hell did this woman become so vocal about executing global rulers?!’ Vanderbilt screamed in the trembling humiliated silence of his mind with his heart hammering against his ribs like a panicked beast. ’She is threatening to butcher the head of a superpower right across the summit floor...!’
Kara didn’t spare the shivering corporate tycoon another glance.
SNAP!
The suffocating gravity vanished as abruptly as it had arrived, leaving the room’s occupants gasping for air like drowning men breaching the surface of a frozen lake.
Kara dipped another shrimp into the spiced garlic butter, chewing with quiet, leisurely satisfaction.
’Idiots,’ Silas thought beneath Kara’s placid unreadable mask.
He had known from the exact second he forged those midnight-blue gloves that they would trigger an international storm.
To power-hungry scions, corporate warmongers, and bureaucratic scavengers, the concept of externalizing elemental pathways without cores was the ultimate holy grail.
They saw a weapon that could turn common foot-soldiers into walking artillery batteries.
’They think it’s a universal tool anyone can slip on,’ Silas mused internally with a small mocking scoff echoing in the privacy of his soul. ’They have zero comprehension of the prerequisites...’
They made new Spirit pathways, Aki could handle that because her veins carried the pure concentrated royal bloodline of her royal ancestors.

If any ordinary person slipped those gloves on and tried to draw from the reservoir, the foreign mana would violently backfire through their meridians, blowing their hands, forearms, and chest into a fine red mist before they could finish an incantation.
’Sell it?’ Silas thought, taking a slow refreshing sip of cold cider as the trembling ministers frantically gathered their scattered papers and broken crystal.
’Not a chance in hell. Those gloves were forged for my Princess, and nobody else in this world is ever putting a hand inside them.’
Then he paused.
’Or maybe I should let them...?’
If it killed someone, would they blame Kara?

To power-hungry scions, corporate warmongers, and bureaucratic scavengers, the concept of externalizing elemental pathways without cores was the ultimate holy grail.
They saw a weapon that could turn common foot-soldiers into walking artillery batteries.
’They think it’s a universal tool anyone can slip on,’ Silas mused internally with a small mocking scoff echoing in the privacy of his soul. ’They have zero comprehension of the prerequisites...’
They made new Spirit pathways, Aki could handle that because her veins carried the pure concentrated royal bloodline of her royal ancestors.

If any ordinary person slipped those gloves on and tried to draw from the reservoir, the foreign mana would violently backfire through their meridians, blowing their hands, forearms, and chest into a fine red mist before they could finish an incantation.
’Sell it?’ Silas thought, taking a slow refreshing sip of cold cider as the trembling ministers frantically gathered their scattered papers and broken crystal.
’Not a chance in hell.
Those gloves were forged for my Princess, and nobody else in this world is ever putting a hand inside them.’
Then he paused.
’Or maybe I should let them...?’
If it killed someone, would they blame Kara?

chapters.title: Chapter 586: Bet On It
paragraphs: "Kar—"
CRACK!𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
With slow insulting rhythm, Kara used her single hand to snap the chitinous tail off a massive shrimp.
She dipped it deep into the spiced butter, swirled it once, and tossed it into her mouth.
CRUNCH!
Beside the table, Silas was thinking behind that composed half-lidded female mask.
’Again, the gloves by themselves are bloody useless to them,’ Silas mused, watching a tiny drop of garlic butter plop onto the high-grade papers of the Council below him.
It was almost comical watching these rulers stew.
The entire theater sitting around this circular ring had completely missed the forest for the trees as they saw an artificial bypass around the bottleneck of cores...
’Fucking hell.’
They believed they were staring at a universal key that could turn common line infantry into multi-elemental artillery units.

What they didn’t know, what no one outside his personal workshop in Blessed Land could possibly understand, was that Rowenna had woven her own personal brand of paranoia from the academy directly into the conductive sub-fabric.

The woman had spent nights under the pale light of her room, according to her, cackling like a madwoman while etching microscopic interlocking counter-divination runes into every square millimeter of the silk threading.
She had proudly declared, with heavy bags under her bloodshot eyes, that it was her "anti-theft intellectual containment spell."

If any mortal artificer tried to cut the seams, dissolve the leather, or probe the mana channels with a spectral needle, the internal runes would instantly destabilize into inert ash, leaving nothing behind but scorched cowhide... with a small gift.
And then there was Thora.
’The dwarf woman is going to blow a gasket when she finds out I tossed them out,’ Silas thought, the corners of Kara’s lips twitching with the ghost of a smirk.

Thora had spent too many hours over an open forge, hammering the star-iron eyelets into the leather with her own calloused soot-blackened hands so naturally, she would undoubtedly scream bloody murder, throw an iron spanner directly at his kneecaps the second he stepped foot back in the Blessed Land smithy, and threaten to dismantle every one of the golems out of spite.

’I’ll just have to buy her a crate of aged alcohol from the markets and a cartload of high-purity ore from the LAB,’ he calculated casually. ’A dwarf with forty pounds of fresh forging stock and five gallons of northern liquor forgets a grudge in about twenty minutes.’
Besides, the mechanics of those gloves were biologically tethered to Aki’s royal bloodline.
The phantom pathways required cellular walls with an absurd elasticity, a rare genetic trait carried only by the true imperial lineage of House Castellian.

Without that exact physiological buffer, any normal Awakened who slipped those gloves on and tried to draw from the secondary reservoir would suffer an instantaneous violent meridian blowout as the foreign mana detonated inside their forearms, blowing their arms into a wet crimson mist before they could even finish visualizing an incantation.
’And they still want it?’
Whoever bought them would spend months having their chief alchemists fry their eyebrows off in cleanrooms, only to realize they were holding an ornamental pair of expensive leather mitts.
At the end of the day, they’d have to come crawling right back to Blessed Land just to ask how to flip the switch.
Across the circular marble slab, President Julian Vanderbilt Senior looked as if his coronary arteries were about to burst under high pressure.
The corporate titan of the Republic of Columbia was gripping the carved armrests of his executive chair with such violent intensity that the polished star-iron trim was groaning under his fingers.

His charcoal pinstripe suit was immaculate, his iron-gray hair combed back with razor precision with his heavy signet rings glinting against the light of the floating optical plates but beneath that multi-billion-credit veneer, his face was the mottled color of bruised plum.
Every single nerve in his skull was screaming.

Since barely a few hours ago, His only son... Julian Junior, was currently floating in an alchemical nutrient tank with his pelvic girdle shattered into powder with his hip joints pulverized by the very people who had been sitting at this table.
’We also failed to get revenge...’

And now the woman representing Blessed Land was casually peeling shellfish over the official documents of the World Council, treating the leaders of humanity like unruly children waiting for a schoolmaster’s nod.

’Stingy, arrogant, low-born bitch,’ Vanderbilt raged within the silent trembling cage of his own thoughts, his blood pounding in his ears like an industrial drop-forge. ’She won the Exhibition... Blessed Land has already secured the rights to the northern mining corridor, the sole extraction concession for the celestial quartz veins, and every nation on this continent will have to pay them billions in maritime tariffs just to buy unrefined ore. She holds the future wealth of a continent in her palm, and she’s being stingy over a single pair of gloves?!’
Vanderbilt’s teeth ground together with a harsh sickening scrape as he forced his breathing to slow, feeling the cold suffocating gazes of the other heads of state boring into his back.
He couldn’t blow this.
...Not now.

The Republic’s aerospace divisions needed that conductive blueprint... If Columbia could adapt those artificial pathways to their mechanized armor suites, they’d break the Directorate’s monopoly on mid-tier mana engines overnight.
Vanderbilt bowed his head with a stiff humiliating jerk of his neck that made every muscle in his shoulders burn with shame.

’All I want is to choke this bitch to death with my bare hands,’ he thought, his fingernails digging into the upholstery. ’I want to drag her by that black hair through the salt flats of Columbia until she begs for mercy.’
Outwardly, his voice was smooth and dipped in the thick syrup of corporate contrition.

"Lord White," Vanderbilt began, his raspy voice trembling slightly as he fought to keep it level. "If my previous overtures were perceived as aggressive, I tender the Republic’s sincerest apologies... The heat of the tournament and the unfortunate medical incidents of the morning have frayed our collective tempers but I must urge you to look past personal grievances. What you hold on your person is not a mere weapon, it’s an epoch-defining breakthrough for our species... The security of humanity, the defense of our continental perimeter against the breaches, demands that—"
"Fine."
Vanderbilt’s jaw locked mid-word.
He blinked, his spectacles slipping a millimeter down his nose. "I... what?"
"I said fine," Kara drawled, not even looking up as she tossed an empty shrimp shell onto the silver platter with a hollow clatter. "You want the gloves? I’ll sell them."
The Great Assembly Chamber seemed to lose all atmospheric pressure in a single collective heartbeat.
Not a single soul moved.

Around the Grand Table, the rulers of humanity froze as if struck by a high-tier petrification spell as the endless sound of the runic dampening arrays carved into the celestial marble felt suddenly deafening, buzzing straight through their boot soles.
To the north, King Zhao Xian of the Shogunate Isles paused, his long white beard fluttering slightly, his eastern eyes widening beneath his dragon-embroidered silk hat.

Beside him, King Minamoto no Masashi, whose hand had remained perpetually glued to the black-lacquered hilt of his ancestral katana, subtly uncurled his calloused fingers with his dark eyebrows twitching in disbelief.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur sat bolt upright in his golden chair.
The bronze-skinned ruler of Khemet, still pale and hollow-eyed after seeing that his favored son was killed, leaned forward so fast his lapis-lazuli collar clicked against his white suit.
Even upon the elevated royal dais, the shadows shifted.
The King of the World, sitting back in his bespoke midnight-navy wool suit, looking like a youthful immortal sovereign barely in his late twenties despite centuries of rule, didn’t shift his posture.

His oceanic blue eyes remained cold, terrifying pools of ancient unmoving ice, but the microscopic distortion of pure mana that constantly hovered around his fingertips momentarily ceased its vibration.
In his lap once more, the Second Princess Kiera tilted her head.
Her royal-blue locks spilled over the King’s tailored lapel, her golden eyes... the unmistakable radiant sign of an Awakened Purple Lord Core... flickering with sudden feline amusement.
She had watched Kara threaten ministers, dismiss the Crown Prince, and mock the court with terrifying arrogance.
Why would a monster who hoarded territory suddenly hawk her primary artifact like a common street peddler?
Up in the mezzanine tier, the independent lords were equally stunned.

Magistrate Bloom’s gray-streaked brows drew together in a sharp V, his hand tightening on the hilt of his saber, while beside him, the second Magistrate adjusted his violet cowl, leaning forward to whisper something that never left his lips.

’If Aki were in this room right now,’ Silas thought, amused by the shock rippling through the hall, ’she’d be throwing a complete royal tantrum... Tugging at her hair, her face bright red, stuttering about how I’m trading away the only thing that made her feel useful.’

Aki was currently sequestered in the dressing suites three levels below, surrounded by terrified royal maids frantically trying to scrub the dried shale from her midnight-blue velvet skirts while walking on eggshells around her newly awakened authority.
But she’d understand eventually... She trusted him, even when his moves looked completely reckless to the rest of the world.
THUD!
Kara reached into her inner coat pocket, pulled out the pair of midnight-blue gloves, and tossed them carelessly onto the center of the celestial marble.
The weave hit the stone with a dull metallic weight.

Under the glare of the quartz skylight, the delicate microscopic runes etched along the knuckles hummed with a soft luminescence with a pale smoldering ember of crimson fire on the right cuff and a faint spiraling ribbon of emerald wind on the left.
"There’s about two small sparks of fire-mana left in the right knuckle," Kara said casually, resting her chin in her palm as she swept her dark eyes across the circle of global rulers.

"Maybe three quick attacks of compressed wind in the left... Just enough for your chief artificers to hook up their sensory needles, calibrate the frequencies, and see how the conduits fire... And who knows, if the winning bid is pretty enough, maybe I’ll even feel generous and charge the reservoirs to full capacity before you take them home... Consider it a private auction with an open floor and the highest bidder takes the prototype."
The silence cracked like winter ice.

’Money-hungry bitch,’ Chancellor Henri de Montmirail thought, his thin spectacles catching the light as his guild arbiters frantically began tapping numbers into their holographic balance sheets. ’She threatens to sever Vanderbilt’s neck ten minutes ago, and now she turns the most sacred assembly in the world into a bazaar stall.’

’Greedy extortionist wren,’ Sir Arthur Pendelton of Albion sneered internally, his silver-haired head tilting down as his cold blue eyes locked onto the glowing star-iron weave. ’She knows every nation here would empty their national reserves to avoid falling behind in conductive weapon research.’
Kara’s grin widened by a fraction, her eyes gleaming with dark predatory mirth.
She didn’t need mind-reading magic to know exactly what every monarch and minister in this room was thinking...
They thought she was an unrefined opportunistic barbarian who cared about nothing but padding her personal vault.
’Good... Let them think it, it’s just as I planned too. A greedy monster was predictable and one with a gold one was even more terrifying.’ Kara thought.
The black haired woman then shifted her gaze up toward the mezzanine tier, looking directly at the platforms reserved for the non-sovereign noble houses.

"What about House Sterling?" Kara called out, her voice cutting through the rising murmurs with effortless volume. "Or the grand Matriarch of House Bloom? You two are sitting on gold mines... Not interested in placing a bid?"

In the Bloom delegation box, Matriarch Etilga Bloom sat as rigid as an obsidian statue with her heavy crimson silk robes pooled around her boots and her terrifying scorched-earth presence radiating outward like an open blast furnace.
Beside her, Seraphina’s father, Magistrate Bloom, remained stony-faced.
Etilga’s lips thinned into a razor-sharp dismissive line.

"House Bloom relies on the pure supremacy of its bloodline flame," Etilga replied, her voice cold and dry as cracked bone. "If a scion of my house requires external leather conduits to ignite their mana, they are unfit to carry the family crest... We have no use for artificial crutches."
A few seats down, Patriarch Lohan Sterling offered a thin noble smile.
His silver robes shimmered under the chandeliers with his pale calculating eyes flicking briefly toward Grand Tsar Volkov across the floor before returning to Kara.

"The Sterling Conglomerate has already concluded a comprehensive infrastructure pact with the Tsardom of Borealis regarding the extraction corridors," Lohan stated smoothly. "It would be an egregious breach of business etiquette for our house to bid against our primary commercial partner. We respectfully decline..."
’Naturally,’ Silas thought, amused by the corporate cowardice. ’Lohan doesn’t want to piss off the seven-foot bear he’s planning to dig trenches with.’

chapters.title: Chapter 587: Bidding On The Gloves
paragraphs: And then there was Amazonia.

Seated at the southwestern arc of the Grand Table, High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva sat completely motionless with her booted feet planted wide and her calloused hands resting flat on the table while her dark olive uniform was adorned with the bleached fangs of river leviathans.
A combat scar ran from her left ear straight down into her collar, framing a face that had seen years of brutal uncompromising warfare.
She didn’t raise a finger and she didn’t give her aides an order.
’Heh, these fools will bleed their treasuries dry,’ Valeria mused with a dangerous smirk playing behind her dark eyes.

She had known Aki since the First Princess was a small quiet girl shivering in the grand corridors of the palace, and more importantly, Amazonia had just signed a formal coalition treaty with Blessed Land before the tournament through Aki.

If Blessed Land ever intended to distribute this technology, or if the schematics were ever released to an ally, Amazonia would receive them through private back-channel courier before the World Council even finished ratifying the paperwork.
Bidding against Columbia right now was nothing more than lighting credits on fire...
"Twelve billion!" Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov boomed, shattering the silence like an artillery shell.
The seven-foot ruler of Borealis slammed an iron-plated fist onto the table, his white dire-wolf mantle shaking violently with his ice-frosted beard bristling.
"Borealis opens the bidding! Twelve billion credits in unrefined platinum bullion, cleared through the northern exchanges within three business cycles!"

"Fourteen billion," Sir Arthur Pendelton countered instantly with his voice sounding smooth and dry as he tapped his star-iron cane against the stone. "Along with full maritime passage exemptions for any merchant fleet bearing Blessed Land’s standard through the Albion Narrows for the next twenty years..."
’How does that fleet thing even work for me?’

"Sixteen billion!" Chancellor Henri de Montmirail barked from the Europa Directorate, his guild arbiters frantically adjusting their projections. "Plus three manufacturing licenses for heavy industrial atmospheric condensers!"

"Twenty billion," Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur spoke, his liquid-gold eyes flashing with intense desperate hunger. "And eighty crates of second-grade solar-jade marrow from the royal reserves of Khemet..."
The bids escalated with terrifying reckless momentum.

It was an grotesque display of global wealth... numbers that could rebuild entire ruined provinces or feed three nations for a decade being hurled across the marble like copper coins in a tavern brawl.

Vanderbilt’s breath was coming in short ragged gasps with the veins along his neck standing out like cords of blue steel, as he watched his rivals reach deeper and deeper into their national reserves.
If Albion got their hands on this, their dueling academies would become untouchable.
If the Directorate took it, their mechanized divisions would dominate the western front.
’No,’ Vanderbilt thought, his vision tinged with red. ’Columbia will have it... Even if I have to mortgage the entire southern rail network.’
"FORTY BILLION!" Vanderbilt roared, rising half an inch from his seat, slamming both palms onto the table with a bang.
The Great Assembly Chamber fell dead silent.

Tsar Volkov let out a low rumbling growl in the back of his throat with his thick eyebrows knitting together as his financial ministers frantically tapped his shoulder, waving red-flagged deficit projections in front of his face.
He cursed in northern dialect and waved them off, slumping back into his furs.
Sir Arthur Pendelton’s lips tightened into a thin bloodless line as he slowly closed his eyes, leaning back against his cane, signaling his withdrawal.
Menes Al-Mansur stared at the table, his knuckles whitening before he let out a bitter exhausted exhale.
Forty billion credits was a simply incomprehensible sum of liquid capital... Enough to cause currency inflation across three continents.
Vanderbilt stood breathing heavily with his chest heaving and his iron-gray hair disheveled while his bloodshot eyes fixed on Kara.

"Forty billion Spirit credits," Vanderbilt panted, his raspy voice shaking with adrenaline. "Direct transfer. Liquid reserves backed by the Columbia Central Treasury... There are loans and no bonds either. Do we have an agreement, Lord White?!"
Kara didn’t flinch as she picked up her crystal flute, took a slow refreshing sip of cold pear cider, and gently set the glass back onto its coaster.
"Forty billion," she repeated slowly, tasting the weight of the number. "Not bad, Mr. President... Not bad at all for an old pair of leather gloves..."
She sat up straight, sliding her boots off the celestial marble and resting her forearms against the table as her dark eyes locked onto Vanderbilt with chilling clarity.

"Two conditions before you touch them," Kara said, her voice dropping into a clean professional tone. "First... payment cleared upfront. I don’t do ninety-day commercial notes, and I sure as hell don’t accept paper IOUs signed by a Columbia trade minister."
Vanderbilt nodded violently.
"Agreed."

"Second," Kara continued, her smirk returning coldly. "You sign a binding legal waiver right here in front of the World Council, the Nine Powers, and every floating tab watching... You explicitly acknowledge that these gloves are highly experimental and volatile military prototypes. If your researchers blow their hands off, if the internal pathways destabilize and vaporize an entire wing of your research lab, or if the user suffers catastrophic meridian blowout... you will not sue, you will not seek council arbitration, and you will not levy trade sanctions against Blessed Land... You buy them as-is. Take it or leave it."
Vanderbilt let out a harsh arrogant snort through his nose.
’She thinks she can frighten me with operational hazards?’ Vanderbilt scoffed in his mind.
Columbia had the finest magical-engineering labs in the modern world.
They’d reverse-engineered ancient Pre-Apocalypse engines so whatever crude fail-safes Blessed Land had cobbled together in their mountain forge would be unraveled by his alchemists within a week.
"The Republic accepts all terms," Vanderbilt stated firmly, his voice ringing with confidence. "Provide your financial routing details, Lord White."
Kara reached into the deep inner breast pocket of her dark coat and around the chamber, ministers, aides, as well as the others leaned forward slightly with their breath held.
’I don’t really know what I’m expecting...’
Well since it was Kara and she was that scary, most expected her to produce a phone with a cruel back or perhaps a tablet or something else...
SLIP!
Kara pulled out a mobile phone.
It was sleek and remarkably thin... encased in an eye-searing vibrant pastel-pink silicone cover patterned with tiny grinning white cartoon kittens batting at balls of yellow yarn.
A cosmic silence descended upon the five tiers of the room.
Across the table, Sir Arthur Pendelton’s spectacles slipped down the bridge of his nose, resting crookedly against his cheek.
Tsar Volkov blinked three times in rapid succession with his mouth slightly agape while
Chancellor Montmirail froze, his hand hovering over his stylus as if his brain had completely stalled.
Even upon the royal dais, Kiera’s golden eyes widened by a fraction with her lips parting in silent bewilderment.

This was the terrifying single-armed monster who had torn an Indus champion into ribbons, threatened to execute a Ruler Of The World over dinner, and insulted the King as well... and she was casually unlocking a phone that looked like it had been stolen from a twelve-year-old schoolgirl in the lower commercial wards.
Kara didn’t care in the slightest as she swiped her thumb across the screen with her cartoon kitten wallpaper disappearing as she brought up a standard mobile banking interface.
’Fuck Evelyn for this though.’
"Minister," Vanderbilt barked, clearing his throat loudly to drown out the sheer absurdity of the moment.
A trembling financial minister in a gray three-piece suit scrambled forward from the Columbia delegation, holding a glowing terminal with shaking hands.
"R-Routing details, Lord White," the minister stammered, his stylus hovering over the input plate.
Kara recited the numbers without looking up from her screen.
"Routing code, 0-9-4-4-B-L. Account number, 7-8-8-9-1-2-0-4. Valoria City Bank..."
The minister froze.
He stared at the numbers then he looked up at Kara with his face turning into an expression of professional horror.

"V-Valoria City Bank?!" the minister squeaked, his voice cracking into a high pitched squeak. "Lord White... that’s a regular savings bank in the city! Their maximum liquid transaction ceiling is one billion Spirit credits! If we attempt to route forty billion credits through their clearance servers, their physical infrastructure will literally explode and their data-coils will melt through the floor too. May I strongly plead that you establish an account with the World Bank instead? The World Bank maintains universal clearance channels across all major powers—"
Kara’s dark eyes slowly lifted from her screen, locking onto the minister with a flat deadpan stare that made the man’s knees violently knock together.

"I don’t have the patience to sit through three hours of that garbage," Kara said smoothly, her voice making chills run down his spine. "I don’t feel like signing ninety pages of identity disclosures, and I certainly don’t care about your clearance limits... Though—"
She tilted her head with her gaze drifting toward the northern arc of the Grand Table, staring directly at the seven World Council Heads.
Five of them sat cloaked in midnight-silk with their faces completely obscured behind featureless white porcelain masks and their immortal presences feeling vast and immovable.

"—maybe the venerable World Council would be so kind as to open an executive zero-limit black account on my behalf?" Kara mused, her voice dripping with insolent mock-sweetness. "No background checks and no tax deductions too... Surely the rulers of humanity can handle a simple banking task for their newly crowned champion?"
The five masked figures remained completely motionless however a whisper of mana stirred beneath their dark hoods.
"Tch. Useless old mummies," Kara muttered under her breath, loud enough to echo clearly across the first three tiers.
Gasps followed as Ministers, corporate aides, and military retainers physically recoiled.
Vanderbilt looked as if he were about to faint, while Sir Arthur Pendelton gripped his cane so hard his knuckles turned blue.
Insulting the World Council Heads... the same entities who had survived the First Apocalypse and whose true names were struck from every historical record was an act of unfathomable blasphemy.
Before the silence could ignite into violence, Magistrate Bloom, sitting unmasked beside the council arc, cleared his throat.

"The World Council has already anticipated this administrative requirement," Magistrate Bloom stated, his stern severe voice cutting through the tension with his cold gaze fixed forward and his hand firm on his saber. "In light of Blessed Land’s decisive ascension, an executive account has been pre-authorized under the name of Kara White within the World Bank’s database."

The second Magistrate, seated beside him in deep violet robes, raised his hand as a small glowing data-shard detached from his ring, floating smoothly across the thirty yards of open air to land softly on the celestial marble right beside Kara’s iced cider.

"The biometric encryption keys and temporary access codes are encoded within," the second Magistrate added calmly. "There are zero transaction caps and complete immunity from international revenue audits."
"Now that’s what I call efficiency," Kara grinned.
She snatched the data-shard from the table and pressed it against the back of her pink kitten phone case.
’Isn’t that how it’s done...?’𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
BEEP!
A bright golden rune flared across the screen, replacing her local bank app with the sleek black-and-gold interface of the World Bank.
"Routing updated," Kara told Vanderbilt’s shaking minister. "Dump the cash... Here’s the number."
The minister frantically stabbed his stylus into the terminal with clicking sounds vibrating from the device as massive funds were being transferred over a pair of gloves.
PING!
Kara’s phone chimed with a cheerful high-pitched 8-bit melody as a glowing notification banner dropped down over her screen.
[WORLD BANK PRIME VAULT: +40,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS DEPOSITED.]
[SENDER: REPUBLIC OF COLUMBIA EXECUTIVE TREASURY!]
Kara’s smile widened.
"Pleasure doing business with you, Vanderbilt."
With a casual careless flick of her wrist, she backhanded the midnight-blue gloves across the table.
SWISH!
They slid smoothly over the polished celestial marble, coming to a halt directly in front of Vanderbilt’s chest.
His hands moved like striking vipers, snatching the star-iron fabric from the table before anyone else could even blink.

His bloodshot eyes shone with feverish triumphant mania as he stroked the conductive leather, his chest swelling with pride, and he quickly tucked the gloves deep into his reinforced inner coat pocket with his breathing finally stabilizing.
"The Republic appreciates your support, Lord White," Vanderbilt managed to say, his voice thick with smug corporate satisfaction. "We will not forget this day."

’You certainly won’t,’ Silas thought behind Kara’s mask, taking another leisurely sip of cold cider. ’Especially when your top five alchemists melt their eyes out trying to read Rowenna’s chicken-scratch runes.’
