chapters.title: Chapter 588: Ladders To Climb?
paragraphs: The chamber slowly settled back into an uneasy breathless quiet as the circus was over.
Now the true, terrifying weight of the summit descended upon the room.
At the northern arc of the table, the central masked figure of the World Council slowly raised her head.
The motion was unnaturally fluid, lacking any micro-movements of human bone and tendon.

When she spoke, her voice was unmistakably feminine, yet it carried a layered multi-tonal resonance, as if three different women were speaking at the exact same pitch with their voices vibrating directly inside the skulls of everyone present.
"Now that the commercial trivialities have concluded," the masked speaker intoned. "We may proceed with the formal business of this assembly."
Every pair of eyes in the Grand Assembly Chamber swung toward Kara.
Kara let out a small tired sigh.

She set her empty crystal glass down, shoved the silver platter of shrimp tails to the side, and finally swung her boots off the Grand Table, sitting upright, resting her elbows on the celestial marble with her right hand drumming a slow beat against the stone.
’Finally,’ Silas thought, his mind sharpening into a razor-thin point of cold focus. ’My turn.’
This was what all the posturing, the blood in the desert, and the public humiliation of the royal house had been building toward...
The World Council was terrified.
For centuries the global hierarchy had been locked beneath an unbreakable ceiling... No mortal had reached the Gold Core threshold in living memory.

The balance of power was a delicate clockwork mechanism managed by the Council and the Nine Powers, and now a living anomaly had come, wielding enough raw power and mana to shatter that clockwork into dust.

"Kara White," the masked speaker continued, her porcelain mask gleaming under the harsh chandeliers. "By the undisputed rite of the world, you have demonstrated a power unseen since the founding era. The Council formally proclaims you Humanity’s Hero... a supreme protector of the terrestrial sphere. It is the collective desire of this assembly that you do not abandon this realm for the higher planes of the Sovereign Realm, but remain anchored here to safeguard our collective borders against the encroaching dark. In exchange for your presence, the Council is prepared to grant unprecedented boons across both realms."
The masked woman began listing the terms, her voice ringing with grand generosity.

"We offer permanent tax exemption across all nine continental corridors, unrestricted passage for Blessed Land’s trade flotillas, and a permanent diplomatic seat at the High Council’s biannual convening—"
"Hold on," Kara interrupted as she raised her right hand, holding up a single slender index finger.
The masked woman’s voice cut off instantly as a sharp collective gasp rippled through the upper stadium tiers.
Nobody, not even the dual monarchs of Shogya nor the Grand Tsar of Borealis, ever dared interrupt a Speaker of the World Council.
It was a breach of protocol that historically warranted execution on the spot!
"Let’s not get ahead of ourselves with poetry," Kara said, dripping with dry unimpressed sarcasm. "Let’s start with the basics, like point number one."
She tapped her extended finger against the marble.

"Before this tournament or hell, this meeting as a whole commenced, the World Council issued an official proclamation stating that if the Lord of Blessed Land presented herself before this assembly in the flesh, she’d be awarded a bounty of nine to ten billion credits. Well... I’m sitting here. I’ve been sitting here for two hours, battling, eating your shrimp and listening to your politicians whine and yet, when I check my newly minted World Bank account, that ten billion is nowhere to be found. Why is that? Are the supreme rulers of humanity running a tab on me?"
The two Magistrates sitting at the table stiffened as the five masked figures remained utterly still, though a faint prickly tension seemed to gather in the air around them.
Kara didn’t wait for an answer as she extended a second finger.

"Point number two," Kara continued, her tone dropping into a lower and far more dangerous tone that sent a shiver down the spines of the listening ministers. "Since you’re so eager to declare me a national treasure and the savior of humanity, it’s only logical I receive absolute immunity... Not the standard diplomatic immunity you hand out to ambassadors, I want immunity on the exact same legal tier as the Supreme Royal Family and if a minister insults me, I can execute him on the spot without a trial... If a guard looks at me wrong, his life is forfeit, and if Vanderbilt looks at my boobs one more time, I can just blast him into oblivion."
"H-huh?!" Vanderbilt stuttered as eyes turned to him, since when had he been looking at her boobs?
Kara slowly turned her head, her dark eyes drifting toward the elevated royal dais.

Her gaze swept right past the silent King, locking squarely onto the empty seat beside him... the station where Aki had spent her entire youth being ignored, degraded, and treated like a piece of worthless court furniture.

"And that immunity extends directly to Princess Aki," Kara said, each word carrying an immovable weight that resonated through the stone. "The way she’s been treated in this court... the insults, the neglect, the pathetic political posturing from men who couldn’t survive ten seconds in the dirt... it ends today. If I hear of a single person in this Citadel treating her like an unwanted stray ever again, the World Council won’t have to worry about the borders... You’ll have to worry about me."
On the royal dais, the King’s jaw subtly tightened.

For the briefest fraction of a second, the oceanic blue of his eyes seemed to swirl with a dark apocalyptic storm of pure mana unraveling and beside him, Kiera’s golden eyes narrowed with her slender hands folding neatly over her silk lap, watching Kara with an unreadable stare but Kara didn’t care.
’Their faces are so annoying...’
She brought her third finger up.

"Point number three, infrastructure," Kara declared smoothly. "Blessed Land is located in an isolated inhospitable mountain range far from the primary trade areas in the Sovereign Realm... That’s terrible for everything so I want a direct high-capacity spatial gate connecting my central keep straight to Central City in the Sovereign Realm that’s built, calibrated, and maintained at the World Council’s expense."
She raised her fourth finger.

"Point number four, territorial assets... I want at least one hundred Hero-tier Summoning Tickets delivered to my vault by the end of the week and several tens of thousands of High-tier Troop Summoning Tickets to bolster my defensive garrisons... Throw in twenty thousand metric tons of your highest-grade of alloys while you’re at it."
She brought her thumb up, opening her entire palm toward them.

"Point number five, commercial ventures... To be honest, I want prime real estate and I want the licensing rights to establish a global luxury hotel and entertainment chain across all Nine Major Powers. You want my face on your posters to reassure the terrified masses that humanity is safe?... Fine, you can use my face for advertising, but I get a twenty-five percent gross royalty on every tourism corridor and commercial hub that uses my name. It should generate enough annual revenue to match the gross domestic product of a medium-sized nation."
Kara leaned forward with a broad shameless grin spreading across her face.

"And finally... I happen to know the World Council maintains a classified vault beneath the Citadel’s foundations, the private treasury of the First Founders right? I want unrestricted access... I go down there with a wagon, I pick out whatever catches my eye like ancient grimoires, lost relics, forgotten divine weapons too... and I take them home. If I can fill a couple of chests, it’d really make my day."
She stopped as the entire room was staring at her in frozen horror.
Vanderbilt looked like he’d forgotten how to breathe.

Sir Arthur Pendelton’s jaw was completely slack while Chancellor Montmirail was trembling so violently that his holographic ledgers were flickering out of alignment and even High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva was looking at Kara with an expression that bordered on disbelief.
Kara paused, looking around at the sea of paralyzed, pale faces.
She blinked, letting out an annoyed exasperated scoff.
"What?" Kara asked, throwing her hands up in mock exasperation. "What’s with those faces? Don’t tell me the mighty World Council is broke. I haven’t even listed the full extent of what I want yet!"

The heavy obsidian pillars of the Great Assembly Chamber seemed to vibrate under the frozen weight of Kara’s words as nobody breathed and not a single leaf of paper rustled across the celestial marble of the Grand Table.
Across the five curving tiers of the amphitheater, aides, corporators, and grizzled frontline commanders sat petrified in their stadium seats, their eyes bulging as they stared down into the pit.

’Is she insane?’ Chancellor Henri de Montmirail screamed within the frantic shivering privacy of his own thoughts, his wire-rimmed spectacles fogging over with rapid horrified breath. ’Not the full extent of what she wants?! What in the name of the First Founders is her endgame? Does she intend to hold the entire planet hostage until every reserve on Earth is bled dry?!’
Across the floor, Sir Arthur Pendelton’s star-iron cane was practically creaking beneath his white-knuckled grip.
His blue eyes, usually cold and unreadable, darted wildly between Kara’s half-lidded face and the towering northern dais.

Even Tsar Nikolai Volkov, a man who had wrestled northern frost-wyrms with his bare hands and laughed at the prospect of war, sat utterly motionless beneath his dire-wolf mantle with his jaw locked like an iron bear-trap.
They all looked at her as though she were a lunatic who had casually walked into a powder magazine holding a lit stick of dynamite, asking for a lighter so she could check the corners for gold.
The silence grew so thick it tasted like iron shavings.

Everyone expected one of the masked Council Heads to interject or for Magistrate Bloom to draw that ancestral saber an inch from its scabbard, or for the ancient woman in midnight-silk to crush the room under another wave of suffocating gravity.
Instead the response came from higher up as from the elevated royal dais, a voice drifted down into the pit.
"All of that is simply far too much to concede at once."
The King sat back against the dark star-iron of his throne with his tailored double-breasted suit of midnight-navy wool falling over his shoulders without a single wrinkle and Kara paused.
Her right hand, which had been resting loosely near the silver platter of shrimp tails, ceased its slow drumming against the marble.
She tilted her head, her dark eyes drifting upward toward the imperial dais, offering the supreme monarch of humanity a slow unimpressed raise of her brow.
"Huh?" Kara drawled, her tone sounding like an annoyed tenant being interrupted by a landlord on rent day.
The King didn’t blink.
In his lap, Kiera Zel Castellian remained still, her golden eyes watching the exchange with detached feline focus with her hands clasped delicately over her pale silk skirts.

"Your demands exceed the reasonable bounds of political parity," the King stated, his oceanic gaze pinning Kara with the weight of an executioner’s stare. "You are a newly discovered Gold Core... You have held lordship for not even a single turn of the seasons, yet you arrive in this chamber, kick your heels onto the sacred marble, and present an exhaustive list of ultimatums as though you were an ancient hegemon dictating terms to a conquered province..."
He paused, his manicured fingers resting casually on his knee.

"A summit is a venue of bilateral negotiation, Kara White," the King continued. "It is an instrument designed to discover a nexus where the collective interests of the world and your sovereign territory meet in equilibrium. What you have presented is not an equilibrium. It’s blatantly extortion..."
The ministers around the table let out a collective silent sigh of relief.
Finally... Someone was setting the boundary! Someone with the divine right of Destruction was drawing a line in the sand against this wild lawless woman!
Everyone held their breath, waiting for Kara’s explosive retort.
They braced for the table to shatter, for her horrifying mana to detonate, or for another wave of vulgar threats to spill from her lips.

sentences.text: The chamber slowly settled back into an uneasy breathless quiet as the circus was over.
Now the true, terrifying weight of the summit descended upon the room.
At the northern arc of the table, the central masked figure of the World Council slowly raised her head.
The motion was unnaturally fluid, lacking any micro-movements of human bone and tendon.

When she spoke, her voice was unmistakably feminine, yet it carried a layered multi-tonal resonance, as if three different women were speaking at the exact same pitch with their voices vibrating directly inside the skulls of everyone present.
"Now that the commercial trivialities have concluded," the masked speaker intoned.
"We may proceed with the formal business of this assembly."
Every pair of eyes in the Grand Assembly Chamber swung toward Kara.
Kara let out a small tired sigh.

She set her empty crystal glass down, shoved the silver platter of shrimp tails to the side, and finally swung her boots off the Grand Table, sitting upright, resting her elbows on the celestial marble with her right hand drumming a slow beat against the stone.
’Finally,’ Silas thought, his mind sharpening into a razor-thin point of cold focus. ’My turn.’
This was what all the posturing, the blood in the desert, and the public humiliation of the royal house had been building toward...
The World Council was terrified.
For centuries the global hierarchy had been locked beneath an unbreakable ceiling...
No mortal had reached the Gold Core threshold in living memory.

The balance of power was a delicate clockwork mechanism managed by the Council and the Nine Powers, and now a living anomaly had come, wielding enough raw power and mana to shatter that clockwork into dust.
"Kara White," the masked speaker continued, her porcelain mask gleaming under the harsh chandeliers.
"By the undisputed rite of the world, you have demonstrated a power unseen since the founding era.
The Council formally proclaims you Humanity’s Hero... a supreme protector of the terrestrial sphere.

It is the collective desire of this assembly that you do not abandon this realm for the higher planes of the Sovereign Realm, but remain anchored here to safeguard our collective borders against the encroaching dark.
In exchange for your presence, the Council is prepared to grant unprecedented boons across both realms."
The masked woman began listing the terms, her voice ringing with grand generosity.

"We offer permanent tax exemption across all nine continental corridors, unrestricted passage for Blessed Land’s trade flotillas, and a permanent diplomatic seat at the High Council’s biannual convening—"
"Hold on," Kara interrupted as she raised her right hand, holding up a single slender index finger.
The masked woman’s voice cut off instantly as a sharp collective gasp rippled through the upper stadium tiers.
Nobody, not even the dual monarchs of Shogya nor the Grand Tsar of Borealis, ever dared interrupt a Speaker of the World Council.
It was a breach of protocol that historically warranted execution on the spot!
"Let’s not get ahead of ourselves with poetry," Kara said, dripping with dry unimpressed sarcasm.
"Let’s start with the basics, like point number one."
She tapped her extended finger against the marble.

"Before this tournament or hell, this meeting as a whole commenced, the World Council issued an official proclamation stating that if the Lord of Blessed Land presented herself before this assembly in the flesh, she’d be awarded a bounty of nine to ten billion credits.
Well...
I’m sitting here.

I’ve been sitting here for two hours, battling, eating your shrimp and listening to your politicians whine and yet, when I check my newly minted World Bank account, that ten billion is nowhere to be found.
Why is that?
Are the supreme rulers of humanity running a tab on me?"
The two Magistrates sitting at the table stiffened as the five masked figures remained utterly still, though a faint prickly tension seemed to gather in the air around them.
Kara didn’t wait for an answer as she extended a second finger.
"Point number two," Kara continued, her tone dropping into a lower and far more dangerous tone that sent a shiver down the spines of the listening ministers.
"Since you’re so eager to declare me a national treasure and the savior of humanity, it’s only logical I receive absolute immunity...

Not the standard diplomatic immunity you hand out to ambassadors, I want immunity on the exact same legal tier as the Supreme Royal Family and if a minister insults me, I can execute him on the spot without a trial...
If a guard looks at me wrong, his life is forfeit, and if Vanderbilt looks at my boobs one more time, I can just blast him into oblivion."
"H-huh?!" Vanderbilt stuttered as eyes turned to him, since when had he been looking at her boobs?
Kara slowly turned her head, her dark eyes drifting toward the elevated royal dais.

Her gaze swept right past the silent King, locking squarely onto the empty seat beside him... the station where Aki had spent her entire youth being ignored, degraded, and treated like a piece of worthless court furniture.
"And that immunity extends directly to Princess Aki," Kara said, each word carrying an immovable weight that resonated through the stone.
"The way she’s been treated in this court... the insults, the neglect, the pathetic political posturing from men who couldn’t survive ten seconds in the dirt... it ends today.
If I hear of a single person in this Citadel treating her like an unwanted stray ever again, the World Council won’t have to worry about the borders...
You’ll have to worry about me."
On the royal dais, the King’s jaw subtly tightened.

For the briefest fraction of a second, the oceanic blue of his eyes seemed to swirl with a dark apocalyptic storm of pure mana unraveling and beside him, Kiera’s golden eyes narrowed with her slender hands folding neatly over her silk lap, watching Kara with an unreadable stare but Kara didn’t care.
’Their faces are so annoying...’
She brought her third finger up.
"Point number three, infrastructure," Kara declared smoothly.
"Blessed Land is located in an isolated inhospitable mountain range far from the primary trade areas in the Sovereign Realm...

That’s terrible for everything so I want a direct high-capacity spatial gate connecting my central keep straight to Central City in the Sovereign Realm that’s built, calibrated, and maintained at the World Council’s expense."
She raised her fourth finger.
"Point number four, territorial assets...

I want at least one hundred Hero-tier Summoning Tickets delivered to my vault by the end of the week and several tens of thousands of High-tier Troop Summoning Tickets to bolster my defensive garrisons...
Throw in twenty thousand metric tons of your highest-grade of alloys while you’re at it."
She brought her thumb up, opening her entire palm toward them.
"Point number five, commercial ventures...
To be honest, I want prime real estate and I want the licensing rights to establish a global luxury hotel and entertainment chain across all Nine Major Powers.
You want my face on your posters to reassure the terrified masses that humanity is safe?...
Fine, you can use my face for advertising, but I get a twenty-five percent gross royalty on every tourism corridor and commercial hub that uses my name.
It should generate enough annual revenue to match the gross domestic product of a medium-sized nation."
Kara leaned forward with a broad shameless grin spreading across her face.
"And finally...
I happen to know the World Council maintains a classified vault beneath the Citadel’s foundations, the private treasury of the First Founders right?
I want unrestricted access...
I go down there with a wagon, I pick out whatever catches my eye like ancient grimoires, lost relics, forgotten divine weapons too... and I take them home.
If I can fill a couple of chests, it’d really make my day."
She stopped as the entire room was staring at her in frozen horror.
Vanderbilt looked like he’d forgotten how to breathe.

Sir Arthur Pendelton’s jaw was completely slack while Chancellor Montmirail was trembling so violently that his holographic ledgers were flickering out of alignment and even High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva was looking at Kara with an expression that bordered on disbelief.
Kara paused, looking around at the sea of paralyzed, pale faces.
She blinked, letting out an annoyed exasperated scoff.
"What?" Kara asked, throwing her hands up in mock exasperation.
"What’s with those faces?
Don’t tell me the mighty World Council is broke.
I haven’t even listed the full extent of what I want yet!"

The heavy obsidian pillars of the Great Assembly Chamber seemed to vibrate under the frozen weight of Kara’s words as nobody breathed and not a single leaf of paper rustled across the celestial marble of the Grand Table.
Across the five curving tiers of the amphitheater, aides, corporators, and grizzled frontline commanders sat petrified in their stadium seats, their eyes bulging as they stared down into the pit.

’Is she insane?’ Chancellor Henri de Montmirail screamed within the frantic shivering privacy of his own thoughts, his wire-rimmed spectacles fogging over with rapid horrified breath. ’Not the full extent of what she wants?!
What in the name of the First Founders is her endgame?
Does she intend to hold the entire planet hostage until every reserve on Earth is bled dry?!’
Across the floor, Sir Arthur Pendelton’s star-iron cane was practically creaking beneath his white-knuckled grip.
His blue eyes, usually cold and unreadable, darted wildly between Kara’s half-lidded face and the towering northern dais.

Even Tsar Nikolai Volkov, a man who had wrestled northern frost-wyrms with his bare hands and laughed at the prospect of war, sat utterly motionless beneath his dire-wolf mantle with his jaw locked like an iron bear-trap.
They all looked at her as though she were a lunatic who had casually walked into a powder magazine holding a lit stick of dynamite, asking for a lighter so she could check the corners for gold.
The silence grew so thick it tasted like iron shavings.

Everyone expected one of the masked Council Heads to interject or for Magistrate Bloom to draw that ancestral saber an inch from its scabbard, or for the ancient woman in midnight-silk to crush the room under another wave of suffocating gravity.
Instead the response came from higher up as from the elevated royal dais, a voice drifted down into the pit.

The King sat back against the dark star-iron of his throne with his tailored double-breasted suit of midnight-navy wool falling over his shoulders without a single wrinkle and Kara paused.
Her right hand, which had been resting loosely near the silver platter of shrimp tails, ceased its slow drumming against the marble.

chapters.title: Chapter 589: The World Council Accepts Your Terms
paragraphs: Chancellor Montmirail choked on his own saliva, frantically dabbing his mouth with a linen kerchief.
"That is unequivocally not what was implied—" the King began, his voice tightening with the faintest edge of sharp frost.
"Save the lecture," Kara cut him off with a long theatrical sigh, waving her hand dismissively.
She slumped back into the plush leather of her chair, rolling her shoulder.

"Look, I’ll be honest with you," Kara said. "I actually enjoy the human world. I like the food... I like the iced pear cider... I like sleeping in real beds and watching pompous nobles turn purple when their bank accounts get dinged... I definitely have zero burning desire to pack my bags, abandon Earth, and run off to Asgard or the deep zones of the Sovereign Realm."
She paused, her half-lidded eyes sharpening into two cold black daggers that locked dead-center onto the King’s face.

"However..." she drawled, her voice dropping a bit and ringing with the terrifying promise of total abandonment, "...if you old fossils insist on playing petty little border games, setting seniority caps, and trying to choke Blessed Land with red tape, then I’ll just pack my things... I’ll take my core, take my assets, cross the void gate, and leave you all to figure out how to stop the next breach or whatever with your pretty parade uniforms and shiny rapiers... Let’s see how well your royal lineage holds the front lines when the sky cracks open and there isn’t a Gold Core standing between your cities and the dark."
A cold suffocating dread swept through the room.
It was the ultimate trump card, the unassailable nightmare of the World Council.

They could manage ambitious lords and they could assassinate rogue Lords but a rogue Gold Core who simply decided to abandon the terrestrial sphere... leaving humanity completely defenseless against the extinction-level horrors lurking in the higher realms, especially at a time where the Suppression Engines were growing weaker was a catastrophe they had no protocol to handle.
’Just like Odin...’
The King remained silent for three long heartbeats.
His gaze drifted downward with his analytical mind searching for leverage.
Every human being had an anchor.

Every mortal had a thread that tied them to the earth... a family line, an ancestral estate, a lover, a child however Kara White had materialized from the void with no recorded family, no bloodline records, and no historical footprint.
Except for one person.

"You speak of departure with remarkable ease, Lord White," the King said softly. "Yet if you were to sever your ties with this realm and ascend entirely to the Sovereign Realm... what would become of my daughter?"
The question hung in the air like a poisoned dart.
Up in the mezzanine, Etilga’s eyebrows twitched.

"Are you truly prepared to abandon the First Princess?" the King asked. "Or rather... Aki, as you so boldly chose to name her in defiance of royal decree? She is an Unawakened and her meridians are inert clay... The raw atmospheric mana of the Sovereign Realm would tear her cellular structure to ribbons within minutes of transport. If you walk away from Earth, you leave her behind, and in this court, without your presence, her life would become remarkably short and remarkably unpleasant."
It was a blatant shameless threat of hostiles-in-waiting.
He was using his own flesh and blood, the daughter he had discarded, stripped of a name, and treated like ornamental garbage for twenty-five years, as a geopolitical hostage to hold Kara’s leash...
Every head of state held their breath.

’Checkmate,’ Vanderbilt thought with a sick vindictive smile threatening to crack his pinstriped facade. ’No matter how strong she is, she cannot bypass the physiological laws of the Great Threshold, it’s quite true, an Unawakened cannot enter the Sovereign Realm and even if they can, not for an extended period of time.’
Kara didn’t flinch as instead a slow grin spread across her lips.
"Leave her behind?" Kara chuckled. "What in the seven hells makes you think I’d ever leave her behind?"
She leaned forward, tapping the celestial marble with her knuckle.
TOC! TOC!

"Open your eyes, Your Majesty," Kara said, her dark eyes flashing with cold ridicule. "Blessed Land has already forged technology that completely shattered your so-called universal laws... Aki had inert channels since her sixteenth birthday, right? The entire world declared her a useless broken vessel and yet barely an hour ago, she walked out into Sector Forty-Four wearing a pair of gloves I threw together in an afternoon, channeled multi-elemental magic through her and single-handedly wiped several nobles off the tournament map."
She paused, letting the words sink like lead sinkers into their stomachs.

"If Blessed Land has already mastered the science of bypassing mana-saturation to let an Unawakened cast magic, what makes you arrogant fools think I haven’t already refined the technology to shield a regular human from the atmospheric pressure of the Sovereign Realm...?"
A chorus of sharp terrified intakes of breath whistled through the chamber.
King Zhao Xian’s eyes widened until the whites showed clearly while Sir Arthur Pendelton dropped his gaze to the table, his mind spinning into mathematical calculations.

’She can transport regular humans across the threshold?!’ Chancellor Montmirail thought, his hands shaking so violently his holographic ledgers flickered. ’If Blessed Land possesses atmospheric bio-containment conduits that can insulate fragile human cellular walls from the Sovereign Realm’s power... that means she doesn’t need Earth at all! She could relocate entire populations! She could establish a colony outside the World Council’s jurisdiction entirely!’
The staggering implication hit the King like a physical blow.
For the first time since the summit convened, the King’s throat subtly hitched.
A cold microscopic drop of sweat formed beneath the pristine royal-blue hair at the nape of his neck.
The leverage hadn’t merely evaporated, it had reversed too...
He was not holding Aki over Kara’s head, Kara was threatening to rob the throne of its ultimate prize while rendering the Council’s border defenses obsolete...
Kara watched the panic ripple through their ranks while being thoroughly satisfied.
’Idiots,’ Silas thought in the warm dark privacy of his soul. ’We haven’t even started any of that but they don’t know that. Bluffing high-born royals is practically free real estate...’
Kara gave a careless dismissive wave of her hand.

"Look, I’m a reasonable woman," Kara drawled, leaning back with an easy sigh. "I understand the World Council is slow and hopelessly out of touch with modern efficiency. It’s fine if you can’t fulfill every single item on my shopping list this very second. I won’t hold it against you... today. I can always come back and nag you about the luxury hotels and the commercial royalties later."
Her tone sharpened, the laziness vanishing into crisp intent.
"However, there are certain foundational assets that must be settled right now... Today. Before I leave this Citadel..."
’I need to ensure the territory expands,’ Silas calculated with cold mechanical precision.
Blessed Land was safe for now, tucked behind its natural mountain barriers but a territory without a proper army was just a golden pig waiting for the slaughter.

If he was going to turn that mountain sanctuary into an impenetrable empire capable of defying both the World Council and the horrors of Sovereign Realm, he needed raw manpower and he needed more elite units.
He needed soldiers who wouldn’t question orders and heroes who could perform miracles.

’This is the World Council,’ Silas thought, almost shaking his head in disbelief. ’They’ve been hoarding the continental tribute of nine superpowers for centuries... How could they possibly have a shortage of summoning stock? What are these ancient fossils even using Hero Summoning Tickets for anyway, paperweights?!’
Kara raised her dark eyes, pinning the silent assembly to their seats.
"The Troop Summoning Tickets," Kara demanded flatly. "The Hero Summoning Tickets... The immunity and access to your private vault. Those are non-negotiable. Deliver them, or I walk."

The silence stretched over the chamber for ten agonizing seconds as the King sat on his elevated throne, the Destruction mana around his hands completely withdrawn, replaced by a heavy suffocating defeat.
He swallowed.
The movement of his throat was tiny and imperceptible to the common delegates in the upper tiers, but to the monarchs seated around the Grand Table, it was a thunderous concession.
"The World Council..." the King spoke. "...agrees to your essential terms."
Kara’s face broke into a broad insufferable smile.

"Now was that so hard?" she laughed, giving the assembly a casual one-handed wave. "See? We can all be civilized when we put our minds to it! I promise I’ll be a wonderful shining beacon of hope for humanity. A real hero... The kind they put on lunchboxes!"
She leaned forward, tapping her chin with her thumb with her expression turning into a mock scowl.

"Though, while we’re on the subject of etiquette... why in the seven hells did you people call that initial billion-credit money a ’bounty’?" Kara asked, her voice rich with petty grievance. "A bounty is what you put on a horse thief or an escaped convict in the border... You weren’t hunting for my head, were you? I’m a distinguished guest! Calling it a bounty was remarkably rude."
A vein pulsed violently on the King’s temple as he took a slow deep breath, willing his royal bloodline not to incinerate the table into ash.
"The Council apologizes for the administrative nomenclature," the King managed to say with his words tasting like vinegar.
With a stiff sharp gesture of his right hand, the King swiped his finger across the glowing runic interface embedded into his royal armrest.
PING!
Kara’s sleek mobile phone, still resting on the celestial marble in its pastel-pink cartoon-kitten glory, let out a cheerful high-pitched chime.
Kara snatched the phone up with her thumb swiping across the screen as a glowing golden banner lit up her display.
[WORLD BANK PRIME VAULT: +10,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS DEPOSITED.]
[SENDER: WORLD COUNCIL TREASURY.]
[CURRENT PRIME BALANCE: 50,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS.]
Kara’s dark eyes drank in the numbers.
Fifty billion Spirit credits...
A nice round fifty billion sitting in an untraceable zero-limit black account backed by the highest monetary authority on Earth.

’Fifty billion...’ Silas thought with a small nostalgic chuckle echoing in the silence of his soul. ’Even with this astronomical mountain of digital gold, converted back into old-world currency, I’m still not quite as absurdly rich as Elon Musk was before I died... The man had hundreds of billions tied up in rockets.’
He gave an internal shrug.
’Well, there’s still plenty of time to grow but regardless, this is more liquid capital than a single human could spend in ten lifetimes. I am gloriously rich.’
Now, of course, came the practical complication.

How was he supposed to siphon twenty or thirty billion credits out of this World Bank executive account and route it into his actual personal account under the name of Silas, without alerting the Council’s intelligence hounds?
’Well, whatever,’ he decided, pocketing the pink phone with a satisfying click. ’I’ll just go meet Evelyn when I get back.’
Kara tapped the table again, looking up at the dais with bright greedy eyes.

"So," Kara remarked, her voice dripping with casual entitlement, "since we’re establishing such a wonderful working relationship... what about a small monthly sovereign allowance? Say, a modest billion credits every thirty days just to cover incidental expenses, high-grade snacks, and general administrative upkeep?"
"No."
The King’s response was instantaneous.

"You have received fifty billion credits within the span of thirty minutes, Kara White," the King stated, his oceanic eyes narrowing dangerously. "The Council’s treasury is not an open tap for your personal luxuries... When you begin executing missions that actively defend the sovereignty of humanity, perhaps then we may revisit the prospect of operational stipends but until then, you will not receive another copper."
Kara held up her hands in mock surrender, offering an easy careless shrug.
"Fair enough, fair enough," she chuckled. "A girl can try. Now... what about the immunity?"
The King folded his hands neatly over his lap.

"As the recognized Lord of Blessed Land, you are hereby granted full immunity within the political and administrative spheres of the terrestrial realm," the King declared. "You are recognized as an independent power under the direct sponsorship of the World Council and no regional magistrate or even a President may levy criminal charges or summon you for judicial arbitration."𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Kara raised an eyebrow. "And Princess Aki?"
The atmosphere on the dais grew profoundly cold as the King’s jaw tightened, his oceanic eyes flickering toward the empty chair on the lower terrace.

"She is my daughter," the King replied stiffly. "She carries the blood of the Castellian line... She is a royal of the supreme house, and I will not tolerate any insolence or disrespect levied against her name."
Around the Grand Table, nearly half the ministers and rulers had to physically bite their tongues to keep from letting out an audible mocking ’Pfft!’
It was a display of hypocrisy so breathtaking it bordered on comedy.
Barely two hours ago, this exact same King had watched in cold uncaring silence while Julian Vanderbilt Senior publicly degraded Aki as an unawakened cripple in the Grand Rotunda.

He had denied her a name, stripped her of her birthright, and blamed her for the death of the Queen for twenty-five years, and now, the second Blessed Land threw its immense weight behind her, he was suddenly acting the part of the fiercely protective patriarch defending the family honor.
Kara let out a quiet mocking snort through her nose, shaking her head.

Every head of state held their breath.

’Checkmate,’ Vanderbilt thought with a sick vindictive smile threatening to crack his pinstriped facade. ’No matter how strong she is, she cannot bypass the physiological laws of the Great Threshold, it’s quite true, an Unawakened cannot enter the Sovereign Realm and even if they can, not for an extended period of time.’
Kara didn’t flinch as instead a slow grin spread across her lips.
"Leave her behind?" Kara chuckled.
"What in the seven hells makes you think I’d ever leave her behind?"
She leaned forward, tapping the celestial marble with her knuckle.
TOC!
TOC!
"Open your eyes, Your Majesty," Kara said, her dark eyes flashing with cold ridicule.
"Blessed Land has already forged technology that completely shattered your so-called universal laws...
Aki had inert channels since her sixteenth birthday, right?

The entire world declared her a useless broken vessel and yet barely an hour ago, she walked out into Sector Forty-Four wearing a pair of gloves I threw together in an afternoon, channeled multi-elemental magic through her and single-handedly wiped several nobles off the tournament map."
She paused, letting the words sink like lead sinkers into their stomachs.

"If Blessed Land has already mastered the science of bypassing mana-saturation to let an Unawakened cast magic, what makes you arrogant fools think I haven’t already refined the technology to shield a regular human from the atmospheric pressure of the Sovereign Realm...?"
A chorus of sharp terrified intakes of breath whistled through the chamber.
King Zhao Xian’s eyes widened until the whites showed clearly while Sir Arthur Pendelton dropped his gaze to the table, his mind spinning into mathematical calculations.

’She can transport regular humans across the threshold?!’ Chancellor Montmirail thought, his hands shaking so violently his holographic ledgers flickered. ’If Blessed Land possesses atmospheric bio-containment conduits that can insulate fragile human cellular walls from the Sovereign Realm’s power... that means she doesn’t need Earth at all!
She could relocate entire populations!
She could establish a colony outside the World Council’s jurisdiction entirely!’
The staggering implication hit the King like a physical blow.
For the first time since the summit convened, the King’s throat subtly hitched.
A cold microscopic drop of sweat formed beneath the pristine royal-blue hair at the nape of his neck.
The leverage hadn’t merely evaporated, it had reversed too...
He was not holding Aki over Kara’s head, Kara was threatening to rob the throne of its ultimate prize while rendering the Council’s border defenses obsolete...
Kara watched the panic ripple through their ranks while being thoroughly satisfied.
’Idiots,’ Silas thought in the warm dark privacy of his soul. ’We haven’t even started any of that but they don’t know that.
Bluffing high-born royals is practically free real estate...’
Kara gave a careless dismissive wave of her hand.
"Look, I’m a reasonable woman," Kara drawled, leaning back with an easy sigh.
"I understand the World Council is slow and hopelessly out of touch with modern efficiency.
It’s fine if you can’t fulfill every single item on my shopping list this very second.
I won’t hold it against you... today.
I can always come back and nag you about the luxury hotels and the commercial royalties later."
Her tone sharpened, the laziness vanishing into crisp intent.
"However, there are certain foundational assets that must be settled right now...
Today.
Before I leave this Citadel..."
’I need to ensure the territory expands,’ Silas calculated with cold mechanical precision.
Blessed Land was safe for now, tucked behind its natural mountain barriers but a territory without a proper army was just a golden pig waiting for the slaughter.

If he was going to turn that mountain sanctuary into an impenetrable empire capable of defying both the World Council and the horrors of Sovereign Realm, he needed raw manpower and he needed more elite units.
He needed soldiers who wouldn’t question orders and heroes who could perform miracles.
’This is the World Council,’ Silas thought, almost shaking his head in disbelief. ’They’ve been hoarding the continental tribute of nine superpowers for centuries...
How could they possibly have a shortage of summoning stock?
What are these ancient fossils even using Hero Summoning Tickets for anyway, paperweights?!’
Kara raised her dark eyes, pinning the silent assembly to their seats.
"The Troop Summoning Tickets," Kara demanded flatly.
"The Hero Summoning Tickets...
The immunity and access to your private vault.
Those are non-negotiable.
Deliver them, or I walk."

The silence stretched over the chamber for ten agonizing seconds as the King sat on his elevated throne, the Destruction mana around his hands completely withdrawn, replaced by a heavy suffocating defeat.
He swallowed.
The movement of his throat was tiny and imperceptible to the common delegates in the upper tiers, but to the monarchs seated around the Grand Table, it was a thunderous concession.
"The World Council..." the King spoke.
"...agrees to your essential terms."
Kara’s face broke into a broad insufferable smile.
"Now was that so hard?" she laughed, giving the assembly a casual one-handed wave.
"See?
We can all be civilized when we put our minds to it!
I promise I’ll be a wonderful shining beacon of hope for humanity.
A real hero...
The kind they put on lunchboxes!"
She leaned forward, tapping her chin with her thumb with her expression turning into a mock scowl.
"Though, while we’re on the subject of etiquette... why in the seven hells did you people call that initial billion-credit money a ’bounty’?" Kara asked, her voice rich with petty grievance.
"A bounty is what you put on a horse thief or an escaped convict in the border...
You weren’t hunting for my head, were you?
I’m a distinguished guest!
Calling it a bounty was remarkably rude."
A vein pulsed violently on the King’s temple as he took a slow deep breath, willing his royal bloodline not to incinerate the table into ash.
"The Council apologizes for the administrative nomenclature," the King managed to say with his words tasting like vinegar.
With a stiff sharp gesture of his right hand, the King swiped his finger across the glowing runic interface embedded into his royal armrest.
PING!
Kara’s sleek mobile phone, still resting on the celestial marble in its pastel-pink cartoon-kitten glory, let out a cheerful high-pitched chime.
Kara snatched the phone up with her thumb swiping across the screen as a glowing golden banner lit up her display.
[WORLD BANK PRIME VAULT: +10,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS DEPOSITED.]
[SENDER: WORLD COUNCIL TREASURY.]
[CURRENT PRIME BALANCE: 50,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS.]
Kara’s dark eyes drank in the numbers.
Fifty billion Spirit credits...
A nice round fifty billion sitting in an untraceable zero-limit black account backed by the highest monetary authority on Earth.

’Fifty billion...’ Silas thought with a small nostalgic chuckle echoing in the silence of his soul. ’Even with this astronomical mountain of digital gold, converted back into old-world currency, I’m still not quite as absurdly rich as Elon Musk was before I died...
The man had hundreds of billions tied up in rockets.’
He gave an internal shrug.
’Well, there’s still plenty of time to grow but regardless, this is more liquid capital than a single human could spend in ten lifetimes.
I am gloriously rich.’
Now, of course, came the practical complication.

How was he supposed to siphon twenty or thirty billion credits out of this World Bank executive account and route it into his actual personal account under the name of Silas, without alerting the Council’s intelligence hounds?
’Well, whatever,’ he decided, pocketing the pink phone with a satisfying click. ’I’ll just go meet Evelyn when I get back.’
Kara tapped the table again, looking up at the dais with bright greedy eyes.
"So," Kara remarked, her voice dripping with casual entitlement, "since we’re establishing such a wonderful working relationship... what about a small monthly sovereign allowance?
Say, a modest billion credits every thirty days just to cover incidental expenses, high-grade snacks, and general administrative upkeep?"
"No."
The King’s response was instantaneous.
"You have received fifty billion credits within the span of thirty minutes, Kara White," the King stated, his oceanic eyes narrowing dangerously.
"The Council’s treasury is not an open tap for your personal luxuries...

When you begin executing missions that actively defend the sovereignty of humanity, perhaps then we may revisit the prospect of operational stipends but until then, you will not receive another copper."
Kara held up her hands in mock surrender, offering an easy careless shrug.
"Fair enough, fair enough," she chuckled.
"A girl can try.
Now... what about the immunity?"
The King folded his hands neatly over his lap.
"As the recognized Lord of Blessed Land, you are hereby granted full immunity within the political and administrative spheres of the terrestrial realm," the King declared.

"You are recognized as an independent power under the direct sponsorship of the World Council and no regional magistrate or even a President may levy criminal charges or summon you for judicial arbitration."𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Kara raised an eyebrow.
"And Princess Aki?"
The atmosphere on the dais grew profoundly cold as the King’s jaw tightened, his oceanic eyes flickering toward the empty chair on the lower terrace.
"She is my daughter," the King replied stiffly.
"She carries the blood of the Castellian line...
She is a royal of the supreme house, and I will not tolerate any insolence or disrespect levied against her name."
Around the Grand Table, nearly half the ministers and rulers had to physically bite their tongues to keep from letting out an audible mocking ’Pfft!’
It was a display of hypocrisy so breathtaking it bordered on comedy.
Barely two hours ago, this exact same King had watched in cold uncaring silence while Julian Vanderbilt Senior publicly degraded Aki as an unawakened cripple in the Grand Rotunda.

He had denied her a name, stripped her of her birthright, and blamed her for the death of the Queen for twenty-five years, and now, the second Blessed Land threw its immense weight behind her, he was suddenly acting the part of the fiercely protective patriarch defending the family honor.
Kara let out a quiet mocking snort through her nose, shaking her head.

chapters.title: Chapter 590: World Vault [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Fascinating how quickly paternal affection blooms when there’s a Gold Core standing in the room," Kara muttered, loud enough for the entire northern arc to hear.
The King ignored the barb, though the subtle destructive vibration around his fingers threatened to unravel the silk of his trousers.
"And finally," the King said, steering the conversation with rigid haste, "there is the matter of your access to the World Vault."
The entire chamber stiffened instantly.
’Did we forget about my other request for the teleportation stuff so I can actually visit Central City...?’
No matter, Kara would ask once she actually got into the world count then a nervous tremor rippled through the ranks of the Nine Major Powers.
The World Vault was not merely a treasury.
It was a mythical sanctum established during the First Apocalypse, a vault constructed beneath the ancient foundations of the Citadel to preserve the relics of a dying world.
It held items salvaged from the Fall of the World... primordial grimoires, soul-forged artifacts, classified weapons whose power could tilt the balance of continental wars.
In centuries, not a single living monarch sitting at this table, not even the ancient Tsar Volkov or Sir Arthur Pendelton, had ever been granted permission to step through its threshold.
The King took a slow heavy breath.
An unmistakable nervous hesitation crept into his regal posture as his oceanic eyes flickered and his fingers clenched into tight tense fists.

"The World Vault contains the foundational heritage of our civilization," the King stated, his voice tight. "Its contents are classified under Omega-level security seals. However... in accordance with our agreement, the Council will permit you entry. You will be escorted to the primary chamber, where you may select three treasures—"
"Five."
The King’s left eyelid twitched violently.
"Three," the King repeated with his voice grinding through clenched teeth.

"Five would do nicely," Kara interrupted smoothly, flashing another brilliant infuriating smile. "I have a growing territory, Your Majesty... Lots of mouths to feed, lots of walls to build... Three is an odd unlucky number and five feels much more harmonious, don’t you think?"
Up on the dais, the King stared down at her with a look of pure murder.

Every single royal instinct in his soul was screaming at him to unleash Destruction, he just wanted to point his finger, unravel her molecular bonds, and turn Kara White into an unrecognizable smear of subatomic ash.
Yet... even if he uncoiled that absolute power, would it even work?
She was a Gold Core.
’She already said it wouldn’t...’

If his Destruction failed to obliterate her in the first second and even bounced off her body a bit, the resulting cataclysm would crack the Citadel in half, drown the summit in the black ocean, and trigger a global civil war humanity could not survive.
The King let out a long agonizing exhale.
"Five," the King ground out, his voice hollow with forced defeat. "You may take five items... No more..."
Kara gave him a cheerful enthusiastic thumbs-up with her right hand.
"Look at that! You’re goated, Your Majesty," Kara grinned shamelessly. "Truly. Some of the times, at least."
The King closed his eyes for a full three seconds, visibly wrestling his temper into submission.
When he opened them, he turned his head toward the northern arc where the five masked World Council Heads sat.
"Number Five," the King commanded, his voice sounding very cold. "Escort the Lord of Blessed Land to the lower sanctuary and supervise the transaction as well."𝓯𝙧𝙚𝒆𝙬𝙚𝒃𝙣𝙤𝒗𝓮𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
From the council bench, the smallest of the masked figures rose to her feet.
She was noticeably short, her slender frame enveloped in heavy hooded robes of midnight-silk woven with anti-divination wards.
Her face was completely concealed behind a smooth featureless mask of polished white porcelain, bearing no crest, no runes, and no human expression either.
Even when the King spoke to her, she didn’t speak back.
She simply offered a curt mechanical nod of her head, stepped off the council dais, and began walking toward the heavy titanium blast doors on the western wall.
As she reached the corridor archway, she paused and motioned with a single silk-draped sleeve for Kara to follow.
"Woah~ Finally some action."
Kara pushed herself up from the executive armchair, gave her shoulders a long lazy roll, and casually strolled toward the doors.
WHOOOSH!

The second Kara stepped within three paces of the short, masked woman, the fabric of space violently sheared as the air in the chamber twisted into a sickening vertigo-inducing spiral of translucent gravitational force.
Kara felt a sudden sharp tug behind her navel as an instantaneous high-velocity spatial displacement that bent her eyesight out of alignment!
POP!
In the blink of a mortal eye, both Kara and the masked woman vanished from the Great Assembly Chamber as not a speck of dust, not a whisper of mana, and not a single residual spark was left behind.
The suffocating pressure that had choked the chamber for the timeshe had been there collapsed instantly, replaced by a hollow quiet.
Across the Grand Table, President Julian Vanderbilt Senior let out a massive shuddering gasp, practically deflating into his executive chair like a punctured tire.

’Gone...’ Vanderbilt thought, his trembling fingers pressing against his inner coat pocket, feeling the reassuring rigidity of the midnight-blue gloves pressed against his ribs. ’That demonic extortionist bitch is finally gone.’
TOC! TOC! TOC!
The rhythmic tapping of a manicured finger against polished star-iron echoed from the northern dais.
Vanderbilt froze, slowly lifting his head.
The King was looking down at him from his throne with his oceanic blue eyes piercing straight through Vanderbilt’s skull.
"President Vanderbilt," the King spoke quietly.
Vanderbilt scrambled to sit upright, adjusting his spectacles with shaking hands. "Y-Yes, Your Majesty?"

"The Republic has acquired the prototype," the King stated flatly. "You will not waste this opportunity on internal delays... Before the sun sets, the Crown will assign Grand Master Varun, the most accomplished Runemaster on the terrestrial plane, directly to your primary research facility in New Columbia."
Vanderbilt’s eyes widened in sudden feverish ecstasy.

Grand Master Varun was a living national treasure, a sage whose understanding of runes was quite legendary... He was quite younger than some of the other Masked members but old enough to be one himself.

"You will dismantle those gloves," the King ordered, his voice dropping into a dark razor-sharp whisper that chilled the room. "You will map every artificial pathway, decipher every containment rune, and replicate the conductive weave... The Crown expects a functioning, mass-producible schematic within thirty days."
Vanderbilt rose to his feet, bowing low from the waist with venomous resolve.
"The Republic hears and obeys, Your Majesty!" Vanderbilt declared, his heart thumping with fierce triumphant malice.

’Just you wait, Kara White,’ Vanderbilt vowed in the dark twisted corners of his mind, his fingers tightening around his lapel. ’Enjoy your fifty billion while you can... The second our artificers crack this weave and mass-produce your secret, Columbia will flood the global market. I will personally make it my life’s mission to see the look on your arrogant face when your precious monopoly is reduced to worthless street scrap.’
SWOOSH!
The disorienting pull of spell snapped off with the clean finality of a closing ledger as Kara blinked with her vision stabilizing in an instant.
The suffocating titanium walls of the Citadel and the bitter salt-air of the ocean were completely gone.
Instead she stood in the center of a colossal underground library that seemed to stretch outward into infinity.
The air was cool and dry, carrying the scent of old books which made Kara’s nose twitch.
Towering bookshelves carved from seamless petrified dark-wood rose fifty feet into the air, arranged in concentric curving rings that formed a massive labyrinth.
Thousands upon thousands of leather-bound grimoires, illuminated scrolls, and glowing crystalline data-slates rested neatly on the shelves as their spines hummed with dormant mana-currents.
There were no windows and no sounds of the outside world.

’We’re deep,’ Silas analyzed instantly, looking up at the vaulted ceiling carved directly from ancient glowing bedrock. ’Miles beneath the crust of the Island... We might even be situated directly beneath the ocean floor itself.’
Curious, Silas let his senses unfurl, nudging a thread of high-frequency vibrational mana outward to probe the perimeter and map the exits—
"I would strongly advise against expanding your spiritual perception in this facility."
The voice was muffled and came from the short hooded woman standing beside her.
Kara paused, looking down at the porcelain mask.

"The foundation of this sanctuary is woven with ninety-six layers of soul-dampening arrays," Number Five explained tiredly. "If your Gold Core mana touches the peripheral wards, the feedback will rebound directly into your nervous system... You will experience an instantaneous high-tier psychic backlash followed by a migraine that will make you wish your skull had been cracked open by a siege hammer."
Kara raised an eyebrow, but surprisingly, she pulled her mana back, letting it settle quietly into her core.
"Good to know," Kara said casually. "I like my brain right where it is."
Number Five turned on her heel and began walking down the wide central aisle of petrified wood with her midnight-silk robes sweeping silently over the polished slate tiles.
Kara strolled beside her with her hands tucked loosely into her coat pockets and her half-lidded eyes casually scanning the titles on the massive shelves.
’[Foundational Core Compaction: Third Era]... [The Seven Calamities of the Rift]... [Theoretical Principles of Void-Conductive Metals]...’

’Rowenna would literally sell her left kidney to spend an hour in this room,’ Silas thought, thoroughly amused. ’She’d probably chain herself to a bookshelf and refuse to leave until they dragged her out with a winch.’
Rowenna really did want to study a lot, according to what Reina was telling him, Rowenna was reading the most books in the Library.
After navigating through three rings of towering shelves, they arrived at a massive circular reception rotunda.
At the center of the rotunda sat an enormous high-backed service counter carved from a single polished slab of fossilized dragon-bone.
It stood nearly six feet high, looming like an ancient fortress wall and mounted on the center of the bone counter was a small ornate brass service bell.
Number Five stopped in front of the counter.
Standing barely five feet tall in her heavy robes, the counter came up past her shoulders.
She stood on the tips of her soft leather boots, stretching her slender neck and extending her silk-draped right arm, straining with all her might to reach the tiny brass button on top of the bell.
Her fingertips grazed the cold metal...
SWOOSH!
With a mocking hiss, the brass bell slid backward across the dragon-bone counter by exactly one meter, stopping just out of her reach!
Number Five froze as her arm remained outstretched in mid-air with her porcelain-masked face stared at the retreating bell for two long agonizing seconds.
Kara let out a low amused snicker, leaning against the edge of the desk.
"Need a hand, short stuff?" Kara offered, smirking. "I can pick you up by the scruff of your robe if you want."
Number Five slowly lowered her arm with her shoulders dropping into a posture of pure exasperation.
"I do not require your assistance," Number Five muttered, her muffled voice dripping with cold murderous venom.
She took a sharp breath, glaring at the empty space behind the counter.

"Musvi, you ancient festering parasite," Number Five cursed, her voice rising into an irritated rasp. "Get out here before I dismantle your precious card catalog and burn your petrified shelves for firewood..."
"Aiya! Such hostility from little Number Five!"
POP!
With a soft swirl of pale violet smoke, a man materialized behind the dragon-bone counter.
He leaned forward, resting both elbows on the polished bone, offering them an energetic flamboyant wave.

He was dressed in immaculate midnight-silk robes that mirrored the World Council Heads, but instead of the featureless white porcelain mask worn by the others, his mask was painted with an enormous comical smiling theater grin, accented by exaggerated red cheeks and spiraling golden eyebrows.

"You wound me, little sister!" the man exclaimed, his voice carrying the lively melodic voice of a wandering bard. "A gentleman spends four hundred years dusting ancient tomes in the dark, and this is the reception he receives?... No ’Good morning, Musvi’? No ’How are your aching joints, Musvi’?... Truly, the youth of the modern council have zero appreciation for classical hospitality!"
’Modern council, what the hell is he talking about?’
He turned his theatrical mask toward Kara, leaning his head to the side.

"And who is this delightful young lady standing in my humble reading room?" Musvi asked, his masked smile practically beaming. "My, my... look at that posture. Look at that glorious untamed power humming beneath the skin. You must be the famous Kara White! The wild girl from Blessed Land who made the mighty King swallow his own teeth in the assembly!"
Kara narrowed her eyes, studying the man before her.
’He’s strong,’ Silas analyzed instantly with a sharp quiet warning bell chiming behind his ribs.
On the surface, Musvi acted like an eccentric retired librarian, but beneath that painted wooden theater mask, Silas could feel the deep unfathomable ocean of a High-Tier Lord.
Yet there was something deeply strange about his core circulation.
It felt sluggish... it was not weak, but dormant instead, like an engine that had been deliberately geared down to run on low power for centuries.
Musvi caught her intense stare and let out a dramatic high-pitched gasp, clutching his chest with both hands.

"Oh my!" Musvi squeaked, taking a step backward. "Please, Lord White, do not look at an old man with such intensity! I am a fragile delicate scholar! My heart cannot handle the fiery gaze of a youthful Gold Core! If you fall in love with me, little Number Five will become terribly jealous, and we simply do not have the budget for domestic disputes in the archive!"
Kara blinked with an incredulous smirk pulling at her lips.
"Are you always this annoying, or is today a special occasion?"
"Every day is a special occasion when you live under miles of granite, my dear!" Musvi winked from behind his wooden eyeholes.
Number Five let out a heavy suffering sigh that sounded like it had been building up for three centuries.

"Enough garbage, Musvi," Number Five said, her voice dry as dust. "By imperial decree of the King and the High Council, the Lord of Blessed Land has been granted authorization to enter the World Vault and claim five ancestral artifacts so produce the master key."

"Oho!" Musvi’s painted eyebrows seemed to gleam with genuine excitement. "The World Vault?! A customer for the deep sanctum?! Splendid! Marvelous! It has been three hundred and eighty years since someone walked through those iron gates... Oh, the dust down there is magnificent and the cobwebs are practically historical monuments—"
"Hold on," Kara interrupted, leaning her hip against the dragon-bone counter.
Musvi paused mid-gesture. "Yes, my fierce warrior maiden?"

"Before we go wandering into the spooky basement," Kara said, holding out her right hand with an open palm, "I want my other assets delivered... The King signed off on the full package so where are my Hero Summoning Tickets and my Troop Summoning Tickets?"
