Vanderbilt rose to his feet, bowing low from the waist with venomous resolve.
"The Republic hears and obeys, Your Majesty!" Vanderbilt declared, his heart thumping with fierce triumphant malice.
’Just you wait, Kara White,’ Vanderbilt vowed in the dark twisted corners of his mind, his fingers tightening around his lapel. ’Enjoy your fifty billion while you can...
The second our artificers crack this weave and mass-produce your secret, Columbia will flood the global market.
I will personally make it my life’s mission to see the look on your arrogant face when your precious monopoly is reduced to worthless street scrap.’
SWOOSH!
The disorienting pull of spell snapped off with the clean finality of a closing ledger as Kara blinked with her vision stabilizing in an instant.
The suffocating titanium walls of the Citadel and the bitter salt-air of the ocean were completely gone.
Instead she stood in the center of a colossal underground library that seemed to stretch outward into infinity.
The air was cool and dry, carrying the scent of old books which made Kara’s nose twitch.
Towering bookshelves carved from seamless petrified dark-wood rose fifty feet into the air, arranged in concentric curving rings that formed a massive labyrinth.
Thousands upon thousands of leather-bound grimoires, illuminated scrolls, and glowing crystalline data-slates rested neatly on the shelves as their spines hummed with dormant mana-currents.
There were no windows and no sounds of the outside world.
’We’re deep,’ Silas analyzed instantly, looking up at the vaulted ceiling carved directly from ancient glowing bedrock. ’Miles beneath the crust of the Island...
We might even be situated directly beneath the ocean floor itself.’
Curious, Silas let his senses unfurl, nudging a thread of high-frequency vibrational mana outward to probe the perimeter and map the exits—
"I would strongly advise against expanding your spiritual perception in this facility."
The voice was muffled and came from the short hooded woman standing beside her.
Kara paused, looking down at the porcelain mask.
"The foundation of this sanctuary is woven with ninety-six layers of soul-dampening arrays," Number Five explained tiredly.
"If your Gold Core mana touches the peripheral wards, the feedback will rebound directly into your nervous system...
You will experience an instantaneous high-tier psychic backlash followed by a migraine that will make you wish your skull had been cracked open by a siege hammer."
Kara raised an eyebrow, but surprisingly, she pulled her mana back, letting it settle quietly into her core.
"Good to know," Kara said casually.
"I like my brain right where it is."
Number Five turned on her heel and began walking down the wide central aisle of petrified wood with her midnight-silk robes sweeping silently over the polished slate tiles.
Kara strolled beside her with her hands tucked loosely into her coat pockets and her half-lidded eyes casually scanning the titles on the massive shelves.
’[Foundational Core Compaction: Third Era]...
[The Seven Calamities of the Rift]...
[Theoretical Principles of Void-Conductive Metals]...’

’Rowenna would literally sell her left kidney to spend an hour in this room,’ Silas thought, thoroughly amused. ’She’d probably chain herself to a bookshelf and refuse to leave until they dragged her out with a winch.’
Rowenna really did want to study a lot, according to what Reina was telling him, Rowenna was reading the most books in the Library.
After navigating through three rings of towering shelves, they arrived at a massive circular reception rotunda.
At the center of the rotunda sat an enormous high-backed service counter carved from a single polished slab of fossilized dragon-bone.
It stood nearly six feet high, looming like an ancient fortress wall and mounted on the center of the bone counter was a small ornate brass service bell.
Number Five stopped in front of the counter.
Standing barely five feet tall in her heavy robes, the counter came up past her shoulders.
She stood on the tips of her soft leather boots, stretching her slender neck and extending her silk-draped right arm, straining with all her might to reach the tiny brass button on top of the bell.
Her fingertips grazed the cold metal...
SWOOSH!
With a mocking hiss, the brass bell slid backward across the dragon-bone counter by exactly one meter, stopping just out of her reach!
Number Five froze as her arm remained outstretched in mid-air with her porcelain-masked face stared at the retreating bell for two long agonizing seconds.
Kara let out a low amused snicker, leaning against the edge of the desk.
"Need a hand, short stuff?" Kara offered, smirking.
"I can pick you up by the scruff of your robe if you want."
Number Five slowly lowered her arm with her shoulders dropping into a posture of pure exasperation.
"I do not require your assistance," Number Five muttered, her muffled voice dripping with cold murderous venom.
She took a sharp breath, glaring at the empty space behind the counter.
"Musvi, you ancient festering parasite," Number Five cursed, her voice rising into an irritated rasp.
"Get out here before I dismantle your precious card catalog and burn your petrified shelves for firewood..."
"Aiya!
Such hostility from little Number Five!"
POP!
With a soft swirl of pale violet smoke, a man materialized behind the dragon-bone counter.
He leaned forward, resting both elbows on the polished bone, offering them an energetic flamboyant wave.

He was dressed in immaculate midnight-silk robes that mirrored the World Council Heads, but instead of the featureless white porcelain mask worn by the others, his mask was painted with an enormous comical smiling theater grin, accented by exaggerated red cheeks and spiraling golden eyebrows.
"You wound me, little sister!" the man exclaimed, his voice carrying the lively melodic voice of a wandering bard.
"A gentleman spends four hundred years dusting ancient tomes in the dark, and this is the reception he receives?...
No ’Good morning, Musvi’?
No ’How are your aching joints, Musvi’?...
Truly, the youth of the modern council have zero appreciation for classical hospitality!"
’Modern council, what the hell is he talking about?’
He turned his theatrical mask toward Kara, leaning his head to the side.
"And who is this delightful young lady standing in my humble reading room?" Musvi asked, his masked smile practically beaming.
"My, my... look at that posture.
Look at that glorious untamed power humming beneath the skin.
You must be the famous Kara White!
The wild girl from Blessed Land who made the mighty King swallow his own teeth in the assembly!"
Kara narrowed her eyes, studying the man before her.
’He’s strong,’ Silas analyzed instantly with a sharp quiet warning bell chiming behind his ribs.
On the surface, Musvi acted like an eccentric retired librarian, but beneath that painted wooden theater mask, Silas could feel the deep unfathomable ocean of a High-Tier Lord.
Yet there was something deeply strange about his core circulation.
It felt sluggish... it was not weak, but dormant instead, like an engine that had been deliberately geared down to run on low power for centuries.
Musvi caught her intense stare and let out a dramatic high-pitched gasp, clutching his chest with both hands.
"Oh my!" Musvi squeaked, taking a step backward.
"Please, Lord White, do not look at an old man with such intensity!
I am a fragile delicate scholar!
My heart cannot handle the fiery gaze of a youthful Gold Core!
If you fall in love with me, little Number Five will become terribly jealous, and we simply do not have the budget for domestic disputes in the archive!"
Kara blinked with an incredulous smirk pulling at her lips.
"Are you always this annoying, or is today a special occasion?"
"Every day is a special occasion when you live under miles of granite, my dear!" Musvi winked from behind his wooden eyeholes.
Number Five let out a heavy suffering sigh that sounded like it had been building up for three centuries.
"Enough garbage, Musvi," Number Five said, her voice dry as dust.
"By imperial decree of the King and the High Council, the Lord of Blessed Land has been granted authorization to enter the World Vault and claim five ancestral artifacts so produce the master key."
"Oho!" Musvi’s painted eyebrows seemed to gleam with genuine excitement.
"The World Vault?!
A customer for the deep sanctum?!
Splendid!
Marvelous!
It has been three hundred and eighty years since someone walked through those iron gates...
Oh, the dust down there is magnificent and the cobwebs are practically historical monuments—"
"Hold on," Kara interrupted, leaning her hip against the dragon-bone counter.
Musvi paused mid-gesture.
"Yes, my fierce warrior maiden?"
"Before we go wandering into the spooky basement," Kara said, holding out her right hand with an open palm, "I want my other assets delivered...
The King signed off on the full package so where are my Hero Summoning Tickets and my Troop Summoning Tickets?"

chapters.title: Chapter 591: Limited Stock? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Number Five closed her eyes behind her mask, pinching the bridge of her nose beneath her midnight-silk hood.
"Ah! Business before pleasure! A woman after my own practical heart!" Musvi cheered, clapping his hands together with a sharp clap.
"Right away, Lord White! One moment please!"
Musvi turned around, humming a cheerful out-of-tune folk melody as he began rummaging through the towering dark-wood shelves behind the counter.

He dragged a rolling ladder across the polished floor with a loud rhythmic clack-clack-clack, reached up to the highest alcove, and pulled down a heavy dust-covered chest carved from tarnished silver.
He dropped the chest onto the dragon-bone counter with a dull heavy thud as a small cloud of gray dust erupted from the lid, making Number Five cough softly behind her porcelain mask.
Musvi rubbed his hands together, his painted theater grin gleaming under the ceiling crystals.
"Let’s see here... administrative allocation... military reserves... ah, yes!"
With a series of rapid rhythmic flicks of his wrists, Musvi began dealing out thick metallic cards across the counter like a blackjack dealer in a high-stakes casino.
SNAP! SNAP! SNAP!
The cards were forged from an ancient alloy, each one etched with glowing complex summoning runes.
Musvi gathered them into two neat precise stacks, squared the edges with a satisfying tap and pushed them across the bone counter toward Kara.
"Tada!" Musvi announced proudly, spreading his arms wide with a flourish. "Your official recruitment allocation, certified by the World Council’s archive!"
Kara looked down at the two piles and she blinked.
She looked closer then she slowly picked up the smaller stack, fanning the cards out between her fingers.
There were four.
...Exactly four golden Hero Summoning Cards.
She turned her gaze to the larger stack. It was roughly three inches thick and she counted the edges with her thumb.
One hundred and fifty... There were one hundred and fifty silver Troop Summoning Cards.
Silence hung over the fossilized dragon-bone counter for three long agonizing seconds.
’Huh?’
Musvi stood behind the desk, his head tilted at an innocent ninety-degree angle with his painted smile looking wide and vacant.
Beside them, Number Five kept her hands tucked deep into her sleeves, staring fixedly at the floor tiles as if suddenly discovering a profound spiritual truth in the grout.
Kara’s left eyelid began to twitch as a deep terrifying vein pulsed along her forehead.
"Musvi," Kara said, her voice dropping into a low vibrating growl that made the brass service bell tremble.
"Yes, my lovely conqueror?"
"What..." Kara began, lifting the four golden cards between her thumb and forefinger, "...in the unholy hell is this?"
Musvi blinked through his wooden mask.
"Those are your cards, Lord White! Top-tier craftsmanship too!"

"I asked for a hundred Hero Summoning Tickets!" Kara yelled, her composure completely shattering as she slammed her palm down onto the counter with a concussive bang. "I asked for tens of thousands of Troop Summoning Tickets! Why the hell are there four?! Why are there only a hundred and fifty troops?! What is this pathetic little deck of cards?!"
She threw her hands up, turning a furious incredulous glare toward Number Five.

"You are the bloody World Council!" Kara roared, her voice echoing through the endless labyrinth of ancient bookshelves. "You rule nine superpowers and you hoard the continental wealth of an entire planet so how in the seven hells is this the entirety of your stock?! Are you running a global empire or a failing pawn shop in the lower slums?!"
Musvi paused.
He slowly lowered his arms, tapping his painted chin with a thoughtful wooden finger.

"Well, you see, Lord White..." Musvi explained, his voice sounding unbothered and carrying a soft apologetic lilt. "...to be completely technically accurate, the last time the World Council’s reserves were refilled was roughly four hundred and twenty years ago."
Kara stared at him, her jaw slack. "Four hundred years?"

"Four hundred and twenty, give or take a winter!" Musvi nodded brightly. "You must understand the historical context, my dear! When the rifts opened during the First Apocalypse, humanity was fighting for its survival... Every house, every legion, and every Lord burned through Summoning Tickets like dry kindling in a furnace! Millions of troops were summoned! Hundreds of legendary heroes were deployed to hold the defensive perimeters! By the time the borders stabilized and the modern Nine Powers were established... well, the terrestrial supply was practically exhausted!"
Musvi leaned forward over the counter, lowering his voice into a conspiratorial whisper that held zero actual secrecy.

"If you truly desire thousands of high-tier Troop Tickets and hundreds of legendary Hero Summons, Lord White, you shouldn’t be digging around in this dusty basement... You need to head straight to Central City in the Sovereign Realm! That is where the true treasuries are anchored!"
He gave another dramatic wink from behind his painted eyeholes.

"In fact," Musvi added cheerfully, "when you eventually visit Central City, you should definitely pay a visit to the Grand Silver Bazaar... You might even run into my lovely daughter! She manages a high-tier trading consortium out there, she’s a wonderful girl and very sharp too while being excellent with numbers... Though, to be fair, I haven’t seen her in three hundred years, so who knows? She might have six children and a fleet of void-caravans by now! Time flies when you’re reading books, doesn’t it?"
Kara stood frozen in front of the counter, holding the four golden cards in her hand, staring at the cheerful masked lunatic before her.
For the first time since she had walked into the Citadel, the terrifying Lord of Blessed Land was completely speechless.
’I... I... I don’t know what to say.’
Kara stared down at the polished fossilized bone counter with her dark eyes completely fixed on the pathetic insulting stacks of metallic cards resting under the amber lamplight.
It felt like an insult to her status... One hundred and fifty silver Troop Summoning Cards and Four golden Hero Summoning Cards?

’Four,’ Silas repeated to himself in the quiet, smoldering privacy of his own soul. ’Four bloody cards... what was supposedly a grand allocation from the supreme rulers of nine global superpowers, and it looks like the leftover stock from a clearance bin in a dying border outpost.’
Beside her, Number Five remained standing in silence with her small hands tucked away inside the cavernous midnight-silk folds of her sleeves.
The featureless white porcelain mask gave away nothing, but the subtle, stiff rigidity of her shoulders betrayed an exhaustion that transcended mortal lifespans.
Across the six-foot-tall dragon-bone counter, Musvi’s painted wooden theater mask was tilted at that exact same bright, cheerful ninety-degree angle.
His red-painted wooden cheeks gleamed beneath the glowing crystals overhead, his oversized carved theater grin wider than a crescent moon.
Kara slowly pinched the bridge of her nose with her single right hand, letting out a long heavy hiss of air through her teeth that rattled the brass paperweights on the desk.
"Musvi," Kara said, her voice dropping into a dry tone that practically dripped with venom.
"At your service, my glorious, broad-shouldered conqueror!" Musvi chirped, leaning both elbows onto the bone counter with an eager flourish.
’What’s with all these names?’

"Let me get this straight," Kara continued, gesturing with her single hand toward the cards. "Again, you’re telling me the World Council, the supreme all-powerful governing body that levies continental taxes on billions of living souls, hoards pre-calamity relics, and struts around the Citadel like gods among insects, is running a military reserve with four Hero Tickets?"
"Yes!" Musvi nodded. "It’s been quite a while since they restocked me though, since the third centur—"

"I don’t give a damn about the third century, you fossilized clown," Kara scoffed, leaning her hip against the counter with a heavy scowl. "I have an entire territory to build... I have walls to raise, watchtowers to garrison, and farmsteads to secure. Furthermore, Blessed Land is situated out in the middle of nowhere. It’s miles away from the established trade corridors, tucked into an isolated valley that doesn’t even appear on the Council’s primary survey maps... How am I supposed to reach the core markets with four heroes and a hundred and fifty footmen? Am I supposed to march them across three mountain ranges on foot every time I need a bag of salt?"
Musvi blinked through the dark circular eyeholes of his mask.

"Oh!" he gasped, striking his open palm with a wooden fist with a sharp sound. "Why didn’t you say so, my dear?! You’re talking about spatial spells right?! You need an anchored bridge! Something that can fold the dimensional threshold and link your private territory sanctuary directly to Central City in the Sovereign Realm!"
’Oh... He has that?’
Kara raised an eyebrow, crossing her single arm over her chest.
"Yeah. Exactly that. Don’t tell me you ran out of those four hundred years ago too."

"Perish the thought!" Musvi beamed, his voice rising into an excited operatic crescendo. "An anchored threshold gate is a staple of high-tier infrastructure! A delicate matter of dimensional power, yes, but nothing an archivist of my peerless caliber cannot unearth! Give me ten seconds... no, eight seconds! Do not blink, Lord White!"
SWOOSH!
Before Kara’s eyes could even track the displacement, Musvi vanished.
There was no crackle of lightning, no displacement of air and no lingering whiff of ozone or vibration of mana as well.
He didn’t slip into the shadows or step through a spatial tear either.
One second he was leaning against the fossilized dragon-bone, and the next, the space behind the counter was vacant making Kara’s dark eyes narrow into cold razor-thin slits.
Her internal senses flared.

Behind the placid exterior of Kara White, Silas pushed his spiritual perception outward, sending an invisible microscopic web of high-frequency vibrational mana sweeping through the cavernous rotunda.
He swept the floor, the vaulted stone rafters fifty feet above, the towering bookshelves of petrified wood, and the shadowed corridors radiating into the archive.
...Nothing.
There was not a trace... It was as if Musvi had never existed in physical reality to begin with.
’What kind of movement technique is that?’ Silas analyzed, a quiet chill settling behind his ribs. ’Even with a Gold Core’s sensing, I can’t track a single thread of his wake.’
Beside her, Number Five let out a heavy suffering groan that sounded like rusty hinges scraping together.
"Every single time," the short woman muttered, her muffled voice dripping with disgust. "Every single time an outsider arrives, he puts on that ridiculous minstrel routine..."
She turned away from the high counter, her midnight-silk robes dragging across the polished slate floor.

Spotting a small ornate wooden armchair tucked into a quiet alcove near the primary bookshelf, Number Five walked over, turned around, and casually allowed her weight to drop backward onto the velvet cushion.
WHOOSH!
There was no chair.
The moment her rear met the carved mahogany armrests, the entire seat dissolved into a faint swirling wisp of lavender mist!
Number Five’s center of gravity betrayed her instantly.
Her legs kicked out beneath her robes, and she plummeted straight down with her backside slamming hard onto the unforgiving stone floor with a hollow thud.
BANG!

"Agh, damn it all to the void!" Number Five cursed loudly, her porcelain mask tilting straight toward the vaulted ceiling as her small fists slammed into the floor tiles. "May your ancient soul rot in the deepest trench of the rift, you miserable moldy old bastard!"
Kara leaned her back against the bone counter, biting the inside of her cheek to keep from laughing out loud.
"Nice landing," Kara remarked, looking down at the heap of midnight-silk. "Real majestic for a World Council Head..."
Number Five slowly pushed herself upright, brushing invisible dust from her skirts with violent jerky motions of her wrists.
She didn’t bother looking for another chair as she simply stood there in the center of the aisle, her small frame practically trembling with frustrated rage.

"It is an illusion spell, or you could say something beyond that..." Number Five snapped, her voice tight and breathy beneath the porcelain. "Musvi does not move through physical space like a normal mortal. The entire foundational structure of this grand library is an external manifestation of his domain so his flesh and the petrified dark-wood are synchronized at a conceptual level... Once he steps away from that counter, he moves across these shelves like an incorporeal wraith... He is everywhere and nowhere simultaneously so unless he deliberately anchors his mass to speak to you, not even the World King could locate him with a direct divination strike."
"I see..." Kara murmured, letting her gaze wander back across the endless curving rows of towering bookshelves as a quiet sobering realization settled into Silas’s thoughts.
The world was vast.
...It was disgustingly and terrifyingly vast.
Back in Sector Forty-Four, it had been easy to feel invincible.
Crushing Devan Varma into the star-iron floor, shattering the nobles, hell even threatening Vanderbilt Senior while eating... it was intoxicating.

But watching Musvi dissolve into thin air and listening to Number Five speak of domain synchronizations served as a blunt cold reminder... The only reason he was standing in this room, dictating terms and stuffing his pockets with billions, was because of the Gold Core.

She turned away from the high counter, her midnight-silk robes dragging across the polished slate floor.

Spotting a small ornate wooden armchair tucked into a quiet alcove near the primary bookshelf, Number Five walked over, turned around, and casually allowed her weight to drop backward onto the velvet cushion.
WHOOSH!
There was no chair.
The moment her rear met the carved mahogany armrests, the entire seat dissolved into a faint swirling wisp of lavender mist!
Number Five’s center of gravity betrayed her instantly.
Her legs kicked out beneath her robes, and she plummeted straight down with her backside slamming hard onto the unforgiving stone floor with a hollow thud.
BANG!
"Agh, damn it all to the void!" Number Five cursed loudly, her porcelain mask tilting straight toward the vaulted ceiling as her small fists slammed into the floor tiles.
"May your ancient soul rot in the deepest trench of the rift, you miserable moldy old bastard!"
Kara leaned her back against the bone counter, biting the inside of her cheek to keep from laughing out loud.
"Nice landing," Kara remarked, looking down at the heap of midnight-silk.
"Real majestic for a World Council Head..."
Number Five slowly pushed herself upright, brushing invisible dust from her skirts with violent jerky motions of her wrists.
She didn’t bother looking for another chair as she simply stood there in the center of the aisle, her small frame practically trembling with frustrated rage.
"It is an illusion spell, or you could say something beyond that..." Number Five snapped, her voice tight and breathy beneath the porcelain.
"Musvi does not move through physical space like a normal mortal.
The entire foundational structure of this grand library is an external manifestation of his domain so his flesh and the petrified dark-wood are synchronized at a conceptual level...
Once he steps away from that counter, he moves across these shelves like an incorporeal wraith...
He is everywhere and nowhere simultaneously so unless he deliberately anchors his mass to speak to you, not even the World King could locate him with a direct divination strike."
"I see..." Kara murmured, letting her gaze wander back across the endless curving rows of towering bookshelves as a quiet sobering realization settled into Silas’s thoughts.
The world was vast.
...It was disgustingly and terrifyingly vast.
Back in Sector Forty-Four, it had been easy to feel invincible.
Crushing Devan Varma into the star-iron floor, shattering the nobles, hell even threatening Vanderbilt Senior while eating... it was intoxicating.
But watching Musvi dissolve into thin air and listening to Number Five speak of domain synchronizations served as a blunt cold reminder...
The only reason he was standing in this room, dictating terms and stuffing his pockets with billions, was because of the Gold Core.

chapters.title: Chapter 592: The Key To The Vault [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’If I were still just Silas Graves, a commoner even if I was wearing an expensive suit, they wouldn’t have negotiated for three seconds,’ he mused, his jaw setting firmly beneath his skin. ’They would have dragged me into a white room, pinned my limbs to a dissection slab with suppression nails, and picked my brain apart to steal the glove schematics. I’m only alive because they think I’m a divine monster they can’t afford to fight...’
A slow sharp smirk pulled at the corner of Kara’s lips.𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
’Which means I just have to milk this position for every single scrap of meat on the bone... If they think I’m an unhinged greedy monster, I might as well play the part to perfection.’
As if sensing the sudden shift in the air, Number Five’s posture stiffened.
She turned her featureless mask toward Kara with her small head cocking to the side as a visible shudder rippled through her midnight-silk robes.

"Why..." Number Five muttered, her muffled voice sounding distinctly uneasy, "...did the temperature just drop by four degrees? What horrific extortionist plot are you conjuring behind those eyes now, Lord White?"

"Who, me?" Kara gasped, holding her single right hand to her chest in mock innocence. "I’m just a simple humble slum girl admiring your lovely interior decorating. I wouldn’t dream of plotting anything..."
"You are a plague," Number Five stated with flat certainty.
POP!
A puff of lavender smoke billowed across the dragon-bone counter, accompanied by a bright cheerful humming noise.
Musvi reappeared exactly where he had been standing before, leaning forward with his elbows on the bone, holding a flat rectangular slab of dark stone between his palms.
"I have returned!" Musvi announced joyfully.
He glanced past Kara, his painted wooden eyes locking onto the small woman standing in the aisle.

"Oh, little Five! Did you enjoy the velvet cushion? I had it woven from primeval nightmare-silk! Remarkably soft, isn’t it? Though it seems your posture hasn’t improved... Still as delightfully compact as a garden gnome, I see!"

"I am going to murder you," Number Five hissed, taking two rapid furious strides toward the counter. "I swear on the First Founder’s tomb, Musvi, I will sever your vocal cords and feed them to the sewer drakes!"
She reached the counter and tried to plant her boots on the stone trim to hoist herself up, but her limbs were simply too short.
She hopped twice with her small fingers clawing uselessly at the polished fossilized edge and her robes tangling around her ankles as she failed to gain an inch of height.

"Aiya! Look at those little hops!" Musvi laughed, clapping his hands together like an amused parent at a festival. "Magnificent form! Splendid verticality! Truly the most adorable Council Head in the last three centuries!"
FSSSSSH!
Number Five froze mid-hop and she slowly lowered her arms.
’Ah, what’s she going to do?’

Number Five didn’t yell and she didn’t curse either. The woman simply turned her entire body around, walked stiffly over to the nearest wall of petrified dark-wood, planted her nose three inches from the polished bark, and stood there in dead silence, facing the corner like a pouting child sent to time-out.
Kara couldn’t take it anymore.
"Pfft, hah!"
A loud sharp bark of laughter escaped Kara’s throat, echoing across the quiet rotunda.
She’d spent the entire morning assuming the World Council Heads were ancient soulless automatons carved from ice and cruelty.

To see the legendary Number Five, a woman capable of bending the assembly chamber with pure spiritual pressure, standing in a corner facing the wall because she couldn’t jump onto a desk was nothing short of cinematic gold.
’They really do have distinct personalities,’ Silas thought, shaking his head with genuine amusement. ’Ancient beings, but still hilariously human under those porcelain shells.’
Musvi cleared his throat, tapping the stone slab against the counter with a rhythmic TOC-TOC-TOC.
"Now then, back to serious business!" Musvi declared, pushing the slab across the bone surface toward Kara. "Take a look at this, Lord White."
Kara stepped forward, picking up the object with her right hand.
It was roughly the size and thickness of an architectural floor tile, carved from a dense midnight-black basalt that felt surprisingly warm to the touch.
Etched into its face was an intricate circular array of silver and violet lines, spatial coordinates woven into a microscopic interlocking geometric mandala that hummed with a deep ringing sound.

"A Space Anchor," Musvi explained. "Crafted during the zenith of the Second Era... If you take this tile, carry it back to your territory in Blessed Land, and embed it into the foundational bedrock of your central keep, it will forge a permanent stable dimensional corridor directly between your personal grounds and the Grand Plaza of Central City in the Sovereign Realm."
Kara raised an eyebrow, turning the heavy tile over in her palm.
The underside was smooth, marked only by a single stylized crest depicting a soaring hawk clutching a compass.

"How old is this thing?" Kara asked skeptically. "When was it last calibrated? I don’t feel like stepping onto a teleporter in my living room and having my torso materialize inside a solid granite mountain three hundred miles off-target..."

"Completely fresh! Practically straight out of the forge!" Musvi waved a hand dismissively. "It was crafted barely four hundred years ago! In sovereign terms, the ink is still wet! Why, several active lords utilize this exact model for their territory... Take Lord Sky, for instance!"
Kara paused, her fingers tightening around the edge of the basalt tile.
"Lord Sky?" she echoed, keeping her voice completely neutral, though Silas’s internal focus sharpened like a needle.

"Indeed!" Musvi nodded brightly. "The reclusive Lord Sky maintains an identical anchor stone embedded within his primary redoubt... It allows him to transport himself, his high-tier retainers, and cargo crates between his territory and Central City at a moment’s notice as well as his whole territory. Furthermore, he possesses a secondary mobile one, a special stone that allows him to execute randomized spatial leaps across uncharted territorial jurisdictions within a three-thousand-league radius."
Musvi leaned forward, his painted grin gleaming in the crystal light.

"That is precisely how Lord Sky manages to locate so many isolated territories, you see! That adventurous fellow spends half his time tumbling through dimensional blind spots and Unknown Zones far outside Central City’s jurisdiction! That is how he stumbled upon Blessed Land in the first place, if I recall the scouting logs correctly!"
’Huh...’ Silas mused internally, a sudden wave of understanding washing over him.
For a while he’d privately wondered how Evelyn had managed to stumble across his territory in the Umbral Basin.
The basin was an inhospitable mana-corroded wasteland surrounded by territorial anomalies.
It had seemed almost absurdly coincidental that another lord had simply wandered into his backyard.
Now the pieces fit together seamlessly.
Evelyn wasn’t just wandering... she was utilizing high-tier space anchors to skip across the dimensional fabric like a flat stone skipping over a lake.
’Being Lord Sky is definitely not an easy job,’ Silas thought with a faint sympathetic wince.
Skipping through uncharted territories meant constantly dropping head-first into hostile beast dens, unstable spatial rifts, and territories with Lords.

’I can see why she was taking her vacation so seriously back in my place. The poor girl is probably running on pure caffeine and adrenaline half the time... The second she resumes her duties, she’s going to be worked to the bone again.’
He made a quiet mental note.
’When I get back, I’ll order what she likes... She’s definitely earned them.’
Kara slipped the heavy basalt anchor tile into her inner coat pocket, letting it rest beside her pink mobile phone.
"Thanks for the tip, Musvi," Kara said, offering him a casual nod. "I’ll make good use of it."
"Always a pleasure to assist a rising star!" Musvi chirped.
In the corner of the room, Number Five slowly turned around.
She pushed herself away from the petrified wood with her hands vanishing back into her midnight-silk sleeves as she strode back toward the counter with stiff dignified grace.

"The preliminaries are settled," Number Five said, her voice completely lacking of its earlier rage, masked once more beneath thick imperial frost. "Produce the master key, Musvi... The assembly is waiting for our return, and I have zero desire to spend another minute in this dusty hole."
"Ah, the key! Of course, of course!"

Musvi reached into the deep voluminous pocket of his embroidered robe, rummaging through an assortment of rattling objects... loose brass cogs, dried paper scraps, a half-eaten candied plum, and a tiny silver magnifying glass... before finally withdrawing an ornate heavy key.
It was roughly nine inches long, forged from an iridescent dark-violet metal that seemed to absorb the ambient light around it.

The shaft was twisted like the horn of an ancient ram, and the teeth were not simple notches, but miniature interlocking clockwork gears that continuously rotated on their own with a small rhythmic ticking sound.
TICK-TICK-TICK!
Musvi held the key up, letting the violet metal catch the crystal glare, before lowering it toward Number Five.

"Here you are, my tiny terrifying Council member," Musvi teased, his painted eyebrows arching playfully. "Do try not to drop it... If it falls into a crack in the floor, you might need a step-ladder to fish it out."
Number Five snatched the key from his wooden fingers with a violent snapping motion of her wrist, quickly tucking it into her sleeve before she could be tempted to plunge it into his throat.
"May your teeth fall out one by one," Number Five muttered under her breath.
Musvi only laughed, offering them both a deep bow from behind the counter, sweeping his silk sleeves so wide they brushed the floor tiles.

"Safe travels into the deep dark, ladies!" Musvi called out, his voice echoing off the vaulted ceilings. "And Lord White... a word of professional advice from an old tired curator who has watched generations turn to dust."
Kara paused, glancing back at the painted wooden mask.

"If you should venture into the deepest forgotten alcoves of the vault..." Musvi said, his voice suddenly dropping its clownish lilt, carrying a strange hollow weight that sent a genuine shiver through the rotunda, "...do not listen to the voices in the stone. Do not answer them and above all else, do not agree to whatever bargains they whisper through the dark."
Kara blinked, her brow furrowing slightly.
"Voices? What kind of voic—"
PING!
Before she could finish the syllable, the world violently fractured and this time, it wasn’t just the gentle sliding transition of standard teleportation.
It was a brutal vertical spatial drop!
The library, the petrified bookshelves, the bone counter, and Musvi’s painted theater grin were violently ripped away in an instantaneous blur of black and violet light.
The crushing gravitational acceleration hammered down onto Kara’s skull like an iron weight, forcing a sharp breath from her lungs as her vision warped into rings of static.
WHAM!
Her boots hit cold unforgiving stone and the air here was completely different.
It was freezing, so cold that Kara’s breath plumed into thick white clouds the moment it left her lips but far worse than the cold was the pressure.
It was an immense crushing weight that pressed against the eardrums, made the teeth ache, and settled across the shoulders like a lead blanket.
Kara reflexively nudged her internal mana, preparing to unfurl her perception to map the perimeter once more.
"Do not."
Number Five’s voice cut through the dark, cold and sharp as chipped obsidian.
Kara looked down.
The short woman was standing beside her, holding the iridescent violet key in her right hand, her heavy midnight-silk robes pulled tight against the biting chill.

"We are miles beneath the continental shelf," Number Five explained, her muffled voice sounding very flat. "The volume of oceanic water pressing down upon the bedrock above our heads is calculated in billions of metric tons... This entire chamber is suspended within a stabilized pressure-bubble but if you push your Gold Core mana into the surrounding stone, the power will disrupt the external equilibrium arrays... The water will not merely flood this corridor, it will hammer through these walls with the kinetic force of a falling moon, vaporizing both of us into biological pulp before you can even form an incantation."
Kara let out a low whistle, pulling her senses back into the core behind her sternum.
"A simple ’keep your hands to yourself’ would have sufficed," Kara drawled dryly.
"With you, Lord White, nothing simple ever suffices," Number Five replied, turning away and marching forward into the gloom.
Kara followed half a step behind, her single right hand tucked into her coat pocket with her boots clicking softly against the dark flagstones.
The corridor was narrow, barely wide enough for two people to walk abreast, carved directly out of solid seamless black basalt that bore no tool marks.
Glowing pale runes, ancient, fading, and written in a dialect that predated the modern Nine Powers by centuries, flickered along the baseboards, casting long eerie shadows across their path.
After thirty paces, the corridor terminated at an enormous terrifying barrier.

chapters.title: Chapter 593: Trash Items [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It was a colossal circular vault door, spanning nearly thirty feet in diameter, set deep into the surrounding mountain of black stone.
It looked less like an entrance to a treasury and more like the primary blast gate of an ancient planetary bunker.

The face of the door was forged from solid lightless void-iron, completely seamless, save for thousands of glowing white runes that twisted across its surface in a massive slowly rotating labyrinth of runic geometry.
At the exact center of the wheel sat an intricate star-shaped keyhole surrounded by three rings of rotating mechanical tumblers.
Kara stopped three paces back, tilting her head up to study the immense structure.
"Imposing," Kara commented, her eyes tracing the intricate flow of mana through the white runes. "Looks like something built to survive an asteroid strike."
"It has survived far worse than that," Number Five said softly, stopping directly before the central mechanism.
She turned slightly, looking back at Kara through the eyeholes of her porcelain mask.

"The World Vault was not designed to keep out common thieves or opportunistic scions..." the woman explained, her tone dropping into a grave solemn tone. "It was constructed to contain artifacts so volatile, so fundamentally hazardous to terrestrial reality, that even the World Council dares not unleash them upon the surface... The outer barrier is woven with high-tier countermeasures."
To illustrate her point, Number Five raised her left arm but she didn’t use mana and she didn’t channel a defensive shroud as well.
She simply extended her open left palm forward, casually pressing her bare unadorned fingertips against the surface of the void-iron door.
SNAP!
There was no sound of a spell firing.
SPLAT-CRUNCH!
In the span of a single horrifying microsecond, Number Five’s entire left hand, from the tips of her slender fingers all the way up to the middle of her forearm, violently ceased to exist.

The flesh, the muscle tissue, the marrow, and the skeletal bones detonated outward in an instantaneous shower of dark crimson blood, severed tendon, and pulverized bone fragments that splattered violently across the black flagstones.
Kara’s eyes widened slightly with her boots remaining firmly rooted, though Silas’s internal reflexes screamed at the sudden violence however Number Five did not flinch.
Hell she didn’t even let out a grunt of pain.
WHOOSH!
A faint pale crimson luminescence sparked from the severed stump of her left arm and in the blink of an eye, the blood vanished.

New marrow shot outward like growing crystal, fresh white bone knitted together with rapid sickening clicks, crimson muscle fibers braided over the skeletal frame like living thread, and pale flawless skin sealed over the flesh with a soft clean pop.
Within two seconds, her left hand was completely restored looking pale and undamaged.
She flexed her fingers once then twice, before pulling them back inside her silk sleeve.

"The peripheral wards," Number Five said calmly, as if she had just brushed a fly off her shoulder, "are keyed to spatial rejection... If any living entity attempts to force entry without the verified master key, the barrier does not repel them. It just unravels the physical matter of whatever touches the surface and should an intruder manage to breach the secondary mechanical seals through brute force..."
She paused, gesturing toward the slowly rotating white runes.

"...the entire internal core of the door is permanently saturated with the ancient concept of Destruction... The same absolute authority wielded by the World King. It will not merely destroy the physical body, it will obliterate the soul, erasing the trespasser’s existence from the dimensional record entirely."
Kara stared at the pristine void-iron door, then glanced down at the woman’s newly regenerated hand.
"Good to know," Kara muttered, crossing her single arm over her chest. "Remind me not to lean on the walls."
Number Five turned back to the center of the door.
She reached into her sleeve, withdrawing the nine-inch iridescent violet key.
With steady precision, she slid the twisting clockwork shaft deep into the star-shaped keyhole at the center of the rotating tumblers.
CLINK!
The key slid in to the hilt without the slightest resistance.
Number Five grasped the ornate horn-shaped bow with both hands, planting her boots wide on the flagstones, and slowly rotated the key a quarter-turn to the right.
TICK-TICK-TICK-TICK... CLACK!
A deafening chime resonated from deep within the void-iron!
The thousands of glowing white runes across the thirty-foot face violently flared with their light shifting from stark white to a deep smoldering gold.
The three rings of mechanical tumblers began to spin in opposing directions, grinding together with the earth-shattering roar of an industrial forge.
RUMBLE-CRUNCH!
Deep within the bedrock, massive counterweights shifted.
Hydraulic seals released with a colossal pressurized hiss that blasted a freezing cloud of dry nitrogen across their shins.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞
HSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!

The massive circular door slowly unlocked, splitting down the center along an invisible jagged seam, and retreated backward into the stone walls with the agonizing ponderous weight of a shifting tectonic plate.
Number Five withdrew the key, tucking it away, and gestured toward the gaping dark threshold.
"Enter, Lord of Blessed Land," Number Five commanded softly. "Welcome to the World Vault..."
Kara stepped across the threshold.
THUD-CLANG!
The second her rear boot cleared the entryway, the massive void-iron doors slammed shut behind them with a cataclysmic deafening roar.
BOOM!
The locking tumblers spun instantly into place with the golden runes shifting back to cold lethal white, sealing them completely inside the subterranean depths but Kara didn’t look back.
She stood at the edge of a massive elevated stone observation balcony, looking out over the expanse before her.
Her breath caught in her throat.
"Well, damn," Kara breathed softly, her half-lidded eyes widening as she drank in the incomprehensible scale of the chamber.
This place simply wasn’t a room... It was an underground continent.
The ceiling arched hundreds of feet overhead, supported by colossal pillars of glowing translucent quartz that cast a soft ethereal azure luminescence across the entire expanse.
The air was dead quiet and preserved under a stasis spell that suspended the decay of time itself.

Stretching out from the base of the balcony, extending far beyond the horizon of the azure light, were endless straight rows of massive star-iron shelving units, glass display pedestals, and sealed stasis vaults.
Each row was broad enough to drive three war chariots abreast, flanked by towering banners of tattered ancient silk bearing imperial crests from long-dead dynasties.
Carved into the black stone flagstones at the entrance of each corridor was a glowing runic numeral.
Kara glanced down at the nearest aisle markers.
[Aisle 1. Aisle 2. Aisle 3.]
Her dark eyes drifted along the endless curving perspective lines, tracking the numbers into the distant blue-lit gloom.
[...Aisle 496. Aisle 497. Aisle 498.]
Kara’s eyelid gave a tiny involuntary twitch.
"That’s a shit ton of stuff," Kara muttered, completely abandoning any pretense of eloquence.
Number Five stepped up beside her on the balcony, leaning her small forearms against the carved stone balustrade with a long world-weary sigh.

"Four hundred and ninety-eight primary aisles," Number Five confirmed, her voice muffled and dry beneath the porcelain mask. "Containing roughly eighty-four thousand cataloged artifacts, reliquaries, ancestral armaments, and forbidden treatises salvaged from the First and Second Eras... It is an administrative nightmare of catastrophic proportions as the sorting manifests alone span three hundred volumes of paper, and half of the original scribes were executed for treason before they finished cross-referencing the fourth wing."
She turned her featureless mask toward Kara.

"I will act as your guide," Number Five said flatly. "I have walked these aisles for centuries so I know the inventory of this vault better than the living monarchs know their own treasuries... If you wander through these corridors unassisted, you will waste three weeks simply reading the identifying plaques."
Kara glanced down at the short woman with a skeptical tilt to her lips.

’Four hundred and ninety-eight aisles...’ Silas thought, genuinely impressed despite himself. ’And an aisle isn’t just a shelf... it’s an entire section packed with vaults, pedestals, and containment alcoves. To memorize the locations and properties of tens of thousands of classified artifacts... how absurdly good is this woman’s memory?’
"Lead the way, shorty," Kara smiled, gesturing forward with her single right hand. "Show me what humanity has been hoarding in the dark."
They descended the grand stone staircase with their boots clicking rhythmically against the pristine flagstones, stepping into the mouth of the first primary corridor.
The air grew noticeably cooler as they walked.
Number Five led the way with brisk mechanical strides, her midnight-silk robes sweeping gracefully over the stone, pointing out the displays with her left hand as they passed.

"The initial sector, spanning Aisle 1 through Aisle 50, houses relics, administrative ledgers, and standard military armaments produced during the regime of the Second World King," Number Five explained, her cadence returning to that of a dispassionate lecturer. "An era marked by extensive territorial consolidation, centralism, and the initial establishment of the Nine Powers’ sovereign borders..."
Kara glanced down a side corridor with her half-lidded eyes scanning the glass display cases.

Rows of polished silver swords, ornate ceremonial cuirasses, gilded scepters, and stacked bundles of ancient treaties rested under preservation wards, looking as pristine as the day they were placed there.
"What about the First King?" Kara asked, glancing down at the short woman. "Where are the relics from the First King’s regime?"
Number Five paused, her head tilting slightly.

"The First King’s artifacts are housed in the deepest and most restricted sectors of the lower vaults," Number Five replied, her tone dipping into a strange cautious hush. "Beyond Aisle 450... However... remarkably few of the items produced during the First King’s era possess any practical military utility."
Kara raised an eyebrow. "Why? Wasn’t he the apex? The legendary founder who unified humanity during the apocalypse?"

"He was an undisputed genius," Number Five said simply. "A visionary who comprehended the mechanics of the soul and the dimensional threshold far beyond anyone before or since but he was also... catastrophically unhinged."
She gave a small dismissive shake of her head.

"Most of the scrolls and tablets preserved from his private sanctum are nothing more than hundreds of volumes of frantic paranoid ramblings... Speculative treatises on trans-dimensional parasitic entities, incoherent mathematical formulas describing the death of the cosmos, and bizarre mechanical blueprints for devices that have no logical function in this reality... He was so brilliant that his mind operated entirely outside the boundaries of human sanity and the Council preserves them out of historical reverence, but as functional weapons, they are largely useless."
"Fair enough," Kara chuckled. "Genius and madness usually share a bunk."
Number Five stopped abruptly in front of a wide elevated display pedestal lined with black velvet, gesturing toward five distinct objects resting beneath glowing blue containment fields.

"In the interest of efficiency," Number Five said, turning toward Kara, "I have pre-selected five exceptional artifacts from the Second Era. Each represents the pinnacle of standard imperial craftsmanship. If you select these five, we may conclude this transaction within minutes and return to the assembly..."
Kara stepped up to the pedestal, looking down at the offerings.
The moment her gaze locked onto the first object, a translucent runic interface flickered before her eyes, displaying the artifact’s classified registry data:
[Item: Old Spirit Sword]
[Tier]: Tier 2 Weapon (Rare)

[Description]: A high-grade officer’s rapier forged during the mid-Second Era... Quenched in the blood of underground frost-drakes and inlaid with refined silversteel filigree to facilitate rapid mana conduction.
[Durability]: 85 / 100
Kara stared at the sword and she blinked.

’A Tier 2 rapier?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing in sheer disbelief. ’She’s offering me a standard factory-stamped officer’s blade? I have apprentices in the Blessed Land smithy who hammer out better conductive steel before their morning tea...’
She shifted her gaze to the second item on the velvet cloth:
[Item: Bulwark of the Iron Vanguard]
[Tier]: Tier 2 Armor (Rare)
[Description]: A heavy kite shield forged from multi-layered star-iron plating. Engraved with kinetic deflection runes capable of reducing physical concussive force by up to fifteen percent.
[Durability]: 120 / 150

’A heavy shield that reduces force by fifteen percent?’ Kara thought, her left eyelid beginning to twitch with mounting irritation. ’A common boulder from the Umbral Basin has better defensive properties than this piece of scrap metal!’
Well that was a lie but still...
She looked at the third item.
[Item: Amulet of the Starlight Well]
[Tier]: Tier 2 Accessory (Rare)

[Description]: A polished silver pendant set with a low-grade astral quartz. Passively increases the bearer’s natural mana regeneration rate by five percent while resting within an illuminated environment.
[Durability]: 40 / 50

’Five percent mana regeneration... only while resting in the light?’ Silas screamed internally. ’Are you joking?! An apple dipped in sugar water gives a better energy boost than this ridiculous necklace!’
She glared at the fourth item.
[Item: Boots of the Wind-Strider]
[Tier]: Tier 2 Armor (Rare)
[Description]: Supple leather boots reinforced with the tendons of northern prairie deer. Slightly reduces the bearer’s physical fatigue while sprinting across flat, unobstructed terrain.
[Durability]: 60 / 75
And finally, the fifth item.
[Item: Elixir of the Minor Titan]
[Tier]: Tier 2 Consumable (Rare)

[Description]: A concentrated alchemical brew refined from ground earth-wyrm scales. Temporarily increases raw physical musculature by ten percent for a duration of twenty minutes. Induces severe muscle cramping and violent nausea upon expiration.
[Durability]: 1 / 1

Silence descended over the black velvet display pedestal as Kara stood completely motionless with her single right hand resting on her hip and her half-lidded eyes slowly lifting from the five pathetic trinkets to lock dead-center onto Number Five’s porcelain mask.
"Number Five," Kara said, her voice dropping into a low terrifyingly calm tone.
"Yes, Lord White?" Number Five replied, her hands tucked neatly into her sleeves. "Are these not magnificent treasures? The craftsmanship of the Second Era is renowned for its elegance."
"Do I look like an idiot to you?" Kara asked flatly.

chapters.title: Chapter 594: Dawn Blade [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "I could not possibly comment on your personal intellectual capacity—"

"These are hot garbage!" Kara snapped, throwing her hand up in pure furious exasperation. "A rusty kitchen knife, a slab of scrap metal, a shiny pebble, a pair of deer boots, and a bottle of poison that makes you puke your guts out after twenty minutes?! What is this, a garage sale in the lower slums?! You promised me entry to the World Vault, and you’re trying to shove Tier 2 common trash down my throat just so you can go back upstairs and take a nap?!"
Number Five let out a tiny barely audible click of her tongue behind her mask, clearly annoyed that her blatant attempt to dump useless warehouse surplus had failed so miserably.
"The items possess historical significance—" Number Five began stiffly.

"Take your historical significance and throw it into the sea," Kara scoffed, spinning on her heel and marching past the pedestal. "I’m not leaving this vault until I find real power... Move, shorty. We’re going deeper."
Number Five sighed, adjusting the hood of her robes, and hurried along behind her.
They walked for nearly twenty minutes, leaving the orderly polished rows of the early aisles far behind.
As they crossed the threshold of Aisle 20, the architecture of the vault began to subtly shift.
The clean straight lines of petrified wood and polished slate gave way to raw jagged bedrock that seemed to have been violently melted and flash-frozen.
The soft azure illumination of the quartz ceiling thinned, replaced by long creeping shadows that clung to the corners of the massive stone arches.
The pressure in the air grew heavier.
TAP! TAP! TAP!
Their boots echoed loudly through the cavernous gloom as eventually, they entered a colossal circular plaza where Aisle 28 intersected with the central arterial road.
At the center of the plaza, elevated upon a massive three-tiered dais of cracked obsidian, sat a structure that made Kara’s steps abruptly halt.
...It looked like an ancient macabre monument.
Resting in the center of the obsidian platform was a complete humanoid skeleton, bleached bone-white by centuries of dry air.
It sat slumped in a kneeling posture upon the stone, clad in the rotting tattered remnants of what had once been an exquisite tunic of royal-blue silk.
Planted directly through the cracked obsidian floor between the skeleton’s knees was an enormous breathtaking greatsword.
The blade was forged from an ancient incandescent golden metal that seemed to actively bleed sunlight into the surrounding dark.
Intricate undulating solar runes were etched along the broad fuller, humming with a deep radiant heartbeat that warmed the freezing air of the plaza.
Both of the skeleton’s bleached bony hands were clamped firmly around the gold-wrapped hilt, locked in a permanent post-mortem death grip that had endured for centuries.
Kara tilted her head as her dark eyes locked onto the golden blade with intense sudden fascination.
"What is that?" Kara asked, pointing her right index finger toward the kneeling monument.
Number Five stopped two paces behind her with her posture growing rigid and uncharacteristically somber.

"That," Number Five spoke, her muffled voice carrying a profound reverent gravity, "is the final resting place of the Second World King... When his life reached its natural limit, he refused to be buried in the imperial mausoleum on the surface so he walked down into this vault alone, took his place upon this dais, drove his personal weapon into the bedrock, and allowed his spirit to dissolve into the world."
She paused, gesturing toward the brilliant sun-lit greatsword.

"The weapon is known as the Dawn Sword," Number Five continued, her voice echoing off the stone pillars. "A sword, forged during the first rebuilding era. It was the Second King’s personal battle-blade, an artifact of such immense volatile authority that—"
SWOOSH!
Before Number Five could finish the word ’authority,’ the space beside her violently emptied.
’Wait, where did she—?!’ Number Five’s thoughts screeched in sudden panic!
Kara was gone.
In a single terrifying blink of pure physical acceleration, Kara crossed the thirty yards of open plaza.
Her boots barely kissed the cracked obsidian of the three-tiered dais with her dark coat flaring behind her like the wings of a hunting falcon but she didn’t hesitate.
’I like this weapon...’
GRAB!
Kara’s single right hand reached out, clamping firmly around the warm gold-wrapped hilt of the Dawn Sword, right between the bleached brittle finger-bones of the Second World King.
CRACK-SNAP!
The centuries-old skeletal fingers shattered instantly under her grip with bone dust showering over the stone.
With a sharp effortless upward jerk of her shoulder, Kara ripped the massive golden blade clean out of the obsidian floor.
SHIIIIIIING!

The metal sang with a deafening crystalline roar that shattered the silence of the plaza as Kara spun the massive greatsword in a fluid casual arc through the air, resting the flat of the golden blade effortlessly against her right shoulder, offering the weapon an admiring half-lidded smirk.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
"Cool sword," Kara drawled with her voice completely smooth.
Down below the dais, Number Five’s porcelain mask tilted up in pure horror.
"NO! DROP IT!" Number Five screamed, her small frame launching forward in a desperate sprint.
Her midnight-silk robes whipped around her legs, her arms reaching outward as her voice cracked into panic.
"DROP IT, YOU IDIOT! THE CORE IS PERMANENTLY BONDED TO THE ROYAL BLOODLINE! IF AN UNVERIFIED SOUL TOUCHES THE HILT, IT WILL DETONATE AN INSTANTANEOUS—"
It was too late.
PING!
The Dawn Sword violently ignited and the dormant solar runes along the golden fuller did not merely flare... they detonated into a supernova of pure golden light.
"It’s too—"
A massive expanding shockwave of warm golden energy erupted radially outward from the blade however it was not a violent tearing explosion.
There was no concussive shockwave of shattering stone, no heat that scorched the skin, and no deafening thunderclap of destruction.

Instead, it was an overwhelming ocean-like flood of pure weightless radiance... a tidal wave of liquid gold that instantly swallowed Kara, Number Five, the shattered skeleton, and the entire plaza in an all-consuming brilliant white-gold embrace, drowning the darkness of the vault in the light of a brand new dawn.

Somewhere beneath the roaring gold, buried deep in the marrow of the light itself, Silas thought he heard something that sounded almost like a sound being spoken... but the thought scattered before he could hold onto it, swallowed whole by the dawn.
WHOOSH!
The blinding sea of liquid gold washed through the endless corridors of petrified wood and dark basalt like the first rising light of a forgotten dawn.
SHUUUUUUUU!
The radiant wave crested against the vaulted ceiling fifty feet above, washing over the glowing blue quartz rafters before smoothly receding like a tranquil tide pulling back from a foreign shore.
The light died down almost instantaneously, snapping shut into a tight focused halo that curled closely around the broad, golden fuller of the greatsword.
Silence descended upon Aisle 28 as a dead suffocating quiet that made the arrays sound like a thunderous roar.
Midway through her frantic desperate leap toward the obsidian dais, Number Five froze.
She hung arrested in the air for a fraction of a heartbeat with her small hands clawed forward and her midnight-silk sleeves whipping around her elbows like storm clouds.
The featureless white porcelain mask was tilted straight toward the platform, yet the paralyzing shock radiating through her posture was loud enough to shake the dust from the stone pillars.
"Huh?" Number Five squeaked.
FLAP! TAP!
Her soft leather boots hit the cracked obsidian floor with an unceremonious stumbling thud.
She landed awkwardly, pitching forward onto her knees before catching herself on the rough stone with her newly regenerated left hand.
The woman whipped her head up, looking wildly across the shattered remnants of the three-tiered dais.

The bleached, centuries-old skeleton of the Second World King lay scattered in brittle fragments across the floor tiles with its desiccated ribcage cracked open and its finger-bones pulverized into fine white silt.
...And standing directly in the center of the ruin looking utterly unblemished, was Kara White.
Kara hadn’t been vaporized into ash at all.
Her dark tailored trousers weren’t singed, her loose coat hung casually over her frame, and her single right hand remained clamped firmly around the gold-wrapped hilt of the colossal greatsword.
WHOO!
Intricate razor-thin solar runes, carved in an ancient script that looked like dancing serpents of molten sunlight, traveled up the broad fuller of the Dawn Blade.
They reached the crossguard, leaped across the star-iron collar, and seamlessly bled onto the pale skin of Kara’s right hand but the runes didn’t burn at all.

They braided themselves into her epidermis like delicate luminescent golden tattoos, weaving around her wrist, crawling along her forearm, and sinking directly through the pores of her skin with a soft warm chime.
PING!
The light died down completely and the golden script vanished beneath her skin, leaving her arm clean and undisturbed.
"That wasn’t so bad..."
Kara lifted the heavy blade, stepping over the shattered vertebrae of the ancient King with a careless crunch of her boot heel.

She swung the massive weapon in a fluid whistling figure-eight through the stagnant air, testing its balance and the weight was terrifying, easily two hundred pounds of solid divine-grade solar alloy, yet in her grip it felt as light as a seasoned training sword.
SHING!
She rested the flat of the golden steel against her right shoulder with her dark eyes narrowing as she stared at the edge.
"Weird," Kara muttered, her voice dropping into a dry perplexed drawl. "The hell is this...?"
Silas’s internal senses were humming violently.
Behind the mask of the single-armed woman, a strange prickling sensation was crawling through his core channels.
It wasn’t foreign mana forcing its way into his circulation, it was a harmonic pulse, almost like a dormant heartbeat that had suddenly discovered an echo in his own chest.
It felt like walking into an old forgotten room in a childhood home and finding a coat that fit his shoulders down to the exact millimeter...
Before he could pull up the System interface to query the blade’s parameters, a sharp choked gasp echoed from the base of the dais.
"You..." Number Five choked out, pushing herself up from the floor with shaking arms.
Her porcelain mask was tilted upward, her voice cracking beneath the silk hood in horror. "You can actually wield it...?"
Kara tilted her head down, looking at the small hooded woman with a half-lidded unimpressed stare.
"I’m holding it, aren’t I?" Kara asked dryly. "Unless you think this two-hundred-pound chunk of gold is floating on its own."

"That is impossible!" Number Five yelled, taking a frantic jerky step forward, her sleeves trembling. "That is the Dawn Blade! It is a primary regalia! The concept was personally by the First King of the World during the early days of the Reconstruction... The First King was the only mind capable of designing soul-bound weapons of that caliber! It was through his private classified blueprints that the Second King, his favored heir, was able to physically forge the weapon for his own campaigns. It is fundamentally hardcoded to the ancestral line of House Castellian and if anyone outside the direct royal bloodline attempts to draw that steel, the internal solar power is supposed to detonate a wave of magic that incinerates the wielder’s nervous system into carbon!"
Kara’s eyebrow gave a microscopic twitch.
’Second King...’ Silas mused internally, his thoughts growing remarkably cold and quiet.
For a brief fleeting fraction of a second, when the blinding light had first erupted from the hilt, an echo had brushed against the fringes of his mind.
He’d dismissed it as a hallucination caused by the sudden surge of radiance, but looking down at the scattered bones of the Second King, Silas felt a cold sharp question settle behind his ribs.

’That’s not possible. I’m not Castellian blood... I’m nobody’s discarded prince, I’m Silas Graves, a slum kid from Sector 5 who got dragged into this world... there’s no royal blood running through my veins right? So why did this thing just open for me like I was born to hold it?’
There were too many things to reason and he just wanted to ignore it... Perhaps it was because of the Gold Core?
Outwardly, Kara let out a long theatrical sigh, resting the pommel on the obsidian floor with a dull clunk.
"Well, whoever built it had great taste in balance," Kara smiled, her expression turning infuriatingly smug. "Thanks for the history lesson, short stuff. I think I’ll take this as my first item..."
Number Five’s entire body went rigid and beneath the porcelain mask, you could practically hear her jaw locking with enough force to crack her teeth.

"You cannot simply take the Dawn Blade!" Number Five argued frantically, her muffled voice rising into an indignant shriek. "It is an irreplaceable artifact and it belongs to the Royal mausoleum! It is a historical pillar of the World Council’s heritage! If the World King discovers that you walked out of the vault carrying the personal sidearm of his direct ancestor—"

"The World King told me to take whatever caught my eye," Kara cut her off flatly, her dark eyes flashing with cold immovable amusement. "Five items with unrestricted access... Those were the terms signed in front of the Nine Major Powers and the entire assembly. What, is the supreme ruler of humanity going to go back on his royal word over an old sword resting on a pile of dead bones? If he wants it back, he can walk down to Blessed Land and ask me for it himself."

Number Five let out a tiny barely audible click of her tongue behind her mask, clearly annoyed that her blatant attempt to dump useless warehouse surplus had failed so miserably.

She paused, gesturing toward the brilliant sun-lit greatsword.

Kara was gone.

GRAB!

CRACK-SNAP!
The centuries-old skeletal fingers shattered instantly under her grip with bone dust showering over the stone.

SHIIIIIIING!
