chapters.title: Chapter 595: New Items! [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Number Five opened her mouth to scream another protest, but the brick wall of Kara’s arrogance hit her like a physical blow.
The small woman’s shoulders visibly slumped.

Her head dropped forward with her chin practically resting against her collarbone, and her knees buckled slightly before she caught herself, letting out a wheezing groan that sounded like a dying bellows.
She was so tired.
Three hundred years of guarding silent shelves, and she was stuck babysitting a greedy terrifying monster who treated divine relics like clearance items in a flea market.
"Fine," Number Five whispered, her voice completely dead of life. "Take it... Take the whole damned dais while you’re at it and see if I care."
"You mean it?"
The woman ignored her then straightened up, waving a weak limp hand toward the blade.

"It is a Soul Weapon," Number Five explained, her tone flat, mechanical, entirely defeated. "Because the core recognized your... whatever freakish biological anomaly you possess... the weapon is permanently bound to your spirit. You do not need to haul it around on your back like a common mercenary, nor do you need to waste space in your Lord Inventory... Will it into your core and it will dissolve into your soul."
Kara raised an eyebrow. ’A Soul Weapon?’
She focused her intent, visualizing the golden blade sinking into the warm ocean of mana swirling behind her sternum.
SHUUUU!
The massive two-hundred-pound greatsword instantly melted into a shimmering stream of golden particles!
The light flowed like liquid mercury into the palm of Kara’s right hand, sinking effortlessly beneath her skin.

In an instant the weight vanished yet deep within her soul space, resting comfortably beside her core, Silas could distinctly feel the sharp radiant presence of the Dawn Blade, waiting to be summoned at the speed of thought.
Number Five stood frozen in the center of the aisle, watching the light disappear.
Beneath the smooth white porcelain, her mind was spinning into frantic wild calculations.

’She actually stored it,’ Number Five thought, a cold sweat beading beneath her midnight hood. ’It didn’t reject her and it didn’t tear her soul apart. Is she... could she possibly be an illegitimate child of the current World King? Another secret affair, like that girl from Shogya?’
It was the only logical explanation that fit the physical laws of the universe.
The World King was known to have fathered Kiera in secret during his visits to the United Hegemony.
If he’d strayed once, what was to say he hadn’t left another seed in some remote forgotten corner of the world?
Kara White had appeared out of nowhere, possessing an unrecorded Gold Core, physical arrogance, and an instinctive disdain for authority that practically mirrored the Castellian royal line...

’No...’ Number Five corrected herself, shaking her head slightly beneath the dark silk. ’The Castellian bloodline is aggressively dominant. Kiera is proof of that, even born to a common concubine from an eastern sector, she inherited the identical royal-blue hair, the imperial facial structure, and the core affinity... The blood never hides but Kara White has black hair, purple eyes, and a frame that looks disconnected from the Castellian lineage as there isn’t a single trace of the royal features on her face.’
While Number Five was spiraling into an existential crisis, Kara was standing on the platform, grinning like an idiot.
SHING!
Kara flicked her wrist as the Dawn Blade materialized in her grip in a burst of golden sparks.
SHUUU!
She willed it back and it vanished into her soul.
SHING!
She summoned it again, twirling it once around her knuckles.
SHUUU!
She unsummoned it.
"Neat," Kara chuckled aloud to herself, admiring her empty palm. "Very convenient with no scabbard getting caught on doorways... I like it."
Number Five stared at her, her eyeholes dead and empty.

’She’s a child,’ the World Council Head realized with soul-crushing despair. ’A terrifying calamity of a woman... with the attention span and maturity of a twelve-year-old boy playing with a stick in the mud.’
Kara turned around, stepping off the dais with a bright sunny grin.

"Alright, tour guide!" Kara announced, clapping her single hand against her thigh with a loud smack. "That’s one down, four to go! Take me to the good stuff and no more of those rusty kitchen knives from the entrance, or I’ll start using this new sword to carve my initials into your bookshelves!"
Number Five didn’t even have the energy to curse.
She simply rolled her eyes behind her mask, turned her back on the shattered skeleton of the Second King, and dragged her boots forward into the gloom.
The expanse of the World Vault was an exercise in sensory numbness.
Minutes bled into hours without the sun or stars to mark their passing.
The rhythmic clack-clack-clack of their boots against the damp basalt floor was the only sound cutting through the endless corridors of petrified wood and humming stasis-cases.
Every twenty paces, another glass pedestal glowed under a pale blue preservation spell.
Every fifty paces, an ornate iron archway displayed the crest of an imperial legion long since ground to dust by the turning of the centuries.

To a scholar or an antiquarian, this place was an infinite paradise of forgotten lore but to Kara, who was actively looking for weapons that could rip a titan apart or fortify a territory against apocalyptic sieges, it was rapidly becoming an agonizing exercise in patience...
Three hours had dragged by... Three grueling dust-choked hours of walking, cataloging, rejecting, and arguing as well...
CREAK!
Kara finally gave up on walking.
She spotted a heavy carved archivist’s chair resting beside a towering filing array in Aisle 100, walked over, and practically dropped her entire weight into it.
"Trash," Kara announced loudly, throwing her head back until her dark hair spilled over the mahogany headrest.

Her voice echoed off the vaulted ceiling of blue-lit quartz, carrying down the corridor like a stone skipping over a frozen pond. "All of it is ornamental trash... I have seen better inventory at a roadside vegetable stand in Valoria City..."
Ten paces away, Number Five didn’t even bother to respond.
The short woman had walked over to a low marble storage chest, climbed onto the surface, and laid down completely flat on her back.
Her arms were folded neatly across her chest, her midnight-silk robes draped over her legs like a burial shroud and her porcelain mask staring blankly straight up at the quartz ceiling.
She didn’t move.

At this point Number Five had completely divested herself of dignity so even if Kara decided to pull a sledgehammer from her coat and start smashing the third-century porcelain urns, Number Five was reasonably confident she’d just lie on this marble slab and listen to the shattering clay with a peaceful smile.
’Well,’ Silas mused internally, rolling his shoulder against the chair’s upholstery, ’it hasn’t been a complete waste of time.’
Resting securely inside his hand, alongside the Dawn Blade sleeping quietly in his soul space, were three additional artifacts.
The second item had been uncovered in the boundary between the final archives of the Second King and the relatively modest austere sector dedicated to the Third King.
Tucked away inside a velvet-lined lead casket was an ancient leather-bound grimoire titled simply... [Treatise on the Compression of the Primary Core: The Creation of a Mana Heart].
Under normal circumstances, Kara wouldn’t have looked twice at a cultivation manual.
Silas already possessed his own training regimens, and his gold-core foundation was an anomaly that standard manuals couldn’t touch.
However, the moment Number Five had begrudgingly explained the book’s contents, Silas’s thoughts had immediately snapped to his subordinates back in Blessed Land.
’Tasmin,’ Silas remembered, his mind drifting to the fierce dark-haired woman who had pledged her life to his banner.
Tasmin had been hitting an agonizing painful bottleneck in her shadow cultivation.
She’d been attempting to forge an artificial Shadow Heart, a secondary condensed mana-organ that would allow her to draw directly from the Umbral Basin’s darkness without poisoning her channels.
She’d spent a lot of time coughing blood in the quiet corners of the barracks, stubbornly refusing to ask for aid.
This book was not an ordinary manual.
It was a comprehensive universal architectural guide on how an Awakened could manually compress their primary core into an autonomous Mana Heart, regardless of their native elemental affinity.

According to Number Five, if a Hero or Troop succeeded in forming a true Mana Heart, their latent affinity for their primary element didn’t just increase, it skyrocketed by several orders of magnitude.

The heart acted as an internal perpetual-motion engine, cleansing mana impurities, drastically cutting casting intervals, and granting the user an instinctual, almost spiritual command over their element.

’If I hand this to Tasmin, she’ll break through that shadow bottleneck within a month...’ Silas realized, his fingers twitching with excitement. ’And not just her. What about the rest of the mages in Blessed Land?... If I establish an elite circle of casters who all possess secondary Mana Hearts, our defensive output will multiply ten times over.’
And then his thoughts wandered further.
’What about Vala?’
Vala was a freak of nature.
Like Silas himself, she commanded a staggering multi-elemental palette, shifting between wind and blistering fire with fluid ease.

’If a mono-elemental mage forms a red or blue Mana Heart... what happens if someone like Vala creates one?’ Silas mused with a slow grin spreading behind Kara’s lips. ’Does the heart manifest as a shifting multi-colored prism? Would it allow her to fuse opposing elements without suffering backlash? The potential is terrifying...’
That single manual alone was worth more to the long-term military survival of Blessed Land than ten wagons of gold.
The third and fourth items, however, were of of a different nature.
They came from an era Silas found himself privately admiring, the reign of the Fourth World King, King Tor Castellian.
...Tor had been an unapologetic monster.
He was a ruthless usurper who had drowned three ducal courts in their own blood to take the throne, personally executing eleven of his brothers on the steps of the palace.

He was notoriously despised by modern court historians, largely because he’d publicly mocked the divine traditions of the throne, flatly refusing to adopt the sacred royal seal of "Zel" simply because he loudly proclaimed that "it sounded like a wet cough from an asthmatic sheep."
He ruled through terror, iron discipline, and an obscene terrifying mastery of close-quarters violence... and from Tor’s private, bloody war-chest, Kara had plundered two pieces.
The third item was the Ash Gauntlet.
It was a single heavy left gauntlet forged from a dull volcanic gray alloy that constantly bled faint cold ash from its seams.
The right gauntlet had been shattered and lost during Tor’s final cataclysmic siege against the western demon-lords, leaving only this solitary piece.
Its function, however, was absurd.

Once per day, the Ash Gauntlet allowed the wearer to physically catch and completely reverse the magical trajectory of an incoming attack, redirecting it straight back at the source with zero degradation of force.

According to the military journals kept in Tor’s display case, the tyrant had once stood atop a breached fortress wall, caught a direct solar-beam fired by a high-tier entity with his bare hand, and hurled it back into the creature’s face, blowing its skull clean off its neck.
And the fourth item... was the Death Mask.
It was a terrifying unsettling artifact.
The mask had been cast in dark unpolished bronze directly over Tor’s severed face mere seconds after his execution on the imperial scaffold.
It captured the tyrant’s final hideous sneering grimace down to the microscopic wrinkles around his lips.
According to Number Five, the mask was saturated with the lingering post-mortem soul-shards of the tyrant’s consciousness.

When strapped to the face during active combat, it allowed the wearer to temporarily bypass their own calculation speed, directly accessing fragments of Tor’s ancient battle instincts, his ruthless spatial awareness, and his terrifying cold-blooded muscle memory.
Nobody in four hundred years had dared touch it...
The Council viewed it as a cursed psychologically hazardous relic that slowly drove its wielders into paranoid homicidal madness.
’Madness is for people with weak mental discipline,’ Silas thought, thoroughly pleased with the acquisition.
He didn’t care about Tor’s psychological baggage.
Silas was a practitioner of the Tide-Blade Arts, a discipline that relied heavily on reading the fluid micro-second shifts in an opponent’s balance and exploiting openings before they fully formed.

If he could slip on the Death Mask during an extreme life-or-death engagement, stacking Tor’s ancient brutal battlefield instincts directly on top of his Tide-Blade mastery, his efficiency would reach a threshold that could challenge even monsters at this level.
Yet, sitting here in this creaking chair in Aisle 100, Kara dragged her single right hand down her face, letting out a groan of pure misery.

"It’s just too much stuff," Kara muttered, her voice muffled against her palm. "Four hundred and ninety-eight aisles... and we’ve barely cleared a hundred. My legs are falling off, my eyes are dry from reading plaques, and ninety-nine percent of these shelves are filled with useless garbage."
On the marble chest, Number Five slowly rolled her head to the side, her porcelain mask staring at Kara with deep silent contempt.

"You have claimed a divine greatsword, an ancient core-condensation treatise, and two classified relics of an executed tyrant," Number Five said, her voice dripping with dry exhausted venom. "Most monarchs would consider any single one of those items the crowning glory of their family dynasty... You have gathered four in three hours, and you sit there whining like a spoiled child who received the wrong flavor of candied plum."

sentences.text: Number Five opened her mouth to scream another protest, but the brick wall of Kara’s arrogance hit her like a physical blow.
The small woman’s shoulders visibly slumped.

Her head dropped forward with her chin practically resting against her collarbone, and her knees buckled slightly before she caught herself, letting out a wheezing groan that sounded like a dying bellows.
She was so tired.
Three hundred years of guarding silent shelves, and she was stuck babysitting a greedy terrifying monster who treated divine relics like clearance items in a flea market.
"Fine," Number Five whispered, her voice completely dead of life.
"Take it...
Take the whole damned dais while you’re at it and see if I care."
"You mean it?"
The woman ignored her then straightened up, waving a weak limp hand toward the blade.
"It is a Soul Weapon," Number Five explained, her tone flat, mechanical, entirely defeated.
"Because the core recognized your... whatever freakish biological anomaly you possess... the weapon is permanently bound to your spirit.
You do not need to haul it around on your back like a common mercenary, nor do you need to waste space in your Lord Inventory...
Will it into your core and it will dissolve into your soul."
Kara raised an eyebrow. ’A Soul Weapon?’
She focused her intent, visualizing the golden blade sinking into the warm ocean of mana swirling behind her sternum.
SHUUUU!
The massive two-hundred-pound greatsword instantly melted into a shimmering stream of golden particles!
The light flowed like liquid mercury into the palm of Kara’s right hand, sinking effortlessly beneath her skin.

In an instant the weight vanished yet deep within her soul space, resting comfortably beside her core, Silas could distinctly feel the sharp radiant presence of the Dawn Blade, waiting to be summoned at the speed of thought.
Number Five stood frozen in the center of the aisle, watching the light disappear.
Beneath the smooth white porcelain, her mind was spinning into frantic wild calculations.
’She actually stored it,’ Number Five thought, a cold sweat beading beneath her midnight hood. ’It didn’t reject her and it didn’t tear her soul apart.
Is she... could she possibly be an illegitimate child of the current World King?
Another secret affair, like that girl from Shogya?’
It was the only logical explanation that fit the physical laws of the universe.
The World King was known to have fathered Kiera in secret during his visits to the United Hegemony.
If he’d strayed once, what was to say he hadn’t left another seed in some remote forgotten corner of the world?
Kara White had appeared out of nowhere, possessing an unrecorded Gold Core, physical arrogance, and an instinctive disdain for authority that practically mirrored the Castellian royal line...
’No...’ Number Five corrected herself, shaking her head slightly beneath the dark silk. ’The Castellian bloodline is aggressively dominant.
Kiera is proof of that, even born to a common concubine from an eastern sector, she inherited the identical royal-blue hair, the imperial facial structure, and the core affinity...
The blood never hides but Kara White has black hair, purple eyes, and a frame that looks disconnected from the Castellian lineage as there isn’t a single trace of the royal features on her face.’
While Number Five was spiraling into an existential crisis, Kara was standing on the platform, grinning like an idiot.
SHING!
Kara flicked her wrist as the Dawn Blade materialized in her grip in a burst of golden sparks.
SHUUU!
She willed it back and it vanished into her soul.
SHING!
She summoned it again, twirling it once around her knuckles.
SHUUU!
She unsummoned it.
"Neat," Kara chuckled aloud to herself, admiring her empty palm.
"Very convenient with no scabbard getting caught on doorways...
I like it."
Number Five stared at her, her eyeholes dead and empty.

’She’s a child,’ the World Council Head realized with soul-crushing despair. ’A terrifying calamity of a woman... with the attention span and maturity of a twelve-year-old boy playing with a stick in the mud.’
Kara turned around, stepping off the dais with a bright sunny grin.
"Alright, tour guide!" Kara announced, clapping her single hand against her thigh with a loud smack.
"That’s one down, four to go!
Take me to the good stuff and no more of those rusty kitchen knives from the entrance, or I’ll start using this new sword to carve my initials into your bookshelves!"
Number Five didn’t even have the energy to curse.
She simply rolled her eyes behind her mask, turned her back on the shattered skeleton of the Second King, and dragged her boots forward into the gloom.
The expanse of the World Vault was an exercise in sensory numbness.
Minutes bled into hours without the sun or stars to mark their passing.
The rhythmic clack-clack-clack of their boots against the damp basalt floor was the only sound cutting through the endless corridors of petrified wood and humming stasis-cases.
Every twenty paces, another glass pedestal glowed under a pale blue preservation spell.
Every fifty paces, an ornate iron archway displayed the crest of an imperial legion long since ground to dust by the turning of the centuries.

To a scholar or an antiquarian, this place was an infinite paradise of forgotten lore but to Kara, who was actively looking for weapons that could rip a titan apart or fortify a territory against apocalyptic sieges, it was rapidly becoming an agonizing exercise in patience...
Three hours had dragged by...
Three grueling dust-choked hours of walking, cataloging, rejecting, and arguing as well...
CREAK!
Kara finally gave up on walking.
She spotted a heavy carved archivist’s chair resting beside a towering filing array in Aisle 100, walked over, and practically dropped her entire weight into it.
"Trash," Kara announced loudly, throwing her head back until her dark hair spilled over the mahogany headrest.
Her voice echoed off the vaulted ceiling of blue-lit quartz, carrying down the corridor like a stone skipping over a frozen pond.
"All of it is ornamental trash...
I have seen better inventory at a roadside vegetable stand in Valoria City..."
Ten paces away, Number Five didn’t even bother to respond.
The short woman had walked over to a low marble storage chest, climbed onto the surface, and laid down completely flat on her back.
Her arms were folded neatly across her chest, her midnight-silk robes draped over her legs like a burial shroud and her porcelain mask staring blankly straight up at the quartz ceiling.
She didn’t move.

At this point Number Five had completely divested herself of dignity so even if Kara decided to pull a sledgehammer from her coat and start smashing the third-century porcelain urns, Number Five was reasonably confident she’d just lie on this marble slab and listen to the shattering clay with a peaceful smile.
’Well,’ Silas mused internally, rolling his shoulder against the chair’s upholstery, ’it hasn’t been a complete waste of time.’
Resting securely inside his hand, alongside the Dawn Blade sleeping quietly in his soul space, were three additional artifacts.
The second item had been uncovered in the boundary between the final archives of the Second King and the relatively modest austere sector dedicated to the Third King.
Tucked away inside a velvet-lined lead casket was an ancient leather-bound grimoire titled simply...
[Treatise on the Compression of the Primary Core: The Creation of a Mana Heart].
Under normal circumstances, Kara wouldn’t have looked twice at a cultivation manual.
Silas already possessed his own training regimens, and his gold-core foundation was an anomaly that standard manuals couldn’t touch.
However, the moment Number Five had begrudgingly explained the book’s contents, Silas’s thoughts had immediately snapped to his subordinates back in Blessed Land.
’Tasmin,’ Silas remembered, his mind drifting to the fierce dark-haired woman who had pledged her life to his banner.
Tasmin had been hitting an agonizing painful bottleneck in her shadow cultivation.
She’d been attempting to forge an artificial Shadow Heart, a secondary condensed mana-organ that would allow her to draw directly from the Umbral Basin’s darkness without poisoning her channels.
She’d spent a lot of time coughing blood in the quiet corners of the barracks, stubbornly refusing to ask for aid.
This book was not an ordinary manual.
It was a comprehensive universal architectural guide on how an Awakened could manually compress their primary core into an autonomous Mana Heart, regardless of their native elemental affinity.

According to Number Five, if a Hero or Troop succeeded in forming a true Mana Heart, their latent affinity for their primary element didn’t just increase, it skyrocketed by several orders of magnitude.

The heart acted as an internal perpetual-motion engine, cleansing mana impurities, drastically cutting casting intervals, and granting the user an instinctual, almost spiritual command over their element.
’If I hand this to Tasmin, she’ll break through that shadow bottleneck within a month...’ Silas realized, his fingers twitching with excitement. ’And not just her.
What about the rest of the mages in Blessed Land?...
If I establish an elite circle of casters who all possess secondary Mana Hearts, our defensive output will multiply ten times over.’
And then his thoughts wandered further.
’What about Vala?’
Vala was a freak of nature.
Like Silas himself, she commanded a staggering multi-elemental palette, shifting between wind and blistering fire with fluid ease.

’If a mono-elemental mage forms a red or blue Mana Heart... what happens if someone like Vala creates one?’ Silas mused with a slow grin spreading behind Kara’s lips. ’Does the heart manifest as a shifting multi-colored prism?
Would it allow her to fuse opposing elements without suffering backlash?
The potential is terrifying...’
That single manual alone was worth more to the long-term military survival of Blessed Land than ten wagons of gold.

He was a ruthless usurper who had drowned three ducal courts in their own blood to take the throne, personally executing eleven of his brothers on the steps of the palace.

He was notoriously despised by modern court historians, largely because he’d publicly mocked the divine traditions of the throne, flatly refusing to adopt the sacred royal seal of "Zel" simply because he loudly proclaimed that "it sounded like a wet cough from an asthmatic sheep."

"Most monarchs would consider any single one of those items the crowning glory of their family dynasty...
You have gathered four in three hours, and you sit there whining like a spoiled child who received the wrong flavor of candied plum."

chapters.title: Chapter 596: Pheonix Egg [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Because I want a good item for my fifth one!" Kara shot back, throwing her hand up in the air. "Something truly ridiculous... Something that makes me smile every time I pull it out! I need a fifth item that actually changes the board, not another dusty ledger or an antique tea kettle!"
It wasn’t that the vault lacked power as the sheer historical wealth here was staggering.
...The problem was the trade-offs.
Every truly "overpowered" item they had passed came saddled with horrifying catastrophic conditions.
Just thirty minutes ago, in Aisle 85, they’d crossed an ancient pulsing black crystal known as the Ascendant’s Thirst.

The artifact possessed a terrifying authority... if crushed against an Awakened’s sternum, it would forcibly compress their mana meridians, instantly elevating their Core Refinement by an entire Tier!
Kara had practically drooled over it for ten seconds, until she read the second line on the runic plaque.
’Cost of Activation: Permanently consumes ninety percent of the user’s remaining natural lifespan.’
Kara had immediately dropped the crystal back into its velvet box as if it were a burning coal.
What in the seven hells was the point of ascending a core stage if you dropped dead of organ failure three years later?
And then there was the Dread-March War Drum...
A single hand-carved drum fashioned from the tanned hide of an ancient leviathan, belonging to the Third King, Alaric the Unsleeping.

When struck in rhythm, the drum’s soundwaves synchronized the cardiovascular pulse and reaction speed of every allied soldier within a five-mile radius to the drummer’s own tempo, completely overriding their fatigue and rapidly refilling their mana channels.
Alaric had famously used it to force an entire exhausted legion to march and slaughter continuously for fourteen days without a single second of sleep.
...It was undeniably god-tier old technology.
Yet Silas had walked right past it.

Why would he drag a noisy cursed drum around the battlefield when he already had Eluned? The woman’s passive aura naturally nourished the stamina of everyone residing in Blessed Land, gently harmonizing their meridians without turning them into mindless sleep-deprived berserkers...
’Plus... it’s not like there’s an item for immortality sitting on these shelves,’ Silas mused bitterly, crossing his boots on the stone floor.
If there had been an immortality elixir, he could’ve downed it and then smashed the Ascendant’s Thirst against his chest five times over to become an immortal god on the spot.
But true immortality was a cosmic paradox... even the ancient World Kings eventually decayed into bone and dust.
And then there were the items that were simply useless.
The Sixth King, the so-called "Mad Cartographer King," had been a comedy of errors.

The man had spent his entire thirty-year reign obsessed with mapping every square inch of the Sovereign Realm, bankrupting half the treasury to fund endless surveying expeditions into the Great Unknown.
He had ultimately died of frost-rot in a ditch after mapping roughly 0.99% of the continental landmass...
His primary legacy in the vault was the Unfinished Atlas.
An enormous rolled parchment map that magically updated itself in real time to reflect newly discovered geography anywhere in the world but the fatal flaw?
The map only displayed terrain that the Mad King personally believed should exist according to his bizarre fractured theological theories!

If the King believed there was an ocean of chocolate three hundred leagues past the northern border, the map faithfully drew waves of brown syrup, completely ignoring the actual colossal mountain range standing in physical reality.
Modern World Council satellite feeds were roughly ten thousand times more accurate.
...And right beside the useless map was the Needle of the Long Return.
It was a common silver tattooing needle.

The plaque proudly declared that anyone marked with its ink would gain an indelible instinctual homing sense that pointed directly toward the exact plot of earth where they were born, no matter how disoriented, blind, or geographically displaced they became.

Kara had stared at the needle for a solid minute, wondering what kind of idiot would waste a treasure slot on a device that essentially functioned as an un-turn-off-able GPS pointing at their childhood bedroom...
And then there was the Garrulous Blade.
The exact weapon Musvi had warned them about back at the library counter.
Tucked into an iron display stand in Aisle 92 was a beautifully forged, perfectly balanced Tier 3 longsword with a grip wrapped in supple dragon-hide.
The steel was sharp, the mana-conductivity was flawless, and the balance was immaculate.
The only problem was that the sword possessed an awakened ego that literally never shut up...
The second Kara had stepped within five paces of the pedestal, a high-pitched noble voice had echoed directly inside her skull.

’Oh? A customer? A woman? With one arm? Fascinating. Your stance is too wide, girl... Your right shoulder is dropping three millimeters lower than your left... Are you trying to cut wood or fight a war? Look at that silk coat, hideous color, truly... Hey, you see that short woman in the porcelain mask beside you? She’s breathing awfully loud... Why don’t you draw me, take two quick strides, and sever her spine at the third lumbar vertebra? It would be hilarious... Do it... Come on, stab her... Just a little poke...’
Kara had immediately stepped backward, shaking her head in disgust.
The weapon was a glorified psychotic instigator that would drive any sane swordsman to leap off a cliff within forty-eight hours just to escape the commentary.

"I’m bored," Kara announced, leaning her head back against the carved mahogany of her chair until the wood groaned. "Number Five... Can’t an overpowered, game-breaking, effortless divine treasure just magically fall out of the sky and land in my lap?"

"No," Number Five replied from the marble chest, not moving a muscle. "This is a royal repository of historical antiquities, Lord White, not a fairy tale for uneducated toddlers. The universe does not bend to the whims of your impatient—"
CLATTER!
Kara shifted her weight, throwing her right arm over the back of the chair.
Her elbow knocked against the edge of a dusty unpolished wooden crate that had been shoved haphazardly beneath a secondary storage rack behind her.
THUD!
The jolt dislodged something resting precariously on top of the crate.
ROLL... DROP... BANG!
A heavy rounded object tumbled off the shelf, bounced twice across the flagstones with a metallic chime, and rolled directly between Kara’s booted feet, coming to a halt against her heel.
Kara paused as she slowly lowered her chin, looking down at the floor.
Resting against the toe of her left boot was an object roughly the size of an ostrich egg, nearly fourteen inches from tip to base.
It was fashioned entirely of what appeared to be solid unrefined gold.
The surface was remarkably rough, covered in overlapping scale-like ridges that felt cold and inert.

It possessed no glowing runes, no humming mana-frequencies, and no visible enchantments as the egg simply looked like a heavy decorative doorstop that some lazy person had tossed into the shadows centuries ago to keep a storage closet open...
Number Five slowly sat up on the marble chest, peering down through the eyeholes of her mask with a tired dismissive tilt of her head.

"Do not waste your time," Number Five said, waving a limp hand toward the floor. "That is merely an unidentified lump of auric slag salvaged from the volcanic trenches of the southern reaches during the First Era... Our chief alchemists spent three decades attempting to melt it down, crack it open, or extract mana from its core but it is non-reactive to all four primary elements. It has zero conductive value, zero spiritual power, and zero utility so it is cataloged as useless scrap metal."
Kara didn’t answer as she leaned down from the chair, extending her single right hand with her calloused fingers wrapping around the cold textured gold scales.
The moment her flesh made direct contact with the surface—
BZZZZZZZT!
A sharp translucent blue interface abruptly materialized in the empty air right before Kara’s eyes, flashing with urgent crystalline clarity.
[System Notice: You have discovered a Phoenix’s Egg!]
[Tier]: Divine Beast (Unranked)
[Status]: Lifeless / In Stasis
Kara’s hand froze.
Her breath caught in her throat, her dark eyes dilating as she stared at the glowing blue text.
’A Phoenix...?’ Silas thought, his heart thumping hard against his ribs.
Before he could even process the words, a secondary data-tab unfolded beneath the primary notice, rapidly detailing the lore of the entity.
[Entity Analysis:] Primordial Phoenix

[An ancient apex avian entity originating from the boundless celestial sea of the higher realms... Possesses an innate command over the flames of absolute rebirth, capable of cycling physical destruction into immortal vitality. Highly revered across all ancient civilizations as a supreme guardian.]
Silas’s mind raced through the descriptions.
It aligned almost beat-for-beat with the mythological legends of his past life, a terrifying immortal bird of divine flame, wielding the authority of resurrection and eternal fire.
Yet looking at the egg resting in his palm, Silas noted the disturbing status tag... [Lifeless / In Stasis].
’If it’s a legendary divine beast... why hasn’t it hatched?’ Silas queried internally, his thoughts probing the System. ’Why does it feel like a cold block of lead?’
PING!
The System interface responded with a crisp update.
[Query Resolution: Hatching Prerequisites]
[The Primordial Phoenix is an entity born of boundless celestial light and natural vibrancy... The egg cannot hatch within cold, lightless environments, nor can it process standard elemental fire.]
[Current Condition: The embryonic soul has fallen into a state of suspended pseudo-death due to prolonged starvation of natural power.]

[Hatching Requirement: The egg requires immersion within a domain saturated with pure concentrated Nature Mana and high-tier vegetative life-force... Upon sufficient saturation, the dormant embryonic flame will ignite, triggering immediate incubation.]
Kara slowly retracted her hand, straightening up in the chair with the heavy golden egg cradled securely against her ribs.
’Nature Mana...’ Silas mused with a wild incredulous grin spreading across Kara’s face.
The World Council’s alchemists had failed to crack it because they were treating it like an alchemical metal.
They’d blasted it with fire spells, soaked it in acid, and tried to channel raw mana into its shell, in a cold sterile lightless vault buried miles beneath an ocean trench...
To a creature born of living sunlight and natural blooming vitality, this vault was a tomb.
’And where in the seven hells am I going to find pure concentrated Nature Mana?’ Silas thought, laughing inwardly at the miraculous absurdity of the universe. ’Elu.’
Eluned was a living Goddess, the embodiment of pristine nature, forest vitality, and untamed vegetative growth.
Blessed Land was practically bathed in her passive aura!

’I don’t need a team of high-tier alchemists,’ Silas realized, his fingers gently tracing the golden scales. ’Elu can help me hatch it... I just need to take this egg back to my territory, dig a nice little hole in the soft soil right beneath Eluned’s sacred roots, let her pour an hour’s worth of pure forest mana into the shell, and watch the damned thing hatch or let her hatch it herself.’
A divine immortal Phoenix soaring over the battlements of Blessed Land...?
A guardian beast that could incinerate entire siege engines with celestial fire and cheat death through the flames of rebirth...?
Kara looked up from the egg, locking her dark eyes onto Number Five with a broad beaming and completely shameless smile.
"I want this," Kara declared, tapping the golden shell with her knuckle with a satisfying clink. "This is my fifth item."
Number Five sat up on the marble chest, blinking through the eyeholes of her mask.
"Sure," Number Five replied instantly with her voice flat then the small woman paused.
She sat bolt upright on the slab, her head cocking to the side as the realization clicked into her brain.
’Five items...’ Number Five thought, a sudden blinding wave of pure euphoric relief washing through her marrow. ’She picked five... That’s five! It’s over... The nightmare is over!’
A visible dramatic transformation swept over the short woman’s posture.

Her shoulders dropped their tension, her spine straightened, and when she spoke, her muffled voice carried a bright bubbly almost musical excitement that sounded completely alien coming from beneath a grim porcelain mask.

"Splendid!" Number Five cheered, clapping her small hands together with a sharp joyous clap. "An exceptional choice! A truly magnificent decorative doorstop! Truly, your aesthetic refinement knows no bounds, Lord White! Allow me to offer my sincerest, most heartfelt congratulations on concluding your selection!"
Kara let out a low chuckle, slipping the heavy Phoenix Egg into her Lord Inventory, where it vanished into the void alongside her new books, the Ash Gauntlet, and Tor’s Death Mask.
"You really couldn’t wait to get rid of me, could you?" Kara teased, rising from the creaking chair.
Number Five jumped down from the marble chest, landing lightly on her feet, dusting off her midnight-silk robes with quick cheerful pats.

"I would rather wrestle a leviathan in my nightgown than spend another forty seconds in this aisle with you, Lord White..." Number Five admitted freely, her porcelain mask tilting up with what felt like a radiant unseen smile. "However... in all seriousness... perhaps at another juncture, under more agreeable circumstances, we can come back here for more items... The Council’s records are vast, and should you fulfill your role as Humanity’s Hero with proper diligence... who knows? Perhaps the deeper wings may open for you once more."
Kara offered the short woman a genuine respectful nod.
"Thanks, shorty," Kara said. "You were a pretty decent guide. For a bureaucrat, anyway."
Number Five paused, looking up at the broad-shouldered woman.
A soft quiet warmth seemed to settle over the small Council Head with her posture softening by a fraction.
"Thank you, Kara White," Number Five murmured softly, her voice barely louder than a whisper. "It was... surprisingly... quite fun."
Kara opened her mouth to reply...
PING!
The spatial extraction runes embedded into ground below her violently ignited.
’They weren’t here befor—’

If the King believed there was an ocean of chocolate three hundred leagues past the northern border, the map faithfully drew waves of brown syrup, completely ignoring the actual colossal mountain range standing in physical reality.
Modern World Council satellite feeds were roughly ten thousand times more accurate.
...And right beside the useless map was the Needle of the Long Return.
It was a common silver tattooing needle.

The plaque proudly declared that anyone marked with its ink would gain an indelible instinctual homing sense that pointed directly toward the exact plot of earth where they were born, no matter how disoriented, blind, or geographically displaced they became.

Kara had stared at the needle for a solid minute, wondering what kind of idiot would waste a treasure slot on a device that essentially functioned as an un-turn-off-able GPS pointing at their childhood bedroom...
And then there was the Garrulous Blade.
The exact weapon Musvi had warned them about back at the library counter.
Tucked into an iron display stand in Aisle 92 was a beautifully forged, perfectly balanced Tier 3 longsword with a grip wrapped in supple dragon-hide.
The steel was sharp, the mana-conductivity was flawless, and the balance was immaculate.
The only problem was that the sword possessed an awakened ego that literally never shut up...
The second Kara had stepped within five paces of the pedestal, a high-pitched noble voice had echoed directly inside her skull.
’Oh?
A customer?
A woman?
With one arm?
Fascinating.
Your stance is too wide, girl...
Your right shoulder is dropping three millimeters lower than your left...
Are you trying to cut wood or fight a war?
Look at that silk coat, hideous color, truly...
Hey, you see that short woman in the porcelain mask beside you?
She’s breathing awfully loud...
Why don’t you draw me, take two quick strides, and sever her spine at the third lumbar vertebra?
It would be hilarious...
Do it...
Come on, stab her...
Just a little poke...’
Kara had immediately stepped backward, shaking her head in disgust.
The weapon was a glorified psychotic instigator that would drive any sane swordsman to leap off a cliff within forty-eight hours just to escape the commentary.
"I’m bored," Kara announced, leaning her head back against the carved mahogany of her chair until the wood groaned.
"Number Five...
Can’t an overpowered, game-breaking, effortless divine treasure just magically fall out of the sky and land in my lap?"
"No," Number Five replied from the marble chest, not moving a muscle.
"This is a royal repository of historical antiquities, Lord White, not a fairy tale for uneducated toddlers.
The universe does not bend to the whims of your impatient—"
CLATTER!
Kara shifted her weight, throwing her right arm over the back of the chair.
Her elbow knocked against the edge of a dusty unpolished wooden crate that had been shoved haphazardly beneath a secondary storage rack behind her.
THUD!
The jolt dislodged something resting precariously on top of the crate.
ROLL...
DROP...
BANG!
A heavy rounded object tumbled off the shelf, bounced twice across the flagstones with a metallic chime, and rolled directly between Kara’s booted feet, coming to a halt against her heel.
Kara paused as she slowly lowered her chin, looking down at the floor.
Resting against the toe of her left boot was an object roughly the size of an ostrich egg, nearly fourteen inches from tip to base.
It was fashioned entirely of what appeared to be solid unrefined gold.
The surface was remarkably rough, covered in overlapping scale-like ridges that felt cold and inert.

It possessed no glowing runes, no humming mana-frequencies, and no visible enchantments as the egg simply looked like a heavy decorative doorstop that some lazy person had tossed into the shadows centuries ago to keep a storage closet open...
Number Five slowly sat up on the marble chest, peering down through the eyeholes of her mask with a tired dismissive tilt of her head.
"Do not waste your time," Number Five said, waving a limp hand toward the floor.
"That is merely an unidentified lump of auric slag salvaged from the volcanic trenches of the southern reaches during the First Era...
Our chief alchemists spent three decades attempting to melt it down, crack it open, or extract mana from its core but it is non-reactive to all four primary elements.
It has zero conductive value, zero spiritual power, and zero utility so it is cataloged as useless scrap metal."
Kara didn’t answer as she leaned down from the chair, extending her single right hand with her calloused fingers wrapping around the cold textured gold scales.
The moment her flesh made direct contact with the surface—
BZZZZZZZT!
A sharp translucent blue interface abruptly materialized in the empty air right before Kara’s eyes, flashing with urgent crystalline clarity.
[System Notice: You have discovered a Phoenix’s Egg!]
[Tier]: Divine Beast (Unranked)
[Status]: Lifeless / In Stasis
Kara’s hand froze.
Her breath caught in her throat, her dark eyes dilating as she stared at the glowing blue text.
’A Phoenix...?’ Silas thought, his heart thumping hard against his ribs.
Before he could even process the words, a secondary data-tab unfolded beneath the primary notice, rapidly detailing the lore of the entity.
[Entity Analysis:] Primordial Phoenix
[An ancient apex avian entity originating from the boundless celestial sea of the higher realms...
Possesses an innate command over the flames of absolute rebirth, capable of cycling physical destruction into immortal vitality.
Highly revered across all ancient civilizations as a supreme guardian.]
Silas’s mind raced through the descriptions.
It aligned almost beat-for-beat with the mythological legends of his past life, a terrifying immortal bird of divine flame, wielding the authority of resurrection and eternal fire.
Yet looking at the egg resting in his palm, Silas noted the disturbing status tag...
[Lifeless / In Stasis].
’If it’s a legendary divine beast... why hasn’t it hatched?’ Silas queried internally, his thoughts probing the System. ’Why does it feel like a cold block of lead?’
PING!
The System interface responded with a crisp update.
[Query Resolution: Hatching Prerequisites]
[The Primordial Phoenix is an entity born of boundless celestial light and natural vibrancy...
The egg cannot hatch within cold, lightless environments, nor can it process standard elemental fire.]
[Current Condition: The embryonic soul has fallen into a state of suspended pseudo-death due to prolonged starvation of natural power.]
[Hatching Requirement: The egg requires immersion within a domain saturated with pure concentrated Nature Mana and high-tier vegetative life-force...
Upon sufficient saturation, the dormant embryonic flame will ignite, triggering immediate incubation.]
Kara slowly retracted her hand, straightening up in the chair with the heavy golden egg cradled securely against her ribs.
’Nature Mana...’ Silas mused with a wild incredulous grin spreading across Kara’s face.
The World Council’s alchemists had failed to crack it because they were treating it like an alchemical metal.
They’d blasted it with fire spells, soaked it in acid, and tried to channel raw mana into its shell, in a cold sterile lightless vault buried miles beneath an ocean trench...
To a creature born of living sunlight and natural blooming vitality, this vault was a tomb.
’And where in the seven hells am I going to find pure concentrated Nature Mana?’ Silas thought, laughing inwardly at the miraculous absurdity of the universe. ’Elu.’
Eluned was a living Goddess, the embodiment of pristine nature, forest vitality, and untamed vegetative growth.
Blessed Land was practically bathed in her passive aura!
’I don’t need a team of high-tier alchemists,’ Silas realized, his fingers gently tracing the golden scales. ’Elu can help me hatch it...

I just need to take this egg back to my territory, dig a nice little hole in the soft soil right beneath Eluned’s sacred roots, let her pour an hour’s worth of pure forest mana into the shell, and watch the damned thing hatch or let her hatch it herself.’
A divine immortal Phoenix soaring over the battlements of Blessed Land...?
A guardian beast that could incinerate entire siege engines with celestial fire and cheat death through the flames of rebirth...?
Kara looked up from the egg, locking her dark eyes onto Number Five with a broad beaming and completely shameless smile.
"I want this," Kara declared, tapping the golden shell with her knuckle with a satisfying clink.
"This is my fifth item."
Number Five sat up on the marble chest, blinking through the eyeholes of her mask.
"Sure," Number Five replied instantly with her voice flat then the small woman paused.
She sat bolt upright on the slab, her head cocking to the side as the realization clicked into her brain.
’Five items...’ Number Five thought, a sudden blinding wave of pure euphoric relief washing through her marrow. ’She picked five...
That’s five!
It’s over...
The nightmare is over!’
A visible dramatic transformation swept over the short woman’s posture.

Her shoulders dropped their tension, her spine straightened, and when she spoke, her muffled voice carried a bright bubbly almost musical excitement that sounded completely alien coming from beneath a grim porcelain mask.
"Splendid!" Number Five cheered, clapping her small hands together with a sharp joyous clap.
"An exceptional choice!
A truly magnificent decorative doorstop!
Truly, your aesthetic refinement knows no bounds, Lord White!
Allow me to offer my sincerest, most heartfelt congratulations on concluding your selection!"
Kara let out a low chuckle, slipping the heavy Phoenix Egg into her Lord Inventory, where it vanished into the void alongside her new books, the Ash Gauntlet, and Tor’s Death Mask.
"You really couldn’t wait to get rid of me, could you?" Kara teased, rising from the creaking chair.
Number Five jumped down from the marble chest, landing lightly on her feet, dusting off her midnight-silk robes with quick cheerful pats.

"I would rather wrestle a leviathan in my nightgown than spend another forty seconds in this aisle with you, Lord White..." Number Five admitted freely, her porcelain mask tilting up with what felt like a radiant unseen smile.
"However... in all seriousness... perhaps at another juncture, under more agreeable circumstances, we can come back here for more items...
The Council’s records are vast, and should you fulfill your role as Humanity’s Hero with proper diligence... who knows?
Perhaps the deeper wings may open for you once more."
Kara offered the short woman a genuine respectful nod.
"Thanks, shorty," Kara said.
"You were a pretty decent guide.
For a bureaucrat, anyway."
Number Five paused, looking up at the broad-shouldered woman.
A soft quiet warmth seemed to settle over the small Council Head with her posture softening by a fraction.
"Thank you, Kara White," Number Five murmured softly, her voice barely louder than a whisper.
"It was... surprisingly... quite fun."
Kara opened her mouth to reply...
PING!
The spatial extraction runes embedded into ground below her violently ignited.
’They weren’t here befor—’

chapters.title: Chapter 597: In The Slums Once More [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Before a single word could pass her lips, the dark basalt aisles, the glowing quartz rafters, and the small hooded woman in the porcelain mask vanished into an all-consuming blinding flash of white light, ripping Kara out of the depths and rocketing her back toward the surface of the world.
WHOOSH!
The white light collapsed and the air that rushed into Silas’s lungs was not spiced pear cider.
It was scorched rubber, stale urine, oxidized motor oil, and the sour grease of boiled tallow.
Kara blinked once, twice, adjusting her optical focus against the sudden murky yellow gloom.
High above, the smog of the lower industrial sprawl hung like a rotten wool blanket, choked with heavy particulates from the exhaust stacks.
Beneath her scuffed leather boots, a pool of black runoff water rippled softly against cracked greasy asphalt littered with discarded ration foils and broken glass.
’What the hell...’
Silas stood completely still in the dark silhouette of the single-armed woman with her jaw tightening as the familiar rancid reek crept straight up her nostrils.
’Sector Six slums...’
It was unmistakable.

Sector Five had been rough, the crumbling concrete tenements where he’d spent years scraping copper wire and hauling iron crates just to buy dry oats for Lia, but Sector Six was an outright graveyard for the living.
It was three tiers below the civil surveillance line, completely abandoned by civil enforcers alike.
’Fuck that porcelain-faced little bitch,’ Silas cursed bitterly in the cold silence of his mind.
Number Five hadn’t deposited him back in the staging pavilion to parade his loot in front of the council, nor had she deposited him outside at least...
The short woman had deliberately twisted the spatial extraction coordinates, dumping him straight into the armpit of the metropolis.

’She was definitely smiling under that mask when she pulled the lever,’ he thought, his mouth twisting into an irritated grimace. ’"It was... surprisingly... quite fun." Fun my ass. She was just waiting to throw me into an open sewer.’
Kara raised her single right hand, waving it sharply in front of her nose to cut through the reek of rotting tallow.
She stepped lightly out of the oily puddle, ducking into the deep shadow of an overhanging fire escape.
The brick alleyway was narrow, choked with rusted iron dumpsters and damp cardboard.
Silas paused, his dark eyes sweeping the perimeter.

Behind his skull, his senses rippled outward in an instant soundless pulse, mapping every rat scurrying through the foundation cracks and confirming what he already knew from years of gutter survival...
Nobody was watching and the city government didn’t waste credits putting surveillance lenses in a sector where people cannibalized the copper wiring out of the lampposts.
With a fluid motion of his single hand, Kara reached toward her hand, slipping off the plain silver signet ring that maintained the illusion.
SHUUUUUU!
The displacement was soundless as the broad shoulders narrowed, the long wild black hair sheared away and the imposing frame of Kara White collapsed inward like cooling glass.

Within the span of two heartbeats, the dark coat and tailored trousers shifted, replaced by a clean charcoal-gray bespoke wool suit, an unbuttoned white collar, and the sharp jawline of Silas Graves as he was much taller than before.
"Ah, feels good to be back."
He rolled his shoulders, feeling his native center of gravity settle back into his joints.
He smoothed down his lapels, adjusting the cuffs of his sleeves, and let out a long quiet breath into the damp gloom.
’Time to go home.’

Silas checked his internal circulation once more, ensuring not a single thread of the Dawn Blade’s lingering warmth or the feeling of the Phoenix Egg leaked past his pores even though they were in his Inventory.
In an area this destitute, a stray drop of that level of mana would draw every desperate rogue Awakened within five miles like sharks to an open vein.
’And I really don’t want to stress myself out dealing with them...’
He turned on his heel, moving down the alleyway with silent effortless strides.

His leather dress shoes barely clicked against the cracked flagstones, slipping through the maze of rusted metal and fire escapes until the towering tenements gave way to an open cracked boulevard that bordered the edge of the perimeter.
Silas reached into his breast pocket and drew out his personal mobile phone, not the pastel-pink kitten monstrosity Kara had used to extort forty billion out of Vanderbilt, but his own black one.
He tapped the glass, intending to call a cab, when his thumb hovered over his primary applications.
’I told Martha and the girls I was leaving for an early morning business trip,’ he mused, a faint genuine warmth softening the cold edge of his eyes.
It wasn’t technically a lie.
He had spent the morning extorting the nine most powerful monarchs on the planet, looting a vault, and securing autonomy.
That was about as high-stakes as business got but Lia didn’t need to know about the World Council, the Destruction mana, or the four golden Hero Tickets sitting in his Lord Inventory.
’Lia deserves a normal life,’ Silas thought firmly. ’She deserves to wake up without worrying about rent, eat fresh fruit until she’s full, and complain about math homework with her friends...’
As for himself, Silas liked his current trajectory.
He wasn’t some tragic avenger brooding in the dark as he had a territory to feed, an army to build, and a life here in the civilized sectors that was rapidly stabilizing.
’That said... I need to start liquidating the raw ores we hauled from the mines,’ he calculated, his mind shifting into cold commercial gears.
Blessed Land had stripped tons of high-grade ores during their mining arc and right now, it was sitting in his warehouse reserves, doing nothing.𝚏𝐫𝚎𝗲𝕨𝐞𝐛𝕟𝚘𝐯𝚎𝗹.𝕔𝐨𝗺
To turn that raw haul into functional untraceable capital for his regular identity, he needed an established institutional partner.
’The Obsidian Anvil Consortium...’ Silas recalled, his eyes narrowing slightly as he recalled the market reports.
The Obsidian Anvil was a massive cross-continental mining and metallurgical syndicate currently running a major commercial partnership with the LAB as of right now.

According to the trade circulars, if an independent contractor supplied them with more than five tons of verified high-purity star-iron within a single calendar month, the syndicate would issue an Obsidian Black Card, an elite border-free commercial passport that bypassed standard customs duties, granted private shipping corridors, and offered unlimited banking clearance.

’Kara White handles the world,’ Silas thought, a slow razor-sharp smirk tugging at his lips. ’After all, she’s a Gold Core monster who terrifies the Council but Silas Graves needs to be a titan in his own right down here... When the time comes to formally present myself to the Bloom family, so when Seraphina and I bring our agreement to the table, I won’t have Matriarch Etilga looking down her nose at me like a penniless orphan clinging to her daughter’s skirts.’
CLACK!
The sharp heavy metallic sound of a hammer cocking broke the quiet of the empty boulevard and Silas stopped in his tracks.
From the mouth of a ruined concrete stairwell ten feet ahead, two men stepped out into the murky streetlights.
They were haggard, hollow-cheeked, and reeked of cheap synthetic narcotics and unwashed linen.
Their clothes were patchwork rags bound with industrial duct tape with their eyes wide, bloodshot, and ugly with the hollow desperation unique to drug fiends.
The taller one raised a rusted large-caliber semi-automatic pistol, pointing the barrel straight at Silas’s forehead.
His hand was trembling violently, his finger twitching against the trigger.

"P-Pockets," the man rasped, spitting flecks of yellow saliva onto the pavement. "Right now, suit boy. Watch, wallet, comm-pad... Throw ’em on the ground or I swear to the void I’ll blow your pretty brains all over that wall!"
Silas stood completely still with his hands resting easily at his sides as he looked at the rusted barrel of the gun.
For a brief quiet second, a strange distant nostalgia rippled through his chest.
He remembered when he was sixteen, dragging home a sack of bruised potatoes through Sector Five, freezing in terror whenever a piece of iron was pointed in his face.
In those days, a single lead slug traveling at high velocity was the hand of death as it meant Lia starving alone in a freezing room.
...Now?
Looking at the lead chamber, Silas didn’t even feel his pulse rise.
With his current bodily refinement and the passive power of his channels, that lead slug would flatten against his forehead like a wet wad of tissue paper, barely leaving a red mark.
A gun felt less like a deadly weapon and more like a poorly manufactured plastic toy.
The second man, shorter and holding an iron pipe wrapped in barbed wire, took an aggressive step forward.
"He didn’t hear you, Mal! Take his coat first! That wool is worth fifty credits easy—"
Silas let out a small tired sigh.
"You mean five hundred thousand..."
STEP!
Silas however simply leaned his weight forward, closing the ten-foot gap in a fraction of a second.
CRUNCH!
Silas’s right hand shot out with his fingers wrapping around the slide and barrel of the semi-automatic pistol like a steel vise.
With a casual, almost absentminded clench of his knuckles, the hardened steel sheared like dried bread.
Springs snapped, the firing pin cracked in two, and the entire receiver crumpled into an unrecognizable lump of crushed scrap metal with tiny brass shards scattering onto the asphalt.
The gunman stared down at his empty shredded palm, his bloodshot eyes threatening to pop clean out of his skull.
"W-Wha—"
"Run along," Silas said calmly, his voice smooth and lacking any malice. "Before I decide your kneecaps look better facing backward."
The two men didn’t wait.
They let out twin high-pitched shrieks of primal terror, turning on their heels and sprinting down the boulevard as if the devil himself had sprouted wings behind them!
Silas watched them scramble for about five paces.
’Wait a second...’
His eyes narrowed as he studied the frayed blue jacket of the taller man and the jagged scar across the back of the short one’s neck.
A memory from three years ago clicked into place.
He had spent two days in an abandoned processing plant cleaning industrial sludge out of a ventilation turbine, earning forty credits to buy penicillin for Lia’s lung fever.

On his walk home, these exact two bastards had ambushed him in a blind corner, cracked his ribs with an iron pipe, and taken every single copper, forcing him to beg a clinic nurse for sample packets in the pouring rain.
’I remember you two,’ Silas murmured with a cold vindictive smile spreading across his face.
VUM!
Silas released an invisible needle-thin sliver of his spiritual pressure, barely a fraction of a percent of his Gold Core density.
THUD! THUD!
Thirty feet away, both men dropped instantly with their consciousness snuffed out like candles in a hurricane.
Their faces planted into the greasy asphalt, completely unconscious.
Silas walked over with his shoes clicking leisurely against the stone as he crouched down beside the taller man, rummaging through his foul-smelling pockets with two fingers.
RATTLE!
He withdrew three crumpled paper bills and a handful of stamped brass tokens.

’Thirty Spirit Credits,’ Silas observed, counting the cash with a dry shake of his head. ’Filthy poor but considering you stole forty from me three years ago, I’ll count this as thirty credits plus interest... Call it divine retribution...’
He pocketed the notes, tossed the empty duct-tape wallet aside, and continued walking toward the sector boundary.
...After breaking their legs and ribs of course.
’Thirty credits... that’s just enough for a high-priority cab to Silverleaf.’
As he crossed the rusted iron bridge that separated the Sector Six quarantine zone from the outer ring, Silas let his mind drift back to the deeper archives of the World Vault.
’I still need to see Aki,’ he thought, his brow furrowing slightly as a serious edge entered his mind.
During his three hours wandering those ancient aisles with Number Five, he had skimmed dozens of personal journals belonging to the early World Kings.
He’d read the erratic paranoid treatises of the First King, and the classified royal medical manifests.
The Castellian bloodline was a walking miracle of genetic dominance, but it was also a curse.
The royal house had accumulated hundreds of lethal enemies over the centuries who lacked the power to challenge the World King openly.

Many of the early princes and princesses had suffered from congenital meridian blockages, esoteric spiritual parasites, and generational curses woven into their bloodlines before they were even drawn from the womb.

’Aki’s channels aren’t inert because she’s defective...’ Silas realized, the memory of her desperate tear-stained eyes flashing in his thoughts. ’When she was using the gloves, I felt the mana circulating through her veins easily so it wasn’t dead... I can guess that it was suppressed or deactivated somehow so maybe her Awakening wasn’t a failure but it was artificially halted from the inside.’
Whether it was a foreign curse planted by an imperial rival, or something far darker buried within the palace itself, he couldn’t be certain yet.
But he knew one thing... He wasn’t going to leave her rotting in that golden cage.
’I’ll have to examine her personally when the summit delegations disperse,’ Silas decided firmly.
Reaching the neon-lit perimeter of the main thoroughfare, Silas spotted an idling cab with its yellow roof-light glowing through the exhaust haze.
He stepped up to the driver’s window, shoved the thirty Spirit Credit notes through the glass, and leaned down.
"Silverleaf District," Silas instructed. "It’s a private residential estate with a good fence and step on it."
