He remembered when he was sixteen, dragging home a sack of bruised potatoes through Sector Five, freezing in terror whenever a piece of iron was pointed in his face.
In those days, a single lead slug traveling at high velocity was the hand of death as it meant Lia starving alone in a freezing room.
...Now?
Looking at the lead chamber, Silas didn’t even feel his pulse rise.
With his current bodily refinement and the passive power of his channels, that lead slug would flatten against his forehead like a wet wad of tissue paper, barely leaving a red mark.
A gun felt less like a deadly weapon and more like a poorly manufactured plastic toy.
The second man, shorter and holding an iron pipe wrapped in barbed wire, took an aggressive step forward.
"He didn’t hear you, Mal!
Take his coat first!
That wool is worth fifty credits easy—"
Silas let out a small tired sigh.
"You mean five hundred thousand..."
STEP!
Silas however simply leaned his weight forward, closing the ten-foot gap in a fraction of a second.
CRUNCH!
Silas’s right hand shot out with his fingers wrapping around the slide and barrel of the semi-automatic pistol like a steel vise.
With a casual, almost absentminded clench of his knuckles, the hardened steel sheared like dried bread.
Springs snapped, the firing pin cracked in two, and the entire receiver crumpled into an unrecognizable lump of crushed scrap metal with tiny brass shards scattering onto the asphalt.
The gunman stared down at his empty shredded palm, his bloodshot eyes threatening to pop clean out of his skull.
"W-Wha—"
"Run along," Silas said calmly, his voice smooth and lacking any malice.
"Before I decide your kneecaps look better facing backward."
The two men didn’t wait.
They let out twin high-pitched shrieks of primal terror, turning on their heels and sprinting down the boulevard as if the devil himself had sprouted wings behind them!
Silas watched them scramble for about five paces.
’Wait a second...’
His eyes narrowed as he studied the frayed blue jacket of the taller man and the jagged scar across the back of the short one’s neck.
A memory from three years ago clicked into place.
He had spent two days in an abandoned processing plant cleaning industrial sludge out of a ventilation turbine, earning forty credits to buy penicillin for Lia’s lung fever.

On his walk home, these exact two bastards had ambushed him in a blind corner, cracked his ribs with an iron pipe, and taken every single copper, forcing him to beg a clinic nurse for sample packets in the pouring rain.
’I remember you two,’ Silas murmured with a cold vindictive smile spreading across his face.
VUM!
Silas released an invisible needle-thin sliver of his spiritual pressure, barely a fraction of a percent of his Gold Core density.
THUD!
THUD!
Thirty feet away, both men dropped instantly with their consciousness snuffed out like candles in a hurricane.
Their faces planted into the greasy asphalt, completely unconscious.
Silas walked over with his shoes clicking leisurely against the stone as he crouched down beside the taller man, rummaging through his foul-smelling pockets with two fingers.
RATTLE!
He withdrew three crumpled paper bills and a handful of stamped brass tokens.

’Thirty Spirit Credits,’ Silas observed, counting the cash with a dry shake of his head. ’Filthy poor but considering you stole forty from me three years ago, I’ll count this as thirty credits plus interest...
Call it divine retribution...’
He pocketed the notes, tossed the empty duct-tape wallet aside, and continued walking toward the sector boundary.
...After breaking their legs and ribs of course.
’Thirty credits... that’s just enough for a high-priority cab to Silverleaf.’
As he crossed the rusted iron bridge that separated the Sector Six quarantine zone from the outer ring, Silas let his mind drift back to the deeper archives of the World Vault.
’I still need to see Aki,’ he thought, his brow furrowing slightly as a serious edge entered his mind.
During his three hours wandering those ancient aisles with Number Five, he had skimmed dozens of personal journals belonging to the early World Kings.
He’d read the erratic paranoid treatises of the First King, and the classified royal medical manifests.
The Castellian bloodline was a walking miracle of genetic dominance, but it was also a curse.
The royal house had accumulated hundreds of lethal enemies over the centuries who lacked the power to challenge the World King openly.

Many of the early princes and princesses had suffered from congenital meridian blockages, esoteric spiritual parasites, and generational curses woven into their bloodlines before they were even drawn from the womb.

’Aki’s channels aren’t inert because she’s defective...’ Silas realized, the memory of her desperate tear-stained eyes flashing in his thoughts. ’When she was using the gloves, I felt the mana circulating through her veins easily so it wasn’t dead...
I can guess that it was suppressed or deactivated somehow so maybe her Awakening wasn’t a failure but it was artificially halted from the inside.’
Whether it was a foreign curse planted by an imperial rival, or something far darker buried within the palace itself, he couldn’t be certain yet.
But he knew one thing...
He wasn’t going to leave her rotting in that golden cage.
’I’ll have to examine her personally when the summit delegations disperse,’ Silas decided firmly.
Reaching the neon-lit perimeter of the main thoroughfare, Silas spotted an idling cab with its yellow roof-light glowing through the exhaust haze.
He stepped up to the driver’s window, shoved the thirty Spirit Credit notes through the glass, and leaned down.
"Silverleaf District," Silas instructed.
"It’s a private residential estate with a good fence and step on it."

chapters.title: Chapter 598: Penelope’s Worries [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The driver looked at the crumpled cash, looked at Silas’s immaculate charcoal suit, swallowed hard, and opened the window properly.
"Sure sire!"
The high-grade security gates of the Silverleaf estate parted with a smooth silent glide.
The yellow cab rolled away into the quiet tree-lined avenue, leaving Silas standing alone on the pristine cobblestone driveway.
The sharp clean scent of manicured pine trees, blooming mountain jasmine, and filtered air washed over him, completely purging the rancid reek of Sector Six from his senses.
Silas let out a long luxurious exhale, loosening his silk tie by half an inch.
’Home.’
He walked up the sweeping driveway with his fingers lightly brushing across the sleek chassis of the Zenith IVR luxury cruiser parked under the portico.
He climbed the wide marble steps, unlocked the reinforced front door with his biometric thumbprint, and swung the heavy oak panel open.
"I’m back," Silas called out softly, stepping into the grand foyer.
CREAK!
He stopped as the person standing in the center of the polished hardwood hallway, staring straight at him, was Penelope Whitmore.
The eleven-year-old girl was frozen like a porcelain doll.
Her vibrant purple hair, identical in shade to her older sister Harper’s, was tied into neat twin pigtails, but her usually pristine clothes were rumpled with her stockings slightly twisted.
Her face was as pale as fresh chalk with her large eyes wide, bloodshot, and rimmed with red... They were trembling with an intensity that looked completely unnatural on a child.
Silas’s brow furrowed as he immediately slipped off his leather shoes, stepping onto the indoor mat.
"Hey, Penelope," Silas said, keeping his tone gentle and grounded. "What’s wrong? Why are you standing in the dark? Where’s Harper?"
He’d noticed Harper’s absence at the World Council Summit earlier that morning.
He’d assumed that House Whitmore, while prominent in commercial trade, simply lacked the standing to sit at the Grand Table alongside the Nine Powers.
Elora hadn’t been in the chamber either, which hadn’t made sense given the classified nature of the proceedings.
Penelope didn’t answer with her usual bratty sharp-tongued arrogance.
Instead, a violent shiver rippled through her small frame.
Her teeth clicked together as she pressed her back against the wall, making way for him to enter with her hands trembling so hard she had to tuck them into her skirt pockets.
Silas stepped into the main living room, his instincts flaring with quiet cold alarm.
"Welcome home, Master Silas!"
Martha hurried out from the adjoining kitchen, wiping her hands on her immaculate white maid’s apron.
The petite middle-aged woman had visible lines of worry etched across her warm forehead, her dark eyes darting nervously toward the purple-haired girl.

"She’s been sitting on that rug since after you left, Master Silas," Martha whispered, leaning close so her voice wouldn’t carry. "She hasn’t eaten a single bite... She hasn’t had a sip of tea and she wouldn’t speak to me, she wouldn’t speak to the young miss... she just kept staring at the front door waiting for you."
On the expansive velvet sofa, Lia and Kaede were huddled together, looking at Penelope with deep agonizing concern.
Lia’s large brown eyes were wide with the tiny crescent scar on her forehead catching the sunlight as she fidgeted with the hem of her oversized knit sweater.

Beside her, Kaede, the dark-haired exchange student from the eastern sector, sat with her hands folded neatly over her pleated skirt with her expressive dark eyes darting between Silas and her purple-haired friend.
’This isn’t a child throwing a tantrum,’ Silas realized instantly. ’Something has gone terribly wrong.’
Silas walked over, kneeling down on one knee in front of Penelope so his eyes were level with hers.
He reached out with his right hand, gently resting his calloused palm against the girl’s trembling shoulder.
"Penelope," Silas said softly. "Look at me... I’m here so tell me what happened."
The touch broke whatever fragile dam was holding the girl together.
Penelope swallowed hard with a ragged choking sob tearing from her throat as tears finally spilled over her lower lashes, carving clean tracks through the dust on her cheeks.
"My sister..." Penelope wept, her voice trembling so violently she could barely string the syllables together. "Silas... my big sister is gone. She’s... she isn’t herself anymore!"
Silas’s jaw tightened. "Take a breath. What do you mean she isn’t herself?"

"She... she left the estate early this morning," Penelope cried, shaking her head frantically, her twin pigtails whipping across her shoulders. "She was supposed to be preparing the trade manifests for the port authority but when she was about to leave... she looked right through me! Her face was completely stiff, like a frozen mask and her eyes... Silas, her eyes weren’t purple anymore! There was this... this horrible sickening green glint spinning behind her pupils!"
The girl grabbed Silas’s sleeve with both hands, clutching the fine charcoal wool as if it were the only lifeline in a storm.

"She talked to me like... like she didn’t even know who I was!" Penelope sobbed, her voice cracking. "She spoke in this dry voice... she just packed a single leather case, walked out to the airfield, and left! Before I came here, even though I didn’t want to, I ran to the city enforcers, but the desk sergeants laughed at me! They said Lady Harper was an adult and had the legal right to travel on business! Nobody would believe me! Nobody! Only you would know... only you can help her! Please, Silas... someone is controlling her! Something is inside her head!"
A cold heavy dread dropped straight into Silas’s stomach but he didn’t hesitate.
He pulled his black phone from his pocket, his thumb rapidly unlocking the screen and navigating directly to Harper’s secure messaging thread.
’Empty...’
His breath hitched.
The screen was completely blank.
A series of twelve encrypted notifications showed that Harper had transmitted an array of urgent messages to his private number before today but he hadn’t even checked upon arriving.
Every single message had been remotely purged from the server side.
’A clean wipe,’ Silas analyzed with his pulse quickening. ’Whoever took her knew she had my number so they scrubbed the text logs to prevent a trace.’
"Hold on," Silas muttered, his fingers flying across the glass.
He tapped into the secondary background locator.
BEEP!
A tiny pulsing red dot materialized on the holographic continental map and Silas stared at the coordinates.
The dot wasn’t in the Europa Directorate... It wasn’t in Columbia, nor was it heading toward the eastern sectors...

It was currently moving at six hundred miles per hour over the southern maritime trenches, cutting straight through international airspace, vectoring directly toward the desert continent of Khemet with the destination being Iunu.
The Sun-Crown’s capital city.
A terrible suffocating chill clamped around Silas’s heart.

’Khemet?’ Silas thought, his mind racing through the events of the morning. ’Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur was pale as a corpse at the Grand Table so why the hell is Harper being flown straight into the heart of the Sun-Crown if she’s mind controlled?!’

"Silas... please," Penelope begged, her small hands tugging frantically at his jacket with her face buried against his chest as she wept openly. "She loves you so much... she talks about you every single night! She talks about wanting to marry you, about building a grand estate together... you have to be her husband! You have to save her! Please don’t let them hurt my sister!"
Lia rose from the couch, her hands clasped tightly against her chest, her brown eyes shiny with unshed tears.
"Big brother... we have to help Lady Harper."
Silas looked down at the weeping girl clutching his coat.
If this were anyone else, he might have paused to calculate the fallout.
He might have questioned whether getting tangled in the internal affairs of the Sun-Crown was worth the risk.
’Harper...’
He closed his eyes for a single second and he saw her bright, mischievous purple eyes.
’That idiot...’
His hand trembled slightly, not with fear, but with a cold rage that made the gravity in the foyer dip by a fraction.
’If anyone touches a single hair on her head,’ Silas swore silently, his teeth locking together, ’I will burn the white walls of Iunu to absolute cinder...’
He opened his eyes with his expression completely calm, not mirroring the rage echoing in his soul.

"We’re going to save her," Silas said firmly, gently patting Penelope’s head. "I promise you, Penelope... I will bring Harper back, and whoever put that green light in her eyes will pay for it a thousand times over..."
He rose to his full height, turning his gaze toward the kitchen.
"Martha."
"Yes, Master Silas!" Martha answered instantly, standing at attention, her apron strings pulled tight.
"Pack our travel cases and book five private first-class flights on the next transport out of the central terminal heading directly to Iunu..."
Martha blinked, her eyes widening. "F-Five, sir?"
Silas looked back at Lia and Kaede.
"Lia," Silas said, offering his little sister a gentle reassuring smile. "You said Valoria Academy had a seasonal recess starting next week, right?"
Lia nodded slowly, her fingers fidgeting. "Y-Yes, but... Big brother, is it safe?"
"It’s completely safe," Silas said smoothly. "Why don’t we turn this into a family trip? We’ll take a little vacation to the southern sun."
He turned toward the dark-haired girl on the sofa.
Kaede’s bright expressive dark eyes lit up with sudden vivid excitement with a charming blush dusting her round cheeks as she sat up straight.

"A trip?!" Kaede gasped, her hands clapping together. "To Khemet?! Oh, I have to call my brother right now! He will definitely let me go if I tell him I’m traveling with Lia’s family! I’m going to pack my sun hats!"
Silas let out a quiet sigh, a massive invisible sweatdrop practically forming behind his ear.
’I’m not sure this is exactly the time for sun hats, kid,’ he thought, shaking his head.
Yet, he knew his sister.

If he tried to leave Lia behind in Silverleaf while he flew off to a hostile superpower, Penelope would scream, Lia would spend three days crying into her pillow, and their household security could be compromised by whatever faction had abducted Harper.

’It’s safer to keep them within my sensory range,’ Silas resolved. ’I’ll book the most heavily fortified, five-star luxury suite in the diplomatic district of Iunu... I’ll leave Martha, Lia, Penelope, and Kaede inside a high-grade place with enough defensive wards to stop an orbital strike and while they’re safe in the hotel... I’ll go hunting.’
He looked down at his phone, watching the red beacon blink steadily across the digital map.
’Hold on, Harper,’ Silas thought, his eyes turning cold as winter ice. ’I’m coming...’
[Republic of Columbia, Deep-Level Research Facility No. 95]
Night had fallen over the western continent.

Deep beneath the jagged red mesas of the Columbia frontier, thirty stories beneath the desert bedrock, Research Facility No. 95 hummed with the staggering multi-billion-credit energy of a nation preparing for war.

President Julian Vanderbilt Senior stood in the primary observation corridor, his iron-gray hair slightly disheveled, wearing a crisp white alchemical laboratory coat over his charcoal pinstripe trousers.
Large protective polarized goggles rested over his spectacles, and a massive self-satisfied grin was plastered across his face.
It was, without question, the greatest night of his entire political career.

Sure, Blessed Land had humiliated him and sure, that monstrous woman Kara White had squeezed forty billion credits out of the Columbia treasury like water from a dry sponge but forty billion was paper! It was numbers on a screen!
What rested inside the reinforced titanium containment chamber ten feet ahead of him was the holy grail of military sorcery... the Mana-Bypass Gloves as he called it.

’Forty billion?’ Vanderbilt scoffed inwardly, his signet rings clicking rhythmically against the stainless-steel handrail. ’The moment we reverse-engineer this artificial neural weave and adapt it to our mechanized infantry suits, Columbia will control the global arms trade for the next century... We’ll make four hundred billion within the first fiscal quarter! That greedy unrefined slum bitch practically handed us the keys to the world!’
And the sweetest part of all was that the World King himself had endorsed the project...
The heavy pressurized blast doors at the end of the corridor slid open with a hydraulic hiss.
HSSSSSSS!
A man stepped into the white sterile light of the observation wing.
Vanderbilt turned, his chest swelling with reverence.

The man approaching looked barely fifty years old, walking with a steady commanding posture, wearing long flowing scholar’s robes woven from midnight-blue star-silk embroidered with silver geometric mandalas.
His gray hair was neatly bound behind his neck, his face stern, weathered, and etched with the profound arrogant confidence of someone who had unraveled the secrets of the cosmos.
This was Grand Master Varun and he was a living legend on the terrestrial plane.
He was over two hundred years old, a great-grandfather of an entire lineage of rune Lords, and widely regarded as the absolute apex runemaster in modern history.

Centuries ago, Varun had been a Lord in the Sovereign Realm, commanding his own territory but when his core was fractured during a disastrous territorial siege and his people died, he had been forcibly ejected from the realm, returning to Earth as an independent adventurer.
Rather than succumbing to despair, Varun had spent the next century and a half dedicating every waking second of his unnatural lifespan to the mastery of runes.
It was an open secret among the high ministries that if any member of the World Council ever perished, Varun was the primary candidate slated to ascend to a seat.
"President Vanderbilt," Varun spoke.

"Grand Master Varun!" Vanderbilt beamed, stepping forward to clasp the scholar’s hand with aggressive corporate warmth. "Words cannot express the Republic’s gratitude for your presence... The World King personally promised your expertise, and Columbia is honored."
Varun offered a stiff thin smile, adjusting the silver sleeves of his robes.

"Let us dispense with the political theater, Julian. I am not here for pleasantries. I was told you secured an anomaly, an external conduit capable of forcing secondary multi-elemental pathways through an Unawakened’s physiology."
"Indeed," Vanderbilt chuckled, gesturing toward the reinforced observation window. "Come. See the future of human warfare."

And the sweetest part of all was that the World King himself had endorsed the project...
The heavy pressurized blast doors at the end of the corridor slid open with a hydraulic hiss.
HSSSSSSS!
A man stepped into the white sterile light of the observation wing.
Vanderbilt turned, his chest swelling with reverence.

The man approaching looked barely fifty years old, walking with a steady commanding posture, wearing long flowing scholar’s robes woven from midnight-blue star-silk embroidered with silver geometric mandalas.
His gray hair was neatly bound behind his neck, his face stern, weathered, and etched with the profound arrogant confidence of someone who had unraveled the secrets of the cosmos.
This was Grand Master Varun and he was a living legend on the terrestrial plane.
He was over two hundred years old, a great-grandfather of an entire lineage of rune Lords, and widely regarded as the absolute apex runemaster in modern history.

Centuries ago, Varun had been a Lord in the Sovereign Realm, commanding his own territory but when his core was fractured during a disastrous territorial siege and his people died, he had been forcibly ejected from the realm, returning to Earth as an independent adventurer.
Rather than succumbing to despair, Varun had spent the next century and a half dedicating every waking second of his unnatural lifespan to the mastery of runes.
It was an open secret among the high ministries that if any member of the World Council ever perished, Varun was the primary candidate slated to ascend to a seat.
"President Vanderbilt," Varun spoke.
"Grand Master Varun!" Vanderbilt beamed, stepping forward to clasp the scholar’s hand with aggressive corporate warmth.
"Words cannot express the Republic’s gratitude for your presence...
The World King personally promised your expertise, and Columbia is honored."
Varun offered a stiff thin smile, adjusting the silver sleeves of his robes.
"Let us dispense with the political theater, Julian.
I am not here for pleasantries.
I was told you secured an anomaly, an external conduit capable of forcing secondary multi-elemental pathways through an Unawakened’s physiology."
"Indeed," Vanderbilt chuckled, gesturing toward the reinforced observation window.
"Come.
See the future of human warfare."

paragraphs: They walked up to the thick triple-layered quartz glass, looking down into the hermetically sealed testing chamber below.
At the center of the chamber, resting upon a pedestal of polished white titanium, lay the pair of midnight-blue combat gloves.
Under the harsh halogen floodlights, the star-iron weave gleamed quietly, the delicate crimson and emerald runes along the cuffs humming with a dormant light.

"Before we initiate physical testing," Vanderbilt noted, tapping the glass with a manicured finger, "the seller, Kara White, made several loud theatrical claims regarding operational hazards... She claimed an unverified user would suffer catastrophic meridian blowout so naturally, I assume it was mere bluster designed to protect her trade secrets. However, as a precaution, I must ask... Grand Master, do you detect any malicious, booby-trapped fail-safes embedded within the weave?"
Varun let out a dry condescending chuckle.

He closed his eyes, raising his right hand toward the glass as an intricate silver runic array flared around his palm, casting an invisible high-density diagnostic pulse through the quartz, washing over the gloves like a spectral net.
For ten seconds, Varun stood motionless, reading the mana reflections then he lowered his hand, his expression dripping with pure disdain.

"Amateurish posturing," Varun declared flatly. "The weave is complex, certainly, the conductive threading utilizes an unconventional high-velocity spiral pattern that mimics capillary action but as for defensive curses? Booby-trapped detonation runes? There are none as the mana channels are completely open too... It is a standard bypass and even a child could wear it."
Vanderbilt let out a loud triumphant laugh.

"Hah! I knew it! The barbarian was trying to scare us with ghost stories!" Vanderbilt turned to his chief research scientist, waving his hand aggressively. "Initiate Phase One! Bring in the test subject!"
Down in the testing chamber, a side door slid open.
A young man clad in a gray institutional jumpsuit walked out, escorted by two armed guards.
He was an Unawakened laborer from the lower Columbia salt mines, heavily compensated with sovereign credits to serve as a test vessel.
"Subject 44," the lead scientist barked over the intercom. "Step forward to the pedestal. Slip your hands into the conduits..."
The young man swallowed hard, his hands trembling slightly as he approached the white titanium stand.
He picked up the midnight-blue gloves, feeling the cool supple star-iron leather against his skin.
’I just have to do this...’
He slid his left hand in then his right.
The gloves fit smoothly, the leather automatically cinching tight around his wrists with a soft click.
CLICK!
The young man stood there for three seconds, blinking.
He looked up toward the observation window with a relieved smile breaking across his nervous face.
"Uh... hey, boss? It feels... totally fine. Kind of warm, actually. Like a winter mitten—"
SPLAT-BOOM!
Without a single microsecond of warning, Subject 44 violently detonated.
The pressure inside his arms simply spiked to forty thousand atmospheres in the span of a single heartbeat...
His forearms, his elbows, his shoulders, and his entire upper torso ruptured outward in an instantaneous shower of pressurized crimson blood, shattered rib bones, and pulverized muscle tissue.
SPLAT!
The concussive wet slap echoed off the titanium walls like a cannon shot, splattering thick steaming red gore across the inside of the observation window.
DRIP! DRIP! DRIP!
The room went dead silent.
Up in the observation deck, Vanderbilt froze mid-smile with his polarized goggles coated in a spray of phantom dread as he stared at the bloody smear on the glass.
Beside him, Grand Master Varun’s jaw went completely slack as his silver mandalas flickered and died.
"W-What..." Varun stammered, his noble composure cracking down the center. "What was that?!"

"Grand Master!" Vanderbilt roared, spinning around, his face turning an apoplectic shade of purple. "You said there were no booby-traps! You said a child could wear it! The man just turned into strawberry jam in front of my eyes!"

"Silence!" Varun snapped, his pride violently wounded as his old eyes flashed with anger. "The fault was on the man... The subject’s cellular walls were clearly deficient! His body was too fragile to absorb the initial sync!"
Varun shoved past the technicians, walking straight to the chamber’s airlock terminal.
"I will personally neutralize the variable," Varun growled, his fingers moving across the control slate.
He etched a glowing golden suppression rune into the console, routing the mana through the chamber’s ceiling projectors.
Down below, a golden beam of light lanced downward, bathing the gloves in an impenetrable suppression rune designed to lock down any foreign feeling.

"There," Varun stated arrogantly, dusting off his blue silk sleeves. "I have laid an imperial Grand Master suppression seal directly over the primary intake valves... Even if an ancient curse were dormant within the threads, it is now bound in chains of iron so bring in the next subject!"

Vanderbilt turned his bloodshot eyes toward the second test subject standing in the holding pen, a stocky middle-aged maintenance worker who was currently shivering so violently he could barely hold his trousers up.
"I-I’m not going in there!" the worker shrieked, backing away from the door. "You saw what happened to 44! He blew up! His ribs hit the ceiling!"

"You will go in there," Vanderbilt hissed, stepping up to the glass and keying the intercom, his voice dripping with ruthless authority, "or I will cancel your family’s medical coverage, evict your wife from the residential sector, and have your sons drafted into the military by midnight... Put the gloves on, or your entire bloodline starves in the dirt."
The worker broke down in silent tears, nodding weakly.

He stepped out into the bloody testing chamber, carefully avoiding the wet chunks of bone on the floor, and reached the pedestal and with shaking pale fingers, the man picked up the gloves, which were now glowing with Varun’s golden suppression runes.
He slid his hands inside.
CLICK!
The gloves cinched.
One second passed... Two seconds... Three seconds...
The worker took a ragged trembling breath as nothing hurt and his arms were still attached.
The golden suppression light was holding firm!
"I-I’m okay..." the worker whispered, looking up at the glass with tear-stained eyes. "I’m not blowing up—"
"Pull the trigger!" Vanderbilt ordered eagerly over the comms. "Form a fist! Channel the wind mana!"
The worker nodded, taking a deep breath, and slowly began to curl his fingers into a tight fist.
PULL! KRZZZZZZZZ-CRACK! SPLAT-BOOM!
The suppression seal was swallowed whole as the backlash this time was twice as violent!

The man’s body didn’t even have time to register the pain, instead, the pressure detonated straight through his cardiovascular system, vaporizing him from the waist up into an explosive cloud of red vapor and pulverized meat that slammed against the ceiling with a thwack.
PLOP!
A chunk of wet lung tissue slid slowly down the observation window, leaving a thick glistening red streak.
"ARE YOU OUT OF YOUR GODDAMN MIND?!" Vanderbilt screamed, completely crashing out.
He grabbed Grand Master Varun by the pristine collar of his two-hundred-year-old star-silk robes, shaking the ancient scholar violently with his spectacles flying off his face.

"You had ONE JOB!" Vanderbilt shrieked, flecks of foam flying from his lips! "One job! You are supposed to be the greatest runemaster on the planet! The World King promised me a genius! I paid forty billion credits for these gloves, and all you’ve done is turn two of my employees into pasta sauce! What the fuck is wrong with you?!"
Varun violently shoved Vanderbilt off him, his face burning bright crimson with humiliation.

"Unhand me, you mongrel!" Varun roared, his voice echoing through the facility. "Do not dare lecture me on the intricacies of the arcane! My suppression seal was absolute! It was swallowed! Something inside those gloves is actively consuming external runic interference!"
Varun turned on his heel with his robes billowing as he stormed straight toward the primary disinfection airlock.
"Grand Master, what are you doing?!" the lead scientist yelled.
"I am resolving this myself!" Varun bellowed, slamming his palm against the override release.

The heavy blast doors hissed open, and the two-hundred-year-old runic master marched directly into the bloody gore-spattered testing chamber with his boots squelching through puddles of fresh crimson runoff.
’I... I... I don’t understand.’
He reached the titanium pedestal, glaring down at the midnight-blue gloves.
’I’ve studied these before.’

He swept his hands forward, channeling his immense century-honed spiritual perception directly into the star-iron weave as he closed his eyes, searching every microscopic thread, tracing every millimeter of conductive silver wire.

’Clean,’ Varun thought, his brow furrowing in maddening confusion. ’It’s completely clean! There are no hidden traps! There are no secondary runes or cores! Why in the name of the First King are these people detonating?!’
His pride, bruised and battered by Vanderbilt’s insults, finally pushed him over the edge.
’I am a Grand Master of Earth...’ Varun told himself fiercely. ’I commanded an army in the Sovereign Realm and my core refinement is unbreakable... If there is an anomaly, it will yield to my will!’
Varun reached down, picked up the gloves, and thrust his hands inside.
CLICK!
The star-iron cinched around his wrists and Varun stood there with his eyes closed as he braced for the spike.
Five seconds passed... Ten seconds... Nothing...
The air in the room was calm and his meridians were steady as not a single thread of mana spiked in his chest.
’So what...?’
Varun slowly opened his eyes, looking down at his gloved hands with a smug arrogant sneer returning to his lips.

"You see?!" Varun shouted toward the observation window, holding his hands up triumphantly. "It was the inadequacy of your people! The mortal vessels were simply too weak! In the hands of a true master, the conduits are completely sta—"
A voice echoed through the sterile chamber as Varun froze.
The voice wasn’t coming from the intercom and it wasn’t coming from Vanderbilt either.
It was a woman’s voice that was smooth, dripping with arrogance while coming directly from the star-iron weave around his knuckles.
"...you’re the pathetic little thieves, huh?"
Up in the observation deck, Vanderbilt and the technicians pressed their faces against the glass with their eyes wide.
"What the hell was that?!"
Varun stared down at his hands, his heart suddenly hammering against his ribs like a panicked drum.
"W-Who is speaking?!"𝕗𝚛𝚎𝚎𝐰𝗲𝗯𝗻𝚘𝚟𝚎𝗹.𝕔𝐨𝕞
"Ahem!"
The voice cleared its throat, sounding remarkably annoyed, as if someone had just woken her up from a mid-afternoon nap.
"Allow me to introduce myself," the voice drawled with sarcasm. "I am Rowenna... The Grand Runemaser of Blessed Land and honestly, I am thoroughly disappointed."
Varun’s breath caught in his throat. "Rowenna...?"

"I regularly weave two distinct fail-safes into my proprietary works to prevent low-tier gutter trash from reverse-engineering my research," Rowenna explained, her tone sounding like an exhausted professor scolding a remarkably stupid student. "The first fail-safe is the conduits require Aki’s blood elasticity, which means common mortals blow up like over-inflated bladders but you already discovered that twice, apparently... How messy and unhygienic, here I was thinking Brida was an ogre."
She let out a dry clicking tut through the leather.

"And the second fail-safe... is specifically designed for arrogant, self-proclaimed ’scholars’ who attempt to perform unauthorized diagnostic scans and steal my intellectual property. It is truly a shame... for you."
Varun’s face went completely pale with his pride instantly flaring into defensive panic!

"Impudent child!" Varun roared, his voice cracking into a high pitch as he raised his gloved hands, his eyes glowing with bright silver mana. "I am Grand Master Varun! The foremost runic authority on the Earth! I have unraveled the works of the First Era! I have mapped runes of the void! There is no rune woven by a backwater hedge-witch that I cannot dismantle!"
Through the star-iron weave, Rowenna let out a loud mocking hysterical peel of laughter.
"Grand Master, my ass!" Rowenna cackled, her voice bouncing off the titanium walls. "Can’t you even see the runes, you blind old bat?!"
Varun blinked with cold sweat drenching his silk collar. ’What runes?! There are no runes!’
"Tch. Pathetic," Rowenna sighed. "Fine. Since you’re so hopelessly beneath my level... allow me to open your eyes."
SNAP!
An invisible veil dissolved within the sub-fabric of the gloves.
BZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZT!
Before Varun’s horrified dilated pupils, the physical reality of the midnight-blue leather violently vanished...
In its place materialized a blinding labyrinthine nightmare of microscopic glowing purple script!

There weren’t ten runes... There weren’t a hundred either... There were tens of thousands of contradictory runic equations, woven so tightly together that they formed an impenetrable three-dimensional cage of pure madness.
Runes were stacked upon runes... spatial vectors collided with feedback loops and elemental bypasses were knotted together like a nest of rabid vipers.
It was filled with runes so monstrous that simply looking at the equations for two seconds made Varun’s nerves bleed with a sharp agonizing migraine tearing through his temporal lobes.

’How is this item even functioning?!’ Varun screamed in the shattered weeping silence of his mind. ’This isn’t an alchemical circuit! This is an arcane disaster waiting for an excuse to detonate! What kind of psychotic demon engineered this monstrosity?!’
The purple runes began to rapidly heat up as the star-iron leather started to glow, turning from dull gray to cherry-red, then to blinding incandescent white.
HSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!
Smoke billowed from the seams with the smell of scorched flesh filling the chamber as the intense heat seared straight through Varun’s palms!

"You see," Rowenna’s voice echoed cheerfully through the white-hot metal, "when I was still an apprentice at the Imperial Academy, before my Lord summoned me to Blessed Land, the senior professors stole my research all the time... They took my papers, took my credit, and called my equations dangerous so I made a solemn sacred vow... the next person who tried to reverse-engineer my work without my express written consent would be the first person I punished with the full weight of my academic wrath."

"RUN!" Varun shrieked at the top of his lungs, spinning on his heel!
He bolted for the airlock door with his blue silk robes smoking as he ran with the desperate speed of a dying beast.
Up on the observation deck, Vanderbilt was already moving backward with his boots scrambling across the polished tiles as he threw his hands up in horror!
"GET BACK, YOU FOOL!" Vanderbilt screamed through the microphone, his face twisted in raw animalistic terror. "DON’T BRING THAT THING OUT HERE! GO BACK INTO THE CHAMBER! GO BACK—"
It was too late.

FLASH!

The white-hot explosion detonated outward directly from his center of mass, vaporizing the ancient two-hundred-year-old runic master into fine subatomic ash in the span of a single picosecond...
And then, the energy expanded.
A colossal expanding sphere of pure golden radiance tore through the airlock, shattering the triple-layered quartz observation window into millions of microscopic dust motes!
In that final frozen second before the blast wave reached his face, before the searing celestial heat stripped the goggles from his skull, Julian Vanderbilt Senior could see it.
Floating in the heart of the brilliant blinding light, hovering like a mocking specter from his worst nightmares...
He saw Kara White’s face.
Her dark half-lidded eyes gleaming with cold lazy amusement wither single right hand waving a cheerful dismissive goodbye.
Her lips curved into that exact same infuriating smile she had worn while chewing shrimp over the official documents of state.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

A deafening earth-shattering roar ripped through the underground foundations of Research Facility No. 95 as the blast wave tore through reinforced titanium bulkheads like wet tissue paper, collapsing thirty stories of desert bedrock into an inferno of fire, smoke, and shattered concrete.

Above ground, far out in the quiet desert of the Columbia frontier, the red mesas violently buckled as a mushrooming pillar of brilliant golden light punched through the crust, illuminating the dark night sky for a hundred miles in every direction, incinerating forty billion credits of ambition into glowing radioactive dust.

WHOOSH!

The royal transport flagship Aethel-Sun carved through the upper thermosphere like a gilded leviathan, its armored hull of polished white titanium and celestial gold alloy deflecting the brutal midday radiance of the Great Dunes thirty thousand feet below.

Escorting it in tight arrowhead formations were eight high-speed combat cruisers of the Sun-Crown’s guard, their jets emitting synchronized hums that parted the thin desert clouds into rippling waves of heat haze.
Inside the Aethel-Sun’s primary observation lounge, the atmosphere was suffocatingly quiet.
The lounge was expansive, floored with dark lapis lazuli tiles imported from the deep mountain veins of the eastern reaches.
Heavy curtains of spun cloth-of-gold hung along the panoramic viewing windows, filtering the harsh glare into a warm amber twilight.
Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur sat upright on a high-backed divan carved from petrified cedar with his posture rigid and formal despite the private quarters.
He still wore his double-breasted military dress uniform of immaculate white wool, the golden pectoral collar resting heavy against his collarbones and its lapis inlay catching the dim light.
His bronze skin, usually flawless and radiating the haughty vitality of the apex solar lineage, looked sallow at the jawline.
His liquid-gold eyes, usually sharp enough to flay an ambassador’s composure across a conference table, were clouded with a deep bottomless exhaustion.
Across the low glass table, seated close enough that their shoulders continually brushed, were the surviving remnants of his bloodline’s martial pride.
Tariq Al-Mansur sat with his forearms resting gingerly on his knees.
The young prince’s face was drawn, dark hollows under his eyes betraying sleepless agony, but his lips were curled into a soft quiet smile as he looked at the woman beside him.
His hands, once the pride of Khemet’s close-quarters sand-dancers, were bound in thick medicated bandages of woven spirit-silk.

Beneath the wrapping, the jagged brittle sensation of vitrified blood-quartz throbbed constantly, a brutal permanent reminder of the moment Seraphina Bloom’s azure flames had crystallized his flesh into brittle glass.
And resting her hand over his bandaged wrist was Safira.
She looked breathtakingly whole with her olive skin smooth and glowing under the amber lights and her long dark hair cascading over her bare shoulders in loose perfumed coils.
To any regular observer, she was unharmed but Menes knew the truth.
He’d been there in the special theater beneath the Citadel only hours after the match concluded...

He’d watched Tariq collapse to his knees, screaming until his throat bled, begging the court alchemists not to sweep away the pile of shattered burnt glass shards that Seraphina had left on the arena sand.

Menes himself, along with three of the highest-tier Sand Shifters in the dominion, had spent seven grueling hours weaving life through those fragments, feeding the girl’s dormant soul-core with pure liquefied solar-quartz until the shattered glass of her body reassembled, grain by agonizing grain, reversing the vitrification before the soul could fully detach into the void.

’This is why our blood makes us so strong,’ Menes thought, his fingers curling slowly against the cedar armrest, feeling the hard gold rings bite into his flesh. ’No other lineage on Earth could survive being reduced to broken glass... We are the children of the living dune... We shatter, and we reassemble. We bleed quartz, and we mend with gold...’
Yet, as Menes looked out the reinforced viewport at the endless expanse of the Great Dunes stretching toward the horizon, a cold sickening tremor seized the pit of his stomach.
’And yet... it’s that exact same blood that makes us so horrifyingly vulnerable.’
He could feel it.
It wasn’t a sensation he could articulate to his marshals or his surviving ministers as it wasn’t a physical mana signature, nor was it a spatial anomaly pinging the flagship’s radar.
It was an ancient chill scraping against the marrow of his bones, a rotten spectral friction that felt like coarse black grit churning inside his circulatory vessels.
Menes was a Fourth Stage powerhouse.
He commanded the authority of the desert sun, capable of melting an entire armored division into slag with a gesture of his hand yet, looking at his own palms, he felt utterly naked.
’I will not survive past today,’ the thought rose within him.
It was the certainty of an animal that heard the executioner’s boots on the cellar stairs.

The ancient sin was coming due and the debt that had rotted beneath the foundations of the White Citadel since the First Rift, the primordial crime their founder had committed against the shadow that birthed their empire, had finally climbed out of the deep dark...

He had already lost his eldest, the Crown Prince, to a border skirmish in the Sovereign Realm years ago and barely a day prior, his third son, Malikar, had been reduced to a pile of lifeless sand in an open-air cafe with his soul devoured before the boy could even draw breath to scream.
Menes’s gaze drifted back to Tariq.
On any normal day, Menes would have looked upon his middle son with cold disdain.
Tariq was too soft and too emotional as well.
He fought with the desperate bleeding heart of a romantic rather than the ruthless calculation required of a royal hegemon as he had risked the entire succession to shield this girl.

Yet now, watching the boy smile, a genuine tender fragile smile that looked entirely out of place in a family that had bred itself for slaughter, Menes felt an agonizing hollow ache rip through his chest.
’If only we had more time,’ the Pharaoh-President thought, the bitter words tasting like ashes on his tongue. ’If only the world weren’t ending today...’
Menes cleared his throat with the sound sharp and metallic in the quiet lounge.
Tariq stiffened immediately, his smile fading, replaced by the guarded defensive posture he’d worn in his father’s presence since childhood.
Safira pulled her hand back slightly, lowering her dark eyes in formal deference.

"The two of you have displayed remarkable resilience," Menes began, donning the mask that had shielded him through three decades of continental politics. "However, we are returning to Iunu... Within twenty-four hours, the High Council will convene to officially ratify the new succession charters following the tragic loss of your brother Malikar..."
Tariq’s jaw tightened at the mention of Malikar’s name with his bandaged fingers clenching into tight brittle fists.

"You are now the sole surviving male heir of House Al-Mansur, Tariq," Menes continued, his liquid-gold eyes narrowing slightly. "The responsibilities of the Sun-Crown will fall entirely upon your shoulders when my time concludes... Which brings us to the domestic reality of your household."
Menes leaned forward, resting his elbows on the table, fixing Safira with a cold piercing stare.

"Safira is the daughter of the Vice President. Her bloodline is distinguished, her martial foundation is exceptional, and her loyalty during the tournament cannot be questioned. However... she was shattered. Her core, while stabilized, carries micro-fractures that will permanently cap her cultivation at the lower tiers of the Third Stage. A Pharaoh-President requires an Empress whose lineage commands authority across the southern alliances. Therefore, as your father and your sovereign, I must decree that Safira cannot hold the primary seat of First Wife... She may enter your court only as a secondary consort or a concubine if you will."
The air in the lounge instantly dropped by ten degrees.
Safira’s breath hitched with her head dropping lower and her knuckles whitening against her silk trousers but she didn’t speak.
In the brutal patriarchal hierarchy of Khemet’s nobility, an emperor’s decree on marriage was absolute.
SH-SH-SH-SH-SH!
A violent hiss of shifting mineral erupted from the carpet as Tariq surged to his feet, knocking his heavy cedar chair backward.
He didn’t cower at all... With an explosive furious roar of mana, he thrust his right arm out, placing his entire body directly between his father and the woman he loved.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-SHING!
Streams of coarse golden sand bled directly through the pores of Tariq’s bandaged forearms.

The mineral grains spun in tight, screaming vortexes of pressure, condensing in mid-air with the sharp ringing of grinding steel, forming three jagged, six-foot-long desert lances that hovered mere inches from Menes’s throat.

"Do not speak of her as if she were an item in a trade manifest!" Tariq roared, his eyes blazing with an unhinged intensity that made his bandages crack with leaking crimson mana. "I don’t give a damn about the southern alliances! I don’t give a damn about the succession charters! When I was lying in the dirt with my hands crushed to powder, she threw herself in front of Seraphina Bloom’s blades to keep me breathing! If I take the Sun-Crown, she sits beside me as Empress, or I’ll burn the throne room to the ground myself!"
The sand lances hummed violently, vibrating with enough concussive force to crack the heavy crystal decanters on the table.
Tariq knew it was madness.
He knew, with certainty, that against his father’s Fourth Stage domain, these three sand lances wouldn’t even pierce the collar of Menes’s uniform.
A single flick of the Pharaoh-President’s finger could unravel Tariq’s core into dust...
Yet, standing there, bleeding from his wrists, Tariq didn’t flinch as he glared into his father’s eyes, ready to die right there on the cabin floor.
Menes stared at the spinning tips of the sand lances and for two agonizing seconds, the silence was deafening.
Then... the Pharaoh-President’s chest hitched.
CLAP! CLAP! CLAP!
A sudden booming bark of laughter tore from Menes’s throat.
He threw his head back with his hands coming together in slow, genuine applause that echoed off the reinforced bulkheads.
"Hah! Hahaha!" Menes laughed, the sound was wild as it lacked the detachment he’d worn for twenty years. "Look at you! Look at my boy!"
Tariq blinked, completely stunned, the sand lances faltering in mid-air.
"F-Father...?"

"You actually grew a pair of balls!" Menes grinned, wiping a genuine tear of amusement from the corner of his eye, his liquid-gold gaze shining with something that looked terrifyingly like pride. "Twenty-four years I spent watching you tiptoe through the court like a frightened hare, worrying about protocols and diplomatic propriety and now, you point steel at your Father’s throat for a woman... That was magnificent!"
Menes lowered his hands with his smile softening into something tired, almost sorrowful.

"She is your Empress, Tariq," Menes said softly, his voice carrying the finality of an irrevocable decree. "The marriage is recognized... You have my full, unconditional blessing. Take her and marry her the second our boots touch the sand of Iunu."
He looked at Safira, who was staring at him with wide tear-filled eyes, completely unable to process the sudden reversal.

"And do not make me wait," Menes added with a melancholic chuckle escaping him. "Give me more grandchildren already... Fill the palace with screaming, unruly brats who inherit their mother’s stubbornness. An old man wants to hold his grandson before his hair turns entirely white!"
